STAR THE DEFECT WAS NEVER WHICH BASE TO PICK. It was that a raw path string is ambiguous by construction, so the answer got deferred INTO a library, and the only thing a library has to guess with is ambient process state. `resolve_canon_order_file` called `std::env::current_dir()`; so did `resolve_sidecar`; so did `discover_config` for a relative start. One function, two callers, two different worlds. STAR SO THE TYPE ANSWERS IT: `AbsolutePath` cannot be constructed without naming a base, and every path override crossing into `ops` is now one. Round 538's rule is unchanged and lives where it belongs — the CLI reads the working directory because a path typed at a prompt is relative to where the user stands — and the MCP wire answers for itself. Measured end to end: from a subdirectory, `--order order.json` still resolves beside the user, and from the workspace root the same name still resolves there and fails naming that path. Nothing an operator sees has moved. STAR AND THE SWEEP FOUND A SECOND, QUIETER SPLIT. `--rules` was joined to the WORKSPACE ROOT while `--order` was joined to the WORKING DIRECTORY, in the same command, in adjacent functions. Nothing said so and nothing could have caught it, because each was locally reasonable. Both now use the base their own wire named. STAR THE PROPERTY IS GATED RATHER THAN ANNOUNCED. `no_library_crate_resolves_a_path_from_the_working_directory` walks every tracked library source and exempts the two wires BY NAME, since a wire is exactly the place that may read it. STAR THE DEAD HELPER IS GONE, not left as a convenience: `resolve_explicit_cli_path` had one caller, that caller was the CWD branch, and when the branch went the function went with it. Round 1001.decision_summary: R1001 (DEBT) — the eighth audit, and the finding is that Round 1000 typed the paths that went THROUGH the library and left the ones the wire opens itself, which is the half-cleanup this repository bans by name. Its own carry said so: "the manifest arguments are not yet typed ... they are the same ambiguity for an agent, and the type is now there for them" — a sentence describing work, in the round that built the type. One line still decides what a relative path means to an agent, and now it decides for EVERY path an agent sends rather than for some of them. STAR AN INJECTION FOUND A HOLE THE AUDIT DID NOT. Replacing `propose_verdict`'s manifest path with a fixed nonsense string left all 96 tests green: nothing in this repository had ever run that tool. It is the generate-gate-repair loop's gate — the one the contract tells an agent to call BEFORE writing for real — so a wire reading the wrong file would hand back a verdict about something the agent never sent. It has a test now, in both directions: the verdict must name what is wrong with THE MANIFEST THE AGENT NAMED, and a path naming nothing must be refused rather than answered. STAR AND THAT SAME INJECTION SHOWED THE ERROR MESSAGE NAMING THE WRONG FILE. `read manifest {}` printed the ARGUMENT while `read_to_string` had opened something else; the two agree in production, so this was a trap rather than a defect — the message a reader would trust in the one situation where it is wrong. It names the file that was actually opened. STAR ROUND 999's REASONING WAS PUT TO A RUN AND HELD. It argued that a mid-manifest failure is the same class as a last-row one because both verbs commit through one primitive. The middle-row arm is written; it fires independently on the row-at-a-time injection, and no injection separates it from the last-row arm. The argument was right, and it is now a measurement rather than an argument. Round 1004.decision_summary: R1004 (DEBT) — the ninth audit. Two carries were work described in prose, and one of them was about the verb an agent is told to trust before it writes anything. STAR ROUND 1001 WROTE THE TEST AND DID NOT WRITE IT: "nothing yet asserts the verdict itself — that a manifest which would violate a continuity rule comes back `rollback` with the rule named, and a clean one comes back `commit`". That is the fourth time this session a carry has described a test in enough detail to write it. It is written: a world with a map and no way between two places, a candidate that walks between them, and the same world's clean candidate beside it. STAR AND WRITING IT FOUND THE SHARP EDGE OF THE VERB. On a workspace that declares no `[continuity] severity`, the refused candidate comes back `verdict: commit` WITH the violation listed underneath — `violation_count: 1`, `gating_violation_count: 0`. Nothing in that answer is untrue and an agent reading `verdict` alone would write a beat the map forbids. That is now asserted, not discovered later: the test drives the same manifest through both configurations and pins both answers. STAR AN INJECTION OF MINE WENT GREEN AND THE GREEN WAS THROWN AWAY. Zeroing `gating_violation_count` changed nothing, because the verdict is decided by a separate `gate.gates` and the count is only reported. Re-injected at the decision — always-commit and always-rollback — and both fire. A green under an injection that never reached the code path is not evidence, which is this session's most-repeated lesson and the first time it has caught me picking the wrong line rather than the wrong anchor. STAR THE SECOND CARRY WAS A DOCUMENTED ASYMMETRY DOCUMENTED ON ONE SIDE. Since Round 999 the MCP schema must say what a path resolves against and a gate holds it there; the CLI said nothing across 96 flag mentions. The half that was documented was the half whose caller could not have guessed. The half left silent is the one whose caller can guess WRONG — a typed path resolves against the working directory while a path declared in the same project's `mnemosyne.toml` resolves against the workspace root, and nothing said so. Four lines of `--help`, gated against the real binary's output.

`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/evidence_replay_smoke.rs` — `the_cli_help_says_what_a_typed_path_is_relative_to`, asserted against the real binary's output rather than the source, because what matters is what a user is shown.

STAR THE ROWS ARE ADDED. `propose_verdict`'s verdict now answers for three rule families rather than two: a transition rule refusing a step the map forbids, a structural invariant refusing an unregistered entity, and an interval rule refusing a pair of beats ordered the other way. The interval violation was FOUND and did not gate: structural violations gate under `[continuity] severity` and interval ones under `interval_severity`, separately. An agent that sets one and not the other gets `commit` beside a violation it asked to be gated on — the same sharp edge Round 1004 pinned, now known to have two independent switches rather than one. The test declares both. STAR THE OTHER CARRY WAS TRIED AND IS A MEASURED LIMIT, not a deferral. `style_check.doc` is watched by the filter the report echoes; the stronger case wants the finding set to vary, and it cannot be authored through this surface. `max_sentence_length` fires at 200 characters and `set_section_intent` caps the field at 200, so the write path forbids exactly what the rule flags; no MCP tool writes a section body; and a store written OUT OF BAND with a longer intent still produced no finding. Three routes, none of which is "I did not try". The case says in place what it proves.

Round 1009.decision_summary: R1009 (DEBT) — the twelfth audit, and BOTH of the audit round's own carries were false claims about the world rather than undone work. Round 1008 was the round that found the carry test failing its own author; its two substantive carries then asserted things that are not true. STAR "`style_check`'s FINDING SET CANNOT BE MADE TO VARY THROUGH ANY SURFACE THIS REPOSITORY EXPOSES" IS REFUTED BY 66 CHARACTERS. I measured ONE rule — `max_sentence_length`, which fires at 200 characters while the intent field caps at 200 — and generalised to every rule. Two of the four T3 rules have no character threshold at all: `cross_doc_reference_explicit` fires on an intent that mentions `DESIGN.md` without the reference form. The case now watches the finding set varying with the filter rather than the filter the report echoes back. STAR "THE DISCLOSURE GATES ARE THE FOURTH FAMILY REACHING THE SAME FIELD" IS ALSO REFUTED. A verdict has two sources: a shape rejection from applying the manifest and the continuity scan over the applied clone. Nothing else feeds it. The three rows already covered both — one shape, two continuity — so the table was complete while its carry said it was missing a quarter of the surface. STAR AND THE OWNER'S CORRECTION IS THE ROUND'S REAL CONTENT: I established that second refutation BY READING THE FILE, which is exactly how the wrong claim was made in the first place. `source` was a `&'static str` assigned in two places, so "this verb has exactly two sources" was only ever settleable by reading. It is a TYPE now — `ViolationSource`, with `ALL` — and the verdict table asserts that the sources it observes equal the sources the type can carry. STAR THE SWEEP NEEDS NO PINNED REVISION, which is why it is cheap enough to run in the normal suite: Round 974's replay rebuilds each kit at the revision that produced it, and that is the right instrument for reproducing bytes. Round 1014.decision_summary: R1014 (DEBT) — Two agent-facing path arguments were resolved against the server process's working directory, and BOTH gates that should have caught it were keyed on the NAME `*_path`. `validate_disclosure_leak.against` and `validate_render_fidelity.against` are paths that are not called one. Each sat in the same struct as an `order_path` that obeys the Round 1002 rule, went straight to `Path::new`, and was invisible to the Round 999 schema gate (which asks whether a property's name ends in `_path`) and to the Round 1000 library gate (which exempts this crate by name). STAR THE CONSEQUENCE WAS WORSE THAN A WRONG BASE. `AtomicStore::load` answers a missing path with an EMPTY store — right for the workspace's own sidecar, where absence is the bootstrap state and a test already pins it — so both render-acceptance gates returned `reextracted_facts: 0`, `off_path: []`, `leaks: []`: the shape of a clean pass, from a gate that had never opened the file. Since Round 1002 requires an agent to send workspace-relative paths, EVERY relative `against` an agent could send produced a passing verdict from a gate that evaluated nothing. That is the failure the contract names in its own words — a gate that evaluated NOTHING must never read the same as a gate that PASSED. STAR DECIDED: AN AGENT-FACING PATH IS A TYPE. `AgentPath` has exactly one way out, `resolve(workspace)` — no `as_str`, no `Deref` — so the base cannot be left unnamed; the two ops entry points take `&AbsolutePath`, and the compiler enumerated all four wire call sites (MCP resolves against the workspace, the CLI against the working directory, which is right there per Round 538). A store the caller NAMED is read by `load_named_store`, which refuses an absent file and says why, while the workspace's own sidecar keeps the opposite and correct policy. STAR AND THE RULE IS NOW STAMPED RATHER THAN COPIED: `agent_facing_tools` writes the resolution sentence into every marked property, and is the ONE reader `list_tools`, `get_tool` and the gate share. That replaced twenty-four hand-typed copies of one paragraph, and made the gate's population the type's marker instead of a naming convention. Of 25 typed path properties, 2 were unreachable by a name-keyed gate — exactly the two that were broken.

`crates/mnemosyne-ops/src/lib.rs` — `disclosure_leak_report` / `render_fidelity_report` take `&AbsolutePath` for `against`, so the base must be named at each wire. `load_named_store` refuses a store the caller named that is not there; `load_atomic_store` keeps bootstrap-empty for the workspace's own sidecar, and the doc says which is which and why they differ.

`crates/mnemosyne-mcp/src/main.rs` — `agent_facing_tools` stamps the resolution rule into every marked property and is the one reader behind `list_tools`, `get_tool` and the gate. Twenty-four copies of the rule paragraph deleted from the field docs.

Round 1015.decision_summary: R1015 (DEBT) — The sibling Round 1014 named, measured and repaired: a sidecar the caller names that is not there was read as an EMPTY STORE, so a one-character typo turned a populated world into a clean bill. Measured on the real binary before anything was changed: `report-entity-kind-migration --sidecar side.json` says "0 unregistered kinds over 1 entity(ies) — every in-use kind is registered", and the same command with `sidde.json` says "0 unregistered kinds over 0 entity(ies) — the store registers no entities, so nothing was checked". Both exit 0, and the second reads like a clean bill while naming its own emptiness as a fact about the store rather than about a file that does not exist. Ninety-six verbs take `--sidecar`. STAR THE REPAIR SPLITS BY DIRECTION BECAUSE THE OTHER HALF WAS MEASURED TOO, and a blanket rule would have broken it: `add-entity-kind --kind place --sidecar side.json` CREATES the file, which is a real workflow. Writes already load for themselves through `run_atomic_mutate`, so making the READ path strict leaves creation untouched — and the distinction is already carried by the argument, since `None` is the workspace's own sidecar, built in or declared by `[atomic] sidecar_path`, where absence is the bootstrap state that a test one line below has pinned since R356. So: `load_atomic_store` refuses a NAMED sidecar that is absent and keeps the permissive rule for the default. STAR AND COUNTING THE CONSUMERS FOUND A FOURTH SITE. `emit_publishable_override_ledger_draft` is read-only but resolved and loaded for itself rather than through the shared reader, which is exactly how it kept the old rule after the read path had lost it; it now shares the loader. That site was found by enumerating every caller of the loader, not by reading the verb the repair began from — the rule being that a gate which rejects a relation must be applied by every reader of it.

`crates/mnemosyne-ops/src/lib.rs` — `emit_publishable_override_ledger_draft` reads through the shared loader instead of resolving and loading for itself, so the fourth site of the defect gets the same rule.
`crates/mnemosyne-ops/src/lib.rs` — `load_named_store`'s refusal is worded for all three of its callers now that it has three, rather than for the render-acceptance gate it was written for.
verification_bullets: STAR MEASURED ON THE REAL BINARY BEFORE THE REPAIR, both directions: read with a typo'd sidecar answered "0 over 0 entities" at exit 0 where the real one answered "0 over 1"; write into a sidecar that does not exist CREATED it at exit 0. The second is why the rule is not blanket.

Round 1018.decision_summary: R1018 (BUILD) — The six cases Round 1017 deleted were restored, and the carry that named how to restore them was half wrong in a way worth more than the half that was right: 108 to 114. Round 1017 measured six order-keyed reports as byte-identical under both of the shared world's canon orders, correctly concluded that the two orders differ by MEMBERSHIP rather than SEQUENCE, and carried "add a third canon-order that reads the same scenes in a different order, plus six needles". That third order was written first thing this round. It moved ONE of the six. STAR THE OTHER FIVE WERE NOT ORDER-INSENSITIVE, THEY WERE EMPTY. Run against the world as it stood, `report_irony_intervals` returned `windows: [], cross_frame_edges: 0`; `report_payoff_substantiation` returned `setups_total: 0`; `report_quest_graph` returned `quests: []`; `report_timeline_gaps` returned `outcomes: [], interval_rules: 0`; and `report_fork_tree`'s single order-dependent field, `at_placed`, was true under every order that contained the fork point, which both of them did. A REPORT WITH AN EMPTY BODY CANNOT BE MOVED BY ANY ARGUMENT, so those five arguments were UNTESTABLE rather than unread, and no amount of reordering was ever going to separate the two. This is the empty-result lesson one layer out from where it was learned: the standing rule asks what a GATE returns for input it cannot check, and the answer that an empty violation list reads the same as a clean pass. Here the instrument doing the MEASURING was the empty one, and it reported "this argument does nothing" for five arguments that in fact do something. STAR THE REPAIR IS THE WORLD, NOT THE CASES. The shared branched story gained the two things those reports read: a SECOND FRAME that holds the way shut while ground truth holds it open, which is the cross-frame divergence dramatic irony is measured over, and a QUEST taken up in the first scene and completed in the third, which is at once a credited setup for payoff substantiation and the reserved `pursues`/`completed_by` roles the quest graph derives from. Both are what the north star actually authors rather than scaffolding, which is the standard the world was declared under. It also gained a fourth road that never reaches the fork point, since whether the fork is placed is the one thing the fork tree reads an order for. STAR AND A FIVE-LINE COPY OF THE WORLD SURVIVED ROUND 1016 AND IS NOW GONE. `report_playable_world`'s order case still carried its own inline sections, facts and two order files — the exact duplication `world!` was built to end — because it also carried a `{ws}` substitution to spell the workspace root out. That substitution was a workaround for the rule Round 1002 REPLACED, so folding the case into the shared world left the helper with no user, and it was deleted rather than kept: a case still using it would be proving the old contract.

Round 1020.decision_summary: R1020 (MEASURE then BUILD) — The carry said a differential could not catch the required half, and the carry was wrong; the measurement that says so is this round's whole point. Rounds 1017 and 1019 both wrote, without running it, that a blanket differential over required arguments "would not have caught `against`, because both arms fail" — and left the required half undesigned on that basis. STAR IT IS FALSE, AND THE REASON IS THE SAME BEHAVIOUR THAT MADE THE BUG INVISIBLE. Round 1014's defect had two halves: `against` resolved against the server process's working directory, and `AtomicStore::load` answered a missing path with an EMPTY STORE. Both were reconstructed here — the wrong base through the residual hole the type still permits, and the empty-store fallback in place of `load_named_store` — and the arms do not fail. THEY BOTH SUCCEED AND ANSWER IDENTICALLY, `reextracted_facts: 0` either way, which is precisely what a two-value differential detects and what a presence-differential never could. The premise reversed the failure mode: an argument read against the wrong base does not error, it reads NOTHING and reports it as an answer. STAR AND THE MACRO NEEDED NO CHANGE TO EXPRESS IT. Every case so far differs by an argument being absent or present, and a required argument has no absent arm — but the base already carries a value and the `=` supplies a second, so the two arms differ by WHICH STORE the gate was pointed at. The form was there the whole time; what was missing was the population. STAR SO THE ACCOUNTING NOW COVERS THE WHOLE SURFACE, AND THE RATIO IT PRINTS IS HONEST FOR THE FIRST TIME. The optional half read as coverage for as long as the required half had no gate to print beside it — 122 of 122 with a parenthetical saying 172 were excluded, which is the shape of a number that describes everything except where the last bug was found. There are now two gates over one generated `EXERCISED` list, and it is the ROUTER that decides which half a pair belongs to: a second generated const would have needed the macro to know a fact about the schema rather than about the case. Required reads 1 of 172, and the 171 are named.

Round 1022.decision_summary:
The required half of the MCP argument surface stopped being a table. Round 1020 opened it with the value-A-vs-value-B form and five hand-written cases; the remaining 163 arguments sit on SEVENTY-SIX tools, so the unit of work was wrong. A tool needs ONE call that is valid; what each of its arguments needs follows from the router's own schema. So `probed!` takes one valid call per tool and probes every required argument of it with a value that names nothing, deriving the probe value and the needle from the declared type. Required unexercised went 167 to 16 on 40 declarations, and a required argument added to a declared tool later is covered by the same declaration.

The measurement that preceded it refuted the defect I went looking for. Twenty-four probes said every existing-ref argument fails loud on an unregistered value (15 of 15), and that a duplicate `add_*` id is accepted as `(no-op)` only when the content is IDENTICAL — divergent content is refused as a silent overwrite. There was no dropped payload. What the measurement did find is that both rules live in hand-written prose at each site and nothing enforces either.

Then the sweep found the thing I was not looking for. TWELVE required arguments are accepted with a value naming nothing and land nowhere in the store, and eleven of them are called `reason`. The primitives validate them non-empty as an "audit-trail safeguard" and never persist them: `set_section_coverage_expectation` writes `section.coverage_expectation` and drops its reason, and `amend_fact` — which is not a deletion, which changes what the canon says — drops the reason the canon changed. Beside them `add_confirmation_event.rationale` IS stored, so the store already has the shape for it and nothing declares why one kind of rationale is kept and the other is not.
changes_bullets: `probed!`: one valid call per tool, every required argument probed with a schema-derived sentinel, and the verdict DERIVED not declared — a mutation is judged by its store, a read by its answer with the echoed value stripped out, and an argument that decided whether the tool wrote at all counts as read

Round 1023.decision_summary:
Round 1022's sweep reported that `add_confirmation_event.timestamp` stored the sentinel `mn-probe-names-nothing` verbatim, and following that found the worse half beneath it: the event id was DERIVED with the clock in it, so the idempotence this primitive documents — "a re-append of the identical act hashes to the same id and is rejected (idempotent append-only)" — was FALSE. Measured before the repair: one act, restamped a second later and then given a string that is not a time, was accepted three times and the ledger held three rows. The max-rigor confirmation ledger is the substrate an external consumer reads as evidence of what was verified, and it could be inflated by one confirmer re-running with a moving clock.

THE CLOCK IS NOT PART OF THE ACT, so it comes out of the id. What distinguishes two genuine verification runs was already in the derivation — `confirming_run`, which the self-confirm invariant forces to differ from the authoring run — so the timestamp could only ever let ONE run record ONE act repeatedly. It stays a field, the recorded provenance of when the confirmer says it looked, and stops being an identity.

AND THE TIME AXIS IS NOW A TIME: exactly `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. Narrower than RFC 3339 on purpose, because the general form admits offsets and fractional seconds and two instants written in different offsets do not sort into the order they happened; one fixed-width UTC form makes lexicographic order chronological, which an append-only ledger gets for free and no later parser can give back. Hand-written rather than delegated — the workspace carries no date dependency and a fixed layout with a range per field and a real calendar day is smaller than one.

The rule had been stated and unenforced in two places at once: the CLI's usage said `--timestamp <iso>` and the MCP schema said "caller-supplied timestamp". Both now read the validator's own const, and both are gated on containing it, because three hand-written copies of one rule is how this recurs.
changes_bullets: `timestamp` out of `derive_confirmation_event_id`: one verification act records once however many times its clock moves, which is what the primitive already documented
`check_utc_instant` in the primitive, so both wires get one invariant structurally rather than by parity: exactly `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, real calendar day, leap second admitted
`UTC_INSTANT_FORM` is the one home for the form; the MCP field doc and the CLI usage line are each gated on containing it
verification_bullets: the measurement is now the assertion: the same act restamped is refused saying "identical act", seven malformed instants are each refused naming what is wrong, a leap day is accepted and 29 February 2026 is not, and the ledger holds one row per RUN
injection I6 (put the clock back in the id) turns it red on the restamped arm; injection I7 (drop the validation) turns it red and leaves the other 218 tests in that crate green
my own first draft of the test was wrong in a way the repair caught: the leap-day arm reused the same act and was refused as a duplicate, so the calendar arms had to become distinct runs
workspace 1719 tests green, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace T1 and T3 = 0
carry_forward_bullets: the store held zero confirmation events, so no id in it changes shape; a store that already held some would need the ids rederived and this round would have been a migration
nothing reads `timestamp` except the id derivation it just left, so the ledger still has no verb that orders or filters by time — the field is now trustworthy and unused

Round 1024.decision_summary:
Ten primitives took a mandatory `reason`, validated it non-blank as an "audit-trail safeguard", and then never persisted it. Round 1022's probe sweep found them by sending a value that names nothing and finding no trace of it in the store; the CLI twin on a scratch workspace said the same, so it was not a wire defect but the primitives' own shape. Beside them `add_confirmation_event.rationale` IS kept, so the store already had the shape and nothing declared why one rationale survived and the other did not. What the prose offered instead — the transaction-time audit is the git history (R330) — does not actually reach: COMMIT_FORMAT.md allows one to three bullets for a whole ROUND, so a per-mutation reason has nowhere to go in a commit message, and an agent resuming through `mnemosyne-cli query` cannot read git at all.

THE REASON BELONGS TO THE CHANGE, NOT TO THE RESULTING STATE, and that decides the shape rather than the cost does. A field on the record holds one reason and the second change destroys the first; a record is changed many times for many reasons. Nor can a row carry a derived id the way a confirmation event does — two amends of one fact for the same stated reason are two acts, and Round 1023 took the clock out of that derivation precisely because identity must come from the act. So the ledger is a SEQUENCE ordered by the order the acts happened, with no id and no timestamp: R330 stands, and the commit that added the rows is when they happened.

IT COSTS ONE ARGUMENT AT ONE CHOKE POINT. `save_with_receipt` is the single save path and already carried three quarters of the row — primitive, target kind, target id — so `save_reasoned` is the same call with the reason, and a primitive cannot accept one and drop it. The row survives its target on purpose: five of the ten writers are removals, and the removed thing is exactly what no other read can answer about, which is why the field-classification gate records `target_id` as deliberately not a live ref.

A LEDGER NOBODY CAN READ WOULD HAVE MOVED THE GAP RATHER THAN CLOSED IT, since the whole argument for the store over git was that an agent reads the store. So `report-mutation-reasons` / `report_mutation_reasons` land with it, `--target` narrowing to one record including a removed one, and the printed total staying the whole ledger so a narrow answer is never read as the whole of it.
changes_bullets: `AtomicStore.mutation_reasons` (schema 46): an append-only sequence, written only by `save_reasoned`, so recording the reason is the same call that writes the file rather than a step nine primitives must remember
`redact_term` records one row per entry it actually rewrote and is the only writer that already knows its round, so `applied_in` rides along instead of being validated and dropped
the read side lands with the write side: `report-mutation-reasons [--target]` on both wires, total always the whole ledger

Round 1025.decision_summary:
The MCP argument surface has no silent set on either half. Optional: 123 of 123 proved by a differential. Required: 10 by a differential and 162 by the probe sweep, with nothing in neither list. The two counts are printed apart every run and never summed, because they are not the same evidence — a differential shows the value the agent sent decided the answer, a probe shows only that the handler validated it or left it observable.

WHAT CLOSED THE LAST FIVE WAS NOT MORE PROBING. Four of them are the shapes the sweep derives no value for — three closed enums behind a `$ref`, whose members serde refuses before the handler sees them, and one array of objects — so each got the thing the sweep could not derive: a second valid value written by hand. The fifth was different in kind. `emit_publishable_override_ledger_draft.reason` was excepted because the tool WRITES NOTHING, so its reason appearing in the answer is indistinguishable from an echo, and Round 1019 rejected echo needles. That exception was earned by the tool's semantics rather than by a limit — the draft IS composed from the arguments — and the honest close was to ask a question an echo cannot answer: whether the value landed in the reason SLOT. The needle is the TOML key beside its value, so a handler that put `reason` where `kind` goes fails it.

AND THE ROUND OPENED BY MEASURING A CLAIM I HAD MADE WITHOUT MEASURING. Round 1024 raised the schema to 46 and I said, in the same breath, that an older binary can therefore no longer open this repository's sidecar. The branch that makes that true had no test: every schema test beside it walks BACKWARD, an older store loading into today's binary. Building an old revision would answer it once. Round 1026.decision_summary:
Round 1025 shipped the argument surface with one carry: the probe cannot tell a correct refusal from an empty answer where a refusal was intended, because it has no way to know which polarity an argument was meant to have. THE CARRY WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS PAID. `query_section` was made to answer `{}` for a section that does not exist instead of refusing, and the whole workspace stayed green — 1727 tests over 135 binaries, nothing anywhere reading the difference between a correct refusal and a fabricated empty answer about a thing that is not there.

So the polarity is a TYPE, the way Round 1014 made a path one, and it stamps a `format` the sweep reads to DERIVE its oracle. Typing the surface then answered a question that had not been asked: how many polarities there are. THREE, and the store is right about all three. `ExistingRef` is refused at the call, naming the value. `FreshId` is the id a new record is filed under, and what it forbids is a SECOND record under an id already held — the rule Round 1022 measured and recorded as hand-written prose with nothing enforcing it. `ScannedRef` is admitted by the call and refused at the SCAN boundary, which is what the field-classification table means by `Coverage::Projection`; marking those `ExistingRef` would have made the type lie about where the refusal happens, and leaving them bare would have said nothing about a reference an agent can dangle.

EACH MARK BOUGHT A DEFECT. `InventoryEntry::section_ref` was recorded in that table as `WritePathOnly` — "the write path validates it" — which was true only of the SHAPE: an inventory entry could name a section that does not exist and no gate anywhere disagreed. Round 847 typed the field a `SectionId` and said in the same entry what the arc did not buy, LOOKUP; this is that step, at both writers, with the parity test `CLAUDE.md` demands of a field two primitives write. And `AtomicSection::resolved_by` sat beside `superseded_by`, classified identically, with `project.rs` saying that projecting it "routes the edge through the existing cross-ref orphan check for free". IT DID NOT: that check reads the STORE field by field and had an arm for `superseded_by` alone. Only one of the two carried a measurement in its note, and it was the one that worked.

THE POPULATION IS THE TYPE'S AND THE BRIDGE IS ONLY A NAME. 116 arguments are marked and 42 of them are looked up or minted under a name no `*_id` gate would have reached — `coord`, `telling`, `world`, `truth_frame`, `at`, `frame`, `unit`, `parameter`, `condition`, `file`. Round 1027.decision_summary:
Ten agent-facing arguments enforced a closed vocabulary the schema did not describe. The wire took a `String`, the handler parsed it, and the refusal spelled the members out — so an agent reading the tool saw `string`, guessed, and learned the set by being refused. THE SETS WERE NOT MISSING. Every one of them is already a Rust enum, and Round 690 had already built the mechanism that carries a type to the agent-facing schema — the optional `schemars` feature this crate alone enables. The wire simply declined to use it.

THE POPULATION CAME FROM THE RESOLVERS, NOT FROM THE MESSAGES, and the difference was the measurement. Reading the sweep's own refusal texts for a set spelled out found NINE. Asking instead which arguments are parsed by a `from_tag` found TEN: `add_confirmation_event.method` says its set as `linkage_check|semantic_review|coverage_attestation` where every other message on the surface uses `join_or`, so a matcher keyed on the phrasing missed the one site that had already drifted. Round 870 built `join_or` to make exactly that impossible and gave three vocabularies a home; SEVEN never got one, and `BindingKind` had `vocabulary()` and was hand-spelled at three sites anyway.

So a vocabulary is DECLARED ONCE and everything falls out of it: `closed_vocabulary!` generates `ALL`, `as_str`, the message, and `from_tag` DERIVED FROM `ALL` — which is what keeps `ALL` load-bearing, since a member missing from it stops parsing loudly instead of quietly shortening a sentence nobody re-reads. The declaration also carries its own parity guard, because serde's spelling is now both what an agent's call is judged by and what the schema shows it, and a tag the wire takes and `from_tag` refuses would be one value set with two definitions.

TYPING THE WIRE MADE THE SWEEP ANSWER A BETTER QUESTION. serde now refuses a non-member before the handler is reached, which is a STRUCTURAL proof no other value gets through, so the probe stops sending a sentinel and sends a SECOND MEMBER — a differential, not a floor. Required arguments proved by differential went 10 to 20 and the probe floor 162 to 152, which is the carry Round 1025 wrote for this exact repair.

THREE THINGS THE WORK ITSELF FOUND. The wire accepted `Superseded`: both surfaces lowercased the tag before parsing and neither the schema nor the help said so, and two of this crate's own fixtures had drifted into that undocumented spelling. A closed set has THREE schema shapes, not two — variants that all carry doc comments land as `oneOf` of `const`, none as a flat `enum`, and a MIX lands as a `oneOf` holding both kinds, which is what `DecisionStatus` takes and what a reader knowing two shapes called `composed` and reported as no closed set at all. And a member equal to the field's default is omitted by the store, so a needle counted in one direction reads a correct handler as one that ignored the argument: the count has to run both ways.

The ledger is append-only, so the sentence in Round 1027 stands and this entry is where it stops being true.

The injection is the whole point of landing it now: dropping ONE member at the string edge — a `filter` that quietly refuses `imply` — turns the test red with the two definitions printed side by side, the refusal listing `imply` as admissible in the same sentence that refuses it. The general form needs no table: `validated` is already the sweep's verdict for an argument whose handler refused a value naming nothing, so the population is every refusal THE SWEEP ITSELF COLLECTED, and the question put to each is whether the property an agent reads says anything about the space — `enum`, `format`, or `pattern`, the three answers JSON Schema has.

The carry said one argument remained (`add_confirmation_event.timestamp`). The gate said EIGHT, across six tools, in four kinds — and the kinds are the finding, because a repair chosen for one of them is wrong for the others:

- TWO WERE A CLOSED SET NOBODY HAD REGISTERED. `add_inventory_entry.status` and `set_inventory_status.status` refuse with `expected active|deprecated|reserved`, and `InventoryStatus` sits in `mnemosyne-core` three declarations below `DecisionStatus` with a hand-written `as_str`, a hand-written case-insensitive `from_str`, and a hand-written `|` message. Round 1027 moved ten vocabularies and walked past this one for exactly the reason it recorded at the time: its refusal is spelled with `|` and it was in no table. The instrument existed and the value set existed; what was missing was the wire using them.
- FOUR WERE REFERENCES THAT COULD NOT CARRY A MARK. `canon_from` and `frame` on both `add_fact` and `amend_fact` are fields of `atomic::FactImport` — the one fact DTO, shared with the CLI importer — and `atomic` does not depend on the MCP crate, so no field of it can be typed with a marker declared there. `COMPOSED_POLARITY` already existed for the `fact_id` case and its stated reason was opposite polarity in two tools; the real second reason is this one, and four rows put both the schema `format` and the polarity oracle onto arguments that had neither.
- ONE WAS A FORM THE SCHEMA STATED ONLY IN PROSE. Round 1023 gave `timestamp` one home (`UTC_INSTANT_FORM`) and gated the two surfaces that STATE it in English. A client cannot act on English. The layout table the checker walks is now a const both readers take from, `utc_instant_pattern()` derives the regular expression from it, and a `UtcInstant` marker publishes that on the property. The pattern is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT — no regex knows February has no 30th — and the parity test asserts the implication that matters (accepted by the checker implies matched by the pattern) and asserts the converse false, so the asymmetry is measured rather than assumed either way.
- ONE WAS A GRAMMAR INSIDE A STRING. `set_section_alternatives` took `<alternative> -- <reason>` lines and split them in the handler, while the schema said `string`. The primitive it calls has always taken `&[RejectedAlternative]`: the WIRE was less typed than the thing it called. It now takes the pair, and it stops sharing `SetSectionBulletsArgs` — which is what the shared struct was hiding, since every other bullet setter takes free prose and this one did not.

Typing the array of objects would have cost the evidence: the probe builds its sentinel from the schema and had no shape for an object, so `alternatives` would have become an exception, and an excepted argument is one whose handler could stop reading it with no run saying so. So the probe learned the shape instead — one element with every required string property set to the sentinel, built from the ITEM schema, so a property added to the element type is sent by the same declaration.

THE ROUND'S OWN DEFECT CAME FROM PLANNING AN INJECTION RATHER THAN FROM READING. Deleting `pattern` from the published property reddened nothing: the parity test proves the derived pattern is honest and says nothing about whether the schema carries it, and the value-space gate is satisfied by the `format` that remains. The assertion that the property publishes the derived pattern is this round's, and it is what injection 1 fires.

Round 1030.decision_summary:
The four debts this round was asked to close each named a thing to measure, and three of the four measurements said something the debt did not.

DEBT M asked why `import_sections.sections` stayed excepted from the probe sweep after the previous round taught the probe to build an element for an array of objects. The round before had written that the exception's survival was "evidence its item schema is not an object of required strings — not evidence about what it is", which was correct and was also an admission that nobody had looked. The diagnostic already prints what the probe MET, and what it met was `{"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/SectionImport"}}`. The element's properties were not there to read.

THAT IS NOT A PROBE LIMIT. It is the rule Round 1014 stated and Round 1027 applied to ten closed sets — a set behind a reference is one the client and the gate must each follow, and a set the client does not follow is a set the agent still has to guess — never once put to the whole surface. Put to it: FOURTEEN of 295 agent-facing properties named a definition instead of showing their shape, and one of them was `add_parameter_gate.op`, a closed vocabulary the round that typed ten of them believed it had already reached. Two of the sweep's three exceptions existed only because of this, and both became unearned the moment the shapes were inlined — the earned-exception assertion required their removal rather than permitting it.

DEBT L asked whether the value-space gate's `enum` answer is reachable. It is not, and the reason is structural rather than incidental: serde refuses a non-member before the handler, so a declared closed set never produces the `validated` verdict the gate keys on, and the arm above it already asserts that such an argument's answer MOVES. The branch stays, because the three answers are the classification and not a prediction; what it now carries is an assertion whose failure says the arm above stopped running.

DEBT N asked whether other shared argument structs hide a constrained value space among free ones, the way `SetSectionBulletsArgs` did. The grouping is derived from the properties the ROUTER exposes rather than from the Rust types, which reaches every tool and also catches the case where separate structs are structurally indistinguishable to an agent — for the reader of a schema those are the same thing. FOUR groups, and the guesses written before the measurement were wrong about three of them. One was the defect again, three declarations away from where the last one was found: `set_section_intent`, `set_section_title` and `set_section_parent_doc` share a `text` field whose documentation reads "New value. FOR INTENT: a single sentence, max ~200 chars" — a per-user rule inside a shape that can only say one thing, applied by an agent's reading to a heading and to a doc identifier as well.

DEBT O asked for the injections the summary round had not run. Three landed, each reddening exactly one test: the clock back into the derived event id, the forward-schema refusal disabled, and one primitive's reason dropped on the floor. The third is worth its own line — it reddens `remove_section_binding_probed` and NOT `every_reason_an_agent_sends_reaches_the_ledger`, which is the division working as designed: that gate proves every reason-taking tool is probed, and the probe is the oracle.

THE AXIS IS DORMANT AFTER THIS. Not because it is exhausted — this round found a fourteen-instance class the arc had walked past twice — but because it no longer needs a person to decide to resume it. Every instrument on it fails on the round that breaks it: a new argument lands in neither accounting list, a new refusal with a silent schema reddens its tool, a new `$ref` reddens the whole-surface gate, a new shared shape reddens the declaration, and a new tool with a required `reason` reddens for want of a probe. The resume condition is those failures, not a note.
changes_bullets: Fourteen agent-facing properties stop naming a definition: `SectionImport`, `FactImport`, `FrameImport`, `EntityImport`, `EntityKindImport`, `PredicateImport`, `BranchImport`, `UnitImport`, `EdgeCostImport`, `EdgeGuardImport`, `DisclosurePlanImport`, `IntervalOp`, `ConvergeEdgeArg` and `DisclosureRevealArg` are now inlined, and `no_agent_facing_property_hides_its_shape_behind_a_ref` walks the property AND its `items` on every tool, printing 295 read / 0 hidden.

`except "op"` and `except "sections"` are gone, removed under protest by the earned-exception assertion once the probe could build their elements. One exception remains and it is the tool that writes nothing.

The value-space gate asserts its `enum` answer is unreachable, with a message that says what a firing would mean: serde refuses a non-member first, so a `validated` verdict on a closed set means the arm requiring such an argument to move the answer stopped running.

`every_shared_argument_shape_is_declared` groups tools by the property map the router exposes and compares the groups to `SHARED_ARGS`, whose rows state the claim that makes sharing safe — that every member means the same by each argument.

`SetSectionTextArgs` becomes `SetSectionTitleArgs`, `SetSectionParentDocArgs` and `SetSectionIntentArgs`, each naming its argument (`title` / `parent_doc` / `intent`) and stating its own value space; the shared `text` doc had carried the intent's length rule for all three.
Three injections re-verify the gates of Rounds 1023, 1024 and 1025, which the previous round had only seen green.
verification_bullets: Workspace 1735 passed / 0 failed / 11 ignored, exit 0; clippy `-D warnings` exit 0; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `validate-workspace` T1 orphan 0, T3 reject/warn/info 0.

The gates print their own populations: agent-facing properties 295 read / 0 behind a `$ref` (was 14); tools sharing an argument shape 3 groups / 3 declared (was 4 undeclared); value space stated for 106 of 106 refused arguments; optional 123 of 123 differential and required 22 differential + 150 probed, both halves 0 unexercised.

The required accounting did NOT move when two exceptions became conclusions, which was checked rather than assumed: `add_parameter_gate.op` and `import_sections.sections` already had hand-written differential cases, so the exception had only withheld them from the probe. The unchanged numbers are the correct answer.
Injection — the clock back into the derived confirmation-event id: exactly `one_verification_act_records_once_whatever_the_clock_says`.
Injection — the forward-schema refusal disabled: exactly `a_store_from_a_newer_schema_is_refused_naming_both_versions`.
Injection — `remove_section_binding` saved without its reason: exactly `remove_section_binding_probed`, and NOT the reason gate, which proves coverage rather than the row.
Every injection ran at full workspace scope and was reverted from a copy; the touched files are byte-identical to their pre-injection state (`cmp`).
carry_forward_bullets: The `$ref` gate reads the property and its `items` and stops there, so a reference nested deeper — inside an inlined element's own field — is outside it. That is a reach stated rather than measured: the round did not count how many such references exist, and the count is what would say whether the remaining depth matters.

`SHARED_ARGS` states that the tools in a group mean the same by every argument, and nothing executes that sentence. The grouping is derived and a group appearing or dissolving reddens, but the CLAIM is a reader's judgement — the divergence it exists to catch was found by reading a doc comment, not by a run.

The probe's sentinel is a value naming nothing, which no length cap refuses, so an argument constrained only by LENGTH never reaches a `validated` verdict and the value-space gate cannot see it. `set_section_intent.intent` is exactly that argument, and its cap is now stated in prose on its own struct rather than by anything the gate reads.

THE AXIS IS DORMANT, and what makes that honest is that resumption needs no decision: a new argument in neither accounting list, a new silent refusal, a new `$ref`, a new undeclared shared shape and a new unprobed `reason` each redden on the round that introduces them. What no instrument covers is a handler that IGNORES a bad value rather than refusing it — the population of every gate here is refusals or differentials, and silence has neither.

Round 1031.decision_summary: R1031 (BUILD) — a declared prerequisite is a promise the road must keep. `QuestNode::prerequisites` has carried a `requires` edge to every consumer since Round 568 under the words "the canon order proves the timing". NOTHING PROVED IT. STAR THE MEASUREMENT CAME FIRST AND IT USED THE ONLY BLIND-AUTHORED BRANCHING CORPUS THIS REPO CAN LOAD. One field of the dnd-quest store was moved — `f-153`'s `requires` object from `q-key` to `q-delver` — which turns "the vault needs the warden's key" into "the vault needs the lantern-boy's errand", and that errand closes at `sc-30p` / `sc-31s`, AFTER the vault does on the two roads that close it at all, and never on `claim`. Under that edit `import-facts` accepted the store, `validate-continuity` reported violations 0, `validate-workspace` passed, and `report-quest-graph` and `report-playable-world` both rendered it and handed a runtime a gate no road can open. Five stations, all exit 0. That is the third destination's class exactly: consistent store, unplayable game — the shape R634/R635/R636 each hit one instance of, every one of them found because a person tripped over it rather than because anything asked. STAR THE FIRST CORRUPTION WAS REJECTED, AND THE REJECTION IS PART OF THE FINDING. Moving the typed object alone failed at `import-facts`: the R446 entities-list invariant requires the object to ride the retrieval key. So the defect this gate is for must carry BOTH halves, which is what makes it an authorable defect rather than a corrupt file — the write path already refuses the file, and refuses nothing about the promise. STAR THE RULE IS STRICT PRECEDENCE ON THE SAME ROAD, AND ITS THREE NON-FINDINGS ARE MEASUREMENTS. On a world-line that discharges the subject quest, the object quest must be discharged there too, at a coordinate strictly before it. `inapplicable` = this road never discharges the subject, so its gate is never opened and there is nothing to prove; `unverifiable` = the world's order cannot compare the two coordinates, so the question cannot be ASKED (B-1: the author's order is silent, not contradictory); and an UNDECIDABLE membership is not a discharge — "we cannot tell whether the player was ever there" is not evidence that they were. All three are emitted as rows rather than skipped, because the satisfied verdicts are drawn from that same denominator. STAR NO SECOND DEFINITION OF WHAT A QUEST IS. The walk shares the R676 `quest_ids` kernel and therefore its shape and role-conflict guards; membership is the one `visibility` decision every other per-world read uses, and precedence is the `CanonOrder::le` the R488/R522 reachability gates ride. The two violation arms are DRAWN FROM the judgement list rather than computed beside it, so the finding and its census cannot come from two different traversals. STAR THE AUTHORED STORE JUDGES 4 AND SATISFIES 3, SO THE GATE IS NOT VACUOUS ON REAL CONTENT.

Round 1032.decision_summary: R1032 (DEBT) — the carry Round 1031 shipped was answerable by the tree it shipped into. R1031 left this bullet: "a `requires` edge could equally promise that the prerequisite is discharged before the dependent is PICKED UP — a second, stricter reading the store has the data for, and that nothing here asks. Not attempted: undone work, not a limit." It named its own status correctly and then left it anyway. STAR THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY IN THE ONE BLIND-AUTHORED CORPUS THIS REPO CAN LOAD, AND IT REFUTES THE STRICTER READING. The reeve hands the party the main charge at `sc-02` (`f-013`, the `pursues` claim on `q-main`) and the warden's key is not lifted until `sc-17` (`f-161`) — fifteen scenes of play between the pickup and the prerequisite's discharge. A pickup-order rule would reject the store a blind author wrote, on the road that keeps every other promise. STAR AND THAT IS NOT A DEFECT IN THE STORE, IT IS THE SHAPE OF A QUEST: you accept an obligation long before you can discharge it, and a gate forbidding that would forbid nearly every quest ever written. So the `requires` promise is about COMPLETION order, which is what R1031 built — but R1031 could not say WHY it had chosen that reading, only that it had. Now it can, and the reason is evidence rather than taste. STAR THE PIN DERIVES BOTH COORDINATES FROM THE FIXTURE RATHER THAN ASSERTING THEM. The pickup comes from whichever fact carries the `pursues` claim on `q-main`, the discharge from whichever carries `completed_by` on `q-key`, and the precedence from the `claim` road as `report-playable-world` actually composes it — so an authored change that moves either coordinate moves the test, and a later round that builds the stricter rule turns this red and inherits the corpus it has to answer for. STAR THE PROCESS FINDING IS THE ONE THE OWNER HAS ASKED ABOUT TWICE: writing the gap down made it read like rigor. The R1005 carry test says a bullet concrete enough to describe the work is undone work — this one described the work, named the data, and was filed anyway. The rule that catches it is cheaper than the rule that describes it: before writing a carry, check whether the tree already answers it.

Round 1033.decision_summary: R1033 (MEASURE) — the arc's remaining surface, produced by a walk instead of by my memory. STAR THE OWNER ASKED WHETHER THE ROUNDS ARE MEANINGFUL AND WHAT IS LEFT, AND THE FIRST HONEST ANSWER WAS THAT THE LEDGER ALREADY KNEW. Counting `carry_forward_bullets` per round: R700-799 filed 4.4 per round, R800-899 4.0, R900-999 3.9, R1000-1032 2.6 — and NOT ONE ROUND IN 333 FILED ZERO. "Pay off every debt" is not a reachable state, and the tracked debt list in memory is a hand-curated snapshot (about 20) rather than the population (85 in the last 33 rounds alone). The rate is falling, but it is not a curve that reaches zero: a round that builds something new discovers something new. STAR AND ROUND 1031 CHOSE ITS CLASS BY READING A DOC COMMENT, which is the "the only one left is X" habit this repository has caught itself in four rounds running, committed one round after recording it. So this round does not build class two. It makes the class list a DERIVED thing. STAR THE POPULATION COMES FROM THE STORE, NOT FROM A LIST. The quest layer of the one blind-authored branching corpus (`structural_fact_ids`, the shipping definition of quest plumbing, plus the facts that pay it off), and per fact the legs it ACTUALLY carries — a retargeted claim object, a retargeted predicate, a dropped payoff edge, a setup that stops expecting, a dropped backreference. Each is applied to the MANIFEST and pushed through the real write path, so what is judged is what an author could commit. 41 corruptions. STAR THE ANSWER IS 6 CAUGHT, 33 SILENT, 2 INERT, 0 REFUSED. Six the continuity gate reports. THIRTY-THREE pass every gate and CHANGE THE WORLD BOTH RUNTIME PROJECTIONS RENDER — nothing but the author's attention stands there. Two change NOTHING either projection carries. And REFUSED is zero because every corruption carries its own entities list, which is precisely the invariant R1031 discovered the write path demands: an author who keeps the store's own rules can commit all 41. STAR THE 33 IS NOT A BACKLOG OF 33 GATES AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT. A gate can adjudicate only where a DECLARED contract exists to compare against — which is what `requires` was, and why R1031 was buildable. Retargeting `pursues` from one quest to another is a different story, not a broken one; no gate can know the author did not mean it. So the measurement's real content is that the quest layer's remaining surface is mostly AUTHOR CONTENT rather than missing enforcement: the R476 ceiling (prose aesthetics and the unbounded commonsense of relevance) showing up here, one layer down. That is a stopping signal, and it arrived from a walk rather than from anyone's judgement. STAR THE TWO INERT ROWS ARE A FINDING, NAMED NOT COUNTED: `f-180/pays_off` and `f-411/pays_off` are payoff edges neither `report-playable-world` nor `report-quest-graph` carries. Scoped honestly — `report-payoff-coverage` is a third read and is not in this walk.

Round 1036.decision_summary: R1036 (MEASURE) — the refuter was asking one corpus, and this repository ships forty-three. STAR ROUND 1035 FILED THE WRONG CARRY AND THE TREE DISPROVED IT IN ONE COMMAND. That round let `dangling is never empty` survive refutation and wrote that "a second authored corpus is what would move it, and there is one authored branching corpus". Branching was the wrong predicate: refutation does not need a fork, it needs an AUTHOR. `git ls-files` finds 43 directories holding a fact manifest beside a `sections.json` and an `order.json` — every blind-authoring experiment this repository has run is an authored store. The population under measurement was 1. STAR ASKED OF ALL OF THEM, `dangling is never empty` IS REFUTED: some author finished paying their setups, and a rule built on the surviving evidence would have rejected them. The evidence behind the one candidate that still stands, `payoffs_to_unmarked is always empty`, went from 4 authored worlds to 41, every one of them at zero. Same walk, same corruptions, same discriminator — only the refuter's population changed, and a verdict changed with it. STAR WIDENING THE POPULATION FIRST LOST EVIDENCE, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING. The dnd-quest record's OWN `facts.json` is the pre-migration manifest that stopped loading — the rot Round 857 found — so a sweep over tracked corpora excludes the only quest-bearing store, and three refutations turned into candidates because the population grew. The corpus under corruption is itself an authored store and has to be in the refuter; a wider net that drops the one sample carrying the reads in question is worse than the narrow one, and it fails in the direction that INVENTS gate candidates. STAR SIXTEEN OF THE 43 NO LONGER LOAD, and that is now counted rather than mentioned. A corpus that stops loading silently shrinks the evidence every rule is judged against. STAR AN INJECTION THAT DID NOT FIRE FOUND A DEFECT IN THIS WALK. Making the workspace declare a rules file every corpus may not have should have cost 31 corpora their rules-reading verbs, and nothing turned red: the per-corpus read counts were PRINTED and never asserted, so a corpus quietly losing reads was invisible. The total is now pinned at 660, and the same injection moves it to 572. A count the program does not read is not a measurement, and this round shipped one for a few minutes.

Round 1039.decision_summary: R1039 (MEASURE) — the population of "two shipped reads answer the same question", derived rather than picked. Round 1037 found a contradiction that had shipped since R568 by comparing `report-quest-graph` against `validate-continuity`, and it picked that pair BY HAND, and it hit on the first try. A hand-picked second pair is the mistake this arc has made four times running, so the population is derived here and the backlog comes out of a walk. STAR THE FIRST DERIVATION WAS VACUOUS AND THE WALK SAYS SO EVERY RUN. Keyed on "a read mentions this id", 220 of the corpus's 220 registered subjects are answered about by more than one read, because `report-playable-world`, `report-playthrough-manuscript` and `report-edge-candidates` each render the whole store. A backlog built on co-mention is noise. That is the R1034 lesson one layer up — a rendering read must not be allowed to masquerade as one with an opinion — and it is now an assertion rather than a sentence, so a shipped surface that stops rendering everything makes the vacuity argument itself go red. STAR A READ ANSWERS ABOUT A SUBJECT WHEN ITS RECORD CARRIES A VERDICT, AND THE VERDICT FIELDS ARE DERIVED FROM THE DATA. A verdict field is one whose values across that read's whole output form a small closed set of short lowercase tokens, none of them a registered id. Rust cannot enumerate the types implementing the store's `closed_vocabulary!` (R1027), and a hand table of verdict field NAMES is the keyed-by-name gate population this repository has spent rounds removing — so the shape is recognised in the data and every field found is printed, which is how a reader checks the walk for inventing them. It finds `state` on the quest graph and `verdict` on the continuity walk: the exact two fields whose disagreement R1037 found. The population drops from 220-of-220 to 81-of-206, and the read-pair table from 55 pairs to 16. STAR THE DERIVATION REPRODUCES THE KNOWN POSITIVE, AND THAT IS ASSERTED. `report-quest-graph <-> validate-continuity` is in the backlog with 4 subjects in common, and `q-main` — the quest R1037's defect was about — is one of them. A derivation that cannot re-find what a hand comparison already proved is a list, not a backlog. STAR SEVEN INJECTIONS LANDED ON TWO ASSERTIONS BETWEEN THEM, SO THE ASSERTIONS WERE RESTRUCTURED. Every check now runs and the failures come out as a named list, the R1026 rule applied to this test's own claims rather than to its findings; re-run against that form, the same seven injections cover all six checks, and one of them breaks the backlog alone.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/common/mod.rs`: the `--help`-derived read panel moves here from the census walk — two walks need it now, and a second copy is how they would come to disagree about which surface a consumer has.

`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/read_agreement_population.rs`: subjects from the store, records as the minimal enclosing object, verdict fields derived from each read's own values, the subject population and the read-pair backlog printed and pinned, with the R1037 pair as the oracle.
The walk's own assertions are a checklist that all run and report as one named list, so an injection shows every claim it breaks rather than the first.

The first seven runs, against the stop-at-first form, landed on exactly two assertions; that is what the restructure is for and it is why the injections were re-run rather than counted twice.

Round 1041.decision_summary: R1041 (BUILD) — the fifth derivation of "do two reads agree" was refuted BY INJECTION, and writing the first declared agreement found a trap the pair was already shipping. Round 1040 left the honest carry: the derived population says WHO answers about a subject, never WHETHER the answers agree. This round tried to close that mechanically, could not, and then closed one row of the backlog the only way that works. STAR TWO DERIVATIONS MEASURED AND REFUTED BY THEIR OWN NUMBERS. RESPONSIVENESS ASYMMETRY, "one read moves under an authorable edit the other ignores", is vacuous: 489 of 581 shared (pair, subject) cells are asymmetric, because two reads legitimately judge one subject along axes with nothing to say to each other. RECORD CONTAINMENT, "one read's records about the subject are a subset of the other's, so they cannot contradict", closes 13 of 581 — and the top backlog pair (`report-playable-world <-> report-playthrough-manuscript`, 72 subjects, every cell moving in lockstep) emits 72 DIFFERING records. STAR THE THIRD WAS REFUTED BY INJECTION, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. DISJOINT EVIDENCE, "no single authorable edit moves both records", is selective enough to read like a finding list: 65 of 581. With R1037's shared `quest_discharges` derivation reverted in the tree, the walk's numbers did not move AT ALL — 65 before, 65 after, `q-main` unflagged in both — while `quest_discharge_agreement_smoke` failed naming the three roads it was built to name. The machinery that DERIVED the backlog cannot see the defect that motivated the backlog. A contradiction is a statement about VALUES; sensitivity is not, and five derivations over read output have now failed to recover one (shape and closure in R1039/R1040, these three here). STAR SO AGREEMENT IS DECLARED ONCE AND THEN ENFORCED EVERYWHERE, and the first declaration is a pair the WALK nominated rather than a hand pick: `report-payoff-coverage <-> report-payoff-substantiation`, 12 subjects in the R1040 backlog. Both reads partition the same population — the (road, setup) pairs whose setup is paid there — and neither reads the other's answer, so nothing was stopping them from drifting apart. Asked of every corpus an author shipped that still loads: 43 asked, 27 answered both reads, 37 roads, 109 paid setups, zero disagreements, and the four totals are ASSERTED rather than printed (R1036: a corpus that stops answering shrinks the evidence in silence). STAR AND THE PAIR WAS CARRYING A TRAP NO CORPUS CAN SHOW. Both reads emitted the same row, `{setup, payoffs}`, and meant different things by it: coverage lists every payoff that CREDITS a setup, substantiation lists, for a substantiated one, only those that DISCHARGE its typed state (R485). A consumer joining the two by setup — which is exactly what this pair is in the backlog for — reads a narrowing as a contradiction in a store where nothing is wrong. All 27 authored corpora credit their substantiated setups with precisely the discharging payoffs, so the corpus cannot refute or exhibit it; the TREE exhibits it, in a three-fact store where a second crediting payoff is prose-only. The narrowed row now has its own type, `SubstantiatedSetup`, and its own field, `discharging_payoffs`, so the two reads can no longer say one word for two things.

Round 1042.decision_summary: R1042 (BUILD) — the second declared cross-read agreement, and the evidence base under BOTH of them was missing its richest store. Round 1041 established the method: five derivations over read output have failed to decide whether two reads agree, so a correspondence is DECLARED once and then enforced over every store an author shipped. This round declares the next pair the R1040 walk ranked, `report-authoring-frontier <-> report-payoff-coverage` (13 subjects in common). STAR THE SHARED QUESTION IS "WHAT STILL DANGLES ON THIS ROAD" AND THE TWO READS DISAGREE ABOUT WHICH ROADS EXIST. The frontier reuses `payoff_coverage` for the lists, so those cannot drift without someone re-deriving one — but `dangling_by_world()` keeps only the worlds with work outstanding, so a road where the author has paid every gun is ABSENT from the frontier's map and PRESENT in coverage's with an empty list. A consumer joining the two by world reads a missing key as "no answer" where coverage says "the answer is none". That omission is now the contract rather than a code comment: the frontier carries exactly the roads coverage calls non-empty, in both directions, and 35 of the 41 roads this tree can ask exercise the omission arm. STAR THE POPULATION BOTH WALKS ASK WAS WRONG, AND R1041 SHIPPED IT THAT WAY. A sweep of TRACKED corpora excludes the migrated dnd-quest record, because its own tracked manifest is the pre-migration file that stopped loading (the rot R857 found) — and that record is the richest store this tree holds: four roads, quests, dangling setups on every road. Round 1036 lost three refutations to exactly this omission and added the record back by hand, in one walk. It is now a shared resolver, `authored_stores()`, so a walk cannot forget it by being written later: the payoff contract's evidence went from 27 stores / 37 roads / 109 paid setups to 28 / 41 / 136, and the frontier contract from 2 roads owing work to 6. STAR THE INJECTION THAT MATTERS IS K3. Removing the migrated record from the resolver turns BOTH agreement walks red, which is what says the addition is load-bearing rather than decorative — K1 and K2 each break one arm of the new contract (the omission and the lists), and the population one is the one that would otherwise have rotted quietly, exactly as it did between R1036 and now.

Round 1043.decision_summary: R1043 (BUILD) — the third declared cross-read agreement, and it found that the two reads key on the same typed step with DIFFERENT SCOPE, so the majority of one read's positive verdicts describe steps the other is structurally unable to see. The pair is the one the R1040 walk ranked next, `report-edge-candidates <-> report-payoff-coverage`; the shared question lives in the substantiation half of that coverage. STAR THE SHARED QUESTION IS ONE TYPED STEP READ TWICE. Both reads look at two typed claims on one (subject, predicate) whose objects differ — a state that moved. `report-payoff-substantiation` calls the later one a DISCHARGE and reports the setup substantiated (R485); `report-edge-candidates` calls the pair a SUCCESSION GAP when no `supersedes_in_frame` chain connects them, which is the store telling the author these two look like one arc. STAR THE SCOPES DIFFER AND THE STRUCTURE CANNOT CLOSE IT. The pair walk behind the gaps skips two facts in different FRAMES, and that is not an oversight: succession is `supersedes_in_frame`, a within-perspective relation by construction. The discharge rule has no frame test at all, because payoff edges cross frames freely (R442). So a ground-truth fact discharges a setup written in a character's frame and NO succession edge could ever record that step. On the one blind-authored corpus 3 of its 5 discharging pairs are cross-frame — the MAJORITY of that store's substantiated verdicts. STAR SO THE RELATION IS DECLARED WITH ITS EXCEPTION AND BOTH ARMS ARE COUNTED. A same-frame discharge must appear to the other read, as a proposed gap or as an already-chained succession; a cross-frame one is NAMED as the class the succession model cannot express rather than quietly skipped, and the edge report proposing one anyway is a disagreement in the other direction. Over every store this tree can ask: 26 discharging steps, 23 same-frame of which 21 are already chained by an author who wired the succession, 3 cross-frame, 0 disagreements. The walk reads only what the two shipped reads emit — no store access — so what it checks is what a consumer joining them actually holds. STAR WHAT THIS ROUND DOES NOT DECIDE: whether a cross-frame state change SHOULD substantiate a setup. That is a design question with an owner. That it is invisible to the succession surface is a measurement, and it is now pinned in both directions so that either side growing or losing the frame test turns red.

Round 1044.decision_summary: R1044 (BUILD) - Round 775 bounded how many literals one generated function body may hold and handed the caller an UNBOUNDED reassembly of those bodies, and the gate that exists to catch exactly that shape could not see it, because both of its sample points sat below the step. It surfaced sideways: a field being added on the quest axis moved that axis's step down onto the store size the gate samples. STAR THE DEFECT IN THE EMITTER. `chunked` emitted `{ let mut v = f0(); v.extend(f1()); ... v }` - one statement per chunk, in ONE frame. At `opt-level = 0` rustc gives every statement's temporaries their own slot and reuses none, so that frame grows with the chunk count and therefore with the store. Measured on R1043's tree with the same probe: the quest artifact wanted under a page to 800 quests and 28 KiB at 1,600, and the playable artifact 32 KiB at 800 against 64 KiB at 3,200 - both outside the sampled pair. The reassembly is now chunked by the SAME rule, recursively: a level whose call list exceeds the bound is itself grouped into functions of at most `CHUNK` calls until one root remains, and the functions APPEND into an out-parameter rather than returning a `Vec` each caller then extends with, which is the slot that was being spent. Depth grows logarithmically - two levels already cover 125,000 items at `CHUNK = 50`. Measured after: playable and quest both 32 KiB at 800, 1,600 and 3,200, flat across a fourfold store on both axes. STAR THE DEFECT IN THE GATE IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING. `stack_needed` bisects to a 4,096-byte grain, so a reading AT 4,096 means "at most one page" and is not a measurement of a cost. R786 took the quest arm to a floor reading at both sizes and the note there argued the ratio "still discriminates". It does not: `big < 2 * small` against a denominator meaning "at most one page" is a claim about the instrument's resolution, and that arm passed over an artifact that was already stepping. A floor reading is now a hard failure wherever a ratio is drawn from it, which is the one assertion here that would have failed at R1043. STAR WHAT THE TRADE COSTS. The quest artifact's small-store cost rises from under a page to 32 KiB and its plateau from 28 to 32 KiB. What it buys is that neither axis grows with the store - the playable one measurably did, doubling for four times the store, and nothing in this repository said so.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-engine-build/src/render.rs`: `chunked_over` bounds the REASSEMBLY by the same rule as the bodies, recursively, and chunk functions append into an out-parameter instead of returning a `Vec` per call site.

`crates/mnemosyne-engine-build/tests/projection_stack.rs`: a figure at the resolution floor is a failure wherever a ratio is drawn from it, and the two notes that argued a floor ratio still discriminates are corrected.
verification_bullets: Workspace 1753 tests green, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, `validate-workspace` T3 reject/warn/info = 0.

Before, on R1043's emitter: quest 4,096 bytes at 800 quests and 28,672 at 1,600; playable 32,768 at 800 and 65,536 at 3,200. After: quest and playable both 32,768 at 800, 1,600 and 3,200 - flat over a fourfold store on both axes.
The control still grows (131,072 then 524,288), so the instrument demonstrably still sees growth rather than reporting flatness because it went blind.
1 injection: R1043's emitter restored under the new gate. The floor assertion fires by name - "the quest artifact read 4096 bytes, which is the 4096-byte resolution floor rather than a cost".
carry_forward_bullets: The pre-fix playable growth was measured at 800 against 3,200 and the post-fix figures at 800, 1,600 and 3,200. Past 3,200 nothing is measured, and the gate itself samples 200/800 - a consumer at ten times this store has no reading here.

The quest artifact now costs 32 KiB where it cost under a page. That is a real regression in absolute terms, taken for a bound that holds at any size; the store size at which the trade pays was not measured.

Rebuilding the probe at 1,600 and above is expensive enough that a sweep of them exhausted this machine's memory mid-round. That is a cost judgement about how much measurement to buy, not a limit of the world, and the owner can call it differently.

Round 1045.decision_summary: R1045 (BUILD) - the fourth declared cross-read agreement, on the next pair from the R1040 backlog: `report-payoff-coverage <-> report-quest-graph`, 10 subjects in common. STAR THE SHARED QUESTION. Both reads answer "is this quest's giving obligation outstanding on this road". Coverage answers about the SETUP - a giving fact is `dangling` in a world when nothing paid it off there. The quest graph answers about the QUEST - `open` means an obligation is outstanding here, `done` means it is discharged. STAR THE READ WAS THROWING THE ANSWER AWAY. The state derivation already intersects the quest's givings with that road's dangling list and kept ONE BIT of the result. That is not cosmetic: `giving_facts` is a STORE-WIDE union over every `completed_by` fact of the quest while the state is per-road, so a consumer holding both could not tell WHICH giving is outstanding here without re-deriving the R442 coverage and the R559 giving binding for itself - the recomputation the projection seam exists to prevent. And the bit is dropped entirely under `done`, which since R1037 reads a visible `completed_by` and consults coverage not at all: a quest completable two ways reads `done` on the road it took while the OTHER way's giving still dangles there, and neither read said so. `QuestWorldState::outstanding_givings` now carries the set, through the engine's view and parts and the baked emitter, so a runtime is handed it rather than told to recompute it. STAR SO THE CONTRACT IS AN EQUALITY RATHER THAN AN IMPLICATION. The walk asserts the outstanding list IS the intersection in both directions, that `open` means outstanding-and-not-discharged and `unknown` is its complement, and it counts `done`-while-owing BY NAME rather than judging it - which read is right about a quest completed one of two ways is a design question with an owner, and this round only measures that the class exists. STAR NO AUTHORED CORPUS SHOWS THE CLASS, SO THE TREE DOES. Every quest in the corpora this tree can load is completed exactly one way, so `a_quest_is_done_where_its_other_giving_still_dangles` in `continuity.rs` is the store that exhibits it, and the corpus count is pinned at 0 so that a corpus growing the class says so. STAR AND THE EVIDENCE IS ONE PAIR, ASSERTED RATHER THAN DESCRIBED. Of 44 stores asked, 16 do not load, 18 declare no telling at all for a per-telling read, and 12 of the 13 remaining (store, telling) pairs declare no quest - so ONE pair carries all 16 quest-road cells. Asking EVERY telling a corpus declares rather than a sole one took the answering pairs from 7 to 13.

Round 1046.decision_summary: R1046 (BUILD) - this crate's three gates weighed 2, 3 and 1 of the four emitters it ships, and the population is now a type rather than three hand lists. THE DEFECT. `render`, `render_quest`, `render_map` and `render_passages` all reassemble through the `chunked_over` R1044 rewrote. The stack gate had fixtures for two of them, R781's composition gate rendered three (map absent since the day that emitter landed), and R775's longest-line gate rendered one and inferred the rest - so the round that changed every emitter's frame shape was measured on half of them, and no gate could say which half. R774 had already written the principle down for the quest axis: an emitter is free to stop calling the shared chunker, and assuming across that seam is why the R769 defect survived to R770. The two emitters added after it were never brought under it, because each gate carried its own LIST and a list cannot report the member nobody wrote into it. THE REPAIR IS A TYPE. `Baked` is one macro table declaring the enum, `ALL`, each artifact's entry point and its return type together, so a variant is undeclarable without them and lands in the population by construction; `artifact()` takes it instead of two strings, so a new artifact that wants the shared assembler must be one. `Baked::fixture` is an exhaustive match, so the compiler - not a reviewer - asks a fifth artifact how it grows.
