Round 1047.decision_summary: R1047 (DEBT) - the round that gated against unmeasured figures shipped one of its own, in the same file, and this measures it instead. WHAT R1046 WROTE. It found that R1044's four stated figures do not reproduce and corrected them, then added a sentence of its own about WHY: "the likely origin is the oversized pair that round measured at, reported as though it were this one." Nothing measured that. It is a claim about numbers, in shipped prose, with no run behind it - the exact defect the round was built to gate against, one paragraph below the gate. THE MEASUREMENT. The knob R788 added exists for this: re-running the gate at `MN_FIXTURE_LINES=1200` gives a second pair, 300 and 1,200 items. Playable reads 32768 flat and quest 28672 flat there, the same as at 200/800, and the playable control reads 139264 then 520192. With the default pair that is four measured control points: 96 KiB at 200 items, 136 at 300, 344 at 800, 508 at 1,200. THE GUESS IS REFUTED BY THEM. The control is monotone in the item count, so R1044's 128 KiB sits between the 200- and 300-item readings, at roughly 285 items, and its 512 KiB sits just past the 1,200-item reading, at roughly 1,210. Those are not four times apart, and `fixture_sizes` refuses any pair that is not - so NO pair this gate can be run at yields "128 then 512". The oversized-pair explanation is not merely unmeasured, it is wrong. WHAT IS ACTUALLY RECOVERABLE. Nothing. R1044's own ledger records that it measured a first, wrong emitter shape in an isolated worktree and discarded it, and a reading from a discarded tree is the only explanation left standing. The header now says that rather than guessing, and the second pair is written down as a reproduction command rather than as a figure this gate produces. A SECOND THING THE PAIR BOUGHT. The shipped flat readings now hold at TWO pairs rather than one: playable 32 KiB and quest 28 KiB at 200/800 and again at 300/1,200. R1044's blindness was a step BETWEEN sample points, so a second pair is the only cheap evidence against another one hiding there, and it is evidence this gate had never had.

No new gate: this round removes a sentence and adds measurements behind the one that replaces it. The claim "no pair yields those figures" rests on the control being monotone in the item count, which the four points show and which the emitter's shape - one body, one statement per item - is the reason for.

Round 1048.decision_summary: R1048 (BUILD) — the biggest pair in the Round 1040 backlog agrees exactly, and writing the check found that neither read could say which question it answered. STAR THE PAIR CAME FROM THE TOP OF THE PROGRAM'S LIST, NOT A SHORTLIST. The previous session left three candidates (32, 24, 13 subjects) and the walk's own ranking starts at 72: `report-playable-world <-> report-playthrough-manuscript`. No round recorded a reason for skipping the first five, and a hand shortlist over a derived population is the mistake this arc has now made in both directions. The pair agrees on all 18 road cells of every corpus that answers both, because the playable world does not re-derive the scene walk — it CALLS the manuscript projection and embeds the result verbatim (Round 558). The contract is a pin on ONE derivation staying one. STAR THE FIRST SWEEP READ AS 18 OF 18 CELLS DISAGREEING AND THE WALK WAS WHAT WAS WRONG. The difference was the `disclosure` column on every begins-event, present on one side and absent on the other, because the manuscript read makes `--telling` optional and answers happily bare. The two reads had not disagreed; they had been asked different questions, and NEITHER ANSWER SAID WHICH QUESTION IT WAS. One store, one verb, three different manuscripts (bare, and one per declared telling), with nothing in the JSON and nothing in the prose header to tell them apart. STAR SO THE UNIT OF WORK WAS WRONG AND THE PROGRAM WAS ASKED FOR THE POPULATION. Declaring the 24 remaining pairs one at a time asks "do these two agree" 24 times and never asks "can either say what it was asked", which is a property of ONE read and is derivable for the whole shipped surface at once. The derivation: every advertised verb, the flags on its own usage line, values only from each corpus's own vocabulary, asked twice — with the flag and without. Over 44 authored stores that is 23 (verb, flag) cells and 485 probes, with 72 further cells named as outside the walk (a file the corpus ships no second copy of, or `--json`, which every probe already passes). STAR THE RULE WAS THE REPOSITORY'S OWN BEFORE THIS ROUND MEASURED IT: EIGHT OF THE TWELVE ARGUMENTS THAT MOVE AN ANSWER'S SUBSTANCE ALREADY TRACKED. `report-frame-view` names all four of its, `report-entity` names its entity, the frontier and disclosure-coverage name their tellings. FOUR DID NOT, and all four were on the three narrative projections a runtime consumes: `report-playthrough-manuscript` `--telling` and `--world`, `report-playable-world --world`, `report-quest-graph --world`. STAR THE REPAIR CARRIES THE VALUE RATHER THAN RE-READING THE PARAMETER. The manuscript projection records `telling` and `world`; the playable world takes its filter FROM the manuscript it embeds; the quest graph takes both FROM the playable world it reuses. ONE write path, and the injections prove the chain: erasing the manuscript's record breaks three cells, the playable world's breaks two, the quest graph's breaks one. `None` is serialized rather than skipped, because a consumer reading `null` learns "no telling was in play, and the disclosure column is missing for that reason", which is a different fact from a key that is not there. STAR THE GATE'S FIRST CUT WAS CIRCULAR AND THIS ROUND SHIPPED THE DEFECT BEFORE CATCHING IT. Recording an argument makes two answers differ BY THAT RECORD, so `--reading-walk` flipped from inert to named the moment the field landed — a field that names itself satisfies "the answer changed and the answer names it". Substance is now judged with the tracking fields stripped, and a scalar like the manuscript's `facts` count stays in, so an argument that moved only it would still be measured. STAR AND THE ENGINE GOT A QUESTION IT HAD NEVER BEEN ASKED. `MapProjection` destructures the playable-world report exhaustively, so the new field made the compiler ask what a projection means by it — and the answer is that a `--world`-filtered read may not build one: it carries ONE road, and a projection keyed by world cannot be told apart from a store that has one. STAR `--reading-walk` IS INERT ON EVERY AUTHORED CORPUS AND THE TREE CARRIES THE CLASS INSTEAD: all 823 scenes of the 28 askable corpora begin at least one fact, so the reading prune removes nothing anywhere, and the gate is quiet for want of a corpus rather than for want of a hole.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-validate/src/continuity.rs`: the manuscript projection records the telling and the `--world` filter it was given; the playable world and the quest graph CARRY them from the projection they embed rather than re-reading the parameters, so one write path answers "which question was asked".

`crates/mnemosyne-ops/src/lib.rs`: the reading prune records that it ran, beside the prune; a tree fixture shows the class no authored corpus has (a scene that introduces no content) and pins that the two answers differ and each says which walk produced it.
`crates/mnemosyne-cli/src/main.rs`: one shared header clause for the three narrative projections — telling, road filter, and reading walk, with "no filter" spelled out rather than omitted.
`crates/mnemosyne-engine/src/projection.rs`: a projection may not be built from a `--world`-filtered read, with a test that reaches the arm the exhaustive destructuring forced.

`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/read_argument_provenance.rs`: NEW — the derived gate over the whole shipped read surface; substance is judged with the argument's own record stripped, so the rule cannot be satisfied by a field that names itself.
`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/manuscript_projection_agreement.rs`: NEW — the fifth declared cross-read agreement, on the backlog's largest pair.

8 revert injections, each over the WHOLE workspace with --no-fail-fast, all 8 fired. The carry chain is what they measure: erasing the manuscript's `world` record breaks three cells, the playable world's breaks two, the quest graph's breaks one.
N1 (the manuscript's telling) is the only one that breaks the pair contract as well, because that contract asks both reads unfiltered; the filtered half is the gate's.
N5 (the prose clause) breaks the prose test ALONE — every other contract in this series reads `--json`, which is what R1045 found leaves the human wire undefended.

The provenance gate cannot see a handler that IGNORES a bad value: its whole population is "the answer moved" versus "it did not", and silence is neither. That limit is the R1030 one, unchanged.

`report-quest-graph --telling` reads INERT in substance on the three corpora that declare two tellings: the quest layer's data does not move with the telling there. Whether that is the telling being irrelevant to quests or those corpora not exercising it is not measured.

Round 1050.decision_summary: R1050 (BUILD) — the one shipped read that is ABOUT the road axis was judged by nothing, and the contract that judges it needs two other reads to say what a road IS. STAR THE DEBT. Round 1049 derived from the shipped surface which reads take a road and split them: a SELECTOR picks part of an answer holding one entry per road, a COORDINATE moves the point the WHOLE answer is evaluated at. It judged the selectors and could only NAME the one coordinate, because holding `report-frame-view --branch` to "the roads you keep say what the unfiltered read said" is refuted by the shipped design on the first run: that read legitimately answers MORE at a fork than at the default road. Its carry said whether the coordinate answers CORRECTLY at the road it is given "is a different contract, and no test in this tree makes it". STAR AND THE OTHER CONTRACT DID NOT REACH IT EITHER. `report-frame-view` is not in the Round 1040 read-agreement backlog: the panel deriving that backlog asks each verb bare and then with the corpus's telling, so a read needing a frame AND a canon coordinate is one of the four it reports UNASKABLE. The read most obviously about roads was in no population at all. STAR WHAT A COORDINATE CAN HONESTLY BE HELD TO — six claims, none of which recomputes the projection. LINEAGE: every fact an answer at road r names sits on a branch the fork tree puts on r's lineage. BOUND: and it starts at a scene that road actually PLAYS. INHERITANCE: a forked road really does name its ancestor's facts, counted rather than asserted. MOVES: asked at the same canon coordinate, a road answers something other than the default road does. DEPENDENCE: delete a fact an author wrote and every road that cannot see its branch answers BYTE-IDENTICALLY, while every probe that named it moves. FAIL-LOUD: a road no registry holds is refused. STAR THE ORACLE IS TWO OTHER SHIPPED READS, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT CIRCULAR. Re-deriving `world_membership` in the test would be the R1041 shape, two spellings of one derivation agreeing because they are the same idea twice. Instead `report-fork-tree` states the TOPOLOGY (fork parents, converge parents, and the confluences a road flows into) and `report-playthrough-manuscript` states the CUT (a fork inherits its parent only to the fork point, so the parent's later scenes are exactly the ones the fork's manuscript does not play). Between them they cover both halves of membership and neither is asked to compute anything it does not already publish. The corpora put 136 (road, fact) pairs on the far side of that cut and 0 leaked, over 3988 named facts. STAR MOVES IS THE CLAIM WITHOUT WHICH THE REST IS SATISFIABLE BY A READ THAT IGNORES ITS FLAG, and the grid taught it its own shape. The default road is on EVERY road's lineage, so a coordinate read quietly answering the default view everywhere would satisfy LINEAGE, BOUND and DEPENDENCE with every count still adding up. But a road must move at SOME point, not at every one: asked at the coordinate where it DIVERGES it has exactly the prefix it shares with its parent, and answering identically there is the contract working. 13 of 13 roads move; all 13 are still at their own divergence. STAR EACH ROAD IS ASKED AT TWO KINDS OF POINT AND THE SECOND KIND IS WHY. A grid of road-ends alone judges a read that is right about a road's whole history and wrong about the shared prefix; the divergence coordinates come from the fork tree, and only the ones a road plays are used. 64 (corpus, road, coordinate) probes, 0 divergences off some road's line. STAR THE SELECTOR/COORDINATE DISCRIMINATOR IS NOW ONE DEFINITION, in the shared module with the road-filter derivation, and the selector walk's numbers are byte-unchanged (5 cells, 112 probes, 8 shape rows, 76 fail-loud) — the refactor is shown to have moved nothing. STAR AND THE R438 PROMISE'S OTHER HALF NOW HAS A UNIT PIN. "A fork's own revisions never leak back into the ancestor's view" was asserted only for STANDALONE branches and only over `holding`, so a registered fork's fact appearing in its ancestor's `unknown` list was never checked — and `unknown` is where it would appear, because a start the ancestor's order cannot compare is undecidable rather than absent. The new test uses a fork coordinate off the ancestor's chain, which is the shape every branching corpus here has.

Each road is asked at its end and at every divergence it plays through.

The panel deriving that backlog still cannot ask FOUR advertised reads, because it only tries a verb bare and then with the corpus's telling. This round asked one of them by supplying every required argument from the corpus's own vocabulary, so the other three are unjudged for a reason now known to be removable rather than structural.

Round 1052.decision_summary: R1052 (BUILD) — the sixth declared cross-read agreement, and the first pair where neither read embeds the other: `report-authoring-frontier <-> report-playable-world`, 57 subjects in common, the largest overlap no contract judged. ★THE TWO READS DECOMPOSE ONE STORE ALONG THE SAME TWO AXES AND HAND BACK DIFFERENT HALVES. The frontier is keyed by SCENE (a coverage row per registered section, plus the placement sets naming the ones no order reaches) and by ROAD only in aggregate (a length and an owned-fact count). The playable world is keyed by ROAD (a manuscript per world-line, its scenes in walk order) and names the sections each road does not travel. So no field here equals a field there, and every one of the seven laws is a JOIN — which is what makes this pair unlike the four before it, where one read called the other's projection and the contract pinned that reuse. ★SEVEN LAWS: ROADS (the frontier knows every road the dump walks, and the ones it knows that the dump does not are EXACTLY the confluences the playable world's own fork tree names — the exception proved by the other read rather than by the test consulting the store); LENGTH (the frontier's `road_scenes` is that road's walk); PARTITION (travelled + off-road partition the frontier's scene census, disjointly and exhaustively); UNPLACED (a section no order positions is off EVERY road); EMPTY (a zero-fact scene begins nothing anywhere); CENSUS (per-scene `≤` plus an equal total IS per-scene equality, with the residual — facts undecidable on every road — counted, not absorbed); DISCLOSURE (a never-planned fact carries NO locator, the R643 arm; a seat the frontier calls early is a locator earlier in the walk than the scene its fact begins at, the R949 arm — both judged from the other side for the first time). ★THE AUTHORED CORPORA LEAVE FOUR OF THOSE ARMS AT ZERO, AND THAT IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN AVERAGED AWAY. 13 (store, telling) pairs answer both reads over 18 roads, and none of them holds a section outside its order, a scene with nothing in it, a seat before its truth, or a confluence that also declares a telling — the one corpus with a merge declares none, so this pair's per-telling half cannot ask it. Four laws over an empty arm are four claims with no evidence, so the TREE constructs the store the authors did not, through the same import recipe (`constructed_corpus`), and the same `judge` runs over both populations with their evidence asserted separately. ★AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THE PROSE WAS WRONG ABOUT WHAT THE CONFLUENCE ASK BUYS — the shape line refuted it in one run. It said the census could not close without asking `--world merge`; in fact both forks walk THROUGH the merge into its continuation (7 scenes each over a 4-scene trunk), so the fact the confluence owns is named on the forks anyway. What the ask does buy is the confluence's own road: its LENGTH and PARTITION are judged nowhere else, and its manuscript carries ONE locator over eight scenes because a fragment leaves the pre-merge trunk undecidable. The number the prose now states is the number the test prints.

So no field here equals a field there, and every one of the seven laws is a JOIN — which is what makes this pair unlike the four before it, where one read called the other's projection and the contract pinned that reuse. ★SEVEN LAWS: ROADS (the frontier knows every road the dump walks, and the ones it knows that the dump does not are EXACTLY the confluences the playable world's own fork tree names — the exception proved by the other read rather than by the test consulting the store); LENGTH (the frontier's `road_scenes` is that road's walk); PARTITION (travelled + off-road partition the frontier's scene census, disjointly and exhaustively); UNPLACED (a section no order positions is off EVERY road); EMPTY (a zero-fact scene begins nothing anywhere); CENSUS (per-scene `≤` plus an equal total IS per-scene equality, with the residual — facts undecidable on every road — counted, not absorbed); DISCLOSURE (a never-planned fact carries NO locator, the R643 arm; a seat the frontier calls early is a locator earlier in the walk than the scene its fact begins at, the R949 arm — both judged from the other side for the first time). ★THE AUTHORED CORPORA LEAVE FOUR OF THOSE ARMS AT ZERO, AND THAT IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN AVERAGED AWAY. 13 (store, telling) pairs answer both reads over 18 roads, and none of them holds a section outside its order, a scene with nothing in it, a seat before its truth, or a confluence that also declares a telling — the one corpus with a merge declares none, so this pair's per-telling half cannot ask it. Round 1053.decision_summary:
`report-authoring-frontier`'s scene census shipped a COUNT, and a count cannot
say WHICH fact it counted. Round 1052 declared this pair's CENSUS law — every
fact the frontier holds at a scene is named there by the playable world — and
could only ever check it as a per-scene `<=` plus an equal total, which is an
equality of NUMBERS. This round measured what that cost rather than arguing it:
two facts trading the coordinates they are anchored at is an edit the playable
world walks a reader straight through (`fx-open` c-01 -> c-02 and `fx-quiet`
c-02 -> c-01 on main), and the frontier's whole report came back BYTE-IDENTICAL.
Not the census alone — with `scene_coverage` set aside the two reports were
equal, so there was no field of that read where the difference could ever have
appeared, and no contract anyone could have written would have closed it. The
hole was in the WIRE, not in the contract. The same class had just been met on
`not_holding` (R1050), which makes it a class rather than an accident.

So `SceneCoverage` names what it counts: `{scene, facts: [id], structural: [id]}`
replaces `{scene, fact_count, structural}`. The count is `facts.len()` and is
kept nowhere — a count printed beside the list it summarizes is a second answer
free to drift from it, and R1049 already watched one datum with two write paths
leave the runtime-read side undefended. The CENSUS law becomes a per-scene SET
equality, with the residual — the facts no road could decide — named rather than
absorbed into a total, so a fact the frontier holds at a scene nobody names it at
is now told apart from a fact nobody could place at all.

The same measurement was made of `structural_facts`, which Round 1052 left
touching no law at all: emptying the per-scene structural subset reddened NOTHING
across 1765 tests. So this round also declares LAW STRUCTURAL — a fact the
playable world hands a runtime with a quest typed leg is one the frontier's
census has already subtracted as plumbing, at the scene it begins. The converse
is NOT a law and is counted instead: a quest GIVING setup is structural because a
completion pays it off, not because it carries a typed leg, so the other read has
nothing to show for it and the three of them are a named residual. The three
quest predicate ids became `pub` so the contract READS the vocabulary the
validator enforces; restating them would be the second copy R676 removed the
quest marker to prevent.

WHAT THIS ROUND DID NOT DO: it declared no new pair, though the backlog's top
undeclared pair was the standing NEXT. That pair's census would read the SAME
`scene_coverage` field, so a law built on it before this change would have
replicated the hole in a second contract. That is checkable rather than a
judgement call, and it is the whole of the ordering argument.

moved the read-agreement walk's ANSWERS-ABOUT population from 98 to 214. A

Round 1054.decision_summary:
Round 1053 changed a shipped wire because no contract could be written over it,
and it pinned that finding in the PAIR file that happened to meet it. What that
pin judges is a property of ONE read: does a census name what it counts. The
same shape had been met once before, on `report-frame-view`'s `not_holding`
(R1050), and written into the ledger as a limit. A shape met twice by hand is a
population nobody has asked the program for — and R1049 already measured what
asking the whole surface is worth, when a question met at one call site turned
out to be a property of a read and, put to every read, named shipping defects.

So the unit is the read surface, and the law is a differential rather than a
rule about field names. Take an edit an author could commit and one read's
answer before and after. If the answer moved and EVERY moving thing in it is a
number, that number is the read's whole account of the change: a consumer learns
that something moved and cannot learn what. A count that rides beside the list
it counts is not in the class and the walk must not flag it — `holding_count`
moves only when `holding` does — and that discrimination comes out of the
measurement, which no rule about names could have made. Both populations are
derived and neither belongs to the new walk: the reads are the shipped `--help`
panel (30 reads, 68 questions), the edits are the store's own legs.

THE FIRST SWEEP CAME BACK EMPTY, AND THE POPULATION WAS WHY. Not one number on
the surface moved alone. The reason was not that the surface is clean: the
derived corruption population says in its own doc that it takes "the legs a fact
ACTUALLY carries", and it carried only the ones that say what a fact CLAIMS —
typed object, predicate, payoff edges, evidence. Every count a shipped read
emits summarizes WHERE a fact becomes true, WHOSE view holds it, or WHICH
world-line authored it, and no edit in that population touched any of the three.
The legs that PLACE a fact and ATTRIBUTE it were added where the population
lives, so all three walks standing on it get them: 41 corruptions became 92,
none refused by the write path. An empty answer from a probe that cannot reach
what it asks about is the failure this arc has now met three times, and it is
the reason the emptiness was investigated instead of reported.

THE SECOND SWEEP NAMED TWO WIRES, and both now name what they count.
`branch_owned_density` shipped `owned_facts`, a count, and moving one fact to
another world-line moved it, moved the `density` derived from it, and moved
nothing else in the whole report — a consumer acting on a density could not open
its own numerator. Rounds 1052 and 1053 had recorded exactly this from the other
side, as a PAIR's limit ("`owned_facts` is what this pair cannot see"); it was
never a limit of a pair. `report-payoff-coverage` shipped `exempt` as the one
class of a four-way classification whose members no field carried, which its own
doc comment said out loud in the words "counted, not listed". Both are lists
now; the counts are `len()` and are kept nowhere.

THE THIRD MEMBER IS ONE THE SWEEP CANNOT REACH, and it is `not_holding` — the
shape that started this. Its two sibling classes ship as lists and it shipped as
a count, and the residual is not recoverable from the rest of the answer either:
it is the frame's population minus the other two, and the population appears
nowhere in the report. That was proved by construction rather than argued, in
the form R1053 used: two facts of two frames trade whose belief they are, so
each frame still holds one standing fact and refuses one lapsed one. Every count
is where it was, and with the residual set aside the two reports are byte-equal
— so on the wire this round replaced, the two stores were indistinguishable
through this read. WHY THE SWEEP IS BLIND TO IT is worth keeping: the panel asks
each read at the END of the road (the R1050 rule), and there every fact of a
frame has already become true, so no single-leg edit moves the residual alone. A
walk over the shipped surface is bounded by the questions the corpus can ask it.

WHAT WIDENING THE EDIT POPULATION COST, measured on the three walks that stand
on it rather than absorbed. The play-break census moved from 6/26/9 to 17/59/16,
and the arc's floor gained a whole leg: a fact can be moved into ANOTHER MIND'S
BELIEF and four shipped reads carry it there without one of them having an
opinion. `report-frame-view` is the read that partitions by frame and it appears
in none of those rows — asked at one frame it loses the fact and at the other it
gains it, which reproduces the store's own diff exactly, and that census
subtracts the store's footprint on purpose so a rendering read cannot pass for a
detector. The coordinate contract went from 3988 named (probe, fact) pairs to
5520 without moving its off-road count off zero, and thirteen probes moved from
"may move" to "must".

THE ROUND'S OWN WAKE, and it is this walk's definition coming due rather than a
discovery: the read-agreement population's SHARED subjects went from 79 to 210
of 214, and the backlog's head became a pair sharing 135 subjects because BOTH
READS ENUMERATE, not because both judge. Three reads stopped counting sets they
did not name and each of those lists holds most of the store, so under the
minimal-enclosing-object record rule nearly every pair shares nearly everything.
R1053 filed this as a question nobody judges; it is now load-bearing, because
the backlog is what the arc steers by. It is open rather than deferred: the
obvious refinement — a subject's record inside a list of ids is its own
membership, not its neighbours' — is wrong as stated, since the frontier's
census lists facts per SCENE and that rule would throw the scene away.

Round 1054.publishable_decision_summary:
Round 1053 changed a shipped wire because no contract could be written over it,
and it pinned that finding in the PAIR file that happened to meet it. What that
pin judges is a property of ONE read: does a census name what it counts. The
same shape had been met once before, on `report-frame-view`'s `not_holding`
(R1050), and written into the ledger as a limit. A shape met twice by hand is a
population nobody has asked the program for — and R1049 already measured what
asking the whole surface is worth, when a question met at one call site turned
out to be a property of a read and, put to every read, named shipping defects.

So the unit is the read surface, and the law is a differential rather than a
rule about field names. Take an edit an author could commit and one read's
answer before and after. If the answer moved and EVERY moving thing in it is a
number, that number is the read's whole account of the change: a consumer learns
that something moved and cannot learn what. A count that rides beside the list
it counts is not in the class and the walk must not flag it — `holding_count`
moves only when `holding` does — and that discrimination comes out of the
measurement, which no rule about names could have made. Both populations are
derived and neither belongs to the new walk: the reads are the shipped `--help`
panel (30 reads, 68 questions), the edits are the store's own legs.

THE FIRST SWEEP CAME BACK EMPTY, AND THE POPULATION WAS WHY. Not one number on
the surface moved alone. The reason was not that the surface is clean: the
derived corruption population says in its own doc that it takes "the legs a fact
ACTUALLY carries", and it carried only the ones that say what a fact CLAIMS —
typed object, predicate, payoff edges, evidence. Every count a shipped read
emits summarizes WHERE a fact becomes true, WHOSE view holds it, or WHICH
world-line authored it, and no edit in that population touched any of the three.
The legs that PLACE a fact and ATTRIBUTE it were added where the population
lives, so all three walks standing on it get them: 41 corruptions became 92,
none refused by the write path. An empty answer from a probe that cannot reach
what it asks about is the failure this arc has now met three times, and it is
the reason the emptiness was investigated instead of reported.

THE SECOND SWEEP NAMED TWO WIRES, and both now name what they count.
`branch_owned_density` shipped `owned_facts`, a count, and moving one fact to
another world-line moved it, moved the `density` derived from it, and moved
nothing else in the whole report — a consumer acting on a density could not open
its own numerator. Rounds 1052 and 1053 had recorded exactly this from the other
side, as a PAIR's limit ("`owned_facts` is what this pair cannot see"); it was
never a limit of a pair. `report-payoff-coverage` shipped `exempt` as the one
class of a four-way classification whose members no field carried, which its own
doc comment said out loud in the words "counted, not listed". Both are lists
now; the counts are `len()` and are kept nowhere.

THE THIRD MEMBER IS ONE THE SWEEP CANNOT REACH, and it is `not_holding` — the
shape that started this. Its two sibling classes ship as lists and it shipped as
a count, and the residual is not recoverable from the rest of the answer either:
it is the frame's population minus the other two, and the population appears
nowhere in the report. That was proved by construction rather than argued, in
the form R1053 used: two facts of two frames trade whose belief they are, so
each frame still holds one standing fact and refuses one lapsed one. Every count
is where it was, and with the residual set aside the two reports are byte-equal
— so on the wire this round replaced, the two stores were indistinguishable
through this read. WHY THE SWEEP IS BLIND TO IT is worth keeping: the panel asks
each read at the END of the road (the R1050 rule), and there every fact of a
frame has already become true, so no single-leg edit moves the residual alone. A
walk over the shipped surface is bounded by the questions the corpus can ask it.

WHAT WIDENING THE EDIT POPULATION COST, measured on the three walks that stand
on it rather than absorbed. The play-break census moved from 6/26/9 to 17/59/16,
and the arc's floor gained a whole leg: a fact can be moved into ANOTHER MIND'S
BELIEF and four shipped reads carry it there without one of them having an
opinion. `report-frame-view` is the read that partitions by frame and it appears
in none of those rows — asked at one frame it loses the fact and at the other it
gains it, which reproduces the store's own diff exactly, and that census
subtracts the store's footprint on purpose so a rendering read cannot pass for a
detector. The coordinate contract went from 3988 named (probe, fact) pairs to
5520 without moving its off-road count off zero, and thirteen probes moved from
"may move" to "must".

THE ROUND'S OWN WAKE, and it is this walk's definition coming due rather than a
discovery: the read-agreement population's SHARED subjects went from 79 to 210
of 214, and the backlog's head became a pair sharing 135 subjects because BOTH
READS ENUMERATE, not because both judge. Three reads stopped counting sets they
did not name and each of those lists holds most of the store, so under the
minimal-enclosing-object record rule nearly every pair shares nearly everything.
R1053 filed this as a question nobody judges; it is now load-bearing, because
the backlog is what the arc steers by. It is open rather than deferred: the
obvious refinement — a subject's record inside a list of ids is its own
membership, not its neighbours' — is wrong as stated, since the frontier's
census lists facts per SCENE and that rule would throw the scene away.

Round 1055.decision_summary:
Round 1054 left one thing load-bearing and named it as the next round's work:
what a RECORD is for a bare id inside a LIST. That round made three shipped
reads name the sets they had been counting, and in doing so it moved the number
this arc steers by — subjects that more than one read answers about went 79 ->
210 of 214, and the backlog's head became a pair sharing 135 subjects because
BOTH READS ENUMERATE rather than because both judge. That was not a discovery
about the read surface. It was this walk's own definition coming due.

A read's record about a subject is meant to be what that read WROTE ABOUT IT.
The rule that shipped until here was "the minimal enclosing object mentioning
the id", which is right where an id sits in a FIELD — a row naming `q-main`
beside `state: unknown` is a sentence about `q-main`, lists and all — and wrong
where a read LISTS ids, because the row then holds every one of them. A fact
listed in a scene's census carried that whole census row, so its record moved
whenever any of its NEIGHBOURS moved, and three lists holding most of the store
made nearly every pair of reads share nearly every subject.

The obvious repair is refuted by the same census. If a list member's record were
its own membership and nothing else, then since the census lists facts PER SCENE
a record that forgets the scene cannot see a fact change the scene it is
anchored at — which is exactly the loss Round 1053 changed a shipped wire to
close. So the record for a bare id in a list is its MEMBERSHIP, ADDRESSED down
through the ancestors that key it: `scene_coverage[scene=sc-05].facts[]`. A map
KEY gets the same treatment for the same reason: what a read wrote about road
`r-1` is the subtree under `r-1`, not the map that holds every other road beside
it. Three occurrence kinds, three arms, each stopping where the read's statement
about that id stops.

The key of an array row is DERIVED, never named per read: the smallest set of
fields holding a registered id in every row whose values, taken together, are
distinct across the rows. Distinctness is what makes it a key — a field every
row carries but two rows share does not say which row you are at. Smallest
because an address should carry no more than what identifies the row.

WHAT THE ADDRESSING FOUND ON ITS FIRST RUN was that two walks had each derived
"the ids this store registers" by hand and DISAGREED about `main`, a world every
store has whether or not it registers a branch. 25 rows across three shipped
reads are keyed by a road, and a walk blind to `main` addressed them by the
position they happened to sit at — an address that moves when a row is inserted
ahead of them, which is a record moving for a reason that is not about that
subject. There is one resolver now (`common::registered_ids`), and it made 16 of
the 25 addressable. The other 9 are the disclosure coverage's
`inert_reveal_pins`, one row per (fact, world), where NEITHER column is distinct
alone — which is why the key is a composite rather than a field.

WHAT A MEMBERSHIP RECORD CANNOT SEE IS ORDER, and this round asserts that rather
than assuming it. Every listed set is watched, on every one of the 92
corruptions, for a permutation that leaves its membership alone; there are none.
The assertion is not vacuous, and that is measured too: an injection that lists
a scene's facts in FRAME order permutes 14 lists under a frame retarget, and the
assertion names every one of them. The day a shipped read orders what it lists,
position joins the address and this walk says so by going red.

AND THE RULE HAS ITS OWN TEST rather than only its numbers. Both rejected rules
produce a perfectly good number, so a number cannot say whether the rule is the
one written down. The definition is pinned on answers the test writes: a
neighbour moving must NOT move this subject's record (what the old rule got
wrong), a fact changing scene MUST move it (what the naive repair cannot see), a
sibling map key changing must not, a row no single field keys is addressed by the
pair that does. That test is the only thing judging the map-key half — injection
I3, a key claiming the whole map, left every surface number untouched and only
the unit oracle went red.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/read_agreement_population.rs`: the record derivation, rewritten as three arms over the three places a read can write an id — a field's value (the minimal enclosing object, unchanged), a map key (the subtree under it, not the map), a bare list element (its membership at an ADDRESS resolved through the keyed ancestors). Row keys come from `key_fields`, the smallest set of id-holding fields distinct across the rows. Two new assertions the derivation owes: ORDER (no edit permutes a listed set while leaving its membership alone) and ADDRESSING (no row addressed by position, no two places sharing one address). Re-derived constants: 221 subjects, 105 of 216 shared, and a 55-pair backlog in a new order.

`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/read_agreement_population.rs` (new test): `a_record_is_what_the_read_wrote_about_that_id` — the definition asked of hand-written answers rather than of the shipped surface, since both rejected rules produce a good number and only an oracle can say which rule shipped. It carries the two refutations that decided the shape and the permutation detector's own positive and negative case.

`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/common/mod.rs` + `counted_without_naming.rs`: `registered_ids` becomes THE one resolver for "the ids this store registers", with the measurement that bought it. The two walks had each written it by hand and disagreed about `main`; the R1054 copy is deleted rather than kept in step by hand.
verification_bullets: Workspace green — 1769 tests, 0 failed, `--no-fail-fast`; clippy -D warnings clean; fmt clean; `validate-workspace` T1 orphan = 0 and T3 reject = 0.

THE POPULATION AS IT NOW RUNS: 221 registered subjects, 29 reads over 66 questions (2 unaskable, both needing a FILE this corpus does not ship, named rather than counted), 92 authorable corruptions with 0 refused by the write path. 216 subjects have a read that answers about them and 105 have more than one — against 214 and 210 before. The backlog is 55 pairs and its head is now `report-playable-world <-> report-playthrough-manuscript` at 102, where it was `report-authoring-frontier <-> report-payoff-coverage` at 135 on the strength of both reads enumerating. `report-payoff-coverage` alone went from answering about 135 subjects to 21.

THE FIRST NUMBER WENT UP WHILE THE SECOND FELL, and that is the same change rather than a second one: an address distinguishes two places that used to collapse. The manuscript writes the same scene row under every road that plays it, so a fact leaving one road's copy left the others serializing identically and the old record set did not move at all.

ADDRESSING: 0 rows addressed by position and 0 address collisions, from 25 by position before the shared resolver and the composite key. ORDER: 0 permutations over 92 corruptions and every list on the panel.

INJECTIONS 6/6 FIRED, each over the whole workspace, control 0 red before and 0 after. I1 (a list member claims the enclosing object, the pre-R1055 rule) = the oracle and the walk, on ANSWERED and BACKLOG. I2 (membership with no address, the refuted repair) = both, plus 279950 address collisions. I3 (a map key claims the whole map) = THE ORACLE ALONE, no surface number moved — the roads are 5 subjects of 221 and more than one read answers about them either way, so the unit test is the only judge of that arm. I4 (a field keys a row without being distinct) = both, plus 172322 collisions. I5 (production: the census lists a scene's facts in FRAME order) = the ORDER assertion, naming 14 permuted lists over 2 questions, plus the R1054 census. I6 (production: `registered_ids` loses `main`, the disagreement restored) = both walks, 16 rows falling back to position.
carry_forward_bullets: THE BACKLOG IS 55 PAIRS AND 49 ARE UNDECLARED, and it is now ranked by co-JUDGING rather than co-enumerating, which is the whole point of this round. Its head is `report-playable-world <-> report-playthrough-manuscript` at 102 shared subjects, then `report-authoring-frontier` against each of those two at 86. Declare the head next; do not skip down the list by hand, which is where R1048 found a defect.

THE R1054 CENSUS'S CONSERVATISM IS NOW UNBLOCKED, and this is undone work rather than a limit. That walk prints `accompanied` because a lossy number escapes when the same edit moves something named elsewhere in the answer for an unrelated reason, and its own header says the narrowing is "scoping the comparison to the record (R1039)". The record is what this round rebuilt, and it is `pub`-shaped inside one test file rather than shared — so the move is: lift the derivation to `common`, scope that census's comparison to the moving subject's record, and re-measure `accompanied`.

ORDER'S ZERO IS OVER EDITS TO FACTS ONLY, and closing that is describable rather than blocked: `corruptions` is derived from a fact's legs, so nothing in the population rewrites the canon ORDER — which an author can equally do, and which is the one edit that would permute a list of scenes without changing its membership. reads name the sets they had been counting, and in doing so it moved the number
this arc steers by — subjects that more than one read answers about went 79 ->
210 of 214, and the backlog's head became a pair sharing 135 subjects because
BOTH READS ENUMERATE rather than because both judge. That was not a discovery
about the read surface. It was this walk's own definition coming due.

A read's record about a subject is meant to be what that read WROTE ABOUT IT.
The rule that shipped until here was "the minimal enclosing object mentioning
the id", which is right where an id sits in a FIELD — a row naming `q-main`
beside `state: unknown` is a sentence about `q-main`, lists and all — and wrong

listed in a scene's census carried that whole census row, so its record moved
whenever any of its NEIGHBOURS moved, and three lists holding most of the store
made nearly every pair of reads share nearly every subject.

The obvious repair is refuted by the same census. If a list member's record were
its own membership and nothing else, then since the census lists facts PER SCENE
a record that forgets the scene cannot see a fact change the scene it is
anchored at — which is exactly the loss Round 1053 changed a shipped wire to
close. So the record for a bare id in a list is its MEMBERSHIP, ADDRESSED down

The key of an array row is DERIVED, never named per read: the smallest set of
fields holding a registered id in every row whose values, taken together, are
distinct across the rows. Distinctness is what makes it a key — a field every

than assuming it. Every listed set is watched, on every one of the 92
corruptions, for a permutation that leaves its membership alone; there are none.

Round 1056.decision_summary:
Round 1054 filed this law's narrowing as a next step and named the move: a lossy
number escapes the whole-answer test when the same edit moves a name somewhere
else for an unrelated reason, so ask whether anything NAMED moved inside the
number's own RECORD instead. Round 1055 rebuilt what a record is. This round
implemented that narrowing, swept it, and REFUTED it — then found the narrowing
that works, and the first thing it found was a shipping defect.

THE PROPOSED NARROWING FAILS ON ITS FIRST FLAG. Scoped to the record, the census
named the manuscript's per-scene `holding_count` under every `branch` and
`canon_from` retarget, 34 edits across two reads. A scene row does not name the
facts holding at it — but the road's EARLIER rows do, and the count at scene N is
the facts that began at or before N and have not ended. Both halves are named
events of the same answer. So the flag is a false positive, and the reason is the
axis rather than the field: a read's account of a subject is not bounded by one
record when the records form a CHAIN.

That is measured, not argued. The replay is a test now, over 823 scenes of 41
roads of 28 authored stores, and it reproduces every count exactly. Writing it
also executed a claim that shipped with the wire in Round 466 and had never been
run — "a delta reconstruction that disagrees with the count has hit an unplaced
coordinate, never a second semantics" — and found that claim INCOMPLETE: 26 of
823 scenes disagreed with no unplaced coordinate anywhere in flight. The second
source is the wire's own semantics, which the report states and nothing had put
to a program: the two end kinds stop at different times. A fact still holds AT
the scene its `canon_to` names (`holds_at` asks `p <= canon_to`) and has already
stopped where a SUCCESSOR begins (that asks `successor.canon_from <= p`). Replay
them alike and 26 scenes come out short.

THE NARROWING THAT WORKS IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION ABOUT THE SAME DATA. A number is
a read's whole account of something exactly when it is NOT A FUNCTION of what the
answer names — and that is decided by PAIRS, not by scope. Two answers that name
identical things and disagree about a number prove the number carries information
nothing named carries. Comparing each answer to the unedited store asks this of
92 pairs; bucketing the sweep's answers by WHAT THEY NAME asks it of every pair,
which is strictly stronger and reaches exactly the escape Round 1054 described.

ITS FIRST SWEEP FOUND ONE, AND IT IS THE R1054 CLASS AGAIN.
`report-payoff-substantiation setups_total` counts every fact marked `expected`
store-wide, while its body classifies only the setups some payoff CREDITED, three
ways. A setup nobody paid — the author's todo, which the coverage sibling names as
`dangling` — appeared in this read only as a contribution to the total. Two edited
stores name identical things and disagree about it (`f-041/branch` against
`f-041/payoff_expectation`), and neither forms that pair with the baseline, which
is why nine rounds of this law never saw it. The wire now carries the fourth
class, carried verbatim from coverage rather than recomputed, on both the `--json`
and the prose surface.

NO AUTHORED CORPUS EXHIBITS THE SHAPE. All 28 satisfy the property as shipped — an
author who marks a setup goes on to pay it — so a sweep of what authors wrote
reads clean and the finding would look like noise. The pin is therefore a
constructed store with one uncredited setup, built through the same import recipe
an author would use (the R1052 rule), and it states the property directly: every
setup the total counts is named in the same answer. It fails on the shipped wire
and passes on the fixed one.

AND THE RECORD DERIVATION IS ONE DEFINITION NOW. `common::wrote_about` is what
both walks read — the read-agreement population asks whether a subject's record
MOVED, and this census asks it where a number SITS, using the same addressing so
the two cannot come to disagree about where a place in an answer is. Lifting it
moved no measurement: 221 subjects, 105 of 216 shared, the same 55-pair backlog,
0 rows addressed by position, 0 permutations.

The manuscript's `holding_count` now has that stronger statement (a replay test), and the other nine do not. Each is a candidate for the same treatment, and each would be its own measurement — this round did the one the record-scoped flag forced it to do.

THE FINGERPRINT IS TWO 64-BIT HASHES, so two answers naming different things could in principle share a bucket and produce a false finding. The alternative is holding 30 reads x 93 stores of report text, which is the machine-budget rule this repo learned the hard way. Named as the mechanism, not hidden: a finding it produces is reproducible from the two edits it prints.

its own answer names it counts, and left exactly one with neither an account nor
a derivation: `report-quest-graph quests[].locators[].scene_ordinal`. This round
closes it, and the reason it was left over is the reason it needs a different
shape from the other three.

AN ORDINAL IS A POSITION, so no set of names can hold as many and the accounting
law is right to name it. `report-playable-world` carries the road its locators
index into — the same answer holds the manuscript, scene by scene, in order — so
that ordinal is held to its own answer and needs no second read. The quest graph
carries `world_line` and `scene` and no scene sequence anywhere in the report. A
reader holding that answer cannot check the number; neither can a test written
over it.

SO THE ORACLE IS THE READ THAT DOES STATE THE SEQUENCE. That is the Round 1050
rule — the oracle is another shipped read rather than a recomputation of the
projection under test, because a recomputed order would be the same thought
written twice, which is the shape Round 1041 named. The manuscript is what a
reader would actually open to find out where `sc-12` falls on `parley`, so it is
what the number is held to.

THE EVIDENCE IS ONE CORPUS'S QUESTS, AND THE LAW SAYS SO. Thirteen answers come
back across the tracked corpora and four quests with twelve locators come out of
one of them — the migrated dnd-quest record is the only corpus this tree holds
that declares a quest at all, which Round 1053 already filed as a real limit
(Z2/DD3, closed by the migration rather than by a law). The reach is printed and
asserted rather than implied: a walk that reached no locator would otherwise
report the same clean surface as a wire that is correct.

WHAT THIS ROUND DOES NOT GET TO CLAIM is that the new law reaches something the
playable-world one cannot. They read different things — the map key a locator is
filed under, against what the locator says its road is — so an edit that mixes
those up ought to split them, and one was written: the road pinned to `main` at
the shared construction site. Both stayed green. The corpus says why, and it is
worth keeping: all twelve quest locators sit on scenes `main` also walks, at the
same index, because a fork inherits the trunk's prefix and every quest here is
disclosed on the trunk. So the injection is blind on this corpus rather than the
law being redundant, and the difference between them is UNMEASURED. A quest
disclosed on a scene only a fork walks is what would measure it.

AND A LOCATOR ON A ROAD THE MANUSCRIPT DOES NOT WALK IS NOT A FAILURE OF THIS
LAW. It is the oracle declining to answer, which is a different verdict and is
counted and named separately. It is 0 today; the day it is not, this walk says
which locator and which road rather than reporting a disagreement it never
measured.
publishable_changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/counted_without_naming.rs`: the quest graph's locator ordinal held to the road the MANUSCRIPT walks under that name — the one number Round 1057's accounting law named with neither an account nor a derivation. The oracle is a second shipped read because this answer carries no scene sequence to be held to; a locator naming a road the manuscript does not walk is a separate verdict, counted and named rather than read as a disagreement. The census constant's doc now states the real derivation of all four numbers it holds rather than three.
publishable_verification_bullets: Workspace green — 1774 tests, 0 failed, `--no-fail-fast`; clippy -D warnings clean; fmt clean; `validate-workspace` T1 orphan = 0, T3 reject = 0.

A CORRECTION TO ROUND 1057, WHICH THIS LEDGER CANNOT AMEND. That entry says the workspace stood at 1774 tests; the run that green-lit it counted 1773, and 1774 is what it counts with THIS round's test added. The number was written from the shape of the round rather than from the run — the Round 1054 habit of asserting a measurement nobody took, recurring in the round that filed it. Nothing else in that entry depends on it: every other number there was read off a log.

THE LAW, MEASURED: 13 `report-quest-graph` answers over 28 authored stores (16 unloadable), 4 quests, 12 locators; 0 naming a road the manuscript does not walk, 0 indexing somewhere else. The reach is asserted rather than implied — a walk that reached no locator reports the same clean surface as a wire that is right.

THE INJECTION THAT FIRED: the shipped ordinal off by one = 6 red over the whole workspace, this law among them, control 0 red before and after. The playable-world ordinal law falls with it, and that is a fact about the WIRE rather than a redundancy between the tests: both reads' locators come off ONE `MapLocator` construction site.

AND THE ONE THAT CAME BACK 0, WHICH IS A MEASUREMENT ABOUT THE CORPUS. To separate the two laws — one reads the map key its locator is filed under, the other reads what the locator SAYS its road is — the road was pinned to `main` at that same site. Both stayed green, so the corpus was asked why: all 12 quest locators sit on scenes `main` also walks, at the same index, because a fork inherits the trunk's prefix and every quest in this corpus is disclosed on the trunk. The injection is blind here, not the law, and the separation is undone work with a named shape rather than a claim this round is entitled to make.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: THE QUESTS ARE ONE CORPUS'S. Thirteen tracked corpora answer `report-quest-graph` and one of them declares a quest, so the four quests and twelve locators this law judges all come from the migrated dnd-quest record. That is the Z2/DD3 limit already on the ledger — closed by the migration Round 857 filed, not by anything a law can do — and it is printed here rather than implied so a corpus that stops declaring quests reads as a smaller number and not as a clean surface.

NOTHING SEPARATES THIS LAW FROM THE PLAYABLE-WORLD ONE ON THIS CORPUS, and the shape that would is describable. They differ in what they read — the map key a locator is filed under, against what the locator says its road is — so an edit that mixes those up should split them, and pinning the road to `main` at the shared construction site split nothing: all 12 quest locators sit on scenes `main` also walks, at the same index. What would separate them is a quest disclosed on a scene only a FORK walks, which no corpus here declares and the tree can construct through the same import recipe (the R1052 rule).

THE ORACLE-DECLINES ARM IS 0 TODAY. A locator naming a road the manuscript does not walk is a different verdict from a disagreement, and this walk separates them; today nothing is in it. The day something is, the walk names which locator and which road.

THE ACCOUNTING LAW IS STILL A GATE ONLY WHERE THE POPULATION MOVES THE NUMBER — 9 of 74 fields. The other 65 hold accounts the unedited store proposed and no second value ever tested, and the way to test them is to widen `corruptions` past the fact legs to the canon order and the section registry (filed twice already, Rounds 1055 and 1056). That is the next round.

THE BACKLOG IS 55 PAIRS AND 49 ARE UNDECLARED, head `report-playable-world <-> report-playthrough-manuscript` at 102 shared subjects. This round used the manuscript as an ORACLE for one field of one other read, which is not the same thing as declaring that pair and does not reduce it.

PROCESS DEBT, IN THE ROUND THAT CREATED IT: the injection harness is still assembled by hand each round, though this session's ten injections all went through the editor path rather than a script. Occupancy was re-checked before each build; cargo ran ~25 times across the session.

Round 1059.decision_summary:
The injection sweep is how this arc says a contract is not vacuous: break the
thing the contract is about, show it goes red, put the tree back. Every round
runs one, and every round has ASSEMBLED it by hand. Rounds 1054, 1055 and 1056
did the assembly in Python against a standing preference that even spike tooling
is Rust; Round 1057 moved it to the editor path, which fixed the silent-fail half
and left the assembly exactly where it was. This round is the promotion, and what
it is worth is not a preference — it is four measured failures, each one a
property a program can hold and a person cannot.

WHAT THE HAND ASSEMBLY HAS ACTUALLY COST, from this ledger rather than from
principle:

- Round 1050 restored a file with its timestamp preserved. A stale build artifact
  answered the next measurement, and the round wrote up a SHIPPING DEFECT THAT
  WAS NOT THERE — caught only after a minimum reproduction and a unit test.
- Round 1053 ran a sweep whose control was already 2 red, so every count in it
  was a subtraction done in someone's head.
- Round 1057 ran one injection whose doc-test targets failed to build, so that
  run covered 146 targets against a control of 151. Nobody noticed until the
  counts were compared afterwards; a smaller number reads as a cleaner one.
- Round 1057 also waited on `pgrep -f "cargo test --workspace"`, a pattern the
  WAITING SHELL'S OWN COMMAND LINE matches, so the wait could not end and one
  elapsed-time reading came out 8x too large.

SO THE PROGRAM HOLDS THEM. The text to replace must occur EXACTLY ONCE, and a
count of 0 or 2 is refused before the suite is asked anything — 0 is the shape
that reads as "the injection did not fire" and 2 is a change nobody described.
The control must be green, and it is a gate rather than a first data point. The
restore is verified by READING THE BYTES BACK, and writing them fresh is what
gives the file a new timestamp, so the Round 1050 failure is unrepresentable
rather than merely detectable. Each run's TARGET COUNT is compared with the
control's, so a run that built a different set of things says so instead of
reporting a smaller number. And the child is waited on, because this process owns
it — there is nothing to poll for and no pattern to match.

IT ALSO ENFORCES THE RULE ROUND 1054 WROTE DOWN AND ROUND 1058 NEEDED. An
injection may name the tests it is aimed at; if none of them go red, that is a
misaimed injection and the sweep FAILS, rather than reporting a clean surface.
Round 1054 aimed at a projection struct instead of the serialized one and got 0;
Round 1058 aimed at separating two ordinal laws and got 0. Both were caught by a
person remembering to be suspicious.

THE PROOF IS A REAL SWEEP, NOT A DESCRIPTION OF ONE. `example.json` is tracked
and runnable and reverts the wire Round 1056 shipped; running it reproduces
exactly what Round 1057 got by hand from the same injection. A shape nobody can
run is a shape nobody copies correctly.

The crate is its own workspace, like `bench/`, `studio/` and
`tools/experiment-harness`, so the root workspace's build, CI and pre-commit
gates never compile it — and it has its own tests, run against a fake suite whose
verdict depends on whether the injection landed, so the harness can be broken on
purpose without running the real suite once.
changes_bullets: `tools/injection-harness/` (new, its own `[workspace]` so the root gates never compile it — the `bench/` / `studio/` / `experiment-harness` pattern): apply an injection, run the suite, read what went red, put the tree back and prove it went back. The refusals are the point — an edit whose text occurs 0 or 2 times, a control that is already red, a restore whose bytes do not come back, a run that reached a different number of targets than the control, an injection that reaches nothing it named. The suite is a manifest field rather than a hardcoded `cargo test`, which is what lets the crate's own tests break the harness on purpose against a fake suite instead of trusting it after one real run.

`tools/injection-harness/example.json`: a tracked, runnable sweep that reverts the wire Round 1056 shipped and names the three tests it must turn red — the shape the next round copies, kept runnable so copying it is not a guess.
verification_bullets: The crate is green on its own — 10 tests (2 unit over log parsing, 8 integration that break the harness on purpose against a fake suite): an injection that fires and a tree that comes back, an edit matching twice, an edit matching nothing, a red control, an injection that reaches nothing it named, a control asked for alone, and both arms of the occupancy floor. clippy -D warnings and fmt clean inside the crate; the root workspace never compiles it (its own `[workspace]`), so nothing about the 1774-test suite moves.

THE END-TO-END PROOF IS A REAL SWEEP OF THIS REPOSITORY, run through the tracked `example.json`: control 1774 passed / 0 failed / 151 targets, then the Round 1056 wire reverted = 1771 passed / 3 failed, target drift 0, and the three red are exactly the three named in the manifest — `payoff_substantiation_names_every_setup_it_counts`, `the_reads_that_count_what_they_do_not_name`, `the_walk_says_what_stands_between_an_authoring_slip_and_the_runtime`. Round 1057 got those same three from the same injection by hand, so the harness is measured against a known answer rather than trusted on its first run.

AND THE RESTORE IS THE PART THAT HAD TO BE PROVEN: the harness read every touched file back and compared bytes before reporting, and `git status` on this repository is clean afterwards. That is the Round 1050 failure — a restore that preserved a timestamp, a stale artifact answering the next measurement, and a shipping defect written up that was not there — made unrepresentable rather than merely detectable.
carry_forward_bullets: THE HARNESS RUNS A SWEEP; IT DOES NOT CHOOSE ONE. What to break, and whether breaking it is evidence for the claim the round is making, is the round's judgement and stays there. Round 1058 is the example: its injection was mechanically perfect and told nobody anything, because the corpus put every quest locator on a scene the trunk also walks.

THE OCCUPANCY FLOOR IS OPT-IN, so a manifest that omits it gets no check. That is deliberate — a harness that refuses on a machine nobody else is using would be worked around, and a worked-around gate is worse than none — but it means the rule is only enforced where a manifest asks for it, and `example.json` does ask.

IT KNOWS NOTHING ABOUT WHAT A TARGET IS. The drift check compares COUNTS of `test result:` lines, so a run that lost one target and gained another reads as no drift. Comparing the target NAMES needs the `Running <binary>` lines, which are in every log this already keeps.

THE OLDER DEBTS ARE UNTOUCHED AND STILL RANKED: SS2 (widen the authorable edit population past the fact legs to the canon order and the section registry — 65 of 74 accounts have never been put to a second value) is the next round; then SS1 (the backlog head at 102 shared subjects) and TT1 (a quest disclosed on a scene only a fork walks, which is what would separate the two ordinal laws).

authored submissions by map and telling

Round 1060.decision_summary:
Round 1059 shipped the injection harness with a drift check that compared COUNTS
of test targets, and filed the obvious hole in the same breath: a run that loses
one target and gains another has a drift of zero. That is not a hypothetical
shape. The failure the check exists for — Round 1057's injection whose doc-test
targets failed to build, so it covered 146 targets against a control of 151 —
is a LOST target, and a rebuild that also picks up a target the control missed
would hide it perfectly.

So the check is by NAME now. Cargo announces every target it runs, and the name
is in that line: `Running unittests src/lib.rs (target/debug/deps/foo-9a3f…)` is
`foo` and `Doc-tests mnemosyne-ops` is `doc:mnemosyne-ops`. The trailing hash is
dropped on purpose — it moves every time the crate is rebuilt, which is every
injection, so a name that carried it would report drift on every run and the
gate would be turned off within a round.

WHAT THE COUNT IS STILL FOR: a suite whose output names no targets at all. The
harness's own tests use one — a shell script that prints a canned cargo verdict —
and a gate that silently stopped checking for such a suite would be the same
class of hole one layer down. So the count comparison survives as the fallback,
and it says which one it used.

THE TWO ARMS ARE ASSERTED SEPARATELY, because a set comparison that can only
ever report "the same" is indistinguishable from no comparison: one test reads a
real cargo log and checks that a target is named by what cargo announces rather
than by its hash; another builds two runs with the SAME COUNT and different
members, and asserts the difference comes out in both directions.

And the real sweep was run again through the tracked manifest, because a gate
that has never been exercised against the thing it gates is a claim rather than
a check.
changes_bullets: `tools/injection-harness/src/main.rs`: a run records WHICH targets it reached rather than how many, and the drift gate compares the sets — reporting what the control reached and this run did not, and the reverse. A target's name is the binary stem PLUS what cargo was running under it, because the stem alone is not unique. The count comparison stays as the fallback for a suite that names no targets, which the harness's own tests use.

And the control now refuses a run whose names do not identify its targets: if two targets share a name, the set comparison is quietly weaker than the count it replaced, and nothing downstream could tell.
verification_bullets: The crate is green on its own — 14 tests (5 unit over log parsing, 9 integration that break the harness on purpose against a fake suite). clippy -D warnings and fmt clean inside the crate; the root workspace never compiles it, so nothing about the 1774-test suite moves.

THE REAL SWEEP AGAIN, through the tracked manifest: control 1774 passed / 0 failed / 151 targets, the Round 1056 wire reverted = 3 red — the three named — with 0 targets missing and 0 extra, and the tree clean afterwards. The occupancy floor fired for the first time on a real manifest rather than a fake one, printing 20602 MiB and 22362 MiB against its 8000 floor.

AND THE NAMES WERE WRONG BEFORE THEY WERE RIGHT, which is why this round exists twice over. The first run under the by-name check reported 151 targets and 148 names; the gap was not a parse that missed three lines but three crates that run unit tests for a library AND a binary under one stem. Three collapsed pairs are three pairs a drift check cannot see. The name now carries what cargo was running, the control refuses any run whose names do not identify its targets, and the real control comes back 151 targets under 151 names.
carry_forward_bullets: THE NAME IS CARGO'S SHAPE. `Running … (target/debug/deps/foo-hash)` and `Doc-tests crate` are what this reads, so a suite that announces its targets some other way is compared by count and the report says which comparison it used. That is a limit of reading a tool's output rather than asking it, and the fallback keeps it from being a silent one.

AN INJECTION THAT FAILS TO BUILD IS NOW CAUGHT BY THE SAME GATE — it reaches no target, so every name the control reached comes back as missing rather than as a smaller number. That was not true of the count check when the build failure was partial, which is exactly the Round 1057 case.

THE OLDER DEBTS ARE UNTOUCHED AND STILL RANKED: SS2 (widen the authorable edit population past the fact legs to the canon order and the section registry — 65 of 74 accounts have never been put to a second value) is the next round; then SS1 (the backlog head at 102 shared subjects) and TT1 (a quest disclosed on a scene only a fork walks).

Round 1061.decision_summary:
An author writes three manifests. The corruption population read one.

Round 1054 widened that population from the legs that say what a fact CLAIMS to

Round 1062.decision_summary:
The sweep recorded a status it never read, and owned a tree it could not put
back.

Two things were true of the injection harness at once, and neither was held. It
parses every run's log for the names in the `failures:` lists AND records the
status the suite exited with — and then judged the sweep on the names alone. The
exit code went into the report and was read by nothing; Round 1060 filed that as
dead data and left it. The other half is ownership: the harness started the
suite as an ordinary child, so a harness that was killed left `cargo test`
running. Round 1061 killed one, the orphan stayed attached to the same log file
and wrote a second copy of seven doc-test targets into it, and the re-run's
control came back as 159 targets under 152 names — refused by the
name-uniqueness gate Round 1060 had built. That refusal is the only reason
anybody found out. The quieter half is worse: a sweep killed between `apply` and
`restore` leaves the injection IN the tree, and the next sweep measures that
injection as its own baseline.

A VERDICT IS TWO HALVES AND EACH IS BLIND WHERE THE OTHER SEES. A failure list
is written by the test harness inside the suite, so it is empty when the suite
never got that far — a target that did not compile, a crash, a signal. An exit
code is one number for the whole run, so it names no test and cannot be compared
with the control's. Recorded side by side and never compared, the pair is worth
exactly the weaker of the two, and the weaker one is silent in the case that
matters. So they are held to each other now: a run that exited non-zero and
named no failing test is not a clean surface, and a run that exited 0 over a log
naming failures is fiction in the other direction. The control is refused as a
baseline on either; every injection run is refused on either, before anything
about what it found is read.

OWNERSHIP THROUGH ONE'S OWN DEATH IS NOT A SIGNAL HANDLER. `SIGKILL` cannot be
caught, so a design in which only the harness can clean up is a design that
cannot clean up. What the kernel offers instead is a relationship arranged in
advance: a child can ask to be signalled when its parent dies, and a process
group can be signalled as one. The suite is therefore no longer started by the
harness. It is started by a SUPERVISOR — one re-exec of this same program —
which leads its own process group, asks for `SIGTERM` when the harness dies BY
ANY MEANS, starts the suite in a group of ITS own so one kill reaches every test
binary rather than only the `cargo` above them, holds the path to the originals,
and re-raises the signal that killed the suite instead of translating it into an
exit code, so a run that was killed is not read as a run that finished. The
originals go to disk before the first edit for the same reason the supervisor
exists: the process holding them in memory is the process that may die.

Two of this repository's four separate workspaces had rotted, and nothing had
failed.

`cargo test --workspace` reaches the root workspace. It cannot reach `bench/`,
`studio/` or the two under `tools/`, because each of those carries its own
`[workspace]` — a deliberate choice, and Round 1059 made the injection harness
one for a stated reason: the root's gates should never have to compile it. The
consequence went unpriced. Their tests run when a person remembers to run them.
The pre-commit hook does gate them, but for `fmt` and `clippy`, and only when
one of their files is staged — so a workspace nobody edits is a workspace
nobody checks.

Asked for the first time: `studio/` does not compile at all — 17 errors, its
source using a `pinion_gpu` that its manifest does not depend on — and `bench/`
has 6 failing tests in `codegen-prototype`, pinned to the markdown-document
model Round 400 removed. Neither had failed anything, because nothing had asked.
Round 784 repaired `studio` once already, under a commit subject that names this
exact shape: repair the crate no gate was watching.

THE RULE IS TOTALITY, NOT A LIST OF WHAT SOMEBODY REMEMBERED. The gate walks the
tree for every `Cargo.toml` that declares its own `[workspace]` — the same walk
the pre-commit hook already does — and every one it finds is either tested or
named with the reason it is not, WITH THAT REASON PRINTED ON EVERY RUN. The
default is fail-closed: a workspace added to this repository is tested by this
gate the moment it exists, and taking one out of it takes writing down why,
where a reviewer reads it. A skip that says nothing is the state this round
found, one layer up.

AND THE GATE ASSERTS ITS OWN REACH. A run that discovered no workspace at all
would print the same nothing as a run where everything passed, so reaching zero
is a failure here. That is the lesson of the empty answer this arc keeps
relearning: an empty result is what "clean" and "never got there" both look
like.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: the two skips are repairs of nothing. `studio` cannot be
built by CI under any arrangement of this workflow — its dependencies are path
dependencies on a sibling repository that no checkout of this one contains — and
`bench` is a closed measurement spike whose failures are now named rather than
unknown. Which of the two to repair and which to retire is a question about what
this project still wants from them, and a gate does not answer it. What changes
today is that both are visible on every push instead of on the day somebody
happens to look.

`studio/` did not compile because the code pinion's build-time forge GENERATES

depend on `pinion-gpu`. That is the same shape the manifest already handles one
line up for `vello`, whose comment says exactly why: generated code names it
here, so a crate reached only transitively is not there at all. One dependency
line, and the crate builds and its test passes.

And the gate's own claim about `studio` was wrong in a way worth more than the
repair. Round 1063 declared it un-gateable because CI cannot check out the
sibling repository — true of CI, and false of the machine where the rot was

the skip is derived instead: for every workspace, the path dependencies that
leave this repository are resolved and the absent ones are named. `studio` is
tested wherever pinion is checked out and skipped where it is not, with the
missing path printed. Ask the machine, do not declare the answer.

`bench/` IS THE CORRECTION. Round 1063 filed its failures as tests pinned to the
markdown-document model retired when the store became the SSOT. Half of that was
wrong, and the split is the finding:

    indent its own comment documents; the sweep left the comment and ate one

    test named `anchor_preserves_cjk` had its CJK input replaced by an ASCII
    heading while its assertions were translated word by word, leaving a test
    whose input could not contain what it asserted. An expectation was
    translated away from the fixture that feeds it: heading `Changelog`,
    expected slug `change-history`.
  - The 11 failures Round 1063 NEVER SAW are the real removed-model rot:
    `markdown_full_scale.rs` reads `docs/DESIGN.md` and five sibling documents
    that no longer exist.

It never saw them because the gate ran `cargo test` without `--no-fail-fast`, so
it stopped at the first failing target and reported 6 where there were 17. A
gate that stops at the first failure reports a number somebody then fixes to.

path is removed in the change that supersedes it, and a carry kept "for now" is
dead code the next agent is tempted to reanimate. The only reason these survived
is that nothing ran them.

Round 1063 gave the separate in-repo workspaces a gate that runs their tests on
every push. Their `fmt` and `clippy` stayed where they had always been: in the
pre-commit hook, which reaches a workspace only when one of its files is STAGED.

difference is not theoretical — it is exactly why `bench` arrived at Round 1064
with 79 clippy findings and never once having been through `rustfmt`. Nobody had
edited it, so nobody had checked it, for as long as that had been true.

So the three checks are one gate now. Every check the root workspace gets, a
separate workspace gets: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets
-D warnings`, and the suite.

AND THERE IS ONE DEFINITION OF THEM. The hook no longer carries its own copy of
those two commands — it calls this script with `--lint-only`, which is precisely
the split the root workspace already has (the hook runs fmt and clippy before a
commit and never the suite; CI runs everything). That is not tidiness. The copy
the hook carried had a defect the other did not: without `--all`, a VIRTUAL
manifest has no targets, so `cargo fmt` printed its own usage and exited
non-zero, and the hook rejected every commit touching `bench` as "unformatted"
having checked nothing at all. Two copies of one rule drift, and the one nobody
runs is the one that drifts silently.
