`tools/twice-compiled` — every number in the census now comes in two. `Cost { times, micros }` replaces the per-unit count; `JobLog` carries the whole job's invocation time and its compiling WINDOW (earliest start to latest exit, taken from the clocks rather than from the order of the lines, because a record is appended when a compiler exits and the earliest start routinely arrives last). `Census` gained `paid_micros` / `floor_micros` / `repeated_within_jobs_micros` / `shared_between_jobs_micros`, split the same way and by the same definition-as-remainder as the counts, so the two halves and the whole cannot drift apart by a rounded microsecond.

`JobLog` keeps the INTERVALS rather than folding them into a window, because a window cannot answer what a window is asked for. `busy_micros` is the union of them — the part of the job with at least one compiler alive, which is what compiling less can shorten — and `idle_micros` is the rest, the minutes a job spends running the binaries it just built. Summing the intervals instead of unioning them would report a job busier than the clock allows and leave it with no idle time at all.

`twice_compiled::Merge` states both sides of merging a pair: the compilations it removes and what they cost, priced at the cheaper of the two jobs' figures; and the merged job's window as a RANGE — never quicker than the longer of the two it replaces, which is also exactly what the pair costs the run today, and never slower than the two end to end. Between them the estimate scales only the BUSY part by the work that remains and carries the idle part across whole. Scaling the whole window would have promised a merged job shorter than either of the jobs it replaces, and the two jobs here with the most to share are the two that spend the longest running what they built.

`Census::surplus_by_crate` returns a priced `Cost` per crate and the report ranks by seconds rather than by rows. That ordering is the round's finding: `build_script_build` heads the row ranking with 409 surplus compilations and is among the cheapest units cargo drives, so a report that ranks by rows recommends a repair for the crates that cost the least.

`Refusal::JobRecordedNoTime` — a job that compiled and whose compilations took no time at all is refused. Counts present, totals adding up, seconds zero: the shape a job running an older recorder leaves, and the one no count can notice. A job that recorded nothing at all is still refused once and not twice.

`tools/rustc-log/injection-sweep.json` and `tools/twice-compiled/injection-sweep.json` (new) — eleven injections between them, each removing one mechanism this round added and naming the test that must go red for it. Both are scoped to their own crate's suite, which reads records rather than building anything, so each sweep is seconds.

`.github/workflows/mnemosyne-validate.yml` — the two comment blocks that state what the recorder records and what the gate asserts now say that a record carries what a compilation cost and that a census with no clocks in it is refused. No step changed; every cache key hashes this file, so the next run is a cold one for every job.
publishable_verification_bullets: THE INJECTION SWEEPS, both green and both non-vacuous: `tools/rustc-log/injection-sweep.json` 5 of 5 fired, `tools/twice-compiled/injection-sweep.json` 8 of 8, missed 0, target drift 0, and each control run green first (9 passed over 4 targets, 28 passed over 5). Every mechanism this round added is pinned by an injection that removes it and a named test that goes red.

THE INJECTION A LOWER BOUND CANNOT CATCH. `the-duration-is-a-constant` writes 1_000_000 µs instead of measuring, which satisfies every assertion of the form "the compilation took at least this long" — the obvious test for a clock. What catches it is the window: the record's start and end must lie inside the window the test itself observed around the child, and a constant large enough to pass the first assertion overruns the second. The start has its own injection (`the-start-is-not-a-clock`) and fails the same assertion from the other end.

THE EXIT STATUS, both halves, because waiting for the compiler is what put it at risk. `a_compilation_that_failed_is_reported_as_failed_and_still_recorded` runs a child that exits 7 and requires cargo to see 7 AND the record to be written anyway; `a_compiler_the_kernel_killed_is_not_handed_over_as_success` runs one that kills itself with SIGKILL and requires 128 + 9. Injections `the-compilers-exit-code-is-swallowed` and `a-killed-compiler-exits-zero` turn each of them red.

THE WINDOW IS PROVED AGAINST THE CASE THAT MAKES IT NECESSARY: two records where the LATER line has the EARLIER start, which is what a long compilation and a short one look like in a log appended at exit. The window is the earliest start to the latest exit, the span is 900 µs, and the work is 1000 µs — larger than the window, because the two overlapped. `the-window-is-the-first-line-to-the-last` reduces it to 400 µs and goes red.

THE TWO ERROR DIRECTIONS ARE PINNED BY THE INJECTIONS THAT FLIP THEM. `the-surviving-compilation-is-priced-at-the-cheapest` prices the retained compilation at the minimum instead of the maximum and turns the floor red; `a-merge-is-credited-with-the-dearer-of-the-two` credits a merge with the larger of the two prices and turns both the census test and the merge test red. Neither could be caught by a total, because both keep every total adding up.

THE FINDING ITSELF IS A TEST. `the_most_numerous_surplus_and_the_dearest_are_not_the_same_crate` builds two jobs that each compile three `build_script_build` units at 5 µs and one `mnemosyne_store` unit at 900, and asserts that the row ranking heads with the build scripts and the second ranking heads with the store — the two orders naming two different repairs. `the-crate-breakdown-is-counted-and-not-priced` stops accumulating the seconds and turns it red along with the per-crate identity.

THE NEW LAW HAS A CONTROL. `a_job_whose_compilations_took_no_time_at_all_is_refused` takes the census that is otherwise accepted, zeroes one job's seconds, and requires exactly that refusal; the accepted census is the same fixture with its clocks intact, and `a_job_that_recorded_nothing_is_refused_once_and_not_twice` holds the two laws apart.

END TO END ON REAL CARGO, not fixtures: `tools/ci-plan` built twice under the recorder into two separate target directories named for two real jobs, then the census read over both. It reported 12 compilations paid, 6 distinct, 50.0% duplicated by rows and 49.0% by seconds (2.2 s paid, 1.1 s floor), each job compiling within a 0.9 s window at 1.2 compilers at once, a merge removing 6 compilations and 1.1 s and lengthening the window from 0.9 s to an estimated 1.0 s — and refused the seven jobs of the workflow that did not run in the smoke, exiting 1, which is the law working.

THE IDLE TIME IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, which is a carry this round refused to write. `the_part_of_a_window_with_no_compiler_alive_is_measured_and_not_assumed` pins the union of the intervals against their sum — two compilers overlapping and a gap after them make a 600 µs window in which 250 µs is busy, where summing would claim 300 µs of busy and no idle at all. `a_merge_estimate_does_not_shorten_the_time_no_compiler_was_alive` builds the pair this repository actually has, jobs that spend nine tenths of their window running what they built, and requires the estimate to be 1900 µs where scaling the whole window says 1000 — a merged job shorter than either of the two it replaces. Both injections (`a-job-is-busy-for-the-sum-of-its-compilers`, `the-estimate-scales-the-whole-window`) turn them red.

THE GATE THAT RUNS THESE WORKSPACES IN CI: `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh tools/rustc-log tools/twice-compiled` clean end to end — `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, the item-citation gate, the blind-wait gate and both suites, checked 2, skipped 0. Suites are 9 tests for the recorder (4 new) and 28 for the census (25 law, 3 against this repository's own workflow), all green.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: THE PRICED CENSUS OF THIS CI DOES NOT EXIST YET, and only a run can make it. The gate reads logs the jobs wrote while doing work they were doing anyway, so the numbers arrive with the next push and cost nothing; the alternative is a local replay, which takes hours and cannot run `msrv` or `cache-budget` at all because GitHub resolves their environment. The next run is a COLD one for every job — every cache key hashes the workflow and the workflow changed — which is the run that gives the structural figure rather than the warm bill.

WHAT THE SECONDS STILL CANNOT SAY IS A JOB'S DURATION. The window is the first compiler's start to the last one's exit: it excludes the checkout, the toolchain install, the cache restore and the artifact upload, and merging two jobs saves one of each of those, which nothing here counts. GitHub knows those numbers and `cache-budget` already reaches the API with a token, so joining a run's job durations to this census is a describable piece of work rather than a limit — it is deferred as a COST judgement, and this bullet is where that is said out loud rather than dressed as impossibility.

QQ3 IS NOW JUDGEABLE AND STILL NOT JUDGED. `sccache` cannot move this census — a cache hit does not stop cargo asking for the unit, so the recorder records it either way — and what it moves is the seconds, which now exist. What would decide it is a job whose unit count is unchanged and whose compiling seconds fall, which is a comparison between two runs and needs the baseline above first. Writing "sccache is the answer" before that is R1090's mistake one field over, which is the mistake Round 1092 named and did not commit.

THE RECORDER CANNOT SEE FOUR THINGS AND ALL FOUR UNDER-COUNT, which is the safe direction for a finding of the form "this work is done more than once". A unit that was already fresh is never handed to a compiler. `rustdoc` does not go through `RUSTC_WRAPPER`. A build script's own `cc` is not `rustc`, and `librocksdb-sys` compiles C in six of these jobs. And now: a compilation that never finished, because the record is written when the compiler exits — that is where the duration becomes known — so a job killed at its timeout loses whatever was in flight.

THE ESTIMATE KEEPS ONE ASSUMPTION AND IT IS NAMED. The idle part of a window is measured and carried across untouched; the compiling part is scaled by the work removed, which assumes the merged job compiles at the rate the two of them did. A runner with a fixed core count makes that very nearly true, and the two bounds around the estimate hold whether or not it is: a merged job is never quicker than the longer of the pair and never slower than the two end to end.

MERGING CAN ONLY EVER SPEND WALL-CLOCK. Two jobs beside one another cost the run the longer of them; one merged job cannot be quicker than that. So the trade this gate now states is compute against minutes, and there is no arrangement of the numbers in which merging is free. That is a property of the shape and not of this repository's figures, and it is worth having in front of whoever reads the census first.

Round 1094 — every one of the 0 jobs rec.decision_summary:
EVERY ONE OF THE 0 JOB(S) THIS WORKFLOW DECLARES RECORDED WHAT IT COMPILED.
That sentence, and an exit code of 0, is what this repository's compilation
census printed when it was asked to measure the thing it was built for. Round
1093 gave the recorder a clock so that the duplication could be priced; the first
use of the priced instrument was a local replay of every job, and the replay
refused all nine of them, joined nothing, printed a clean zero on every line, and
signed off. Nothing was wrong with the workflow. Nothing had been measured.

THE REPLAY WAS CLOSED BY THE WIRING THAT GAVE THE GATE ITS POPULATION. A local
replay will not run a job whose environment only GitHub can resolve —
`RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: ${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}` is read from a step this
machine does not run, and replaying `msrv` on the dev toolchain would report its
units as shared with every other job, which is the loudest wrong answer available
here. That refusal is right. What it did not know is that Round 1092 had put
`MNEMOSYNE_RUSTC_LOG: ${{ github.workspace }}/rustc-log/<job>.log` on EVERY job
in the file — an expression only GitHub resolves, and one the replay OVERWRITES
with a path of its own before it runs a single step. So it refused all nine jobs
over a value nobody reads. The entrance has been shut since the day the recorder
was wired in, and it stayed shut because a replay costs hours and nobody ran it
again: the round that closed it had taken its own measurements before it landed.

THE REPAIR IS ONE LIST WITH TWO USES. `REPLAY_SETS` names the two variables the
replay owns; they are applied to every step it runs, overriding whatever the
workflow spells, and they are exactly the names the unresolvable-expression check
skips. A variable set in one place and read in the other cannot come apart when
both read the same list, and a debug assertion at the override site says so if
anyone adds a third.

THE GATE DOES NOT REPLAY ITSELF, which is the same correction one step further
out. Its job downloads what the other jobs wrote and joins it, so replaying it
means running the census over a directory the replay is still filling, and
counting the instrument's own build as a cost CI pays. That is the mistake this
crate already corrects once — on a runner it drops its own log from the census —
and the replay had no equivalent. The exemption is DERIVED from the manifest the
step names, like the recorder's own, so it stays exactly as wide as the thing it
excuses.

BUT THE DEFECT WORTH THE ROUND IS THE SECOND ONE. A census that reached no jobs
at all printed every total as zero and exited as though the file were in good
order — and that is not a wiring bug, it is a gate that cannot tell its silence
from its success. The subject of this gate is what TWO jobs both compile: a
census of one job has no cross-job duplication BY CONSTRUCTION, and a census of
none has nothing. Both print a clean zero. So the gate now states its own reach
before it reads anything from the census: fewer than two jobs covered is a
refusal, whatever the totals say. The jobs a caller declares absent are
legitimate — the gate's own job on a runner, the jobs a replay cannot reproduce —
but a census in which that list has swallowed everything is a measurement that
did not happen.

THIS REPOSITORY HAS A TEST FOR THIS EXACT SHAPE AND IT DID NOT COVER THE OTHER
DOOR. `this_workflow_has_the_jobs_the_census_is_worth_taking_of` asserts that the
workflow declares more than two jobs, precisely because a census over one is
vacuous — written the same day the gate was, and true the whole time. It is an
assertion about the FILE. The replay's skip list is what decides how many of
those jobs a census actually covers, and nothing asserted anything about it. So
the new test reads the live workflow and pins the skip set to exactly three jobs
by name and reason, and a fourth job becoming unreplayable tomorrow turns it red
instead of quietly leaving the census.

WHAT THIS COST AND WHAT IT BOUGHT: the priced census of this CI still does not
exist, because the run that was supposed to produce it produced nothing. It can
now be produced without a push. And the finding it produced instead is worth more
than the numbers would have been on their own — an instrument's second entrance
had been welded shut for a round, and the only thing that could notice was
somebody running it.

A `debug_assert!` at the override site fails if a variable is ever set there without being named in the list.

`twice_compiled::unresolvable` moved from the binary into the library, where a test can reach it. It was the one decision in this crate that chose which jobs a census covers and it lived in `main.rs`, so nothing could assert anything about it; the round it was written in, it silently began refusing every job in the file.

`twice_compiled::GATE_MANIFEST` (new) — the replay does not replay the gate's own job. Derived from the manifest the step names, like the recorder's exemption, so it stays exactly as wide as the thing it excuses.

`Refusal::CensusCoversTooFewJobs` (new) — the gate states its own reach BEFORE reading anything from the census. Its subject is what two jobs both compile: one job has no cross-job duplication by construction and none has nothing, and both print a clean zero on every line. The jobs a caller declares absent are legitimate; a census in which that list has swallowed everything is a measurement that did not happen.

Six existing law fixtures now declare two jobs where they declared one. Not a workaround for the new law — a fixture of one job is a census this gate would refuse in production, and every one of those tests was making its point over a population the gate cannot legitimately be given.
verification_bullets: THE DEFECT WAS FOUND BY RUNNING IT, not by reading it. A local replay of the whole workflow, launched to price this CI's duplication, refused all nine jobs and printed `0 compilations across 0 job(s)`, `duplicated 0 (0.0%)`, and `every one of the 0 job(s) .github/workflows/mnemosyne-validate.yml declares recorded what it compiled` — exit 0, in under a second, with an empty log directory beside it.

THE LIVE WORKFLOW IS THE FIXTURE for the repair. `the_jobs_a_local_replay_cannot_run_are_exactly_these_three` reads the tracked file and pins the skip set to `cache-budget` (needs a token), `msrv` (a toolchain GitHub resolves from a step this machine does not run) and `twice-compiled` (the gate itself) — and asserts that what is left is at least the two jobs a census needs. Before the repair it skipped all nine; a job that becomes unreplayable tomorrow turns it red rather than quietly leaving the census.

THE NEW LAW HAS BOTH ITS ARMS AND A CONTROL. `a_census_that_reached_fewer_than_two_jobs_is_refused` covers the case the replay produced (every declared job absent, `covered: 0`) and the case one job produces (`covered: 1`, whose zero is arithmetic rather than a finding), and then the same census with two jobs covered, which is accepted.

IT IS LOAD-BEARING ACROSS THE FIXTURE SPACE, which is how the round found out the existing fixtures were unfaithful: six law tests failed on the new refusal because each declared a single job, a shape the gate would refuse in production. They now declare two and still make their own point, so the new law is proved by six tests it was not written for.

INJECTION SWEEP 11 of 11 FIRED, missed 0, drift 0, control 32 passed over 5 targets. The three new injections are the two defects of this round and the third correction: `a-census-of-no-jobs-reads-as-clean` restores the vacuous green, `a-job-is-skipped-for-a-variable-the-replay-replaces` restores the closed entrance and turns the live-workflow test red as well, and `the-replay-replays-the-gate-itself` puts the instrument back into its own reading.

SUITES AND GATES: 28 law tests and 4 against this repository's own workflow, all green; `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh tools/twice-compiled` clean end to end — fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, item citations, blind waits and the suite.
carry_forward_bullets: THE PRICED CENSUS STILL DOES NOT EXIST, and this is the round that made it producible. The replay now runs six of the nine jobs on this machine, each cold in a git worktree of its own, and it takes hours; the CI figure is a push away and answers a different question (the bill that run actually paid, against the structural duplication a cold replay measures). Both are wanted and neither is in hand.

WHAT NOTICED THIS WAS A PERSON RUNNING THE THING, and nothing else could have. The gate's own suite was green throughout, the workflow was correct, the wiring was correct, and the entrance had been welded shut for a round. The general shape — an expensive path that only a human ever exercises, gated by nothing — is not repaired by this round: only the replay's SKIP LIST is now asserted, not that the replay still produces a census. A cheap end-to-end that replays one job and requires a non-empty result would close it, and it is not built.

A CENSUS OF TWO JOBS IS THE MINIMUM THIS GATE ACCEPTS, not the minimum worth having. Nothing here refuses a census of two when the workflow declares nine, so a replay that lost six jobs to a new expression would pass the reach law while measuring a third of the file. The honest limit would compare the covered count against what the workflow declares, and the reason it is not written today is that the legitimate absences differ per caller — the runner drops one job, the replay drops three — so the threshold is a judgement this round has no measurement behind.

A PUSH CARRIES A RANGE AND THIS GATE ASKED ABOUT ONE COMMIT. Round 1093 and
Round 1094 went up together in a single push; the workflow moved in the FIRST of
them, which legitimately invalidated all eight cache keys in the file, and every
job correctly rebuilt from nothing. The gate that judges that asked `git diff
HEAD~1 HEAD` — the tip commit alone, which had touched no hashed input — and
reported eight legitimate cold builds as a defect. `cache-budget` failed sixteen
seconds in, main went red, and `twice-compiled` was skipped behind it, so the
priced census the two rounds before this one existed to produce did not run.

THE GATE REFUSED FOR A REASON OUTSIDE ITS OWN LAW, which this repository has
already named as the same failure as a gate that does not fire. The law is that
a cache built from nothing inside a run means that job paid for a cold build, and
that this is excused when the key's own hashed inputs legitimately moved. The
inputs HAD moved. The question was simply asked over the wrong interval, and
every part of the machinery around it was working: the budget arithmetic was
fine at 8.57 GB of 10, the `created_at` reasoning was fine, and the eight
messages it printed were each individually true of the commit it looked at.

THE RANGE IS NOW THE RUN'S. The workflow hands the gate `github.event.before` —
the commit the push started from, which is the runner's own answer to "what does
this run cover" — and the gate diffs from there. On a `pull_request` there is no
such commit and none is needed: the runner checks out a merge commit whose first
parent is the base branch, so the existing `HEAD~1..HEAD` is exactly the change
the pull request proposes, and the fallback is correct BY CONSTRUCTION rather
than by luck. `range_start` is a function of what the runner said and what the
checkout holds, it lives in the library where a test can reach it, and every one
of its four answers is pinned: the push range, a branch created by this push
(GitHub spells that as all zeros, and there is no earlier commit to ask about),
a commit the checkout is too shallow to hold, and no push range at all.

THE CHECKOUT IS NOW THE WHOLE HISTORY, and the argument is that a push's commit
count is unbounded. Depth 2 was exactly enough for the question the gate used to
ask; every fixed depth is a guess about how many commits somebody pushes at once,
and the guess fails SILENTLY — the named commit is simply not there, the gate
narrows back to the range that failed today, and the verdict looks the same. The
cost was measured rather than assumed: this repository's pack is 13 MB over 891
commits, against a job that otherwise takes seventeen seconds.

different questions, and a number that does not carry its interval is a number
whose meaning a reader has to guess — the same class as the report lines Round
1093 made carry their units. The summary prints `over df48a8d..HEAD, the commits
this push carried` or `over HEAD~1..HEAD (…)` with the reason, so a narrowed
range can never again look like a full one.

Round 1096 — a path only a person runs i.decision_summary:
A PATH ONLY A PERSON EVER RUNS IS A PATH NOTHING GUARDS. Round 1094 found its
own instrument welded shut: the compilation census has two entrances, and the
expensive one — the local replay that reproduces every job's build on this
machine — had been refusing every job in the workflow for a round while the
suite stayed green. That round repaired the wiring, added a law against a census
that reached too few jobs, and pinned the replay's skip list against the live
workflow. Then it wrote down, as the carry it could not close, that only the SKIP
LIST was now asserted — not that the replay still produces a census — and named
the fix it had not built: a cheap end-to-end that runs the replay and requires a
non-empty result. This round builds it, and then finds the same hole one door
along and closes that too.

THE GAP WAS NOT SUBTLE AND IT WAS NOT SMALL. Every decision in this crate that
was not a reading of records lived in `main.rs`, and nothing here ran the binary,
so `main.rs` had no test of any kind. That is the worktree per job, the two
variables the replay overrides, the log named for the job that wrote it — and
also the OTHER entrance: the workflow read off `$GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF`, and the
gate dropping its own still-building job from its own census. Seven injections in
this round are seven real ways to break that file, and not one of them was
readable before it.

TWO OF THE FIVE DO NOT EVEN FAIL LOUDLY. A replay that gives every job the same
tree leaves the first job with a census and every job after it with an empty log,
because cargo runs no compiler for a unit that is already fresh — the duplication
this gate exists to count disappears into what looks like jobs that compile
nothing. A gate that counted its own half-built job would refuse the very push it
is part of, for a job that did nothing wrong.

THE FIXTURE IS A REPOSITORY, BECAUSE THE REPLAY IS. It is a workflow of two or three jobs, a dependency-free crate they all compile, a copy of the recorder's
own source, and a git commit for `git worktree add … HEAD` to check out. The real
binary is then run over it AS A PROCESS, and its exit code and its report are the
assertions — because the defect being guarded against was an exit code of 0 under
a report of clean zeroes, and a test that called a function would not have been
reading the thing that lied. Two jobs and not one: the reach law from Round 1094
refuses a census of fewer than two, so the fixture has to be a population the
gate accepts in production.

WHAT MAKES THE FIXTURE FAITHFUL IS THE SPELLING. Every job writes
`MNEMOSYNE_RUSTC_LOG: ${{ github.workspace }}/rustc-log/<job>.log` and a
`RUSTC_WRAPPER` in the same form — the exact shape that closed the entrance, an
expression only GitHub resolves and one the replay replaces before it runs
anything. A simplified fixture would have been green on the day. The control for
it is a variable the replay does NOT own, carrying the expression the `msrv` job
carries, and the two cases it produces are two of the six tests: a replay that
reaches one job, which has no finding available to it and must be refused rather
than reported, and a replay that reaches none, which must not print the sentence
a file in good order prints.

THE PROOF IS THE SWEEP AND NOT THE GREEN. Eighteen injections fired, missed 0,
drift 0, over a control of 38 passing tests. Two of the numbers in it are the
point. four of the eighteen turn exactly ONE test red and in every case it is a new
one, so four of the defects this round can now name had no reader at all. And
`a-job-is-skipped-for-a-variable-the-replay-replaces` — the injection that
restores Round 1094's actual defect — now turns four tests red where it turned
two: the end-to-end catches the thing that was missed, through the path that was
missed, rather than by an assertion about the file.

WHAT IS STILL NOT ASSERTED, NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED: that the six
replayable jobs of THIS repository's workflow produce a census when they are
replayed. Their steps are the real suites and gates, they take hours, and no test
can run them. What is asserted is the two halves either side of that — which of
the live jobs a replay would refuse, and that the machinery produces a census
from the jobs it does run — and the middle is a cost, not a limit of the world.
changes_bullets: `tools/twice-compiled/tests/entrances.rs` (new) — BOTH ways into this gate, run as the program a person runs. It builds a fixture repository (a workflow, a dependency-free crate every job compiles, a copy of the recorder's source, one commit) and then runs the real binary as a PROCESS, reading its exit code, its report and the logs it wrote. Before this the whole of `main.rs` had no test of any kind, because nothing in the crate ran the binary.

Four tests for the replay entrance. Three are one per answer it can give: it reached both jobs and the census holds the unit they share; it reached one, which has no cross-job finding available to it and is refused rather than reported; it reached none, and does not get to print `every one of the … job(s) recorded what it compiled`. The fourth is the two rules about a step — a `rustup` or `sudo` step installs what this machine already has and is named as skipped rather than run, and a step that FAILS is named rather than fatal, because the compilations it already paid for are already in the log.

Two tests for the runner entrance, which had the same absence for a different reason — it is exercised on every push, so a break there is loud, but the two decisions in it still had no reader. The workflow is read out of the middle of `$GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF`, and the job the gate is RUNNING IN is dropped from the census because its build is still in flight. The control removes `$GITHUB_JOB` — explicitly, since on a runner the suite is itself inside a job — and requires the gate to refuse itself, which is what says the drop is load-bearing rather than tidy.

The fixture spells `RUSTC_WRAPPER` and `MNEMOSYNE_RUSTC_LOG` as `${{ github.workspace }}/…`, the exact form that closed this entrance for a round; a simplified fixture would have been green on the day. Its control is `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: ${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}` — an expression the replay genuinely cannot resolve — carried by one job in the second test and by both in the third.

The positive replay test asserts the FINDING and not merely a non-empty file: both jobs compile the same crate in worktrees of their own, so `Census::shared_between_jobs` must exceed zero. It also poisons `MNEMOSYNE_RUSTC_LOG` in the process it launches, so a replay that stopped setting it for the steps it runs leaves a file the test can find rather than an absence it would have to explain.

Seven injections added to `tools/twice-compiled/injection-sweep.json`, all in `main.rs` and all previously unreadable: the replay not applying the two variables it owns, every job replaying into one tree, every job recording into one file, the replay running the steps that install what this machine already has, a failed step ending the replay, the gate counting its own half-built job, and the workflow reference read whole instead of from `.github/` on.

`tempfile` added as a dev-dependency, matching the three sibling tools that already use it. The 13 units it brings are compilations this repository's CI pays for in a fourth tool workspace and this gate will report them; a hand-rolled temporary directory would have been a second answer to a question this repository has already answered three times.
verification_bullets: INJECTION SWEEP 18 of 18 FIRED, missed 0, drift 0, control 38 passed and 0 failed over 6 targets. Eleven are the earlier rounds' and are unchanged; the seven new ones are each a real way to break `main.rs`, and each was unreadable before this round because nothing in the crate ran the binary.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT SAYS THE GAP WAS REAL: four of the seven turn exactly ONE test red, and in every case it is a new one. A replay that reuses a tree finds every job after the first already fresh, so cargo runs no compiler and the job reads as one with nothing to build; a replay that runs the steps installing what this machine has changes the compiler under its own measurement; a failed step made fatal throws away every job after the first gate that goes red; a gate that counts its own still-building job refuses the push it is part of. Nothing in this crate could see any of the four.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT SAYS IT IS THE RIGHT GAP: `a-job-is-skipped-for-a-variable-the-replay-replaces` restores Round 1094's actual defect, and now turns FOUR tests red where it turned two. Two of the four are these new ones, so the end-to-end catches the thing that was missed, through the path that was missed, and not by an assertion about the file.

`a-census-of-no-jobs-reads-as-clean` likewise goes from one red to three: the reach law's own test, plus both new tests for a replay that reached one job and none. Round 1094's law is now proved through the process that prints the verdict as well as through the function that decides it.

THE SIX TESTS RUN IN 4.11 SECONDS TOGETHER — four build the recorder and one dependency-free crate per worktree, two compile nothing at all. That is what makes this a gate rather than a ritual: the path it guards costs hours, and the reason it stayed broken for a round is that nobody pays hours twice.

SUITES AND GATES: 38 tests green in this crate (law 28, entrances 6, this repository 4); `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh tools/twice-compiled` clean end to end — fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, item citations, blind waits and the suite; `mnemosyne-cli validate-workspace` clean.

A HYPOTHESIS MEASURED AND REFUTED BEFORE THIS ROUND RELIED ON IT: that a local replay under-counts cross-job duplication because each job's worktree sits at a different path. The same crate built from two different directories emits the same `-C metadata` (`58c5a4da79a5ef2c` both times), so a path package is shared across worktrees exactly as a registry one is. That is what lets the fixture's jobs share a unit at all, and it says the local replay's cross-job figure is not distorted by where its trees are.

The push that carried Rounds 1093 and 1094 started a run in which `cache-budget` refused and `twice-compiled`, which waits on every other job by `needs`, was SKIPPED rather than run. Round 1095 is the repair of that refusal, so the next push is the first that can produce the number — and until one lands this remains undone work with a name rather than a limit.

Their steps are the real suites and gates; a replay of them is hours on this machine and would be hours of runner time if it were scheduled. What is asserted either side of it is which live jobs a replay would refuse and that the machinery produces a census from what it runs. Round 1097 — HEAD is a name, not a revis.decision_summary:
`HEAD` IS A NAME, NOT A REVISION, AND A REPLAY OUTLIVES WHAT IT NAMES. A CI run
measures one commit: every job of it checks out the same sha, and that is what
makes their compilations comparable. A local replay of the same workflow gives
each job a git worktree of its own and asks for `HEAD` each time — and it takes
hours, so `HEAD` is free to move underneath it.

IT MOVED. While a replay of `mnemosyne-validate.yml` was running on this machine,
a second session working in the same tree committed Round 1095. The replay had
already taken `item-citations`, `server-features`, `side-workspaces` and
`uncompiled-sources` from the commit before it; `unrun-tests`, the fifth, was
checked out at `93fc27d`. One census, two source trees, and NOTHING IN THE REPORT
SAID SO. The numbers survived only because that commit touched no manifest and no
lockfile, so cargo's `-C metadata` was unchanged and the units still matched. A
commit that had bumped a dependency would have produced a census in which the
fifth job shared nothing with the other four — which reads exactly like a job that
resolves its features differently, the sentence this whole instrument was built to
put a number on.

THE REPAIR IS TO ASK ONCE. `git rev-parse HEAD` runs before the first worktree,
and the hash it returns is what every worktree is made from. That is one line of
behaviour and it removes the whole class: the census is of a commit, whatever the
repository does afterwards.

THE OTHER HALF IS THAT THE REPORT NOW SAYS WHICH COMMIT. A measurement that
cannot name what it was of cannot be put beside another measurement, and this
repository has two instruments now producing numbers for the same question — a
cold local replay and a CI run — whose whole value is in being compared. The
replay prints `every job from <sha>, resolved once` before it starts, and the
test asserts that line appears EXACTLY ONCE with the repository's own hash in it.
Once is the law, not a nicety: a line per job is precisely the defect, so the
count is the oracle rather than the presence.

WHAT FOUND THIS WAS READING THE LOG OF A REPLAY THAT DIED. The round before this
one built the end-to-end that keeps the replay entrance open, and then went to
read the census the replay had produced — and the log said `unrun-tests` had been
checked out at a commit that did not exist when the replay started. The same
reading found that the replay had not finished at all: its last job never ran,
and the worktree of the one before it was still on disk, because the process was
killed with the session that started it. Both facts came from the same place, and
neither is visible in the census the replay leaves behind.

compiling. Of those, 1922 exist because the work is split across jobs and would
go away if those jobs were one, and 842 are a job compiling a unit twice inside
itself over its own separate workspaces, which merging cannot reach. The counts
reproduce Round 1092's cold-CI figures (5402 / 2684 / 2718) closely enough to
treat the population as stable.

Round 1099 — seven and a half gigabytes.decision_summary:
SEVEN AND A HALF GIGABYTES THAT SKIPPED NO COMPILATION AT ALL. `unrun-tests`
kept the last whole-`target` cache in this repository — 7.83 GB of an 8.57 GB
demand against a 10 GB budget, and 135 seconds of that job spent restoring it.
Two runs price what it bought. Run 31294232766 built every key from nothing,
because the push before it moved the workflow, and `unrun-tests` compiled 773
units. Run 31295304780 restored 7466 MB on an exact hit — `Cache hit`, `Cache
restored successfully`, in its own log — and `unrun-tests` compiled 773 units.
The same 773, the same 670 distinct, the same 103 repeats. Not one compilation
was skipped.

NOTHING BEFORE THIS COULD HAVE NOTICED. A cache that restores is green; a job
that compiles what it did not need to is green and merely slow; and the budget
gate built by Rounds 1090 and 1091 asks whether a cache is KEPT, which this one
was, perfectly, at 91% of the budget. What made the question answerable is the
instrument of Rounds 1092 and 1093: a census of every `rustc` a job runs, which
turns "was the cache warm" into a number that a cold run and a warm run either
agree on or do not.

WHY, AS FAR AS IT IS MEASURED AND NOT ONE STEP FURTHER. Cargo's fingerprint is an
mtime comparison, and a fresh checkout gives every file this repository owns a new
mtime. Measured on this machine over one workspace: cold, 33 compilations;
rebuilt immediately, 0; and after touching only this repository's own sources, 9
— every one of the 9 a crate this repository owns, and not a single dependency. A
tar round-trip of the build tree with nothing touched does the same 9. So the
checkout accounts for everything the repository owns and accounts for none of its
dependencies, which stayed fresh in every local variant. The runner recompiled the
dependencies too, so something there does what none of these do, and the one
difference left untested is that the runner round-trips `~/.cargo/registry`
through the same cache. That is named as the untested half rather than asserted.

THE REPAIR IS TO STOP KEEPING THE TREE, and it is licensed by the observation
whatever the mechanism turns out to be: a cache that skips no compilation is
paying 135 seconds and 91% of a budget for nothing. The registry and git caches
stay — 0.65 GB between them, and what a cold `cargo fetch` costs is not measured
as idle by anything here.

AND A TEST HAD TO BE INVERTED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH THE ROUND. Round 1090's
suite required at least one key to keep a build tree, and its stated reason was a
sentence: that this repository's slowest jobs are the ones a cold `target` costs
half an hour each. That sentence was never measured, and this round measured the
only key it still applied to. So the assertion is not relaxed to admit the change
— it is turned around. No key may keep a whole build tree, and the way to add one
back is a census showing it skips compilations, which `tools/twice-compiled` now
prints on every run. The evidence is a push away rather than an argument. Its
control is the sibling test that counts six holders in the pre-repair declaration
through the same reader, so a reader that stopped seeing trees turns that red
rather than making this vacuous.

That was a sentence, not a measurement, and the measurement contradicts it. The assertion is INVERTED: no key may keep a whole build tree, and adding one back takes a census showing it skips compilations.

WHAT IS THEREFORE NOT CLAIMED: that mtime is the whole reason. GATES: `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh tools/cache-budget tools/twice-compiled tools/ci-plan` clean end to end — fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, item citations, blind waits and three suites (cache-budget 13 + 5, twice-compiled 28 + 7 + 4, ci-plan 23). `mnemosyne-cli validate-workspace` clean.

Round 1101 — a prefix hit is invisible t.decision_summary:
A CENSUS IS A MEASUREMENT ONLY IF IT SAYS WHAT IT WAS TAKEN UNDER, and Round 1099
is what the missing sentence costs. That round compared two runs' censuses of one
job, called the first cold because every cache key had moved, found the numbers
identical, and deleted a 7.83 GB cache that was saving 426 compilations and ten
minutes. Round 1100 measured the revert and put it back. The carry it left named
the repair as joining the two instruments this repository already had.

THAT REPAIR WOULD HAVE CONFIRMED THE ERROR, and measuring it is this round's
first finding. `actions/cache@v6` declares exactly ONE output, `cache-hit`, and
its own manifest says a `restore-keys` prefix match returns `false` for it — the
action that did the restoring cannot say whether anything arrived. `cache-budget`
cannot either: it reads a cache created inside the run as one the run BUILT FROM
NOTHING, and `actions/cache` saves whenever the primary key missed, so a job
warmed by a prefix hit is described in the words used for a job that compiled
from an empty disk. Both instruments report the invisible state as cold. Joining
them joins two answers to a question neither was asked.

SO THE THIRD STATE IS MEASURED ON THE DISK, WHICH IS WHERE IT IS. `tools/restored`
is a dependency-free instrument that every cached job runs twice — once
immediately before its `actions/cache` step and once immediately after — over
that cache's own declared paths. What arrived is the difference, and the control
for whatever the earlier steps left in `~/.cargo` is the same tree measured
seconds earlier. Read with the action's `cache-hit`, that difference separates
four states where there were two: an exact hit, a PREFIX HIT (the one that was
invisible), nothing at all, and the contradiction where the action claims a hit
and no bytes arrive. The fourth is a variant rather than a fallback, so every
consumer must say what it does about it.

THE CENSUS NOW REFUSES TO BE QUOTED WITHOUT IT. `tools/twice-compiled` loads the
record beside each job's compilation log, prints the state on the line under
every job's counts and again under the totals, and refuses a job that declares a
cache and did not say. The population that owes a record is derived from the
workflow's cache declarations rather than from the jobs that compile — the two
gate jobs compile plenty and cache nothing — and the paths a job measured are
held against the paths its cache holds, which is what makes writing that list
twice safe.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM. The bytes that arrived are not the bytes that were
USEFUL: cargo decides that per unit from fingerprints this instrument does not
read, and a prefix hit restores a tree that is warm and stale at once. The
question answered is the one that was got wrong — did this job begin with a tree
or with nothing — and it is answered per run, in the run's own log, by a program
rather than by a person holding two reports.
changes_bullets: `tools/restored` — a new dependency-free workspace. `restored before <paths…>` opens a per-job record and measures each cached path; `restored after` re-measures the SAME paths (read back from the record, so the list has one spelling) and closes it with `actions/cache`'s own `cache-hit`. `Warmth` derives four states from the two answers, including the contradiction.

`.github/workflows/mnemosyne-validate.yml` — the seven cache-declaring jobs each gain `MNEMOSYNE_RESTORED`, an `id:` on the cache step, and the two measuring steps around it. The instrument-build step now builds both instruments under an empty `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, and `twice-compiled` derives that exemption from a list of instrument manifests rather than from one.

`tools/twice-compiled` — `Declared` replaces `declared_jobs`: one value holding both populations, because they come from one file and a two-argument signature is one a caller can fill from two workflows. `load` reads `<job>.restored` beside `<job>.log`; `judge` gains seven refusals; the report prints the state per job and under the totals.

`tools/twice-compiled/src/main.rs` — the replay owns three more variables, so a replayed census records that it started from nothing, which is what a replay does. It restores no cache and now says so instead of leaving a reader to remember it.

THE JOIN, AND IT IS NOW WORTH MAKING. This gate reads what STORAGE holds; R1101
built the instrument that reads what a job's DISK received. Neither answers the
other's question, which is why joining them was not obviously useful before
there was a third state to join: with only "the key hit" and "the key missed",
both readings agree and both are wrong about the same job. With the disk in
hand, `Recreated` stops guessing and prints what each owner actually got — or
says NOT MEASURED, which is a different sentence from a cold build and is the
one it is entitled to.

AND THE JOIN YIELDS A VERDICT NEITHER SIDE COULD REACH: a job that began with an
EMPTY tree while an archive `restore-keys` could have served was already in
storage. That is the cost the whole budget exists to buy off, and it was
invisible three times over — `cache-hit` is false for a prefix match either way,
the API cannot say what a disk received, and a legitimately invalidated key was
EXCUSED here, so a job that fell all the way through to nothing on a lockfile
bump was reported as the honest price of one. The excuse is now exactly as wide
as it should be: a dependency change excuses a MISSED KEY, never an empty disk.

WHICH GENERATION COUNTS IS THE WHOLE OF THE CARE. A job that missed its key
writes a new archive in its post step, so by the time this gate asks the API
that archive heads the prefix — counting it would make every genuinely cold
first run of a key look like a job that ignored a cache. What was available is
whichever generation PREDATES the run, superseded ones included, because

Round 1103 — a measurement that does not.decision_summary:
THE CARRY R1102 NAMED IS CLOSED, and closing it needed one missing thing rather
than a new gate: a shared coordinate. `ci-plan` reads a workflow twice — once for
the `run:` steps and once for the `actions/cache` steps — and returned two
populations with no position in either. So the question "do this job's two
measuring steps sit on the two sides of its restore?" had no answer in the file
at all. R1102 answered it by OBSERVATION instead: a pair that brackets nothing
measures a difference of zero, every job then reads as having started from an
empty tree, and an empty tree beside a restorable generation is a refusal. That
detects the mistake from a run. It does not fire on the file that is wrong.

BOTH STRUCTS NOW CARRY WHERE THE STEP SITS, counting EVERY step and not only the
ones that `run:`. That distinction is the whole of it: an index among `run:`
steps alone would place a step before a cache step it in fact follows, which is
the same number wearing the right shape. With one coordinate, `judge_wiring`
becomes a law about the file: every job with a cache measures each side exactly
once, the `before` sits ahead of every cache step the job declares and the
`after` behind every one of them, and a job that measures a restore it never
performs is refused from the other direction.

THE REGION AND NOT THE STEP. A job may declare more than one cache, and the
record brackets all of them — so the law is against EVERY cache the job declares
rather than one. A measurement that slipped between two of them reports the
second one's arrival as nothing, which is the same silence in a smaller place.

THE LAW SEPARATED FROM THE RECORD LAWS, because it needs nothing that ran.
Every other restore law joins a record to a declaration and is rightly silent
about the jobs a caller declares absent — the gate's own job, the jobs a local
replay cannot reproduce. These hold for a job that has never run, so
`RestoreIsNotRecorded` moved across with them: it was already a law about the
workflow, sitting inside a loop that skipped absent jobs.

AND THE ROUND'S OWN REGRESSION IS THE BEST EVIDENCE THE LAW WORKS. Recognising
the measuring step needs the command, and the command's spelling belongs to
`restored` for the reason `Side::word` does. The first version held the CI path
as a constant — and this repository runs the program by TWO paths, the release
binary in the workflow and the debug binary a local replay builds. The gate's own
replay suite turned red on the entrance the constant could not see. So the crate
publishes its NAME: a word is the program when it IS that name or ends in it
after a `/`, which keeps the step that BUILDS it — `tools/restored/Cargo.toml` —
out of the answer.

THE FIXTURE WAS WRONG IN EXACTLY THE WAY THE LAW REFUSES. The replay fixture
appended its `actions/cache` step after all of a job's `run:` steps, so both
measurements sat on one side of it. Nothing could see that before this round; the
control for the law was declaring the defect. Its cache step is now woven in at a
position the fixture states, and a position past the end is an assertion rather
than a silent append.

`tools/restored/src/lib.rs` — `PROGRAM` and `sides_measured`: which sides of the restore one `run:` step measures. The NAME and not a path, because this repository runs the program by two of them; a word qualifies when it is that name or ends in it after a `/`, which leaves the step that builds it out.

`tools/twice-compiled/src/lib.rs` — `judge_wiring`, a law over the workflow with no census at all: each side measured exactly once, the `before` ahead of every cache step the job declares and the `after` behind every one, and a job with no cache that measures a restore refused from the other side. `Declared.caches_at` carries where the caches sit. `RestoreIsNotRecorded` moved into it, since it was always a law about the file.

`tools/twice-compiled/tests/entrances.rs` — the replay fixture declared its cache AFTER both measuring steps, which is the defect the law refuses. Its position is now a field of the fixture job, woven in, and a position past the end is an assertion.
verification_bullets: INJECTION, three sweeps over the three workspaces this touches: 13 injections, 13 fired, 0 missed, 0 target drift. Controls green — `tools/twice-compiled` 62, `tools/restored` 38, `ci-plan` 14.

THE COORDINATE IS PROVED FROM BOTH SIDES AND FROM THE WRONG COUNTING. Dropping the position from the `run:` steps, from the cache steps, or counting only the `run:` ones each turns the live-file law red — the third is the one that still looks like a position.

Assertion moved; the injection now fires the test that is named for it.

THE LIVE FILE IS THE NON-VACUITY, AND THE LAW IS SHOWN TO BITE ON IT. `tools/twice-compiled/tests/this_repository.rs` walks every cached job of `mnemosyne-validate.yml`, moves that job's first measurement past its own cache step, and demands the refusal — seven jobs, not a fixture.

THE ROUND'S OWN REGRESSION WAS CAUGHT BY THE SUITE, not by reading: holding the CI path as a constant made the replay's debug binary invisible, and `a_replayed_job_records_that_it_started_from_nothing` turned red. It is now an injection of its own.

That is the strict direction and it is also the only one available: a `run:` step is a shell script, and no reader of the text can say what the shell will execute. Every invocation in this repository is a direct one, and the law's own refusal is what would announce the day that stops being true.

TWO INSTRUMENTS, TWO UNITS, ONE LINE APART — found by reading run 31307111606, and it is undone work rather than a limit. `cache-budget` prints `7.83 GB held` from the API, which is the COMPRESSED archive, and immediately under it `27258 MB restored` from the disk, which is not. Every other key reads 0.15 GB against 246 MB. Both numbers are right and neither says which quantity it is. The repair is the report saying so where the two adjoin, and what makes it a round of its own is that the renderer is `println!` in `main.rs` with no reader — R1096's lesson, which this repository has already paid for once.

Extending it means either wiring that workflow the same way or naming the exemption; the second is a claim about a job that caches, and this round makes neither.

XX2 STANDS AND STILL GATES THE ARC: why the runner recompiles DEPENDENCIES is unmeasured, and the untested difference is that `~/.cargo/registry` rides the cache too. No compilation cache can be judged before that is known.

Round 1105 — a delta between two runs th.decision_summary:
FOUR ROUNDS MADE EACH CENSUS SELF-DESCRIBING AND NOTHING HELD TWO OF THEM
TOGETHER. That was the standing carry from R1101, R1102, R1103 and R1104: a
census now says what it compiled AND what each job started from, which is what a
comparison needs and is not itself one. The reader was still doing the join by
hand, and the one time a reader did it, they got it backwards — R1099 read two
censuses side by side, called the first cold because its keys had moved, found
the counts equal, and deleted a 7.5 GB cache that was saving 426 compilations
and ten minutes. Both runs had been warmed through `restore-keys`.

SO THE LAW IS ABOUT THE UNITS. Every count in a census is of a COLD build by
construction — cargo runs no compiler for a unit that is already fresh — so what
a job began with is the unit its numbers are in, and a subtraction across two
different units is not a measurement. `compare` reports a per-job difference
only where both sides began in the same state, and names why each of the others
is not a difference: a job that began differently, a job that said what it
started from on one side only, a job in one census and not the other.

THE TOTALS ARE BEHIND A FUNCTION AND THE FIELDS ARE PRIVATE. That is the whole
of the design, because the totals are what a reader quotes and a total is a sum
over a POPULATION — one job in a different state spoils all of it and not merely
its own row. `Comparison::totals()` returns `None` while anything is
incomparable, so the number R1099 quoted cannot be reached at all rather than
being available beside a warning. The process exits 1 on it, because the verdict
of this entrance is its exit code.

THE STATE IS THE VARIANT AND NOT THE SIZE. No two runs restore the same number
of bytes, so comparing whole values would call every real pair incomparable —
and a check nobody can ever satisfy is a check nobody keeps. `Warmth::same_state`
takes the discriminant FROM THE TYPE, so a fifth state cannot be added and
quietly left out of it. What that does not model is magnitude: 246 MB and 27 GB
are one state to it. So the report prints BOTH figures rather than only the
verdict — the reader is owed the numbers the predicate does not look at.

IT READS NO WORKFLOW, WHICH IS A DECISION AND NOT AN OMISSION. The two censuses
may be of two different commits, whose workflows declare different jobs; that is
something this ANSWERS rather than needs told. Being handed `--workflow` is
therefore a refusal, not something to drop on the floor. And the input shape is
what `gh run download` actually writes — one subdirectory per artifact — because
a loader that knew only the flat shape a runner hands the gate reads that as a
run in which nothing recorded anything, and nothing prints as a clean zero.
changes_bullets: `tools/twice-compiled/src/lib.rs` — `compare`, `Comparison`, `Delta`, `Incomparable`, `Totals`. The totals are behind `Comparison::totals()` with private fields, so a sum over a population in which one job changed state cannot be reached at all rather than being available beside a warning.

`restored::Warmth::same_state` — the discriminant, taken from the type. Two prefix hits of 246 MB and 27 GB are one state; comparing whole values would call every real pair incomparable, so the report prints both figures instead.

`load_collected` reads the per-artifact subdirectories `gh run download` writes, as well as the flat directory a runner hands the gate. One job recorded in two places is an error, not whichever the walk reached last.

`Entrance` + `read_arguments` — the three ways in, read in the library where a test can ask. `compare` refuses `--workflow`: the two censuses may be of different commits, which it answers rather than needs told.
verification_bullets: INJECTION: 8 injections, 8 fired, 0 missed, drift 0, control 76 green. The size taken for the state, the totals reachable through a confounded job, the same silence read as a difference, only the flat directory read, a job recorded twice overwritten, a workflow silently ignored, a comparison of nothing signing off, and the verdict never reaching the exit code.

THE EXIT CODE IS INJECTED TOO, which is why this entrance is also run as a process: `main` returning 0 regardless leaves every library test green and the report perfect. That injection turns red exactly the tests that run the binary.

ZERO AGAINST ZERO IS NOT A DIFFERENCE OF NONE, and the first cut of `totals()` got it wrong: two empty directories have nothing incomparable, because nothing was compared, and both totals are honestly empty. It was caught reading the control back rather than by a test, so a test and an injection now hold it — the exit code says 1 and the report says NEITHER CENSUS HOLDS A JOB.

END TO END ON TWO REAL RUNS, and it refused them — correctly. `31301559640` predates `tools/restored`, so seven of its jobs left no record of what they started from while the same jobs in `31307111606` did. The tool names all seven and withholds the totals rather than subtracting counts taken in unknown units. That is the first cross-run comparison this repository has been able to make, and its answer is that this particular pair cannot be compared.

THE STALE-BINARY TRAP CAUGHT ME AND IS WORTH RECORDING: that end-to-end run first printed NO TOTALS and exited 0, because `target/debug` still held the binary the last injection had built with `exit(0)`. A sweep restores sources, not artefacts. Rebuilding gave exit 1.

Round 1107 — a horizon is not a job's si.decision_summary:
A GATE PRINTED ITS OWN HORIZON AS A JOB'S SHORTCOMING, and R1106's carry named
it the moment it landed. `cache-budget` joins what GitHub STORES against what
each job's DISK received, and for the one cache owner it can never be handed a
record for it printed "`replay` did not say what it started from" — the sentence
for a job that could have been heard and was not. Run 31313164921 printed it
again, beside eight owners that had all said.

WHY IT CAN NEVER BE HANDED THAT RECORD is not a shortfall anywhere: a restore
record is a file on a runner, the only thing that carries it off is an
`actions/upload-artifact` step, and what that step produces is an artifact OF A
RUN. The gate's own job downloads the artifacts of the run it is inside, whose
jobs are one workflow's jobs. `evidence-replay.yml` declares a cache and is not
that workflow, so its owner is in the report and out of reach — and R1106 had
just established that the repair the old sentence asks for, wiring a measurement
into that workflow, is the WRONG repair, because that workflow uploads nothing
and the file would die with its runner.

SO THE REPORT SAYS WHICH OF THE THREE IT IS, and derives all three. `Unheard`
is the verdict: `ItsOwnSilence` for an owner whose records were collectable
here, `NothingCollectsIt` when its workflow uploads no artifact at all,
`AnotherWorkflow` when the records belong to another run's artifacts, `NoRun`
when this is not a run. Only the first is a gap in this repository; the others
are the reader's horizon, said as the reader's.

THE ORDER IS PART OF THE DECISION. An owner in another workflow that also
collects nothing is BOTH, and the two sentences send a reader to different
places: one says a cross-run reader would hear it, the other says nothing will
ever hear it. The far-reaching reason is printed, because acting on the nearer
one is the wasted repair R1106 refused.

AND THE READING BEHIND IT NOW HAS ONE HOME. Two gates need to know which
workflow a run is of — the census gate loads that file, this gate joins it
against every declaration's source — and the census gate had been cutting
`owner/repo/<path>@<ref>` for itself. Two cuts of one string are two answers
about which file a gate is judging, which is the shape `ci-plan` exists to
remove, so `workflow_of_reference` is there and both call it. It also gained
the half neither had: the name is HELD AGAINST the tracked files. A path
nothing tracks compares unequal to every declaration's source, so a gate that
merely cut would report every job in the repository as belonging to somewhere
else — a verdict shaped like a reading with nothing behind it.

THE ONE ANCHOR OUTSIDE THE READING IT CHECKS is a record in hand. Every
sentence above rests on which workflows collect, and a reader answering "none"
would explain all eight owners with a reason nobody wrote — entirely
self-consistent and entirely wrong, which is the class of defect this round is
about. So a record read for an owner whose workflow this gate reckons collects
nothing is a refusal: the observation cannot be argued with by the reading.

A SWEEP HAD STOPPED PROVING ANYTHING AND SAID SO ONLY WHEN RUN. Re-running the
census gate's injection sweep refused at its own anchor: R1103 inserted a line
between the two the sweep matched on, so that injection has applied to nothing
since, and the harness's exactly-once rule is what caught it. The anchor is
repaired here; a gate over every sweep's anchors is not this entry's, and it is
undone work rather than a limit.

A SWEEP HAD STOPPED PROVING ANYTHING AND NOTHING SAID SO FOR FOUR ROUNDS. An
injection sweep is how this arc says a contract is not vacuous: it breaks the
thing the contract is about and requires the named test to go red. The break is
exact text — `from` must occur EXACTLY once in the file it names — and the
source it names moves. R1103 inserted one line between the two lines the census
gate's `every-job-owes-a-restore-record` matched on. From that commit the
injection applied to nothing, and because the harness refuses a sweep WHOLE at

`tools/twice-compiled/injection-sweep.json` looked exactly like a proof and was
a file. R1107 found it by re-running that sweep for an unrelated reason.

THE ONLY READER OF AN ANCHOR WAS A SWEEP BEING RUN, and a sweep is run when
somebody decides to run one — tens of minutes of suite time each, so nobody runs
them all. That is the whole defect: the decay is silent, the cost of noticing is
a decision, and a decayed sweep is indistinguishable from a sound one by
reading.

SO THE ANCHORS ARE A LAW NOW, and it runs no suite. Whether an anchor still
applies is a question about TEXT, and it is answered by the very function the
harness itself uses — the fused snapshot-and-pre-flight pass — so the law and
the tool cannot come to different answers about what applies. It costs
milliseconds and it covers every sweep this repository tracks, which is the
part no person was ever going to do.

AND THE POPULATION HAD TO BECOME DERIVABLE BEFORE IT COULD BE ASKED. Two
conventions were in use: eight sweeps written to be run from the repository
root, and two written to be run from `tools/injection-harness`, with `repo` and

each manifest's `_` prose. A second reader cannot read prose, so the base is now
the MANIFEST'S OWN DIRECTORY — the one base a file always knows. A sweep is
runnable from anywhere, and the tree it is about is derivable from the file
rather than from a convention somebody remembered.

suspected. `tools/uncompiled-sources` grew a SECOND call site with the same
three lines, so its anchor matched twice — the quieter failure, because the edit
would still land, on whichever copy came first, and the sweep would report a red
nobody described. That second site had its own law and no injection aimed at it;
it has one now. And `tools/item-citations` was the sweep written to the other
convention, unreadable from the root at all.

own sweep is `self-check.json` and the worked example is `example.json`; a glob

Round 1109.decision_summary:
THE QUESTION THE DEBT LEDGER HAD CARRIED AS A PREMISE HAD NEVER BEEN MEASURED.
"The runner recompiles dependencies too, and why is unmeasured" has stood as
carry XX2 across five rounds, with an experiment sketched for the WHY — a
dedicated `CARGO_HOME` and a cold fetch. Nobody had asked the prior question.
Every job of this CI writes down every `rustc` it runs, argument for argument,
and the input file is one of those arguments: the answer to "were these
dependencies" was already inside artifacts this repository has been downloading
for a week. What was missing was a reader. `twice_compiled::read` parsed the
crate name, the fingerprint, the emit list and the crate types, and dropped the
path on the floor.

SO A UNIT NOW SAYS WHOSE SOURCE IT WAS, and the reading is off CARGO'S LAYOUT
rather than off this workflow: `registry/src/<index>/<name>-<version>` is where
cargo unpacks a fetched crate whether anything caches it or not, and `compare`
— which holds two censuses that may be of two different commits — has no
workflow to consult. What makes that reading ANSWERABLE about a cache is a
separate joining, and it is a test against the live file: the trees this
workflow caches under a cargo home are exactly the two `Origin` calls fetched,
so a third one added tomorrow turns red here instead of quietly compiling into
units the split calls the checkout's.

AND THE NUMBER IS LARGE. Of the 5544 compilations run 31316052015 paid for,
4095 — 73.9% — are crates cargo fetched, and they are 2489.3 of its 4169.6
compiler-seconds, 59.7%. Every one of the seven cached jobs in that run
restored `~/.cargo/registry` and `~/.cargo/git` on an EXACT hit. The cache is
doing what it says: it brings the sources. Nothing brings their compiled form,
and three quarters of what this CI compiles is therefore work a hit did not
spare. That is the ceiling any compile cache would be aimed at, and until now
it was a guess.

THE READER CAUGHT ITS OWN GAP BEFORE THE NUMBER WAS QUOTED. Its first totals
came to 5378 where the ledger's said 5531, and the 153 missing were not lost
silently: a keyed compilation whose arguments do not hold EXACTLY ONE
free-standing input is refused as unplaced rather than guessed at, and the
count of them is printed. All 153 were `clippy-driver`. `cargo clippy` sets
`RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER`, so for every workspace member cargo runs `<recorder>
<clippy-driver> <rustc> <arguments…>` and the record carries TWO program paths
ahead of the first flag — the reader had been reading the second one as a
source file. The repair is cargo's own contract rather than a list of driver
names: a wrapper is handed the next program in the chain, so the chain is every
word before the first one beginning with `-`, at any depth and for a driver
this repository has never heard of.

AND THE OTHER HALF OF THIS ROUND WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT SAID SO. The
record header has always kept the compiler's path, "because the MSRV job runs a
different `rustc` over the same sources", and the key dropped it — so this
round expected to find MSRV's 324 compilations and the clippy passes merged
into stable's and reported as removable duplication. Adding the driver to the
key left the floor of a real eight-job census at 2707 distinct units, exactly
where it was. Nothing merged. The field stays, for the reason the fields beside
it are given — a cargo release that narrows `-C metadata` must make this reader
split rather than merge — but it is documented as an assumption made explicit,
not a defect repaired.
changes_bullets: `tools/twice-compiled/src/lib.rs` — `Origin` (`Registry` / `Git` / `Tree`) with `fetched()`, read off cargo's unpack layout and demanding the whole of it: `registry/src` on its own is a pair any repository may have, so an index directory and a `<name>-<version>` below it are required. The strict direction is chosen and named — this instrument exists to find out whether the runner recompiles dependencies, and a rule that guessed generously would answer its own question.

`tools/twice-compiled/src/lib.rs` — `arguments_of`, the wrapper chain. cargo hands a wrapper the next program along as its first argument, and `cargo clippy` makes that chain two long, so the chain is every word before the first one beginning with `-`. It is cargo's contract rather than a list of driver names, and it holds at any depth.

`tools/twice-compiled/src/lib.rs` — `Invocation::Unplaced(Unplaceable)`: a keyed compilation whose arguments do not hold exactly one free-standing input leaves the units entirely, carrying the crate name and THE WORDS it found where one path should be. `Refusal::JobRanCompilationsThisReaderCannotPlace` refuses over it and prints them, so the repair is in the refusal rather than in a megabyte of records.

`tools/twice-compiled/src/lib.rs` — `Unit::driver`, the program the recorder ran. Measured to split nothing on a real census and kept for the reason the fields beside it are given, documented as that rather than as a repair.

`tools/twice-compiled/src/lib.rs` — `JobLog::by_origin` / `fetched`, `Census::by_origin` / `unplaced`, `Cost::absorb`, and `Delta::origins` / `unplaced` so a comparison says WHOSE code its difference is in. `side_by_side` builds both breakdown pairs, because "how are two of these held together" must not have a second answer that fills the gaps differently.
`tools/twice-compiled/src/main.rs` — the per-job split and the totals it is a share of, plus the not-placed lines. `compare` has no workflow to refuse against, so what it owes is the line.

`tools/twice-compiled/tests/law.rs`, `tests/entrances.rs`, `tests/this_repository.rs` — 13 new tests, including the control that tells the rule from a substring search (a crate of ours called `registry`), both directions the flag list can be wrong in, and the live-file joining: the trees this workflow caches under a cargo home are exactly the two `Origin` calls fetched.

`tools/twice-compiled/injection-sweep.json` — 10 new injections, one per mechanism: the chain, the package shape, the exactly-one rule, the refusal, the split counting compilations rather than rows, the driver, the rows only one census had, and the three readings that live in `main.rs`.
verification_bullets: THE MEASUREMENT, on run 31316052015 (nine jobs success, zero annotations): 4095 of 5544 compilations are crates cargo fetched — 73.9% — and 2489.3 of 4169.6 compiler-seconds, 59.7%. Seven of the eight measured jobs restored `~/.cargo/registry` and `~/.cargo/git` on an EXACT hit; the eighth declares no cache. `unrun-tests`, the one job that also caches `target` and restored 27258 MB exactly, still compiled 461 fetched units in 244.9 s.

THE READER CAUGHT ITS OWN GAP AND THE GAP WAS REAL. Its first totals came to 5378 against the ledger's 5531, and the 153 difference was the unplaced count rather than a silent loss. All 153 were `clippy-driver` chains, which the round then read for what they are; the totals now reproduce 5531 and 2707 exactly, and the unplaced count is zero.

THE FIRST SUCCESSFUL CROSS-RUN COMPARISON THIS REPOSITORY HAS RUN. `twice-compiled compare` over runs 31313164921 and 31316052015 — both begun from exact hits, so R1105's law permits the delta — exits 0 over eight comparable jobs: +13 compilations, ALL of them in the checkout (side-workspaces +7, uncompiled-sources +3, unrun-tests +3), which is exactly the `[lib]` target R1108 added. The fetched row of every one of the eight jobs is unchanged to the unit. Without the split, +13 would have had no cause in it.

THE DRIVER EXPECTATION WAS REFUTED BY THE MEASUREMENT BEFORE IT SHIPPED AS A CLAIM. Adding the compiler to the key left the floor of that census at 2707 distinct units, unchanged — so no two records that shared a unit disagreed about their compiler, and neither the MSRV job nor the clippy passes were inflating the duplication this crate reports. The doc comment says the measured thing, not the expected one.

INJECTION: 36 injections, 36 fired, 0 missed, drift 0, control 91 green over 6 targets. One of the ten new ones came back green first time and was the ORACLE's fault, not the suite's: the fixture had no unit compiled twice, so counting rows and counting compilations were the same number and the injection that swaps them changed nothing. The fixture now holds a repeat and asserts that it does.

GATES: `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean on `tools/twice-compiled`; its suite 91 green; the anchor law over all eleven tracked sweeps green (21 tests) after the sweep grew; `mnemosyne-cli validate-workspace` clean.
carry_forward_bullets: A PATH CANNOT SAY IT IS NOT CARGO'S. `Origin` demands cargo's whole layout below the pair that names it, and a crate of this repository's own called `registry` holding a `src/<name>-<version>/` would still read as fetched. Nothing in a path distinguishes those two, and the reader is given no repository to check against — `compare` holds censuses of two commits and has neither. The direction is chosen and the rule is the tightest one a path admits.

THIS INSTRUMENT SAYS WHAT WAS COMPILED AND CANNOT SAY WHAT WOULD HAVE BEEN. That 73.9% of compilations are fetched crates is a measurement; that a compile cache would remove them is not, and no census of what ran can be made to answer it. XX2's second half — WHY a runner recompiles dependencies whose sources it restored exactly — still needs the experiment it has been carried with: a dedicated `CARGO_HOME` and a cold fetch, run twice, which is a thing done to a machine rather than read off one.

THE DRIVER IN THE KEY IS A MACHINE-SPECIFIC STRING, so a census taken on a runner and one taken by a local replay now share no unit at all. That is the cost of keeping what the record says instead of parsing a meaning out of it, and it is affordable only because `compare` is for two runs of the same CI. A comparison of a runner against a replay was never available and is now unavailable for a second reason.

THE COUNTS ARE STABLE ACROSS RUNS AND THE SECONDS ARE NOT. The two runs compared here differ by 13 compilations and by 155.6 seconds of compiler time over an unchanged 5531 of them — runner speed, not work. So a delta in seconds is not readable as a change in what CI does, and every finding this arc has drawn has been drawn from the counts. Pricing a repair still needs the seconds, and they carry that noise into it.

dependencies" was already inside artifacts this repository has been downloading
for a week. What was missing was a reader. `twice_compiled::read` parsed the
crate name, the fingerprint, the emit list and the crate types, and dropped the
path on the floor.

SO A UNIT NOW SAYS WHOSE SOURCE IT WAS, and the reading is off CARGO'S LAYOUT
rather than off this workflow: `registry/src/<index>/<name>-<version>` is where
cargo unpacks a fetched crate whether anything caches it or not, and `compare`
— which holds two censuses that may be of two different commits — has no
workflow to consult. What makes that reading ANSWERABLE about a cache is a
separate joining, and it is a test against the live file: the trees this
workflow caches under a cargo home are exactly the two `Origin` calls fetched,
so a third one added tomorrow turns red here instead of quietly compiling into
units the split calls the checkout's.

AND THE NUMBER IS LARGE. Of the 5544 compilations run 31316052015 paid for,
4095 — 73.9% — are crates cargo fetched, and they are 2489.3 of its 4169.6
compiler-seconds, 59.7%. Every one of the seven cached jobs in that run
restored `~/.cargo/registry` and `~/.cargo/git` on an EXACT hit. The cache is
doing what it says: it brings the sources. Nothing brings their compiled form,
and three quarters of what this CI compiles is therefore work a hit did not
spare. That is the ceiling any compile cache would be aimed at, and until now
it was a guess.

THE READER CAUGHT ITS OWN GAP BEFORE THE NUMBER WAS QUOTED. Its first totals
came to 5378 where the ledger's said 5531, and the 153 missing were not lost
silently: a keyed compilation whose arguments do not hold EXACTLY ONE
free-standing input is refused as unplaced rather than guessed at, and the
count of them is printed. All 153 were `clippy-driver`. `cargo clippy` sets
`RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER`, so for every workspace member cargo runs `<recorder>
<clippy-driver> <rustc> <arguments…>` and the record carries TWO program paths
ahead of the first flag — the reader had been reading the second one as a
source file. The repair is cargo's own contract rather than a list of driver
names: a wrapper is handed the next program in the chain, so the chain is every
word before the first one beginning with `-`, at any depth and for a driver
this repository has never heard of.

AND THE OTHER HALF OF THIS ROUND WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT SAID SO. The
record header has always kept the compiler's path, "because the MSRV job runs a
different `rustc` over the same sources", and the key dropped it — so this
round expected to find MSRV's 324 compilations and the clippy passes merged
into stable's and reported as removable duplication. Adding the driver to the
key left the floor of a real eight-job census at 2707 distinct units, exactly
where it was. Nothing merged. The field stays, for the reason the fields beside
it are given — a cargo release that narrows `-C metadata` must make this reader
split rather than merge — but it is documented as an assumption made explicit,
not a defect repaired.

The strict direction is chosen and named — this instrument exists to find out whether the runner recompiles dependencies, and a rule that guessed generously would answer its own question.

INJECTION: 36 injections, 36 fired, 0 missed, drift 0, control 91 green over 6 targets.
