Round 1126.decision_summary:
THE ONE THING THIS GATE SAYS THAT A SUITE COULD NOT ASK IT WAS THE REPORT, AND
THAT IS WHERE R1125's DEFECT LIVED FOR THREE GREEN RUNS. `render_comparison` has
been the library's since R1096 measured what a decision written in `main.rs`
costs — the whole of what a suite can ask of `main` is an exit code — and the
census report, the surface a person actually reads on every push, was the half
never moved. So the only test able to see whether that report read anything at
all had to REPLAY a job in a worktree of its own and read the words off a
subprocess. A lookup that could never hit shipped in three commits under that.

THE REPORT IS NOW `twice_compiled::render`, WHICH RETURNS A STRING. What it
prints did not change, and the check that it did not is the entrance suite:
those tests run the binary and read its stdout, they were not touched, and they
pass. `main` prints what the library returns and keeps only its exit code.

ONE READER PER DATUM, WHICH IS THE PART THAT WOULD HAVE PREVENTED R1125 RATHER
THAN CAUGHT IT. That round's defect was two readers of one datum drifting apart:
R1122 keyed the census by the record's FILE, took the judge and the budget gate
to the new key, and left the report asking by job. There is now a single
`started_from` — what a restore is reported as, and the only place that lookup
happens — so the law can hold the report against WHAT THAT RETURNS instead of
against a phrase a test spells for itself. An oracle that spells the words is the
oracle R1125 shipped: it asked for `started from`, which `started from: NOT SAID`
contains too, so the suite agreed with the exact output it existed to prevent.

AND A SECOND LAW, BECAUSE A CONSISTENCY LAW CANNOT ASK WHAT THE LINE SAYS. The
first holds the report against `started_from`, so a wording that dropped the
cache from the line would move both sides together and pass. The second asks that
the line carry the cache the restore NAMES and the state in the warmth's OWN
words — both derived from the datum rather than written here — because a job with
two caches has two states, and a sentence that gives one without saying which is
the substitution R1117 split the record to prevent. The third is the control that
makes the first non-vacuous: the same restore, read against a census that no
longer holds its record, must read differently. A reader that never hits prints
the same thing either way, which is what a lookup that cannot hit looks like from
the outside.

THE MOVE ITSELF SURFACED A HAZARD WORTH THE ROUND ON ITS OWN. Both crates export
a `names_its_job` and they answer about DIFFERENT FILES — `<job>.log` in this
one, `<job>.<nickname>.restored` in `restored` — so the unqualified spelling
compiles in the library, resolves to the wrong one, and silently drops every
unreadable record from the only line that names it. Moving the code changed which
name was in scope; nothing but reading the two definitions would have said so.

Round 1127.decision_summary:
THIS GATE'S `main.rs` NAMED A DEFECT IT HAD ALREADY SHIPPED, AND NOTHING COULD
HAVE STOPPED IT SHIPPING AGAIN. Its doc comment says the exit codes are three
answers and not two — `0` the law holds, `1` tests are dark, `2` the gate could
not judge — and that one code for the last two mislabels whichever it did not
mean, "which is the failure R1078 shipped". That sentence is the whole reason
the third code exists, and it was written above a file NOTHING RAN.

MEASURED BEFORE REPAIRED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING. An injection that
turns the refusal path into a clean pass — R1078's defect, put back verbatim —
was run against the suite as it stood. It went SILENT: not one test of the
thirteen changed colour. The other six injections of that sweep all fired, so
the library was guarded the whole time and only the PROGRAM was undefended.
Reading the file would have suggested this; the sweep is what says it.

THE READER IS `tests/entrance.rs`, AND IT IS TREES RATHER THAN CALLS. What
decides a verdict here is the join of two readings — what the tree compiles, and
what CI runs — and both are asked of cargo and git about a real directory, so a
fixture that called functions would be answering a different question. Each case
is a git repository with one dependency-free crate, a stub lister, and a
workflow, and the ONLY thing that varies between them is the cargo command that
workflow issues. Everything else being equal is what makes the exit code
attributable to that one line.

FOUR CASES, BECAUSE THE CODE `2` HAS TWO ROADS. A tree whose CI runs every test
exits 0 and says so; a tree with a test CI filters out exits 1 and NAMES it; a
tree whose CI issues no `cargo test` at all is UNJUDGED rather than clean; and a
directory that is not a cargo tree is the same 2 for the other reason — a hook
runs with the repository root as its working directory and may be this gate
pointed at another tree entirely. A reader shown only the first road would
conclude the code means "CI issues no test command".

THE ORACLES ARE READINGS, THE R1126 DISCIPLINE APPLIED. The refusal is asserted
in the words the type prints for itself, so a rewording moves the assertion with
it; the dark test is named from the constant the fixture is built from; and each
case carries its MIRROR — the clean sentence must NOT appear on the two failing
paths, and the test CI does run must NOT be reported dark, which is what keeps
this from passing for a gate that reports everything.

AND THE NEW READER PAID FOR ITSELF IMMEDIATELY. Two injections that previously
reached only the library tests — the population probe no longer asking for every
feature, and the dark set inverted — now turn the entrance tests red as well. An
end-to-end reader is not a duplicate of the unit ones; it is the only thing that
sees them composed.

found that `tools/unrun-tests` names R1078's defect in its own doc comment above
a `main.rs` nothing ran; this gate's doc comment says the identical thing — the
exit codes are three answers and not two, `0` the law holds, `1` Rust exists
that nothing compiles, `2` the gate could not judge, and one code for the last
two mislabels whichever it did not mean. It was the same story underneath.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, EVEN THOUGH THE ANSWER WAS PREDICTABLE. The injection
that turns this gate's refusal path into a clean pass was run against the suite
as it stood and went SILENT across twenty-five tests, while the eleven
injections aimed at its library all fired. Predicting a silence and measuring
one are different claims, and only the second belongs in a ledger.

THE READER IS `tests/entrance.rs`, AND ITS FIXTURES ARE TREES BECAUSE THE
LIBRARY'S ARE NOT. `tests/gate.rs` reaches every mechanism by calling `examine`
directly, which is the right shape for a mechanism and the wrong one for this:
what the BINARY decides is which answer a whole reading amounts to, and the
pieces of that reading — what git tracks, what cargo compiles, what the lister
declines — are only assembled by `run`. So each case is a git repository the
binary is pointed at, and the cases differ by one file apiece.

FOUR CASES, BECAUSE `2` HAS TWO ROADS HERE TOO. A tree cargo compiles all of
exits 0 and says so; a tracked file no target reads exits 1, is NAMED, and the
tests it hides are listed under it; a tree git holds nothing of is UNJUDGED
rather than clean; and a directory that is not a cargo tree is the same 2 for
the other reason. A reader shown only the third would conclude the code means
"git tracks no Rust".

THE ORACLES ARE READINGS. The refusal is asserted in the words `Refusal`
prints for itself, the orphan is named from the constant the fixture is built
from, and every case carries its mirror — the clean sentence must not appear on
the failing paths, and the file that IS compiled must not be reported, which is
what keeps the finding case from passing for a gate that reports everything.

THE THIRD SIBLING NEEDED NOTHING. `tools/blind-waits` already runs its own
binary through `CARGO_BIN_EXE_`, which is how this round knows where to stop:
the population was three gates printing from `main.rs`, and it is now zero.

Round 1129.decision_summary:
R1128 SAID THE POPULATION WAS EMPTY AND IT WAS NOT. That entry closed with "of
the gates that print a report from `main.rs`, two had no reader and now have
one, the third already ran its own binary" — and the population it named was the
wrong one. The question that matters is not WHO PRINTS from `main.rs`; it is
WHOSE BINARY NOTHING RUNS. Asked that way, `tools/cache-budget` was still in it,
and the check that found it was the one run to close R1128 out. The ledger is
append-only, so this entry is the correction rather than an edit of that one.

WHY IT LOOKED DONE: R1104 MOVED THE WORDS AND LEFT THE CODES. That round put
this gate's report into the library precisely so a suite could read it — the
sentence in `main.rs` says so — which took it off every list of "gates that
print from main". What stayed behind is the DECISION: `2` when a refusal is
`Unreached`, "I could not look", and `1` when the caches themselves break the
law. Half a repair is the hardest kind of debt to see, because the part that was
done is what the eye lands on.

MEASURED SILENT, LIKE THE OTHER TWO. The injection that collapses those two
answers into `1` — R1078's failure, in the third gate to hold it — was run
against the suite as it stood and fired NOTHING across fifty-two tests, while
the thirty-five injections aimed at the library all fired.

`gh` IS STUBBED, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE QUESTION ASKABLE AT ALL. What GitHub
holds for a repository cannot be arranged by a test, and holding it against what
the workflows declare is this gate's entire job — so the stub supplies one side,
the fixture's workflow the other, and the stub prints exactly the rows
`held_caches` parses. The precedent is this repository's own hook smoke test,
which drives `pre-push` against a stub `gh`.

AND THE RUNNER'S VARIABLES ARE REMOVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED ABSENT. This suite
runs on a runner too, where `GITHUB_RUN_ID` is set and would send the gate down
a second reading the stub does not answer for. Green here and red there is the
shape R1119 paid for, and the fixture clears all three variables the binary
reads.

THREE CASES, ONE PER ANSWER, AND THE MIDDLE ONE IS THE POINT. A repository whose
declared cache fits exits 0 and both says so and prints what it read; one over
budget exits 1, because the gate LOOKED and the finding is about the repository;
one whose workflows declare no cache at all exits 2, because an empty answer
there is the reader failing rather than the repository being tidy. The injection
that made the last two the same code turns the third red, and the injection that
made them both `2` turns the second red — both directions of the collapse are
now refused.

Round 1130.decision_summary:
THE ONE SEAM BETWEEN THIS GATE AND THE STORAGE IT JUDGES HAD NO ORACLE OF ANY
KIND, and R1129 wrote that down as its own carry: `gh` is stubbed in every test
here, so what those tests prove is the gate's READING of an answer and not that
GitHub answers in that shape. Why it had none is worth naming exactly. The
answer was flattened by a `--jq` expression before this program ever saw it, and
that expression is a program in a language nothing in this repository can
execute — there is no `jq` on this machine, and `gh` itself needs a network and
a credential. No test could be written against it, so no injection could be
aimed at it, and the expression was free to name fields the API had stopped
sending.

WHAT THE PROJECTION THREW AWAY IS THE ONLY THING IN THE ANSWER THAT CATCHES A
SILENT FAILURE. `.actions_caches[] | "\(.size_in_bytes)\t\(.created_at)\t\(.key)"`
drops `total_count`, which is GitHub's own statement of how many caches the
repository holds. Every other way this read can fail is loud: a row missing a
size does not parse, a body that never arrived is empty. A read that STOPS EARLY
is a well-formed page describing a smaller repository — and smaller is the
direction that PASSES a budget. Measured rather than argued: with the count
check removed, an answer saying the storage holds two caches and carrying the
one that fits makes this gate print `every cache this repository declares is one
it keeps` and exit 0, on a storage half of which it never saw.

AND THE EMPTY ANSWER WAS TWO ANSWERS WEARING ONE FACE. A `gh` that failed
quietly and a repository that genuinely holds no caches both arrived as an empty
stdout, and both were read as a storage of zero bytes. GitHub tells them apart
itself — a repository holding nothing says so IN A PAGE — and the projection
erased the difference on the way in.

SO THE READING MOVED INTO THE LIBRARY AND BECAME TYPED. `Held` deserialises from
GitHub's own field names, which is what makes a renamed `size_in_bytes` a red
test rather than a gate quietly pricing every cache in the repository at
nothing; the fields this gate does not want — `id`, `ref`, `version`,
`last_accessed_at` — are ignored on purpose, because a reader that refused
unknown fields would go red the day GitHub adds one, which is a gate failing for
somebody else's work. `main.rs` keeps two lines and neither of them is a
decision: R1126's rule, and the one R1129 measured the cost of leaving half
applied.

THE FIXTURES ARE RECORDINGS, AND ONE OF THEM IS THE FAILURE ITSELF.
`tests/actions-caches.one-page.json` and `tests/actions-caches.paginated.json`
are what the API printed for this repository, byte for byte — the same eleven
caches the same minute, answered in one page and in four. That the two read to
the same rows is the control for the pagination handling: `gh --paginate` prints
one JSON object PER PAGE rather than one merged document, which is measured here
rather than assumed. The stop-early case is then not invented at all — it is the
FIRST PAGE of that recording, sliced at the byte the parser ends it on, which is
exactly what a `gh` without `--paginate` prints.

AND THE QUESTION IS IN THE LIBRARY TOO, BECAUSE `--paginate` WAS INVISIBLE. A
stub that ignores its arguments answers a gate that stopped asking for the flag
exactly as it answers one that did not, and this repository holds more caches
than one page carries — dropping it reads eleven as three. So the stub records
what it was handed, and the oracle SPELLS THE FLAG OUT rather than comparing the
question against the constant it came from: that comparison agrees with every
edit to the constant, including the one that drops the flag.

THE HALF THAT IS NOT DONE IS WRITTEN DOWN HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE NOTICED.
This gate makes a SECOND `gh` call — `.run_started_at`, for the run window — and
that one is still a projection with no reader, for the reason R1129's carry
gives: clearing `GITHUB_RUN_ID` is what makes these fixtures deterministic and
is also what skips that reading. R1128 is the round that shipped a wrong "the
population is empty", and the lesson it paid for was that the eye lands on the
half that is done.

`tools/cache-budget/src/main.rs` — the `--jq` projection and the tab-separated parsing are gone; `held_caches` is two lines of process plumbing and no decision.
`tools/cache-budget/tests/github.rs` — new: eight laws over two RECORDED real bodies of this repository's own cache storage, including a stop-early answer sliced out of the recording itself.

`tools/cache-budget/tests/entrance.rs` — the stub answers in GitHub's shape and records what it was asked; three new arms — an answer that stops early, one that never arrives, and the question naming every page.
`tools/cache-budget/injection-sweep.json` — five new injections, one per new law, including the two that could not be written while the projection lived in `gh`.
`tools/cache-budget/Cargo.toml` — `serde` and `serde_json`, with the reason the projection they replace could not be tested.
verification_bullets: `tools/cache-budget` sweep: 45 injections, ALL FIRED, missed 0, control 66 passed / 0 failed / 7 targets — five of them new and aimed at this round's reading.

THE FALSE GREEN IS RECORDED RATHER THAN REASONED: with the count check removed, an answer claiming two caches and carrying the one that fits printed `every cache this repository declares is one it keeps` and exited 0 (`target/injection-logs/an-answer-that-stopped-early-is-believed.log`).
THE TWO RECORDINGS AGREE: eleven caches answered in one page and in four read to the same rows, values and all — the control for reading a concatenated stream as one answer.
THE SEAM'S UNTESTABILITY WAS MEASURED TOO: `command -v jq` finds nothing on this machine, which is why no injection could ever have been aimed at the expression this round deleted.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, item-citations (6/6 targets clean) and blind-waits all clean; `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh tools/cache-budget` green, with `--locked` over the lockfile the two new dependencies changed.
carry_forward_bullets: 🔴THE SECOND `gh` CALL IS STILL A PROJECTION AND THAT IS UNDONE WORK, NOT A LIMIT: `run_window` asks for `.run_started_at` through `--jq`, and the entrance clears `GITHUB_RUN_ID` — which is what makes the fixtures deterministic and what skips that whole reading. The next round records a real run body, dispatches the stub on the endpoint asked for, and gives the run window an entrance.

⛳A RECORDING IS FROZEN. These bodies prove the reader handles what GitHub sent on 2026-08-10, not what it will send. What the typed read buys is that a shape change becomes a NAMED refusal at runtime instead of a silent misread; a suite with no network cannot do better than that.

⛳THE COUNT CHECK ERRS TOWARD RED AND THAT IS A CHOICE. A cache saved by another job of the same run between two pages makes the pages disagree, and this refuses rather than guesses — a false red a person reads beats a false green nobody does. This repository answers in one page today, so that path has never run against the real API.

Round 1131.decision_summary:
THE SECOND HALF OF THIS GATE HAD NO READER AT ALL, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER
THAN INFERRED. `tools/cache-budget` asks two questions of GitHub: what caches it
holds, and when the run this gate is inside began. R1130 gave the first a typed
reading and a recorded body. The second was still a `--jq` projection, and the
entrance suite could not reach it for a reason R1129 wrote into its own carry:
clearing `GITHUB_RUN_ID` is what makes a fixture deterministic, and it is ALSO
what skips the whole run window. Applied to R1130's tip, an edit that makes the
binary never look at `GITHUB_RUN_ID` at all — no run, ever, on any runner —
leaves the suite at 66 passed, 0 failed. Nothing in this repository would have
noticed the gate losing half of what it does.

WHAT THAT HALF DECIDES. The run window is where a cache stops being a number and
becomes a verdict: a cache created BEFORE the run began is one `restore-keys`
could have served, and one created after it is a job that rebuilt from nothing —
green, unannotated, and half an hour long, which is the failure this gate was
built for. The window also carries the excuse: a key whose own hashed inputs
moved in this push was legitimately invalidated, and that is git's answer to the
globs the key names, over the range the run covers.

SO THE READING IS TYPED AND THE QUESTION IS WRITTEN DOWN. `run_started_in` reads
`run_started_at` off GitHub's answer and refuses two ways that used to be one: a
body without that field is a READ THAT FAILED and names the field, and a blank
stamp is a refusal that names the RUN. The old projection could not tell them
apart — `--jq` on a body missing the field prints a line, and a reader taking
the printed text as the stamp cannot tell a timestamp from an error page. And a
blank read is not harmless: every cache in the repository was created after the
beginning of time, so a zero start time reports EVERY job as having rebuilt.

`run_query` NAMES THE RUN, AND THAT IS NOW ASSERTED. `runs/{id}` and `runs` are
different resources, and a start time belonging to some other run excuses every
cache built after it. A stub answers a question about a run whichever run it
names, which is precisely how this would go unnoticed — so the fixture's `gh`
records every call it takes, and the case reads the run id back out of the
question.

THE STUB DISPATCHES ON THE ENDPOINT, because the binary now asks twice. One
answer for both is a stub that agrees with a gate asking the wrong endpoint —
the same class of hole as a stub that ignores its arguments. The run it answers
with is a RECORDING of a real run of this repository's CI (`tests/actions-run.json`,
run 31376754536), which is what makes the entrance test's start time arrive in
the spelling GitHub really uses: TO THE SECOND from this endpoint, and to the
fraction from the cache endpoint. `law.rs` proved the comparison survives that
difference; what nothing proved until now is that the difference is real, and a
fixture writing both in one spelling would have agreed with a comparison that
could not survive it.

AND THE FIXTURE HAS A HISTORY NOW, WHICH BOUGHT A THIRD ANSWER. The window diffs
`HEAD~1..HEAD` when the runner names no push range, so a checkout holding ONE
commit cannot answer — `fetch-depth: 1` is a real runner state. The gate refuses
there rather than reading an unanswerable diff as an empty one, because "nothing
changed" is what EXCUSES a key the run rebuilt: reading it that way refuses
every key the commit had every right to move. That wiring, too, had never run.

Round 1132.decision_summary:
THE GATES ANSWER TWO KINDS OF NO AND NOTHING CHECKED THAT THEIR CALLERS TOLD
THEM APART. `1` is "these sites break the law" and `2` is "I could not read
enough of this tree to have an opinion" — the distinction R1078 paid for, and
the one R1127, R1128 and R1129 found unread inside three gates in a row. Those
rounds gave each gate's own exit codes a reader. What they left, and named in
R1129's carry, is the OTHER side of the same seam: an entrance test proves the
PROGRAM, and whether the hook and the side-workspace lister read that program's
answer correctly is a different population — `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/
git_hooks_smoke.rs`, where the exit-2 branch had never run.

FOUR COLLAPSES, ALL MEASURED SILENT AGAINST THE SUITE AS IT STOOD. Making the
hook report an unreadable tree as a blind wait; making it COMMIT one; making the
lister do the first of those; and taking away the lister's own "I was not
started in a tree" code. Each was applied to the tree, and each left all twelve
pre-existing cases green. The one that matters most is the second: a gate with
no verdict is not a gate with nothing to say, and treating `2` as a pass commits
a tree part of which was never read.

THE LEVER IS A FILE THE COMPILER NEVER SEES. Every gate in front of the
blind-wait one formats and compiles what a crate root REACHES, while
`tools/blind-waits` walks the TREE — so a module nothing declares walks past
`cargo fmt`, `clippy` and the citation gate untouched and then cannot be parsed,
which is `Refusal::Unparsed` and exit `2`. That is not a contrivance: it is the
class the gate's coverage report exists to count, and it is the only shape that
reaches the refusal without being stopped by a gate in front of it.

AND THE LISTER'S OWN TWO CODES HAVE NO READER ANYWHERE, WHICH IS SAID OUT LOUD
RATHER THAN REPAIRED BY INVENTION. `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` exits `2`
when it was not started in a tree and `1` when a workspace failed its gate; the
hook and CI both treat any non-zero as a rejection, so the difference survives
only as words on a screen. A distinction with no reader drifts — so the suite is
the reader now, holding both codes with a control that answers the other one.
Giving the hook a second message for a case that means "the hook itself is
broken" would be inventing a consumer; recording what the codes mean, where a
change to them turns something red, is not.

THE SWEEP IS NEW AND SO IS ITS SUBJECT: `.githooks/injection-sweep.json` aims at
SHELL, with a Rust suite as the oracle. The hooks and the lister are 500 lines
that gate everything else in this repository, and the only reason they are
injectable at all is that R899's smoke suite drives the real files over
throwaway repositories rather than copies of them.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/git_hooks_smoke.rs` — three cases: the hook telling a gate that could not read from one that found a defect, the lister doing the same one level down, and the lister's own two codes with a control for each.
`.githooks/injection-sweep.json` — new: four injections over the hook and the lister, oracled by that suite; the first sweep in this repository whose subject is shell.
verification_bullets: MEASURED SILENT: all four collapses left the twelve pre-existing cases green — each injection reddens exactly the case R1132 added, and nothing else.
`.githooks` sweep: 4 injections, ALL FIRED, missed 0, control 14 passed / 0 failed / 1 target.

THE EXIT-2 LEVER WAS ASKED OF THE PROGRAM, not assumed: `blind-waits` over a workspace holding one unattached unparseable file answers `NO VERDICT — 1 file(s) did not parse` and exits 2, while `cargo fmt --check` over the same tree exits 0. The historical trigger the hook's comment names — a workspace with no test code — is exit 0 today and says so in words.
`cargo test -p mnemosyne-cli --test git_hooks_smoke` green, 14 passed in 70 s.

Round 1133.decision_summary:
ONE FIXTURE, ONE CONSTRUCTOR, AND THIS ROUND IS THE HALF-ROUND IT TOOK TO SAY
SO. R1131 gave this suite a `Fixture` with four fields — what the workflow
declares, what each of the two GitHub endpoints answers, and how deep the
checkout's history is — and left the two-argument `tree(caches, answer)` in
front of it as a wrapper over the other two.

TWO CONSTRUCTORS FOR ONE FIXTURE IS NOT A CONVENIENCE. The older one CANNOT NAME
two of the four fields, so the next case that needs a run answer or a shallow
history does not extend it — it grows a third constructor beside it, which is
exactly how a suite ends up with three ways to build one thing and no way to see
what varies between two cases. The house rule for a superseded path is that it
goes in the same change that supersedes it; this one survived by half a round,
and half a repair is the debt this session has spent three rounds naming.

WHAT THE CASES READ LIKE NOW is the argument for it: each one names the field it
cares about and inherits the rest, so `caches: page_claiming(2, …)` and
`commits: 1` are the whole of what makes those two cases different from the
clean one. Nothing about the tree is expressed as a boolean whose meaning a
reader has to go and look up.

THE ORACLE FOR CODE MOTION IS THAT THE SAME LAWS STILL FIRE. The injections all
anchor in `src/`, so a test-side refactor that quietly disconnected a case would
show up as an expectation that stopped being met rather than as a red test — and
the sweep is what says it did not: fifty injections, all fired, none missed.

Round 1134.decision_summary:
THIS ROUND IS A RED CI PAID OFF, AND THE DEFECT WAS A POPULATION FIXED BY
DIRECTORY. `tools/injection-harness/tests/sweeps.rs` holds the law that every
tracked sweep still APPLIES — an anchor is exact text, the source it names
moves, and a sweep that no longer applies looks exactly like one that holds. Its
population was every tracked `.json` under `tools/`, on the argument that sweeps
live there. That argument stopped being true TWICE IN ONE SESSION, in opposite
directions:

- R1130 put three RECORDED API BODIES under `tools/cache-budget/tests/`, and
  this law read them as sweeps and turned main red for holding a fixture. That
  is the failure this entry pays off.
- R1132 put a sweep at `.githooks/injection-sweep.json` — aimed at SHELL, which
  is the text in this repository most likely to move out from under an anchor —
  and NOTHING COULD SEE IT. A law about anchors rotting could not see the sweep
  most likely to rot.

SO THE POPULATION IS NOW EVERY TRACKED `.json` IN THE REPOSITORY, and the
classification is derived from the files rather than from where they sit under
one directory. A file that READS as a manifest is a sweep and its anchors must
apply. One that does not is judged too: if it sits in a directory that already
holds a sweep, or is NAMED like one, it is a sweep that stopped parsing and is
reported — that is the hole a filter would leave, and it is the hole this law
exists to refuse.

THE ONE CLASSIFIER THAT COULD NOT BE USED IS THE OBVIOUS ONE. Two manifests in
`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/` are INPUTS TO TESTS: the trees they name are
materialised by the test that runs them, so their anchors cannot apply to this
checkout. The tempting filter — "a sweep whose files are missing is somebody's
fixture" — is the very question this law asks, so it would reclassify every
ROTTED sweep as a fixture and pass. The classifier is therefore WHERE THE FILE
LIVES: `tests/` is cargo's own word for a directory of test inputs, and no sweep
this repository runs is in one. The other direction is closed by name: a file
called `injection-sweep.json` under `tests/` is refused, so a runnable sweep
cannot walk into the skipped set.

WIDENING IT FOUND THREE THINGS ON THE FIRST RUN, one of them made by this very
round: the harness's own `self-check.json` carried an injection anchored on the
`ls-files` line this round rewrote, so the sweep that proves this law is not
vacuous had come loose as the law was being repaired. It is re-aimed, and the
sweep was RUN: ten injections, all fired.

WHAT LET IT REACH main IS NOT THE RULE BUT MY VERIFICATION. I ran
`scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh tools/cache-budget` — the workspace I had
changed — and the law that broke lives in a DIFFERENT workspace. The gate that
runs all twelve is CI's, and locally it is one argument-free invocation of the
same script. A change that adds a FILE, rather than code, is exactly the shape
whose blast radius is not the workspace it was added to.

Round 1135.decision_summary:
A TRUE FINDING WITH A FALSE SENTENCE INSIDE IT, AND IT TURNED main RED. Run
31394095606 refused `Linux-cargo-side-` as `Recreated`: saved by this run, so the
primary key missed, with nothing the key hashes having moved in this push to
explain it. Every clause of that was accurate. The claim it MAKES was not — this
refusal exists to name a cache that was AVAILABLE AND WASTED, and there was no
archive under that prefix at all.

THE CAUSE CHAIN, READ OFF THE RUN RATHER THAN GUESSED. R1130 changed
`tools/cache-budget/Cargo.lock`, which is one of the globs `side-workspaces`
hashes, so the key moved. The run carrying that change FAILED — at the
side-workspace job itself, R1134's defect — and `actions/cache` does not save
from a failed job, so the new key's archive was never written. No older
generation survived. The next run therefore compiled from an empty tree, and the
gate told main that its rebuild was unexplained.

THE STRUCTURAL REASON IT COULD NOT BE ANSWERED: the range this gate diffs for an
excuse is THIS PUSH (`e0cba16..HEAD`). A key legitimately invalidated in an
EARLIER push has no excuse to offer here, and no commit anybody can make will
give it one. A refusal nobody can act on is one somebody switches off, which is
the R1079 shape this repository keeps refusing to ship.

SO THE CONDITION THE SIBLING REFUSAL STATES OUTRIGHT IS NOW STATED HERE TOO.
`RestoredNothingWithAGenerationHeld` requires a generation that predates the run;
`Recreated` did not, and the two are about the same storage state seen from two
instruments. With nothing restorable, a cold build was unavoidable whatever the
workflow says.

WHAT DROPPING THE REFUSAL DOES NOT DROP. The report still prints the cold state
per owner — the case asserts that, because a repair that removes the evidence
along with the verdict is a hole. And the one ACTIONABLE cause of a whole prefix
being absent is eviction, which is refused by this gate's budget law: a
repository asking for more than its 10 GB is caught there, by the arithmetic,
not by a per-key guess. R1089's real case had demand at 24.78 GB.

FIVE LAW TESTS WENT RED THE MOMENT THE CONDITION WENT IN, AND THE FIXTURES WERE
WRONG. That is the R1103–R1106 rule earning its keep once more: suspect the
fixture first. One of them measured a job restoring 7.4 GB by prefix hit in a
storage the fixture said held nothing — a prefix hit IS an archive being
restored, so that fixture had been describing two incompatible worlds. Each now
holds the generation the refusal is about wasting, and the state without one has
a case of its own.

AND THE FIX WAS REPRODUCED LIVE, NOT ONLY IN FIXTURES: the gate was run against
the real API with the failed run's own id and range, and exits 0 where CI
recorded 1.

Round 1136.decision_summary:
THE HOOK READ GITHUB IN A LANGUAGE ITS OWN SUITE COULD NOT RUN, AND THAT WAS
MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BUILT. `.githooks/pre-push` reports the CI state of
the commit a push builds on, because nothing in this repository could see a red
CI and four consecutive red runs went unnoticed for eleven hours (R890), and
because a conclusion is not the whole of what a run says (R893). It did that with
three `gh -q '<expression>'` calls. `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/
git_hooks_smoke.rs` — the suite that exists to hold the hooks up — stubs `gh`
with lines ALREADY FILTERED, and its own header said what that costs: "a wrong
`--json` field or jq expression in the hook would still pass here".

TWO INJECTIONS, RUN RATHER THAN ARGUED, EACH INTO THE REAL HOOK:

  - `.conclusion` renamed to `.verdict` in the run filter: 14 passed, 0 failed.
    With a real `gh` every conclusion then prints as `-`, which is the string the
    hook substituted for a run that had not concluded, so the red-detection that
    followed can never match. A RED commit reports clean.
  - `annotations_count` renamed to `annotation_count` in the check-run filter: 14
    passed, 0 failed. No annotated check is ever selected, so every commit
    reports "no CI annotations" — the exact blindness R893 added the call to end.

Both fail SILENTLY IN THE DIRECTION THAT READS AS GOOD NEWS, which is the
property R1130 named when it moved `cache-budget` off the same kind of
expression: a read that comes back short is a well-formed answer describing a
healthier repository than the one that exists.

THE REPAIR IS R1130's, APPLIED WHERE R1130 SAID IT WOULD HAVE TO GO. The reading
becomes a program — `tools/ci-state`, a separate workspace like every other gate
under `tools/` — which asks `gh` for RAW JSON and reads it into named fields.
Three recordings of what GitHub actually sent for this repository are the
fixtures, one of them a three-page `--paginate` answer of the same nine checks,
and every drift case is a mutation of one of them that names the drift it models.

ONE ENDPOINT INSTEAD OF TWO, AND IT IS THE PER-COMMIT ONE. `gh run list --limit
20` is a WINDOW: a commit that has fallen off the end of the twenty most recent
runs was indistinguishable from a commit nothing ever ran on, and the hook
printed the second sentence over both. `repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<sha>/
check-runs` is asked ABOUT the commit, carries GitHub's own `total_count` beside
its rows so a short read is loud rather than silent, and names the JOB rather
than the workflow — which is the grain the last two reds in this repository
actually differed at (R1134 was one job of nine, R1135 another).

THE TYPE NEARLY REBUILT THE COLLAPSE IT REPLACED, and the test that names the
drift is what found it. serde treats a DERIVED `Option` FIELD AS OPTIONAL: a body
that stopped carrying `conclusion` deserializes to nine `None`s without
complaint, and this reporter would then print a red commit as one whose checks
have not finished — `(.conclusion // "-")` again, inside a type. `deserialize_with`
is what takes the implicit default away, so a missing key is a named refusal and
only an explicit `null` is a check still running.

THREE ANSWERS WHERE THE PROJECTION HAD TWO. A commit whose checks are still
running is neither red nor clear; the old filter wrote a dash for it and then
asked whether any line ENDED in one of four failing words, so "still running" and
"green" were one answer. `skipped` is deliberately not failing — this
repository's workflow skips a job whose inputs did not change on every green
push, and the recording carries one.

WHAT IS LEFT TO THE HOOK IS CARRIAGE, and its suite now stubs `cargo` where it
used to stub `gh`, because that is the seam the hook still owns: the right
program, a lockfile it may not rewrite, THE COMMIT IT MEANT, and every word the
reporter said passed through. The fixture had to change for the third of those to
be answerable at all — `origin/main` and `HEAD` were the same commit there, so a
hook reporting on the work being PUSHED instead of the work it LANDS ON would
have passed the law unmarked. HEAD now moves past `origin/main` first.

A GATE CAUGHT THIS ROUND'S OWN DEFECT, AND IT IS WORTH WRITING DOWN WHICH ONE.
The hook first spelled the call `--manifest-path "$reporter"`, with the path
assembled on the line above. `locked_resolution_smoke` reads every cargo command
this repository issues and asks which workspace's lockfile each resolves; it
answered `Unreadable` and turned the root suite red. The reason is a real
asymmetry: `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh`'s commands are read off the
LISTER'S OWN EXPANDED OUTPUT, where the shell has already resolved its variables,
while a hook is read STATICALLY, where `$reporter` names nothing. The law already
said what to do — a runtime-assembled path is readable when the literal tail
after the variable carries a directory of its own — so the manifest is now
spelled out in the command. That is the better line anyway: a reader sees which
workspace is being run without following an assignment.

AND THE `-f` GUARD IN FRONT OF THE REPORTER WAS NOT WRITTEN. A reporter that is
not there makes `cargo run` fail, which is a branch that already prints the true
sentence; a separate guard would be a branch nothing in this hook's suite could
reach, since the reporter is resolved from THIS checkout where it always exists.
A branch with no reader is the shape R1127 to R1129 measured three times over.
changes_bullets: `tools/ci-state/` (new workspace) — the reading, as a program: named fields for a check run and an annotation, `total_count` held against the rows that arrived, the answer's own `head_sha` held against the commit it was asked for, and a verdict with four answers (nothing ran / red / still running / clear). `main.rs` keeps only what a suite cannot reach — a process, its status and its two streams — and exits 2 exactly when no report could be produced at all.

`tools/ci-state/tests/` — three RECORDINGS of what GitHub sent for this repository on 2026-08-10 (a commit's nine checks in one page, the same nine in three pages, and the one annotation behind its failing job), the drift laws over them, the report's sentences, and the binary run AS A PROCESS with `gh` stubbed by an otherwise-empty `PATH`.

`.githooks/pre-push` — the three `gh -q` calls and the twenty-run window are gone; it resolves the reporter from ITS OWN checkout, asks it about `origin/main`, and prints a distinct sentence when the reporter itself could not run.

`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/git_hooks_smoke.rs` — the `gh` stub becomes a `cargo` stub that pins the call the hook still owns, and the fixture moves HEAD past `origin/main` so that "which commit" is a question this suite can answer.

    hook substituted for a run that had not concluded, so the red-detection that
    followed can never match. A RED commit reports clean.

    passed, 0 failed. No annotated check is ever selected, so every commit

Both fail SILENTLY IN THE DIRECTION THAT READS AS GOOD NEWS, which is the
property R1130 named when it moved `cache-budget` off the same kind of

healthier repository than the one that exists.

20` is a WINDOW: a commit that has fallen off the end of the twenty most recent

drift is what found it. serde treats a DERIVED `Option` FIELD AS OPTIONAL: a body

Round 1137.decision_summary:
GG1b DID NOT NEED REPEATED RUNS. IT NEEDED A TERM NOBODY HAD COUNTED, AND THE
REPEATS WERE ALREADY PAID FOR.

THE QUESTION AS IT STOOD. Does the `unrun-tests` cache pay for itself? The ledger
carried one subtraction: a warm job compiled 332 units in 194.6 s where a cold one
compiled 1017 in 409.2 s, so the cache saves about 214 s of compiling and costs
134 s of restoring — net about +81 s. A later run made the same subtraction come
out at +27 s, with the whole difference in the restore seconds, and from that it
was concluded that settling it required RUNNING ONE COMMIT REPEATEDLY. That plan
survived four rounds as the next step and was about to consume hosted runs.

TWO THINGS WERE WRONG WITH IT, and both were answerable without a single new run.

FIRST, THE REPEATS EXIST. Every push runs this workflow and GitHub keeps each
run's per-step timings TO THE SECOND, for at least the last 40 runs. The noisy
term is sampled dozens of times over in history. Commissioning runs to measure it
was buying a thing already owned — and the reason nobody had looked is that `gh
run view --json jobs` projects those timings away as `null`, while the REST
endpoint underneath carries them.

SECOND, AND THIS IS THE ROUND: THE SUBTRACTION IS MISSING THE SAVE.
`actions/cache` writes the archive back whenever the primary key missed, as a
`Post Cache …` step of the same job, and no version of the recorded arithmetic
counts it. This repository moves every cache key on any push that touches a
lockfile or the workflow, which is most of them.

WHAT THE 40 RUNS SAY, per cache, in seconds (n / median):

  every test compiled is one CI runs :: cargo (unrun tests)
      restore  n=27  median=129  max=384   total=3471
      save     n=27  median=101  max=252   total=2001
  … and since R1121 split it in two:
      build directory   restore n=5 median=154   save n=5 median=119
      cargo home        restore n=5 median=3     save n=5 median=11
  whole-run cache overhead across the sample: n=40, median 249 s, TOTAL 12 116 s.

SO THE ARITHMETIC, WITH THE TERM PUT BACK. Against about 214 s of compiling
saved: 214 − 129 − 101 = −16 s on the pre-split figures, and 214 − 154 − 119 − 3 −
11 = −73 s on the split ones. THE CACHE COSTS MORE WALL-CLOCK THAN IT SAVES, and
the missing term is the same size as the entire claimed benefit — several times
the ±27 s of noise that motivated the repeats. A measurement is not made more
precise by repeating it around a term it does not contain.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, said plainly. The 214 s saving is ONE cold/warm
pair, on two different commits, and it is the ledger's number rather than this
program's: what a cache SAVED is compile seconds that did not happen, which no
timing of a run that used it can contain. The cost side is now 40 runs deep; the
saving side is still one pair. What has changed is which side the uncertainty is
on, and that the sign no longer depends on the noisy term at all.

THE PROGRAM IS PERMANENT ON PURPOSE. R1124 deleted a five-round-old "owner
decision" after re-deriving it, and named the cause: the ledger had kept the
NUMBER and not the DERIVATION, so nobody could tell whether it had gone stale.
`tools/cache-price` is that derivation as something runnable — the next time this
question is asked, it is a command rather than an argument.

THIS ROUND CLOSES THE CI ARC, BY THE OWNER'S WORD AND WITH A COUNT BEHIND IT.
The last forty-seven commits carry the scope `(ci)` without a break, and their
centre of gravity was cache economics: R1107 to R1125 built the instruments, R1126
to R1133 found three gates whose own exit codes nothing read, R1134 to R1136
repaired the population of a law, a cache refusal and the hook's reading of
GitHub. Some of that is north-star work — whether a gate FIRES, and whether its
answer has a reader, is the substrate an AI checks itself against. Cache
economics is not: it is build-farm cost. It kept regenerating as "an owner
decision" because the question had no runnable derivation, and it now has one and
a sign. The next arc leaves CI.

AND THE RECORDINGS TAUGHT TWO LAWS RATHER THAN CONFIRMING THEM. The runs
endpoint's `total_count` is 499 against a three-row page — it counts every run the
workflow ever had, so the neighbouring endpoint's identically-named field cannot
be read by the same law. And a SKIPPED job reports stamps that run BACKWARDS
(`14:01:37` to `14:01:36`), which a midnight carry alone turns into 86 399
seconds; the ceiling that refuses it exists because a recording had it.
changes_bullets: `tools/cache-price/` (new workspace) — what this repository's CI caches cost in wall-clock, read off runs already paid for: typed reading of the workflow-runs and run-jobs endpoints, the restore/save pair as the unit, a clock that states the domain it is correct over, and a spread that reports min/median/max/count rather than a mean, because the subject is how far a term SPREADS.

`tools/cache-price/tests/` — three RECORDINGS (a green run's jobs, the red run before it, and the workflow's own run list), the drift laws over them, the pairing and clock laws, and the binary run AS A PROCESS with `gh` stubbed by an otherwise-empty `PATH`.

`tools/cache-price/injection-sweep.json` — eleven injections, one per distinction, including the one that expresses this round's own subject as code: reading `Post Cache x` as a second restore, which prices a cache at its restore alone and is exactly the arithmetic the ledger carried.
verification_bullets: RUN LIVE AGAINST THE REAL GITHUB API OVER 40 RUNS of `mnemosyne-validate.yml`, which is the measurement this round is: nine caches priced, `unrun tests` at restore n=27 median 129 s max 384 s and save n=27 median 101 s max 252 s, the post-R1121 split pair at restore median 154 s / save median 119 s (build directory) and 3 s / 11 s (cargo home), and a whole-run cache overhead of n=40, median 249 s, total 12 116 s.

`tools/cache-price` suite: 27 passed / 0 failed over 6 targets — 12 reading laws against the recordings, 12 pairing/clock/spread laws, 3 entrance cases that run the BINARY with `gh` stubbed by an otherwise-empty `PATH`. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
`tools/cache-price` sweep: 11 injections, ALL FIRED, missed 0, control 27 passed / 0 failed.

TWO OF THOSE INJECTIONS CAME BACK 0 RED ON THE FIRST SWEEP, AND BOTH WERE HOLES IN THIS ROUND'S OWN ORACLES rather than laws that held. (1) Every bad stamp the clock test used was refused BEFORE the fields were parsed — three carried no `T` and the fourth was caught by the hour bound — so a reader answering `0` for a field it could not read passed untouched; two inputs that actually reach the parse were added. (2) The recording carries `started_at` at BOTH the job and the step level, so renaming it in the body is satisfied by whichever type still requires it, and taking the attribute off `Step` alone stayed green; each type is now asked by itself, with an explicit-null control. The sweep is 11/11 only after both.

THE FIRST INJECTION IS THIS ROUND'S SUBJECT AS CODE: reading `Post Cache x` as a second restore — the prefixes overlap — prices a cache at its restore alone, which is precisely the arithmetic the ledger carried. It reddens nine cases.
carry_forward_bullets: ⛳THE SAVING SIDE IS STILL ONE PAIR. The 214 s figure is a single cold/warm observation across two different commits, and it lives in the ledger rather than in any program. Joining it would mean reading each run's compile census out of its LOG, which is neither structured nor kept forever — so what this round changed is that the uncertainty now sits on the side the sign does not depend on.

⛳THE OVERHEAD SAMPLE MIXES TWO POPULATIONS and does not separate them: a run whose key HIT pays a restore and no save, a run whose key MISSED pays both. The medians here are over both, which is the right number for "what does a cache cost this repository per run" and the wrong one for "what does it cost when it misses". The data to split it is in the same bodies; nothing here does it yet.

⛳WHETHER THE SAVE IS ON THE CRITICAL PATH IS NOT ASSERTED. `Post Cache` runs after the job's work, so it extends that job's wall-clock, and `unrun-tests` is the busiest job — but this program prices steps, not the run's critical path, and reading one from the other needs the job graph.

⛳THE RECORDINGS ARE FROZEN, as `tools/ci-state`'s are: they prove what GitHub sent on 2026-08-10 and 2026-08-11. Typed reading buys a NAMED REFUSAL the day the shape moves, not a suite that predicts it.

⛳THIS PROGRAM JUDGES NOTHING. It has no exit 1 and no threshold, deliberately — the decision it feeds is the owner's, and a gate that failed CI on a cache being expensive would be a gate nobody could act on from a commit.

Round 1139 measured one sweep's whole red set — 41 reds where a run scoped to a single crate had shown 29 — and wrote what it found into the manifest's prose. Prose decays without saying so. Delete one of the twelve tests that scope could not see, add a guard, or run the same manifest narrow again, and the sweep says something different while the sentence beside it goes on claiming the old number. This round makes the claim data.

`red_set` is a manifest field with two values, and the point of it is that A SWEEP ANSWERS TWO DIFFERENT QUESTIONS WITH ONE SET OF RUNS. `at-least` is the default and is what every manifest meant before the field existed: `expect_red` names tests that MUST go red and says nothing about the rest, which is the only honest reading for a sweep whose whole red set nobody has measured — fourteen of the fifteen this repository tracks. `exhaustive` says `expect_red` names the WHOLE set, so a red the manifest does not name fails the sweep instead of being counted beside it. One manifest claims it: the frame-view contract sweep, which now carries all 41 names Round 1139 recorded.

WHAT THAT BUYS BEYOND A PINNED NUMBER IS THAT MIS-SCOPING BECOMES SELF-DETECTING, with no rule about packages or directories anywhere in it. Run an exhaustive manifest narrower than it was measured and the reds it can no longer reach come back as `missed`; run it wider, or run it after somebody adds a guard, and the new ones come back as reds nobody described. The failure Round 1138 shipped — a red set of one, read off a run that could not have seen the edited crate's own suite — is loud in both directions from here, and a subset claim is silent in both.

THAT IS ALSO THE ANSWER TO THE LAW ROUND 1139 COULD NOT WRITE. Its carry named a rule that would flag a sweep whose test command does not run the package it edits, and measured that such a rule would be wrong about at least one tracked manifest: the harness's own `self-check.json` edits a manifest under another tool's directory ON PURPOSE, because that file is an INPUT to the law under test rather than a read whose guards are being counted. The fact that tells the two apart is what the manifest CLAIMS its red set to be, and that is now a field rather than a sentence.

AND THE CLAIM HAS ONE SHAPE THAT CANNOT BE TRUE, refused at read time rather than after the suites: exhaustive over an EMPTY expectation. Under the weaker claim an empty `expect_red` is honest and documented — an exploratory sweep says what went red and judges nothing — but under this one it asserts that breaking the read changes nothing, which is the single outcome a sweep exists to DETECT rather than to declare. The refusal is the same trade the dry-run pre-flight makes, and for the same measured reason: the sweep this claim was built for is 85 minutes of suites, and a claim that cannot be true should not cost them.

AND THE FIELD OPENED A HOLE THE SAME CHANGE CLOSED. Every optional key is one a manifest may simply not carry, so a misspelled `red-set` would read as absent: the sweep would run under the weaker claim while its author read their own spelling and believed the stronger one — silent in the direction that looks like a pass. `deny_unknown_fields` on all three manifest types turns an unknown key into a named refusal, which meant declaring `_`, the header prose every manifest already carries, as a field. Round 1141 — a scoped run says what it d.decision_summary:
A live consumer runs this gate over five workspaces, pays 108.9 seconds for it, and therefore runs the binding axis on push instead of on commit — so violations arrive in batches nobody can attribute to a commit, twice in two days. They asked for two things. This round closes both, and the second one only because the owner asked why it had been left.

4-B IS A RUN SCOPED TO THE FILES A COMMIT TOUCHED, and the hard half is not the scoping. `validate-code-refs --paths <file>...` narrows the READ SET by intersection with the configured paths, never widens it, because the law it has to keep is an EQUALITY: a scoped run's answer about the named files is exactly the whole run's answer restricted to those files, same violations at the same lines. A path outside the configured paths is therefore not judged at all — judging it would make the scoped mode a second gate wearing the first one's name, greening what the other rejects. It is reported instead, and a requested path gets one of three answers rather than a silence: `matched_files` is what this run judged, `out_of_read_set` is on disk and covered by no configured path, `not_found` is a typo or a file the commit deleted. A hook hands over every changed file; those are three different pieces of news and only the first is about the file's contents.

THE SECOND LAW GENERALISED PAST THE REQUEST. The spec-side axes ask whether a store claim has a witness ANYWHERE, so a partial read set answers them wrong, and they are reported as not judged. Writing that report showed the same silence was already shipping in three other modes, all of them printing `0`: `--filter-id` judges the decay axis alone and published twelve zeros, `decay` itself is judged only when a caller names an id and published a zero on every ordinary run, and the four opt-in axes published zeros whenever their severity was unset. Zero is what a judged-and-clean axis prints. So the rule is now one rule everywhere — A COUNT IS PUBLISHED ONLY WHERE A MEASUREMENT HAPPENED, `null` otherwise, with the axis named and a machine-readable reason beside it. A consumer reading `impl_missing_count == 0` was reading "your tree is clean" off a run that never looked.

THAT REQUIRED THE AXIS TO BECOME A VALUE. `AuditAxis` owns the thirteen kind tags — `CodeRefViolation::kind_tag` delegates to it, so a violation and a verdict about its axis cannot be two names — plus which half of the audit it belongs to and whether it is opt-in. One map of verdicts is built per run; the scan takes EVERY one of its skips by asking that map rather than by re-deriving `filter_id.is_none() && severity.is_some()` beside the code it guards, and the report prints `not_judged` from the same map. One decision, two readers, which is the shape this project requires of a datum with more than one writer. The run also checks itself: if an axis the map called unjudged emitted anything, the command fails rather than publishing a report that reads consistent. A self-review found the last borrowed zero hiding in the REJECTION MESSAGE — the one line a consumer is guaranteed to read announced `BindingUnbacked=0` while scoped — and it now says `binding_unbacked=not judged`.

4-A IS ONE PARSE PER FILE, AND IT WAS ALMOST DEFERRED ON A REASON THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE INSPECTION. The plan was to ship 4-B and defer 4-A because its payoff is calls divided by distinct files touched and nobody had that ratio. Three things were wrong with that. The payoff decides HOW MUCH the change buys, not whether it is right — the consumer said as much themselves. The deferred work contained a defect this very round had written down as a correctness problem: the resolver took a path and read the file AGAIN, while the caller was holding the bytes it had extracted the citations from, so two reads of one file could disagree and the symbol answer would be about a file the citation was never in. And "we cannot measure it here" was false: the timing cannot be measured in a tree with no resolver configured, but the RATIO is a count over the store and the citation list, and counting needs no clock.

SO THE TRAIT IS REPLACED RATHER THAN EXTENDED (no `_vN`, no legacy carry): `resolve_symbols_at(file, source, &[u32]) -> BTreeMap<u32, String>`. A line list, so the caller — which already groups citations by file, because that is how it reads them — asks once per file. The SOURCE, so nothing in a plugin touches the disk; each plugin's tests pin that by resolving against a path that does not exist, which is the oracle for "the answer came from these bytes". And the tree-sitter query, which was recompiled PER CITATION alongside the per-citation parse in both plugins — the half of the cost the consumer's report did not name — is compiled once per process. Both call sites, both plugins, both transport stubs and every test moved in the same change.

AND THE RATIO IS NOW A NUMBER THE CONSUMER'S NEXT RUN PRINTS. The Round 855 symbol census reports `N citation(s) over F file(s) reach a resolver — F call(s)`: N was the old call count and the old parse count, F is the new one, and N/F is the payoff. It is counted from `symbol_expectation`, the SAME predicate the scan judges by, so the census cannot price something other than what the gate asks for; a test holds the prediction against what a counting resolver actually received. It prints whether or not a resolver is configured, which is what makes it answerable in the tree that hosts this gate.

ONE THING THEY EXPLICITLY DID NOT ASK FOR IS ALSO CLOSED. Their side note reported that a generated ledger drifted from its source document — a heading changed in the document, the store kept the old title, every validator green because the store was consistent with itself — and that no update path was visible from the CLI surface. The setters existed. What did not exist was any mention of them WHERE A CALLER IS STANDING WHEN THEY NEED ONE: `import-sections` refused a divergent section with "supersede + re-create to revise", which is the answer for a changed DECISION and not for a changed source. The refusal now names both ways forward. A surface a consumer cannot find is a surface they do not have.
changes_bullets: `validate-code-refs --paths <file>...` (variadic, repeatable, refuses an empty list): `PathScope` narrows the read set by intersection with the configured paths and never widens it; `PathScopeCoverage` classifies every requested path as matched / out_of_read_set / not_found and reports `read_set_total`, so the narrowing is a number and an unread file is named rather than silent.

`AuditAxis` (13 axes) + `AuditSide` (citation-side decidable from one file plus the store, spec-side needs the whole tree) + `NotJudged` (path_scope / decay_filter / no_decay_filter / axis_disabled) + `AxisVerdicts`; `CodeRefViolation::axis()` is exhaustive over both enums and `kind_tag()` delegates to it, so a new violation shape cannot be added without deciding whether a scoped run can judge it.

Every skip in `SetEqualityValidator::scan` asks the verdict map instead of re-deriving its condition; `read_set()` is the one place a run decides what it reads, and the scan, the citation index, the proposal path and the symbol census all go through it. A count is published only where a measurement happened (`null` otherwise) in the JSON, the summary line AND the rejection message; `not_judged` names each unjudged axis with a machine reason and a sentence; the run fails if an axis reported unjudged emitted a violation.

`SymbolResolver::resolve_symbols_at(file, source, &[u32]) -> BTreeMap<u32, String>` replaces `resolve_symbol_at(file, line)`: one call per file over the caller's own bytes, with the tree-sitter query compiled once per process instead of once per citation. Both plugins, both call sites, both transport stubs and their tests move in the same change; each plugin pins "the answer came from the passed bytes" by resolving against a path that does not exist.

`SymbolAxisCoverage` gains `checked_citations` / `checked_files` — the axis's price, counted from `symbol_expectation` (the same predicate the scan judges by) and printed whether or not a resolver is configured, because the tree hosting this gate configures none and could never have timed it.

`comment_mode_coverage` and `scan_id_citations` take the run's read set instead of re-walking the configured paths, so a scoped run's coverage report describes what it judged; `import-sections`' divergent refusal now names both ways forward (supersede + re-create for a changed decision, `set-section-title` / `-parent-doc` / `-parent-section` for a changed source).
verification_bullets: Nine laws written RED before the surfaces existed: six for the path scope (equality against the whole run, the unjudged axes named with null counts, the three answers a requested path can get, the exit code a commit hook rests on, the human report, the refused empty scope) and three in the library (the axis table is one name space, a scope normalizes what a caller hands it, judged / unread / absent are told apart). One of the six passed before the flag existed — for the wrong reason, `unknown flag` — and its oracle was tightened until it went red too.

Five more for one-parse-per-file: a file with three checked citations is put to the resolver ONCE with all three lines; the batched answer equals the per-line answers exactly (in C++ across BOTH resolution paths); the source handed over is the file's own bytes; and each plugin resolves against a path THAT DOES NOT EXIST, which is the oracle for the answer coming from those bytes rather than from a second read.

The census equals the demand: a counting resolver's recorded calls and lines match `checked_citations` / `checked_files` exactly, and the fixture discriminates — a bound citation whose section records no symbol is judged and is NOT a resolver call, so a census counting `cited and bound` would say five where the gate asks four.

Whole workspace, final tree: 1858 passed / 0 failed / 159 targets (the injection harness's control run). `cargo fmt --all --check` exit 0 and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` exit 0, both measured without a pipe after Round 1139 read `tail`'s exit code for clippy's.

Measured on this tree: `validate-code-refs` 0.70 s whole, 0.15 s for `--paths` over two files. The saving here is reads and extraction, NOT parses — this workspace configures no symbol resolver, which is exactly why the census reports the axis's price as a count instead of a duration.

NOT YET MEASURED: the injection sweep (`crates/mnemosyne-cli/sweeps/citation-path-scope.sweep.json`, ten injections over the whole workspace) has run its CONTROL and no injection. It ships claiming `at-least` rather than `exhaustive` for that reason, and its red sets are the author's predictions until a full run replaces them.
carry_forward_bullets: A scoped run still WALKS the whole tree — five times, one per read-set derivation — and reads and parses only the scoped files. The consumer's resolver-off measurement (0.66 s over five workspaces) is the upper bound on what that walk costs. Collapsing the five walks into one is the same neighbourhood as 4-A and was not done here.

The payoff RATIO is now derivable but still unmeasured on the tree that has it: this workspace configures no symbol resolver, so its own census prints the price of an axis it never pays. The number that decides what 4-A bought is theirs to print on their next run.

The consumer's §4-A says 118 seconds where their own table sums to 108.86; unresolved, and stated to them rather than smoothed over. Their 18.7 ms per citation is a LOWER bound, since it divides by an upper bound on calls — the census's N is the actual divisor from here on.

`AuditAxis::all()` walks a `next()` chain, so a new variant cannot compile without being given a place in the order; a variant added as the new end that nothing points at would be unreachable, and only the tests here would notice.

The reply document (`claudedocs/sce-lift-request-4b-reply.md`) is written and NOT delivered — routing is the owner's, and delivery is judged by the banner on their document rather than by a file in this tree.

Our own pre-commit still runs the whole-tree gate rather than `--paths` on the staged files: 0.70 s here, and scoping it would drop the spec-side axes from our commit gate to buy nothing. A decision, not an omission.

Round 1143.decision_summary: R1143 (BUILD) — the argument `--paths` is handed is now law, not just code. STAR ROUND 1141 PINNED WHAT THE MODE MEANS AND NOTHING ABOUT WHAT IT TAKES. Six laws state the semantics — the scoped answer equals the whole run's answer restricted to those files, and the axes it cannot judge are named — and every one of them is written against the one spelling this repository types by hand, a plain workspace-relative path. `PathScope::new` has four more branches: an absolute path is stripped to the tree, a `./` prefix is removed, a path outside the tree is refused, an empty string is refused, and one naming the workspace root is refused as "not a narrowing"; `selects` reads a directory as everything under it; the flag itself is variadic, repeatable, and stops at the next `--` flag. All of that is promised to the consumer in a reply document they have not been sent yet, and exactly ONE of those branches had a test — the empty LIST. The rest was code with no reader, on the one surface a hook generates mechanically and a person never types. STAR THE ORACLE IS EQUALITY BETWEEN SPELLINGS, NOT ACCEPTANCE. A run handed `./src/a.rs` that quietly matched nothing would also "accept" it, exit 0, print an empty violation list and a clean report — which is the exact failure this whole mode exists to prevent, arriving through the argument instead of through the axis. So each spelling of one file must produce the SAME answer as the plain one (matched files and violations both), and the control is required to be non-empty first: one file judged, one violation found, so an equal answer is equal to something. STAR AND THE READING THAT SENT ME LOOKING WAS WRONG, which is the round's own lesson. I predicted from the source that `--paths .` would be accepted and select nothing — `strip_prefix("./")` looked like it could not match a bare `.`, leaving a scope that matches no file and reports a clean tree. The test says otherwise: Rust's `Path::strip_prefix` compares COMPONENTS, `.` and `./` are the same one component, and both are refused by the root rule with the message naming the spelling. The hole I went to fix was not there, and only running it could say so. STAR SEVEN LAWS, ALL GREEN ON FIRST WRITE, WHICH IS THE HONEST RESULT: no defect was found in this surface. What changed is that the surface can no longer drift in silence — every promise in section 1 of the reply now has something that fails when it stops being true, including the two that compose (`--filter-id` picks the axis, `--paths` picks the files, and they are applied at different places so neither implies the other) and the three packed into one sentence about the flag being variadic, repeatable and non-greedy. The non-greedy half is what makes the variadic half safe: a greedy list swallows `--severity-missing` and its value, and the run is then scoped to two paths that are not files under severities that were never applied.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/path_scope_arguments.rs` — seven laws over the strings a hook produces: one file spelled three ways gives one answer; a directory is everything under it (and the configured root of the read set answers exactly what the unscoped run answers); a path outside the tree is refused naming both it and the tree; a scope that narrows nothing is refused in every spelling (`.`, `./`, the absolute root); an empty argument is refused as an argument rather than as a missing value; the flag is variadic, repeatable and stops at the next flag; and `--filter-id` with `--paths` narrows the axis and the files independently.
No production code changed. Every branch these laws cover already behaved correctly — this round is the reader they did not have.
verification_bullets: 7 tests pass in `path_scope_arguments`, all green on first write. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` exits 0 (an `unwrap_or_else` with a constant was the one thing it caught, and it was mine). `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

STAR THE REFUSAL ORACLES WERE TIGHTENED AFTER THEY FIRST PASSED. Each asserted only that stderr mentioned `--paths`, which every refusal from this flag family satisfies — including ones for the wrong reason. They now assert the SENTENCE (`names the workspace root, which is not a narrowing`, `is outside the workspace`, `was given an empty path`) and that the message quotes what it was handed. The first version would have gone green on a run refusing `.` because the flag was unknown.

NON-VACUITY OF THE EQUALITY LAWS is carried by their controls: the plain spelling is asserted to judge exactly one named file and to find exactly one violation in it BEFORE any other spelling is compared to it.

MEASURED, not read: `--paths .` and `--paths ./` are both refused with `names the workspace root, which is not a narrowing`, contradicting this round's own source-reading, which had `.` accepted and matching nothing.

Round 1144.decision_summary: R1144 (BUILD) — a symbol-level claim with nothing to check it now stops the run, and this tree states why it configures no resolver. STAR THE DEBT SAID "OUR DOGFOOD NEVER EXERCISES THE SYMBOL AXIS" AND THE OBVIOUS CLOSURE WAS WRONG. Configuring `[plugins.symbol_resolver.rust]` and recording symbols on the five bound files is what that debt asked for, and the tool answered before the config was a minute old: `propose-implementations` reports 7 (section, file) pairs and 7 UNRESOLVED cites. Every `§<id>` citation in this repository sits in a module-level doc comment, because a section here describes a module rather than a function. No citation is inside an item, the symbol axis therefore has an empty population, and a configured resolver would never be called once — config that looks like it works, which is the Round 860 shape this repository already refuses elsewhere. The toml edit was reverted and replaced by the measurement and its reason. STAR AND THE REAL HOLE WAS THE OTHER DIRECTION. A store that records a symbol for a language no `[plugins.symbol_resolver.<lang>]` entry covers has made a claim nobody checks, and until this round the run said nothing and exited 0. Round 855 settled that shape one step out — a resolver entry that cannot be BUILT is a config error rather than a warning, because `severity_binding = reject` reads as symbol-level enforcement while the run performs none. A symbol recorded for an uncovered language is the same sentence with the halves swapped, and it is the state a consumer reaches by following their own cost measurement: SCE priced this axis by deleting their resolver blocks and re-running, which left every symbol binding in their store unchecked and every run green in 0.66 seconds. STAR TWO ANSWERS, DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT SHAPES. Round 1142's verdict is a fact about the RUN'S CONFIGURATION — `no_resolver` when the map is empty — chosen over the more precise data-dependent form so the axis does not appear and disappear from a consumer's `not_judged` list as sections are edited. This round's refusal is a fact about THE STORE AND THE CONFIG TOGETHER, and incoherence between the two is exactly what a gate is for. Neither subsumes the other: a tree with no claims and no resolver is reported and not refused, and that is this repository. STAR THE REFUSAL IS DOWNSTREAM OF THE REPORT, which the first implementation got wrong. Bailing beside the census killed the JSON document, and three laws written the hour before failed with "stdout is not json" — a consumer's gate parses this command's output, and answering a diagnosis with a parse error is worse than the silence being fixed. It now joins `reject_msgs` with every other refusal this command makes, so the report prints and then the run fails. STAR THE BOUNDARY IS A LAW, not a comment: an unreached language that CLAIMS NOTHING costs nothing. `unresolved_languages` counts FILES and always has (Round 855's advisory); `unchecked_citations` counts CLAIMS, and only the second is a defect. Widen the refusal from one to the other and every adopter with a second language in the tree is refused for prose they never wrote.

`mnemosyne-cli` — that count joins `reject_msgs`, naming how many claims are unchecked and which `[plugins.symbol_resolver.<lang>]` entries would check them. Not severity-gated (no severity turns this axis off, so no knob could mean "unchecked claims are acceptable") and not in decay mode (`--filter-id` judges one axis by design).

`mnemosyne.toml` — the measurement that says why this tree configures no resolver: 7 (section, file) pairs, 7 unresolved cites, every citation module-level. Replaces the resolver block this round first added and then withdrew.

Round 1145.decision_summary: R1145 (BUILD) — the sweep ran, and fifteen of sixteen injections proved their laws are not vacuous; the sixteenth proved a claim this session had already written into the ledger was false. STAR WHAT WAS SPENT AND WHAT IT BOUGHT. Three hours thirty minutes of whole-workspace suites: one control (1870 passed, 0 failed, 161 targets, drift 0 against the same numbers `verify.sh` measured independently an hour earlier) and sixteen injections, each editing one read and running everything. Every `expect_red` in the manifest is now what that run REPORTED rather than what the author expected, and fifteen of the sixteen came back with `missed` empty. The laws of Rounds 1141, 1142, 1143 and 1144 hold and CAN BREAK, which are two different statements and only the second needed a machine. STAR THE SIXTEENTH IS THE ROUND. `the-wire-hands-rust-the-other-languages-resolver` gives the `rust` key the C++ resolver and reddens NOTHING — all 1870 tests green, no compile error, the injection applied and the suite ran. Round 1142's entry says the config-to-plugin wire, which had carried no test at all, now has a reader. That is measured FALSE. Round 1146.decision_summary: R1146 (DEBT) — the fixture that could not tell two resolvers apart now can, and the injection that reddened nothing reddens two tests. STAR ROUND 1145 MEASURED A CLAIM OF MINE FALSE AND THIS IS THE REPAIR. Round 1142 wrote that the config-to-plugin wire finally had a reader; Round 1145's sweep gave the `rust` key the C++ resolver and 1870 tests stayed green. The ledger is append-only, so that sentence stands where it is and this entry is its correction. STAR A MISMATCH-ONLY FIXTURE CANNOT NAME WHICH RESOLVER RAN, and that is a fact about the shape rather than about this particular spelling. The old tree had one citation, inside `fn alpha`, with the store recording `beta`. Every possible answer — `alpha`, some other name, or nothing at all — leaves `beta` unmatched, so the violation count is 1 in each case and the assertion holds while the wrong plugin runs. There was no assertion that could have failed, because the found symbol is not on the wire: a `symbol_mismatch` violation carries file, line and section id and never the name that was resolved. STAR SO THE FIXTURE GOT A SECOND SITE, and the two together triangulate. `src/drift.rs` records `beta` for a method the Rust grammar calls `alpha` — one violation, expected. `src/matched.rs` records `gamma` for a method the Rust grammar calls `gamma` — clean, and it is the half a wrong resolver cannot fake. A resolver answering NOTHING drops the count to 0; a resolver with a different vocabulary reddens the clean site and raises it to 2. Both are one number away from correct and both fail. STAR AND THE SPELLING WAS THE OTHER HALF. `fn alpha() { … }` at top level is ALSO a valid C++ function definition — return type `fn`, name `alpha` — so the two grammars genuinely agreed and no arrangement of assertions over that text could have separated them. The methods now sit inside `impl` blocks, which C++ cannot read the same way. Round 1096 already wrote this down: the spelling of a fixture is what makes it a control. STAR MEASURED, NOT ARGUED, both directions in one sitting: with the tree as it stands, five tests green and exactly one symbol violation, at `src/drift.rs:5`. With the C++ resolver injected into the `rust` key by hand, `symbol_mismatch_count` is 2 and `src/matched.rs:5` is the second — the clean site reddening, which is the failure mode this fixture was rebuilt to make visible. Restored and green again, byte-identical by `git diff`. The prediction that the resolver might answer NOTHING is the other arm; what the run actually showed is the different-vocabulary arm, and the fixture fails on either.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/symbol_axis_reach.rs` — the fixture is two files instead of one: a drift site whose recorded symbol is not what the Rust grammar answers, and a matched site whose recorded symbol is. Both citations sit inside `impl` block methods, which C++ does not read as the same declaration. Law 2 now asserts exactly one violation AND that the matched file carries none.

The census assertions move with it (two citations over two files), the refusal message count in law 5 moves from one claim to two, and law 3's cpp file gets its own section so it is not a citation of a section that binds another file.
No production code changed. The defect was in the control, not in what it controls.

Restored: `git diff` empty, five tests green, one violation at the drift site.
