Round 1147.decision_summary: R1147 (BUILD) — debug info is now carried by the crates a person debugs, and by nobody else; a clean test build of this workspace went from 11 GB to 3.9 GB. STAR THE MEASUREMENT THAT STARTED IT. `target/debug` had reached 41 GB, and the shape of it was not this workspace: `librocksdb-sys` held EIGHTEEN build directories at 15.00 GB, its rlib four copies at 3.34 GB, and nineteen `grpc_*` test binaries sat at 230.4 MB each. `cargo clean -p librocksdb-sys` reclaimed 18.5 GB and `-p mnemosyne-server` another 7.8 GB — 26.3 GB of duplication across 3,771 files. That reclaim is a one-off; this round is why it accumulated. STAR WHY 230 MB PER TEST BINARY. Every file under a crate's `tests/` is its own crate and its own LINK, so `mnemosyne-server` produces twenty-two of them, and each embeds the full DWARF of RocksDB and the tonic stack. Nobody steps into those. What a panic in this repository points at is a workspace crate, and what a backtrace needs from it is file and line — which is `line-tables-only`, not the type and variable graph. So `[profile.dev.package."*"] debug = 0` for dependencies, `line-tables-only` for the workspace, and `split-debuginfo = "unpacked"`, which on Linux leaves DWARF in the `.o` files instead of copying it into every binary that links them. Nineteen links of one dependency graph is precisely the duplication that copy produces. STAR MEASURED UNDER IDENTICAL CONDITIONS, both directions, because the first comparison I ran was not one: a tree that has built under BOTH profiles holds both sets of artifacts, and it read 25 GB — larger than the baseline, while every individual binary had shrunk. `cargo clean` then `cargo test --workspace --no-run`, twice: the default profile gives 11 GB, `grpc_smoke` at 230.4 MB, 93.84 s; this profile gives 3.9 GB, the same binary at 46.5 MB, 76.03 s. A 65% smaller tree and a 80% smaller binary, and the build got faster rather than slower. STAR WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE. `[profile.release]` is untouched, `debug-assertions` is untouched, and no behaviour moves: 161 suites, 1870 tests, 0 failed under the new profile. What a debugger can see inside a dependency is what changed, and the reclaim measured above is what it was costing.

Round 1148.decision_summary: R1148 (BUILD) — this crate's twenty-two integration test binaries became two, and the one that stayed apart is the round. STAR WHY LINKS AND NOT FILES. Every file under a crate's `tests/` is its own crate and its own LINK, so `mnemosyne-server` produced twenty-two executables that each statically linked the whole RocksDB plus tonic graph. Measured before Round 1147's profile change they were 230.4 MB apiece; after it, 34 MB apiece, and there were still twenty-two — 0.66 GB of one dependency graph written down twenty-two times. Consolidating is `autotests = false` plus one `[[test]]` target whose file loads the others with `#[path]`, so no file moves and each keeps its `#![cfg(feature = "…")]` as a module-level inner attribute. STAR THE CHECK BEFORE THE MOVE ASKED THE WRONG QUESTION AND STILL FOUND NOTHING. Sharing a process makes anything process-global into shared state, so the check looked for `set_current_dir`, `env::set_var` and `env::remove_var` across every test in the workspace. Zero. What it missed: `tracing`'s callsite interest cache is PROCESS-global even though `subscriber::with_default` is thread-local, so a test capturing spans can miss a callsite while another thread installs a dispatcher. STAR AND THE FOUR-THREAD GREEN WAS LUCK. The consolidated suite passed 1870 / 0 at `RUST_TEST_THREADS=4`. Raised to 32 on a machine with 125 GB of RAM — done because the owner asked whether taking 32 threads every time was right, not because anything looked wrong — `handler_span_hierarchy_smoke` failed with `expected gate.evaluate child span, captured: ["test.parent", "audit.append"]`. The span is emitted unconditionally by `handler.rs`; the capture missed it. STAR SO IT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN NAMED A FLAKE. Alone it passed; the whole binary re-run passed; thirty runs with no load passed. Under four spinning cores it failed 2 of 30. The same experiment on the pre-consolidation layout, same load, same thirty: 0. The consolidation is the cause, and the repair — giving that one file its own `[[test]]` target back — measured 0 of 30 and then 0 of 100. Thirty greens were not the argument: at a 7% rate, 0.93^30 is 11%. A hundred is 0.07%. STAR THE REPAIR IS NOT A FILE MOVE, IT IS A LAW. Moving one file back fixes today and nothing else; the next span-capturing test added to `all.rs` brings the flake back. `consolidated_test_isolation.rs` walks every `tests/all.rs` in the workspace, reads each one's own `#[path]` list, and refuses any included file that touches something the process owns — the tracing dispatcher, the working directory, the environment, the global allocator — naming the file, the construct, the mechanism and the repair. A second law pins this case by name, in both directions: the file must not be in the shared binary AND must still have a target of its own, because `autotests = false` means a file with neither is a test nobody runs.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-server/Cargo.toml` — `autotests = false` plus two targets: `all` (twenty-one files) and `handler_span_hierarchy_smoke` (its own process, with the measured reason in the comment).

`crates/mnemosyne-server/tests/all.rs` — the consolidated target. Loads each file with `#[path]` so nothing moves, declares the shared `common` module once, and states in its header which file is deliberately absent and why.
`crates/mnemosyne-server/tests/*.rs` — seven files change `mod common;` to `use crate::common;`, because a `mod` inside a `#[path]`-loaded module resolves against that module's own directory.

`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/consolidated_test_isolation.rs` — two laws: no file in a consolidated target may touch a process-global (walked, not listed, so a second crate consolidating is covered the day it does), and the span-capturing server test is in neither the shared binary nor nowhere.
verification_bullets: STAR THE FLAKE WAS MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, under four spinning cores: consolidated 2 failures in 30, pre-consolidation 0 in 30, repaired 0 in 30 and then 0 in 100. The last number is the one that licenses the word "fixed" — at the measured 7% rate, thirty greens happen 11% of the time by chance and a hundred happen 0.07% of the time.

STAR THE GATE WAS INJECTED, not assumed: putting the file back into `all.rs` reddens BOTH laws, and the message names the file, the construct (`with_default`), the mechanism (process-global callsite interest cache) and the repair (give it its own `[[test]]`). Restored byte-identical, `git diff` empty.

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` exit 0; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

THIS ROUND'S VERIFICATION RAN ON ANOTHER MACHINE because this one could not finish it: the same suite died here after 48 minutes with 14 GB of swap held. That is a fact about the host, and it is recorded because a green from a different machine is a green about that machine.
carry_forward_bullets: THE DENYLIST IS A DENYLIST. `consolidated_test_isolation.rs` names six constructs, each with a mechanism, and the seventh will be found the way the first was — by a test failing. There is no way to ask the compiler whether a test mutates process state, because the property is about what the code reaches at runtime through dependencies the scanning crate cannot see. The honest shape is a list that grows on evidence, and this round is its first entry.

`mnemosyne-cli` STILL HAS SEVENTY-FIVE TEST BINARIES. The same argument applies to them — they are smaller (7.7 MB each against the server's 34 MB) so the disk case is weaker, but the link count is the same shape. Whether to consolidate them is undecided and now has a measured precedent on both sides: the saving is real and so is the isolation cost.

Round 1150.decision_summary: R1150 (DEBT) — Round 1148's consolidation shipped a defect that CI caught and this repository's own verification could not, because the verification never compiled the failing tests. STAR WHAT BROKE. Four `grpc_otlp_*` tests call `init_otlp_tracing_subscriber` or its `_with_config` sibling, and that helper ends in `.try_init()` — the PROCESS-WIDE dispatcher install. A process has one. Folded into a single binary, the first of the four wins it and the rest die with "a global default trace dispatcher has already been set". CI reported three failures rather than four for that reason: the winner passed. STAR WHY THE VERIFICATION WAS BLIND, and this is the part worth keeping. Every one of those files is `#![cfg(feature = "otlp")]`. `cargo test --workspace` without `--all-features` compiles them to NOTHING, so Round 1148's "142 targets, 1872 passed, 0 failed" was true and said nothing about them — a green over code that was never built. CI runs `cargo test -p mnemosyne-server --all-features --locked`, which is why it saw what three machines' worth of local runs did not. A verification whose command differs from the gate's is measuring a different population, and the difference is invisible in its own output. STAR AND THE GATE WRITTEN ONE ROUND EARLIER FELL THROUGH ITS OWN DOCUMENTED HOLE. `consolidated_test_isolation.rs` scans the TEST file's text for `set_global_default`; these files contain no such string, because the install is one hop away in `src/grpc.rs`. Its own header said the denylist cannot see "what the code reaches at runtime, through dependencies this crate does not see" — and the next commit was the demonstration. The repair is to DERIVE the wrappers: the gate now reads the crate's own `src/` for functions whose bodies install a global, and refuses a shared-binary test that merely CALLS one. Textual and one hop deep, which is what a test can do without a compiler; a wrapper calling a wrapper is a stated limit rather than a claim. STAR A SECOND HAND-WRITTEN NUMBER DIED THE SAME WAY. That gate asserted `scanned >= 20` as its non-vacuity floor, and moving four files out legitimately made it 18 — the constant this repository keeps catching in other people's code, written by the author of the gate that catches it. It is replaced by a law that derives its own subject: every `tests/*.rs` in a crate is either included in `all.rs` or declared as its own `[[test]]`, because under `autotests = false` a file that is neither is a test NOBODY RUNS and reads exactly like a passing one.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-server/Cargo.toml` — the four `grpc_otlp_*` tests get their own `[[test]]` targets beside `handler_span_hierarchy_smoke`, with the mechanism recorded: one process, one global dispatcher.

`crates/mnemosyne-server/tests/all.rs` — those four leave the shared binary; the header states both ways this file has been wrong and the two rules that follow (own the process, own the target — directly OR through a helper; and verify with the features CI uses).

`crates/mnemosyne-server/tests/grpc_otlp_{collector_e2e,config_smoke,sampling_zero_smoke}.rs` — back to `mod common;` now that each is a target again, which is where a top-level test crate resolves it from.

`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/consolidated_test_isolation.rs` — the gate derives global-installing function names from the crate's own `src/` and refuses a shared-binary test that calls one; and its `scanned >= 20` floor is replaced by the orphan law (no `tests/*.rs` may be neither included nor declared).
verification_bullets: STAR THE VERIFICATION COMMAND IS NOW CI'S. `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast`: 146 targets, 146 ok, 0 failed, 1881 passed, cargo's own exit 0. Round 1148's green was `--workspace` WITHOUT `--all-features`, which compiled the four failing tests to nothing; the same tree under CI's flags is what caught them.
`cargo test -p mnemosyne-server --all-features --locked` locally: 81 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` exit 0. `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

STAR THE GATE WAS INJECTED BOTH WAYS. Putting a `grpc_otlp_*` file back into `all.rs` reddens the derived-wrapper rule, and the message names the file, the wrapper (`init_otlp_tracing_subscriber`), the mechanism and the repair. Restored byte-identical.

STAR THREE FALSE READINGS WERE PAID FOR ON THE WAY, and each is now a hook rather than a note. A poller announced DONE while 128 targets remained, because its `case` glob matched the literal in its own command (guard rule D). An `ssh … | tail` handed the harness tail's exit status, so a run that printed "2 targets failed" was reported as exit 0 — the Round 1139 trap, twice in one day. And `rsync -a` carried the SENDER's mtimes to the receiver, so cargo skipped the rebuild and ran binaries compiled from bytes no longer on disk: measured, a file stamped 2020-01-01 arrives stamped 2020-01-01 (guard rule E).
carry_forward_bullets: THE DENYLIST GREW BY DERIVATION, NOT BY LISTING, and that is the only reason it now covers this case; the next one will still be found by a test failing rather than by the gate reasoning ahead. A wrapper that calls a wrapper is not followed — one hop is what a text scan can honestly claim.

THE SWEEP MANIFEST IS STILL UNMEASURED AGAINST THIS TREE. Rounds 1146, 1148 and 1150 each changed something a red set depends on (a fixture, the target layout, four more targets). `red_set: exhaustive` waits on one full run of `citation-path-scope.sweep.json`, and the last attempt was abandoned when its harness was found still alive and rewriting the tree under a verification.

Machines are named by their specs from here on, which says more anyway: `a 32-core, 125 GB host` over `pc2`.

Round 1152.decision_summary:
R1152 (BUILD) — The two tree-sitter backends were 290 and 481 lines of which
the overwhelming majority was ONE algorithm written twice: parse the caller's
bytes once, find the declarations, take the smallest whose extent covers each
requested line. Round 1151 published the gap that says three more backends are
coming (`go`, `python`, and a `.kt` row the table does not have), and three more
copies would have made that algorithm the fourth, fifth and sixth transcription
— with every defect then needing to be found five more times. This round moves
the walk into `mnemosyne-plugin-tree-sitter-core` and leaves each language crate
holding only what is actually its own.

FOUR THINGS DIFFER BETWEEN BACKENDS, AND ONLY FOUR: the grammar, the query that
names its declaration nodes, how a name comes out of one of them, and whether a
comment immediately above a declaration counts as documenting it. Those four are
a `LanguageSpec`. The Rust and C++ crates are now that struct plus a `name_of`,
and the next three languages are the same shape rather than the same file again.

THE PORT'S ORACLE IS THE OLD ANSWER, NOT A REVIEW OF THE NEW CODE. Round 1126's
rule for moved code: the pre-port implementation, copied verbatim from HEAD, was
run beside the spec-driven one over a real corpus, every line, and the two must
agree byte for byte. Rust: 313 tracked files, 221787 lines, 187728 answered, 0
disagreements. C++ has no corpus in this repository, so the consumer's tree was
the corpus — 1469 files, 235962 lines, 184074 answered, 0 disagreements. Both
harnesses were deleted in this round; they were an oracle for one move, not a
gate. That equality is what lets the Rust query change shape (from capturing
NAME nodes and climbing to the item, to capturing the item and reading its name
field) without the change being a matter of opinion.

AND THE ENGINE'S OWN TEST FOUND A DEFECT THE PORT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED. The
doc-comment rule asked whether the node at the cited point IS a comment.
`descendant_for_point_range` returns the SMALLEST node covering a point,
anonymous tokens included, and grammars disagree about whether a comment is a
leaf: C++'s `comment` is one, so the question worked; Rust's `line_comment` has
children, so the same question answers `//` and the rule never fires. C++ was
the only backend with the rule switched on, so nothing in the tree could see it
— it looks exactly like a language that chose not to have the rule, which is
precisely what the next three backends would have looked like. The engine now
climbs to the enclosing comment node. Re-measured over the same C++ corpus
because the fix touches that path: 43030 comment lines, 0 where climbing changes
the answer, so the differential above still speaks for the shipped bytes. (14 of
those lines do not land on a comment node at all — text inside a string or
inside a block comment — and both readings answer nothing for them, which is why
the number that matters is the 0 and not the 43016.)

`running 0 tests` WAS THE REASON TO LOOK. The core crate held the whole
algorithm and had no test of its own; the defect above is what was behind that
zero. It now has six laws, and the first of them is the one no language crate
can state: two specs over one grammar, one query and one `name_of`, differing in
NOTHING but `documented_kinds` — and the same line resolves two ways. That
asymmetry is the real difference between the shipped Rust and C++ backends, so
an engine that quietly applied the rule to everything would have changed one of
them with no language test noticing.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-plugin-tree-sitter-core/` — NEW. `LanguageSpec` (grammar, query, `name_of`, `documented_kinds` + `comment_kind`, and the per-PROCESS query cache the language crate owns), `TreesitterResolver` over it, `field_text` for the common name-extraction shape, and `comment_ancestor` — the climb that makes the doc-comment rule work in a grammar whose comment node has children.

`crates/mnemosyne-plugin-tree-sitter-rust/src/lib.rs` — the walk is gone; what remains is `SPEC` (item-capturing query, a `name_of` whose kind filters keep `impl Foo<T>` out of the answer, and an EMPTY `documented_kinds`) plus the same unit laws, two of them new: a doc comment above an item does NOT bind to it here, and a generic `impl` is not named after its type expression.
`crates/mnemosyne-plugin-tree-sitter-cpp/src/lib.rs` — same, keeping the declarator descent and the `DOCUMENTED_KINDS` list that switches the rule ON.

above a declaration, no blank line, documents it. Rust's spec takes no such

the comment a `type_declaration` sibling, so the rule did not fire for by far

wrapper's single spec. A GROUPED declaration still answers NOTHING: a comment
above `type ( First; Second )` documents the group, which has no one name, so

backends meet it again. Pass 2 asks which declaration COVERS a line and needs
the `*_spec`, whose extent is the member; pass 1 asks which declaration a
comment SITS ABOVE and needs the wrapper, which is the sibling. A query written
for one and reused for the other is wrong in a way that only shows up in one of

Round 1154.decision_summary:
R1154 (BUILD) — Python, the second of the three backends SCE named, and the one
that empties the list. `.py` has routed to the language `python` since Round 855
with nothing behind it, which is worse than an omission: Round 1144 made a
recorded symbol for a language no resolver covers a REFUSAL, so a consumer with
a Python runtime could not record symbol-level bindings at all — the run stops —
while `severity_binding = reject` read as symbol-level enforcement over the
file-level binding they were left with. Their tree has the citations: three of
their commits enrol the Python runtime, bind citations no reader could reach,
and move a docstring to where the citation gate reads a comment.

THAT LAST ONE DECIDED THE SPEC. The obvious reading — "Python documents from a
docstring INSIDE the definition, so the doc-comment rule is the wrong
instrument" — is wrong twice over. A docstring is a string expression, not a
comment, so it is not what this rule is about AND not somewhere a citation can
live: the gate reads comments. What a `§` citation in Python actually is, is a
`#` line, and it sits directly above the `def` or `class`. So Python takes the
rule, and `decorated_definition` is listed beside the two definition kinds
because the comment's neighbour is the decorator's wrapper, not the `def` inside
it.

AND THE RULE ITSELF WAS WRONG, IN A WAY TWO LANGUAGES HAD ALREADY HIDDEN. It
asked the comment's next SIBLING what it documents. Inside a Python class body
the `block` node begins at the first STATEMENT, so a leading comment is a child
of the `class_definition` and its next sibling is the block — "not a
declaration" — and every documented method bound to the class. The sibling
assumption had survived two backends: C++ puts the declaration beside the
comment, and Rust switches the rule off. The engine now asks the ROW after the
comment run and climbs from there, which is a question about position rather
than about tree shape.

THE FIRST VERSION OF THAT CLIMB MOVED 151 ANSWERS, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY
THIS ROUND KNOWS. Taking the INNERMOST declaration beginning on the row binds
`// doc` above `struct mobj_s *snext;` to `mobj_s` — the struct being pointed AT
— rather than to the field, and puts a leading macro in place of a class name
(`class SCXML_API Foo`). Taking the OUTERMOST declaration that still begins on
that row moves NONE: over 43095 comment lines of the consumer's C++ corpus, the
new rule and the old agree on all 10109 the old bound, and add 30 the old left
to fall through to an enclosing scope. Zero moved, thirty gained — a strict
superset, which is the only shape in which changing a rule the consumer already
runs is not a migration.

WHAT THE LIST BEING EMPTY CHANGES. `languages_without_backend` has been a
shrinking CLAIM about the build since Round 1151, pinned by an equality each
round edited. Empty, it is the invariant those rounds were walking toward: every
language a file can map to has a resolver, so an extension row added without a
backend fails at the moment it is ADDED. Kotlin is the test of that — `.kt` is
on no row today, and the round that adds the row must bring the backend in the
same change or this contract refuses it.

`crates/mnemosyne-plugin-tree-sitter-core/src/lib.rs` — the doc-comment rule stops walking siblings. It finds the contiguous comment run in the tree (consecutive comments ARE siblings everywhere), then asks the ROW after it and climbs to the OUTERMOST declaration that still begins on that row. The header records why outermost: innermost binds a field's comment to the struct its type points at.
`crates/mnemosyne-plugin-tree-sitter-cpp/src/lib.rs` — one new law for exactly that shape (`struct mobj_s *snext;`), so the 151-answer regression cannot be reintroduced silently.

docstring INSIDE the definition, so the doc-comment rule is the wrong

asked the comment's next SIBLING what it documents. Inside a Python class body
the `block` node begins at the first STATEMENT, so a leading comment is a child

declaration" — and every documented method bound to the class. The sibling
assumption had survived two backends: C++ puts the declaration beside the
comment, and Rust switches the rule off. The engine now asks the ROW after the
comment run and climbs from there, which is a question about position rather

fallen through to the enclosing scope looking exactly like a language that chose

THE GRAMMAR WAS ASKED, NOT GUESSED. A throwaway probe printed the parse of a
representative file, and the answer decided the spec: `class_declaration`,
`function_declaration`, `object_declaration` all carry `name: (identifier)`, and
KDoc is a `block_comment`.

AND KOTLIN SPELLS A CLASS MEMBER AND A LOCAL THE SAME WAY. Both are
`property_declaration`, so the kind alone cannot separate them the way C++'s
`field_declaration` and `declaration` do — and binding a citation to a local

node it cannot name, that one guard covers both passes.

rule the `c` case was an instance of: an extension whose spelling differs from

Round 1156.decision_summary:
R1156 (DEBT) — The push of Rounds 1151 to 1155 turned `origin/main` RED, and the
job that caught it was one nothing before a push had ever run.

WHAT BROKE. `tools/injection-harness/tests/sweeps.rs` asks whether every tracked
injection still APPLIES to the tree it names. An anchor is EXACT TEXT, and two
of the anchors in `citation-path-scope.sweep.json` named source those rounds
rewrote: `the-resolver-goes-back-to-the-disk` pointed at the parse site in the
Rust plugin, which Round 1152 moved into the shared engine, and
`the-wire-hands-rust-the-other-languages-resolver` pointed at the `if / else if`
chain in `main.rs`, which Round 1151 replaced with the backend table. Both now
occur zero times. That is precisely the decay this gate exists for — a sweep
that refuses is a proof nobody is running, and it looks exactly like one that
holds — and re-aiming them is the smaller half of this round.

WHY FIVE GREEN LOCAL RUNS SAID NOTHING, which is the half worth keeping. This
repository has FIFTEEN workspaces. `cargo test --workspace` means the ROOT one;
the others carry their own `[workspace]` precisely so the root gates never
compile them. Their SUITES were run by CI and by nothing else: the pre-commit
hook reaches a separate workspace only when a `.rs` file INSIDE it is STAGED,
and only for the lint half. So the CROSS-WORKSPACE direction had no reader at
all — editing ROOT source can rot a side workspace's test, and that is exactly

Round 1157.decision_summary:
R1157 (DEBT) — Two of the five backends were PORTS and had an oracle that needed
no invention: the old implementation run beside the new over every line of a real
tree. Rust's answered 0 disagreements over 313 files and C++'s 0 over 1469. THE
OTHER THREE HAD NO OLD ANSWER, so Go, Python and Kotlin shipped on unit laws over
hand-written shapes plus one two-site end-to-end fixture each — a sample chosen
by whoever wrote it, which is the population a defect hides outside of. Rounds
1153 and 1154 each found one that way and both were shapes the single-line cases
could not see.

THREE LAWS A CORPUS CAN STATE WITHOUT A PREDECESSOR, each about the engine rather
than a language's vocabulary: batching changes no answer; an answer is text that
occurs in the file it came from; and the reach is a number above a floor derived
from the corpus. The corpus is the consumer's tree — the only real Go, Python and
Kotlin here, and the code these backends were built for. When it is absent the
contract FAILS rather than skipping, because a measurement that quietly stops
measuring reads exactly like one that holds.

MEASURED: go 220 files / 37353 lines / 30213 answered; python 219 / 26428 /
20153; kotlin 689 / 110351 / 97980. Zero batch disagreements and zero answers
absent from their source, in all three.

AND THE FIRST ORACLE WAS BOTH SLOWER AND WEAKER. It asked per line — one parse
per line of 174000 lines, 891 seconds, which is a CI budget this repository does
not have. Replacing it with an INTERLEAVED SPLIT (every line in one call against
odds in one call and evens in another) costs three parses per file, runs in 20.9
seconds, and asks the sharper question: a per-line call has no NEIGHBOURS to be
confused by, so it could not have seen an interleaving defect at all. The two
forms agree on this corpus, and the numbers above are identical under both.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. The laws are about self-consistency and provenance, not
about correctness: a resolver that answered the enclosing class for every line
would pass all three. What pins the vocabulary is still the two-site fixture per
language in `symbol_axis_reach.rs`, where a wrong grammar's answer moves the
count. These laws close the population gap, not the oracle gap.

Round 1158.decision_summary:
R1158 (DEBT) — Six rounds carried the same sentence: a `symbol_mismatch`
violation records file, line and `§id` and DROPS the symbol the resolver
answered. The name was in scope at the emit site and thrown away, so a consumer
learned that a citation had drifted and had to open the file to learn to what.

WHY IT WAS THE ONE CARRY THAT GREW. Round 1154 repaired the doc-comment rule and
that repair BOUND thirty citations in the consumer's tree which had previously
resolved to an enclosing scope — measured, 0 answers moved and 30 gained over
43095 comment lines. Every one of those is a site where their store may record
the old, coarser name. So the next run puts a fresh `symbol_mismatch` in front of
someone who cannot tell, FROM THE REPORT, whether their code moved or this
resolver started answering. The payload is what tells those two apart, and
shipping the thirty without it would have been shipping the ambiguity.

BOTH NAMES, BECAUSE A DRIFT IS A PAIR. `read: Option<ReadSymbol>` carries what
the resolver FOUND and the set the store EXPECTS. A set, not a member: a section
legitimately records more than one symbol for one file, and printing whichever
one the comparison happened to reject would look definite and be arbitrary. The
JSON gains `found` and `expected`, and the human line gains "code says `alpha`,
store records `beta`" — the R1045 lesson is that a claim proved only against
`--json` leaves the line a person reads free to say less, and the reader of that
line is exactly the one who would otherwise open the file.

AN OPTION ON A VARIANT EIGHT KINDS SHARE IS A SMELL UNLESS ITS POPULATION IS
PINNED, so it is pinned twice: a lib test drives the real scan over a tree with
one drifted citation and one unbound one and requires the payload on exactly the
first, and the end-to-end law walks the binary's JSON and requires `found` to be
present iff `kind == symbol_mismatch`. The kind's own payload would be the tidier
home — `ViolationKind::SymbolMismatch { found }` — and it was rejected for a
reason worth recording: that enum is a `Copy` tag read as a key by the severity
map, the axis map and `kind_tag`, so giving it a `String` moves the cost onto
every one of those readers to spare one field on one variant.

ABSENT RATHER THAN NULL when no symbol was read, which is the same distinction
Round 1141 drew for the axis counts one level up: the presence of the key is
itself the answer to "did anything read the code here".
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-validate/src/code_refs.rs` — new `ReadSymbol { found, expected }`; `CodeRefViolation::Citation` gains `read: Option<ReadSymbol>`; the symbol axis fills it at the one emit site that resolves a name and the other seven sites state `None` with the reason; `to_cli_json` adds `found` and `expected` when present and omits both otherwise; `Display` gains a second arm carrying the pair; a lib law drives the real scan and requires the payload on exactly the symbol axis.

`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/symbol_axis_reach.rs` — law 2 now reads `found` and `expected` out of the violation JSON, and walks every violation to require the payload iff the kind is `symbol_mismatch`.
Nine construction sites and eight destructuring sites updated, all found by the compiler rather than by search.
verification_bullets: RED FIRST. The end-to-end law was written before any production line and failed on the absent keys; the payload was added after.

THE INVARIANT IS PINNED FROM BOTH SIDES, and each side is non-vacuous by construction. The lib law asserts exactly one symbol drift in its fixture (or the equality is about an empty set) AND that the run produced a violation from another axis (or `None` is never exercised). The end-to-end law walks every violation the binary printed and requires presence iff `kind == symbol_mismatch`.
THE HUMAN LINE IS COVERED TOO, not only `--json` — the R1045 defect was a claim that held on the machine wire while the line a person reads said less.
`cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast` exit 0; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` exit 0; `cargo fmt --all --check` exit 0.
MECHANICAL EDITS WERE COMPILER-DRIVEN. Seventeen sites, every one located by `cargo check --message-format=short` and edited at the line it named — no pattern replacement over a 10000-line file.

ONE FALSE START, recorded because it cost a cycle: the lib law was first written against invented APIs (`AtomicBinding`, `SetEqualityValidator::default`, `store.view()`), none of which exist. The fix was to copy the construction the file's own `scan_paths_no_resolvers_ns` helper already uses.
carry_forward_bullets: THE SCE REPLY NOW OWES A WIRE CHANGE TOO, and that is a consequence of doing this first rather than after: a `symbol_mismatch` violation gains `found` and `expected` keys, and its human line gains a clause. Both are ADDITIVE — no field was renamed or removed — but a consumer parsing the text line by position rather than by prefix should hear it from us.

THE OTHER SEVEN CITATION AXES READ NO CODE, so they carry nothing. Whether any of them SHOULD is a real question this round did not open: `citation_unbound` knows which files the section does bind, and a report that named them would spare the same file-opening this round spared. violation records file, line and `§id` and DROPS the symbol the resolver
answered. The name was in scope at the emit site and thrown away, so a consumer
learned that a citation had drifted and had to open the file to learn to what.

that repair BOUND thirty citations in the consumer's tree which had previously
resolved to an enclosing scope — measured, 0 answers moved and 30 gained over
43095 comment lines. Every one of those is a site where their store may record
the old, coarser name. So the next run puts a fresh `symbol_mismatch` in front of
someone who cannot tell, FROM THE REPORT, whether their code moved or this
resolver started answering. The payload is what tells those two apart, and
shipping the thirty without it would have been shipping the ambiguity.

the resolver FOUND and the set the store EXPECTS. A set, not a member: a section
legitimately records more than one symbol for one file, and printing whichever
one the comparison happened to reject would look definite and be arbitrary. The

PINNED, so it is pinned twice: a lib test drives the real scan over a tree with
one drifted citation and one unbound one and requires the payload on exactly the
first, and the end-to-end law walks the binary's JSON and requires `found` to be
present iff `kind == symbol_mismatch`. The kind's own payload would be the tidier
home — `ViolationKind::SymbolMismatch { found }` — and it was rejected for a
reason worth recording: that enum is a `Copy` tag read as a key by the severity
map, the axis map and `kind_tag`, so giving it a `String` moves the cost onto
every one of those readers to spare one field on one variant.

ABSENT RATHER THAN NULL when no symbol was read, which is the same distinction
Round 1141 drew for the axis counts one level up: the presence of the key is
itself the answer to "did anything read the code here".

Round 1159.decision_summary:
R1159 (DEBT) — The build machine went unused for a whole session, and the reason
was not laziness: LOCAL IS THE SHAPE THAT HAPPENS WHEN NOTHING DECIDES. Fourteen
heavy verifications ran here, eight of them whole-tree suites of ten to twenty
minutes, on a host at load 15-21 sharing 31 GB between six repositories, while a
32-core machine sat idle behind a skill written for exactly that. The skill was
opened once, late, and only to copy a procedure whose decision had already been
made by hand. Its rule requires the chooser to state a reason IN NUMBERS, and
this session stated none eight times — which is the evidence that nothing was
choosing rather than that it chose wrong.

SO THE DECISION MOVED OUT OF A DOCUMENT AND INTO A PROGRAM, machine-wide, outside
every repository: it measures local memory, swap and load, probes the registry's
hosts for capacity, reads the repository's own declaration of what to send, keeps
a record of how long each command took and WHERE, prints the reason every run,
and returns the WRAPPED command's exit status. With no declaration and no
reachable host it is a transparent pass-through — measure, log, run here, same
status — which is the property that makes it safe in front of fifty-one
repositories. This entry names it by function rather than by path because the
program is machine-local tooling and this ledger is public.

TWO OF ITS OWN DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY RUNNING IT, not by reading it, and both were
the failure it exists to prevent. The remote destination carried `$HOME` as a
LITERAL — rsync does not expand it — so the first real remote call transferred
NOTHING and reported exit 0 over a tree that was never sent. The reason the
transfer failure was invisible is the second defect: every step was wrapped in
one subshell whose last statement ended `|| true`, so the subshell exited 0 and
two failed transfers were swallowed. Each step is checked on its own now, and the
trees are PROVEN equal afterwards — `HEAD` plus the porcelain status, because
rsync reports what it sent and not that the far side matches.

AND ITS FIRST REAL USE CAUGHT A DEFECT ROUND 1157 HAD SHIPPED. That round's
corpus laws read an ABSOLUTE PATH to a tree that exists on one machine, and
failed hard when it was absent — a hardness the entry called a virtue. The virtue
holds where the corpus is. Everywhere else, including CI, it is a red about the
HOST rather than about the code, and Round 1157 is committed and unpushed, so
pushing it as written would have turned `main` red on arrival. Ten more local
runs would have stayed green for ever; one run somewhere else answered in eleven
minutes. That is the whole argument for a second machine, made by the machine.

THE REPAIR IS THE `0`-VERSUS-`null` RULE ONE LEVEL UP. The path is overridable,
and an absent corpus now PRINTS that the three laws are unguarded on this host
and passes, rather than failing about the host or skipping in silence. Passing is
a DEBT and is registered as one: the laws are guarded where the corpus is and
nowhere else, so closing it means a corpus the repository itself ships.

WHAT THE CHOOSER IS NOT: smart. It is deterministic and it states its reason, and
four observed decisions were three defensible and one silly — `cargo --version`
was sent to another machine because the repository's single memory hint (24 GB
for its heaviest test) is applied to every command in it. Named limits: no notion
of whether the local build cache is warm; the timings key is the literal command
string, so each new shape costs one local run to learn; the last measurement is
used rather than a median; and a remote measurement is mostly TRANSFER yet is
compared against a local threshold.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/resolver_corpus_laws.rs` — the corpus path is overridable by environment, and its absence prints that the three laws are unguarded on this host and returns, instead of failing about the host. The comment records that passing is the debt and what closing it costs.

Machine-local, outside this repository and therefore not shipped with it: the build-placement wrapper (measure, decide, log, run, record), and the two Bash-guard refusals whose prescription named a script only this repository has — now naming the machine-wide wrapper, which is what makes the refusal actionable in the other fifty.
verification_bullets: FIVE REAL CALLS, each probing one property rather than the whole thing at once: exit-code fidelity (a wrapped `exit 7` came back as 7); a forced remote run from an empty remote tree; the same command twice, where the second stayed local because the first had been recorded; stale-lock reaping (two locks, one a dead pid, and the parallelism divisor went from 2 to 1); and the full workspace suite, which it sent away on its own.

THE FULL SUITE ON THE BUILD MACHINE (32 cores, 125 GB): 702s, exit 101, and the one failing target was `resolver_corpus_laws` — the Round 1157 defect. Locally the same commit had been green thirty minutes earlier. Both readings are true; they differ in the HOST, which is the difference the corpus test was silently depending on.

BOTH ARMS OF THE REPAIR RUN HERE. With the corpus present: go 220 files / 37353 lines / 30213 answered, python 219 / 26428 / 20153, kotlin 689 / 110351 / 97980, zero disagreements — unchanged from Round 1157. With `MNEMOSYNE_RESOLVER_CORPUS=/nonexistent`: `NOT MEASURED: no corpus at /nonexistent … The three laws below are unguarded on this host`, exit 0.

THE TRANSFER IS PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED: `trees agree: HEAD 83a818f7, working state identical`. That line is what the first version could not say, and its absence is why that version reported success over an empty remote tree.
The guard refusal was re-probed after its prescription changed and still fires (`cargo test … | grep` denied, now pointing at the machine-wide wrapper).
carry_forward_bullets: THE CORPUS LAWS ARE GUARDED ON ONE HOST AND NOWHERE ELSE. Passing on absence is this round's debt, not its resolution: a defect those three laws would catch now reaches CI unseen. Closing it means a corpus the REPOSITORY ships — a small but real body of Go, Python and Kotlin under `crates/` — after which the consumer-tree run becomes a recorded measurement rather than the only guard.

THE CHOOSER OVER-SENDS SHORT COMMANDS, measured: a repository declares ONE memory hint for its heaviest test, and that hint is applied to every command in it, which is why a version query crossed the network. The signal available before any measurement is the command TEXT, so the fix is a named heuristic (whole-tree shapes only) rather than a cleverness — and it should be labelled as one.
A REMOTE MEASUREMENT IS MOSTLY TRANSFER and is compared against a threshold meant for local cost. The wording was corrected to say where each number was taken; the COMPARISON still mixes them.

NO REFUSAL YET FOR BYPASSING THE WRAPPER. The guard denies a verdict piped into a filter, so calling a heavy suite directly and unpiped still goes unmeasured — twice in this session. That refusal is its own round, and it must arrive with the red call that proves it fires; writing it now, off, would be the rule that never fires.

THE OTHER TWO OF THE OWNER'S FOUR REMAIN: a written criterion for the doc-comment rule (five languages, five shapes, no stated way to choose a sixth), and the SCE reply — which now owes the wire change Round 1158 made as well as the thirty new C++ bindings from Round 1154.
THE INJECTION SWEEP IS STILL UNRUN, and it is now the only job on this machine that plainly wants the other one: about two hours, against the twenty seconds the corpus laws turned out to need.

Round 1161.decision_summary:
R1161 (DEBT) — Round 1160 registered Y1: the three resolver corpus laws read a
checkout that exists on ONE machine, and everywhere else — the build machine,
and CI — they printed `NOT MEASURED` and PASSED. This closes it, and the way it
closes reverses what Round 1160's own carry note prescribed. STAR THE CARRY SAID
"SHIP A SMALL BUT REAL CORPUS" AND TWO MEASUREMENTS SAID OTHERWISE. This
repository tracks 0 Go, 0 Kotlin and 2 Python files and has never vendored
third-party source (`git ls-files` for vendor / third-party / NOTICE: nothing),
and the grammar crates it already depends on ship no test corpora either
(`tree-sitter-{go,python,kotlin-ng}` in the registry hold `src/parser.c` and
queries, and zero `.go` / `.py` / `.kt`). So the choice was vendoring upstream
files into a public repository that has never carried any, or something else.
STAR THE SOMETHING ELSE IS THAT TWO JOBS WERE TANGLED HERE. DISCOVERY asks what
shapes nobody imagined, needs a real tree at volume, and is a ONE-SHOT
instrument — Round 1157 ran it over 174,132 lines for 0 disagreements, which is
what the Rust and C++ PORT harnesses did before being deleted. REGRESSION asks
whether the engine's invariants still hold, and must run everywhere. Law 1 is
METAMORPHIC (batching must not change an answer), and for a metamorphic property
a frozen sample is the weaker instrument: 30 vendored files find their
unforeseen shapes exactly once and are a fixed regression corpus forever after.
STAR AND A BUILT CORPUS BUYS THE ONE THING A VENDORED SAMPLE CANNOT — A DERIVED
POPULATION. `LanguageSpec::pattern_count` reads how many declaration patterns a
backend's query DECLARES and `patterns_exercised` reads which of them a source
reached, both off the compiled query via `tree_sitter`'s own `pattern_index`.
Law 0 requires every declared pattern to be reached, so a backend that grows a
pattern reddens this until the corpus grows a shape: THE CORPUS CANNOT SILENTLY
LAG THE BACKEND. A real tree can only ever report what it happened to contain.
STAR LAW 3 STOPPED BEING A CONSTANT. It was `answered > lines_total / 20` — the
hand-written floor this repository keeps catching in other people's code, and
Round 1150 was bitten by its own. The composer plants every declaration and
knows which one covers each line, so over the built corpus the law is now a full
ORACLE: every line is compared by NAME, in both directions, and a line answering
something nobody planted fails as loudly as a line answering nothing. The floor
survives only for the real tree, where nothing knows the right answers — which
is the honest reason it existed. STAR THE RESIDUE, STATED RATHER THAN COVERED: a
built corpus only holds shapes somebody thought of. What that trades for is that
"did I think of it?" becomes "does the backend's query name it?", a question
with an owner and a red test. The discovery pass stays for the other half, and
is now opt-in and NEVER silent: unset means the laws already ran on the built
corpus, and a variable naming a tree that is not there FAILS, because a
measurement asked for and not taken is not the same as one nobody asked for.

and `LanguageSpec::patterns_exercised`, the denominator and the numerator of
what a corpus covers, both read off the compiled query and `tree_sitter`'s own
`pattern_index` rather than off a list beside it. The doc says why counting
ANSWERS cannot substitute: two patterns can produce the same name and a third
can produce none, so an answer map cannot tell "never reached" from "reached
and declined to name".
`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/resolver_corpus_laws.rs` — the corpus is now BUILT
from per-language shapes composed in four adjacencies (each alone, all in
order, all reversed, all twice), so every shape stands beside a different
neighbour and two placements of one form never share a name. Law 0 (every
declared pattern is reached) is new; law 3 becomes an oracle over planted
names; the `NOT MEASURED and return` path is gone. The real-tree pass survives
as opt-in discovery that must measure when asked.
`crates/mnemosyne-cli/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` — the plugin core as a
dev-dependency, because the contract now asks the query itself.

22 files of a few lines each against the real tree's 174,132 lines. It is not

carry_forward_bullets: A BUILT CORPUS HOLDS ONLY SHAPES SOMEBODY THOUGHT OF, and no assertion in it

R1162 (DEBT) — Round 1161 left Y2 as the same axis it had just worked: law 0
made a backend's QUERY claims checkable, and the other half of the same spec —
which declarations a comment above them documents — was still claimed by nobody
and checked by nothing. `documented_kinds` being EMPTY switched the whole pass
off, so a backend declined the rule by writing `&[]` and no law asked why. Four
of the five shipped backends switched it on and the fifth off; the fifth's own
doc said "which one is right is a question with an answer" and left it there.
STAR THE FIFTH'S ANSWER WAS NOT A DECISION, IT WAS AN UNSERVED LANGUAGE. The
reason to hesitate over Rust was real and it was about the WIRE: Rust spells
"documents the module I am in" as `//!` and "documents the item below" as `///`,
and both are a `line_comment` — so a rule keyed on the comment's node kind would
have bound a module-level citation to whatever declaration happened to follow
it. That is the Round 1154 shape exactly, a contract that cannot close a hole
its wire carries no information about. STAR EXCEPT THAT THE GRAMMAR DOES CARRY
IT, which a test asked and prose never had: `tree-sitter-rust` records
`inner_doc_comment_marker` under `//!` and `/*! */` and `outer_doc_comment_marker`
under `///` and `/** */`. So the answer was to extend the wire by one field
rather than to keep a language switched off — an off switch and an unserved
language look identical from outside, which is how this one stayed for five
rounds. STAR THE CRITERION IS NOW THREE QUESTIONS ANSWERED WITH DATA, on
`DocCommentRule`: what does this grammar call a comment, which of those
spellings document the scope they are INSIDE, and which declarations may a
comment above be documenting. There is no fourth answer of "none of them" — the
rule is not optional, and the value that used to mean "off" is now the one a law
refuses. The question with no field is written down beside them: is there a
spelling that means something else in the SAME POSITION and that the grammar
does not mark. C++'s Doxygen `///<` is the near case and it is not in the same
position — the pass starts from the first non-whitespace character of the cited
row, and on a trailing comment's row that character is code. Measured over the
1471-file C++ corpus this repository is put to: 78 trailing-doc comments, 0 of
them starting their own line. STAR EVERY CLAIM IS NOW WITNESSED BY A CORPUS, the
population derived from the spec exactly as law 0 derives its own: 32 witnesses,
one per declared kind across all five backends, each with a CONTROL that is the
same source with one blank line inserted. The control is the half that says pass
1 did the work — without it a witness also passes for a comment pass 2 happened
to cover with the same name. STAR AND WRITING THE LAW FOUND A DEFECT THAT WOULD
HAVE MADE THE WHOLE RULE SILENT FOR RUST. `tree-sitter-rust` includes the
trailing newline in a DOC comment's extent and not in an ordinary comment's, so
`end_position().row` was a row the comment holds no text on: the pass looked one
row past the declaration for exactly the comments the rule exists to serve and
answered nothing. Ordinary `//` comments bound correctly the whole time, so
every hand-written case would have passed. STAR THE PORT ORACLE COULD NOT HAVE
FOUND ANY OF THIS. Rust's and C++'s backends were ports, and a port's oracle is
agreement with its predecessor — which cannot see a defect the predecessor also
had. Rust's agreed line for line over 313 files and 221,787 lines while both
bound a `///` citation to the wrong item.

Round 1164.decision_summary:
R1164 (DEBT) — two carries, and one of them said no program could close it.
STAR THE ONE THAT SAID SO. Round 1162 wrote down a limit: a spec that NAMES an
inward marker is witnessed by a law, and a spec that names none is claiming its
language has no such spelling — which nothing could check, because "there is no
such spelling" had no query behind it. It does. A grammar publishes its
node-kind table, and every kind it NAMES after a comment is a spelling somebody
gave a comment's name to. The law now requires that set to equal what the spec
accounts for: a comment kind, an inward marker, or a kind named here with the
reason it is neither. Rust's five come out as two comment kinds, one inward
marker, and two set aside — `doc_comment` is the TEXT inside a doc comment
rather than a comment node, and `outer_doc_comment_marker` marks the case the
rule already serves. THE LIMIT THAT REMAINS IS NARROWER AND IS STATED: this
reads the kind's NAME, so a grammar that called its inner-doc form something
else would not appear. It is the failure that actually happened, though —
`inner_doc_comment_marker` sat in Rust's table for five rounds while the spec
said the language could not be served — so this is the law that would have named
it. STAR THE OTHER CARRY IS B2, AND ITS PREMISE HAD ALREADY EXPIRED. It asked
the report to publish which patterns are "covered by a law" and which are "only
declared"; law 0 dissolved that distinction for three backends and Round 1163
dissolved it for the last two, so every declared pattern is corpus-covered by
construction and the number worth publishing is the DENOMINATOR. What the report
now carries per backend is `declaration_patterns` and the whole doc-comment rule
— comment kinds, inward markers, documented kinds. STAR WHICH IS THE ANSWER TO A
QUESTION A CONSUMER CANNOT OTHERWISE ASK. Round 1162 changed where a Rust `///`
citation binds, and nothing they run could have told them: the answer lived in a
list inside a crate of ours, which is the same shape as the prose gap list this
verb exists to replace. The law's oracle is `IN_PROCESS_BACKENDS`'s own spec
through the binary, so it checks that what the report prints is what the
resolver will do rather than that two lists in this repository agree.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/src/backends.rs` — `InProcessBackend` carries its
`LanguageSpec`. A field and not an `Option`: every backend this build ships is
a tree-sitter backend, and a nullable one would let a row publish an absence
as a fact.
`crates/mnemosyne-cli/src/main.rs` — `describe-symbol-axis-reach` publishes
`declaration_patterns` and `doc_comments` (comment kinds, inward markers,
documented kinds) per backend, in both the JSON and the text form. The count
is `null` rather than `0` when a query does not compile.
`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/symbol_axis_reach.rs` — law 6b: the published rule
must equal the spec the resolver answers from, and exactly one backend must
have an inward spelling, or the field is decoration.
`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/resolver_corpus_laws.rs` — the comment-kind
accounting law, its population read off `tree_sitter::Language`'s own node-kind
table, plus the per-subject list of kinds set aside with reasons.
`crates/mnemosyne-cli/Cargo.toml` — the plugin core as a dependency, because
the table now names the type.
verification_bullets: STAR BOTH NEW LAWS WERE INJECTED. Dropping `doc_comment` from Rust's set-aside
list reddens the accounting law printing both sets side by side — `left` the
four the spec accounts for, `right` the five the grammar has. Publishing an
empty `inward_markers` from the report while the spec still holds one reddens
law 6b and nothing else. Both restored.
STAR THE ACCOUNTING LAW PASSED ON ITS FIRST RUN, which is the shape to be
suspicious of, and the injection above is why it is not taken on trust. What
it found is that four grammars name exactly one comment-ish kind (`comment`),
Kotlin names two, and Rust names five.
STAR THE REPORT WAS READ, not only asserted: `describe-symbol-axis-reach` now
prints, for Rust, `13 declaration pattern(s); a line_comment / block_comment
directly above any of 13 declaration kind(s) documents it — unless it carries
inner_doc_comment_marker, which documents the enclosing scope instead`, and for
C++ the same sentence with one comment kind, 7 patterns, 6 kinds and no
exception clause.
`cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast`: 155 targets,
1961 passed, 0 failed (1959 before; the two new laws are the difference).
STAR AND THE FIRST READING OF THAT NUMBER WAS 1957, which is the count this
round nearly filed. The log holds 155 `test result` lines and the pattern that
sums them matched 154: cargo printed a `Running` line INTO the middle of one
result line, so a target's `4 passed` was silently dropped by the filter
rather than by the run. The reconciliation is the check — 155 lines, 155
matched — and a summing filter that cannot say how many lines it saw is the
same shape as a gate that cannot say what it reached.
`cargo clippy --workspace --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D
warnings` exit 0. `cargo fmt --all --check` exit 0.
`mnemosyne-cli validate-workspace` exit 0.
carry_forward_bullets: THE ACCOUNTING LAW READS A NAME. A grammar whose inner-doc form is called
something with no "comment" in it is invisible to it, and no assertion can say
otherwise: the node-kind table publishes spellings, not meanings. What changed
is that the unchecked claim is now the narrow one — "this grammar has no
comment-ish kind I failed to consider" — rather than the wide one it replaced.
THE REPORT PUBLISHES THE RULE AND NOT ITS CONSEQUENCE. A consumer reads which
kinds bind and which marker declines; what they would have to do with that is
resolve a line, which is the resolver's job and not a report's. Nothing here
lets them ask "what would this build answer for THIS file" without running the
gate, and nothing in this round proposes that they should.

Round 1167.decision_summary:
R1167 (DEBT) — Round 1158 shipped the symbol axis's payload and wrote its own
residue down: THE OTHER SEVEN CITATION AXES READ NO CODE, SO THEY CARRY NOTHING.
That sentence was half wrong, and the wrong half is the round. Two of the seven
read something and threw it away. `citation_unbound` looks up the files the
cited section DOES bind — that lookup IS the test — and kept only the boolean.
`prose_fact_assertion` matches one of eight spellings in two languages and bound
it to `_verb`. Both left a consumer doing exactly what Round 1158 spared them on
the symbol axis: opening the store, or re-deriving a list that lives in a crate
of ours.

STAR ONE FIELD, NOT THREE. `read: Option<ReadSymbol>` becomes `evidence:
Option<CitationEvidence>`. Three parallel `Option`s would be eight states of
which five are nonsense and one restated invariant per field; the enum has four
states and `AuditAxis::evidence` — exhaustive over all thirteen axes — says
which one each kind must be. The kind's own payload is still the tidier home and
still refused for Round 1158's reason: `ViolationKind` is a `Copy` tag read as a
key by the severity map, the axis map and `kind_tag`.

STAR WHAT QUALIFIES AS EVIDENCE IS NOT A JUDGEMENT CALL. Every variant is a
value the axis ALREADY COMPUTED and dropped. The other five compare an
identifier against a key set and read nothing at the site, and now say so BY
NAME in the table rather than by an absence a reader has to interpret. Nothing
was invented to fill a column.

STAR AN EMPTY BINDING SET IS AN ANSWER. A section that binds nobody yields
`bound_files: []`, not absent evidence: "you are not in the list" and "there is
no list" are different repairs, and that is the `0` vs `null` distinction of
Round 1141 one level down.

STAR THE PUBLISHED WIRE NAMES ARE ASKED, NOT SPELLED. `EvidenceShape::wire_keys`
publishes the `--json` key set per shape, a lib law holds it against what
`to_cli_json` actually writes, and the end-to-end law derives its expectation
from it. Serializer to declaration to law, with no link stated twice.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-validate/src/code_refs.rs` — `CitationEvidence` (symbol drift, section bindings, assertion verb), `EvidenceShape` + `wire_keys`, and `AuditAxis::evidence` as the declaration every emit site is checked against.

Same file — `CodeRefViolation::Citation.read` becomes `evidence`; the unbound and prose emit sites publish what they had been dropping; `to_cli_json` gains `bound_files` and `assertion_verb`; `Display` gains a clause per shape.
Same file — the hand-built all-thirteen-axis fixture becomes `every_violation_shape()`, so the laws that must hold for EVERY axis read one list rather than each carrying its own.
`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/symbol_axis_reach.rs` — law 2b: a tree that provokes all three evidence axes through the binary, checked on the wire AND on the line a person reads.

STAR SEVEN INJECTIONS, EVERY ONE CONFIRMED FIRING. Dropping the unbound evidence, dropping the verb, and rendering the unbound clause without the files each redden both the lib law and the end-to-end law — the third with the wire untouched, so it is the human line alone that catches it. Declaring the wrong shape for an axis reddens four laws. Renaming a published wire key reddens the serializer-agreement law.

The loop now runs in law 2b as well, over the tree that provokes all three, and the same injection reddens it.

R1170 (DEBT) — R1169 IS WRONG AND THIS IS THE CORRECTION. It opened by
announcing that Y3's ten-round blocker was a premise rather than a fact: that
`claudedocs/` is not gitignored, that 880 files under it are tracked, and that
twenty-five `send-*` replies are the tracked precedent. The conclusion was
right for the wrong reason and two of the three facts are false.

STAR I ASKED THE PROGRAM A NEIGHBOURING QUESTION AND READ ITS ANSWER AS MINE.
`git check-ignore -v claudedocs/` exits 1, and I read that as "nothing under
here is ignored". The rule is `/claudedocs/*`, which matches CHILDREN: a
directory that is not itself ignored can have every file inside it ignored, and
those are different questions with different answers. Asked about the file, the
same command exits 0 and prints `.gitignore:25:/claudedocs/*`.

STAR AND I READ A FILESYSTEM LISTING AS A TRACKED SET. The list of `send-*`
replies I cited as precedent came from `ls -1 claudedocs/*.md`, not from
`git ls-files`. Asked properly: of 34 `send-*` documents on disk, ZERO are
tracked. Of the 880 tracked paths, 879 are experiment evidence under `phase1-*`
and one is `population-census.json` — precisely the two exceptions `.gitignore`
declares in its own comments, three lines below the rule I misread.

STAR THE FILE ITSELF SAID SO IN WORDS. Line 24 reads "Claude working scratch
(RFC drafts, maintainer replies) — local only". The ledger's premise was not a
stale belief of mine; it was this repository's stated policy, and the memory
note that carried it was correct while I overruled it.

STAR WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS THE PART THAT MATTERED. Writing the reply was
never blocked — it is written, and it sits in the place this repository intends
maintainer replies to sit. Only routing is the gate, exactly as the ledger said
for ten rounds. So Y3's work is discharged; what was false was my account of
WHY it had been possible all along, and R1169's commit carries that account.

STAR THE ENTRY IS NOT BEING REWRITTEN. It is local and unpushed and deleting it
would cost nothing today, which is the argument against: the frozen ledger is
worth more than a tidy record, and an error that a later entry corrects is the
mechanism this store has for exactly this. R1169 stands with its claim, and this
entry is the one a reader of it must find.

verification_bullets: THE QUESTION ASKED THE RIGHT WAY: `git check-ignore -v <the file>` exits 0 and names `.gitignore:25:/claudedocs/*`. Asked about the directory it exits 1. Both were run; the second is the one R1169 quoted.

THE TRACKED SET, FROM `git ls-files` AND NOT FROM `ls`: 880 paths under `claudedocs/`, of which 879 match `claudedocs/phase1-` and one is `population-census.json`. `git ls-files "claudedocs/send-*"` returns 0 rows against 34 such files on disk.

An ignored path is skipped in silence, the commit succeeds, and `git status` comes back clean because there is nothing it will admit to seeing. The only thing that said so was `git show --stat`, read afterwards and for another reason. Whether a round should end by reading what its own commit contains is a real question this session does not settle: it is one more command per round against a failure that has now happened once.

Round 1172.decision_summary:
`mnemosyne-cli` kept seventy-six integration test binaries, and the cost of them
was not a number anybody had to argue about: Round 1171's commit died in the
pre-commit item-citation gate at a ten-minute timeout, and that gate documents
every target `cargo metadata` lists. Measured here with the crate's artifacts
cleaned, it took 7m21s and the whole of the wait was ONE step — `documenting
mnemosyne-cli` with seventy-six `--test` flags on it. Seventy-six of this
workspace's hundred test targets were in one directory.

So they are one binary. `tests/all.rs` declares seventy-four of them as
`#[path]` modules over the shared `tests/common/mod.rs`, `autotests = false`
makes it the only automatic target, and two files keep targets of their own.
This is Round 1148's repair for `mnemosyne-server`'s twenty-two files applied to
the crate that grew the larger pile, and the law that keeps it safe
(`consolidated_test_isolation.rs`) was already walking `crates/*/tests/all.rs`
when this arrived: a file that touches what the PROCESS owns — working
directory, environment, tracing dispatcher, global allocator — may not share a
binary, directly or through a helper.

WHAT THE CONSOLIDATION MEASURED, same command, same machine, same starting
state:

  - the item-citation gate: 7m21s -> 27s, over a census that went from 130
    documentable targets (100 Test) to 57 (27 Test); rustdoc wrote 11,397 files
    / 158 MB and now writes 7,552 / 100 MB. Both runs started with `target/doc`
    removed, so neither was reading the other's answer.
  - `cargo test -p mnemosyne-cli --all-features --no-run` from `cargo clean -p
    mnemosyne-cli`: 29.94s -> 4.43s, repeated at 4s. 78 executables -> 5.

WHAT A LAW HAS TO SAY THAT IT DID NOT SAY BEFORE. The existing law says which
files may not SHARE a binary. It says nothing about the other direction, and
that direction is how the pile grows back: a file declared as its own `[[test]]`
for no reason costs a link and a rustdoc unit on every commit and reads exactly
like one that had to be. Two laws close it, and both are derived rather than
listed:

  - `a_separate_test_target_is_one_the_process_or_ci_forces` — an exception is
    earned by the PROCESS (the same predicate the first law rejects an included
    file with, now one function read by both, so the two cannot come to
    disagree) or by a CI command that NAMES it with `--test` (a target that
    exists to be built alone). Nothing else.
  - `a_test_target_a_ci_command_names_is_one_that_exists` — the failure
    consolidation makes possible and nothing else catches: fold in a file a
    workflow still selects by name and `cargo test --test <name>` fails with
    "no test target named", in a scheduled job that may not run for a week.

The two exceptions this crate keeps are what those laws accept:
`evidence_replay_smoke` and `pinned_revision_rechecks_evidence_smoke`, which
`evidence-replay.yml` selects with `--test`; folded in, that job would build
every other test file in this crate to run one. Across the repository seven
targets stand apart and all seven are earned — the other five are
`mnemosyne-server`'s, one for capturing spans and four for the OTLP install.

THE LAW NOW LIVES UNDER ITS OWN RULE, and getting there is the same repair.
Until this round it could not be judged by the law it states: its denylist
spells `env::set_var` and `set_current_dir` as string literals, so a scanner
matching a whole file's TEXT reported the file that names the constructs it
hunts. Reading SYNTAX (`syn`) instead ends that — a literal is a literal, a
comment is nothing, and `env::set_var` can be asked as a path suffix rather
than as a substring that `mine::set_var` also satisfies. The exception it used
to need is gone, and the law is one of the seventy-four modules it judges.

ASKING THE OTHER DIRECTION FOUND A REAL HOLE, in a crate this round was not
touching. The derivation of "which of this crate's own helpers install a
process-global" was textual and ONE HOP deep, and said so as a known limit.
`init_otlp_tracing_subscriber` installs nothing itself — its entire body is
`init_otlp_tracing_subscriber_with_config(...)`, one hop further — so the
one-hop reading returned only the second name, and the two server test files
that call the first were invisible to the law written for them. Round 1150 had
already shipped that class of defect once. It came back here as two targets the
new law called unearned, which is how a limit that had been written down for
four rounds finally had a case. The derivation is now a FIXED POINT over the
crate's own `src/`, following private hops as well as public ones, reading a
function's code with comment lines dropped (the doc comment of the next function
lands in this one's segment, and a name mentioned in prose is not a call). All
four `grpc_otlp_*` targets are now earned by the reason their manifest always
claimed.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/all.rs` — new. Seventy-four of this crate's test files as `#[path]` modules over one `#[path = "common/mod.rs"] mod common`, with the two rules for adding one written where they are needed.

`crates/mnemosyne-cli/Cargo.toml` — `autotests = false`; `[[test]]` for `all` and for the two earned exceptions, each carrying its reason; `toml` as a dev-dependency, because "is this file a declared target, or only a string that appears in the manifest" is exactly what a text search cannot tell apart.

Twenty test files — `mod common;` becomes `use crate::common;`. A `mod` inside a `#[path]`-loaded module resolves against that module's own directory, so the shared harness is declared once by the root and reached by path.

`tests/surface/*.rs` — `use crate::sweep` becomes `use super::sweep`, and the corruption sweep's compile-time OWNER moves from `authoring_surface` to `all`. What the guard is FOR did not move: the memo is a `OnceLock` per process, so a second target that compiles it pays the whole 312-store sweep again. Its refusing arm gains the name it used to answer to, which is now a module rather than a target.

`tests/consolidated_test_isolation.rs` — two new laws (an exception is earned by the process or by CI; a `--test` a CI command writes names a target that exists); both denylist readings moved from a file's TEXT to its SYNTAX with `syn`, which is what let this file stop matching its own table and join the binary it judges; the process-global predicate extracted so both directions read ONE definition; the installer derivation made a fixed point over the crate's own `src/`, closing the one-hop limit; the population walk derived from `ci_plan::tracked_manifests` rather than from two hardcoded directory names; the orphan check reading the manifest's PARSED `[[test]]` entries rather than asking whether its text contains `tests/<name>.rs`.

`tools/ci-plan` — `CargoCommand::values`, the repeatable-flag reader, with its test: `value` answers with the first, which is right for `--manifest-path` and wrong for `--test`, and a command naming two targets while a reader sees one is a half-answer that reads like a whole one.
Root `Cargo.toml` — `syn`'s `visit` feature, for the borrowing walk the two readings above are built on.
verification_bullets: THE GATE THAT KILLED A COMMIT, MEASURED BOTH WAYS FROM THE SAME START: `tools/item-citations` went 7m21s to 27s, over a census that fell from 130 documentable targets (5 Bin, 25 Lib, 100 Test) to 57 (5, 25, 27). BOTH runs began with `cargo clean --doc`, so neither read the other's answer, and rustdoc really ran in the second — it wrote 7,552 files / 100 MB where the first wrote 11,397 / 158 MB. The verdict is unchanged: every item citation in this workspace names an item, 0 defects, 0 targets unreached.
LINKING, same command each side, each from `cargo clean -p mnemosyne-cli`: `cargo test -p mnemosyne-cli --all-features --locked --no-run` went 29.94s to 4.43s, repeated at 4s. 78 executables to 5.

THE COUNT IS THE CHECK CONSOLIDATION ACTUALLY NEEDS, and it closes: `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` is 1968 passed, 0 failed. Round 1171 measured 1965 with that same command and this round adds exactly three tests — the two laws below and `ci-plan`'s repeatable-flag reader. Nothing was dropped in the fold.
AND THE SAME THING FROM THE OTHER SIDE, about the whole repository: `unrun-tests` reports 2,651 tests compiled across 15 workspaces and 2,651 run by CI. No test went dark.

REPEATED, because a shared process is what this round bought: the consolidated binary ran four times (308, 312, 312, 312 tests as the laws landed), 0 failures, 369s to 487s each. Four is the number; the carry says what four is worth.
NON-VACUITY — THE LAW READS THIS CRATE'S NEW `all.rs`: a probe `#[path]`-including the law file itself came back with six named reasons rather than silence.

NON-VACUITY — THE SYNTAX READING TELLS PROSE FROM USE: `env::set_var` and `set_current_dir` written in a COMMENT inside an included file, green; the same file with an actual `std::env::set_var(...)` call, red, naming the file and the reason.

NON-VACUITY — CI'S NAMES: renaming the `evidence_replay_smoke` target turned `a_test_target_a_ci_command_names_is_one_that_exists` red, naming the workflow and the job that select it, and `a_separate_test_target_is_one_the_process_or_ci_forces` went red on the same injection independently, as an unearned exception. Two readers, one defect, neither borrowed from the other.

THE FIXED-POINT REPAIR HAS A CONTROL AND A TREATMENT rather than an argument: with the one-hop derivation, `grpc_otlp_smoke` and `grpc_otlp_collector_e2e` came back unearned; with the chain followed to a fixed point, both are earned by the call they always made.

GATES: `cargo fmt --all --check` exit 0; `cargo clippy --workspace --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` exit 0; `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` 14 checked / 0 skipped; `unrun-tests` clean; `validate-workspace` clean, T3 reject 0 / warn 0, T4 0, orphan refs 10+0 unchanged.

WHAT WENT WRONG IN THE MEASURING, recorded because it will happen again: the first whole-suite run came back red on the isolation law, and the defect was in the RUN and not in the tree — this round edited `all.rs` while that suite was in flight, and the law reads the tree at RUNTIME from a binary compiled before the edit. A test that reads files has a result belonging to the tree AS OF its run. It is the sibling of "concurrent cargo hands back a stale binary" with the arrow reversed, and the remedy is the same: declare the run void and run it again.
carry_forward_bullets: THE DENYLIST IS STILL A DENYLIST, and that is the world rather than the round. Reading a file's SYNTAX made the MATCH exact — a construct named in a comment, or written as a string literal in the table that lists it, is no longer a use of it, which is what finally let the law live under its own rule. It did not make the LIST complete. "Does this test mutate process state" is a question about what the code reaches at RUNTIME through crates this one never parses, and answering it would take whole-program effect analysis. A named list of constructs, each with a reason, is a claim a reader can check; the next entry arrives the next time something is measured, as `with_default` did.

THE CALL CHAIN STOPS AT THE OWNING CRATE'S `src/`, and widening it was measured against rather than skipped. A test file can only be matched on an installer's NAME, and the population of names decides the false positives: within one crate `init_otlp_tracing_subscriber` is unambiguous, but across every workspace crate a `run` or a `new` that transitively installs would flag every test file that mentions those words. `syn` gives syntax, not resolution — which `run()` a call names is a question only a compiler answers, and that is the limit under both readings. A test that reaches a process install through a SIBLING crate's helper is therefore invisible here; none does today, and the loud direction was chosen for the one that could.

A SUITE THAT DOES NOT FLAKE IN FOUR RUNS IS NOT A SUITE THAT CANNOT. Cargo runs test BINARIES one after another and the tests inside one in parallel, so folding seventy-four files together raised concurrency: two tests that shared an on-disk resource by the luck of being in different processes now do not. Round 1148 is the precedent for what that costs to KNOW — a test that failed 2 of 30 runs, where thirty greens were not an argument and a hundred were. Four whole-binary runs is this round's evidence and its honest form is a count of runs, not a proof of absence.

WHAT DISK THIS BOUGHT WAS NOT MEASURED, deliberately. Round 1160 already refuted the "these binaries are why the tree is 37 GB" hypothesis by measuring them at ~21 MB apiece, so the axis measured here is the one that actually stopped a commit: the gate's wall clock and the link count behind it. A byte figure would have needed a rebuild of the pre-consolidation tree to be worth stating, and nothing depends on it.
