  - the item-citation gate: 7m21s -> 27s, over a census that went from 130
    documentable targets (100 Test) to 57 (27 Test); rustdoc wrote 11,397 files
    / 158 MB and now writes 7,552 / 100 MB. Both runs started with `target/doc`
    removed, so neither was reading the other's answer.
  - `cargo test -p mnemosyne-cli --all-features --no-run` from `cargo clean -p
    mnemosyne-cli`: 29.94s -> 4.43s, repeated at 4s. 78 executables -> 5.

WHAT A LAW HAS TO SAY THAT IT DID NOT SAY BEFORE. The existing law says which
files may not SHARE a binary. It says nothing about the other direction, and
that direction is how the pile grows back: a file declared as its own `[[test]]`
for no reason costs a link and a rustdoc unit on every commit and reads exactly
like one that had to be. Two laws close it, and both are derived rather than
listed:

  - `a_separate_test_target_is_one_the_process_or_ci_forces` — an exception is
    earned by the PROCESS (the same predicate the first law rejects an included
    file with, now one function read by both, so the two cannot come to
    disagree) or by a CI command that NAMES it with `--test` (a target that
    exists to be built alone). Nothing else.
  - `a_test_target_a_ci_command_names_is_one_that_exists` — the failure
    consolidation makes possible and nothing else catches: fold in a file a
    workflow still selects by name and `cargo test --test <name>` fails with
    "no test target named", in a scheduled job that may not run for a week.

The two exceptions this crate keeps are what those laws accept:
`evidence_replay_smoke` and `pinned_revision_rechecks_evidence_smoke`, which
`evidence-replay.yml` selects with `--test`; folded in, that job would build
every other test file in this crate to run one. Across the repository seven
targets stand apart and all seven are earned — the other five are
`mnemosyne-server`'s, one for capturing spans and four for the OTLP install.

THE LAW NOW LIVES UNDER ITS OWN RULE, and getting there is the same repair.
Until this round it could not be judged by the law it states: its denylist
spells `env::set_var` and `set_current_dir` as string literals, so a scanner
matching a whole file's TEXT reported the file that names the constructs it
hunts. Reading SYNTAX (`syn`) instead ends that — a literal is a literal, a
comment is nothing, and `env::set_var` can be asked as a path suffix rather
than as a substring that `mine::set_var` also satisfies. The exception it used
to need is gone, and the law is one of the seventy-four modules it judges.

ASKING THE OTHER DIRECTION FOUND A REAL HOLE, in a crate this round was not
touching. The derivation of "which of this crate's own helpers install a
process-global" was textual and ONE HOP deep, and said so as a known limit.
`init_otlp_tracing_subscriber` installs nothing itself — its entire body is
`init_otlp_tracing_subscriber_with_config(...)`, one hop further — so the
one-hop reading returned only the second name, and the two server test files
that call the first were invisible to the law written for them. Round 1150 had
already shipped that class of defect once. It came back here as two targets the
new law called unearned, which is how a limit that had been written down for
four rounds finally had a case. The derivation is now a FIXED POINT over the
crate's own `src/`, following private hops as well as public ones, reading a
function's code with comment lines dropped (the doc comment of the next function
lands in this one's segment, and a name mentioned in prose is not a call). All
four `grpc_otlp_*` targets are now earned by the reason their manifest always
claimed.
publishable_changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/all.rs` — new. Seventy-four of this crate's test files as `#[path]` modules over one `#[path = "common/mod.rs"] mod common`, with the two rules for adding one written where they are needed.

`crates/mnemosyne-cli/Cargo.toml` — `autotests = false`; `[[test]]` for `all` and for the two earned exceptions, each carrying its reason; `toml` as a dev-dependency, because "is this file a declared target, or only a string that appears in the manifest" is exactly what a text search cannot tell apart.

Twenty test files — `mod common;` becomes `use crate::common;`. A `mod` inside a `#[path]`-loaded module resolves against that module's own directory, so the shared harness is declared once by the root and reached by path.

`tests/surface/*.rs` — `use crate::sweep` becomes `use super::sweep`, and the corruption sweep's compile-time OWNER moves from `authoring_surface` to `all`. What the guard is FOR did not move: the memo is a `OnceLock` per process, so a second target that compiles it pays the whole 312-store sweep again. Its refusing arm gains the name it used to answer to, which is now a module rather than a target.

`tests/consolidated_test_isolation.rs` — two new laws (an exception is earned by the process or by CI; a `--test` a CI command writes names a target that exists); both denylist readings moved from a file's TEXT to its SYNTAX with `syn`, which is what let this file stop matching its own table and join the binary it judges; the process-global predicate extracted so both directions read ONE definition; the installer derivation made a fixed point over the crate's own `src/`, closing the one-hop limit; the population walk derived from `ci_plan::tracked_manifests` rather than from two hardcoded directory names; the orphan check reading the manifest's PARSED `[[test]]` entries rather than asking whether its text contains `tests/<name>.rs`.

`tools/ci-plan` — `CargoCommand::values`, the repeatable-flag reader, with its test: `value` answers with the first, which is right for `--manifest-path` and wrong for `--test`, and a command naming two targets while a reader sees one is a half-answer that reads like a whole one.
Root `Cargo.toml` — `syn`'s `visit` feature, for the borrowing walk the two readings above are built on.
publishable_verification_bullets: THE GATE THAT KILLED A COMMIT, MEASURED BOTH WAYS FROM THE SAME START: `tools/item-citations` went 7m21s to 27s, over a census that fell from 130 documentable targets (5 Bin, 25 Lib, 100 Test) to 57 (5, 25, 27). BOTH runs began with `cargo clean --doc`, so neither read the other's answer, and rustdoc really ran in the second — it wrote 7,552 files / 100 MB where the first wrote 11,397 / 158 MB. The verdict is unchanged: every item citation in this workspace names an item, 0 defects, 0 targets unreached.
LINKING, same command each side, each from `cargo clean -p mnemosyne-cli`: `cargo test -p mnemosyne-cli --all-features --locked --no-run` went 29.94s to 4.43s, repeated at 4s. 78 executables to 5.

THE COUNT IS THE CHECK CONSOLIDATION ACTUALLY NEEDS, and it closes: `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` is 1968 passed, 0 failed. Round 1171 measured 1965 with that same command and this round adds exactly three tests — the two laws below and `ci-plan`'s repeatable-flag reader. Nothing was dropped in the fold.
AND THE SAME THING FROM THE OTHER SIDE, about the whole repository: `unrun-tests` reports 2,651 tests compiled across 15 workspaces and 2,651 run by CI. No test went dark.

REPEATED, because a shared process is what this round bought: the consolidated binary ran four times (308, 312, 312, 312 tests as the laws landed), 0 failures, 369s to 487s each. Four is the number; the carry says what four is worth.
NON-VACUITY — THE LAW READS THIS CRATE'S NEW `all.rs`: a probe `#[path]`-including the law file itself came back with six named reasons rather than silence.

NON-VACUITY — THE SYNTAX READING TELLS PROSE FROM USE: `env::set_var` and `set_current_dir` written in a COMMENT inside an included file, green; the same file with an actual `std::env::set_var(...)` call, red, naming the file and the reason.

NON-VACUITY — CI'S NAMES: renaming the `evidence_replay_smoke` target turned `a_test_target_a_ci_command_names_is_one_that_exists` red, naming the workflow and the job that select it, and `a_separate_test_target_is_one_the_process_or_ci_forces` went red on the same injection independently, as an unearned exception. Two readers, one defect, neither borrowed from the other.

THE FIXED-POINT REPAIR HAS A CONTROL AND A TREATMENT rather than an argument: with the one-hop derivation, `grpc_otlp_smoke` and `grpc_otlp_collector_e2e` came back unearned; with the chain followed to a fixed point, both are earned by the call they always made.

GATES: `cargo fmt --all --check` exit 0; `cargo clippy --workspace --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` exit 0; `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` 14 checked / 0 skipped; `unrun-tests` clean; `validate-workspace` clean, T3 reject 0 / warn 0, T4 0, orphan refs 10+0 unchanged.

WHAT WENT WRONG IN THE MEASURING, recorded because it will happen again: the first whole-suite run came back red on the isolation law, and the defect was in the RUN and not in the tree — this round edited `all.rs` while that suite was in flight, and the law reads the tree at RUNTIME from a binary compiled before the edit. A test that reads files has a result belonging to the tree AS OF its run. It is the sibling of "concurrent cargo hands back a stale binary" with the arrow reversed, and the remedy is the same: declare the run void and run it again.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: THE DENYLIST IS STILL A DENYLIST, and that is the world rather than the round. Reading a file's SYNTAX made the MATCH exact — a construct named in a comment, or written as a string literal in the table that lists it, is no longer a use of it, which is what finally let the law live under its own rule. It did not make the LIST complete. "Does this test mutate process state" is a question about what the code reaches at RUNTIME through crates this one never parses, and answering it would take whole-program effect analysis. A named list of constructs, each with a reason, is a claim a reader can check; the next entry arrives the next time something is measured, as `with_default` did.

THE CALL CHAIN STOPS AT THE OWNING CRATE'S `src/`, and widening it was measured against rather than skipped. A test file can only be matched on an installer's NAME, and the population of names decides the false positives: within one crate `init_otlp_tracing_subscriber` is unambiguous, but across every workspace crate a `run` or a `new` that transitively installs would flag every test file that mentions those words. `syn` gives syntax, not resolution — which `run()` a call names is a question only a compiler answers, and that is the limit under both readings. A test that reaches a process install through a SIBLING crate's helper is therefore invisible here; none does today, and the loud direction was chosen for the one that could.

A SUITE THAT DOES NOT FLAKE IN FOUR RUNS IS NOT A SUITE THAT CANNOT. Cargo runs test BINARIES one after another and the tests inside one in parallel, so folding seventy-four files together raised concurrency: two tests that shared an on-disk resource by the luck of being in different processes now do not. Round 1148 is the precedent for what that costs to KNOW — a test that failed 2 of 30 runs, where thirty greens were not an argument and a hundred were. Four whole-binary runs is this round's evidence and its honest form is a count of runs, not a proof of absence.

WHAT DISK THIS BOUGHT WAS NOT MEASURED, deliberately. Round 1160 already refuted the "these binaries are why the tree is 37 GB" hypothesis by measuring them at ~21 MB apiece, so the axis measured here is the one that actually stopped a commit: the gate's wall clock and the link count behind it. A byte figure would have needed a rebuild of the pre-consolidation tree to be worth stating, and nothing depends on it.

Round 1173.decision_summary:
R1173 (DEBT) — A CARRY SAID "MEASURED AGAINST" AND NOTHING HAD BEEN MEASURED.

Round 1172's second carry explains why the process-global call chain stops at
the owning crate's `src/` rather than reaching every workspace crate, and it
opens: "widening it was measured against rather than skipped." It was not
measured. It was argued — correctly in kind, from the shape of the matcher —
and then written up in the voice of a measurement, which is the one thing this
repository has decided its own prose may not do. The ledger is append-only, so
Round 1172 stands as written and this entry is the correction.

MEASURED NOW, by the injection that carry describes: point
`global_installing_fns` at every tracked package's `src/` instead of the owning
crate's and re-run the laws.

The fixed point makes **`main`** an installer. Some binary's `main` reaches the
dispatcher install, the chain closes over it, and from there every function
whose body names `main` is an installer too. The denylist then refuses
`report_playthrough_manuscript_smoke.rs` from the shared binary — a file that
touches nothing the process owns, flagged because it names the most common
identifier in the language.

So the carry's CONCLUSION survives and its EVIDENCE now exists, and the
measurement is sharper than the argument was: the argument guessed `run` and
`new`, and the tree answered `main`. The reason the widening cannot work is
therefore not "some name might collide" but "the first name it finds already
does" — a test file can only be matched on an installer's NAME, `syn` gives
syntax and not resolution, and which `main` an identifier refers to is a
question only a compiler answers. The limit is where Round 1172 put it; the
sentence describing it was the defect.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ROUND rather than a fix to the last one. The atomic store
is the audit trail and its entries are frozen: an entry that quietly grew a
measurement it did not have when it was written would be worse than the
overclaim, because nothing downstream could tell the two apart. Round 1170
corrected Round 1169 the same way, one round later and in the open.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/consolidated_test_isolation.rs` — `global_installing_fns` gains the measurement under its doc comment: the widened walk makes `main` an installer and refuses `report_playthrough_manuscript_smoke.rs`, so the boundary is now documented by a result rather than by a worry. No behaviour change; the walk is where Round 1172 left it.
verification_bullets: THE INJECTION IS THE MEASUREMENT, and it was run and reverted: with `global_installing_fns` pointed at every tracked package's `src/`, `a_test_that_owns_a_process_global_does_not_share_a_binary` goes red with one violation — `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/report_playthrough_manuscript_smoke.rs` "calls `main`, which installs a process-global dispatcher in this crate's own src". The installer set it derives holds `main` beside `init_otlp_tracing_subscriber` and `init_otlp_tracing_subscriber_with_config`.

THE CONTROL IS THE SHIPPED WALK: reverted to the owning crate's `src/`, the same law is green and the seven separate targets are the same seven, each earned. Two runs, one difference, so the difference is attributable.
NO BEHAVIOUR MOVED, so the verification is the suite that was already green: the four consolidation laws pass inside the consolidated binary, and this entry changes one doc comment.
carry_forward_bullets: NOTHING PREVENTS THE NEXT SENTENCE OF THIS KIND, and that is the honest statement rather than a plan. `validate-workspace` reads the store's structure, not the truth of its prose; no gate can ask whether "measured" names a measurement that happened. What is available is the discipline this entry exercises — when a carry uses the word, run the thing before the entry is appended — and the record that the failure mode is recurrent rather than novel: the memory has carried "do not assert an unverified measurement" since two consumers pushed back on exactly that, and Round 1172 wrote one anyway, inside the paragraph explaining a limit.

Round 1174.decision_summary:
R1174 (DEBT — a third of the evidence was dark and nobody held the reason). The
session opened on the north-star question the RESUME left: return to narrative
after thirteen rounds on gates. Re-measuring the narrative track's position is
what that return asks for first, and the tree answered with a number nobody had
read as a defect. `payoff_read_agreement` prints it every run: 44 authored
corpora asked, 28 answered, 16 could not. The count was never silent. WHY was.

THE RECIPE HELD THE REFUSAL AND KEPT THE NAME. `authored_stores()` matched
`Err(_) => unloadable.push(name)` — the import's own message was in hand at the
moment of judging and a string was stored instead, which is the R1167 shape
exactly. With the message carried, the sixteen classify in one read: THIRTEEN
were dark to schema drift alone, and THREE are first submissions their own
experiment recorded as rejected. Twelve of the thirteen refuse on R708's removal
of the free-text `value` / `scalar` object shape; all thirteen also predate
R732's entity-kind registry; one predates R752's turn from disclosure `first_at`
PAIRS to per-branch trigger sets. Not one of them was an authoring defect.

THE UPGRADE IS IN THE RECIPE, NOT IN THIRTEEN REWRITTEN MANIFESTS, and that is
the only shape keeping both halves true. The product does not soften: the write
path still rejects the removed shapes exactly as R708/R732/R752 decided. The
record does not move: an experiment's manifest is what its author shipped, and a
report citing it cites the file in git. `upgrade_corpus_manifest` carries a
manifest across all three breaks on the way IN to a throwaway workspace, the way
one migrates a database before replaying it, and it is scoped to
`corpus_workspace_try` rather than to `workspace_try` — the manifests a walk
writes ITSELF include ones deliberately malformed to prove a refusal, and an
upgrade that repaired those would turn a negative case green while the walk
still called it evidence.

THE ONE INFERENCE, STATED. All three breaks replaced free text with a DECLARED
closed vocabulary, and the only vocabulary a pre-break record contains is the
one it used — so each is closed over the corpus's own usage. A store built this
way answers "which values may this predicate take" with its author's USAGE
rather than its author's INTENT, and a walk asking about REJECTION of an unlisted
token must not use one of these records as its witness. Two predicates could not
be carried at all (`bond_state`, `box_state`: declared `scalar`, used by no fact,
and an empty closed set is itself rejected — "an empty closed set would re-open
the free-text hole"); they are DROPPED, and `dark_corpus_accounting` pins the
drop by name so it is not a quiet one.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE BOUGHT, measured rather than promised: corpora answering both
payoff reads 28 -> 41, the (world, setup) pairs they compare 136 -> 362,
discharging steps 26 -> 102, facts named holding across every scene 18734 ->
20061. THREE emptiness rules that no loadable corpus could refute are now
REFUTED (`report-frame-view: unknown`, `report-frame-view: holding`,
`report-playthrough-manuscript: begins`) — a rule nothing can refute while a
third of the population will not load is a rule the corpus was never asked. One
read argument moved Inert -> Named for the same reason. And two arms that the
tree's own constructed store had been carrying alone are now carried by an
author's: fourteen empty-scene checks, and fifteen scenes the reading prune drops.

A CONTRACT THAT HAD NEVER MET A CONFLUENCE. Lighting the corpora broke
`filtered_read_selects`, whose claim is that a filtered read answers, for the
roads it keeps, exactly what the unfiltered read already said. R533 decides
otherwise and says so in `playthrough_manuscript`: the default dump sweeps the
PLAYTHROUGHS, and a confluence's shared suffix already renders inside each
parent's manuscript, so a fragment is answerable only BY NAME. No loadable corpus
declared a confluence, so the contract read as universal because nothing had ever
tested the one case it does not cover. The carve-out reads the store's own
`is_confluence` predicate, applies only when the filtered answer holds exactly
the asked fragment, and is COUNTED (2) with its non-vacuity asserted — an
exclusion nobody counts is indistinguishable from a contract that holds. No
shipped read was wrong here; the law was.

WHAT NOW KEEPS IT. `dark_corpus_accounting` states the terminal condition as two
halves: every dark corpus is a `-first-submission` record, AND the accepted
sibling of each one loads. The second half is what makes the first a claim rather
than an assertion about a directory name — the same author's next submission of
the same corpus goes through, so the refusal is demonstrably about the submission
and not about the schema. Beside it the upgrade's per-corpus ledger is pinned, so
an upgrade that starts changing something else cannot do it quietly.
changes_bullets: `UnloadableCorpus { name, reason }` replaces the bare name `authored_stores()`
returned: the import's refusal is CARRIED instead of dropped, with one
`Display` for a flat skip list and one `named_reason()` for the bucketed
walks, so seventeen call sites cannot drift into seventeen phrasings.
`upgrade_corpus_manifest` in the corpus recipe carries a fact manifest across
the three vocabulary breaks it may predate — R708's removed `value`/`scalar`
object shape, R732's entity-kind registry, R752's `first_at` pair lists — by
closing over the vocabulary the corpus itself used. Scoped to
`corpus_workspace_try` (the tracked corpora) and NOT to `workspace_try`, whose
manifests include ones a walk deliberately malformed to prove a refusal.
`CorpusUpgrade` records what was carried and what was NOT: values re-shaped,
predicates re-declared, predicates DROPPED (declared `scalar`, used by no
fact, and an empty closed set is rejected), entity kinds declared, `first_at`
lists regrouped. `AuthoredStore.upgrade` carries it and the store's NAME says
`(upgraded at load)`, because such a record answers about a predicate's
vocabulary with its author's usage rather than its author's declaration.
`filtered_read_selects` learns the R533 rule it had never met: a confluence
fragment is answerable only BY NAME, so a filtered read holding exactly the
asked fragment has no unfiltered answer to be held to. Read off the store's
own `is_confluence` predicate, counted, and its non-vacuity asserted.
`dark_corpus_accounting` (new): every dark corpus is a `-first-submission`
record AND its accepted sibling loads; and the upgrade's per-corpus ledger is
pinned so it cannot start changing something else quietly.
Thirty-one pinned evidence numbers across fourteen walks move with the wider
population, three emptiness rules move CANDIDATE to REFUTED, and one read
argument moves Inert to Named.
verification_bullets: `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked`: 1970 passed / 0 failed. The
arithmetic closes against R1173's 1968 — the two new laws in
`dark_corpus_accounting` are the difference.
The population moved where it was measured, not where it was claimed: corpora
answering both payoff reads 28 -> 41, (world, setup) pairs compared 136 ->
362, discharging steps 26 -> 102 (cross-frame 3 -> 15), facts named holding
18734 -> 20061, road-filter probes 112 -> 228.
Three emptiness rules that no loadable corpus could refute are now REFUTED by
one (`report-frame-view: unknown`, `report-frame-view: holding`,
`report-playthrough-manuscript: begins`), and two arms the tree's constructed
store carried alone are now carried by an author's: 14 empty-scene checks and
15 scenes the reading prune drops.
The confluence carve-out is non-vacuous by assertion: 2 structures answered
for a fragment the unfiltered dump does not sweep, from the corpus whose
`dawn` branch converges `sluice` and `ride`. Its sibling `convergence-probe/v1`
declares no confluence and does not trigger it, so the variable is measured.
The dnd-quest fixture was tested for redundancy rather than assumed: the
upgraded tracked manifest is byte-equal to it in branches, entities, entity
kinds, facts, frames and predicates, and differs by exactly one
`disclosure_plans` entry — so it is a corpus PLUS a telling, not a legacy copy.
clippy `-D warnings` 0, `cargo fmt --check` 0, `validate-workspace` 0 (T3
reject 0, orphan refs 10+0 unchanged, decay surface 0).
A number in this round was wrong once before it was right: a mis-scoped grep
read the argument census as 14 Named / 2 Inert and a claim was written around
"eight more arrived by evidence". The workspace run refuted it (14 / 9, one
moved), which is the R1173 lesson arriving on schedule — a sentence about a
measurement is not the measurement.
carry_forward_bullets: THE UPGRADE READS USAGE, NOT INTENT, and no program can close that gap. The
removed shapes declared no vocabulary, so "which values may this predicate
take" is answered from what the corpus wrote; a walk asking whether an
UNLISTED token is rejected must not use one of these thirteen records as its
witness. Two predicates could not be carried at all and are dropped by name.
THREE CORPORA STAY DARK AND SHOULD. Each is a first submission its own
experiment recorded as rejected — a surface object outside the entity
registry, and two section manifests wrapped in an object where the wire takes
an array. Upgrading those would erase the record of what was turned back,
which is the only thing a first submission is for.
`bx` STILL CANNOT CARRY A ROUND THAT CREATES A FILE (Z13, second sighting).
The new law had to be `git add`-ed before the build machine could see it,
because `bx` rsyncs tracked files and says only "the remote working tree
differs" without naming untracked as the cause. Machine-global tool, so the
repair is not this repository's to route.
THE NARRATIVE TRACK'S OWN POSITION IS STILL UNMEASURED. This round re-lit the
corpora the position would be measured ON, but the north-star scoreboard is

what that return asks for first, and the tree answered with a number nobody had
read as a defect. `payoff_read_agreement` prints it every run: 44 authored
corpora asked, 28 answered, 16 could not. The count was never silent. WHY was.

moment of judging and a string was stored instead, which is the R1167 shape
exactly. With the message carried, the sixteen classify in one read: THIRTEEN

Round 1175.decision_summary:
R1175 (DEBT — a test suite that cannot be run twice at once, proved by running
it twice at once). Round 1174's verification ran `check-side-workspaces.sh`
twice with an overlap, and `tools/experiment-harness`'s
`seal::tests::a_changed_input_is_an_error_not_a_reseal` panicked on a
`NotFound` writing a file into a directory it had just created. Run alone,
the same suite is green. That difference is the finding.

THE FIXTURE PATH IS A CONSTANT, SO TWO RUNS ARE ONE RUN. Both `tmp()` and
`kit()` compose their path from `std::env::temp_dir()` and a name fixed in the
source — `eh-seal-test-match`, `eh-stamp-changed` — and every test ends by
REMOVING that path. Two processes running the suite therefore share one set of
directories, and the second's `create_dir_all` is followed by the first's
`remove_dir_all` before the write lands. Nothing about it is probabilistic in
the way "flake" suggests: the tests are correct in isolation and wrong the
moment anything else is running them, which on a build machine three
repositories share is the normal case rather than the unlucky one.

THE PROCESS ID IS THE MISSING COORDINATE. A fixture directory is per-RUN state
and was named as though it were per-TEST state; adding `std::process::id()`
makes the name say which run owns it. It is not a retry, not a lock, and not a
serial-test attribute — those all treat the collision as scheduling. The paths
simply did not name enough to be unique, and now they do.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS CRATE. The evidence this repository trusts is
produced by runs on a shared machine, and the failure mode here is one where a
green suite and a red suite differ by WHO ELSE WAS RUNNING. Round 1148's
2-in-30 tracing failure and Round 1172's process-global installer denylist are
the same family: state a test binary does not own, named as though it did. This
one was found the honest way — by an overlap that actually happened, with the
real message read rather than the word "flake" written.
changes_bullets: Six fixture paths across the side workspaces name the PROCESS: `tmp()` and
`kit()` in `tools/experiment-harness/src/seal.rs`, the scratch directory in
its `declare.rs` test, `scratch()` in `tools/unrun-tests/tests/gate.rs`, and
both of `tools/unrun-tests/tests/entrance.rs`.
The doc comment on each says WHY the pid is in the name — a fixture directory
the test also REMOVES is per-RUN state, and a constant path claims it is
per-TEST state — and names the four sibling crates that already did this, so
the next reader sees a convention rather than a one-off.
verification_bullets: The defect was REPRODUCED before it was named: two overlapping
`check-side-workspaces.sh` runs on the build machine, and the panic read
`Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound }` at the `fs::write` one line after
`create_dir_all`. Run alone the same suite was green, which is the difference
that identified the cause.
The fix is measured the only way that means anything here: the suite run TWICE
CONCURRENTLY, both arms 40 passed / 0 and 4 passed / 0. The overlap is
evidenced rather than assumed — the two runs started one second apart and each
took 28 seconds, so they were in flight together for essentially their whole
duration.
Six sites were repaired, found by reading every `temp_dir()` use across the
side workspaces: two helpers in `experiment-harness/src/seal.rs`, one test in
its `declare.rs`, and three in `unrun-tests`. Four sibling crates
(`injection-harness`, `rustc-log`, `twice-compiled`, and this crate's own
`cli_smoke`) already named the process, so this is a convention that existed
and had holes, not one invented here.
carry_forward_bullets: THE PID MAKES CONCURRENT RUNS SAFE AND SAYS NOTHING ABOUT A CRASHED ONE. A
run killed between `create_dir_all` and its own cleanup leaves its directory
behind, and nothing sweeps it; the paths are under the system temp dir, so the
system does. Naming this rather than adding a reaper: a reaper would have to
decide whether a live run owns a directory, which is the same ownership
question the pid just answered, asked again from outside.
NOTHING STOPS THE SEVENTH ONE. Six sites were found and fixed by reading every
`temp_dir()` use in the side workspaces, and four other crates were already
doing it right — so the convention exists and only discipline holds it. The
law that would enforce it is the R1172 shape: read the SYNTAX (a fixture path
composed under `temp_dir()` whose format string names no per-run value) rather
than the text, because a `grep` for `process::id` cannot tell a path that is
unique from one that merely mentions it. That law is buildable and is not
built here; it is registered as undone work, not as a limit.

Round 1176.decision_summary:
R1176 (BUILD — the two largest authored records this project holds were outside
the population, and four schema drifts were the whole reason). Round 473's
scale-floor experiment is the one measurement this track has of whether the
substrate survives a novel's scale: two extractors each read a 100 KB story,
blind, and built a store from it (plain beat loop 3-0, dangling 3 vs 5). Those
stores then sat in a directory outside this repository, so the twenty-odd laws
written since Round 1036 — every one of which asks the tracked corpora — had
never once been asked about the biggest records here. The north-star scoreboard
could not be re-read because its evidence was not reachable. Population 44 ->
46, loading 41 -> 43.

WHAT STOPPED THEM, asked of the program one at a time. None of the four is about
what either author wrote, which is the whole point: a record that stops loading
because the schema moved is not evidence about the record.

  1. R708's removal of the free-text `value` / `scalar` object shape — the same
     break thirteen corpora needed carried in Round 1174, EXCEPT that this
     corpus's typed legs live in `typing-proposals.json` rather than in the fact
     manifest. The vocabulary the upgrade derives is USAGE, so reading the
     manifest alone read this author as using nothing, dropped every declared
     predicate as inert, and then the proposal import failed on the predicate it
     had just dropped. The derivation had to widen to the corpus's reviewed
     proposals (`upgrade_corpus_manifest(facts, also_used)`).
  2. A SPLIT MANIFEST. The blind harness wrote its registries to
     `registries.json` and a later pass's facts to `supplement.json`, and
     `import-facts` takes one manifest. Unioned by array key in ONE resolver
     (`corpus_fact_manifest`), which also collapsed four call sites that each
     opened `facts.json` themselves — four readers is how they come to disagree
     about what a corpus contains.
  3. THE REVIEWED SECOND PASS WAS NEVER APPLIED. A corpus whose typed legs and
     succession edges arrive as reviewed proposals builds UNTYPED without them,
     and typed legs are the only thing the transition and exclusivity rules can
     see at all. The recipe now runs `import-typing-proposals` and then
     `import-edge-proposals`, and their claim-sha re-check is the carriage's own
     verifier: a proposal that survives is proof the carried manifest still holds
     the claim its author reviewed.
  4. R614's ROOT WORLD-LINE. This author calls the root `trunk`; the canon
     order's base edge set IS `main`'s road, so a corpus that calls its root
     anything else has a root with no road and every fork declares a parent whose
     road is empty. Renaming is the one carriage available. Scoped by "the corpus
     declares this root" it BROKE a corpus that already loaded
     (convergence-probe/v2); narrowed to "the root a fork names as its parent",
     with the root's own declaration row dropped because `main` cannot be
     declared.

THE R697 CARRIAGE IS THE ROUND'S REAL ANSWER, AND IT REFUTES THE GUESS THAT
PRECEDED IT. This corpus's transition rule is `allowed: [["alive", "dead"]]`,
the pair list Round 697 moved into the store, and today's parser rejects the
whole rules file for it. The open question was whether today's transition class —
an adjacency PREDICATE whose facts are the edges — can express a token lifecycle
at all, or only entity endpoints. It CAN, and the measured shape is: one
adjacency predicate, the FROM token registered as an entity, one edge fact per
authored step. The write path taught both halves of the constraint by rejecting
twice — a typed subject must be a registered entity, and it must also appear in
that fact's own `entities`. This is the ONE place the corpus recipe invents
rather than derives, so every row it adds is reported in `TransitionCarriage` and
pinned per arm by a law of its own: a walk that counts this store's entities is
counting one the recipe added, and it can now say so.

MY FIRST NON-VACUITY CLAIM WAS ITSELF VACUOUS. Asking the carried store whether
`dead -> alive` is licensed answers "no" for the wrong reason — neither arm
CONTAINS that step, so an empty refusal set says nothing about the carried rule
and everything about what the extractors happened to write. The law now AUTHORS
the reverse arc into the manifest an author could equally have written: both arms
then emit exactly one `rule_transition_invalid`, where the corpus as shipped
emits none.

THE CENSUS THAT MOVED UNCOVERED TWO HOLES OF MY OWN, both the Round 1174 shape
one level down.

  - THE PERTURBATION WALK'S "FREE FACT" WAS MANIFEST-BLIND. It deletes a fact
    nothing else refers to, because a refused edit is not a move an author could
    have made (the R1033 rule) — and it read `facts.json` alone. It offered
    `a26-ledger-back`, which store-A's typing proposal types and its edge
    proposal succeeds, so `import-typing-proposals` rejected the entire rebuild
    and one branch's perturbation was lost. That rule had been half-true for as
    long as every corpus kept its references in one file. Repaired, the walk runs
    104 deletions where it ran 94, with the refusal count back to 0.
  - THE REFUSAL IT PRINTED HELD NO REASON. `import-typing-proposals` does not
    fail in the ordinary sense: a rejected proposal is a VERDICT printed beside
    the accepted ones, and the process exits 1 with stderr EMPTY. The recipe
    formatted stderr alone, so the walk printed `import-typing-proposals:` and
    stopped there. That is Round 1174's own finding — the evidence in hand at the
    moment of judging, and a blank stored — one level below where that round
    closed it.
changes_bullets: The two blind stores are tracked corpora now,
`claudedocs/phase1-scale-floor-experiment/store-{A,B}/`: fifteen files carried
in byte-for-byte, so every corpus law asks 46 corpora where it asked 44, and 43
stores where it asked 41.
`corpus_fact_manifest` is the ONE reader of what a corpus's fact manifest holds
— `facts.json` unioned by array key with `registries.json` and
`supplement.json`. Four walks that each opened `facts.json` go through it.
`upgrade_corpus_manifest` takes the typed usage that lives OUTSIDE the fact
manifest (`also_used` = the corpus's reviewed typing proposals), because the
vocabulary it derives is usage and this author's usage is there.
The corpus recipe applies the reviewed second pass: `import-typing-proposals`
then `import-edge-proposals`, read from the corpus directory, after the bulk
imports and through the same R708 rewrite.
`upgrade_corpus_rules` carries a pre-R697 `allowed` pair list into the
store-native map — an adjacency predicate, the FROM token as an entity, one edge
fact per step — and `TransitionCarriage` reports every row it adds.
The R614 root-world rename is scoped to a root a FORK names as its parent, and
drops the root's own declaration row. Scoped wider it broke a corpus that
already loaded.
The perturbation walk's free-fact search reads the corpus's reviewed proposal
manifests as well as its facts (`corpus_proposal_manifests`), so a fact a
proposal targets is not offered as deletable.
An import refusal is formatted from whichever stream the verb spoke on
(`import_refusal`), and the two proposal imports are asked in `--json` so a
rejection names the rejected rows instead of an empty string.
New law `scale_floor_corpus_carriage`: both arms are in the population with
their reviewed pass (scenes, facts, typed legs, chained facts pinned per arm),
the carried life arc licenses the authored step and REJECTS an authored-in
reverse one, and the carriage's whole output is pinned per arm.
Every census pin the growth moved is now what the population measures, with the
reason in its own claim rather than only in this entry: the movements are
attributed to these two stores by arithmetic (+10 roads, +345 scene walks, +625
partition rows, +63 payoff edges, +77 empty-scene sightings) rather than
adjusted until green.
verification_bullets: THE CARRIAGE IS BYTE-CHECKED AGAINST THE SOURCE RUN. All fifteen files
compared with `cmp` against the out-of-tree run: six at each arm's root, seven
under `manifests/`, and `order.json` against the source's `canon-order.json` —
the one rename, because the recipe's config names `order.json`. Nothing else
came across: the harness's own built sidecar (`story-{A,B}.atomic.json`) and its
Python build scripts are not the author's record and are not tracked.
WHAT THE ARMS ACTUALLY CARRY, measured through the write path rather than read
off the manifest: store-A 60 scenes / 83 facts / 19 typed / 9 chained, store-B
65 / 97 / 19 / 9. The facts include the one edge fact per arm the R697 carriage

Round 1176.publishable_decision_summary:
R1176 (BUILD — the two largest authored records this project holds were outside
the population, and four schema drifts were the whole reason). Round 473's
scale-floor experiment is the one measurement this track has of whether the
substrate survives a novel's scale: two extractors each read a 100 KB story,
blind, and built a store from it (plain beat loop 3-0, dangling 3 vs 5). Those
stores then sat in a directory outside this repository, so the twenty-odd laws
written since Round 1036 — every one of which asks the tracked corpora — had
never once been asked about the biggest records here. The north-star scoreboard
could not be re-read because its evidence was not reachable. Population 44 ->
46, loading 41 -> 43.

WHAT STOPPED THEM, asked of the program one at a time. None of the four is about
what either author wrote, which is the whole point: a record that stops loading
because the schema moved is not evidence about the record.

  1. R708's removal of the free-text `value` / `scalar` object shape — the same
     break thirteen corpora needed carried in Round 1174, EXCEPT that this
     corpus's typed legs live in `typing-proposals.json` rather than in the fact
     manifest. The vocabulary the upgrade derives is USAGE, so reading the
     manifest alone read this author as using nothing, dropped every declared
     predicate as inert, and then the proposal import failed on the predicate it
     had just dropped. The derivation had to widen to the corpus's reviewed
     proposals (`upgrade_corpus_manifest(facts, also_used)`).
  2. A SPLIT MANIFEST. The blind harness wrote its registries to
     `registries.json` and a later pass's facts to `supplement.json`, and
     `import-facts` takes one manifest. Unioned by array key in ONE resolver
     (`corpus_fact_manifest`), which also collapsed four call sites that each
     opened `facts.json` themselves — four readers is how they come to disagree
     about what a corpus contains.
  3. THE REVIEWED SECOND PASS WAS NEVER APPLIED. A corpus whose typed legs and
     succession edges arrive as reviewed proposals builds UNTYPED without them,
     and typed legs are the only thing the transition and exclusivity rules can
     see at all. The recipe now runs `import-typing-proposals` and then
     `import-edge-proposals`, and their claim-sha re-check is the carriage's own
     verifier: a proposal that survives is proof the carried manifest still holds
     the claim its author reviewed.
  4. R614's ROOT WORLD-LINE. This author calls the root `trunk`; the canon
     order's base edge set IS `main`'s road, so a corpus that calls its root
     anything else has a root with no road and every fork declares a parent whose
     road is empty. Renaming is the one carriage available. Scoped by "the corpus
     declares this root" it BROKE a corpus that already loaded
     (convergence-probe/v2); narrowed to "the root a fork names as its parent",
     with the root's own declaration row dropped because `main` cannot be
     declared.

THE R697 CARRIAGE IS THE ROUND'S REAL ANSWER, AND IT REFUTES THE GUESS THAT
PRECEDED IT. This corpus's transition rule is `allowed: [["alive", "dead"]]`,
the pair list Round 697 moved into the store, and today's parser rejects the
whole rules file for it. The open question was whether today's transition class —
an adjacency PREDICATE whose facts are the edges — can express a token lifecycle
at all, or only entity endpoints. It CAN, and the measured shape is: one
adjacency predicate, the FROM token registered as an entity, one edge fact per
authored step. The write path taught both halves of the constraint by rejecting
twice — a typed subject must be a registered entity, and it must also appear in
that fact's own `entities`. This is the ONE place the corpus recipe invents
rather than derives, so every row it adds is reported in `TransitionCarriage` and
pinned per arm by a law of its own: a walk that counts this store's entities is
counting one the recipe added, and it can now say so.

MY FIRST NON-VACUITY CLAIM WAS ITSELF VACUOUS. Asking the carried store whether
`dead -> alive` is licensed answers "no" for the wrong reason — neither arm
CONTAINS that step, so an empty refusal set says nothing about the carried rule
and everything about what the extractors happened to write. The law now AUTHORS
the reverse arc into the manifest an author could equally have written: both arms
then emit exactly one `rule_transition_invalid`, where the corpus as shipped
emits none.

THE CENSUS THAT MOVED UNCOVERED TWO HOLES OF MY OWN, both the Round 1174 shape
one level down.

  - THE PERTURBATION WALK'S "FREE FACT" WAS MANIFEST-BLIND. It deletes a fact
    nothing else refers to, because a refused edit is not a move an author could
    have made (the R1033 rule) — and it read `facts.json` alone. It offered
    `a26-ledger-back`, which store-A's typing proposal types and its edge
    proposal succeeds, so `import-typing-proposals` rejected the entire rebuild
    and one branch's perturbation was lost. That rule had been half-true for as
    long as every corpus kept its references in one file. Repaired, the walk runs
    104 deletions where it ran 94, with the refusal count back to 0.
  - THE REFUSAL IT PRINTED HELD NO REASON. `import-typing-proposals` does not
    fail in the ordinary sense: a rejected proposal is a VERDICT printed beside
    the accepted ones, and the process exits 1 with stderr EMPTY. The recipe
    formatted stderr alone, so the walk printed `import-typing-proposals:` and
    stopped there. That is Round 1174's own finding — the evidence in hand at the
    moment of judging, and a blank stored — one level below where that round
    closed it.

Round 1177.decision_summary:
R1177 (DEBT — the round that carried two corpora in had a second half nobody had
reached, because cargo stops at the first failing target). R1176 drove
`cargo test -p mnemosyne-cli` from 6 failures to 0 and I read that as the tree
being green. It was not: `mnemosyne-cli` has three test targets, cargo runs them
in order, and every run of the convergence had died inside `all` — so
`evidence_replay_smoke` had never been reached at all. The moment `all` passed,
three failures appeared in a target this round had not touched once. The rule
that would have shown them on the first run is `--no-fail-fast`, which this
project's own memory carries as the first of seven injection rules and which I
did not use.

WHAT THE THREE SAID, and none of them was noise.

  1. ELEVEN OF THE CARRIED FILES WERE INPUTS NO RECORD DECLARED. The evidence
     record demands that every tracked file shaped like a mutate verb's input be
     declared exactly once and sealed by sha256 — the R882 lesson, where a
     hand-list read "covered" while seven classified inputs sat undeclared. The
     scale-floor kit had a report and a run log but no `replay.json` at all,
     which was invisible while none of its files was manifest-shaped.
  2. THE RECORDED-CORPUS SWEEP CALLED THEM EVIDENCE NOTHING CAN OPEN. It rebuilds
     every recorded corpus with today's binary and, for one today refuses, asks
     whether a pinned replay revision can. Both stores answered no to both, which
     is the shape of decayed evidence — and it was WRONG, because they are opened
     on every run by the carriage R1174 built.
  3. THE POPULATION CENSUS HAD STOPPED BEING THE RECORD OF WHAT EACH AXIS SAID.
     `claudedocs/population-census.json` is regenerated in the same commit as the
     change that moves the population, so its history is what each axis said
     when. Two axes moved: directed transition rules 27 -> 29 and file-only run
     trees 239 -> 254.

THE SWEEP'S DICHOTOMY WAS INCOMPLETE, AND THAT IS THE REAL FINDING. It knew two
readers — today's raw substrate, and the revision that produced a corpus — and
R1174 had since added a THIRD: the corpus carriage, which migrates a manifest
that predates a schema break on the way into a throwaway workspace, leaving the
product and the tracked file untouched. Measured, that third reader accounts for
NINE of the thirteen corpora this sweep calls refused. They were passing only
because eight of them happen to be pinned by a replay as well; the two new ones
had no such coincidence, and that is how a law with a missing arm becomes
visible. The sweep now asks all three, through the same recipe the population
laws use, and reports which reader answered for each.

THE SWEEP WAS ALSO READING A THIRD OF ONE RECORD. Its rebuild opened
`facts.json` alone, so for a corpus whose author split the manifest it reported
"frame `ground-truth` not present in the frames registry" — an artifact of the
reading, dressed as a refusal by the substrate. Through the union resolver the
same corpus now refuses for its ACTUAL reason, R708's removed `scalar` shape on
`life_state`, which is the same break twelve other corpora carry. The union
carries no schema upgrade with it, so what this sweep asks — does today's binary
take the author's manifest as written — is unchanged.

AND THE FILES MOVED, WHICH CORRECTS R1176's ENTRY. That entry names the stores at
`claudedocs/phase1-scale-floor-experiment/store-{A,B}`; they are at
`.../run/store-{A,B}` from this round on. The reason is that the seal tools
declare and stamp what sits under a kit's RUN TREE
(`experiment-harness declare-run-tree` walks `/run/` and nothing else), so a
manifest outside it is an entry a person maintains by hand — and a record no
program maintains is the class of decay this whole gate exists to catch. Moved,
the two tools wrote all fifteen declarations and all fifteen digests themselves.

THE UNION FIX IS CHECKED BY THE MESSAGE IT CHANGES: before it, both stores
refused with "frame `ground-truth` not present in the frames registry"; after

the carriage exists, and it is now what the sweep prints.
The record's fifteen digests were written by `experiment-harness stamp-inputs`
("15 input(s) newly sealed, 0 re-checked and unchanged") after
`declare-run-tree` wrote the fifteen declarations ("15 run artifact(s) newly
declared, 651 already declared").
`cargo test -p mnemosyne-cli --no-fail-fast` on the build machine: all three
targets green. `tools/experiment-harness` 44 passed / 0 — the record it writes
is read back by its own seal tests. clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`
clean; `validate-workspace` clean.
ONE FALSE START, RECORDED because it cost two runs: the build machine refused
twice with "the remote working tree differs from this one". The cause was the
rename — its mirror keeps what rsync sends and rsync never deletes, so the
pre-move directories were still there and its population would have been 48
corpora rather than 46. The wrapper's tree-equality check is what caught it;
clearing the two stale paths made the trees agree.
carry_forward_bullets: A SECOND TARGET CAN STILL HIDE BEHIND A FIRST ONE'S RED. `--no-fail-fast` is
discipline, not a mechanism: nothing in this tree makes a local run cover every
target the way CI does. The shape that would is a check on the command a round
verifies with, and it is not built here. What IS true today is that CI runs each
target by name, so the exposure is one round long — which is exactly how these
three were found, one round late.
THE CARRIAGE READER MAKES THE SWEEP'S THREE BUCKETS OVERLAP, and the printed
counts say so rather than partitioning. A corpus can be carried AND pinned, and
eight are. Reporting the buckets independently keeps each number the answer to
its own question; a partition would have to choose a precedence, and the choice
would then be the thing a reader has to know.
THE RECORD PINS BYTES, NOT A REBUILD, FOR THIS KIT. `no_replay` is honest — no
revision of this repository ever ran that import — but it means the seal can say
the manifests have not changed and cannot say that replaying them reproduces the
store the experiment graded. The store the harness built is not tracked, so
there is nothing to compare a rebuild against. Closing this would mean carrying
the out-of-tree `story-{A,B}.atomic.json` in as a fixture and declaring what
today's recipe is allowed to differ from it by, which is a round of its own and
a question (what may a carriage legitimately change?) this round has not asked.

Round 1179.decision_summary:
R1179 (DEBT — the injection that was supposed to prove R1178's new law was itself
misaimed, and the reason it shipped that way is that proving one injection cost
the whole manifest). R1178 wrote four injections into
`tools/cache-budget/injection-sweep.json` and ran the sweep once. Three were
surgical. The fourth — `a-key-is-judged-over-the-interval-its-own-workflow-could-
have-seen` — named three tests and reached two: it breaks the READER
(`last_run_in` finds no earlier run), and
`every_declared_key_is_judged_over_its_own_workflow_history` hands `windows_asked`
its OWN resolver, so no edit to the reader can ever reach it. The harness said so
in its own words and exited 1: "aimed at {…} and did not reach it — a sweep that
comes back 0 is a misaimed injection until something says otherwise".

TWO MECHANISMS WERE BEING PROVED BY ONE INJECTION. The reader and the decision
that consumes it are separate, with separate readers, and an injection aimed at
both is aimed at neither. The repair is the second injection this round adds: it
takes the interval from the push even where a run IS available, which is exactly
the reading that turned main red on run 31695396997, and it fires all three of the
tests that read that decision.

AND THE REASON THAT SHIPPED IS A TOOL LIMIT, WHICH IS THE OTHER HALF OF THIS
ROUND. `injection-harness` took a manifest and nothing else, so the price of
asking "does the injection I just wrote reach the test I aimed it at" was every
injection in the file — 52 of them, twenty minutes, to check four. A verification
that expensive gets written down as an intention rather than run, and that is not
a discipline problem: it is a missing argument. `--only <name>` (repeatable) now
scopes a sweep, and the same question that cost twenty minutes cost 24 seconds
this round — measured, on the two injections above.

THE SCOPE TRAVELS INTO THE REPORT, because a scoped run is a fact about a smaller
population and the report already carries that lesson in its first field: R1138
read a `fired` set off a sweep scoped with `-p mnemosyne-cli`, where the edited
crate's own suite never ran, and nothing in the document said so. A report of four
injections of fifty-six must not be shaped like a sweep of all of them, so
`scope` is `EveryInjection { count }` or `Only { names, of }` and is printed
either way — the unscoped case says which population it was, rather than saying
nothing.

A NAME THAT MATCHES NOTHING IS A REFUSAL. A misspelled `--only` that ran zero
injections would print a clean report and exit 0 — the "0 means suspect the
injection" rule failing in the one place nobody re-reads, the spelling of the
thing being asked for. It refuses, naming what was asked for and what the manifest
carries.
changes_bullets: `injection-harness` takes `--only <name>`, repeatable: it scopes the snapshot, the anchor dry-run and the sweep to the named injections, in the MANIFEST's order rather than the arguments' (two runs naming the same injections differently would be two orderings of one measurement).

The selection is `injection_harness::select`, in the library where a suite can drive it, and it refuses a name no injection carries — naming what was asked for and what the manifest holds, because a `--only` typo that ran nothing would print a clean report and exit 0.

The report carries `scope`: `EveryInjection { count }` or `Only { names, of }`, printed in both modes. A scoped report is a fact about a smaller population and used to be shaped exactly like a full sweep's.

`a-key-is-judged-over-the-interval-its-own-workflow-could-have-seen` no longer claims `every_declared_key_is_judged_over_its_own_workflow_history`: that test injects its own resolver, so the reader this injection breaks is one it never calls.

New injection `the-interval-comes-from-the-workflow-that-declares-the-key` breaks the DECISION instead — the interval is taken from the push even where a run is available — and reaches all three tests that read it.

`--only` also fixed this round's own fixture: the first draft of the two-injection fixture edited text the fake suite does not watch, and the harness refused it as misaimed before any assertion could pass.
verification_bullets: THE MISAIM WAS FOUND BY THE TOOL, NOT BY READING. R1178's full sweep exited 1 with "a-key-is-judged-over-the-interval-…: aimed at {every_declared_key_is_judged_over_its_own_workflow_history} and did not reach it". The other three injections of that round were surgical, and the report says so: `a-failed-run-saved-nothing-…` and `the-run-being-judged-cannot-bound-…` each fired EXACTLY their one named test, 0 missed, 0 unexpected.

THE REPAIR IS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED: the new injection fires all three of `every_declared_key_is_judged_over_its_own_workflow_history`, `a_key_is_asked_about_the_interval_its_own_workflow_could_have_seen` and `a_cache_rebuilt_after_its_lockfile_moved_outside_this_push_is_not_a_defect` — 0 missed, 0 unexpected — and the corrected reader injection now misses nothing either.
AND THAT CHECK COST 24 SECONDS. Both injections, by name, against a control of 97 passed / 0 failed over 7 targets. The same question cost the full manifest — 56 injections — before this round.

`--only` is proved three ways in `tests/harness.rs`, over a real tree and the real binary: the named injection runs AND the other does not (a filter that ran everything and reported one would agree with half of that); an unscoped run still names its population; a name matching nothing exits non-zero and says what it was asked for.

`cargo test` for `tools/injection-harness` with `--no-fail-fast`: 39 passed, 0 failed (harness 28, sweeps 8, self-check 3). `cargo clippy --tests --all-features -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean, on the build machine, which reported the trees identical before each run.
THE ANCHOR GATE STILL HOLDS over every tracked sweep in the repository, which is what says the new injection's `from` text is exact and occurs once.
carry_forward_bullets: A SCOPED SWEEP CHECKS THE ANCHORS IT WILL APPLY AND NO OTHERS, WHICH IS THE HONEST SEMANTIC AND STILL A NARROWER GUARANTEE. The dry-run exists because a typo in the ninth of nine costs the control plus eight whole-suite runs; scoped to one injection it can only say that one is exact. What keeps the rest honest is the anchor gate in `tools/injection-harness/tests/sweeps.rs`, which reads EVERY tracked sweep on every commit — so the narrowing costs nothing that is not already covered by something running more often.

Round 1180.decision_summary: Round 1176 carried the scale-floor experiment's two blind re-extraction stores into the tracked population; this round asks the question that carriage was for, which is whether today's gates still say what the June 2026 blind grader said. They do, exactly: D1 0/0, D2 0/0, D3 3/5, D4 0/0, primary endpoint 3 for the plain arm and 5 for the loop arm, on 60 and 65 scenes across three ending world-lines each. That score is now a law rather than a session's measurement, because a score is the thing that decays silently: five hundred rounds of gate work have landed since the extraction was graded, and a verb that quietly stopped counting an axis would leave every store in the tree greener than it is. This is the only corpus in the repository with a published, independently-graded answer to check against. The axes are not asserted against themselves — the mapping from each D-class to today's violation vocabulary is checked against grading.deterministic.defect_metrics in the protocol manifest, whose sha256 the R473 entry pinned before any prose existed, so the definitions cannot have been fitted to the result. The score itself is pinned in code rather than parsed out of evidence/defect-tables.md, because that document is not sealed by the kit record (declare-run-tree walks the run tree only), and a law that read its expectations out of an unsealed file would move whenever the file moved. Two things are NOT the same as June, and both are pinned rather than hidden. Today's continuity read finds one violation the graded classes do not name — an evidence_unreachable fact on arm B, whose check is R522 and therefore five months younger than the grading; the endpoint is class-scoped so the score is untouched, but the violation map this law builds is EXHAUSTIVE rather than filtered, so a graded kind the engine renamed would surface as an ungraded one instead of counting zero forever. And D4's zero turns out not to come from the continuity gate at all: the injection written to move that axis never reached it, because import-facts rejected the manifest under the R433 fork-boundary invariant. So D4's law is the refusal, asked of every primitive that can write supersedes_in_frame — the bulk manifest, add-fact, amend-fact, and the reviewed edge import that gave these stores their edges in June — for both shapes D4 names, the sibling-branch edge and the succession cycle. All four refuse with the same message. Three axes are shown to MOVE on these arms rather than merely reading zero, which is the R1176 lesson one layer on: an absence a corpus cannot produce is a coincidence, not a law.

Round 1181.decision_summary: R1181 (DEBT — main was red, and the gate that turned it red was behaving correctly on a machine nobody tested it on). Run 31703011291 on 7ced933 failed one job, `separate in-repo workspaces`, on one assertion in the cache-budget entrance suite: the words the gate handed to `gh` carried `&branch=main` and the test expected them without it. The suite that R1178 and R1179 both ran was green each time, because the difference is not in the tree at all. R1178 taught the gate to bound a cache key's interval by the workflow that declares it, and bounding it needs a branch, so `main.rs` began reading GITHUB_BASE_REF and GITHUB_REF_NAME. The entrance fixture spawns the binary with a named environment precisely so a runner's own variables cannot change the answer — its module doc says so, in those words, and names GITHUB_RUN_ID as the case it was paying for. The rule was right and the LIST went stale: two new reads arrived and the fixture never heard of them, so on a developer's shell (both unset) the gate asked the unscoped question the assertion expected, and on a runner (both set) it asked the scoped one. Reproduced exactly by setting GITHUB_REF_NAME=main and running the same test, which is how a fixture that describes an impossible runner gets found: a real run is always of a branch, so the fixture had been simulating a machine that does not exist. The repair is in two parts and the second is the one worth the round. The environment is now one value, `environment(run)`, that the spawn applies and a new law reads; and that law asks `main.rs`'s own SYNTAX, through syn, for every name a std::env::var call reads, then asserts the fixture names all of them. A first draft of that walk collected string literals only and reported three of the five reads as the complete set, which would have made the law agree with a stale list for the same reason the stale list was wrong; constants declared in those sources are now resolved from them, a constant imported from another crate resolves through a table that holds the constant itself rather than a retyped copy, and a name this walk cannot resolve stops it loudly rather than counting as no read. The non-emptiness check is the defect itself: dropping GITHUB_REF_NAME back out of the list fails the new law, naming that variable, at the fixture rather than four commits later on a runner.

Round 1182.decision_summary: R1182 (BUILD — N16: the stale list that turned main red was one of fifteen, so the question moved out of a fixture and into a gate). R1181 repaired `cache-budget`'s environment list and gave that one crate a law that reads `main.rs`'s syntax; every other workspace in this repository still held the same shape and nothing asked. This round builds `tools/named-environment`, a sibling of `blind-waits` and `unrun-tests` under the same three-code contract, and wires it into `pre-commit` and `check-side-workspaces.sh` so all fifteen workspaces are asked on every commit. What it holds against each other is what the PROGRAM reads — every std::env::var call in the binary target, its package's library, and every local package reachable through a declared path — against what the TEST that spawns it says. Which test spawns which binary comes from env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name>"), the one spelling cargo checks at compile time. The verdict rests on MENTION rather than on control, and the weaker word was forced by measurement rather than chosen: the first draft asked for the arguments of .env / .env_remove and could not answer for the very fixture it was written for, because R1181 had just moved that environment into a list the spawn loops over, so the arguments are a loop variable no walk can read. A gate that refuses the tidiest spelling of the shape it enforces is one people route around. Mention is a necessary condition for control, it survives any factoring, and its failure is never a false alarm — a test whose sources never say GITHUB_REF_NAME is certainly not deciding what GITHUB_REF_NAME is; the report prints both numbers so the weaker basis cannot pass for the stronger. Round 1183.decision_summary: R1183 (DEBT — N20: the arm R1182 left unread, and the sweep that could not have read it). R1182 gave `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` a third gate under the three-code contract its two siblings use, with the same pair of sentences — exit 1 says these sites break the law, exit 2 says I could not read enough of this tree to have an opinion — and nothing read either one. It matters more in this arm than in the two beside it, because BOTH ARMS EXIT 1: the lister rejects a workspace whose environment gate found a defect and one whose environment gate could not be read with the same code, so the sentence is the only thing carrying the difference, and the wrong sentence sends somebody into a workspace hunting a defect nobody claimed exists. The reader is one case over ONE TREE WITH ONE FILE DIFFERENT — a binary reading a name the walk cannot resolve answers 2, the same tree with a literal its spawning test never says answers 1 — and each half asserts both the sentence that must appear and the sentence that must not. THE INJECTION THAT WOULD PROVE IT COULD NOT HAVE RUN, and that is the round's larger half. `.githooks/injection-sweep.json` addresses its suite as `--test git_hooks_smoke`, and R1171 folded seventy-six of the cli crate's test files into one `all` target: from that commit cargo answered `error: no test target named git_hooks_smoke`, the harness refused at its pre-flight with "the control reached no test target at all" (measured: 0 passed, 0 targets), and the eight injections that prove the hooks' own gates are not vacuous had been proving nothing. The harness refusing loudly is correct and reaches nobody — a sweep is run when somebody decides to run one, and the point of tracking these files is that nobody has to decide. So the answer is a law rather than three edits: `every_sweep_names_a_suite_this_tree_can_still_run` asks CARGO, per sweep, in the tree that sweep declares, whether every package and every target its command names still resolves. Round 1184.decision_summary: R1184 (DEBT — N22, the names a plan is addressed to, plus two silent-fails the work walked into). R1183 asked whether a sweep's command still names a suite that EXISTS and found three that did not. This is the same question one level in — whether the tests its `expect_red` lists name are still there — and it gets TWO readers, because neither can be both exact and always-on. THE EXACT ONE COSTS NOTHING AND FIRES WHEN A SWEEP RUNS. The harness already runs a control before it applies anything, and libtest prints every name it executed; those lines were read for the `failures:` list and dropped otherwise. Read into a set they are the population every expectation is addressed into — the harness's own words, module paths and macro expansion already done — and held against it at pre-flight, a stale name stops the sweep before a single injection is applied. Before this it arrived as `missed`, the word a MISAIMED injection also gets, after the whole suite had run once per injection. "I could not read the names" is kept apart from "the names are wrong": a log with no per-test lines gives an empty population in which every expectation looks stale, so that case PRINTS what it declined to judge, and `--control-only` keeps its contract untouched. THE ALWAYS-ON ONE IS WEAKER ON PURPOSE. `every_test_a_sweep_names_is_one_this_tree_still_has` walks each sweep's declared tree with `syn` and asks whether each expectation's LEAF name is a `#[test]` function anywhere in it. It does not resolve the module path, and that is a decision rather than an omission: resolving `audit::tests::x` means following `mod` declarations and `#[path]` attributes from each target root — a rule that already exists in `tools/named-environment`, that cost R1182 three defects to get right, and a second spelling of which is the SSOT defect this repository keeps paying for. The module half is left to the pre-flight, which gets it exactly and for free; what is left here is total for the decay that actually happens, and it fires on the commit that renames the test, where the person who can fix it is. IT FOUND TWO ON ITS FIRST RUN AND ONLY BY BEING WRONG FIRST: the draft treated any item-position macro invocation as a reason to refuse, twenty files here invoke one, and a TRUE finding came back as "cannot answer". `frame-view-playable-agreement.sweep.json` named `tests::report_frame_view_branch_reaches_the_answer` and `tests::report_frame_view_order_path_reaches_the_answer`, and asked of cargo with `--list` rather than of a reading, neither exists anywhere. A guard that suppresses every verdict because something somewhere might have generated something is the vacuity this device exists to detect, so a file that did not PARSE is a refusal and a macro is a sentence carrying its count. AND THE RULE THE TWO READERS SHARE IS NOW ONE RULE: `answers_to` lived in `main.rs`, where R1096 had already recorded what a decision with no reader costs. THE SECOND HALF OF THIS ROUND IS TWO SILENT-FAILS IT WALKED INTO, both found by WHERE a test ran rather than by reading it. `git_hooks_smoke` passes here and on one build host and failed on the other with `commit-msg must REJECT an emoji, but it accepted`. The hook's two content rules — no emoji, English only — are `grep -P` over Unicode code-point classes ending in `2>/dev/null`, which makes every way of going wrong identical to "no match". The obvious reading is a grep without `-P`; the measurement says that host has one and lacks a UTF-8 LOCALE, in which a four-byte emoji is four characters and no code-point class matches. So the CAPABILITY is probed — a real emoji through the real expression, because a flag probe would have passed on the very host that was broken — the locale is repaired when it can be, and only an unrepairable machine is refused, loudly. The case names `LC_ALL` so the other machine's condition is reproducible on this one. The second is the hook smoke's cargo stub, whose exemption list for sibling gates was hand-kept and had gone stale once already (R1182); it now asks the SHAPE — a manifest under this repository's `tools/` that is not the CI reporter's is some other gate's business — so a gate added to the hook needs no edit here.

Round 1185.decision_summary: R1185 (DEBT — Z15 measured, and the measurement found the third arm). Z15 was recorded as "the remote rustdoc reach count differs between runs" — `bench` item-citations at 24/28 then 26/28 where local was 28/28 — with three candidate causes and the standing advice to check a remote red locally before believing it. It is re-measured here rather than reasoned about, and the experiment is the SAME one: the same command, pinned to the same host, repeated. TWICE 28/28, once with two other repositories' locks held. Today it does not vary on its own. A FAILURE TO REPRODUCE IS NOT A FIX, so the old condition was rebuilt by hand: bx's own `bx_prune_target`, taken from the program rather than re-written, sent to the host and run against the tree WHILE the gate ran. Its ceiling was lowered so pass two would fire without waiting for the directory to reach 40 GB, and that is the one thing changed. It deleted 23 GB down to 7, the gate went back to compiling, `librocksdb-sys` then would not build, and `item-citations` answered 2 — "a package does not check, so nothing can be said about the citations in it" — which is exactly right. WHAT THE PERSON SAW WAS `bench carries a citation that names no item`. There is no such citation in `bench`. That sentence is the whole of Z15: not a count that wobbles, but a caller that prints a FINDING for an answer that was a REFUSAL, so a remote red reads as a defect in the tree and somebody goes looking for prose that is not wrong. `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` read the citation gate with a bare `if !`, collapsing 1 and 2 — the same shape R1183 closed for the blind-wait and environment arms one day earlier, still open in the third, and the only one of the three ever observed doing damage in the wild. The arm now answers in three codes like its siblings, with a case that drives BOTH through a `cargo` shim (the subject is the arm, not the gate: a fixture that made the real gate answer 2 would have to hold a tree that passes fmt and clippy and then fails to compile for rustdoc, which is a different measurement) and two injections that each kill one of its assertions. THE AMPLIFIER IS WORTH RECORDING SEPARATELY, because it makes every concurrency defect in this repository bigger than it looks: `.cargo/config.toml` sets `[build] target-dir = "target"`, a RELATIVE path resolved against the config's own directory, so all fifteen workspaces — root, bench, studio and twelve tools — build into ONE `<repo>/target`. Measured on the build host: exactly one target directory exists there. Two concurrent runs of this repository therefore collide even when they are checking different workspaces, which is why the serialisation added to `bx` earlier today is not a nicety, and why the 7-target compile failure that started this thread was never a defect in the tree either.

Round 1186.decision_summary: R1186 (DEBT — N23, and what the refusal was standing in for). The injection harness compared each run's target coverage as a SET of names, and refused any sweep whose control ran two targets under one name: "82 targets under 81 distinct names — a drift check cannot see a pair it cannot tell apart". That refusal stopped the widest sweep this repository has, and the pair it stopped for is honest. Cargo announces a test target by a path relative to ITS OWN package and names no package, so the folded `tests/all.rs` suites of `mnemosyne-cli` and `mnemosyne-server` are both announced `all:tests/all.rs`, and no reading of that log can tell them apart. MEASURED, on the tree: 82 targets, 81 names, the one shared name exactly that pair. THE INVARIANT THE REFUSAL PROTECTED IS COMPARABILITY, AND UNIQUENESS WAS ITS PROXY. A count of targets per name is comparable whether or not names are unique: a run that loses one of the two `all` targets comes back with that name at 1 against the control's 2, which is the drift said exactly. What uniqueness bought over a multiset is the ability to say WHICH of an indistinguishable pair went missing — and nothing in cargo's output can say that, so the proxy was refusing sweeps for an answer it could not have given either. What the old check ALSO caught is kept as its own law, because it was two checks wearing one message: a `test result:` line with no `Running` line before it is a target the by-name comparison is blind to, which would make the comparison weaker than the count it replaced. That is now asked of the control AND of every injected run, and the second reader is the one nothing else would have caught — such a run's announced names match the control's exactly, so the drift check is silent, and it reddens the test it was aimed at, so the aim check is silent too. THE FALSE REASON IN THE CODE WAS CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN REPEATED. `target_name` justified dropping cargo's dep hash with "it moves whenever the crate is rebuilt, which is every injection". Across one sweep's control and two injected runs — three whole rebuilds of an edited crate — all four hashes were byte-identical; it is the `-C metadata` fingerprint and a source edit does not touch it. So the hash WOULD have separated the pair, and it is dropped for the reasons that survive measuring: it is cargo's internal spelling rather than a fact about coverage, it is unreadable in the one place the name is ever printed, and it changes nothing this tool DOES. AND THE SWEEP THE FIX UNBLOCKED FOUND SOMETHING WORSE THAN THE BLOCKAGE. The frame-view manifest declares its red sets exhaustive — a claim measured at R1139/R1140 against a 157-target tree that R1148 and R1171 folded to 82. Re-measured whole: five of the seven sets came back unchanged, and the two that did not had been DELETED FROM by R1184, which read a verdict it should never have been given. `tests::report_frame_view_branch_reaches_the_answer` and `tests::report_frame_view_order_path_reaches_the_answer` are generated by `macro_rules! exercised!` in `mnemosyne-mcp`; syn does not walk macro bodies, so the commit-time law that reads `#[test] fn` names out of the syntax could not see them and answered "this tree no longer has that test" about two tests this tree runs. R1184 had already met the macro problem at the TREE level and fixed it there — a macro must not silence every verdict — and then left the same blindness rendering a verdict per NAME. The message hedged and the assertion did not. The way out is neither refusal nor a hedged verdict but a weaker question that can be answered: STRONG ground is a `#[test] fn` of that name in the syntax; WEAK ground is the name appearing among the TOKENS of an item-position macro invocation, which proves nothing about what the macro does and rules out the only verdict this law is entitled to render. Tokens rather than the invocation's text, so a name inside a string literal is not mistaken for one. Over this repository that is 451 expectations judged, 449 by syntax and 2 by tokens alone — the weak ground carries exactly the two names that paid for it.
