Round 1187.decision_summary: R1187 (DEBT — N25, and the second door it opened). N25 recorded that `item-citations` had no fixture for its own exit 2: the caller-side reader R1185 built was driven through a `cargo` shim, correctly, because the subject there was the ARM — which left the number that arm branches on asserted by the shim that produced it and by nothing else. That is measured here rather than argued: with the gate's refusal collapsed into the finding's code (`exit(2)` to `exit(1)`, one line, on the pre-round tree) THE WHOLE PRE-ROUND SUITE STAYED GREEN — 30 tests, 19 unit and 11 over real cargo workspaces. Every case asked `status.success()`, which is one bit, and one bit cannot tell a finding from a refusal. That the injection channel was live rather than the tree stale was proven separately by making the same refusal `exit(0)`, which reddens exactly two of those cases. AND THE MISSING FIXTURE HAD A SECOND DOOR BEHIND IT. Exit 2 was reachable only through an `Err` — before the run starts, or when cargo cannot check a package — but a run that STARTS can also end with no verdict: a target rustdoc could not open is judged `Indecisive`, and `report_verdicts` returned a bool, so a workspace whose every readable citation resolved and whose one unopenable target nobody could speak for left this gate as `false`, wore exit 1, and made BOTH of its callers print `a citation names no item` over a tree that carries none. That is the recorded Z15 sentence arriving through the verdicts instead of through an error, where R1185's repair could not see it. Round 1188.decision_summary: R1188 (DEBT — a budget declaration that was a repaired defect's high-water mark). `.claude/remote-build.toml` declared `peak_gb_per_task = 24`, and the placement program reads that number twice: a host with less available RAM than it is not a candidate at all, and a run's thread budget is `available / peak`. The number came from Round 1076, where one test of `authoring_surface` reached 23.9 GiB resident with 24.2 GiB more in swap on a 31 GiB machine and was killed at 22m33s having finished nothing. AND `.cargo/config.toml`, in this same repository, already recorded the rest of that story: "the defect that produced THAT number was in the test and is repaired there". The code moved and the number did not — a paragraph two directories away said the measurement was obsolete, and the budget that was derived from it went on being read as a standing fact about this repository. RE-MEASURED rather than argued about, on the build machine (32 cores, 125 GB), warm, under `/usr/bin/time -v` at `--test-threads 1`, judged by a completion sentinel rather than by a log going quiet: that same test now peaks at 732,320 kB (0.70 GiB) in 3m20s with zero swapping, and the WHOLE workspace suite peaks at 1,603,380 kB (1.53 GiB) in 15m29s, also with zero swapping, exit 0. The declaration is now 2, which is that measurement with headroom. WHAT THE STALE NUMBER COST WAS NOT SLOWNESS, IT WAS A FLEET THAT WAS NOT THERE, and both sides of that were measured by running the placement program before and after the edit. Before: a build machine with 21 GB available printed as `not a candidate` because 21 < 24; a 28 GB machine allowed exactly one thread; the 125 GB machine held at `112/24 = 4` threads with 28 of its cores idle. After: three candidates at 28 / 14 / 8 threads, and the binding constraint is free cores rather than a repaired defect's high-water mark. A stale safety margin does not present as caution — it presents as machines that are not offered. The placement program itself needed no change; it reads what the repository declares, and the repository was declaring something that had stopped being true. This governs the RUN side only: compile-side width is bounded separately by `jobs = 4` in `.cargo/config.toml`, which is untouched, and that file now carries the re-measurement beside the 23.9 GiB paragraph the budget was read out of.

Zero swapping in both

the first attempt at the whole-suite measurement was cut off at 270s by the wrapper with no exit code, which is why it was re-run detached with a sentinel; a truncated run reports as a failure and says nothing about memory

the effect on placement was measured by running the placement program itself before and after the edit, not derived from the rule: before, a 21 GB machine printed as `not a candidate` and the two others were held at 1 and 4 threads; after, three candidates at 28 / 14 / 8

and the new width was not shipped unmeasured: the whole workspace suite ran at `RUST_TEST_THREADS=28` and came back exit 0 with zero failures in 9m32s, peaking at 819,756 kB — so the width this declaration now buys is green, faster than the one thread it was measured at, and uses less than the model reserves for it

the placement gate was run by hand, because it has no automatic reader, and it FOUND SOMETHING: one of its cases had been written against this repository's declared 24 and failed on a correct change to it, while another had become a permanent skip. Both are repaired by making the budget an argument the way the fleet already is — each case now writes the declaration it needs into a throwaway directory — and the gate is 8 of 8 green, with the skipped case running and refusing for the first time
carry_forward_bullets: this declaration has NO reader inside this repository. Nothing here parses it, so nothing here can go red when it drifts from the machine it describes — which is how a number its neighbouring file had already contradicted survived every run for two days. The only reader is a machine-global program outside this checkout, and that asymmetry is not repairable from this side alone

and a budget is a measurement with an expiry that nobody records. What was found here is not that 24 was wrong when it was written — it was right, and the run that produced it really did die — but that the repair which made it wrong carried no obligation to re-measure. A gate could re-measure periodically; the cost is a full suite under an accounting harness per check. IT IS NOT ATTEMPTED HERE, AND THAT IS A COST JUDGEMENT NAMED AS ONE

the two measurements disagree about how memory scales and neither explains it. At one thread the largest process peaked at 1.53 GiB; at twenty-eight, running the same suite, it peaked at 0.78 GiB. Round 1189.decision_summary: R1189 (DEBT — the declaration that nothing in this checkout read). R1188's first carry said it plainly: `.claude/remote-build.toml` has no reader inside this repository, so a declaration that drifts from the machine it describes cannot go red here, and that is how a budget its neighbouring file had already contradicted survived two days. THE LAW IS NOW ONE SENTENCE: every top-level key this repository declares is one the program that reads it reports reading, with the value the declaration gives. It is ASKED OF THE PROGRAM rather than of a copy of its schema, and that is the whole design — `bx` extracts with line patterns rather than with a TOML parser, and the two languages are not the same one, so a value that moves into a table, gains a decimal point or changes its quoting stays valid TOML and stops matching. A gate carrying its own list of keys would be a second spelling of the thing under test: it would agree with the file while the program disagreed with both. The seam is new and small: `bx --explain-declaration` prints every key it has an extractor for with what it extracted, INCLUDING the ones that found nothing, because a report of only what was found cannot tell "this program does not know that key" from "it knows it and your spelling did not match", and those are the two halves of the failure. `tools/unread-declaration` holds the strict reading of the file against that answer, and `.githooks/pre-commit` Gate 5e reads its three codes on EVERY commit rather than on a staged path — the half that actually rots is a machine-wide program outside this checkout, and it stages no file here. THE GATE FOUND A DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN. `exclude` was declared here and extracted by nothing. All five repositories on this machine declare it, and in one of them the excluded path is TRACKED — `scxml-core-engine`'s `/embed` is sent on every transfer by a repository that declared it never would be. This is the `packages` story repeating exactly: documented for as long as the format was, four repositories declaring it, nothing reading it, and the absence surfacing only when a new build machine failed a compile for a missing header. This repository's own `exclude` was inert, because `send = "tracked"` was doing the protecting the key was credited with, so it is deleted with that measurement recorded in its place; the skill's format block now states that the key is declared and not enforced, and the choice between implementing it and dropping it from the format stays where machine-global decisions belong. AND RUNNING THE PROGRAM'S OWN GATES FOUND A SECOND DEFECT, which is the other half of what this round paid for: `bx` exited 1 without running anything for ANY repository that declares nothing and takes the remote path, because `packages`, `target_cap_gb` and `s` were assigned only inside the `-f "$decl"` branch and `set -u` killed it at the first use. Every backup on this machine carries it, and that file's own header promises a transparent pass-through for exactly the case it broke. It is fixed by initialising those three where the other six already were, and the argv gate now runs its probe from a declaration-less tree as well — its population had been one repository, and it was the one that declares.

`.githooks/pre-commit` Gate 5e reads the gate's three codes on every commit rather than on a staged path, because the reader that rots is outside this checkout and moves no byte in it

the program-side rot mode was injected rather than argued about: a copy of `bx` with ONE line removed, the one reporting `peak_gb_per_task`, turns the gate from 0 to 1 naming exactly that key, against a control of 0 on the same declaration. root `cargo fmt --all --check`, root `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, the gate crate's own fmt and clippy, the separate-workspace gate over every side workspace, and both of the program's own gates green after the change

This is the `packages` story repeating exactly: documented for as long as the format was, four repositories declaring it, nothing reading it, and the absence surfacing only when a new build machine failed a compile for a missing header. This repository's own `exclude` was inert, because `send = "tracked"` was doing the protecting the key was credited with, so it is deleted with that measurement recorded in its place; the skill's format block now states that the key is declared and not enforced, and the choice between implementing it and dropping it from the format stays where machine-global decisions belong. AND RUNNING THE PROGRAM'S OWN GATES FOUND A SECOND DEFECT, which is the other half of what this round paid for: `bx` exited 1 without running anything for ANY repository that declares nothing and takes the remote path, because `packages`, `target_cap_gb` and `s` were assigned only inside the `-f "$decl"` branch and `set -u` killed it at the first use. N17, carried from Round 1182: `named-environment` decides WHICH TEST SPAWNS WHICH BINARY from `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name>")`, and its module doc said that a test finding its binary some other way "is invisible here, and the report says so rather than letting the silence read as coverage". It said the LIMIT and never its SIZE. A spawn the walk did not recognise was missing from the judgement and from every number at once, so a tree holding none of them and a tree made of them printed exactly the same report. THE POPULATION IS NOW EVERY `Command::new(..)` IN A TEST TARGET: the ones spelled the way cargo checks are judged as before, and the rest are counted and printed with what they were pointed at, so the hole is a number a person can act on. AND THE FIRST CENSUS WAS WRONG IN THE DIRECTION THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THAT NUMBER A LIE, which is why it was measured before it was believed: 120 sites in this workspace, 6 attributed, 114 reported unnameable — when almost every one of those 114 is `cli_binary()`, a helper ONE HOP away whose body is the very macro being looked for. This gate already resolves a constant and a parameter on the environment side; refusing the same hop on the program side would have printed a hole it made itself, in a report whose whole purpose is to size holes honestly. With binders resolved — a function, constant, static or `let` whose body names the macro — the answer is 89 attributed and 31 not, and the 31 are LEGIBLE rather than a lump: eleven `"git"`, two `"tar"`, one `"sh"`, four spawns of a shell script this repository's own hooks live in, three `env!("CARGO")`, three `std::env::var("CARGO")` with a fallback, one `let` this walk does not follow — and TWO THAT NAMED CARGO BY THE BARE LITERAL. PATH decides which cargo that is, so a machine whose PATH cargo is a different channel from the one running the test would have had that sentence printed about this repository, about a revision that is fine. Six neighbouring spawns in the same tree already went through `CARGO`; these two were the asymmetry. Both are repaired to the spelling the neighbours use, and the shape is now a LAW rather than a habit: a `Command::new` whose argument is a literal this tree could have named another way — one of its own binaries, or the cargo that is running the test — is a defect, while `"git"`, `"tar"` and `"sh"` have no such spelling and are the limit. Round 1191.decision_summary: R1191 (DEBT — the evidence no tool call could seal, and the comment that said otherwise). N14, carried from Round 1180: `evidence/defect-tables.md` is the SSOT of the blind grader's score, and NO record declared it. The two verbs between them left no way to change that — `declare-run-tree` takes its population from `git ls-files` filtered on `/run/`, and `set-input-role` refuses to create an entry by design, because creating one there would break the exactly-once rule the coverage gate depends on. So the round that needed the document pinned its numbers in code instead, and wrote down why: "the document is not sealed by the kit record ... Frozen in code, the two disagree loudly if either side is edited". THE FIRST HALF WAS TRUE AND THE SECOND WAS NOT. Nothing read the document, so editing it was silent — the law would have gone on asserting a June 2026 score against a table that no longer said it, and the only thing that could have noticed was a person reading both. That is the same shape this arc keeps paying for: a claim of loudness with no reader behind it. MEASURED ACROSS THE TRACKED KITS, because the debt named one file and the population is larger: 193 tracked files sit outside every run tree, 15 of them are declared, and all 15 are `replay-input` — which is to say nothing that is EVIDENCE was declared anywhere in the corpus, in any kit. `declare-evidence` is the missing call: named paths, a caller-given role, and four refusals — a path git does not track, one outside the unit, one under a run tree (that walk decides ownership across every record, and reaching in from here would declare a nested kit's file twice), and one some record already declares. THE PATHS AND THE ROLE ARE THE CALLER'S BECAUSE NO WALK CAN ESTABLISH THEM: a brief, a runbook, a report and an agent's transcript share a directory, and Round 953 refused exactly this kind of inferred claim when it declined to call `mnemosyne.toml` raw agent output. NO NEW ROLE WAS NEEDED, and that was checked rather than assumed — `raw-agent-output` carries no location constraint, and the kit's own runbook states the provenance: the defect tables come from S13, the isolated blind re-extraction session, and the three verdicts from S14-S16, the judging sessions. The six evidence documents of the scale-floor kit are now declared with that role and sealed by `stamp-inputs`, which makes `every_declared_input_still_hashes_to_its_sealed_digest` the reader the scoreboard's claim always needed. Measured by editing one heading in the table: that test goes red naming the file, and the tree is byte-identical again after the edit was undone. The scoreboard's comment is corrected in the same change — the mechanism was repaired, not the wording.
changes_bullets: `declare-evidence` creates declarations for named files outside every run tree, with the role the caller gives, and refuses four ways rather than guessing
the decision is a pure function over the facts the machine supplies, so each of the four refusals has a case instead of being reachable only through git and a real kit tree
the scale-floor kit declares its six evidence documents as `raw-agent-output` — the provenance its own runbook states — and `stamp-inputs` sealed their digests
`scale_floor_scoreboard`'s comment no longer claims a loud disagreement it did not have; it names the reader that now provides one
verification_bullets: the seal was proved to have a reader by editing the document rather than by reading the gate: one heading changed, and `every_declared_input_still_hashes_to_its_sealed_digest` went red naming `evidence/defect-tables.md`. The edit was undone and the file is byte-identical to its copy, and the gate is green again — control, injection, control

the population was measured before the verb was designed, and the first count was wrong: filtering unit-relative paths on `run/` counted a NESTED kit's `v3/run/…` as outside a run tree. Re-asked with the gate's own rule (`/run/` anywhere in the path): 193 outside, 15 declared, all `replay-input`

the role was established from the kit's own runbook rather than inferred — S13 for the tables, S14-S16 for the verdicts — which is why no new vocabulary member was added; `raw-agent-output` already carries no location constraint, and the record gate accepted all six on the first run

six new cases over the decision function, one per refusal plus the shape the verb exists for plus a batch that fails whole, so a mistyped `--path` never leaves half a record. The harness suite is 46 unit and 4 end-to-end, all green
fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, the whole root workspace suite, and the separate-workspace gate over every workspace
carry_forward_bullets: 178 tracked files outside a run tree are still undeclared, and this round declared six of them. The rest are briefs, runbooks, reports and manifests whose provenance no walk can settle — the verb exists now, and what remains is a per-kit judgement a person or an agent has to make with the kit's own runbook in hand. A walk that guessed would put inferred claims in records whose whole value is that their claims are true

the coverage of that gap has no number a gate watches. This round measured it by hand (193 / 15 / 178); nothing re-measures it, so the day a kit lands with unsealed evidence is a day nothing says so. The shape that would close it is a law over kits rather than over files, and it needs the per-kit judgement above to exist first

`stamp-inputs` seals what is declared, so the digest of a file nobody declared is not a fact anywhere. The two halves — declaring and sealing — are separate calls on purpose, and nothing enforces that the second follows the first

Round 1192.decision_summary: R1192 (DEBT — a fixture that wrote the program it then ran, paid the round after it landed). Round 1191's separate-workspace verification turned red on a crate that had nothing to do with it: `unread-declaration`'s `a_key_the_program_does_not_extract_is_a_finding` failed with `could not run /tmp/…/never-heard-of-exclude — Text file busy (os error 26)`. The case is correct in isolation and had been green in every run of that crate alone; it is wrong the moment eleven cases are in flight, which under `check-side-workspaces.sh` on a build machine is the normal case rather than the unlucky one. THE MECHANISM IS OWNERSHIP, NOT SCHEDULING. Round 1189 built each case's answering program by WRITING a shell script into a temporary directory and then executing it. A file this process holds open for writing cannot be executed, and the descriptor does not have to be this thread's: another case's `Command::spawn` forks, the child inherits every open descriptor, and it holds them across exactly the window in which this thread execs the file it has just closed. Round 1193.decision_summary: R1193 (DEBT — the seventh site, and the gate that stops it). N2, carried from Round 1175 in four words: NOTHING STOPS THE SEVENTH ONE. That round repaired six fixture paths that joined a name fixed in the source onto `std::env::temp_dir()`, after two overlapping runs of `check-side-workspaces.sh` made one delete the other's directory between its `create_dir_all` and its write. The root is the MACHINE's, shared by every process on it, so a fixed name under it is not per-run and not per-test state — and the code that builds one almost always removes it too. The six were found by reading, four sibling crates already had the convention, and what was missing was a mechanism rather than more discipline. `tools/unowned-scratch` is that mechanism: a path derived from the process-wide temp root names the process. THE UNIT IS THE FUNCTION, and that is forced by the two spellings this repository actually uses — one chains `.join(format!(..))`, the other binds the root and `push`es onto it on a later statement. An expression-chain rule reads the first and not the second, and a gate that refuses the tidier spelling of the shape it enforces is one people route around. Function-scoped mention is weaker than "the pid is in this path" and it is the strongest thing checkable without following a value through statements; its failure is never a false alarm, because a function that never says `process::id` is certainly not putting it in a path. THE GATE'S FIRST RUN WAS ELEVEN FALSE ALARMS, and that is the round's most useful measurement: every site in this repository spells the name inside `format!`, and `syn` does not walk a macro's body — the same blindness Round 1186 met from the other side when a law asserted that macro-generated test names were absent from a tree that held them. The repair is to read the invocation's TOKENS for a `process :: id` sequence, group by group so adjacency is real where it was written. Re-measured after it: 166 files across seventeen workspaces, eleven functions reach the shared root, ELEVEN of them name the process, zero findings. The tree already obeyed the law; what it did not have was anything that would notice when it stopped. A second self-defect surfaced the same way: `target` in this repository is a SYMLINK to a shared build cache, and the first walk fell through its directory branch and passed over it without a word, printing zero build artifacts — a zero that meant "nobody looked". Directory symlinks are now counted and named in the coverage line.

Round 1194.decision_summary: R1194 (DEBT — N4, carried from Round 1177 as the one shape that round could name and not build). A SECOND TARGET CAN STILL HIDE BEHIND A FIRST ONE'S RED: `cargo test` stops at the first target that fails, the targets behind it are never asked, and the number a reader is shown is one target's. `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` records what that cost the first time it ran without the flag — it reported that `bench` had 6 failures, and the 6 were one target's; there were 18 — and R1177 then shipped three defects that CI found a round later. Its carry named the missing piece exactly: `--no-fail-fast` is DISCIPLINE, a habit that has to be remembered on every invocation and that says nothing at all when a target fails to COMPILE, and the shape that would close it is A CHECK ON THE COMMAND A ROUND VERIFIES WITH. `tools/unreported-targets` is that check, and `scripts/verify.sh` — which is that command — now runs it after every wrapped run. THE POPULATION IS ASKED OF CARGO RATHER THAN WRITTEN DOWN: the set of test targets a command runs is the command's package selection, its features, its `--test`/`--lib` filters and its manifest all at once, which only cargo knows, so the gate re-issues THE SAME WORDS with `--no-run --message-format=json` appended and holds the artifacts against the `Running` lines in the run's own log. Identity is the executable's file name, which carries cargo's metadata hash and is the one string both sides print. WHICH ARTIFACTS COUNT WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, and getting it wrong would have been permanent: a package with a `[[bin]]` makes cargo emit TWO executables for that target — the plain binary, which no test run ever executes, and its test harness, which every run does — so a gate taking every artifact with an `executable` would report the plain binary as a target that never ran, on every clean tree, forever. `profile.test` is the discriminator and the fixture carries both shapes. A QUIET RUN IS A REFUSAL RATHER THAN A VERDICT: `cargo test -q` prints no `Running` line at all, so reading its log as evidence would report every target as never having run — the gate answers 2 there, and the wrapper turns a command cargo called green into a non-zero, because "nothing said this run was covered" must not arrive wearing the same face as "it was". THE THIRD MEASUREMENT WAS AGAINST THIS ROUND'S OWN EXPECTATION: the first fixture asserted that two of four targets ran behind the red and the answer was three — the BIN's test harness runs before any integration test does — and the gate was right where the assertion was wrong. AND THE SWEEP FOUND A LIVE ONE: of the 23 cargo test commands this repository's CI and scripts issue, 19 carry `--no-fail-fast` and 3 name a single target, so nothing can hide behind anything; the twenty-third was `cargo test --workspace --locked`, the largest suite in the tree, and it is fixed here.
changes_bullets: `tools/unreported-targets` is the law: every test target a run compiled is one that run reported a result for, with the population asked of cargo (`--no-run --message-format=json`) rather than kept in a list that would rot

`profile.test` separates the executables a test run executes from the plain binaries it does not, which is the one distinction between this gate and a permanent false alarm on every tree holding a `[[bin]]`

three codes, and the third is the point: nothing to cover is 0 WITH ITS REASON PRINTED, a target that never ran is 1, and a log that cannot say (a quiet run) or that names a target this command does not build is 2

`scripts/verify.sh` runs it after every wrapped command — this is the command a round verifies with, which is what R1177's carry named — and a green run whose coverage cannot be established now leaves through a non-zero
the wrapper's log name carries the process id, so two runs sharing a label and a second cannot append into one file that the gate would then have to refuse
`.github/workflows/mnemosyne-validate.yml` gains `--no-fail-fast` on `cargo test --workspace`, the one multi-target test command in this repository that lacked it
verification_bullets: the cases are REAL CARGO RUNS rather than logs this round wrote: what the gate claims is a fact about cargo, and a hand-written fixture log would prove only that the gate reads this round's sentence about cargo. Every case builds a workspace, runs cargo in it, and judges what cargo actually printed

the pair that matters, same tree and same red target, only the flag differing: `cargo test` reports 4 compiled / 3 reported and names `beta` as the target that never ran; `cargo test --no-fail-fast` reports 4 compiled / 4 reported / 1 doc-test and is clean. The fixture asserts that cargo really did stop early (`tests/beta.rs` appears nowhere in the first log), so the case cannot quietly stop being a case

the first draft of that assertion said two targets ran and the answer was three: the lib's unit target and the BIN's test harness both run before `tests/alpha.rs`. The count is now written out with the reason, and the doc-test count is asserted at 0 there and 1 in the run that carries on — a first-failure run silently drops those too

the refusals were run rather than described: a green `-q` run's log is asserted to hold no `Running` line before the gate is asked, and a whole run's log judged against a `--test alpha` command yields three targets the command does not build and no verdict
a tree that does not compile is an ERROR, not a tree full of targets that never ran — the population comes from cargo and cargo cannot answer for a tree it cannot build
colour end to end: the unit test proves the stripper reads a sequence this round typed, and a second case asserts that cargo really coloured its output on this machine before judging it clean

the wiring measured through `scripts/verify.sh` itself, three arms: the hiding run printed `NEVER RAN test beta of probe` and left with the command's own 101; the covered run printed 4 of 4 and no complaint; and a command cargo exited 0 on left through the wrapper with 2, which is the verdict this round changed

24 of 24 in the gate's own workspace, and every gate `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` applies — fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, item citations, blind waits, named environment, unowned scratch — over the new workspace

the workflow edit was put to the program that reads it rather than to a reading of it: `unrun-tests` parses the changed line as `cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast` running 1978 of the 1980 it can see, and accounts for the new workspace's 24 of 24
carry_forward_bullets: THE CI SUITE STEPS ARE NOT JUDGED BY THIS LAW, AND THAT IS THE NEXT ROUND RATHER THAN A LIMIT. It was attempted here and stopped for a reason worth writing down: `ci-plan` counts a `run:` segment as a cargo command only when its FIRST word is `cargo`, so routing CI's suite through `scripts/verify.sh` would make that command INVISIBLE to `unrun-tests` — the gate that currently accounts for 2778 tests across 23 CI test commands. Closing it means teaching that reader about a wrapper handing its command after a bare `--`, which moves another gate's population and has to be measured as its own change. What this round did instead is fix the one command that lacked `--no-fail-fast`, so CI's exposure is the flag rather than nothing

A RUN NOBODY WRAPPED IS A RUN NOBODY JUDGES. The mechanism sits in `scripts/verify.sh`, and a wrapper is chosen — a bare `cargo test` typed into a terminal is covered by nothing here. What makes this more than the discipline it replaces is that the wrapper is where this repository's verification already goes and that its refusal is loud; what it cannot do is reach a command that never arrived

DOC-TESTS ARE COUNTED AND NOT COVERED. `--no-run` compiles no doc-test and reports no artifact for one, so their population cannot be asked of the program that answers for every other target; deriving it would mean re-implementing cargo's target selection, which is a second spelling of a rule cargo owns and would drift from it. The log's `Doc-tests` count is printed beside the numbers so a reader is never left thinking they were included — and a first-failure run drops them entirely, which the fixture asserts

THIS LAW IS ABOUT ONE RUN'S OWN COVERAGE, NOT ABOUT WHAT ITS COMMAND SELECTED. A command naming too few packages covers everything it compiled and says nothing whatever about the rest. That is `unrun-tests`'s question, asked of the whole tree against every CI command; the two are deliberately different and neither subsumes the other. A round verifying with a narrow command still gets a narrow answer, honestly labelled

THE POPULATION COMES FROM A SECOND CARGO INVOCATION, so a tree edited between the run and the judgement would be judged against a population it no longer has. `scripts/verify.sh` holds its build lock across both, which closes it there and only there; a caller invoking the gate by hand later is on its own, and the coherence check is what would notice

Round 1195.decision_summary: R1195 (DEBT — main was red, and R1193 put it there). Round 1193's module documentation shows the two spellings this repository uses for a scratch path, as a two-line fragment in a fenced block marked `ignore`. THAT FENCE IS NOT A COMMENT TO RUSTDOC: an `ignore` block is registered as a doc-test that only a command passing `--ignored` will run, and no command in this repository's CI passes `--ignored` for that workspace. So the fragment became a test that exists and that nothing runs, `tools/unrun-tests` said exactly that, and the `every test compiled is one CI runs` job on `0a23ea7` failed. THE REPAIR IS THE HONEST FENCE RATHER THAN AN EXEMPTION: those two lines are statements without a function around them, shown to a reader as prose. They were never Rust for rustdoc to compile, `text` says so, and the phantom test stops existing rather than being excused. Measured across the whole tree: that workspace's population falls from 11 to 10, its suite runs 10 of the 10 it can see, and the gate goes from 1 unrun test to 2778 compiled and 2778 run, exit 0. WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT WHERE THE GATE LIVES is the part worth keeping. `unrun-tests` runs in CI and nowhere else — no hook calls it, `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` does not, and the pre-push hook by construction reports the state of the commit being built ON rather than the one being pushed. R1193 was verified locally with every gate its own change touched and none of them was this one, so the red could not be found before the push and was not: it was found here, at the start of the next round, by a run of the gate for an unrelated reason. That is the exposure the push gate's "read the run it started" rule exists to bound, working exactly as written — and it is one round long every time. AND A SECOND ONE, IN THE SAME SESSION AND OF THE SAME SHAPE, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE ROUND 1194'S ENTRY WAS ALREADY WRITTEN WHEN THE SUITE ANSWERED: that round's first spelling of its own wiring bound the gate's manifest to a shell variable and passed `--manifest-path "$coverage"`, which `locked_resolution_smoke` refused — `ci-plan` can place a path a shell assembles only when the literal tail names a directory, and a command it cannot place is one it cannot check for `--locked`. It turned the root suite red (tally `Unreadable: 1`, 330 passed) and was repaired inside that round's own commit, by writing the manifest out in the command and deleting the variable, so there is one spelling and it is the one the reader can see. Both findings are the same sentence: a gate that is only run by somebody deciding to run it is a gate whose red is one decision away from never being seen.

Round 1196.decision_summary: R1196 (DEBT — N38 CLOSED). THE LAW: every `cargo test` this repository issues is issued THROUGH the wrapper that judges what the run covered, and a bare `--` hands the rest over as a command in its own right. R1194 built the coverage law — every test target a run compiles is one that run reported a result for — and put its mechanism in `scripts/verify.sh`, which is where a round's own verification command goes. That left the law reaching exactly as far as somebody remembering to type the wrapper: CI's five `cargo test` steps and all eighteen separate workspaces' suites were outside it, which is to say the largest and most consequential runs in this tree were the ones nothing judged. N38 recorded the reason wrapping them was not simply a matter of typing it: `ci_plan::parse_script` counted a shell segment only when its FIRST word was `cargo`, so `scripts/verify.sh -- cargo test --workspace` DELETED that command from every population built on that crate — the gate that asks which tests CI runs would have lost the command that runs 1987 of them and reported the tests behind it as dark. Both halves land in one change because either alone is a defect. THE READING IS THE GENERAL ONE rather than a list of known wrappers: everything up to a bare `--` belongs to the program in front of it, what follows is a command, and it recurses because a wrapper may carry a wrapper. Cargo's own `--` is explicitly not that — a head that is already `cargo` is split once and never re-read, or `cargo test -- --nocapture` would go hunting a second command inside its own harness arguments. What the reading cannot do is refuse to invent one: `grep -- cargo file` would read as a cargo command here, and that is chosen over a list of wrappers because the mistake is LOUD (the judging gates answer `Unreadable` for a subcommand nobody has measured) where a stale list is silent. THE WRAPPER'S LOCK HAD TO BECOME RE-ENTRANT, and that is this round's own debt paid inside it rather than a nicety: `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` now runs each suite through the wrapper, and RULEBOOK asks a round to run THAT script through the wrapper too, so one of these sits inside another. An flock belongs to the open file description, so the inner run opening the same path waits for a lock its own ancestor holds and is never woken — a hang, not a slow gate. `VERIFY_LOCKS_HELD` carries the absolute paths this process tree already holds, PATHS rather than a flag because this repository's gates run over another tree as well as their own and a marker meaning "some lock is held" would silently stop serialising the second one. AND THE POPULATION IS THE MEASUREMENT: 2782 tests across 19 workspaces run by 23 CI test commands before, 2791 run by 23 after, with the 26 non-test commands unchanged — the nine added are exactly the nine tests this round wrote, and not one command left the population.
changes_bullets: `ci_plan::cargo_invocation` reads a bare `--` as a hand-over and recurses through every hop, and `CargoCommand::carrier` keeps what handed the command over; `parse_script` and `lister_declared_commands` both go through that one reading, so a wrapper the workspace lister prints is read the way a wrapper a workflow writes is

`scripts/verify.sh` takes its build lock re-entrantly across the process tree (`VERIFY_LOCKS_HELD`, exported absolute paths), because this round puts one of these inside another and an flock held by an ancestor cannot be taken again
`scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` runs every separate workspace's suite through the wrapper, and both workflows do the same for all five of their `cargo test` steps

`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/judged_test_runs.rs` is the law, in two halves: every `cargo test` this repository issues names the wrapper, AND the wrapper it names is the one that runs `tools/unreported-targets` — the second half is what stops the first from being a check on a path spelled in five files

`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/verify_wrapper_smoke.rs` gives the wrapper its first reader at all: the wrapped command's own exit status comes back, and the three parts of re-entrancy separately (the skip, the identity of the lock, the export)
`tools/ci-plan/injection-sweep.json` carries three new injections for the new reading rules, and one stale anchor is repaired
verification_bullets: THE POPULATION WAS MEASURED EITHER SIDE rather than reasoned about, both on the build machine (32 cores, 125 GB): before, 2782 tests compiled across 19 workspaces and 2782 run by 23 CI test commands with 26 non-test commands beside them, exit 0; after, 2791 run by 23 with the same 26, exit 0. The commands are the same commands and the +9 is exactly the nine tests this round wrote, which is the shape a wrapper that hides nothing has

SEVEN INJECTIONS, ONE OF THEM REFUTED. Six landed on exactly one test each and no other: an unwrapped workflow suite; the wrapper pointed at another gate's manifest; the re-entrancy skip removed; the lock identity weakened to "some lock is held"; the marker left unexported; the wrapper returning `tee`'s status. The seventh was mine and was wrong — replacing `PIPESTATUS[0]` with `$?` left the suite GREEN, because `set -o pipefail` three lines above already makes the two agree. The honest control for that law is `PIPESTATUS[1]`, which does turn it red, and a defect assumed rather than measured would have been recorded as one

three of those are now IN the tracked sweep rather than only in this round's hands, and were run through the harness: `a-wrapper-carries-no-command`, `cargos-own-marker-starts-a-second-command` and `what-carried-the-command-is-thrown-away` each report 0 missing and 0 extra against a control of 35 passed, 0 failed

the nesting was exercised for real and not only in a fixture: `scripts/verify.sh -- scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` completes, the inner run prints that this process tree already holds the lock, and the suite it wraps is judged 3 of 3

root suite through the wrapper: green, 57 test targets compiled and 57 reported, 25 doc-test runs outside that law; every separate in-repo workspace through the same gate: checked 18, skipped 0, and each of the eighteen now carries its own coverage verdict (21 of 21, 6 of 6, 5 of 5, and so on); `cargo clippy --workspace --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` both clean

THE TWO DEFECTS THIS ROUND'S OWN VERIFICATION SHIPPED, recorded because they are its most useful measurements. Adding a field to `CargoCommand` broke two construction sites in SEPARATE workspaces (`tools/uncompiled-sources`, `tools/unrun-tests`) and the first commands run here compiled neither; `unrun-tests` refused and its refusal carried the diagnosis in its own numbers — 2749 across 17 workspaces by 21 commands, exactly the two suites that did not build. Then the side-workspace gate found the second: a tracked injection anchor in `tools/ci-plan/injection-sweep.json` matched 0 times because this round's edit moved the line it names, which is a proof that had stopped running while looking exactly like one that holds
carry_forward_bullets: A WRAPPER HIDES A CARGO COMMAND FROM THE BUILD PLACER TOO, and that is the shape this round just closed here, standing one level out and unread. The machine-global tool that decides where a heavy build runs recognises cargo by a command's first word, so a run issued as `verify.sh -- cargo test …` is placed as though it were not a build: it keys its history on the command, detects cargo by it, and decides whether the run WRITES from it. The repair is not this repository's to make — that tool is shared by six checkouts and its routing is the owner's — so what this round can do is say that the same reading it fixed in `ci-plan` is missing there

THE REPOSITORY'S OWN REMOTE-BUILD DECLARATION ISSUES A `cargo test` FROM A TABLE KEY, and no reader can be asked for it: the declaration's extractor answers top-level keys only, so that command is in neither this round's law nor the lockfile law's population. It is the one test run in this tree that nothing judges, and it also carries no `--locked`. Naming it rather than fixing it, because wrapping it would blind the placer above and adding the flag alone changes another tool's input with no gate here able to check the result

A COMMAND A WRAPPER TAKES WITHOUT A BARE `--` IS STILL NOT READ. That is the strict direction rather than an omission: the words in front of `cargo` could be anything, and guessing which of them take an argument of their own is how a reader starts answering about a command nobody runs. `timeout 60 cargo test` is the shape, and it is pinned by a test so the limit is stated rather than discovered

THE WRAPPER STILL CANNOT REACH A COMMAND NOBODY HANDED IT. What this round closed is CI and the workspace gate; a `cargo test` typed straight into a terminal is outside the law by construction, and RULEBOOK's instruction to use the wrapper is discipline, not mechanism

Round 1198.decision_summary: R1198 (DEBT — N12 CLOSED). THE LAW: an injection that has never been shown to fire is not a proof, and a sweep proven WHOLE must stay whole. The three laws this repository already held over its sweeps ask whether the anchor still applies, whether the suite still exists and whether the named tests still exist — every one of them a question about TEXT, every one of them answerable without running anything, and every one of them true of an injection that would redden nothing at all. Writing an injection is cheap and running one costs a suite, so that is exactly where a sweep stops being evidence with nothing to say so. THE RECORD IS WRITTEN BY THE HARNESS AND BY NOTHING ELSE, which is the whole of what makes the gate over it worth anything: a row somebody could type is evidence of nothing. It is written AFTER the run's own judgement — a suite that did not finish, a target set that drifted, an injection that missed what it named all disqualify it first — and it keeps the DEFINITION beside the result rather than a hash of it, so a reader of a failure sees what was proven and an edit to the injection strands the old evidence instead of carrying it forward. WHAT IS ENFORCED AND WHAT IS COUNTED, decided rather than assumed: proving all 309 injections this repository tracks means running sixteen sweeps, which is the cost the owner has deferred, so a sweep with no record is COUNTED and NAMED. The teeth are on the claim: only a run over the whole manifest may write `complete`, and a record that claims to be whole while some injection has no row is a manifest that gained one since — which is precisely N12's case, and `--only` makes clearing it the price of one injection. THAT SEPARATION IS A REPAIR OF THIS ROUND'S OWN FIRST DRAFT, in which any record at all demanded completeness: the first cheap `--only` run then put the other sixteen injections of that sweep under an obligation, which is the opposite of what R1179 built `--only` for. AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT TO SATISFY THE LAW FOUND WHY IT WAS NEEDED. `tools/ci-plan/injection-sweep.json` could not be run whole at all: libtest prints a `#[should_panic]` test as `test <name> - should panic ... ok`, the harness read everything before ` ... ` as the name, and an `expect_red` naming such a test could therefore never be matched — so since R1183 the pre-flight had been refusing that entire manifest, and every `--only` run went on passing because that check is scoped to what a run selects. A sweep that cannot be run whole is a proof nobody is making, which is the sentence the law above this one is written in.

the harness writes it after judging the run and merges rather than replaces, so a `--only` run proves one injection without erasing what a wider one established; the record is named from the MANIFEST and not from its directory, because `tools/ci-plan/` holds two sweeps and one record per directory made the second one's evidence answer to nothing

`every_injection_a_record_covers_is_one_that_has_fired` is the law: a record that claims to be whole must cover every injection, a row must match the injection as written today, and a row for an injection the manifest no longer has is evidence answering to nothing. What has no record is counted and named with its cost rather than failed
the sweep classifier learns that a firing record is a legitimate neighbour of a sweep, recognised BY READING IT so a corrupt one is still caught by the rule it would otherwise hide behind
the harness reads a `#[should_panic]` test by its own name — the literal suffix and not ` - `, which a doc-test's own name holds
three injections in the harness's self-check aim at the three decisions above, and `tools/ci-plan`'s two sweeps are proven whole

three injections aimed at exactly those three decisions, each landing on its own test and no other (`0 missing, 0 extra`, control 58 passed / 0 failed): a corrupt record read as an absent one, a name-only comparison carrying old evidence forward, and a record belonging to a directory

carry_forward_bullets: 252 INJECTIONS IN 15 SWEEPS HAVE NO RECORD, and the gate names every one of those sweeps with the count it holds. Producing the evidence means running them, which is the cost this repository's owner has already deferred once and which nothing here should spend on its own. What changed is that the number is now asked for and printed rather than being a thing nobody could have said.

A RECORD SAYS AN INJECTION FIRED ONCE, NOT THAT IT WOULD FIRE NOW. The definition it was proven against is compared, so editing the injection strands the evidence; a change to the CODE it is aimed at that leaves the anchor intact does not, and only running the sweep again would say. THE THREE HEAVIEST SWEEPS ARE THE ONES LEAST LIKELY TO GET A RECORD. The cheap sweeps will accumulate evidence as a side effect of ordinary rounds and those three will not, so the census will go on naming them — which is the honest shape, not a gap to paper over.

Round 1199.decision_summary:
R1199 (DEBT — N45 CLOSED). THE LAW: a record this repository writes under a build directory is one something collects, and a directory nothing collects is named rather than left to grow. WHAT WAS MEASURED FIRST, because the debt as filed named one directory and the tree held three. `cargo sweep --installed --dry-run`, which is what `scripts/gc` delegates the whole of `target/` to, answered `Would clean: nothing` on 2026-08-14 while that tree held 1537 record files and 86 MB across `target/verify-logs` (764 files, 48 MB, oldest sixteen days), `target/injection-logs` (271 files, 26 MB) and `target/bx-logs` (502 files, 12 MB in two days). Nothing had ever removed one of them, and nothing could have: cargo-sweep knows what an ARTIFACT is, and every one of these is a RECORD.

THE POLICY IS A BYTE BUDGET, EVICTED OLDEST-FIRST, AND THE GC'S OWN HEADER HAD TO BE ANSWERED RATHER THAN OBEYED. Round 829 refuses to sweep `target/` by age and says why: an age window "keeps stale artifacts that happen to be recent and deletes live ones that happen not to be". THE FINDING: R1198's law over firing records is correct everywhere and UNREACHABLE in exactly one place, which is the place it matters most. A row proven against an injection that has since been edited is evidence about a different injection, and the law says so by turning red. For every sweep in this repository that red appears somewhere the sweep does not look — except one. `tools/injection-harness/self-check.json` runs the HARNESS'S OWN SUITE as its control, and that suite is where the law lives. So editing a proven injection there reddens the control, the harness refuses to start on a red control, and the `--only` run that would clear the row can never happen. The escape R1199 used — `git checkout` on the record — worked only because that row was still uncommitted. For a committed one the only way out was to delete the whole record and re-prove every injection in it, which is precisely the cost R1179 built `--only` to avoid.

THE FIX IS TO VOID THE EVIDENCE THE RUN IS ALREADY ON ITS WAY TO REPLACING, before the control reads it. After the pre-flight, so a manifest that will be refused for a loose anchor loses nothing; before the control, which is the whole point. Only the injections this run SELECTED, and among those only the rows that actually disagree — decided by the same predicate the gate uses, so the tool and the law cannot come to different answers about which row is stale.

VOIDING IS NOT LAUNDERING, and the difference is exact: this removes evidence rather than inventing any, it removes only what the gate would already call void, and the run doing it is on its way to proving that injection again. A row that still describes its injection is left alone — nothing about it is stale, and dropping it would be throwing away a proof. AND THE COMPLETENESS CLAIM CANNOT SURVIVE IT: `complete` says a whole run established every row, so with one gone the claim has nothing under it, and leaving it set would be the one shape R1198 built this file to catch.

A fixture sweep whose suite READS ITS OWN RECORD — going red while a stale row is in it — is what the self-check is, in eleven lines of shell. Without the voiding pass that case is `the control is 1 red before any injection` and no argument gets past it; with it, the run the sweep needs is exactly the run its own stale row was forbidding.

THE FINDING: R1198's law over firing records is correct everywhere and UNREACHABLE in exactly one place, which is the place it matters most. A row proven against an injection that has since been edited is evidence about a different injection, and the law says so by turning red. For every sweep in this repository that red appears somewhere the sweep does not look — except one. `tools/injection-harness/self-check.json` runs the HARNESS'S OWN SUITE as its control, and that suite is where the law lives. So editing a proven injection there reddens the control, the harness refuses to start on a red control, and the `--only` run that would clear the row can never happen. The escape R1199 used — `git checkout` on the record — worked only because that row was still uncommitted. For a committed one the only way out was to delete the whole record and re-prove every injection in it, which is precisely the cost R1179 built `--only` to avoid.

THE FIX IS TO VOID THE EVIDENCE THE RUN IS ALREADY ON ITS WAY TO REPLACING, before the control reads it. After the pre-flight, so a manifest that will be refused for a loose anchor loses nothing; before the control, which is the whole point. Only the injections this run SELECTED, and among those only the rows that actually disagree — decided by the same predicate the gate uses, so the tool and the law cannot come to different answers about which row is stale.

VOIDING IS NOT LAUNDERING, and the difference is exact: this removes evidence rather than inventing any, it removes only what the gate would already call void, and the run doing it is on its way to proving that injection again. A row that still describes its injection is left alone — nothing about it is stale, and dropping it would be throwing away a proof. AND THE COMPLETENESS CLAIM CANNOT SURVIVE IT: `complete` says a whole run established every row, so with one gone the claim has nothing under it, and leaving it set would be the one shape R1198 built this file to catch.

THE DEADLOCK IS REPRODUCED END TO END RATHER THAN ARGUED. A fixture sweep whose suite READS ITS OWN RECORD — going red while a stale row is in it — is what the self-check is, in eleven lines of shell. Without the voiding pass that case is `the control is 1 red before any injection` and no argument gets past it; with it, the run the sweep needs is exactly the run its own stale row was forbidding.

AND ONE STEP OVER FROM THE TRAP IS ANOTHER, CLOSED IN THE SAME ROUND. A run voids the rows it selected, so a stale row for an injection it was NOT asked about goes on reddening the control — correctly, since that evidence is void too. What the reader sees, though, is a failing test name with nothing connecting it to a file only this tool reads. The refusal now names those rows and the flag that clears them, and says it only when it is true, so it cannot become the line that is always there.

THE NEW LAW IS PROVEN NOT VACUOUS BY AN INJECTION, in the sweep it is about: stop voiding and 3 tests go red — the two the injection names and `every_tracked_sweep_still_applies_to_the_tree_it_names`, which is the documented artefact of injecting into `src/` at all, left in `unexpected` rather than claimed, exactly as this manifest's own prose says to.

Round 1201.decision_summary:
R1201 (DEBT — N13 CLOSED). THE LAW: a red nobody named is still a measurement, and the judgement available for it is against the last one. R1179 left this in as many words — "the unscoped `unexpected` set is still not judged here" — and named what it costs: R1178's `a-dependency-bump-…` reddened three tests beyond the ones it claimed, all three legitimate, "and nothing would have said if a fourth appeared that was not". Under the default claim there is no rule an unnamed red breaks, so a repaired injection's red set can grow, or shrink, in silence.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE IS THAT THERE IS SOMETHING TO COMPARE AGAINST. R1198's firing record keeps the WHOLE set a run measured — `tests` is every test that went red under the injection and not under the control, the named half and the unnamed half together — and that turns an unanswerable question into an answerable one: not "is this red allowed" but "is this the same set as last time". No field was added and no schema moved; the data has been there since R1198 and nothing read it twice.

THE COMPARISON IS ONLY MADE WHERE IT IS ENTITLED TO BE. A row whose DEFINITION no longer matches its injection is evidence about a different injection, and R1200 voids exactly those before the control runs — so a row still in the record when this comparison happens is one the run may hold itself against. The baseline is read ONCE, after that voiding and before this run writes anything, because a baseline read afterwards is this run's own output.

REPORTED AND NOT FAILED, and that is the decision rather than an omission. A new red under an unchanged injection is most often a guard somebody has just written; a sweep that went red for that is a sweep people stop running, and this repository has measured what an over-firing gate costs more than once. Failing on an unnamed red is what `red_set: exhaustive` is for, and the manifests that claim it accept exactly that price. What was missing was never the failure — it was that nothing SAID.

BOTH DIRECTIONS, because the one that matters is not the one that grows. A test that used to go red under an injection and no longer does is where a guard has been weakened, and it is invisible to any check that watches a count go up. The line names both sets and says which is which.

AND SILENCE WHEN NOTHING MOVED, asserted by its own case: a message printed on every run is a message nobody reads, which is the same as the silence this round is about.

Round 1202.decision_summary:
R1202 (DEBT — N6 CLOSED). THE LAW: a kit that declares no replay says WHICH of two reasons it is, in a word a program reads, and its own declared evidence has to agree with the word. R1177 left `no_replay` as prose with one thing standing behind it — `why.len() > 30` — and a claim checked by its character count is a claim checked by nothing. This one is load-bearing: a kit that declares no replay is exempt from the ENTIRE replay half of the evidence gate, which is the single largest exemption any record in this repository can claim.

THE MEASUREMENT CAME FIRST AND IT CHANGED THE LAW, which is the part worth keeping. The obvious rule is "a kit with no replay holds nothing a verb takes", and the classifier that already decides which tracked files are input-shaped can answer it exactly. Asked of the corpus, it says: `factsfirst-craft` holds ZERO such files and `scale-floor` holds SIX — two stores' `sections.json`, `typing-proposals.json` and `edge-proposals.json`, every one of them declared `run-artifact`. One law over both would have turned main red on a record whose claim is honest, because the two kits are not making the same claim: one says nothing it produced can be imported, the other says the import happened OUTSIDE this repository so there is no revision worth pinning. That is R1178's shape exactly — one question asked of a population whose members answer it differently — and the only thing that caught it was asking before writing.

SO THE REASON IS TYPED AND EACH TYPE CARRIES THE CHECK IT CAN CARRY. `nothing-a-verb-takes` is the strong claim and is checkable in full: no declared input is input-shaped. `built-outside-this-repository` is the weaker one and its check is the mirror: at least one IS. The second arm is not symmetry for its own sake — a kit holding nothing importable and claiming the weaker reason would be stating something true that says LESS, and letting a record pick the weaker of two true claims is how the informative one stops being written. What is NOT checkable is named rather than implied: "no revision of this repository ever ran that import" cannot be falsified from inside this repository, and a record claiming it is trusted on that half.

AND THE SCHEMA DELIBERATELY DID NOT MOVE, against the rule that file's own header states twice. That rule exists so a record written to an older shape is TOLD SO rather than having a new field ignored — and this one is told, by name, where it is parsed: a replay-less record without `no_replay_reason` panics with the reason it panicked. A bump would have bought a second way to say the same refusal at the price of rewriting a literal in 30 records and 4 runbooks for a case 28 of them cannot reach, and a tax that size is how a version stops being moved at all. The departure is argued in the constant's own comment rather than made quietly.

THE KEY IS `no_replay_reason` AND NOT A NESTED `reason`, and that is a precision the sibling law forced. The vocabulary table this gate keeps is read by a SECOND law, which rejects a runbook that teaches a value the gate refuses, and it finds fields by name in prose. `reason` is a word a runbook uses about anything at all; a generic key would have turned an unrelated sentence in a document into a red main.

Round 1203.decision_summary:
R1203 (MEASUREMENT, code 0 beyond a pointer comment — what R1177's N5 carry actually costs, in numbers). That carry said the record "pins bytes, not a rebuild" for `scale-floor`, and named the repair: carry the out-of-tree `story-{A,B}.atomic.json` in as a fixture and declare what today's recipe is allowed to differ from it by. Three things were unknown when it was written, and all three are now measured.

WHICH STORES THEY ARE. Four candidate stores sit on this machine, in two extraction trees, and the section ids do not tell them apart — `sc-01` is in all of them. The section TITLES do: `scale-floor`'s `run/store-A` manifests match `belvoir-extraction/store-A/story-A.atomic.json` on 4 of 4, its `store-B` matches `belvoir-extraction/store-B` on 4 of 4, and the `saltglass-extraction` pair matches neither. That is the discriminator chosen by measurement rather than by the first field that looked like an identifier, which is the R1194 lesson one axis over.

WHAT THE REBUILD HALF WOULD COST: it has no subject at HEAD. Asked of the gate that already classifies every tracked corpus input, 47 of 154 no longer parse with today's binary — and FOUR of them are `scale-floor`'s own: `registries.json` and `typing-proposals.json`, in both stores. A rebuild cannot be run here to be compared with anything, at any revision this repository has, which is the same fact `no_replay` states from the other side. So the second half of R1177's carry is not deferred work, it is work with nothing to act on until either a revision that reads those manifests exists (none does — the import never ran here) or the manifests are rewritten into today's shape, which would change the evidence the experiment graded.

WHAT REMAINS IS INTAKE, AND IT IS WORTH DOING ON ITS OWN. The graded stores are 64 KB and 72 KB and sit OUTSIDE version control, on one machine, unsealed. They are the artifact the experiment's scores were read off, they cannot be regenerated by anything this repository can run, and the record that describes the run pins the manifests around them and not them. That is irreplaceable evidence one disk failure from gone — a sharper statement of the debt than "the record cannot pin a rebuild", and a smaller one.

AND THIS ROUND DID NOT PERFORM IT, WHICH IS A DECISION AND NOT AN OMISSION. Bringing 136 KB of sealed evidence in means copying bytes exactly; the two mechanisms available to this session are a shell write, which this repository's hook refuses on a project file, and reproducing the bytes through an agent's context, which is not byte-exact by construction and is wrong on the one axis — fidelity — that the whole record exists to guarantee. The remaining shapes are a person's `cp`, or a harness verb that copies and stamps in one step. Choosing between them is the owner's, and inventing the second one to get past a guard that is right would be the wrong reason to build a program.

Round 1204.decision_summary:
R1204 (BUILD — N5's intake half, closed). THE LAW: evidence enters this tree through a program, and the program records where the bytes came from. Declaring, sealing, assigning a role and re-verifying a seal are all verbs here; the moment evidence CROSSES INTO the tree was the only step with no program, and it is the step that handles bytes nothing can regenerate. R1203 measured what that cost on one kit: `scale-floor`'s two graded stores — the artifacts its scores were read off — sat outside version control on one machine, 64 KB and 72 KB, sealed by nothing, unrebuildable at any revision this repository has.

THREE THINGS A COPY CANNOT DO, each already paid for somewhere here. It cannot REFUSE: evidence overwritten by a later, different file is the one edit a seal exists to prevent, and the seal is written afterwards, by the same hand. It leaves the RECORD to a second step, so the tree can hold evidence nothing declares — the state R1191 found and counted: 193 files outside every run tree, 15 declared, none of them evidence. And it forgets WHERE THE BYTES CAME FROM: after a copy the record can say "this is a run artifact of this kit" and nothing anywhere says these bytes were carried in or from what, which leaves the provenance in a session transcript — the exact kind of claim R1202 spent a round moving out of prose.

SO `carry-run-artifact` DOES ALL OF IT IN ONE CALL: copy the bytes verbatim, refuse a destination outside the unit's run tree, refuse one already holding DIFFERENT bytes (identical bytes make it a no-op, which is what makes re-running safe), stage the file so the declaring walk can see it at all, then drive the EXISTING declare and stamp rather than a second copy of either, and write `carried_from` beside the entry.

AND THAT FIELD BUYS THE LAW THAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A NOTE: where the source still exists on the machine asking, the carried bytes must still hash to what the record sealed. It catches the one thing a seal alone cannot — a carried artifact edited in place and re-stamped, which leaves a record that is internally consistent and no longer describes what the run produced. ITS THREE-WAY ANSWER IS THE WHOLE POINT: matches, differs, or the source is not on this machine — because a two-answer check would have to fold "I could not look" into one of them, and folding it into agreement is the failure this repository keeps paying for. Measured on both kinds of machine in this round: on the build machine 0 re-checked and 2 NOT JUDGED, on the workstation that holds the extraction trees 2 re-checked and 0 unreachable.

THE OBJECTION THIS ROUND STARTED FROM WAS ITS OWN, AND IT WAS WRONG. A hook here refuses a shell write to a project file, and the first reading of that was "building a program to get past a guard that is right". The guard's requirement is that an agent not write project files by unreviewable side effects — and for 64 KB of JSON the review is not a diff, it is the DIGEST. The verb prints it and the record keeps it, which serves the guard's purpose better than either a copy or an agent reproducing the bytes through its own context, the second of which is not byte-exact by construction and is wrong on the one axis the whole record exists to guarantee.

WHAT IT DID NOT DO: the rebuild half of R1177's carry stays exactly where R1203 left it, with its measured cause. Four of this kit's own manifests cannot be read by today's binary, so no comparison can be run against the stores now carried in — what changed is that the comparison now HAS a target, on the day a revision that reads those manifests exists.

Round 1205.decision_summary:
R1205 (BUILD — N52 closed, and every debt this round created paid inside it). THE LAW: a check runs over EVERY separate workspace before the next check runs anywhere, cheapest first — and "cheapest" is a measurement this gate now prints on every run rather than a belief written into its order.

WHAT WAS WRONG. `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` ran workspace-major: each of the 19 separate workspaces got all six checks before the next one was touched. So the CHEAPEST question about the LAST workspace was answered behind every expensive question about the other eighteen. Formatting is the question that costs least and the one a round trips most often, because the command a person types to fix it — `cargo fmt --all` at the root — reaches a SMALLER population than this gate checks: the root workspace and nothing else. Twice in one session (Round 1200, Round 1204) that arrangement bought one sentence about formatting with a multi-minute wait.

THE FIRST TWO GUESSES WERE BOTH WRONG, AND MEASUREMENT IS WHAT SAID SO. This round opened by repeating the debt's "8 minutes"; the warm floor is 38.5 s, and the eight minutes belonged to a tree that had something to rebuild. The second guess was that `clippy` was the expensive check; over all 19 workspaces warm it is 6.38 s, while `named-environment` is 22.97 s and `item-citations` 12.32 s.

SO THE ORDER IS KEYED ON SOMETHING THE WARM TOTAL DOES NOT SHOW, and that was measured too: the same workspace, one source file touched, before and after. fmt 154 -> 117 ms, waits 138 -> 107, scratch 110 -> 111, named 1689 -> 1590 — all unchanged. clippy 192 -> 770, citations 289 -> 9158. R1206 (BUILD — the half R1205 named as undone work rather than as a limit). THE LAW: one command formats what one command checks, and the fixing side does not keep its own list of what that is.

WHAT WAS WRONG, and it is the oldest shape in this repository's ledger: ONE DATUM, TWO HOMES. The datum is "which package manifests must be formatted". `cargo fmt --all` at the root answers it for the root workspace; this repository has twenty, and the other nineteen carry their own `[workspace]` precisely so the root's commands never reach them. So the CHECK side had a program that walks and discovers, and the FIX side had a person reading a gate's rejection and assembling `cargo fmt --manifest-path` commands by hand out of a population only the gate knew. R1205 closed the reading side's cost — the formatting verdict for all 19 workspaces now lands in the first 2% of a side-gate run — and named this side as work nobody had done, so that it could not be mistaken for something the world prevents.

`scripts/fmt.sh` DOES NOT KNOW WHICH WORKSPACES EXIST, and that is the design rather than a shortcut. It takes the formatting commands the gate DECLARES — `--list`, the same output `tools/ci-plan` already reads — and runs those same words with `--check` removed. The set it writes is the set the gate reads BY CONSTRUCTION, not by two lists that happen to agree; a workspace added to this repository joins both at once, and there is no second walk to drift. The root workspace is `cargo fmt --all`, which is cargo answering "which packages are in this workspace" — the one question this script must not answer for itself.

AND IT REFUSES A CHECK THAT IS NOT CHECKING. If a declared formatting command carries no `--check`, the gate is running a formatter and reading its exit code as a verdict; this script would be the only thing in a position to notice, so it says so rather than quietly dropping a flag it never found.

THE LAW OVER BOTH IS A TEST THAT RUNS THE PROGRAMS. `formatting_population` holds the two `--list` outputs against each other in both directions: a manifest the gate checks and the formatter does not write is a file this repository can REJECT and has no command to FIX, and a manifest the formatter writes and the gate never checks is a file nothing is watching. Reading either script's source for a list of workspaces would have been a third spelling of the walk, and the reason there is one walk is that a second one disagrees.

ITS TEETH ARE MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED. Three injections, run whole, each firing exactly the one test the manifest names and nothing else: a fixer that stops reaching a workspace (`bench`, nine of the twenty-seven manifests), a fixer that keeps `--check` — the failure that looks EXACTLY like success, since it exits 0 on a formatted tree, prints the same lines and writes nothing — and a fixer that drops the root, which is the half that already worked and therefore the half a repair drops while its author watches the other one.

WHAT THE DEBT ASKED FOR AND DID NOT GET. N52 asked for a line in `RULEBOOK.md` and a mechanism that knows to run the cheap reader first. It got neither, because after R1205 neither is needed: the gate answers formatting first by construction, and the rejection it prints now names ONE command instead of one per manifest. A checklist line would have been a second home for an instruction the gate already carries.

Round 1207.decision_summary:
R1207 (BUILD — N7 closed). THE LAW: the interval a cache miss is judged over starts at the run that WROTE that key's archive, and what wrote it is a step of a job, never a run's conclusion.

WHAT R1178 LEFT, AND IT LEFT IT KNOWINGLY. That round bounded the interval with the newest run of the declaring workflow that CONCLUDED SUCCESS, and wrote the residue down: "what actually leaves an archive is the cache-declaring JOB; a run can conclude success with that job skipped, or fail with it having already saved… every case it would change makes the interval NARROWER, which is the direction that produces the spurious red this round exists to repair." The reasoning was that leniency in a case nobody had produced beats strictness whose failure mode is a red main on a correct repository.

THE CASE HAD BEEN PRODUCED 122 TIMES. Asked of the API over this repository's newest hundred runs of `mnemosyne-validate` on `main`: 19 runs concluded failure or cancelled, and inside them 122 cache-declaring jobs ran their `Post Cache …` step to success — archives really written, at commits the gate passed over. The opposite case, a successful run whose declaring job did not save, has happened 0 times. So the residue was not a hypothetical; it was the common case, and it ran in the LENIENT direction: bounding with an older run widens the interval, and a wider interval excuses a miss whose hashed inputs moved before the archive was actually last written.

AT THE GRANULARITY THE ANSWER ACTUALLY HAS, the disagreement is 134 of 900. Nine declarations over those hundred runs, each asked as the gate asks — the newest five of that workflow, started strictly earlier, at another commit: 739 bounds unchanged, 134 where today's is OLDER than the truth, and 16 more where this gate had no bound at all and fell back to the push range while the step had one.

AND ONE RECORDING CARRIES BOTH HALVES OF WHY IT HAD TO BE PER KEY. Run 31782330835 concluded FAILURE. Inside it, seven cache jobs finished and their save steps concluded `success`; the job that failed carries its two save steps at `skipped`. Two keys, one run, opposite answers — so no reading at RUN level can be right about both, and the bound moved from the workflow to the cache step. That recording is now `tools/cache-budget/tests/actions-run-jobs.json`, byte for byte, sha256 5877bc0a….

THE JOIN IS THE STEP'S NAME, and it is why `ci-plan` now REFUSES a cache step that has none. GitHub reports the save as `Post <the step's name>`; two unnamed cache steps in one job are indistinguishable in that answer, and a join that took whichever came first would bound one cache's interval with another cache's save. Every cache step in this repository is named; a fixture that was not is what found the rule.

WHAT IT COSTS, stated because it is a real cost: up to one extra API call per candidate run, and the answers are held so nine declarations over two workflows buy at most twelve calls rather than forty-five. Two refusals guard it, both in the widening direction that this round exists to remove: a jobs page GitHub truncated is unreadable rather than "that step did not save", and a job that says it COMPLETED and carries no step list is unreadable rather than the same.

IT WAS RUN AGAINST THE LIVE API BEFORE IT WAS COMMITTED, old and new, on the same data: both exit 0, and on today's history the bounds agree — which is the 76% case and says this change does not turn `main` red for a correct repository. What it changes is the 15% where a failed run sits between the last green one and HEAD.
