Round 1225.decision_summary:
R1225 (BUILD — a push gate stops answering a question about somebody else's working tree). On 2026-08-16 three finished, locally-verified rounds could not be published. `pre-push` runs `scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` over every separate in-repo workspace, `studio` path-depends on the sibling `pinion` checkout, and a session in THAT repository was mid-edit — three unused imports in `pinion-core`. Nothing in this tree was wrong and nothing in this tree could fix it. The owner chose the narrow answer: take `studio` out of the PUSH gate and leave it in every other reader.

THE FLAG NAMES NO WORKSPACE, and that is the difference between this and a hardcoded exception. The gate already decides ownership per workspace and prints it — `LOCK <ws> ours` or `LOCK <ws> foreign — it resolves against trees this repository does not own` — because Round 1110 needed the same answer to decide where `--locked` may be used. `--ours-only` consumes that existing answer, so a second sibling-dependent workspace is treated the same way the day it arrives and no list has to be maintained.

IT IS THE SAME REASON `--locked` WAS ALREADY OFF THERE, one step further. A workspace whose resolution changes when somebody else commits cannot have its lockfile pinned by this repository; a workspace whose COMPILATION depends on somebody else's uncommitted edits cannot have its verdict given by this repository either. The gate had already conceded the first half and was still asserting the second.

WHAT IS GIVEN UP, recorded rather than implied, because this is a loosening: `studio` now has no UNCONDITIONAL automated reader. CI has no sibling checkout and skips it — that path already existed and is why the gate distinguishes "not on this machine" from "not ours". What remains is the pre-commit gate when a side `.rs` is staged, and the whole-gate run the round checklist asks for, which is DISCIPLINE rather than mechanism in this repository's own vocabulary. Round 784 had to repair this crate precisely because no gate was watching it, so the risk is not hypothetical. The trade is taken because a gate that blocks on another repository's working tree reports something other than what it claims to, and a reader who cannot tell those apart learns the wrong thing from a red.

THE SKIP IS LOUD BY CONSTRUCTION. The gate's closing line already names what it checked and what it skipped, and it already fails when it checked nothing at all — "a green run that checked nothing is the failure it exists to prevent". `--ours-only` adds a SKIP line carrying the workspace, the reason, and the foreign paths that caused it, so a green push never quietly means less than it did yesterday.
changes_bullets: `--ours-only` skips the workspaces that resolve against trees this repository does not own, consuming the ownership answer the gate already prints
pre-push passes it, so a sibling repository being mid-edit no longer blocks a push this repository has fully verified
the skip names the workspace, the reason and the foreign paths; the whole gate is unchanged and still covers everything
verification_bullets: TWO INJECTIONS, ONE PER HALF, because a flag that is passed and inert and a flag that works and is never passed fail identically from a distance. Removing `--ours-only` from the hook goes red with "`pre-push` does not run the side gate with `--ours-only`, so a sibling repository's working tree can still block a push from this one"; disabling the skip inside the gate goes red with "`--ours-only` still checks `studio`, which resolves against a tree this repository does not own". Both trees restored byte-identical

THE LAW WRITES DOWN NO WORKSPACE NAME. It reads the gate's own `LOCK <ws> foreign` lines to learn which workspaces are foreign, requires the flag to drop exactly those and NOTHING else, and fails loudly if the tree ever has none — a flag with nothing to drop would make the case pass for the wrong reason, and the message says so and asks for both to be deleted
IT ALSO ASSERTS THE PLAIN LISTER STILL OFFERS THEM, so "the flag dropped it" cannot be satisfied by the workspace having been unreachable all along

`--list` IS THE ORACLE RATHER THAN A FULL RUN: what is under test is WHICH workspaces are chosen, and choosing is exactly what the lister prints. A full run would spend minutes compiling to re-answer a question already on screen

THE EVENT THIS ROUND ANSWERS IS ON THE RECORD, not hypothesised: the push of R1222-R1224 was refused at 2026-08-16 with three `pinion-core` unused-import errors, and the same push succeeded twenty minutes later when the other session finished, with nothing in this repository changed between the two attempts
root workspace suite + clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings + the separate in-repo workspaces (the WHOLE gate, not `--ours-only`), run through scripts/verify.sh
carry_forward_bullets: `studio` HAS NO UNCONDITIONAL AUTOMATED READER NOW, and that is the price rather than a side effect. CI cannot see it (no sibling checkout), pre-push no longer asks, and what is left is the pre-commit gate WHEN a side `.rs` is staged plus the whole-gate run the round checklist asks for. This repository has a word for that difference — mechanism versus discipline — and has recorded that a checklist line is the second one. Round 784 repaired this crate because no gate was watching it; the shape that produced that rot is partly back

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT PROPERLY IS ATTRIBUTION, NOT EXEMPTION: compile `studio` and read WHERE the errors point — a failure whose every diagnostic names a path outside this checkout is not this repository's verdict, and one that names a path inside it is. That is decidable and was not attempted here, because it keeps the sibling compile on every push (minutes) and the owner chose the narrow answer. It is undone work rather than a limit, and this is where the next round would start if the loosening turns out to cost something

NOTHING MEASURES WHETHER `studio` ROTS AGAIN. The honest instrument would be a record of when the whole gate last ran green over it, so a reader could see the gap grow; there is none, and the crate's own history says the gap is what precedes the rot

THE FLAG IS ABOUT OWNERSHIP, NOT ABOUT SPEED, and must not become the way a slow workspace is dropped. The predicate is `LOCK … foreign`, which is a fact about where a manifest resolves; anything wanting to skip for another reason needs its own predicate and its own argument

Round 784 had to repair this crate precisely because no gate was watching it, so the risk is not hypothetical. The trade is taken because a gate that blocks on another repository's working tree reports something other than what it claims to, and a reader who cannot tell those apart learns the wrong thing from a red.

THE SKIP IS LOUD BY CONSTRUCTION. The gate's closing line already names what it checked and what it skipped, and it already fails when it checked nothing at all — "a green run that checked nothing is the failure it exists to prevent". `--ours-only` adds a SKIP line carrying the workspace, the reason, and the foreign paths that caused it, so a green push never quietly means less than it did yesterday.

pre-push passes it, so a sibling repository being mid-edit no longer blocks a push this repository has fully verified
the skip names the workspace, the reason and the foreign paths; the whole gate is unchanged and still covers everything

Both trees restored byte-identical

THE LAW WRITES DOWN NO WORKSPACE NAME. It reads the gate's own `LOCK <ws> foreign` lines to learn which workspaces are foreign, requires the flag to drop exactly those and NOTHING else, and fails loudly if the tree ever has none — a flag with nothing to drop would make the case pass for the wrong reason, and the message says so and asks for both to be deleted
IT ALSO ASSERTS THE PLAIN LISTER STILL OFFERS THEM, so "the flag dropped it" cannot be satisfied by the workspace having been unreachable all along

`--list` IS THE ORACLE RATHER THAN A FULL RUN: what is under test is WHICH workspaces are chosen, and choosing is exactly what the lister prints. A full run would spend minutes compiling to re-answer a question already on screen

Round 784 repaired this crate because no gate was watching it; the shape that produced that rot is partly back

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT PROPERLY IS ATTRIBUTION, NOT EXEMPTION: compile `studio` and read WHERE the errors point — a failure whose every diagnostic names a path outside this checkout is not this repository's verdict, and one that names a path inside it is. Round 1226.decision_summary:
R1226 (BUILD — the output-schema arc, step four: the four answers this wire assembled by hand become types, and one of them was a second spelling all along). What remained after Round 1224 split three ways: three tools that answer PROSE, and four that built their answer with a `serde_json::json!` literal at the wire. This does the four. A literal is a shape with no type — it cannot carry an output schema, nothing can compare it against anything, and it is where a duplicate hides without ever being called one.

`redact_term` HELD THE FINDING. Its handler listed the five fields of a redaction hit — entry_id, field, index, original, redacted — into a `json!` object, one by one. `RedactionHit` is a struct with exactly those five fields, and the reason the handler re-spelled them is that NEITHER `RedactionHit` NOR `RedactionReport` DERIVED `Serialize`. So the wire had a second spelling of a type that existed all along, and no test could compare the two because only one of them was a type. They derive it now and the literal is gone rather than schematised: the report IS the answer, flattened under a struct that adds the one field the literal contributed (`primitive`).

The other three were smaller and the same kind. `describe_schema` already returned `SchemaContract` and wrapped it for no reason; it now returns it, and with no failure path it returns `Json<T>` rather than `Result<Json<T>, _>`. `describe_frontier_axes` and `emit_publishable_override_ledger_draft` each get the struct their literal was pretending to be — `{axes}` and `{entry_id, in_sync, ledger_draft}`.

THE COUNT IS 102 OF 105, and what is left is exactly the three prose tools. `validate_workspace`, `validate_projection` and `list_sections` each RENDER a summary from a report they already hold, so typing them is not a conversion: it decides whether the tool's answer BECOMES that report, which changes what an agent reads. That is the owner's call and the arc stops here without it.
changes_bullets: the four tools that built their answer with a json! literal now return types, and publish schemas for them — 102 of 105
RedactionHit and RedactionReport derive Serialize at last, so the MCP wire stops re-spelling five fields the struct already had
describe_schema returns the contract it always built, with no Result around an operation that cannot fail
`tool_json`, the hand-serializer every tool used to answer through, has no callers left and is deleted — the compiler is what noticed
verification_bullets: THE WIRE IS UNCHANGED AND THE EXISTING LAWS ARE WHAT SAY SO: `redact_term` is in the sweep, so both the description law and the schema law ran over its actual answer, and the description Round 1221 wrote for it names `primitive`, `dry_run`, `hits` and `ledger_drafts`. A flatten that dropped or renamed any of them would have gone red there rather than in a new test

INJECTED AND RESTORED BYTE-IDENTICAL: `#[schemars(skip)]` on the flattened report — the one thing that could make a `#[serde(flatten)]` answer and its schema disagree — goes red with "`redact_term` answered with [dry_run, hits, ledger_drafts], which its declared output schema does not describe. Schema properties: {primitive}". That is the evidence schemars carries the flatten through rather than an assumption that it does
THE COUNT MOVED 98 TO 102 IN ONE COMMIT and is asserted, so none of the four could have been converted without the arc's ledger saying so, and none can lose its schema quietly

`describe_schema` RETURNS `Json<T>` WITH NO `Result`, which is worth stating because every other converted tool has one: the operation reads a static contract and cannot fail, and wrapping it in a Result would have been a refusal branch nothing can reach — the vacuous arm this repository keeps deleting
mnemosyne-mcp 246 tests green; root workspace suite + clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings + the separate in-repo workspaces (the WHOLE gate), run through scripts/verify.sh
carry_forward_bullets: THREE TOOLS REMAIN AND THEY ARE ONE QUESTION FOR THE OWNER, not three pieces of work. `validate_workspace`, `validate_projection` and `list_sections` each hold a typed report and RENDER a human-readable summary from it. Typing them means deciding whether the tool's answer becomes the report — which changes what an agent reads, from a paragraph it can quote to a structure it must walk. Nothing here can decide that: this repository has no measurement of which an agent uses better, and inventing a shape to make a count reach 105 is the drift it keeps deleting
THE ARC'S NUMBER STOPS AT 102 OF 105 AND THAT IS ITS FINISHED STATE unless the owner answers above. A later reader should not treat the gap as unfinished work

`RedactionReport` IS NOW SERIALIZABLE AND THE CLI DOES NOT USE THAT. It has one consumer, the MCP wire; the CLI renders its own text. So the derive is not a second path into a shared shape today, and if a second consumer arrives the two must be held to one answer — the parity discipline this repository already applies to fields with two write paths
NOTHING PROVES A CLIENT VALIDATES ANY OF THIS (R1223's carry, unchanged), and the error half still carries no schema (R1222's, unchanged)

Round 252.decision_summary: Parser CommonMark conformance — recognize indented fenced code blocks (§98) and require whitespace after ATX hash sequence (§62)
changes_bullets: crates/mnemosyne-validator/src/parser.rs: fenced-code-block detection now allows 0–3 leading spaces (CommonMark §98). Previously `line.starts_with("```")` required the fence at column 0, so indented fences (common inside list items) were ignored and their body lines were re-interpreted as ATX headings.

crates/mnemosyne-validator/src/parser.rs::parse_heading: require space, tab, or end-of-line after the `#{1,6}` sequence and reject lines with 4+ leading spaces (CommonMark §62). Previously `#1 prose` and `    # x` were lifted to headings, creating spurious numbered H1 sections from inline `#N` prose references.

crates/mnemosyne-validator/src/parser.rs tests: 5 regression tests added — `atx_heading_requires_space_after_hashes`, `atx_heading_rejects_four_plus_leading_spaces`, `parse_markdown_indented_fence_is_recognized`, `parse_markdown_round_trips_indented_fence_with_hash_lines`, `parse_markdown_inline_hash_number_in_prose_is_not_heading`.

crates/mnemosyne-cli/src/main.rs::cmd_validate: when round-trip fails, dump the section_id and cross_ref BTreeSet diff (a-only / b-only, capped at 15 / 20 entries) so authors can locate which typed-fact tuples drifted between parse → emit → re-parse. Diagnostic only fires on failure path — happy-path output unchanged.
verification_bullets: cargo test --release -p mnemosyne-validator: 28 parser tests pass (23 pre-existing + 5 new regression tests).

watching-zenoh adoption regression: round-trip mandatory 10/13 → 13/13 with parser fix alone, no source-markdown edits required. T1 orphan total 87 → 75 across changelog-config alignment + parser fix.
mnemosyne self-application validate-workspace unaffected: docs=1/1, T1 orphan=0, round-trip=1/1, style violation counts unchanged from pre-fix baseline.
carry_forward_bullets: list-item-nested fences (CommonMark §49) — where the fence indent matches the enclosing list item's content-indent column rather than 0–3 spaces — remain unhandled; the parser still treats them as plain prose. Full coverage requires list-item state tracking, which is a larger refactor than this conformance round. Acceptable carry: no current Mnemosyne self-doc or known external workspace depends on this case.
diagnostic dump in cmd_validate could later evolve into a structured `--diff-format=json` flag for tooling consumers; current eprintln-only form is sufficient for human authoring loops.

Round 335 — adopt the typed DecisionStat.decision_summary: Convergence C status half. The cascade Salsa input SectionRecord carried decision_status as a String, bridged from the typed SectionSkeleton at build time via DecisionStatus::as_str with a None-to-active string fallback — the explicit deferral recorded in Round 327 (the cascade input keeps a stringly-typed status, bridged at the conversion boundary until convergence C adopts the typed enum). Round 326 already made the skeleton carry Option<DecisionStatus>; this round closes the gap by making SectionRecord mirror that type directly, so the projection is lossless and section_decision_violation compares the typed Some(DecisionStatus::Superseded) — the same pattern the runtime module's section_decision_status already uses on the skeleton. This is the bounded, independently-verifiable status half of convergence C; the larger incremental-projection half (wiring the Salsa cascade into the live render path) stays deferred because it is entangled with B (live index reads) and D (the unified write path). Removing the only DecisionStatus::as_str caller surfaced a duplicate: mnemosyne-query held a private decision_status_str that re-implemented as_str verbatim. Route the query SectionView string projection through the canonical as_str and delete the duplicate, so one canonical lowercase label serves the one view boundary that still needs a string.

Round 337 — decide the incremental-proje.decision_summary: Decide convergence C's incremental-projection architecture jointly with D, resolving the two questions R336 surfaced, derived from the cost-no-object textbook + Phase-0 AI-efficiency mandate. (1) CQRS split: the cli/ops write side appends to the git-native log (SSOT) and stays RocksDB-free (R328); the read side owns the RocksDB index + Salsa cascade and projects, meeting at the core::Transport seam. (2) Salsa memoization is in-process, so C is a warm read-side projection service, not a new authoring-CLI edge; the host binary is bound when the first warm consumer exists (MCP the natural first home per Phase 0; a standalone server daemon deferred per YAGNI invariant #3), and the cli keeps its one-shot full-rebuild path for human/CI use. (3) Engine = fine_grained.rs; the coarse runtime.rs design (monolithic snapshot_payload, non-incremental by construction) is retired at C's implementation (no-legacy-carry). (4) Layer-1 design_doc content feeds the projection engine as Salsa inputs — the engine is a Layer-3-producing read model, not the Layer-0 core, so invariant #4 holds; validation needs only the Layer-0 skeleton. (5) Sequencing (no half-finished): validation projection first (Layer-0 walking skeleton proving the warm-host + RocksDB-free split), then the render projection (the chosen target) superseding the full-rebuild auto_regenerate. Design only — no code; D is co-designed with C, not sequential.

Round 340 — convergence D incremental re.decision_summary: Replace ProjectionService::reload's wholesale rebuild with reconcile_branch_index, which reuses the live BranchIndex handle and every unchanged per-record handle and mutates only the fields that changed — so a re-sync re-executes only the changed entities' sub-queries (size-independent invalidation) and the warm Salsa memo cache survives. This delivers the incremental advantage the fine-grained engine exists for on the validate_projection(refresh=true) path R339 wired; build_branch_index stays the wholesale path for initial construction. Section and ChangelogEntry reconcile field-by-field by stable key (entity_id / round_number); CrossRef and FrozenList reconcile at set granularity since relation rows have no stable identity; the BranchIndex lists reset only on membership change, so a field-only edit does not invalidate the aggregator's list dependency.
changes_bullets: mnemosyne-cascade: add reconcile_branch_index — re-sync an existing BranchIndex to a new fact snapshot by applying the minimal Salsa-input delta. Section and ChangelogEntry reconcile field-by-field keyed by entity_id / round_number (a matching key reuses the record handle and sets only the fields that changed; a new key allocates; a dropped key falls out of the list); CrossRef and FrozenList reconcile at set granularity since relation rows carry no stable identity (identical projected tuples keep the old handles, otherwise the list is reallocated).

The BranchIndex Vec and map fields are reset only when membership changes, so a field-only edit leaves them bit-identical (the same mutated handles) and the aggregator's dependency on the list is not invalidated — only the changed record's sub-query re-runs.

mnemosyne-projection: ProjectionService::reload now re-syncs via reconcile_branch_index instead of project_branch (the build_branch_index wholesale path), reusing the warm BranchIndex handle so unchanged entities keep their memoized sub-queries across a re-sync; build still uses the wholesale path for initial construction.

Effect: the validate_projection(refresh=true) path R339 wired is now actually incremental — a single-section edit re-executes only that section's sub-query rather than the whole branch, the defining property the fine-grained Salsa engine exists for, now exercised on a live path.

Round 346 — sever the cascade→facts re-e.decision_summary: Make the CQRS RocksDB-free invariant (R328/R337/R338, ARCHITECTURE.md sections 4-5) true structurally, not just behaviorally. The mcp binary still linked librocksdb-sys via the sole chain mnemosyne-store(rocksdb) → facts → cascade → projection → mcp. Root cause: cascade imported the 5 canonical fact structs from mnemosyne-facts, but R328 MOVED those structs to mnemosyne-core (facts only re-exported them) and cascade uses none of facts's RocksDB-coupled API — so cascade→facts was pure pre-R328 re-export residue. Fix: cascade depends on mnemosyne-core (not facts) and imports the structs from there; the now-dead public struct re-export is removed from facts (facts publicly exports only its own codec/persist binding, matching its crate doc); facts persist.rs imports the structs from core directly. Severs the sole chain — cascade/projection/mcp are now RocksDB-free at link time, store confined to the facts/index/server write subgraph. server/store/facts/index stay orphaned-but-kept (convergence substrate, invariant #1) — unchanged.

Round 351.decision_summary: Fix two latent UTF-8 mid-codepoint panic defects in the validate-code-refs citation extractors (mnemosyne-validate/code_refs.rs), surfaced by an independent robustness review. Both used a hardcoded +1 byte advance at an offset that can sit on a multibyte char boundary: (1) extract_citations's word-boundary-reject branch did start = i + 1 — with a non-ASCII entry_id_prefix, i is at a multibyte boundary and the next line[start..] slice panics; (2) is_external_section_cite computed the last whitespace-delimited token via rfind(char::is_whitespace).map(|i| i + 1) in two places — char::is_whitespace matches multibyte Unicode whitespace (U+00A0, U+2028), so +1 lands mid-codepoint and the token slice panics. Both are the SAME bug class already fixed in the sibling extract_inventory_citations_with_tail (Round 279 Bug #1, char_indices-driven) but never propagated to these two functions. Fix (1) advances by the matched char's len_utf8; fix (2) routes both whitespace-split sites through one new last_whitespace_token_start helper that advances by len_utf8 — a single helper so the fix cannot be half-applied to one site and missed at the other, the very omission this round closes. Reachable only via non-default config (non-ASCII entry_id_prefix / configured external_section prefixes), so no default-path crash, but a general-purpose validator must not panic on adversarial source content. Code-only; no atomic store or GENERATED.md change; R279 audit anchor verified present.

Round 354.decision_summary: Delete the caller-less unvalidated AtomicStore::entry_mut and section_mut accessors (mutate-API safety / no-legacy-carry). entry_mut was a create-on-miss &mut accessor whose own docstring flagged it a deferred carry ("remains create-on-miss until a parallel fail-loud refactor") and whose sibling comment called it "back-compat with the v1 path" — exactly the legacy-carry signal CLAUDE.md says to remove in place. It granted write authority to changelog_entries under a strictly weaker invariant set than append_changelog_entry (the half-enforced-invariant anti-pattern: a typo'd entry_id would silently materialize an empty entry, bypassing the R298 required-field gate). section_mut was already fail-loud (R287) but equally caller-less, superseded by section_mut_strict. Both had zero callers in production and tests — the strict variants delegate to get_mut directly, not to the bare accessors. Deleted both and reworded the three comments (add_section docstring + both _strict variants) that named them. No behavior change.

Round 369 — strip_section_marker canonic.decision_summary: strip_section_marker canonical in mnemosyne-core — DRY 5 verbatim §-marker normalize sites (two private helpers + 3 inline copies), the R353/R357/R358 canonical-converter class
changes_bullets: Added `mnemosyne-core::strip_section_marker(&str) -> &str` — the canonical normalizer that strips a section id's optional leading `§` reference marker (`§43` -> `43`, bare ids pass through). The marker-strip operation and its `'§'` literal now live in one L0 place instead of being re-derived per call site.

Three crates had independently re-derived the identical idiom `s.strip_prefix('§').unwrap_or(s)`: `mnemosyne-mcp::strip_section` (23 callers) and `mnemosyne-cli::strip_section_prefix` (22 callers) were verbatim private helpers, plus inline copies in ops/query.rs, cli/main.rs arg-parse, and parser/lib.rs split_section_number. Two crates writing the same private helper is the canonical-converter DRY class of Round 353 / Round 357 / Round 358.
Deleted mcp's `strip_section` wrapper as pure redundancy — every one of its 23 callers was a `.to_string()` closure with no fn-pointer use — and routed them to the imported canonical via rename.

Kept cli's `strip_section_prefix` as a thin owned-`String` adapter that delegates to the canonical: it has genuine ergonomics an `&str`-returning fn lacks (its result is stored in arg structs and it is used as a `.map(strip_section_prefix)` fn pointer in four places). The strip logic is single-sourced; only the owned-return adaptation is local.
The 3 inline normalize sites (ops query, cli main arg-parse, parser split_section_number) now call the canonical directly.

Deliberately left untouched the 3 conditional-parse sites that branch on marker presence — parser:338 (`strip_prefix('§')?`), parser:577 (`if let Some` + `'§'.len_utf8()` byte advance), query:331 (`if let Some`): those test or extract conditioned on the marker, a different operation than normalize, and a `&str -> &str` helper cannot express the presence test. Also left the ~30 `format!("§{}")` display/error sites: prepending the sigil in human-facing strings is not the strip operation, and routing them through a const would harm readability for no behavior benefit.

Round 373 — import-sections bulk section.decision_summary: Add import_sections: bulk section-create from a JSON manifest as one atomic transaction (3-way idempotency: absent=create / identical=no-op / divergent=reject), reusing add_section's extracted in-memory core so there is exactly one section-create write-path.
changes_bullets: Extracted add_section's validate+construct into build_candidate_section (shared in-memory core, no insert/no save); add_section now = build + dup-reject + insert + 1 save, and the bulk import_sections = N build/classify + 1 save. Both shape a new Section through the one core → a single section-create write-path, NOT a bespoke second writer (CLAUDE.md half-enforced-invariant rule).

Extracted normative_excerpt validation into build_normative_excerpt, now shared by the post-create setter AND the inline-at-create path; manifest entries anchor the excerpt frozen-at-create (RFC-002 FR-1). Added a field-invariant parity test that feeds the same edge inputs through both write paths and asserts identical accept/reject verdicts.

import_sections runs a 3-way classification per entry: absent->create / byte-identical->no-op (idempotent re-run) / divergent->reject the WHOLE manifest. Atomicity is free via run_atomic_mutate: any reject returns Err before the single save, so the freshly-loaded store is discarded and the disk is untouched; an all-no-op manifest writes nothing (written_bytes 0). Manifest order = parents before children (a child resolves a parent inserted earlier in the same batch).

Round 375 — strip § sigil in import-sect.decision_summary: Fix import_sections leaking the § citation sigil into store keys (a §-form manifest rendered §§ double-sigil, silently): strip § in the shared build_candidate_section so add_section and import_sections normalize section_id + parent_section identically for every caller.
changes_bullets: build_candidate_section (the one shared section-create core) now strips a leading `§` citation sigil from section_id AND parent_section via mnemosyne_core::strip_section_marker (trim-strip-trim). add_section and import_sections both route through it, so a citation-form manifest entry (`"§scxml-1"`) stores the bare key `scxml-1` regardless of caller — symmetric with the CLI/MCP add_section paths that already stripped. Also fixes parent_section lookup for §-form manifests (now matches the bare stored keys).

The bug (SCE-found, R373 regression): import_sections' CLI handler did not strip §, unlike cmd_add_section, so a §-form manifest stored `§scxml-1` and generate-docs rendered `### §§scxml-1` (double sigil). validate-workspace round-trips fine (store internally self-consistent) so it was SILENT corruption. Fixing in the shared core (not just the CLI handler) closes the footgun for every caller — direct primitive, CLI, and any future MCP import tool.
Chose strip (lenient, accept §-or-bare) over reject-at-parse, to match add_section's established normalization behavior.

The add_section behavior change (now strips via the core) broke no existing test — full atomic suite 116 pass.

Round 377 — commit↔ledger gate multi-wor.decision_summary: commit↔ledger drift gate (R293/R301) assumed a single-workspace repo: it scanned repo-global commit subjects for (R<n>) labels and diffed against one workspace ledger, so in a multi-workspace mono-repo a sibling workspace round label false-flagged every workspace (SCE adoption report). Round-namespace relabeling deferred YAGNI: the gate is a Mnemosyne self-development invariant that does not apply to a pure consumer ledger.

Round 383 — set-membership symbol bindin.decision_summary: RFC-002 FR-3 symbol enforcement under-represented the store. The validator indexed Implementation.symbol as section->file->symbol via an iterator .collect() into BTreeMap, so when a section recorded more than one symbol in the same file (which add_section_implementation explicitly allows — set semantics, only exact (file,symbol) dups rejected) the collect kept only the last, and a legitimate cite inside any earlier symbol falsely surfaced as SymbolMismatch. R383 makes the index set-valued (section->file->{symbols}); a cite is bound at symbol granularity iff its resolved enclosing symbol is a MEMBER of the registered set. Round 384 — Path B curation tooling (pro.decision_summary: Path B (code->section binding) adoption needs a curation path: an external consumer with thousands of existing citations cannot hand-author every section->file->symbol implementation entry. R384 adds propose-implementations, a read-only tool that scans the cited code, resolves each citations enclosing symbol via the language SymbolResolver, and emits the proposed implementation sets (plus ready-to-run add-section-implementation commands) for maintainer ratification — the review doubles as an audit of where each section is cited. Paired with it, the cpp resolver gains documented-symbol semantics: a section citation in source is conventionally a doc comment ABOVE the declaration it documents, but tree-sitters smallest-enclosing-node would bind it to the outer namespace/class; documented_symbol detects a comment that (with no intervening blank line) immediately precedes a declaration and binds to that declaration instead, falling through to enclosing scope for file-header/taxonomy comments. Both additive and read-only; no severity or scan behaviour changes.

Normative (default) keeps the axiom; Informative exempts prose-only sections (terminology / overview / references) that have nothing to implement here, so an external-spec ledger's meta sections no longer drown real gaps in false impl_missing. The enum is canonical in mnemosyne-core beside BindingKind (not the medium-neutral skeleton); the field is adapter-local on AtomicSection beside bindings, skipped from JSON when default so unclassified stores stay byte-identical. schema_version 5 to 6 migrates declaratively (serde default, no load arm); the default is the conservative no-op so no migration report is needed. Round 391 — North Star clarified: spec i.decision_summary: Clarifies the ARCHITECTURE North Star (section 1) so its model is not re-derived. A specification is one instance of a narrative (spec subset narrative), not a coordinate second pillar: spec-compliance is the tractable beachhead, a game-engine narrative manager is the encompassing target, and the North Star does not change as the medium widens. Facts are multi-axis: the actual/historical fact and each agent's understood fact are distinct facts on distinct axes, both true; frames are never cross-validated for agreement, and an actor's behaviour derives from its own frame. branch is therefore the epistemic-frame mechanism (coexisting perspectival truths, never merged), which is the deep reason the bitemporal/branch foundation is load-bearing, not speculative. Validation is frame-scoped: strict within a frame, cross-frame disagreement is data not a violation. Adds section 1.1 and tweaks the North Star blockquote to mark the subset relation. Doc-only; ARCHITECTURE is hand-maintained (not round-trip).

Round 404 — scan_content_drift: offline.decision_summary: Add the offline revalidation gate that makes the EPUB-as-content-SSOT claim trustworthy. scan_content_drift re-hashes each excerpt's stored text against its declared text_sha256 entirely offline (no EPUB, no Python); a non-empty hash that no longer equals sha256(text) is a HashMismatch finding — the cache was edited out-of-band (direct sidecar JSON edit, bypassing the mutate API which guarantees the hash at write time). NormativeExcerpt owns the predicate (recompute_text_sha256 + text_sha256_matches). The [content_drift] severity config defaults to reject (unlike [spec_drift]'s warn) because a cache diverging from its own hash is corruption, never a legitimate intermediate state. validate-content-drift composes the mismatch list (severity-gated) with the R402 backfill report's unrevalidatable count (informational), single-sourcing each concern. EPUB-file provenance (epub_sha256/epub_path) + commit-EPUB + SCE runbook are a separate axis deferred to R405.
changes_bullets: New mnemosyne-validate::scan_content_drift (sibling of scan_spec_drift): offline re-hash of each excerpt's stored text vs its declared text_sha256; a non-empty hash that no longer matches sha256(text) is a HashMismatch finding (out-of-band tamper / direct-JSON edit of the cache).
NormativeExcerpt gains recompute_text_sha256() + text_sha256_matches() (None when empty = unrevalidatable), so the type owns its content-integrity predicate.
New [content_drift].severity config (default reject; mirror of [spec_drift]) validated at config load; a cache that diverges from its hash is never a legitimate intermediate state.

New validate-content-drift CLI verb: prints HashMismatch findings (severity-gated) plus the unrevalidatable count sourced from the R402 excerpt_hash_backfill_report (informational, never gates) — each concern single-sourced.

Round 405 — EPUB-file provenance: SpecSo.decision_summary: Close the EPUB-as-content-SSOT loop with the EPUB-file provenance anchor. SpecSource gains epub_path + epub_sha256 pinning the committed content-SSOT EPUB. validate-content-drift, when those are set, re-hashes the committed EPUB file offline and compares to the pin — a mismatch (the EPUB was swapped/updated) or a missing file is gated under [content_drift].severity alongside the per-excerpt cache scan. This is the more fundamental gate: if the EPUB file drifted, every excerpt is suspect even when each still matches its own now-stale hash. The mismatch is also the trigger for the Layer B remediation (re-run medium-forge, import-epub-excerpts, re-pin epub_sha256), which stays Python/CI-side per the hexagonal boundary. docs/EPUB_SSOT_RUNBOOK.md documents the full external-consumer adoption path so SCE can formally switch its 196-section W3C ledger.

validate-content-drift now also re-hashes the committed EPUB file at epub_path vs epub_sha256 (offline file hash, no Python); a swapped/updated or missing EPUB is gated under [content_drift].severity alongside the per-excerpt content scan, so one green run means EPUB-file pinned AND every cache matches its hash.

Round 406 — seal-excerpt-hashes: seal co.decision_summary: SCE's RFC reply showed that EPUB-as-content-SSOT is one model, not the only one: a consumer whose excerpt text is authored by its own extractor (SCE's direct-body scope is finer than the EPUB div granularity — 0/196 byte-identical, projecting EPUB text would collapse 196 precise excerpts into 167 heading-polluted overlapping blobs) treats its own text as SSOT, with the EPUB file pin as source provenance only. R403 deleted the hand-authoring setter assuming EPUB is the sole text source, leaving no way to fill text_sha256 from already-stored text (report-excerpt-hash-backfill reports only; import-epub-excerpts is EPUB-sourced). seal_excerpt_hashes fills the gap: for each excerpt with an empty text_sha256, set text_sha256 = sha256(text), sealing the authored text as its own revalidation baseline — never overwriting text and never re-sealing a populated hash (a wrong populated hash stays drift for validate-content-drift). This unblocks SCE's 196 excerpts without regression and generalizes the model: excerpt text may be EPUB-projected or consumer-authored, unified by the integrity hash and the EPUB-file provenance pin.

Round 407 — medium-forge heading-scope e.decision_summary: SCE adopted the full EPUB-as-content-SSOT model (committed EPUB = authoritative excerpt text), un-holding ask 2. medium-forge must extract at HEADING granularity, not container subtree: W3C SCXML section ids are finer than div1..div4 (Appendix D has ~15 h4 function sections under one div1), so container.text_content() collapsed 29 distinct ids onto one blob (0/196 byte-identical). New --text-scope {container,heading}: heading mode emits each section's direct body (heading to next heading, descendants excluded) with the heading text excluded (the body-only canonical rule — the heading already lives in AtomicSection.title), porting SCE's proven heading-to-next-heading extractor for cutover diff fidelity. Container-only sections emit the locator only (no text), so import-epub-excerpts skips them while import-epub-anchors keeps the pointer. An anchor-collapse guard signals distinct ids that resolve to identical text via needs_review + confidence 0.0 rather than emitting a duplicate sha. EPUB rendering is unchanged; no Rust or schema change (import-epub-excerpts already overwrites text+text_sha256 unconditionally). Resolves the gating dependency for SCE's full EPUB-SSOT cutover.

Ports SCE's proven heading-to-next-heading BodyExtractor (the algorithm that produced the correct 196), whitespace-collapsed, script/style dropped.

Round 409 — parent_doc canonical post-R4.decision_summary: SCE asked the canonical value of AtomicSection.parent_doc after R400 removed the render path. Investigation: parent_doc is a mandatory non-empty L0 SectionSkeleton field (medium-neutral; surfaced in query / facts / schema / cascade index; mutable via set_section_parent_doc) and is NOT validated against any file post-R400 (the file-path interpretation died with the markdown-doc parser and render). CANONICAL: parent_doc is a free-form LOGICAL owning-document / namespace label, not a filesystem path and not provenance (provenance lives in normative_excerpt.anchor_url + [workspace.spec_source]). Of SCE's three options: option 2 (clear/null) is structurally impossible (mandatory non-empty); option 1 (keep docs/GENERATED.md) is a harmless-but-stale render-era leftover, not canonical; option 3 (a meaningful logical doc id) is correct, with the caveat that the target is a grouping label, never a source URL. Re-binding is cosmetic (no functional consumer breaks) and safe (set_section_parent_doc is a dedicated mutable setter, not frozen-ledger). Aligned the dogfood's sections to the logical label mnemosyne-design so adopters can follow the canonical without diverging from upstream. parent_doc is not on a deprecation roadmap.

Round 412 — activate BindingKind::verifi.decision_summary: Activate the reserved Verifies binding kind. A verifies binding records a test/evidence artifact for a section; it counts as neither implements-coverage nor a code↔spec citation edge, so it is excluded from the bidirectional citation set-equality — a verifies test file is externally mapped (e.g. a conformance manifest) and is not required to cite the section. Unblocks SCE registering verification bindings ahead of the VerificationMissing coverage gate.

Round 414 — cleanup: exhaustive sort_key.decision_summary: Session-review cleanup of two R413 structural smells. (1) Remove the sort_violations (a,b) wildcard tiebreaker that defeated the exhaustive-match discipline — it compiled with a missing same-rank arm and panicked at runtime (the R413 verify-axis bug, caught only by live e2e); replace with a single exhaustive sort_key match so a new variant is a compile error. (2) Extract is_verification_gap as the single-source predicate mirroring classify_section_coverage, so the verify gate and any future positive projection cannot drift. Add a CLI smoke test locking the opt-in/gate/exempt wiring.

Round 430 — narrative fact entity: frame.decision_summary: Phase 1A build Round A (of the A/B/C decomposition ratified with R429): the narrative fact entity lands. NarrativeFact = a claim held in exactly one epistemic frame over a canon-time extent in structure-section coordinates, with mandatory evidence provenance, recorded conflict assertion edges, and in-frame succession for time-indexed belief change — the storage half of the North Star sentence that frames are sparse non-privileged axes (a believed-fact and the ground-truth fact are distinct facts, both true, never cross-validated; absence in a frame = unrecorded, not false). Frame mechanism per the design round: frames-as-data at the SSOT log layer (a registry + an axis field), no inheritance or overlay (the multi-axis model leaves nothing to overlay); branch-KV remains the read-side projection realization when scale materializes the index. Canon closure is DERIVED: a superseded belief's effective end comes from its successor's canon_from, never written back (append-only, frozen-ledger genre). Both write paths route one shared builder (R305 parity); quote hashes are computed at write so a stored hash can never start out wrong (R404). Schema v11 to v12 is a declarative default — all four consumer stores load unchanged. Proven against the real corpus: the 27-chapter Dracula PoC store took 4 frames + 10 hand-extracted facts (3 cross-frame conflict clusters, 2 in-frame belief changes) in one atomic transaction with forward succession refs, idempotent on re-run. Round B (continuity gate) and Round C (frame-at-T projection) follow.

Round 430 — narrative fact entity: frame.publishable_decision_summary: Phase 1A build Round A (of the A/B/C decomposition ratified with R429): the narrative fact entity lands. NarrativeFact = a claim held in exactly one epistemic frame over a canon-time extent in structure-section coordinates, with mandatory evidence provenance, recorded conflict assertion edges, and in-frame succession for time-indexed belief change — the storage half of the North Star sentence that frames are sparse non-privileged axes (a believed-fact and the ground-truth fact are distinct facts, both true, never cross-validated; absence in a frame = unrecorded, not false). Frame mechanism per the design round: frames-as-data at the SSOT log layer (a registry + an axis field), no inheritance or overlay (the multi-axis model leaves nothing to overlay); branch-KV remains the read-side projection realization when scale materializes the index. Canon closure is DERIVED: a superseded belief's effective end comes from its successor's canon_from, never written back (append-only, frozen-ledger genre). Both write paths route one shared builder (R305 parity); quote hashes are computed at write so a stored hash can never start out wrong (R404). Schema v11 to v12 is a declarative default — all four consumer stores load unchanged. Proven against the real corpus: the 27-chapter Dracula PoC store took 4 frames + 10 hand-extracted facts (3 cross-frame conflict clusters, 2 in-frame belief changes) in one atomic transaction with forward succession refs, idempotent on re-run. Round B (continuity gate) and Round C (frame-at-T projection) follow.

Round 431 — continuity gate: frame-scope.decision_summary: Phase 1A build Round B: the continuity gate lands — the validation half of the North Star sentence whose storage half was R430. scan_continuity evaluates the RECORDED conflict assertion edges frame-scoped: a same-frame pair whose DERIVED canon extents co-hold at any point is a violation; a cross-frame pair is data, counted and never gated. Effective extents are derived at scan exactly as designed (stored canon_to, cut by any in-frame successor's canon_from — nothing written back); a stored end that outlives its successor's start is itself flagged. Canon order obeys guardrail B-1: it is a DECLARED partial order (canon-order/v1 edge JSON, consumer/medium-adapter generated, cycles reject, optional sha256 pin per the R428 authority-input rule) — section-id spelling is never consulted, non-comparable pairs surface as a count and never gate, and equality needs no declaration so the gate already catches same-coordinate contradictions with no order file. Guardrail B-2 is structural: conflict scoping lives in one same_scope predicate that widens to frame-x-branch when the world-line axis lands. Opt-in via the [continuity] table (severity default reject, the content-drift rationale: a same-frame simultaneous contradiction is wrong data, never a legitimate intermediate state). Proven on the real corpus: the Dracula store's 4 recorded conflict pairs are all cross-frame = 0 violations under reject (the multi-axis thesis executing), and a fabricated same-frame overlap was caught at its exact canon point with exit 1. Round C (frame-at-T projection) remains.

Round 432 — frame-at-T read projection:.decision_summary: Phase 1A build Round C, completing the ratified A/B/C decomposition: the frame-at-T read projection lands. frame_view answers the question the whole slice was built for — what does frame F hold at canon point T — by routing the SAME holds_at semantics the continuity gate uses, so gate and view share one predicate and cannot drift (the R390 single-source discipline, locked by a consistency test: any overlap violation the gate reports at point p must show both facts holding in the view at p). The projection is three-state honest under the declared partial order (guardrail B-1): a fact is holding, definitively not holding, or UNKNOWN when a coordinate its verdict depends on is not comparable to the query point — a quest-DAG arm queried from a sibling arm reports unknown rather than silently absent. Read-only verb report-frame-view (order/store resolution identical to validate-continuity), no schema change, no new authoritative state. Acceptance on the real corpus closes the North-Star slice: seward at ch-12 believes the illness while ground-truth at ch-10 simultaneously holds the vampire facts; at ch-16 seward's belief has swapped to F07 by derived closure with nothing written back — coexisting perspectival truths, frame-scoped queries, never cross-validated. The Phase 1A v1 slice (R430 entity + R431 gate + R432 projection) is complete; remaining Phase 1 work is consumer-pull.

Round 433 — world-line branch axis: (fra.decision_summary: AI-authoring greenlit as the live consumer; the sec 7.10 build order executes, pull 1 of 3: the world-line branch axis (sec 7.9 axis 2) lands. A branch is which-world, a frame is who-believes - the four-axis decomposition holds and the two never conflate; per-branch ground truth is the (branch, frame) composite. NarrativeFact gains an additive branch field (serde default main, the default never serializes, so every pre-branch store round-trips byte-identical; schema v12->v13, declarative default, no migration arm). Guardrail B-2 executes exactly as written at R431: same_scope widens frame -> (frame, branch) as a key-widening, not a rewrite - same-frame facts on different world-lines never conflict (cross-branch pairs are data, like cross-frame pairs), and in-frame succession never crosses a branch (world-line divergence is data, not succession; enforced at the write path and re-checked by the scan). Canon order goes branch-relative (B-1 carried): canon-order/v1 gains an optional branches map of per-world-line edge sets, each composed with the shared base - the same quest node can legitimately order differently on two branches, which a single global DAG cannot express (it would be a cycle). frame_view scopes to one world-line (--branch, default main) behind a derived fail-loud unknown-branch boundary (no registry: known = main, fact-carried, or order-declared; a typo'd branch must not read as an empty world).

Round 434 — authorial retract/amend: axi.decision_summary: Pull 2 of the sec 7.10 build order: the authorial correction path lands. The four-axis decomposition (sec 7.9) separates in-world belief change (axis 1/3: in-frame supersession, predecessor stays in the log) from author-time correction (axis 4: the claim itself was mis-written and must stop existing or change in place). Before this round a typo was permanent - any revision of a written fact divergent-rejected with NO alternative path, and the reject message actively gave WRONG advice (recommending in-frame supersession, which fabricates an in-world belief change out of an authorial slip). Two primitives close the gap: retract_fact (remove an unreferenced fact; inbound conflict edges / succession pointers block it fail-loud with the referrer list, so scan invariants never see a dangling target; mandatory reason, the remove_section audit-safeguard precedent; no tombstone - transaction time is the git history of the log per R330) and amend_fact (in-place revision keeping the id, routed through the SAME shared builder as add_fact/import_facts per the R305 parity rule, with inbound successors required to stay same-(frame, branch) so succession scope cannot be corrupted). Round 438 — branch fork-point: shared-hi.decision_summary: The R433 branch axis shipped scoping without divergence semantics - the design's own justification for branch != frame was copy-on-write shared history, yet a branch view was as sparse as a frame: a story forking at chapter 30 lost chapters 1-29 on the branch view, the gate under-detected contradictions against inherited facts, and the module-doc claim that the log carries everything the index needs was false without a fork datum. This round closes that tension the way the four-axis decomposition wants it closed: Branch.forks_from records WHERE a world-line diverged (forest by construction - parents must pre-exist, forks are immutable), visibility becomes a three-state world-membership judgment (inherited-In / definitively-Out / order-cannot-decide-Unknown, surfaced never gated), holds_at evaluates in the QUERY world with successor visibility filtering (a fork's revision of an inherited belief is in-world change that never leaks back into the ancestor's view), conflicts evaluate in the pair's JOIN world (siblings share no world = data), succession may point along the lineage, and a branch's composed canon order inherits every ancestor's declared edges. forks_from = None preserves the standalone-world semantics exactly - every pre-fork store and test gates identically. For the pinion AI-first runtime this is the primitive that makes playthrough-as-branch and route-divergence authoring representable.
changes_bullets: Branch.forks_from{branch, at} (mnemosyne-core BranchFork), schema v15->v16; None = standalone world (R433 semantics preserved exactly); parent must pre-exist + fork immutable after registration = ancestry is a forest BY CONSTRUCTION, no cycle writable; build_branch_fork = the one fork-invariant place shared by add_branch and the manifest path

world visibility (3-state, B-1 honest): a fact on an ancestor branch is In iff canon_from <= that lineage's departure point, Out when comparable-and-after, Unknown when the declared order cannot decide (surfaced, never gated); holds_at is now world-relative and a successor ends a predecessor ONLY where the successor itself is visible - a fork's revision never leaks back into the ancestor's view

Round 439 — conflict-edge claim pins: st.decision_summary: A conflict edge is a recorded SEMANTIC judgment about claim content (sec 7.4) - but R434's amend could change the judged text out from under the judgment, leaving the gate evaluating an assertion about words that no longer exist. This round applies the codebase's own drift discipline (R404 content pins, R420 drift->Stale) to the judgment layer: every ConflictAssertion pins the target's claim sha256 at judgment time, computed by the primitives and never caller-supplied; the scan compares pins against current claims and surfaces ConflictEdgeStale demanding re-affirmation. The re-affirmation path is the amend itself - amending a fact restamps its OUTBOUND judgments (the amender freshly asserts its own edges) while INBOUND judgments go stale, which is exactly the asymmetry the axis-4 model wants: you can re-state what you believe, you cannot silently keep others' statements about your old text. Clean break v16->v17 with no compat shim (pre-release; no committed store carries an edge; the old shape fails loud). Succession deliberately stays unpinned: it relates fact identities, not wordings.
changes_bullets: NarrativeFact.conflicts_with: bare target ids -> ConflictAssertion{target, target_claim_sha256} (mnemosyne-core), schema v16->v17 - CLEAN BREAK, no compat shim (pre-release rule; no committed consumer store carries an edge; an old-shape store fails to load LOUDLY rather than silently dropping the pin)

the pin is computed by the primitives, never caller-supplied (R404): validate_fact_refs becomes validate_and_stamp_fact_refs (the one shared pass - add_fact / import_facts post-staging snapshot / amend_fact all route it); add_fact_conflict stamps from the target's current claim; FactImport keeps bare ids (the authoring face is unchanged)
amend semantics: amending a fact RESTAMPS its outbound judgments (the amender freshly asserts its own edges); inbound judgments pointing AT the amended fact go stale instead - never auto-refreshed

scan_continuity surfaces ConflictEdgeStale{fact_id, target, stamped_sha256, current_sha256}; the pair is still evaluated (explicit conservatism both ways: staleness gates under reject, the overlap check is not suppressed)
validate_continuity smoke fixture now records its edge through the real primitive instead of hand-written JSON (the pin cannot be hand-authored)
verification_bullets: drift round-trip unit test: fresh stamp = 0 stale; amend the TARGET -> exactly 1 ConflictEdgeStale; amend the edge-owning fact (same content) -> outbound restamp -> 0 stale (the re-affirmation path works end-to-end)

Round 440 — hardening: one fork walk, to.decision_summary: The second session review held R433-R439 to the lifetime-project standard and found five defects; this round pays all of them plus one live bug the fix surfaced. The deep one was a fail-loud asymmetry: the scan re-checked conflict/succession targets against out-of-band edits while trusting frame/branch/entity registry membership and section refs entirely to the write path - and the lineage lookup PANICKED on an unregistered fact branch instead of erroring. The shared gate/view boundary now re-checks the store's full referential closure (an Err, because a store that fails it is corrupt and the semantics are not evaluable - distinct from missing conflict targets, which remain evaluable data findings), making every downstream lineage lookup total by invariant. The fork-chain traversal existed in three subtly-different copies across two crates - exactly where drift bugs breed - and is now ONE core function all paths route. Fixing the review findings surfaced a real R439 bug: import_facts verdicted before stamping, so an idempotent re-import of a manifest with conflict edges false-diverged on empty pins - stamping now precedes verdicts on both write paths (R305 parity restored, regression-tested). Also paid: the B-2 module doc citing a deleted predicate, the seven-argument holds_at hiding behind a clippy allow (WorldCtx bundle), and the unexplained stamp-only divergence message (now names the re-affirmation path).

check_order_against_store -> check_store_boundary: gate와 view가 공유하는 단일 boundary가 fact integrity까지 재검사 (frame/branch/entity registry 멤버십, canon/evidence section refs, evidence 비공백) - succession/conflict target만 재검사하던 half-enforced 비대칭 해소; 미등록 branch fact의 lineage 인덱싱 panic 경로가 구조적으로 소멸 (boundary가 Err를 먼저 반환)
WorldCtx{world, lineage, order, successors} 번들: holds_at 7-인자 + clippy allow 제거, 의미론이 "world에 대한 판정"으로 읽히는 형태로 재구조화
B-2 모듈 doc drift 수정 (삭제된 same_scope 지칭 -> join_world)

Round 441 — typed-claim/rule-gate design.decision_summary: The recorded design round R437 deferred (do-not-improvise carry honored). The typed leg: NarrativeFact gains an OPTIONAL authored TypedClaim{subject: entity-id, predicate: registered-id, object: Entity(entity-id)|Value(scalar)} beside the required prose claim - B-1 applied to typing (declared at write time in the same act as the prose, never NLP-inferred), binary predicates only, subject and entity-object must be registered AND members of the fact's entities list (the retrieval key is never silently widened). Partial coverage IS the design: probed on the 10 real Dracula claims, 3 type cleanly, 5 are compound prose where typing forces the per-claim split the prose tolerated, 2 are negative-epistemic and stay prose-only (open-world: absence = unrecorded, never false) - the deterministic gate covers the typed subset while recorded edges and the future LLM-discovery adapter cover the rest, three conflict sources one gate. Predicates are load-bearing refs (rules key off them; a typo'd predicate silently escapes its rule - the R436 write-side-typo lesson), so they become the 4th fail-loud registry carrying object_kind entity|scalar for builder shape-checking; per the R440 carry, build Round A performs the registry dedup in the same change that adds the 4th. Rules are consumer vocabulary and never enter L0: a narrative-rules/v1 declared artifact (the canon-order/R428 authority-input pattern, optional sha256 pin) with exactly TWO classes covering the named trio - exclusive{predicate, per: subject|object} (location exclusivity per subject, conservation/custody per object; same-value co-holding duplicates are consistent, not gated) and transition{predicate, allowed} riding the in-frame succession edge (succession IS the declared adjacency - adjacency over a partial canon order is ill-defined; unchained same-subject/predicate visible pairs are surfaced as a WORLD-scoped count, never gated). Evaluation lands inside scan_continuity as new violation variants and MUST reuse WorldCtx::holds_at verbatim as its third reader - the probe's binding finding: a paper interval model with an inclusive successor boundary produced 4 false positives on correctly chained real arcs; the half-open successor cut is load-bearing. Frame x branch scoping carries unchanged (cross-frame and fork-world pairs proved inert on real data), succession chains become structurally rewarded (a forgotten chain is now a caught overlap), and rule findings are derivations re-evaluated each scan - no staleness, no pins (judgments keep their R439 pins). Opt-in = authoring the rules file; violations ride the existing continuity severity knob. Design only: no schema or production code this round; build = Round A then Round B, consumer-pulled.
changes_bullets: design doc sec 7.12 (claudedocs/fictional-adapter-design.md): TypedClaim{subject: entity-id, predicate: registered-id, object: Entity|Value} as an optional authored leg beside the prose claim; predicate registry as the 4th fail-loud registry with object_kind shape check; narrative-rules/v1 consumer-declared artifact with TWO rule classes (exclusive{predicate, per: subject|object} + transition{predicate, allowed} riding succession edges); scan_continuity integration via new violation variants; non-goal revisit triggers; build decomposition Round A/B

no store schema change and no production code this round (design only; the store mutation is this entry)
verification_bullets: probe 1: correctly chained real arcs green including the A-B-A location revisit; probes 2-4: forgotten location chain, destroyed-to-alive transition, double custody each caught at the exact offending pair

probes 5-6: cross-frame (jonathan's castle belief vs ground-truth england) and fork-world (alive-lucy on a lucy-lives fork vs dead on main) both inert - frames/worlds never cross-validated carries into the rule class unchanged

Round 443 — session review of R441-R442:.decision_summary: The R436/R440 cadence applied to the two newest rounds: hold R441 (typed-claim/rule-gate design) and R442 (setup/payoff coverage) to the lifetime-project standard before anything builds on them. Three findings, all repaid in-session. The real one is in the R441 probe: the exclusive rule's consistency skip ('a restated fact is not a violation') was implemented one-sided - it skipped equal OBJECTS under per:subject but never skipped equal SUBJECTS under per:object, so a restated custody fact (the same holder stated twice) would false-positive as a two-holder conservation violation. The principle is now pinned symmetric - the skip applies to the NON-KEYED leg, both directions - in the probe and in design sec 7.12, so build round B inherits the rule, not the bug. The review also caught the reviewer: the first regression fixture left the restated fact's extent open, which IS a genuine two-holder conflict with the later custody transfer, and the gate correctly flagged it - the fixture was wrong, not the gate; extent closed. Finding 2 is an R442 omission: a payoff edge whose endpoints no world ever sees together (sibling-branch endpoints, both existing) was silent dead data - the setup's world shows dangling (the symptom) but nothing surfaced the edge itself, so an author who paid a gun on the wrong world-line got no signal that the edge credits nowhere. PayoffCoverageReport.uncredited_edges now lists edges that credited in no world, with B-1 honesty (an edge touching an undecidable-visibility endpoint is withdrawn, not declared dead). A write-side reject for this is impossible by design: world-coherence depends on the declared canon order, a validate-time artifact the mutate primitive never sees. Finding 3: the pays_off forward-ref-within-manifest path (the succession symmetry) was untested; covered. DEBT-1 (ARCHITECTURE doc drift) was checked on the way in and verified already paid.

Round 447 — payoff dead-edge masking fix.decision_summary: The R445 Detroit slice's Finding 3 closed: the R443 uncredited_edges surface withdrew an edge from the global dead-edge pool whenever ANY world saw EITHER endpoint as Unknown - and since parallel protagonist chains make every cross-chain fact Unknown in the other protagonist's forks, the surface went structurally silent on exactly the corpus shape that ratified it (R445 falsified this live: the genuinely dead F-K13 -> F-K05 edge was masked under the parallel-chains order and surfaced only under a discourse interleave). Edges that credit nowhere but met a genuine could-credit undecidable world now surface as a new undecidable_edges report field instead of silently draining (the no-silent-caps rule: silent withdrawal reads as 'no dead edges' when it means 'could not decide'), and they are deliberately never listed as definitively dead (B-1 honesty both directions). Verified on the live Detroit store: the parallel-chains order and the discourse-interleave order now agree on the dead edge - the order declaration choice (R445 Finding 5) no longer changes whether a dead edge is visible, only how much becomes undecidable.

Round 450 — session review of R449: padd.decision_summary: The R436/R440/R443/R448 cadence applied to the rules-gate build before anything stacks on it. One real finding, falsified live before fixing: load_narrative_rules validated shape with trimmed compares and the scan boundary checked the predicate registry with .trim(), but the evaluation filtered typed facts by EXACT predicate equality — so a whitespace-padded predicate in a declared rules file passed every check and matched nothing, silently disarming the rule it declared. That is the precise silent-escape class the fail-loud predicate boundary exists to prevent (the R436 write-side-typo lesson), reproduced against the Detroit store: the padded strict vocabulary reported rules=1 violations=0 where unpadded fires 2. The fix follows the one-invariant-one-place doctrine: whitespace normalizes INTO the stored values at load (rule id, predicate, transition legs), and the scan boundary now compares EXACT so the two readers of a rule's predicate (registry check, fact filter) can never again disagree about what the rule names; a padded programmatic rule that bypassed the loader fails loud naming the padded string. Re-verified end-to-end over live MCP stdio in the same window (the R448 verification-gap lesson): the config rules_path path fires, and an override pointing at a padded declaration also fires post-normalization. Second finding: the per-world reporting contract for exclusive violations existed only in prose - now pinned by a test asserting a violating main pair inherited by a fork reports in BOTH worlds, main first (the world is part of the finding; the R441 probe's executable model). Architectural sweep found nothing else to repay: the per-world scaffolding duplication between the exclusive and unchained halves diverges in its inner logic (abstraction would be speculative), and two lenient-parse behaviors are recorded as observations rather than changed — a typo'd top-level key parses to zero rules but the count is surfaced never silent, and per-rule unchained dedup double-counts only when two transition rules name one predicate (probe-verbatim, frozen semantics).

Assessed and deliberately left: typed_object_key stays local with its promotion trigger; the ops envelope mirror is the R435 pattern; per-world co-hold cost is scale-gated (measure first). Round 453 — T1-A trap corpus: rules-gate.decision_summary: The owner fired the Tier 1 backlog (design doc sec 10, recorded post-R452) and T1-A executed first: mutation testing of the deterministic validator on the Detroit slice (R445 corpus, 26 facts / 8 worlds / 6 rules, schema v19). Blind protocol via existing machinery: trap-manifest.json authored with per-class expectations and sha256-pinned BEFORE any detection run (R404/R428 pin pattern; the pin is restated in this entry's changes bullet because the manifest itself is gitignored claudedocs — the committed ledger is the tamper-evidence), nine one-fault variants planted (additions through the real add-fact --sidecar primitive, removals and the write-rejected fault through direct JSON edit — the R440 out-of-band boundary), detection runs executed by a separate blind agent with no manifest access, grading by diff against the pin. Results: 5/5 structural trap classes detected in their DESIGNED channels — typed resurrection gated (rule_transition_invalid, dead to alive), typed double-custody gated (rule_exclusive_overlap), stripped succession edge surfaced (unchained_state_pairs 0 to 1 and correctly NOT gated: deviancy carries no exclusive rule, so the surface-only honesty channel is doing real work), removed payoff credit surfaced (dangling grows by exactly the two orphaned setups), and the sibling-world supersession caught TWICE — the write boundary rejects it (succession never crosses world-lines; divergence is data, not succession) and, planted out-of-band, the scan independently gates it as succession_cross_branch: defense in depth observed live, the silent-gap hypothesis refuted. False positives 0/2 dedicated specificity probes: the unmodified control is clean, and the knows-what-they-cannot-know trap — typed cross-frame contradiction PLUS an explicit recorded conflict edge, maximal temptation — stays data (cross_scope_pairs 1 to 2, zero violations): the North-Star perspectival axiom holding under adversarial pressure. Untyped-miss rate 2/2: prose-only twins of the two gated traps are invisible to every deterministic channel, as designed — the LLM-discovery pull now carries a measured number instead of an assumption. One manifest authoring error recorded and kept honest by the pin: V2 expected the overlap reported in both parent and fork world (the R450 contract), but the planted fact lands at a node incomparable with the fork cut, so the fork classifies it visibility-unknown and the single-world report is CORRECT per design — the wrong expectation stays in the pinned manifest and is corrected only in the graded report. This is the rules-gate (R449) field-proof in the role max-rigor verification played for SCE; grading SSOT = claudedocs/phase1-detroit-poc/traps/trap-report.md.

Round 454 — T1-B Detroit visualization s.decision_summary: T1-B (design doc sec 10) answered its empirical question — does the picture yield insight the JSON rows do not — YES, four concrete instances on the Detroit slice, with zero substrate change. A one-shot gitignored generator renders existing report verbs only: report-frame-view sampled per (world, frame, node) so the holds-decision is the verb's at every cell, report-payoff-coverage for the fork-tree badges; the viz computes NO interval algebra of its own — extents are runs of sampled nodes and divergence windows are nodes where both ends of a recorded conflict edge hold, i.e. the projection-is-the-interface principle executed literally with the gate's own semantics. The four instances: (1) irony-window EXTENT — daniel's false belief (Connor is unarmed) co-holds with ground-truth's concealed-gun fact from det-h-negotiation to the END of w-connor-gun's world-line because nothing ever supersedes the belief; per-node frame-view calls cannot show that the window never closes, the picture shows it in one glance — direct empirical pull for the Tier-2 dramatic-irony-intervals verb, whose exact derivation the spike's client-side sweep already prototypes; (2) sibling-fate contrast — per-world dangling badges on the fork tree render the R442 inherited-dangling finding as a one-saccade pattern (the same setup paid in one sibling, dangling in the other); (3) the order-declaration CHOICE becomes visible — under the parallel-chains declaration every frame timeline shows holds-unknown gaps at chapter-incomparable nodes, making R445 Finding 5 readable rather than abstract (the interleaved declaration would close the gaps for a reader); (4) the half-open succession cut renders as a clean bar handoff at the exact node, in every world that sees the chain. Friction recorded as promotion triggers, not repairs: an irony-interval verb should carry world and node-span explicitly, and the R453 violation-record asymmetry (transition has no branch field) was met again from the consumer side. Tier 1 closes with this round; spike-note SSOT = claudedocs/phase1-detroit-poc/viz/spike-note.md.

Round 455 — dramatic-irony intervals: Ti.decision_summary: The first Tier-2 promotion fired on the T1-B pull (R454: the window-extent insight was the spike's strongest picture-over-rows instance, and its client-side sweep already prototyped the derivation; the owner's no-silent-fail-scripting ruling made absorbing the Python layer the same change). A literary concept becomes a deterministic derivation with nothing inferred: the irony marker is the AUTHORED cross-frame conflict edge (B-1 — same-frame edges are the gate's territory, counted and skipped), and the window is the node SET of a query world where the one holds-semantics says both ends are simultaneously in effect — WorldCtx::holds_at VERBATIM as its 4th reader (gate, frame view, rules gate, irony report; the R441 no-own-interval-algebra finding carries), node universe = store sections (the gate's co-hold idiom). Scoping is the derived-finding model of the R452 pin, necessarily: a cross-frame edge has no join world by construction, so the report sweeps every query world and a window inherited by a fork reports in both worlds (the R450 contract). The window is deliberately a node set plus starts (minimal co-hold nodes) and an open flag (the set contains a maximal node of the world's declared composed order — the R454 'belief never closes' headline as a first-class signal), never a (from,to) span: under a partial order the co-hold region need not be contiguous and a span would lie. Honesty surfaces: per-world windowless (both endpoints visible, never co-holding — a belief corrected before the truth lands is data, not absence) and undecidable (an Unknown endpoint, B-1, never classified); store-wide cross-frame/same-frame totals (no silent caps); an Out endpoint makes the edge another world's business. Never gated — irony is craft signal, not defect (the dashboards-never-gate principle), so no severity knob exists. Dogfooded live on Detroit: the spike's exact window reproduced (F-H04 concealed gun vs F-H05 'Connor is unarmed', opens at det-h-negotiation, OPEN at world-line end, inherited into both gun-fork outcome worlds — Daniel dies still holding the false belief), and the two order declarations agree on start and openness while the interleaved one honestly widens the node set with now-comparable cross-chapter beats (the R445 comparability-vs-occurrence wrinkle, now visible in a report). The spike's generate.py is deleted in the same change (no-legacy-carry; the HTML stays as frozen evidence).

Round 456 — session review of R453-R455:.decision_summary: The R436-cadence adversarial review ran against the R453-R455 window under the owner's restated standard (textbook structure over cost, lifetime-project bar, North-Star and SSOT fidelity). Verdict first: the spine held — the irony verb is a pure derivation over the one holds_at with no second interval algebra, it reads across frames but JUDGES nothing (no violation class, no severity knob: frames stay never-cross-validated, the perspectival axiom intact under a verb whose entire subject is cross-frame divergence), the store remained the single directly-validated SSOT (R455 entry substance self-contained, trap-corpus sha256 pin committed inside the R453 entry while the artifacts stay gitignored), and the trap corpus measured the system rather than bending it. Four findings, all repaid in-round. The substantive one: the R455 windowless verdict conflated two different honesty states — a pair whose starts the declared order CANNOT COMPARE was labeled windowless, asserting -the belief never overlaps the truth- where the truthful claim is -the declaration cannot order them- (under a richer declaration the same pair may be a window; the gate already encodes exactly this distinction as unordered_pairs, so the report diverged from the codebase's own idiom). Pre-fix evidence is pinned in the round itself: the R455 undecidable-fork test asserted windowless=1 on a parallel-chain pair and passed. Fixed by mirroring the gate: per-world unordered edge list, windowless now requires comparable starts. Finding 2: the WorldCtx::holds_at successors input was hand-rolled identically at three sites (scan, frame view, irony) — the R440/R452 two-copy rule fired at three; successors_index is the one builder. Finding 3: irony_intervals read CanonOrder's private reach representation to decide world-line ends — the judgment moved onto the order type as is_maximal(branch, node) with a new test pinning that isolated sections (in the store, outside the declaration) are never maximal. Finding 4: the CLI report verbs carried byte-identical flag parsing — parse_narrative_report_args extracted at the second copy. Assessed and deliberately left, recorded with reasons: the per-world lineage scaffolding across the three readers (R450 verdict carries — inner logic diverges), the gate-vs-report conflict-pair collection (shared idiom, divergent side effects — not a sweep), and the R453 branch-field asymmetry (still no consumer friction). 819 tests, Detroit live unchanged, MCP stdio re-verified with the four-way per-world shape.
