Round 457 — LLM typing discovery design:.decision_summary: The owner opened the LLM-discovery gate and the design round ran R441-style (design only, build frozen, consumer-pulled). Scope refinement first: sec 7.10 gap 5 named conflict-discovery, but the R453 trap corpus quantified the real gap as TYPING - the deterministic layer misses untyped prose faults 2/2 and catches their typed twins 5/5, and typing alone is measurably sufficient (a typed double-custody gates immediately via exclusive; a typed resurrection surfaces via unchained) - so v1 is typing discovery: proposed typed legs for EXISTING untyped facts, nothing else. The B-1 crux is a reconciliation, not an exception: R441 pinned -typed legs are declared at write time, never NLP-inferred-, and discovery honors it by relocating inference OUTSIDE the store - the LLM's output is quarantined in a reviewable sha256-pinnable typing-proposals/v1 artifact, a typed leg enters only through the declared amend path where the authored act IS the review plus import, and the amend reason records provenance; -never NLP-inferred- precisely means -never SILENTLY NLP-inferred-. This is the R428 authority-input pattern's third instance (after canon-order and narrative-rules), and the substrate gains zero LLM clients: any agent session (Claude today, pinion later) reads report-typing-candidates (the one-call input package: untyped facts + claim sha256s + registered predicate/entity vocabulary - AI-first context economy, unregistered vocabulary never proposable), writes the proposals file, runs import-typing-proposals. Safety rails pinned: the R439 judgment-time content pin re-targeted (each proposal stamps the claim text it interpreted; import re-checks, so a fact amended after proposing fails loud as stale instead of silently mis-typing revised prose); all-or-nothing import with full per-proposal verdicts and --dry-run (the file is the reviewed artifact - make it fully valid, no half-applied state); every typed invariant rides the ONE R305/R446 builder site so the import path adds zero new invariant sites; fill-blanks only; no confidence scores (the reviewable substance is the rationale, not a number the model can inflate). Round 460 — session review of R457-R459:.decision_summary: The R436-cadence adversarial review ran against the typing-discovery window (R457 design, R458 candidates, R459 import + blind acceptance) under the owner's restated standard. Verdict first: the architectural spine held — B-1 survived its hardest test yet (an NLP-inference feature built WITHOUT the store ever ingesting un-reviewed inference: quarantined artifact, declared import, fill-blanks only), the typed invariants stayed in the one R305/R446 builder, the blind acceptance protocol measured the system rather than flattering it, and no finding touches the North-Star axes. Four findings, all repaid in-round. The substantive one: the lowercase-hex sha256 encoding existed in SIX hand-rolled implementations across four crates — including both ends of the cross-crate claim pin, stamped by report-typing-candidates in mnemosyne-validate and re-checked by import_typing_proposals in mnemosyne-atomic; an encoding change on either side would have mass-staled every proposal silently, the half-enforced-invariant class operating across crate boundaries. Consolidated to ONE mnemosyne_core::sha256_hex (with the encoding pinned by its own test: 64 lowercase hex, deterministic), converting schema's production-unused pub fn (deleted with its test), atomic's private fn plus publishable/audit hash_hex, cli's EPUB re-hash, validate's claim pin + authority-pin + catalog + confirmation hash_file, and two test-local copies; unused sha2 deps dropped from three crates; project.rs's u64 key derivation keeps direct sha2 deliberately (different encoding family). Finding 2: R459's MCP import handler hand-rolled a SECOND mutate-lock acquisition beside run_mutate — extracted with_mutate_lock so receipt-shaped and verdict-report-shaped mutates share THE one acquisition site (two lock sites are how two mutate paths drift). Finding 3, the process one: the R459 build deviated from the frozen design's apply-via-amend-acts prose for good reasons (amend restamps outbound judgment edges — the amender's-fresh-assertion semantics, wrong for a mechanical typing fill; amend reasons are validated but never persisted, the R434 transaction-time-audit model) — but the deviation went unrecorded at build time; sec 7.15 now carries the declared as-built correction, and the lesson is pinned: frozen-design deviations are recorded in the deviating round, not discovered by the next review. Finding 4: sec 7.15's V7 acceptance expectation was stale after R459 exceeded it; amended with the result. Round 466 — playthrough manuscript: Tier.decision_summary: The second Tier-2 promotion fired on two pulls: the owner question the backlog entry answers ('a human cannot read the graph' — N worlds = N linear manuscripts) and the Tier-3 A/B authoring experiment, whose blind-preference grading needs a readable per-world linearization as its consumption interface. Nothing is inferred — the manuscript is a deterministic projection of declared data. Scene sequence = the query world's GOVERNING composed order linearized (Kahn over the closure, lexicographically smallest ready node first; CanonOrder::linearize, on the order type per the R456 rule). The composed order is partial, so the emitted sequence is ONE valid reading and never claims otherwise: every adjacent emitted pair the order cannot compare surfaces as undeclared_adjacencies — the sec 7.14 span lesson carried from intervals to sequences (silently totalizing an incomparable pair would lie about what the author declared, B-1). Scene events are declared coordinates verbatim, two end kinds with distinct semantics: expired (canon_to equals the node — the fact holds AT it, through it, its last scene) vs superseded (a visible successor's canon_from equals the node, the event names the cutter); holding_count is judged by WorldCtx::holds_at VERBATIM as its 5th reader (gate, frame view, rules gate, irony report, manuscript — one semantics), so the delta story and the holds judgment cross-check each other instead of drifting into a second semantics. Honesty surfaces complete: unplaced_facts (a visible fact whose canon_from / canon_to / cutting successor's canon_from the world's order never names, with the offending field), undecidable (Vis::Unknown, never placed, never counted), sections_outside_order (isolated coordinates, R456: never scenes); no silent caps. The --world filter is the consumption unit (one manuscript per reading/grading session), fail-loud on a typo. Never gated — a manuscript is a reading surface, not a defect detector. successors_index now carries the successor's id beside the fact (the manuscript names the cutting fact): one index, every reader updated in the same change. Round 467 — session-load reads: identifi.decision_summary: A live session-load miss exposed two gaps with one root. query --term "Round 466" --scope changelog returned [] against a store whose latest entry IS Round 466 — indistinguishable from the entry being absent, the silent-miss failure mode this codebase repays on sight. Cause 1: the R292 term scan never matched identifier keys. That was an omission, not a recorded exclusion — the v1 out-of-scope list names pointer fields and enums but never IDs, no test pinned the absence, and IDs are exactly what an agent greps for at session start. Cause 2: the R410 list_changelog read model (round-number-ordered whole-ledger projection, built for the deferred Studio timeline) had no CLI or MCP surface, which is what pushed a listing need through a substring search in the first place. Both repaid in one round: identifier keys become searched fields symmetric across the three kinds under kind-qualified names (section_id / entry_id / inventory_id — one shared filter namespace, no ambiguity, opt-out via the same field filter); and the existing projection is exposed verbatim as query --list-changelog plus the list_changelog MCP tool — no new read model, wiring only. The honesty payoff: an ID-pattern search that returns 0 hits now means the ID does not exist, and the session-load question 'what are the latest rounds' is a listing verb, not a grep idiom.

Round 468 — query_term field filter fail.decision_summary: The R467 carry named the surviving member of the silent-miss class it had just repaid for identifier keys: a --field name no scanner checks (a typo, a field outside the scanned scope, or a stale doc vocabulary) returned 0 hits indistinguishable from a true empty result. This round closes it at the only correct site — inside query_term itself, ahead of the scan, where CLI and MCP both arrive — because validating in ops or the CLI parser would re-create the half-enforced-invariant shape the R295 paste-error made canonical: one write path strict, the sibling permissive, the invariant effectively absent. Three per-kind field rosters become the validation vocabulary; scope decides which rosters apply, so a Section-only field under changelog scope is rejected as loudly as a typo, and the error message hands back the scope's complete valid-name list (fail fast, fail informatively). The roster cannot drift from the scanners on discipline alone, so a test pins the equivalence: every roster name, filtered against a fully-populated store, must hit its own field. The sweep also caught a live instance of the class: the MCP fields-arg doc had advertised implementations — a name no scanner has checked since the bindings rename — meaning an agent following the tool's own documentation got the silent 0-hit forever. Doc corrected, contract stated. The query_term read path now has no silent-miss surface: IDs scan (R467), names validate (R468), the advertised vocabulary is the real one (R468).

Round 469 — A/B authoring experiment des.decision_summary: The sec 10 Tier-3 entry's gate fired (trap corpus R453 done, discovery verbs R458-R464 complete, owner pull 2026-06-11) and this round spends it entirely on design, because the experiment's validity floor IS the session separation: a session that designs the grading and then writes the story has contaminated both. The trial answers three questions under three disciplines. Floor (does the Mnemosyne loop reduce deterministic consistency defects in a long branching story?): two arms, identical original premise and structure quota, identical 3-session budget with fresh context per session — plain arm writes prose, loop arm authors store-first with gates at session end repairing before delivery; graded NOT on the loop's own store but on a blind re-extraction of BOTH proses under one pinned recipe, the symmetric-referee move the design considers its keystone. Ceiling (is either preferred?): per-world linear reading copies — the R466 manuscript verb's pulling consumer — judged blind by 3 fresh LLM sessions on a pinned 5-axis rubric; per the R464 V9 lesson this leg pins procedure and refuses to pin an outcome. Economics: token totals and prevented-defect counts, measured open. One pre-registered outcome only (PRED-1: plain >= 3 endpoint defects AND loop < plain); the bridge finding (judge-cited errors invisible to the D-metrics = untyped residue on live prose) connects the R453 miss-rate to real authoring. Everything an execution session will follow — premise, prompts, recipes, rubric, runbook S0-S11 — lives in one manifest whose sha256 is pinned in this entry before any execution session exists.

Round 471 — A/B authoring experiment exe.decision_summary: Executed the R469/R470-pinned blind A/B authoring experiment end to end (S1-S11, one day, claude-fable-5 throughout): plain vs Mnemosyne-loop agents each authored the Saltglass branching novella in 3 fresh sessions, one blind session re-extracted both proses under one recipe, three blind judges read matched world-line copies, and the reveal round graded the sealed predictions. Headline: the only pinned outcome (PRED-1 floor) is REFUTED on both conjuncts — the plain story re-extracted to 0 primary-endpoint defects (pin required >=3) and the loop story to 1 (boots-custody fork-boundary fault the loop author never recorded), so loop < plain failed too. The control self-organized: the plain agent invented an unprompted in-file continuity ledger, turning the comparison into freeform-notes vs typed-store+gates — at 29-30 scenes on this model tier, notes suffice for every deterministically-detectable class. What the experiment bought instead: PRED-4 confirmed with margin (judges cited >=4 real continuity defects on the plain story that no D-metric caught, and ~8 across both arms vs 1 gated total — the untyped residue dominates, and fork-seam leaks are its dominant class in BOTH arms), PRED-3 landed at 1.48x tokens/scene (below the predicted 1.5-4x band; overhead is cache-read, friction decays to 0 by session 3), preference PLAIN 2-1/6-3 with the recorded weighting inverted (judges chose whole-world bookkeeping over the loop's admitted prose+knowledge-discipline superiority), and the loop's protection was measured as min(store-coverage, gate-power) with coverage binding. Full tables and analysis: claudedocs/phase1-ab-experiment/ab-report.md (run-log, verdicts, sealed label map alongside).

Round 473 — scale-floor experiment desig.decision_summary: The A/B trial (R469 design, R471 execution) refuted the floor hypothesis at 29-30 scenes because the plain control self-organized a freeform paper-Mnemosyne that sufficed at that scale; the R471 verdict named the next move first — push the single variable corpus-length x session-count past the context horizon the A/B run never reached. Round 475 — scale-floor experiment execu.decision_summary: The scale-floor experiment designed in R473 (sec 7.19, manifest sha256 18ea118a) executed across 17 session-separated blind rounds; the label-map sha256 verified MATCH at reveal (50092c40, sealed S13 by coin flip with the orchestrator blind — the flip result was never displayed, so extraction and judging ran with nobody knowing the mapping). story-A = plain (60 scenes), story-B = loop (65 scenes). RESULT: the floor hypothesis is REFUTED AGAIN. Floor (blind re-extraction, one fixed recipe both stories): plain primary-endpoint = 3, loop = 5; D1/D2/D4 = 0 for both, all signal in D3 dangling required setups. PRED-1 (plain >= 3 AND loop < plain) fails on the second conjunct — scale broke plain's floor (A/B plain = 0 -> scale plain = 3) but loop did not produce fewer defects (5 > 3), the same direction as A/B. Preference (3 blind judges, one matched world-line each): plain SWEPT 3-0 (confront, confess, escalate). Economics: loop $0.553/scene vs plain $0.324 = 1.71x, ABOVE the A/B 1.48x — PRED-3 (loop cheaper at scale) refuted; the store sidecar is rewritten whole on each mutate, so its cost rises with corpus and never converges below plain. The decisive finding: loop's store passed EVERY deterministic gate (D1/D2/D4 = 0) yet LOST on plot causation the store does not model — judges cited a load-bearing self-contradiction ('Surel' called both an alias and the avenger's true name), a named murderer (a bed-patient) with no established access to the locked-room draught (the access fits the nurse Brandt), an unmotivated second killing, and a six-week investigation packed inside a three-week snow-in. STORE-CONSISTENCY IS NOT CAUSAL COHERENCE: the guarantee the store delivers (declared-state consistency) held perfectly but is orthogonal to what makes a mystery hang together, and that gap is precisely where the loop lost. The D-metric counts 'dangling' identically for both stories, but plain's 3 were intentional dramatic irony (the confront judge PREFERRED them) and loop's 5 were partly broken causation — the human judge separates craft from defect where the deterministic gate cannot (PRED-4 confirmed, subject INVERTED: loop carried the untyped residue, not plain). Honesty: this was a confirmatory venue (built where the store should pay off — long multi-session branching authoring), so the null result = improvised notes suffice at 60 scenes / Fable tier, NOT that the store is useless; it is silent on larger scale, weaker tiers, multi-author work, or the store's spec/audit home where declared-fact consistency IS the property the store delivered perfectly here. SSOT = scale-floor-report.md.

Round 476 — scale-floor result refined:.decision_summary: R475 framed the loop's losses as "store-consistency != causal coherence", but on reflection (owner challenge: timeline should be store-guaranteed) that binary is too coarse. The line between what the store can and cannot guarantee is a MODELING-DEPTH CONTINUUM, not a fixed boundary, with three bands. Band 1 — what the store already gates: custody, life-status, scene order (loop scored D1/D2/D4 = 0). Band 2 — what the store COULD gate but currently does not: timeline/scalar arithmetic (the "six-weeks-in-three-weeks" fault; A/B's "1913 / twelve years / 1923" is the same band) and same-entity multi-fact contradiction (the "Surel" alias-vs-true-name fault, catchable by forcing typed predicates so two claims about one entity collide). The store RECEIVES these as facts; its current gates (exclusive/transition) just do no arithmetic and do not force typing. Band 3 — what looks structurally out of reach: the murderer's missing locked-room access. The refinement: even Band 3 is reachable by PRECONDITION/AFFORDANCE modeling — if an action fact ("Surel poisons via the consulting-room draught") is required to carry its precondition facts (access = same-location + authority), the author must fill them, and filling them surfaces the contradiction (Surel is a lower-floor bed-patient; the draught sits in the locked consulting room only the doctor's key opens). So Band 3 is not "forever invisible"; it is "deeper to model". The TRUE ceiling — what the store cannot reach at any depth — is prose aesthetics (voice, surprise, reader pleasure) and the unbounded commonsense of which world-facts are even relevant; those stay with the author/model (the manifest's recorded ceiling bound). The trade-off R475 understated: deeper modeling catches more but raises authoring burden, and at 60 scenes / Fable tier plain's loose improvised notes were cheaper than loop's strict-but-Band-1-only gating. The product implication SHARPENS: the carries are not just drift detection but a DEPTH LADDER — scalar/arithmetic gates, typed-predicate enforcement, precondition/affordance modeling, prose-vs-store drift — each catching a band the current store misses, each at a cost. This does NOT reverse R475 (loop still lost 3 vs 5, plain still swept preference 3-0); it relocates the loss from "the store's limit" to "the store's unbuilt depth", which is a product direction, not a dead end.

Round 476 — scale-floor result refined:.publishable_decision_summary: R475 framed the loop's losses as "store-consistency != causal coherence", but on reflection (owner challenge: timeline should be store-guaranteed) that binary is too coarse. The line between what the store can and cannot guarantee is a MODELING-DEPTH CONTINUUM, not a fixed boundary, with three bands. Band 1 — what the store already gates: custody, life-status, scene order (loop scored D1/D2/D4 = 0). Band 2 — what the store COULD gate but currently does not: timeline/scalar arithmetic (the "six-weeks-in-three-weeks" fault; A/B's "1913 / twelve years / 1923" is the same band) and same-entity multi-fact contradiction (the "Surel" alias-vs-true-name fault, catchable by forcing typed predicates so two claims about one entity collide). The store RECEIVES these as facts; its current gates (exclusive/transition) just do no arithmetic and do not force typing. Band 3 — what looks structurally out of reach: the murderer's missing locked-room access. The refinement: even Band 3 is reachable by PRECONDITION/AFFORDANCE modeling — if an action fact ("Surel poisons via the consulting-room draught") is required to carry its precondition facts (access = same-location + authority), the author must fill them, and filling them surfaces the contradiction (Surel is a lower-floor bed-patient; the draught sits in the locked consulting room only the doctor's key opens). So Band 3 is not "forever invisible"; it is "deeper to model". The TRUE ceiling — what the store cannot reach at any depth — is prose aesthetics (voice, surprise, reader pleasure) and the unbounded commonsense of which world-facts are even relevant; those stay with the author/model (the manifest's recorded ceiling bound). The trade-off R475 understated: deeper modeling catches more but raises authoring burden, and at 60 scenes / Fable tier plain's loose improvised notes were cheaper than loop's strict-but-Band-1-only gating. The product implication SHARPENS: the carries are not just drift detection but a DEPTH LADDER — scalar/arithmetic gates, typed-predicate enforcement, precondition/affordance modeling, prose-vs-store drift — each catching a band the current store misses, each at a cost. This does NOT reverse R475 (loop still lost 3 vs 5, plain still swept preference 3-0); it relocates the loss from "the store's limit" to "the store's unbuilt depth", which is a product direction, not a dead end.

Round 477 — drift detection designed: cl.decision_summary: The scale-floor carry's first depth-ladder rung — drift detection — is designed (design-only, build owner-gated). PROBLEM: a store fact's claim ("setup X pays off") is never checked against whether the prose supports it; in scale-floor (R475/R476) the loop self-marked "12/12 paid", passed every gate (D1/D2/D4 = 0), yet the prose left threads unresolved — a claim-vs-evidence DRIFT invisible to the deterministic gate. It is distinct from R404 byte-integrity (did the text change) and from R428 artifact-hash staleness (did a confirmed artifact change); this is whether the claim ever matched the evidence AT ALL — a semantic check that a deterministic gate cannot do, so it needs an LLM. REUSE, NOT NEW SUBSTRATE: the R428 confirmation-event infrastructure carries almost all of it — ConfirmerKind::Model, method = semantic_review, verdict = Confirm | Refute, required rationale, and crucially SELF-CONFIRM REJECT (max-rigor sec 4.7), which is the exact fix for the loop's false assurance: an authoring run can no longer confirm its own "paid" claim — an independent confirmer must review prose-vs-claim before the fact counts as confirmed. R457-459 discovery carries the rest (report-candidates -> import-verdicts, all-or-nothing, --dry-run, claim-sha staleness, the B-1 isolation that keeps LLM reasoning outside the store). THE ONE NEW PIECE: ConfirmationClaim (today section-only: VerifiesBinding / SectionCompleteness) gains a FactEvidence { fact_id } variant — "fact.claim is supported by fact.evidence" — which lets the entire confirmation machinery apply to a narrative fact; new surface = 1 enum variant + 2 verbs (report-drift-candidates / import-drift-verdicts), no new substrate. v1 scope = payoff facts (precisely the loop's 12/12 case); venue-neutral, extending to every claim-evidence fact and to spec normative_excerpt sections (the claim-evidence shape is identical). ACCEPTANCE corpus already exists: the Belvoir loop store carries the "12/12 paid" drift, so blind acceptance = run drift detection and check the confess/escalate fake-payoff facts come back Refuted, matching what the S13 blind prose extraction found independently (pre-pin the refute set, R453 mechanism). HONESTY: the confirmer is an LLM so the verdict is not deterministic, but it is recorded as an audit-trail confirmation-event with sha256 pins (R428 spirit: the determinism is in the ledger of who-confirmed-what, not in the judgment); self-confirm reject is the load-bearing rule; band boundary (R476) — drift detection catches "the claim is not in the evidence" (absence/mismatch), NOT "the claim is good" (aesthetics = the true ceiling). SSOT drift-detection-design.md.

Round 478 — session review of R473-R477:.decision_summary: Session review of R473-R477 (the scale-floor design -> execution -> refinement -> drift-design arc). Findings repaid. PRIMARY: the R477 drift design was over-optimistic about reuse. Verified against the code — confirmation is SECTION-COUPLED today: ConfirmationClaim::section_id() assumes every variant carries a section_id, and append_confirmation_event fail-louds if that section does not exist (R287). So the FactEvidence variant is NOT a clean "1 enum variant + no new substrate"; it forces generalizing the confirmation target from "always a section" to "section | fact" (section_id() branches into a target-existence check, the append-time validation looks up narrative_facts for the fact case). It is still the SAME confirmation mechanism (self-confirm reject, staleness, projections all carry — no new trust model), but the honest build surface is "generalize the claim-target abstraction + the two verbs", not a one-line drop-in. drift-detection-design.md corrected with an R478 note. SECOND: the acceptance premise, previously unchecked, is now VERIFIED — the Belvoir loop store carries 162 facts, 21 of them pays_off WITH evidence, a real falsifiable drift target (the S13 blind extraction found confess 1 + escalate 4 fake payoffs from prose alone; drift detection should Refute exactly those). The acceptance corpus is not vapor. THIRD: the belvoir-{plain,loop,extraction,judging} workspaces are clean (agents cleaned their import-manifest temp files; no .sN-*.json residue to sweep). FOURTH: methodology lesson generalized — post-hoc normalization (the reading-copy metadata strip) never fully closes; I failed it twice because my strip and my verification shared the same pattern blind-spot, so the structural fixes are (a) input-side hygiene (keep store-work out of the graded deliverable) and (b) verification INDEPENDENT of implementation (the blind judge, prompted to actively flag non-story text, was the ground truth my self-check structurally could not be). FIFTH: memory bloat noted (project_ab_experiment_run.md now spans A/B + scale-floor + drift design) — a future split candidate, not repaid now (no functional harm). No code findings (the arc was design + experiment, code 0). Doctrine intact: store-direct, frozen-ledger respected (R476 refined R475 via a NEW entry, not a body edit), citation hygiene held.

Round 479 — evidence preserved as git SS.decision_summary: Session review R478 surfaced an SSOT smell on a deeper, owner-prompted pass: the scale-floor ledger entries (R475/R476) assert results in the git SSOT, but the EVIDENCE was not preserved there — the belvoir-* workspaces are local-only (no remote), run-log/report were gitignored, and the judge verdicts lived only in transcript jsonl. For a project that IS an audit-ledger, the conclusion was preserved while its grounds were not — a 5-year-later re-verification would have had nothing to check. R479 repays the evidence half: claudedocs/phase1-scale-floor-experiment/ is now git-tracked (a scoped .gitignore exception; the rest of claudedocs stays ignored), and an evidence/ subdir preserves the raw graded deliverables (plain-story.md, loop-story.md), the D-metric (defect-tables.md), and the final judge verdicts (confront 1st-round + confess/escalate re-judged — the metadata-clean valid set), alongside the already-present run-log / report / manifest / label-map. The conclusion (plain 3 / loop 5, preference 3-0) is now independently re-checkable against its own evidence in the same SSOT. DEFERRED (owner decision, not this round): the experiment-harness ad-hoc-scripting smell — the reading-copy assembly, the shuffle, and the metadata strip were one-off Python/bash scripts, deleted and non-reproducible, violating the no-silent-fail-scripting doctrine (and the strip failed twice, fragile). That repays as a tools/ Rust crate (medium-forge precedent) BEFORE the next experiment (R480+). Doctrine note: the gitignore exception is principled — claudedocs-gitignored holds for transient analysis scratch; the exception is scoped to permanent falsifiable evidence, which an audit-ledger project must preserve. The core (ledger entries, design docs, production code) was already textbook this arc; the smell was confined to experiment infrastructure.

Round 480 — experiment-harness built as.decision_summary: R479 deferred the experiment-harness ad-hoc-scripting smell: the A/B (R471) and scale-floor (R475) experiments did reading-copy assembly, the arm shuffle, and metadata stripping with one-off Python/bash that was then deleted, leaving the experiments non-reproducible and running silent-fail-capable scripting inside a project whose whole thesis is fail-loud verification. R480 repays it as tools/experiment-harness, a separate in-repo workspace (the bench/studio pattern; its own [workspace] so the root build, CI, and pre-commit clippy never compile it) depending only on serde, serde_json, and sha2, with randomness read directly from /dev/urandom so a missing entropy source is a loud error, never a silent fallback. Three subcommands, each repaying one named step. assemble (reading-copy assembly plus the metadata strip) joins story prose to the report-playthrough-manuscript --json (R466) per-world scene order by scene id, drops the scaffolding HTML comments and CHOICE: directive lines, and normalizes the heading sc-NN to title only; a world-order scene with no prose, a duplicate scene id, or a body that strips to nothing is a hard error — the exact silent-fail the deleted Python committed when an empty-default lookup emitted a blank scene unnoticed. shuffle does blind A/B labeling by a /dev/urandom Fisher-Yates and prints a sha256 seal to be recorded in the ledger before reveal. verify-seal is the reveal and audit half, exiting non-zero on a map edited after sealing. Proven by dogfood on the archived Belvoir store-A: assemble reproduces all three judged reading copies (confront, quiet-confess, quiet-escalate) with a prose-only diff of zero — the only delta is a handful of separator lines where the harness places a rule at every scene boundary more regularly than the deleted script. The deleted, non-reproducible transform is now faithfully reproduced by a versioned fail-loud tool, so an auditor can re-derive the exact blind copies the judges read. Token accounting stayed out of scope (manual gen-versus-reread judgment, not an ad-hoc-scripting artifact); deeper CHOICE and ENDING stripping is an explicit future flag, not a silent default. The harness is now the substrate the next experiment must use in place of throwaway scripts.

Round 481 — claim-vs-evidence drift dete.decision_summary: Scale-floor (R475/R476) exposed that store-consistency is not causal coherence: the loop arm self-marked its setups paid, passed every deterministic gate, yet the prose left threads unresolved — a claim-vs-evidence drift the gates cannot see, because they validate the store's internal consistency and never whether a claim is borne out by the evidence it cites. R477 designed the fix and R478 corrected it (confirmation is section-coupled, so this generalizes the claim target, not a one-variant drop-in). R481 builds it by reusing the R428 max-rigor confirmation machinery and adding one claim target — ConfirmationClaim::FactEvidence { fact_id }, "fact.claim is supported by fact.evidence" — reviewed by a model on the semantic_review method with the load-bearing self-confirm reject: an authoring run can no longer rubber-stamp its own claim, which is exactly the false assurance the loop fell into. The R287 target-existence check generalized section to section|fact through a new ClaimTarget, and — because confirmation_events now has a second write path (import_drift_verdicts beside append_confirmation_event) — the invariant set was factored into one shared validate_confirmation_event that both call, with a field-invariant parity test (the R305 half-enforced-invariant rule). Two verbs mirror the R458/R459 discovery pattern: report-drift-candidates (read — every payoff fact with its claim, evidence quote, and claim_sha256 plus its current review status, serving as both the drift-verdicts/v1 authoring contract and the drift surface) and import-drift-verdicts (write — all-or-nothing, dry-run twin, claim-sha staleness re-check, self-confirm reject). A FactEvidence claim never reaches Confirmed via the verifies required-evidence-set (no deterministic tool can judge prose), so the surface reads the semantic-review leg directly; a verdict drifts to Stale when the claim text changes after review (R420 reused, store-only — no files). Schema v19 to v20 (a v20 store carrying a fact_evidence event must not silently load on a v19 binary). v1 scope is payoff facts; venue-neutral by construction — the claim-vs-evidence shape is identical for spec normative_excerpt sections, a later extension.

Round 482 — drift acceptance pre-registe.decision_summary: R481 built drift detection and proved the surface on the Belvoir loop store (21 self-claimed payoffs, 0 reviewed). R482 pre-registers the BLIND acceptance (R453 mechanism) BEFORE the independent reviewer runs, so the bar cannot move after seeing the verdicts. An isolated Pinner session, given only the prior scale-floor finding (scale-floor-report.md + defect-tables.md) and the store — not the R481 internals — derived the expected result set and sealed it as claudedocs/phase1-drift-acceptance/expected-refutes.json, sha256 ff3e2b13a2ba2beb80060dba44dc95a223a4afe28d6a162a144767bec0fd9d79, pinned here before execution. The honest scope: drift v1 checks claim-vs-CITED-evidence per fact, not global causal coherence, so the Pinner kept only the IN-band threads. Expected refute set = 2 facts whose cited payoff scene's own prose negates the claim: f-confess-chart-explained (sc-59 leaves the burning never reaching) and f-escalate-method-toll (sc-63 leaves the chart never guessed and the kinship the reader's not hers; its bundled ledger leg does pay off). Degenerate guard = 4 clean payoffs a refute-everything reviewer must fail: f-diary-opened-confront, f-diary-opened-confess, f-roeder-suicide-confront, f-roeder-suicide-confess. Out of band (excluded, the R476 ceiling) = 5: two whose claims honestly narrate non-resolution and only break in global payoff-coverage bookkeeping (f-escalate-diary-sealed-final, f-escalate-forged-unproven), one impossible-physical-access (f-roeder-murder-escalate, Band 3), one cross-scene same-entity Surel-name contradiction (f-helene-identified-confront, Band 2), one delivered-payoff-with-missing-motive (f-escalate-lindqvist-payoff). Two scale-floor faults (the six-weeks-in-three-weeks timeline, the telegram-pays-off-nothing critique) have no asserting payoff fact among the 21 and are not entered. PASS pin: the blind reviewer refutes BOTH in-band facts AND confirms ALL 4 guards; an out-of-band miss is the expected drift ceiling, recorded not failed. The reviewer (S-REVIEW) runs next in an isolated workspace; the R481 builder must not run it (R453/R469 keystone).

Round 484 — drift redesigned all-determi.decision_summary: R483's blind acceptance falsified the v1 thesis: drift v1 put an LLM verdict in the gate (a FactEvidence confirmation, model / semantic_review), and two independent model reviews diverged on 3 of 21 contested facts (~14%) while the pinned ground truth itself carried a verified error. A single model judgment is not authoritative, and a quorum of models only multiplies the same untrusted judgment. The owner's decision: the gate must be DETERMINISTIC and AI must leave the trust loop entirely. This is not new architecture but the original one — narrative.rs already states the typed leg exists so the deterministic rule gate covers the typed subset; v1 was the deviation, and the deterministic typed layer is already 0-error. v2 principle: the gate checks DECLARED typed structure against declared typed structure (the existing conflict / exclusivity / transition / coverage gates); AI is advisory only, proposing typed legs from prose via the R457-459 typing-discovery loop (report-candidates to import-proposals, all-or-nothing, deterministically validated, owner-confirmed) and never rendering a gating verdict; the irreducible NLU judgment ("does this prose mean what this typed leg says") is the AUTHOR's act of declaring a leg, not a gate. The two drift classes go deterministic. Class A (the scale-floor "claimed paid, prose never delivers"): payoff_coverage today credits a setup on the mere existence of a pays_off edge — it counts the edge, not the substance; strengthen it so an Expected setup carrying a typed state (subject, predicate, V0) is substantiated only by a payoff fact carrying a typed leg on the same (subject, predicate) with a different value V1 (a state change, optionally transition-rule-legal), yielding deterministic paid / unsubstantiated (a bare edge with no typed backing) / unverifiable (untyped on the load-bearing dimension, surfaced never silently passed). Class B (f-helene, claim contradicts its own cited evidence): needs no new mechanism — once the cited scene's load-bearing content is a typed fact, the existing typed exclusivity gate catches it (helene|name|true-family vs helene|name|borrowed = one subject, two incompatible values of an exclusive predicate). The v1 path (ConfirmationClaim::FactEvidence, drift-verdicts/v1, import-drift-verdicts, report-drift-candidates verdict surface, fact_claim_drifted, the drift.rs DriftStatus projection) is the falsified approach, retired in the SAME change that lands the deterministic substantiation gate (not before — removing it now would leave no drift surface); the R481 entry stays the frozen record of the dead end and R483 is its falsification. Build decomposition follows in later rounds; this round is design-only (code 0), grounded by reading R442 payoff_coverage, R446 TypedClaim, and R449 transition/exclusive rules.

Round 485 — drift v2 built all-determini.decision_summary: R484 designed the all-deterministic drift redesign; R485 builds it and retires the R481 LLM-verdict path in the same change (no-legacy-carry). The new deterministic surface is report-payoff-substantiation (read-only): per query world it refines payoff_coverage's credited (paid) set, classifying each credited setup as substantiated (the setup carries a typed state (subject, predicate, V0) AND a crediting payoff fact carries a typed leg on the SAME subject+predicate with a different value — a state change that discharges it), unsubstantiated (the setup is typed and at least one crediting payoff is typed, but none carries the discharging state-change — a hollow payoff, the deterministic analogue of the drift R481 chased with an LLM), or unverifiable (the typed data needed is absent — the setup is untyped, or every crediting payoff is prose-only — surfaced never silently passed; the author types it via the typing-discovery loop and the gate then decides). No model judgment anywhere: the verdict is a pure comparison of declared typed legs, deterministic and re-runnable. Class B (the f-helene "claim contradicts its own cited evidence" drift R483 found) needs no new mechanism — a fixture proves the EXISTING typed exclusivity gate catches it once both load-bearing legs are typed (one subject cannot hold two incompatible values of an exclusive predicate). The whole R481 path is retired: the FactEvidence ConfirmationClaim variant, the ClaimTarget generalization (target() reverted to section_id(), validate_confirmation_event re-inlined into append_confirmation_event — restoring the pre-R481 single write path), the drift-verdicts/v1 import primitive and structs, the validate drift.rs module, the confirmation.rs artifact_drifted fact-branch, the ops/cli/mcp drift wiring, the drift CLI smoke, and the 12 drift unit tests. Schema v20 to v21 records the FactEvidence removal (no canonical store carried such an event; the dogfood store's only ones lived in a throwaway grading copy). AI is now fully OUT of the drift trust loop (the R483 lesson banked) — the gate is the typed/structural deterministic layer, and the typing-discovery loop (R457-459, AI-advisory, deterministically validated) is the only prose-to-type bridge.

Round 486 — drift v2 deterministic accep.decision_summary: Closing the loop the R485 dogfood opened (92% of Belvoir payoffs unverifiable because untyped). v1's acceptance needed a blind reviewer because the verdict was an LLM judgment; v2 is deterministic, so its acceptance needs only the real corpus, faithful typing, and the gates — no AI in any verdict. On a working copy of the Belvoir loop store (the archive stays pristine), the load-bearing name facts were typed faithfully: a name-status scalar predicate, a trunk fact f-surel-name-cover typed helene|name-status|forged (faithful to sc-06's "a name that was not her name, a borrowed coat"), f-helene-identified-confront amended to type its claim helene|name-status|true-family (faithful to "under her own true family name"), and an r-name-status exclusive rule. Results, all deterministic and no AI: (1) Class B PROVEN — with both name-status facts in the same (frame, branch) scope, validate-continuity fires rule_exclusive_overlap at sc-53 (the f-helene contradiction v1 needed an unreliable LLM for, R483, now a pure typed-value comparison); (2) Class A works — report-payoff-substantiation shows the diary chain f-diary-sealed <- f-diary-opened-confront substantiated (a real integrity sealed->opened state-change discharge), f-helene-identified-confront -> f-forged-papers unsubstantiated (the payoff's name-status leg does not discharge the setup's held-by state — hollow or under-typed), and 10 still unverifiable (untyped); (3) a GAP found deterministically — the REAL f-helene defect is cross-branch (trunk forged inherited by confront vs confront true-family), and with the forged fact on trunk the gate reports 0 violations, because the (frame, branch) scoping (R433: sibling world-lines never conflict) excludes it even though confront INHERITS the trunk fact across the fork. Visibility inherits across a fork; conflict-scoping does not — an asymmetry. A branch contradicting its own inherited ancestor (not a sibling) is a within-world contradiction that should be catchable; the fix (a follow-on round) is ancestor-aware conflict scoping (compare against ancestor-inherited facts, still not siblings), distinct from the R433 sibling-divergence-is-data invariant. Code 0; the re-runnable recipe and findings are preserved in claudedocs/phase1-drift-acceptance/DETERMINISTIC-ACCEPTANCE.md (git SSOT, R479).

Round 487 — R486 cross-branch gap retrac.decision_summary: R486 reported a deterministic-gap finding: that the exclusivity gate missed the real f-helene contradiction because it is cross-branch (a trunk assertion the confront branch inherits vs the confront claim), and proposed an ancestor-aware conflict-scoping fix as the follow-on. On building that follow-on, the premise was checked first and found false: it was a TEST ERROR, not a gap. The Belvoir trunk facts live on the spine branch (58 of them; confront and quiet fork from spine at sc-20, confess/escalate from quiet at sc-40). R486 declared the trunk forged-name fact on the main branch instead — an unrelated world-line that confront never inherits — so the gate correctly treated it as data and reported zero violations. Placing the same fact on the real trunk branch (spine), the gate FIRES: validate-continuity reports rule_exclusive_overlap on r-name-status at sc-53 in the confront world, comparing the confront true-family claim against the inherited spine forged fact. The join_world scope resolver (mnemosyne-validate continuity) already makes an ancestor branch and its descendant the same conflict scope (a pair is in-scope when one branch is the other's ancestor-or-equal); only SIBLING world-lines are data (the R433 divergence-is-data invariant). So ancestor-inherited contradictions were always caught — there is no scoping gap and no fix is needed; the user-greenlit ancestor-aware-scoping change is unnecessary. Code 0: this round retracts the false R486 gap finding (frozen ledger — corrected by a new entry, not by rewriting R486) and corrects the evidence doc. Methodology lesson banked: R486's gap was an unverified post-hoc inference (reasoned about scoping without checking the branch topology), the same scale-floor R476/R478 trap — a conclusion that survives only because nothing independent checked it; the independent check here (what branch is the trunk?) is the ground truth. Net: drift v2 is complete and field-correct — exclusivity catches contradictions same-branch AND ancestor-inherited, substantiation classifies payoffs substantiated/unsubstantiated/unverifiable, and AI is out of the verdict.

Round 488 — wrong-branch footgun made lo.decision_summary: R486's "gap" was a wrong-branch authoring error (a trunk fact defaulted to `main` while the trunk was the named branch `spine` the forks inherit), and the system accepted it silently — add-fact validated, validate-continuity passed, and the conflict gate simply never compared the misplaced fact, so a real contradiction would have gone uncaught. R488 makes that footgun fail loud. New deterministic continuity check: a fact's canon coordinate (canon_from, and canon_to when set), IF positioned in the store's canon by some branch's order, must be a node in the fact's OWN branch composed order; otherwise the fact sits on the wrong world-line and emits FactCanonOffBranch. A coordinate named by NO branch order is the orderless / forward-declared mode and is tolerated unchanged (the R440 boundary doctrine). The check reuses CanonOrder (a new names(branch, node) helper over the existing reach_for composition) and runs in scan_continuity, the deterministic gate — the right layer, because the composed canon order is a separate declared artifact the lower atomic write primitives cannot see (so write-time reject is not available; the gate is the trust anchor, the R485 principle). Honest boundary: this catches "the coordinate is not in this branch at all" (the default-to-main case, and any sibling whose world-line lacks the node); it does NOT catch a coordinate that is validly in multiple world-lines declared on the wrong-but-valid sibling — that residual is the same prose-vs-declaration intent-faithfulness class the gate cannot close by construction. Dogfood: the exact R486 stray fact (f-surel-name-cover on main, canon_from sc-06 positioned in spine) now fires fact_canon_off_branch; the correctly-authored belvoir-loop archive stays at zero violations (no false positives), and the mnemosyne dogfood store carries no narrative facts so the commit gates are unaffected.

Round 489 — timeline-scalar interval gat.decision_summary: Depth-ladder rung 1 (R476: scalar/arithmetic gates) is designed as a surface-not-gate after the timeline-scalar PoC (2026-06-13, code 0, phase1-timeline-poc/, gitignored) field-proved the pull the linear scale-floor experiment could not see. The owner challenge re-opened the R475/R476 deferral: the North-Star venue is AAA-game narrative, where the player traverses a branching order the author cannot control, so timeline faults amplify. The PoC: a 2-world-line inheritance slice where the SAME inherited rule (ratification needs 42 days) is clean in the lawful world-line (84-42=42) and a contradiction in the hasty one (31-10=21), while validate-continuity maximally armed (canon order + four exclusive rules + severity reject) returned violations 0 — the fault is a cross-predicate magnitude relation no same-predicate equality gate can express. FIT is small: the scalar value already rides TypedObject::Value, canon order + holds_at already give the per-world read, so the missing piece is read-side arithmetic only, no store-schema change. Design: an interval rule class in narrative-rules/v1 (third beside exclusive/transition, additive under deny_unknown_fields), shape value(left)-value(right) op bound evaluated per frame-world-subject; one class hosts both the gap fault (rung 1) and the ordering/precondition fault (rung 3) via a const-0 bound. Determinism preserved (AI never in the gate, R484/R485): a pure numeric comparison of declared typed legs; the scalar parse fail-louds (interval_operand_unverifiable, the R450/R468/R485 no-silent-skip), the author types it via advisory typing-discovery R457-459. Surface-not-gate: the primary consumer is a read verb report-timeline-gaps (read-first like report-payoff-substantiation R485, cross-frame = data), an opt-in severity wiring into validate-continuity is a follow-on (R413/R419/R423 knob). Reader reuse: report-timeline-gaps is the next holds_at reader (irony R455 4th, playthrough R466 5th), owns no interval algebra (R441 binding rule); one evaluator function both consumers call (R305 parity). v1 boundary: bare-number arithmetic in a single implicit unit; cross-unit normalization is v2 on pull. Design-only, code 0; the build is a separate owner-triggered round restating this shape (R452). SSOT = fictional-adapter-design.md sec 7.20; pull evidence = phase1-timeline-poc/findings.md.

Round 490 — timeline-scalar interval gat.decision_summary: R489 designed the interval rule (depth-ladder rung 1, design sec 7.20); R490 builds it. A new narrative-rules/v1 class `interval` checks, per (frame x world x subject), value(left) - value(right) op bound — op in {ge,le,eq,gt,lt}, bound a literal const or a same-subject scalar predicate. Same-subject by construction (the measured pull: codicil ratified-on-day - codicil signed-on-day >= codicil min-ratify-gap-days), the cross-predicate magnitude relation no exclusivity gate can express. Determinism is preserved (AI never in the gate, R484/R485): a pure numeric comparison of declared typed legs. The scalar parse fail-louds — an operand that is non-numeric, absent on the right/bound leg, or resolves to more than one distinct holding value is surfaced as interval_unverifiable (a count, never gated, the R450/R468/R485 no-silent-skip), never silently passed. ONE evaluator (scan_interval_rule) keyed on the left operand fact and evaluated at THAT fact canon coordinate, resolving the earlier right/bound operands via WorldCtx::holds_at — the gate single point-quantified reader, no parallel time algebra (R441); report-timeline-gaps (the read surface, sec 7.20 step 2) will call the same function (R305/R390 parity). The predicate existence check now covers every referenced predicate (left + right + predicate-bound) in one site (R436 typo guard). Leg/class coherence is extended (R443): an interval rule rejects per/allowed, exclusive/transition reject right/op/bound, and the bound rejects unless exactly one of predicate/const. Wired into scan_continuity under the existing opt-in --severity (default off = surface-not-gate; the read verb and a per-class severity are follow-ons). Live: the timeline PoC hasty world now fires rule_interval_violation (31-10=21 < 42), lawful stays clean (84-42=42 >= 42), interval_unverifiable 0 — the fault that passed the maximally-armed gate (violations 0, R488 PoC) is caught. AS-BUILT DEVIATION from sec 7.20: the design wrote operands as left/right; the build reuses the rule existing primary predicate field for the LEFT operand. RUNG-3 CORRECTION: the PoC ordering fault (signed-on-day vs coming-of-age-day) is CROSS-subject (codicil vs edmund), so it is NOT a const-0 bound on this same-subject class — cross-subject relations are a wider shape, deferred. 5 unit tests, clippy clean, cargo test --workspace green; no store-schema change (v21).

Round 492 — per-class interval severity:.decision_summary: R489 designed the timeline-scalar interval gate, R490 built it (wired into scan_continuity under the shared --severity), R491 built the report-timeline-gaps read surface; R492 builds design sec 7.20 step 3 — per-class opt-in severity, decoupling the interval (timeline) gate from the structural continuity gate. New [continuity].interval_severity (Option Severity, default OFF) plus a validate-continuity --interval-severity override. The gate exit now partitions: structural violations (conflict / off-branch / succession / exclusive / transition) gate under severity; interval (RuleIntervalViolation) violations gate ONLY under interval_severity, OFF by default. So interval is surface-not-gate by default — the violation is always produced as data (in the gate report and in report-timeline-gaps) but never causes a nonzero exit unless the author opts in. R490 had interval riding the shared --severity (rejecting structural also rejected interval); R492 separates them. Doctrine refinement: R449 recorded that rule violations ride severity with no separate knob because a same-frame rule violation is wrong data never a legitimate intermediate state — that holds for EXCLUSIVE and TRANSITION, but INTERVAL is the exception: a scalar timeline gap can be an intentional authored time-bend (games bend time deliberately), so it gets its own knob, the SpecDriftSection legitimate-intermediate-state rationale. The multi-severity precedent is the code-refs gate (severity_missing/binding/coverage/...). Wired: config ContinuitySection.interval_severity, ops ContinuityScanReport (interval_severity plus interval_violation_count), CLI partition plus --interval-severity plus the violations line printing structural=N interval=N, MCP description. Live on the timeline PoC store (interval-only violation): --severity reject alone exits 0 (was exit 1 under R490), --interval-severity reject exits 1, --interval-severity warn exits 0. 3 new tests plus clippy clean; no store-schema change (v21). Remaining sec 7.20 follow-ons: cross-unit normalization (v2), rung-3 cross-subject, the R453 trap-corpus blind grade.

Round 493 — causal coherence is authorin.decision_summary: Two causal-coherence candidates were PoC-tested this session (code 0) and BOTH REFUTED; the meta-conclusion is preserved as git SSOT. The owner asked whether before/after causal relationships are deterministically verifiable, and from the depth-ladder two candidate mechanisms were tested. (1) A causes edge class (a recorded fact-to-fact causal dependency): REFUTE. Live on a flashback slice, the effect-before-cause invariant is ALREADY surfaced as payoff_before_setup (R442, legal mystery/flashback structure, surfaced never gated) — a causes gate over DISCOURSE order would false-positive on every flashback; over STORY time it is the interval gate (rung-1, R490). Acyclicity reuses the SuccessionCycle scan (R463); dangling-cause is rung-3. The only net-new piece (a causal cycle among non-succession facts) is unmeasured, YAGNI. (2) rung-3 cross-subject preconditions (the locked-room: Surel poisons via the consulting-room draught but is a keyless ground-floor patient — the scale-floor measured causal defect): REFUTE new substrate. Two live tests: Test 1 (action declared, no preconditions) = violations 0, the fault invisible (the gate cannot derive that administer-draught requires co-location + authority, commonsense); Test 2 (preconditions declared as concrete typed facts) = EXISTING exclusivity fires both (per-subject location, per-object custody). So the contradiction-check is existing exclusivity (zero new gate); the gap is FORCING (nothing makes the author declare the preconditions); the cross-subject must-equal relation is NOT needed (a concrete required leg suffices for the static case); the only value-add is an AI-advisory precondition-discovery (reuse R457-459), a future pull not justified by one instance. META-CONCLUSION: both decompose into existing mechanisms (exclusivity / SuccessionCycle / interval / payoff) + more authoring (declaring the load-bearing facts). The store causal-coherence reach is bounded by AUTHORING BURDEN, not by missing gates — the empirical confirmation of the R476 depth-ladder thesis. Round 494 — AI-first coverage is bound b.decision_summary: R493 concluded causal coherence is authoring-bound (causes + rung-3 both REFUTED — the gates are sufficient, the gap is authoring); R494 LOCATES that gap precisely via a self-extraction PoC and unifies the session. The agent (an AI) performed the self-extraction LIVE — authoring a 3-scene slice and extracting its own load-bearing facts — with the deterministic continuity gate as the OBJECTIVE judge (not self-graded). One gate (at-location exclusivity per subject), two contradictions of the same shape differing only in EXPLICIT (stated) vs IMPLICIT (entailed): Helene confined to the sickroom + seen at the conservatory (both stated) = explicit; the letter burned in the study with only Helene motive but her location unstated = implicit. Three live results: (1) Run 1, faithful extraction of stated facts only = 1 violation, the explicit contradiction (sickroom vs conservatory) fires, the implicit one is SILENT (helene-at-study was never stated, so a confined Helene burning the letter has no facts to fire on — the coverage gap, deterministic); (2) Probe — report-typing-candidates surfaces 0 untyped facts: the discovery tool surfaces UNTYPED EXISTING facts, but the load-bearing fact is MISSING entirely, so no deterministic tool can surface a fact never recorded; (3) Run 2 — inferring the unstated precondition (helene-at-study) and adding it makes the implicit contradiction fire, the loop closes but only via INFERENCE. Secondary: un-extracted MOVEMENT transitions left three locations co-holding (the same implicit-fact gap in a second guise — prose carries states, not the moves between them). CONVERGENCE: all three session PoCs point to one conclusion — the gates are sufficient; AI-first end-to-end coverage (the scale-floor R475 binding constraint) is bound by the AI INFERENCE of IMPLICIT load-bearing facts (preconditions, transitions), which no deterministic tool can supply (a missing fact is invisible). LEVERAGE: an AI-advisory implicit-fact inference step in the authoring loop — propose the entailed preconditions/transitions from each scene prose (the R457-459 discovery pattern but AI-driven, not human-approved, per the AI-first North Star), record them, let the existing gates check. Testable only under the scale-floor blind session-separated protocol (R469): does AI inference of implicit facts measurably raise coverage without costing prose quality (the open regime question). HONEST BOUNDARY: a single self-authoring agent cannot blind-measure its own coverage RATE (the contradictions are mine) — this is a MECHANISM demonstration (faithful extraction structurally omits unstated entailments), not a statistic; the AAA-scale rate is the deferred blind protocol. The true ceiling (R476) stands: the gate checks declared facts; whether inferred preconditions are the right/complete set is commonsense, author/model. Round 495 — facts-first dissolves the ex.decision_summary: R494 located the AI-first coverage bottleneck in prose-to-facts extraction (the AI under-infers implicit facts); R495 records the owner facts-first reframing, PoC-validated at the mechanism level: flip the order to facts-to-prose and the extraction gap DISSOLVES. The agent authored a Belvoir-mystery fact-base TRUTH-FIRST (the load-bearing helene-at-study in the truth frame up front, because authoring the murder truth cannot omit placing Helene at the scene), gate-checked it, and hand-rendered prose as a PROJECTION. Three live results: (1) the fact-base gate-checks clean with the truth-vs-belief divergence as DATA (validate-continuity violations 0, cross_scope 1) — the perspectival frame model (north-star: agent-belief is not ground-truth, both true) carries the misdirection without a false alarm; (2) report-irony-intervals (R455) surfaces the divergence as a deterministic window (household sickroom vs truth study, opens at sc-murder) — the mystery engine made queryable, not lost; (3) contrast — a same-frame error (Helene in two locations IN the truth frame) IS caught (rule_exclusive_overlap, exit 1), so facts-first does not weaken the gate: cross-frame = mystery (data), same-frame = real error (gated). Truth/revelation separation was demonstrated by two hand-rendered prose projections of the SAME base: the household projection withholds the truth (never states helene-at-study) = mystery; the truth projection reveals it. Mystery and consistency coexist because the truth lives in the checked base and the prose reveals selectively. WHY THE GAP DISSOLVES: in prose-to-facts the load-bearing fact was never stated so extraction missed it (R494); in facts-to-prose it is in the base by construction, there is no lossy extraction step, the gate validates the base BEFORE prose, and the prose is a projection that cannot assert what the facts lack. This re-derives the north-star architecture thesis (every artifact is a projection of the one substrate) and is the CYOA-renderer backlog direction. WHAT IT ADVANCES: the AI-first authoring loop is not extract-better-from-prose but author-the-fact-base-first (gates checking it live), then project prose. HONEST BOUNDARIES: hand-rendered (no automated facts-to-prose renderer exists, CYOA unbuilt); prose CRAFT untested (does facts-first yield good narrative or wooden list-prose — the scale-floor craft tension where plain won; needs the blind session-separated judge R469); fact RELEVANCE still authoring-bound (facts-first forces declaring the load-bearing facts but does not invent which are relevant — the R476 ceiling). Round 501 — disclosure (discourse) layer.decision_summary: Designed the disclosure (discourse) layer (code 0): the rhetorical axis selecting which facts surface, when, and how, between the fact base and prose — the orthogonal third axis R500's 3-0 craft loss exposed; rung-1 frame-limit tested before rung-2 plan built.
changes_bullets: Provenance + diagnosis: R500 executed the facts-first craft blind-test and lost preference 3-0 to plain (3 blind judges, 9/9 world-lines; prose-quality means 3.11 vs 4.33), while PRED-1 fidelity HELD — render-as-projection is gate-clean end to end. The precise cause (owner insight 2026-06-13): rendering A FRAME stated ALL that frame holding facts (the omniscient truth frame, the telling-dial stuck at max), so the prose front-loaded the solution. fidelity != craft; the gap is a MISSING axis, not a substrate fault — R500 proved the fact substrate sound and it is NOT redesigned here.

The diagnosis = a missing ORTHOGONAL axis. Three axes, the third absent today: (1) truth — what is true (substrate, sound); (2) belief/frame — who knows what (epistemic; the branch frame engine, R430); (3) disclosure — what the READER is told, when, how (rhetorical/discourse; MISSING). R500 collapsed axis 3 into axis 2 (render-a-frame = expose all that frame facts), but frame is epistemic (who knows) and disclosure is rhetorical (what the reader is told) — orthogonal. Narratology names this: fabula (the full fact set = the fact base) vs syuzhet/discourse (selection, order, focalization, disclosure-rate, mode). sec 7.21 jumped fabula to prose with no discourse layer between.

Orthogonality made precise (the schema must NOT reconflate — that conflation IS the R500 bug): the FOCAL frame of a scene BOUNDS the max exposable (a fact the focal character cannot know is unrenderable in tight third — a frame matter, a different gate); the DISCLOSURE plan selects WITHIN that bound (what of the knowable is surfaced, in what mode, when). So a render = the intersection of focal-frame and disclosure-slice; disclosure decisions are per (fact x telling/reader-channel), NEVER per (fact x character-frame). A close-third detective who KNOWS the killer (frame) can still WITHHOLD it from the reader until the reveal (disclosure) — reader-knowledge is not focal-frame-knowledge.

Unification thesis (absorb, do not duplicate — the CLAUDE.md half-enforced-invariant guard): the disclosure axis GENERALIZES five things already in the codebase. payoff_expectation / pays_off (R442) = disclosure TIMING (a setup is disclosed before its payoff). report-irony-intervals (R455) = a disclosure-STATE divergence (reader told X, a character-frame excludes X). The exposure-PoC three additive primitives (sec 10 Tier-3, fragment-exposure / FromSoftware model, 2026-06-11) map one-to-one: exposure-surface binding = the disclosure EVENT (this scene/object discloses fact F in mode M); exposure-coverage = the disclosure-COVERAGE report; exposure-order = the disclosure first-at coordinate + the premature-leak gate. payoff and irony stay the ONE reader each; the disclosure checks DELEGATE to them, never re-implement.

Data model — the DISCLOSURE PLAN (stored, deterministic, gate-checkable). A named TELLING over the fact base (telling:mystery, telling:dark-souls) = a POLICY (default mode, default = withhold — the sparse-frame ethos already named on the discourse axis for the R442 unmarked default: never serialized when default) + sparse per-fact OVERRIDES { fact -> { mode: state | hint | imply | withhold, first_at: the discourse coordinate where the reader first learns it (distinct from the fact canon coordinate = when it is TRUE), surface: the optional scene/object the disclosure rides on } }. MULTIPLE plans over one base = many tellings: disclosure is the DIAL that turns one fact base into Dark-Souls-fragment / classic-mystery / expository-thriller (the North Star "one substrate -> many tellings," now concrete).

Determinism boundary (AI never in the gate — R484/R485 holds by construction). STORED + deterministic: the plan (mode + first_at + surface). RENDER-TIME craft (LLM Layer B, not stored, not gated): HOW to realize mode=imply (which object, which phrasing — "imply via the stopped clock"), and the prose itself (blind-judge graded, never self-graded). The GATE = premature-leak, checked by BLIND RE-EXTRACTION (the exact R500 technique): re-extract the prose, assert no fact whose mode is in {withhold, hint, imply} appears as a STATED fact before its first_at — deterministic over re-extracted facts vs the plan, so the AI stays out of the gate. Disclosure-order delegates to payoff (R442); disclosure-coverage (disclosed / hidden-by-design / never-planned) is surface-not-gate (the R442 dangling-is-a-todo discipline; the THIRD coverage instance after R389/R390 spec + R442 payoff).

render-brief becomes the CARRIER (sec 7.21 step 2, previously just a --frame filter). Per scene it now carries the per-fact disclosure decisions { state F1, F2; hint F3; imply F4 via the clock; withhold F5, F6 }. R500 found the render step "near-mechanical given only the holding-fact list" — the disclosure plan is precisely the craft-bearing input that bare list LACKED: the LLM is no longer told "recite these facts" (which produced the wooden told-prose) but given a show-don't-tell instruction set. This is the concrete mechanism by which the disclosure layer is expected to close the R500 craft gap.

The ladder + YAGNI sequencing (cheapest test first; build new substrate only on demonstrated need — the R499/R500 test-before-build discipline). RUNG 1 (ZERO new substrate): render from a LIMITED focal frame (close-third on a character, not the omniscient truth frame R500 used); auto-withholds what the focal character does not know; this is the render-brief --frame filter ALREADY designed (sec 7.21 step 2, YAGNI-deferred) used with a non-omniscient frame — the single biggest lever, since R500 max-exposure omniscient render is the worst case. RUNG 2 (the genuinely new axis): the explicit per-fact disclosure plan above; build GATED on rung-1 craft re-run showing frame-limitation INSUFFICIENT. Reconciliation with the exposure PoC: "player as a sparse frame" was the closest existing primitive, but its two recorded GAPS — A1 (no primitive records "fragment X exposes fact F") and A6 (canon-order is in-world time, not player-discovery order, so "exposed too early" is inexpressible) — are EXACTLY the disclosure axis showing through; the player-frame is a special case (reader-knowledge approximates an in-world frame grown by diegetic exposure), not the general model.

The exposure PoC is sec 10 Tier-3 (2026-06-11, code 0), not a round number, and is cited as such.

Code 0 — design round (the R496/R499 pattern). Build + clippy unchanged; the fact substrate is NOT redesigned (R500 proved render-as-projection fidelity sound — PRED-1 held). Only the missing discourse layer between facts and prose is drawn.

North Star confirmed, not broken: "projection is the interface; one substrate -> many tellings" — the disclosure axis is the dial that was missing to make "many tellings" real, deepening the multi-axis/perspectival model to truth + belief-frame + disclosure. AI-first end-to-end unchanged: the disclosure plan is authored + gate-checked like any fact, the render is the AI Layer B, the gate stays deterministic (blind re-extraction).

Acceptance is DEFINED, not yet pinned (execution is a future owner-triggered round): re-run the R500 craft blind-test WITH the disclosure layer (rung-1 frame-limited render FIRST), graded by the blind, session-separated judge — the craft gap closing is the success signal. The R500 contamination bound carries: this lineage designed the mechanism and may NOT author or blind-judge its own prose (the R469 discipline).
carry_forward_bullets: Build is pull-gated and per-half (R496/R499): rung-1 = the render-brief --frame filter (sec 7.21 step 2, already YAGNI-deferred) used with a non-omniscient focal frame; rung-2 = the explicit disclosure plan, built ONLY if rung-1 craft re-run shows frame-limitation insufficient. Do not build either speculatively.

Absorb-don't-duplicate guard (CLAUDE.md half-enforced-invariant): payoff (R442) and irony (R455) remain the single reader each; disclosure-order and disclosure-state checks DELEGATE to them. The exposure-PoC three additive primitives (surface-binding / coverage / order) are the disclosure plan storage / coverage report / premature-leak gate — build them as ONE axis, not five features, when pulled.

Round 502 — session review of R501: the.decision_summary: Sharpened R501's determinism boundary (code 0): the disclosure premature-leak gate is mode-INDEPENDENT (every planned fact non-extractable before its first_at, payoff a special case); the gate checks only the exposed/withheld binary + first_at timing, while state/hint/imply is craft (blind-judged) — the half-enforced-invariant the R501 wording conceded.
changes_bullets: Finding (session review of R501, this lineage's own entry): R501 bullet 6 wrote the disclosure premature-leak gate as "no fact whose mode is in {withhold, hint, imply} appears as a STATED fact before its first_at" — two defects. (a) The mode enumeration is wrong: premature-leak is mode-INDEPENDENT — a mode=state fact also must not leak before ITS first_at, and withhold is simply first_at = never. (b) It implies the gate distinguishes state/hint/imply, but blind RE-EXTRACTION yields only a BINARY signal (extractable / not): a successful HINT is meant to let the reader infer the fact, so a good extractor surfaces it — indistinguishable from a statement. The gate therefore CANNOT grade state-vs-hint. As written that is the CLAUDE.md half-enforced-invariant anti-pattern (a gate claiming to enforce four modes while actually enforcing a binary = no invariant + silent broken state), and it blurs exactly the determinism boundary the R483-R488 drift arc and R484/R485 (AI never in the gate) make this project's keystone.

The corrected boundary (the design DIRECTION of R501 is unchanged; only the gate wording is sharpened). DETERMINISTICALLY GATE-CHECKABLE (re-extraction is the technique; the gate is deterministic over the extracted fact set): (1) WITHHOLD — a withhold-mode fact must NEVER be re-extractable in this telling (the binary); (2) first_at TIMING — EVERY planned fact F must not be re-extractable before its first_at coordinate (mode-independent; payoff R442 is the special case setup.first_at precedes payoff). CRAFT, never gated (blind judge): the state / hint / imply gradation AT or after first_at — HOW a disclosed fact is conveyed. The four modes are an AUTHORING vocabulary (the render-brief instruction set, the craft-bearing input R500 lacked); only the exposed/withheld binary + the timing are ENFORCED. The render skeleton is deterministic, craft fills it — the project's standing division, now stated precisely for disclosure.

Methodology precision: "the R500 technique" names the blind RE-EXTRACTION method (re-extract prose, run a deterministic gate over the extracted facts) that premature-leak REUSES — it does NOT mean premature-leak is already validated. R500's PRED-1 checked CONTRADICTION with the base (D1 + D2 + D4 = exclusivity / succession / etc.), not disclosure TIMING; premature-leak is a NEW gate (non-disclosure-before-first_at), pinned only at the acceptance re-run, never by R500. R501's "the exact R500 technique" must be read as the method, not a proof.

Two R501 under-specifications recorded (defer to build, no silent gap): first_at is per (fact x telling x WORLD-LINE) — reading order differs per branch, consistent with the existing per-world reporting contract (R455 irony, R466 manuscript); and surface (the object/environment a disclosure rides on, "imply via the stopped clock") has no substrate mapping yet (fact vs entity vs section) — a build-time decision, flagged not guessed.

publishable_changes_bullets: Finding (session review of R501, this lineage's own entry): R501 bullet 6 wrote the disclosure premature-leak gate as "no fact whose mode is in {withhold, hint, imply} appears as a STATED fact before its first_at" — two defects. (a) The mode enumeration is wrong: premature-leak is mode-INDEPENDENT — a mode=state fact also must not leak before ITS first_at, and withhold is simply first_at = never. (b) It implies the gate distinguishes state/hint/imply, but blind RE-EXTRACTION yields only a BINARY signal (extractable / not): a successful HINT is meant to let the reader infer the fact, so a good extractor surfaces it — indistinguishable from a statement. The gate therefore CANNOT grade state-vs-hint. As written that is the CLAUDE.md half-enforced-invariant anti-pattern (a gate claiming to enforce four modes while actually enforcing a binary = no invariant + silent broken state), and it blurs exactly the determinism boundary the R483-R488 drift arc and R484/R485 (AI never in the gate) make this project's keystone.

The corrected boundary (the design DIRECTION of R501 is unchanged; only the gate wording is sharpened). DETERMINISTICALLY GATE-CHECKABLE (re-extraction is the technique; the gate is deterministic over the extracted fact set): (1) WITHHOLD — a withhold-mode fact must NEVER be re-extractable in this telling (the binary); (2) first_at TIMING — EVERY planned fact F must not be re-extractable before its first_at coordinate (mode-independent; payoff R442 is the special case setup.first_at precedes payoff). CRAFT, never gated (blind judge): the state / hint / imply gradation AT or after first_at — HOW a disclosed fact is conveyed. The four modes are an AUTHORING vocabulary (the render-brief instruction set, the craft-bearing input R500 lacked); only the exposed/withheld binary + the timing are ENFORCED. The render skeleton is deterministic, craft fills it — the project's standing division, now stated precisely for disclosure.

Methodology precision: "the R500 technique" names the blind RE-EXTRACTION method (re-extract prose, run a deterministic gate over the extracted facts) that premature-leak REUSES — it does NOT mean premature-leak is already validated. R500's PRED-1 checked CONTRADICTION with the base (D1 + D2 + D4 = exclusivity / succession / etc.), not disclosure TIMING; premature-leak is a NEW gate (non-disclosure-before-first_at), pinned only at the acceptance re-run, never by R500. R501's "the exact R500 technique" must be read as the method, not a proof.

changes_bullets: Verification + fairness verdict (this session reviewed the externally-executed R504). R504 + its run/ artifacts are real and uncommitted. The contamination-repair episode was investigated by walking the full .clean diffs: the manual normalization is FAIR — symmetric in kind (same scaffolding categories stripped from both arms: bracket annotations, CHOICE blocks, the all-six-setups answer key, world-line maps), prose-preserving (no scene prose altered; the only added lines are normalized headings), heading-normalization symmetric (A 29/29, B 33/33), and the strip rule is label-INDEPENDENT.
