Round 613 — the COORDINATE axis designed.decision_summary: The COORDINATE axis, designed — and the design ROUND is the finding, because my first design was REFUTED before it could be built. Setting: R611 fixed the FACT axis by silently widening the COORDINATE axis, which BLINDED two deterministic gates (validate-render-fidelity for a divergent world now REWARDS a render that delivered the trunk's ending and FLAGS the faithful one; R488's wrong-world-line guard goes silent past the fork) and put phantom scenes on the pinion seam. R612 fixed the fact axis properly with the membership lattice and deliberately did not touch this. So: `CanonOrder` is asked TWO different questions and answers both from one derived node set — PRECEDENCE ("can this world's order COMPARE a and b?", which must stay GENEROUS: R611's widening is MEASURED to have repaired four gates, and both reviewers confirm no case needs it narrowed) and ROAD ("which coordinates does this world TRAVEL, and where does it END?", which must be BOUNDED). Splitting them is the round's surviving thesis. THE DRAFT I WROTE derived the road from the R612 membership lattice. Two independent adversarial reviewers implemented it against the real crates and ran it over all 46 store-times-order pairs in the repo, and it is WRONG — not marginally: its own seed clause re-admitted the exact leak it was written to block; applying the FACT bound to EDGES collapsed a playable world's road to a single node, turning its own facts into false positives; on a REAL store it silently made a world's ENDING the story's OPENING scene, so the terminal gate would pass prose that renders only the briefing — a silent wrong answer from the gate that exists to catch silent wrong answers; and it would newly reject 381 facts across 13 pairs in four breakage classes where I had admitted one, INCLUDING the confluence's own facts, which are the very subject of MNEMO-GAP-003. THE LAW THAT EXPLAINS ALL OF IT, and the reason no patch to the draft can work: FACTS INTERSECT AT A MERGE, ROADS UNION AT A MERGE. They are DUALS. A fork CUTS facts (conjoin a bound) but OVERRIDES the road (its own out-edge at the departure coordinate replaces the inherited one). R612's intersect deletes the parents from a confluence's membership BY DESIGN — that is what makes the fact axis right — so for any world whose prefix runs through a merge, the member edge set no longer holds the edges that carry the road. One lattice cannot serve both axes. THE MODEL: road = an OVERRIDE WALK. A coordinate is on W's road iff it is a declared SEED, or an edge into it leaves a coordinate ALREADY on the road, declared by the CLOSEST member branch declaring an out-edge there (own beats nearest fork ancestor beats the base). No fact-bound is consulted on the road axis at all — which is precisely why it neither collapses nor forces the order to compare coordinates on a parallel chain (the R456 incomparable-is-first-class idiom the draft violated). Validated against every topology in the repo, including the two real stores the draft broke, which it leaves PASSING. THE SUBSTRATE FINDING (and the correction of my own false refute-first): the store CANNOT distinguish "W forks in FACTS ONLY and continues down the trunk" from "W forks and ENDS at its own beat" — both encode as forks_from with no edge set, and my draft silently reinterpreted the first as the second, which IS the 381. The resolution is not a new field but a DECLARATION-COMPLETENESS fail-loud that NAMES the ambiguity and hands the author the lever, so the default (undeclared = the trunk) is both correct and loudly named. That converts a LYING gate into an honest one at zero migration cost. Code 0. The build is R614, gated on ratification.

Round 614 — the ROAD axis built: names/l.decision_summary: The COORDINATE axis, BUILT to the R613 design — and the three deterministic gates R611 blinded are measurably un-blinded. `CanonOrder` was answering TWO different questions from one derived node set: PRECEDENCE ("can this world's order COMPARE a and b?") and ROAD ("which coordinates does it TRAVEL, and where does it END?"). R611 had to widen the first — that widening is MEASURED to have repaired four gates, including a disclosure leak that was passing at exit 0 — and in doing so it silently widened the second, which is what made `validate-render-fidelity` REWARD a render that delivered the trunk's ending and FLAG the faithful one, silenced R488's wrong-world-line guard past a fork, and put phantom scenes on the pinion seam. R614 splits them: `reach` keeps powering `le`/`comparable`, UNCHANGED and generous; a new `road` powers `names`/`linearize`/`is_maximal`, bounded. THE ROAD IS AN OVERRIDE WALK, not a bound: a coordinate is on W's road iff it is a declared SEED, or an edge reaches it FROM a coordinate ALREADY on the road, declared by the CLOSEST member branch declaring an out-edge there. A branch that declares its own successor at a shared coordinate REPLACES the inherited one; a branch that declares nothing CONTINUES its lineage's road. The `u is already on the road` requirement is what refuses the leak: a confluence legitimately declares a merge edge from EACH parent, so a SIBLING's exclusive coordinate is NAMED by a branch every downstream world belongs to — under a node-set union it leaks (the R611 defect, and the R613 draft's seed clause re-admitted it); under the override walk the edge simply cannot fire from a source the world never reaches. CRUCIALLY the road lineage is NOT `world_membership`: facts INTERSECT at a merge, roads UNION, and R612's intersect deletes the parents from a confluence's membership BY DESIGN — deriving the road from the fact lattice is what collapsed the refuted draft. No fact-bound is consulted on the road axis at all, which is also why it never asks the order to compare coordinates on a parallel chain, where they are legitimately incomparable rather than past. THE SUBSTRATE AMBIGUITY IS NAMED, NOT GUESSED: a branch that declares no road rides its lineage's road on, so its ENDING is the trunk's — correct for a world-line diverging only in FACTS, wrong for a divergent ending whose road was never declared, and the store cannot tell them apart. So `undeclared_roads` + a CLI NOTICE hands the author the lever instead of silently picking a reading. That is what keeps this NON-BREAKING: measured over 70 real store-times-order pairs, ZERO newly-rejecting — against 381 newly-rejected facts for the refuted draft on the same corpus. `is_maximal` now reads the road and `terminals()` returns the END SET, because a world-line legitimately has several ends.

Round 614 — the ROAD axis built: names/l.publishable_decision_summary: The COORDINATE axis, BUILT to the R613 design — and the three deterministic gates R611 blinded are measurably un-blinded. `CanonOrder` was answering TWO different questions from one derived node set: PRECEDENCE ("can this world's order COMPARE a and b?") and ROAD ("which coordinates does it TRAVEL, and where does it END?"). R611 had to widen the first — that widening is MEASURED to have repaired four gates, including a disclosure leak that was passing at exit 0 — and in doing so it silently widened the second, which is what made `validate-render-fidelity` REWARD a render that delivered the trunk's ending and FLAG the faithful one, silenced R488's wrong-world-line guard past a fork, and put phantom scenes on the pinion seam. R614 splits them: `reach` keeps powering `le`/`comparable`, UNCHANGED and generous; a new `road` powers `names`/`linearize`/`is_maximal`, bounded. THE ROAD IS AN OVERRIDE WALK, not a bound: a coordinate is on W's road iff it is a declared SEED, or an edge reaches it FROM a coordinate ALREADY on the road, declared by the CLOSEST member branch declaring an out-edge there. A branch that declares its own successor at a shared coordinate REPLACES the inherited one; a branch that declares nothing CONTINUES its lineage's road. The `u is already on the road` requirement is what refuses the leak: a confluence legitimately declares a merge edge from EACH parent, so a SIBLING's exclusive coordinate is NAMED by a branch every downstream world belongs to — under a node-set union it leaks (the R611 defect, and the R613 draft's seed clause re-admitted it); under the override walk the edge simply cannot fire from a source the world never reaches. CRUCIALLY the road lineage is NOT `world_membership`: facts INTERSECT at a merge, roads UNION, and R612's intersect deletes the parents from a confluence's membership BY DESIGN — deriving the road from the fact lattice is what collapsed the refuted draft. No fact-bound is consulted on the road axis at all, which is also why it never asks the order to compare coordinates on a parallel chain, where they are legitimately incomparable rather than past. THE SUBSTRATE AMBIGUITY IS NAMED, NOT GUESSED: a branch that declares no road rides its lineage's road on, so its ENDING is the trunk's — correct for a world-line diverging only in FACTS, wrong for a divergent ending whose road was never declared, and the store cannot tell them apart. So `undeclared_roads` + a CLI NOTICE hands the author the lever instead of silently picking a reading. That is what keeps this NON-BREAKING: measured over 70 real store-times-order pairs, ZERO newly-rejecting — against 381 newly-rejected facts for the refuted draft on the same corpus. `is_maximal` now reads the road and `terminals()` returns the END SET, because a world-line legitimately has several ends.

Round 615 — evidence is a ROAD question:.decision_summary: Paying the debt R614 itself created, and closing the R613 review carry. R614 moved the R488 wrong-world-line guard onto the ROAD axis but left EVIDENCE reachability on `le` alone — and the two are ONE principle ("could this world have SEEN that scene?"), so a single rule was left carrying two different invariants: exactly the half-enforced-invariant trap this project forbids, and I introduced it one round earlier. PROVEN exploitable before fixing, not assumed: on the shipped R614 binary a fact on a divergent `ending` cited a scene that only its SIBLING travels, and the gate returned 0 violations — the generous precedence order still connects that scene, because a confluence declares a merge edge from EVERY parent. Both halves now ask the road. The naive tightening then DOUBLED the violation count on two real stores while naming ZERO additional facts, so the round also fixes the reporting: a fact whose OWN coordinate is off-road is already named by FactCanonOffBranch, and there is no world in which to ask "could it have seen that" when the beat itself is not on the road — the evidence axis stays quiet about it. Also closed: an ORPHANED ROAD EDGE (a declared edge whose source the branch never reaches) now fails LOUD instead of silently truncating a world-line, possibly at its own ending — 0 of 83 real pairs trip it, including the detroit store whose branch legitimately declares a road segment starting BEFORE its fork point. And the AUTHORING CONTRACT: describe-schema's `branches` registry now carries the world-line model a blind author cannot otherwise self-serve — the two axes and their DUAL merge behaviour (facts INTERSECT, roads UNION), that authoring a MERGE RELOCATES TRUNK OWNERSHIP onto the confluence, that the base `edges` ARE main's road while each `branches` entry is that world-line's own road segment, that a branch declaring no road inherits the TRUNK'S ENDING and what that costs at the render-fidelity gate, and that evidence is a road question — with a concept-pin test so the prose cannot drift off the code again, which is precisely how R611 and R614 went wrong. Finally, the R613 review asked for the merge-edge convention to be PINNED; having built the walk, the honest answer is that no pin is needed — the "you must GET there" requirement makes the choice unobservable — and the contract now says so rather than inventing a rule.

Round 616 — MNEMO-GAP-005 reviewed: both.decision_summary: MNEMO-GAP-005 (from the-tide-that-counts) asked for two things: a per-fact provenance facet (Canon/Invented/Structural) and a branch-owned-density projection. A cost-no-object review (three independent adversarial reviewers plus measurement against the real 827-fact consumer store) refuted BOTH designs before any build — the R613 pattern, where the refutation is the round's most valuable output. Density: the proposed denominator (own segment = road(B) minus the union of parent roads) collapses to EMPTY on every confluence, because a converging parent forward-inherits the merge suffix, so it is a divide-by-zero on a legal store — proven on the real R614 fixture. Provenance: measured against the real store, the trichotomy is the wrong shape because its two axes have opposite derivability and opposite granularity. STRUCTURAL (quest plumbing) is per-fact and fully derivable (typed quest predicates unioned with the completed_by->pays_off giving-setup binding the quest graph already computes) — verified to reproduce all 80 plumbing facts exactly with zero false-positives — so storing it would only duplicate the quest structure. CANON-vs-INVENTED is per-branch and genuinely NOT derivable (branch != main mislabels the 543 canonical weave confluence facts, 66 percent of the store), but it is adaptation-fidelity metadata — vacuous for an original work and the same class the gap itself defers as out-of-charter for its canon-manifest denominator. Owner decision C: derive structural natively (zero schema) and keep canon-vs-invented consumer-side, consistent with the north-star (original-work authoring; adaptation fidelity is a consumer concern like SCE). The per-fact trichotomy is dropped; density lands corrected (own-declared-segment denominator, road-consistent numerator, Option for the empty-own-segment signal). This is a code-0 design round; R617 builds density and R618 builds the derived structural coverage split.
changes_bullets: REJECTED the gap's per-fact provenance facet (`NarrativeFact.provenance {Canon,Invented,Structural}`): three independent adversarial reviewers plus measurement against the real 827-fact consumer store converged that it is the wrong shape — it stores the one thing that is fully derivable and mis-locates the one thing that is not, per-fact, with a `canon_from` naming collision. No `NarrativeFact` schema change lands.

STRUCTURAL (quest plumbing) is DERIVED, not stored: `structural = (typed.predicate in {pursues,requires,completed_by}) UNION (an Expected fact paid off by a completed_by-typed fact)` — the same completed_by->pays_off giving-setup binding `quest_graph` already computes (R559/R568). Storing it would duplicate the quest structure and could drift; deriving it is exact.

CANON-vs-INVENTED stays CONSUMER-SIDE (owner decision C): it is a real per-world-line property but genuinely NOT soundly derivable, and it is adaptation-fidelity metadata (vacuous for an original work) — the same class the gap itself defers as out-of-charter in its canon-manifest denominator. Charter = original-work authoring; adaptation fidelity is a consumer concern (the SCE precedent). Considered and set aside: `Branch.canonical: bool` (a per-branch, byte-stable native home) — declined as out-of-charter under decision C, recorded for revisit if the charter scope changes.

The §3b density projection is corrected before build: the gap's denominator (own segment = `road(B) \ union(parent roads)`) collapses to EMPTY on every confluence (a converging parent forward-inherits the merge suffix, so `road(C)` is a subset of the parents' union), which is a divide-by-zero on a legal store. Ratified replacement: denominator = the world's OWN DECLARED road segment (a new `CanonOrder` field + `own_road_segment` accessor over the private per-branch edge set), numerator road-consistent (facts with `branch==B` whose `canon_from` is in that own segment), `density: Option<f64>` = None for an empty own segment (a facts-only / undeclared-road divergence that rides the trunk — a signal, never 0 or infinity), main as the baseline.

AFFIRMED: no `set-fact-provenance` (or any per-field fact setter) — facts have no per-field setters; add/import/amend all route the single `build_candidate_fact` (R305 parity), and a setter would be a second write path bypassing it.
verification_bullets: The density divide-by-zero was PROVEN, not assumed: computed the gap's `road(B) \ parent-roads` against the real R614 fixture `road_axis_override_walk_bounds_each_world_line` — the confluences `weave1` and `weave2` both yield an EMPTY own segment (their entire road is inherited from parents), so `owned/0.0` = NaN/inf, a serialize-or-lie failure on a valid store (the R613 failure mode: the gate that exists to catch silent wrong answers producing one).

STRUCTURAL derivation verified against the real consumer store (the-tide-that-counts, 827 facts): the derived predicate reproduces all 80 id-regex plumbing facts EXACTLY — 0 missed, 0 false-positive; and of 43 `Expected` setups, the 22 give-setups classify structural while the 21 genuine Chekhov setups do not. So deriving structural is exact, no schema needed.

CANON-vs-INVENTED non-derivability verified on the same store: `branch != main` = 639 facts but the consumer's invented set = 96 (braid + ending); the 543 `weave-*` facts are `converges_from` confluences = CANONICAL re-convergent threads, so a branch-based derivation would mislabel 66% of the store. Round 617 — branch-owned density built:.decision_summary: Builds the corrected §3b density from R616's ratified design. The denominator is the world's own declared road segment (a new CanonOrder field + own_road_segment accessor), NOT the gap's road(B) minus the union of parent roads, which collapses every confluence to empty (a converging parent forward-inherits the merge suffix) and divides by zero on a legal store. The numerator is scoped to that same own segment, so a fact at the shared fork coordinate is counted in owned_facts but never inflates the density (the R613 fact/road dual-axis trap). The numbers are honest per world but are deliberately NOT claimed to match the consumer's external coverage.py divisor (that tool was not shared).

Round 619 — cost-no-object review of R61.decision_summary: An owner-requested cost-no-object review (three independent adversarial reviewers — SSOT/structure, north-star/cost, correctness/silent-fail — plus self-audit) held R617-R618 to the lifetime-portfolio bar where a smell or silent-fail is a defect. It found real defects a solo self-review had passed clean. Sharpest: the R617 density metric measured the WRONG question — its own-declared-segment denominator hid the very 'looks full by inheritance' dilution the gap was filed to surface (on the real store the divergent endings read nearly as dense as the trunk, and a fact-rich facts-only world read a confusing None), and it carried a correctness bug (a branch declaring an edge into its inherited attach coordinate counted that coordinate as own, a silent 2x error on a legal store). Both are fixed by dividing owned facts by the FULL traversed road instead, which also let the entire own_road machinery be deleted (net -304 lines). Second: structural_fact_ids duplicated quest_graph's giving-setup rule and had ALREADY diverged (flat vs kind:quest-gated) — fixed by extracting one shared kernel quest_giving_setups both call. Also: the structural coverage is now exposed as a flat fact-id set (not only a per-scene count) so the consumer can join it per-fact and retire its heuristic; the R618 structural test was vacuous on the Expected guard and is rewritten to lock all three guards; the MCP tool description is updated. Verified end-to-end on the real store: divergent forks now read low (0.12-0.47) against main 2.94, structural_facts = 80 matching the consumer's plumbing set. R617's committed entry stays as the audit trail of what was first built; this records the correction.
changes_bullets: Density denominator corrected: `owned_facts / |full road traversed|` (`linearize(B).len()`) replaces R617's own-declared-segment. The own-segment version measured the WRONG question — it divided by the handful of scenes a world declared, hiding the long inherited span that IS the "looks full by inheritance" dilution the gap wanted flagged (a divergent world read nearly as dense as the trunk; a fact-rich facts-only world read a confusing "rides the trunk" None). The full traversed road surfaces dilution (a world riding a long road owning little reads LOW) and is bug-free.

REMOVED the own_road machinery entirely (field + own_road_of + own_road_segment accessor + its test): besides measuring the wrong signal it had a correctness bug — a branch declaring an edge INTO its inherited attach coordinate (the shape R615's own error message invites) counted that inherited coordinate as own, a silent 2x error on a legal store. The full-road denominator needs none of it. BranchDensity is now {owned_facts, road_scenes, density: Option<f64>} (None only for a store with no order).

SSOT: extracted `quest_giving_setups` as the SINGLE home of "a quest's giving setup is an Expected fact its own completed_by fact pays off (gated on kind:quest)". `quest_graph` (per-quest index) and `structural_fact_ids` (union) both read it, so they can no longer disagree — the R618 duplication had ALREADY diverged (structural was flat, quest_graph gated on kind:quest), a real "one semantic, two resolvers, divergent answers" defect.

`structural_facts` (the flat structural fact-id set) now rides the frontier report beside the per-scene `scene_coverage.structural` count, so a consumer can JOIN it to each fact's branch and actually RETIRE its external id-prefix heuristic (a per-scene aggregate alone could not be joined per-fact). Round 620 — discoverability defects: the.decision_summary: The first playable consumer (the-tide-that-counts: 852-fact store, running branching VN) filed a field report concluding Mnemosyne lacked world-state, player projection, carrier semantics, open predicates, and a map — and was wrong 7/7, rebuilding ~1,100 lines of Python outside the store. Reviewed adversarially: the count is 9, not 7 (the report also missed QUEST_PRED_REQUIRES = the declarative prerequisite, and its own claim that no round ever discussed fact-to-fact derivation is refuted by R493, which PoC-tested a causes edge and REFUTED it on data). The report's thesis is therefore CONFIRMED and its evidence is the proof: this is a DISCOVERABILITY failure, not a capability gap. Measured causes, all Mnemosyne-side and all mechanical: (1) the CLI bare-invocation usage string was a second hand-maintained command list that had drifted to omit every narrative verb (validate-continuity, describe-schema, report-playable-world, report-quest-graph, report-typing-candidates) while still naming 52, so it read exhaustive; (2) the auto-loaded MCP onboarding resources affirmatively taught that the store has 4 closed-form entity types, citing a Round 60 that is off-main, a claim already stale by R273; (3) CLAUDE.md's own citation-hygiene protocol told agents to prefix-match round-NNN-- against list_sections, which returns spec sections only, so it answers does-not-exist for all 366 rounds; (4) README framed the narrative half as deferred future work and speculated primitives that were never built. The consumer was not careless: the documented onboarding path told them the substrate did not exist. DECISION: fix the front door, and kill the drift class rather than refresh its instances — no restated counts, point at describe-schema. R585 built describe-schema because THIS consumer reported THIS gap; it still did not reach them, so the fix is routing, not another artifact.

Round 621 — R620 self-review: 5 ledger c.decision_summary: Owner-requested cost-no-object review of R620 (three independent adversarial reviewers: correctness / SSOT-structure / charter). R620's thesis and its structural move (delete the second command list) survive; its ledger does not. FIVE corrections, append-only (R620 is pushed and frozen). The sharpest is self-inflicted: R620's own synthesis says the store's three rule classes are all INVARIANT-shaped and that no GUARD-shaped primitive exists — and then R620 cited R493, whose every decomposition target is a violation-detector, as refuting the field report's request for a guard. The synthesis refutes the refutation. R493 answered causes-as-gate; the report's 3b asked derives_from-as-guard; they are different questions and the consumer's explicit hedge was right. Second: R620 claimed R527 gap #2 was never refuted and never built while the SAME entry credits the requires predicate as the consumer's missed capability — R559 refuted gap #2 and R568 built it; the true residue is only the STATE-EXPRESSION guard (trust >= 3), which no round owns. Third: the round about unverified hand-maintained counts asserted an unverified hand-maintained count (53, not 52) into a permanent ledger, and the deleted list also named a verb that dispatches to nothing, proving the drift was BIDIRECTIONAL and a one-directional gate insufficient. Fourth: R560 never knowingly reverted R547 — it cites R547 approvingly and calls itself a correction of its own looser restatements; the R546-plus-R560-versus-R547 reading is this author's reconstruction, not any round's finding. Fifth: the round's most valuable output (3a/3b/3c are ONE missing guard direction; the store already has a condition evaluator in the Interval rule class, pointed the wrong way) lived only in gitignored scratch while CLAUDE.md names changelog_entries the SSOT — it is now here. STANDING LESSON reaffirmed at cost: solo self-review missed all five, exactly as at R619 (7 findings). Independent adversarial review is not optional at this bar. The structural debt R620 left (a test gating two hand-maintained lists instead of one derived table, plus the doc surfaces it never swept) is carried to R622-R624, named not silent.

Round 623 — the doc gate: a documented v.decision_summary: The generalization R620 named and did not build, and R622 carried: a gate for the docs. R620 and R622 fixed real doc defects — a config key dead since Round 400 shipping in five copy-paste blocks ~220 rounds later, both READMEs' quickstart failing to parse, a CI example invoking a verb deleted with GENERATED.md, a _vN-banned identifier living inside two docs — and every one of them was found by a person reading. That is the same posture that let them rot in the first place, so the round is not done until the question is decided by a machine. Two questions about tracked docs are decidable and are now gated: a verb a reader is told to run must dispatch, and a mnemosyne.toml a reader is told to paste must parse through the real loader. The verb oracle is --help, which R622 made a projection of the COMMANDS table, so the gate cannot drift from dispatch. IT IMMEDIATELY EARNED ITSELF: both READMEs documented a CLI commit verb recording design-doc transactions to RocksDB column families — it has never dispatched, and mnemosyne-store is not even a CLI dependency. Three independent adversarial reviewers and two rounds of hand-sweeping missed it; the gate named it in one run. Getting it precise mattered more than getting it built: the first parser read cargo's own --force as a verb, the second cut --help to help, the third mis-paired fence backticks with prose, and the fourth silently MISSED the English commit mention because the inline span wrapped a line while catching the Korean one — an under-detecting verification path, the exact failure this arc condemns. A gate that cries wolf gets ignored and a gate that under-detects is worse than none, so both floors are counted and the non-vacuity is proven by injection.

Round 624 — a config section that exists.decision_summary: The last gateable question in the R620-R624 discoverability arc: a config section that exists must be NAMED by the guides. R623 gated what a doc tells you to RUN; this gates what it tells you the software HAS. The oracle is derived, not restated — WorkspaceConfig's every field is serde(default) with no skip_serializing_if, so serializing a minimal parse yields all 13 section names at runtime, and a hand-written list would have been exactly one more copy of the thing this arc exists to delete. It earned itself immediately: the MCP guide an agent auto-loads named 4 of 13 sections and omitted [continuity] — the narrative gate's own config — which is a mechanical restatement of the consumer's error #7 (they believed validate-workspace was their narrative gate, never learned validate-continuity was configurable, saw green, and shipped an unchecked world). docs/SCHEMA_GUIDE.md, the full field-level reference, documented [[publishable_override_ledger]] zero times. Both fixed, from the type and from the repo's own working entries rather than from memory. Precision was again the hard part and again caught before landing: the first check would have falsely flagged [plugins] (documented as its subtable) and the two Vec sections (written [[name]]), and a gate that cries wolf gets ignored as surely as one that under-detects. HONEST RESIDUE: the bootstrap skill an adopter meets FIRST lives outside this repo and no gate here can see it, while still teaching GENERATED.md and emitting an unparseable config; and two resources remain oriented to the spec half only, which is a judgment call no gate decides.

Adding a 4th `RuleClass` variant and satisfying only what the compiler demanded left the workspace compiling clean, 293 tests green, and the contract SILENTLY OMITTING the new class. The authority against drift was drifting.

THREE COMMENTS ASSERTED A SAFETY THAT DID NOT EXIST — and one sat on the enum's own definition. "an added class fails to compile HERE, so a new rule can never go undescribed" (schema.rs), "an added DisclosureMode variant fails to compile HERE (and in the variant array below)" (the most explicit lie — it names the array), and RuleClass's own doc: "an added class breaks its exhaustive match (the single-source drift guard) instead of silently going undescribed". Half of each was true and it was the wrong half: the match forces a DESCRIPTION; nothing forced the ENUMERATION. All three deleted and replaced with what is actually enforced (R611's rule: never state an unproven assumption as fact in a comment).

THE FIX IS DERIVATION, NOT A NEW DEPENDENCY — and my own design was REFUTED before build by an independent reviewer. I proposed adding `strum` on the premise that "pure Rust cannot force enum enumeration without a macro". FALSE: serde's derive ALREADY writes every variant's published tag and hands the list over through the `Deserializer::deserialize_enum(name, variants, visitor)` TRAIT SIGNATURE — an API contract, not an error-message format. strum would have been a SECOND derive macro regenerating what the first already generates, on these exact types.

STRUM WOULD ALSO HAVE PICKED THE WRONG SPELLING, which is the sharper half: the contract publishes SERDE tags (`withhold`), strum yields Rust variants (`Withhold`), so the bridge (`as_str()`, whose doc CLAIMS "matches the serde representation") stays hand-written and unenforced. serde capture returns the published string BY CONSTRUCTION, closing the enumeration axis and the spelling axis in one move.

ALL FOUR PRODUCERS now derive through one oracle (`serde_variants` + `variant_from_tag`), not the two I first scoped: `disclosure_mode_values`, `payoff_expectation_values`, `predicate_object_kind_values`, `rule_class_specs`. The exhaustive `match` in each caller is KEPT — it forces a gloss per variant, which was always the true half of those comments. Round-tripping the tag back through serde means no hand-written tag-to-variant table replaces the hand-written array.

THE TEST WAS A SECOND MIRROR and is now a real pin. It hardcoded all four lists, so both sides agreed at the stale value and adding a variant left the contract short AND the test green. Membership assertions are now tautological (the producer derives), so they are DELETED rather than re-pinned in the test — moving a hand-list from production into a test is not a fix. What is pinned instead is NOT tautological: vocabularies are non-empty (vacuity), every published class round-trips through serde, and every enum's `as_str()` AGREES with the serde tag the contract publishes — a live production mirror (receipts, CLI/MCP json) whose doc claims parity that nothing enforced until now.

SEVEN VARIANTS THE AUTHORITY NEVER PUBLISHED now have vocabularies: `IntervalOp` (ge/le/eq/gt/lt) and `ExclusiveKey` (subject/object) existed ONLY as hand-typed strings inside a prose blob (`"op": "ge"|"le"|…`). An author reading the contract could not enumerate them. Both derive through the same oracle.
verification_bullets: THE FIX IS PROVEN AGAINST THE EXACT INJECTION THAT BEAT THE OLD CODE. Before: add `RuleClass::Probe`, satisfy the matches, leave the array → contract omits it, 293 tests green. After: add the variant, the compiler still forces the gloss, and the contract carries it with ZERO hand-edits to any list — `['exclusive','transition','interval','probe']` — BECAUSE THERE IS NO ARRAY TO FORGET. THE ORACLE CARRIES A VACUITY GUARD, because the failure mode it prevents is its own: a capturer that silently returned `[]` would make every vocabulary read as "no values" and every downstream check pass vacuously (the R510 F5 class). It asserts non-empty and fails loud.

Round 630 — remove_section refuses to st.decision_summary: R630 closes DEBT-A+B: `remove_section` gets the referential guard it never had, and DEBT-B's "safe by absence" becomes a tripwire instead of an invisible constraint. THE DEFECT, proven e2e on the real 852-fact consumer store before the fix: remove_section was `sections.remove()` plus a reason check, so it silently orphaned every reference the WRITE path validates — a fact's canon_from/canon_to/evidence, a disclosure decision's first_at pin and surface scene, and a child section's parent_section — with validate-workspace still GREEN. That is R626's own sentence (the write path forbids what the delete path creates) one collection over, and it reaches the SPEC half via parent_section, the co-equal north star. THE FIX: `inbound_section_refs` walks the REAL collections (not a hand list — R629's lesson applied to a referential scan), one clause per field a `sections.contains_key` write-path site already guards; remove_section refuses to strand what the write path refuses to point at a missing section, naming each referrer. THE GUARD NAMES ITS HATCHES (R626's lesson): retract/amend the fact, remove-disclosure the decision, set-section-parent-section --none the child — the refusal message names all three so the remedy is followable, unlike R626's first cut. DEBT-B: entities/branches/frames/predicates are referenced too but have no remover, so those refs are safe by ABSENCE — invisible in the code, which is how it gets lost. A NEARLY-SHIPPED DEFECT: I first encoded that as a const whose comment claimed it "fails to compile until its author writes the scan" — it did no such thing, the exact false-safety-comment class R629 had just convicted; deleted and replaced with `every_remover_pairs_with_an_inbound_scan`, a source tripwire that fails the day a new remove_* identity primitive lands unacknowledged (detection not derivation, R622 — future functions cannot be derived). MY ENTIRE RULING WAS REFUTED — all three claims, by counterfactual experiment, and the reviewers' answer is better than mine. I claimed their `state` was FORCED (an untyped fact cannot take `withhold` or `first_at`, so state/hint/imply with no pin is the only legal way to attach a `surface`). The mechanism is real and precise — the write predicate `mode == Withhold || has_first_at` (`atomic/lib.rs:5210-5212`) is the IDENTICAL boolean to the leak gate's targeting `if !is_withhold && pin.is_none() { continue; }` (`disclosure.rs:214`), so the legal-for-untyped set IS the gate-skipped set — but the ATTRIBUTION is false: they use `withhold` ZERO times in all four plans (`default_mode` is absent, so withhold is already the default and an override is unnecessary — the arm never bound), and at the 5 TYPED player facts, where `first_at` was fully legal, they wrote bare `state` with no pin on all five. Where the invariant did not bind they wrote the identical shape. It was CHOSEN. And the counterfactual kills the causal claim outright: bypass the invariant, author an untyped `withhold`, run the gate — it still errors "un-gateable". Un-gateability is intrinsic to untypedness; the invariant only moves discovery from gate-time to write-time. It is a messenger, not a cause. I claimed the disease was typed coverage (9.7%); that collapsed by my own stated criterion. The leak gate's coverage of their `player` telling is EXACTLY ZERO (`targeted=0`) because targeting is `withhold || first_at` and the plan has neither — TYPING ALL 852 FACTS WOULD MOVE `targeted` FROM 0 TO 0. And `first_at` ("where the reader FIRST LEARNS it") is semantically inapplicable when player agency decides when a fact is learned, at any typing level. Their option (a), a fifth `dug` mode, is refuted for a reason I missed: `imply` ALREADY IS that mode ("realised via an object/environment — the Dark-Souls item-text"). Their option (c) is refuted on a false premise of mine: three of the five telling-consumers (`disclosure_coverage`, `playable_world`, `quest_graph`) take one store and no re-extraction — the MCP contract calls playable-world "Reading surface, never gated", render-free BY DESIGN — and they DID render it (`i18n.py:91-130` builds the game's text from `report-playable-world --telling player`). Their option (b), a telling-level access/agency flag, SURVIVES: mode (how plainly the telling commits) and access (must the audience ACT to get it?) are orthogonal axes that the reader-centric vocabulary conflates. THE FINDING THAT REFRAMES THE ROUND, measured and verified by me: `surface.scene == canon_from` for 1,099 of 1,099 overrides across all four plans, zero exceptions — the field is a BYTE-EXACT HAND-COPY of a value the store already holds, and only 11 carry an `object` (a real carrier). AND WE COMPELLED IT: `continuity.rs:3974` emits no locator without a surface, their engine reads locators exclusively, so dropping one surface makes a climax fact VANISH from the game (737→736 locators) while `report-disclosure-coverage` still calls it `disclosed`. The consumer had to hand-copy `canon_from` 1,099 times or the facts would not exist for their game. By R620's own lesson that is OURS, not their carelessness — and a hand-maintained copy always drifts: theirs drifted twice, 7 facts, found by a person reading. TWO LIVE DEFECTS OF OURS, found independently by both reviewers and reproduced by me: (1) a `withhold` override carrying a surface EMITS A LOCATOR with `mode: "withhold"` — verified, 7 locators for `f-original-sin` at `scene_ordinal: 17` — because there is no mode filter at the emission site; their engine DELETED its withhold filter (commit 17c1340, "Withheld facts emit no locator"), a premise true only because nobody has yet surfaced a withheld fact, so the story's core truth would print onto the game screen through the map seam, past the leak gate. (2) `continuity.rs:3915` documents `locators` as "in walk order"; they are ordered by `canon_from` while each `scene_ordinal` is the SURFACE's — an injected divergence produced an inversion (53→17). Both are latent exactly until someone uses `surface` for the carrier design it exists for. THE DESIGN, licensed by measured fault and NOT built this round: derive the locator scene from `canon_from` when no surface is authored, gated on `mode != withhold`. That collapses 1,099 hand-copies to the 11 real carriers, makes all 7 historical drifts UNREPRESENTABLE rather than detectable (R622's derivation-over-detection), restores `surface` to the sparse override its own doc describes, and closes defect (1) in the same move. REFUTED AS BUILDS, each measured: `surface.object ∈ fact.entities` fires on 4 of 11 and its hits are the MOST correct uses (`ent-bunok`, the store's own designed leaker) — it would forbid the Dark-Souls model the field exists for; `surface == canon_from` as a GATE forbids the design; scene-is-a-section and object-is-registered are already enforced at the write path; off-road-surface is vacuous on this store (all 7 roads span all 66 scenes). The one residual check worth keeping is a REPORT, not a reject: a surface strictly BEFORE its fact's `canon_from` places reader access outside the interval where the claim holds — 0 of 1,099 on the real store, 6 of 7 injected, and honest about the miss (detection there is partly directional luck). It must not gate: `continuity.rs:2903` keeps continuity green while authoring, and a surface is authored before its scene exists. Round 644 — from_tag serializes but woul.decision_summary: R644 pays the code leg of DEBT-PROSE: the from_tag/as_str pair on a manually-labelled enum is TWO hand-written mirrors of serde's own tag list, and only ONE of the two is compiler-forced. `as_str` is an exhaustive `match self`, so a new variant fails the build until its arm is added; `from_tag` is a `&str` match ending `_ => None`, so a new variant SERIALIZES through serde but silently fails to PARSE BACK — nothing forces the arm. That is precisely the class Round 629 convicted for `describe-schema`'s vocabularies, one step downstream: there the missing enumeration silently dropped a variant from the published contract; here the missing from_tag arm silently makes a round-trip lossy. Six enums carry the pair (`ConfirmerKind`, `ConfirmMethod`, `Verdict` in mnemosyne-atomic; `PredicateObjectKind`, `PayoffExpectation`, `DisclosureMode` in mnemosyne-core), all six `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` with both `Serialize` and `Deserialize`, so serde is ALREADY the two-way authority and the two match arms are the third and fourth mirrors of it. Measured first, per R493: all six pairs are SYMMETRIC today (every emitted tag parses back), so there is no live defect — this is a TRIPWIRE against a future variant, the R629/R634 shape, not a repair of a broken round-trip. The gap it closes is a real absence: Round 629 already pinned `as_str <-> serde` for THREE of the six (DisclosureMode, PayoffExpectation, PredicateObjectKind, via `as_str_matches_serde` in the describe-schema contract test), but only in the as_str direction and only for the three that reach `describe-schema`; the from_tag direction was pinned for NONE, and the three atomic enums (ConfirmerKind, ConfirmMethod, Verdict) were pinned in NEITHER direction because they are not part of the published schema contract. The fix is DERIVATION, not a second copy (R622): the new pin binds both directions of all six pairs to the ONE variant oracle Round 629 already built, `serde_variants::<T>()` — the serde-derived list captured through the `Deserializer::deserialize_enum(name, variants, visitor)` trait signature, promoted to `pub(crate)` so the pin reaches it instead of standing up a second oracle. For every published tag it asserts `from_tag(tag)` parses AND `as_str(that) == tag`, so a new variant added without its from_tag arm fails here, and a from_tag/as_str that disagrees with serde's spelling fails here — the vocabulary is never re-typed in the test, only round-tripped. Both directions proven load-bearing by injection: adding a `Verdict::Inconclusive` variant with its as_str arm (compiler-forced) but WITHOUT its from_tag arm fails "from_tag rejects the published serde tag `inconclusive`"; misspelling `PredicateObjectKind::Scalar`'s label to `"Scalar"` fails "as_str disagrees with the serde tag `scalar`". The pin is non-vacuous by the same oracle's own emptiness guard (an empty variant list would make it pass over nothing) plus an explicit `!tags.is_empty()` assert. What R644 removes is the SILENCE: the mirrors may stay, but they can no longer drift from serde or from each other without a red test.

Six enums carry the pair (`ConfirmerKind`, `ConfirmMethod`, `Verdict` in mnemosyne-atomic; `PredicateObjectKind`, `PayoffExpectation`, `DisclosureMode` in mnemosyne-core), all six `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` with both `Serialize` and `Deserialize`, so serde is ALREADY the two-way authority and the two match arms are the third and fourth mirrors of it. Measured first, per R493: all six pairs are SYMMETRIC today (every emitted tag parses back), so there is no live defect — this is a TRIPWIRE against a future variant, the R629/R634 shape, not a repair of a broken round-trip. The gap it closes is a real absence: Round 629 already pinned `as_str <-> serde` for THREE of the six (DisclosureMode, PayoffExpectation, PredicateObjectKind, via `as_str_matches_serde` in the describe-schema contract test), but only in the as_str direction and only for the three that reach `describe-schema`; the from_tag direction was pinned for NONE, and the three atomic enums (ConfirmerKind, ConfirmMethod, Verdict) were pinned in NEITHER direction because they are not part of the published schema contract. The fix is DERIVATION, not a second copy (R622): the new pin binds both directions of all six pairs to the ONE variant oracle Round 629 already built, `serde_variants::<T>()` — the serde-derived list captured through the `Deserializer::deserialize_enum(name, variants, visitor)` trait signature, promoted to `pub(crate)` so the pin reaches it instead of standing up a second oracle. For every published tag it asserts `from_tag(tag)` parses AND `as_str(that) == tag`, so a new variant added without its from_tag arm fails here, and a from_tag/as_str that disagrees with serde's spelling fails here — the vocabulary is never re-typed in the test, only round-tripped. Both directions proven load-bearing by injection: adding a `Verdict::Inconclusive` variant with its as_str arm (compiler-forced) but WITHOUT its from_tag arm fails "from_tag rejects the published serde tag `inconclusive`"; misspelling `PredicateObjectKind::Scalar`'s label to `"Scalar"` fails "as_str disagrees with the serde tag `scalar`". The pin is non-vacuous by the same oracle's own emptiness guard (an empty variant list would make it pass over nothing) plus an explicit `!tags.is_empty()` assert. This does NOT remove the hand mirrors — `from_tag` has 31 live call sites and `as_str` its own, so both are real API, not dead code; collapsing them onto `serde_plain`/`variant_from_tag` (the oracle already deserializes a tag to its variant) is a larger change with a caller migration and belongs to its own round. What R644 removes is the SILENCE: the mirrors may stay, but they can no longer drift from serde or from each other without a red test.

Round 645 — DEBT-C ruled: typing the rej.decision_summary: R645 rules DEBT-C at code 0, and the ruling is that DEBT-C's own scoping — Round 629's "type the reject path, then invariants() DERIVES like the other five vocabularies" — is CATEGORY-CONFUSED. Two independent adversarial reviewers refuted my candidate typed-enum design before any build, converging on the same measured verdict from different angles, and I re-ran every load-bearing number. THE PARTITION KILLS THE DERIVE PREMISE. describe-schema publishes 13 named invariants; the write path carries ~150 distinct reject messages through AtomicMutateError::Validation (measured: 141 direct Validation construction sites + 72 Result<_,String> helper rejects funnelled in at the primitive boundary via .map_err(Validation)). The mapping is many-to-one AND two-thirds unmapped: ~30-40 narrative-fact ref-integrity messages fold into the 13 (evidence-provenance alone renders 7 distinct messages; registered-entities 3; pays-off-exists 4), while ~110 messages have NO invariant home at all (the ~10 --reason audit gates, ~13 section field-caps + Round-298 gates + mandatory fields, 8 binding-file path-normalization rules, entry_id/inventory/confirmation/normative_excerpt conformance, and the manifest wrappers that are recursive pass-throughs of an inner error). So the two horns are: a 13-variant enum whose Display cannot reproduce 150 messages (each variant becomes a sub-discriminated field-bag) and leaves ~110 sites on a catch-all String — reintroducing the stringly-typed reject for two-thirds of the surface; or a ~150-variant enum whose serde_variants yields 150 implementation-detail tags that are NOT the 13 curated kebab names, ballooning the contract from 13 teaching guarantees to 150 path-normalization rules and destroying its purpose. Neither is the five-vocabulary shape. THE CATEGORY ERROR, which is the real finding: for disclosure_mode/payoff_expectation/predicate_object_kind/rule_class/quest-predicates, THE ENUM IS THE DOMAIN — a field of that type can hold nothing but a variant, so serde_variants::<T>() is authoritative by construction, the type's inhabitants ARE the value set. There is NO type whose inhabitants are the invariants; the set being enumerated is "the conditions the write path chooses to reject," which lives in imperative control flow (the if cond { return Err } statements), not in any data type. An InvariantViolation enum is a labelling scheme laid over that control flow by hand — its variants are names an author HOPES correspond 1:1 to reject sites, and no compiler law forces either (i) every return Err to carry a distinct variant, or (ii) a variant's prose to match the condition it is attached to. Proven: a reviewer injected a genuinely new write-time reject (a SENTINEL check in build_candidate_fact) — it compiled clean, describe-schema stayed at 13 invariants, and the whole suite stayed green; but under the typed design the same reject could reuse any existing variant and escape identically, because nothing ties a variant's meaning to the if it tests. Typing the reject path would RELOCATE R629's "second mirror the compiler claims to force but doesn't" one level up, at ~150-site cost, while looking MORE authoritative because it is typed. Round 629 fixed the EASY case where the type was the domain; DEBT-C tried to generalize it to a case where the analogy breaks. THE GAP IS REAL BUT NOT R493-LICENSED FOR A BUILD. The reviewer's injection is redundant with the current state: the store already enforces ~150 rejects while publishing 13, and ~110 reject classes are already unpublished with the repo green — that is not a regression to catch, it is the standing shape of a curated contract. invariants() has drifted ZERO times: two deliberate edits in its life (R587 birth, R627 fix), never an accidental omission. The harm is bounded — every unlisted reject is FAIL-LOUD with an actionable message (surprise, not the silent wrong-vocabulary corruption R629 fixed) — and NO production code branches on the reject KIND: ops/lib.rs:424 binds Validation(msg) and wraps it verbatim, atomic_cli.rs:88 maps Validation(_) to "validation" and displays, and a grep for any .contains()/== on a Validation message is empty. So typing has zero measured consumer, and the classification motive (make it derive like the five) is category-confused. Both motives fail. THE RULING: DEBT-C as scoped is REJECTED and RE-SCOPED toward closure, not build. invariants() being hand-maintained is CORRECT for its kind — a curated documentation contract, categorically unlike the five closed-enum vocabularies — and Round 629's "then derive the invariant list" was the mis-generalization. IF drift-catching is later wanted, the honest artifact is NOT a typed enum and NOT sold as derivation: it is a small fail-loud pin giving the ~13 reference-integrity invariants a canonical id and asserting each reaches a live enforcement path (the continuity gate already re-checks these same refs out-of-band per invariant_enforcement, so that mapping has a second home) — ~13 lines, inherently hand-maintained, honest about being a behavioural guard over a curated summary rather than a derivation from a type. That pin is itself unlicensed today (zero measured drift) and is recorded, not built. The R305 field-invariant-parity discipline (two write paths on one field must enforce the same invariant set) is untouched and remains the real structural guard on the reject path; DEBT-C was never about that.

Round 646 — C1 refuted: a requires-cycle.decision_summary: R646 rules R637's catalogue item C1 (a quest-prerequisite acyclicity check) at code 0: REFUTE-AND-CLOSE as a validate-continuity gate. An independent adversarial reviewer refuted my candidate BUILD ruling before any build — the eighth first-design refutation of this arc — and the refutation is stronger than my case, because it convicts R637's own framing, which I had inherited. THE CATEGORY ARGUMENT R637 USED IS WRONG FOR requires, and that is the load-bearing finding. R637 said "a cycle is a contradiction (never legitimate, not even mid-draft)" and placed C1 in validate-continuity by the same line that puts SuccessionCycle there. But that intuition is succession's, borrowed without re-deriving it from requires' semantics. A SUCCESSION cycle is truth-corruption: supersedes_in_frame means "the older fact no longer holds", so A supersedes B and B supersedes A makes both facts simultaneously superseded — they sit in the store live-and-latest while silently never holding anywhere (continuity.rs:1244). There is no coherent authoring waypoint where that is valid; it is a genuine contradiction, and continuity gates it. A REQUIRES cycle is well-defined unsatisfiability, verified in source: requires is surfaced ONLY as `prerequisites` metadata on the quest node (continuity.rs:4446), and it does NOT feed quest-state computation — per-world state derives from giving-fact payoff coverage (:4416), and unresolved_quests fires only when a quest has no giving setup at all (:4374). So a requires-cycle where each quest has a discharger produces a completely uncorrupted result: the quests get their normal states and the cycle sits as declared-but-unsatisfiable prerequisite metadata. That is exactly why R637's own injection measured validate-continuity violations 0 AND why my minimal 2-cycle reproduction (q-a requires q-b, q-b requires q-a) exits 0 — nothing is silently false, the store's meaning is simply "these quests are mutually blocked / never openable", which is unsatisfiability, the same genus as a dangling prerequisite that continuity DELIBERATELY tolerates ("a WIP story has dangling setups by definition", :2903). By continuity's OWN stated line — GATES CONTRADICTIONS and REPORTS INCOMPLETENESS — a requires-cycle falls on the REPORT side. R637 put it on the gate side by misclassifying it, and its ruling is internally contradictory: R637 says the play-readiness class (C2 obligation-with-no-discharger, C4 unsatisfiable-precondition) cannot be folded into validate-continuity without breaking the WIP-green contract, yet says C1 belongs in validate-continuity today — the ONLY distinguisher is "cycle = contradiction", and removing it relocates C1 next to C2/C4 in the unbuilt play-readiness class. A requires-cycle ("these quests can't open") is a strict sibling of C2 ("this quest can't be discharged"); gating one while parking the other outside is incoherent. R493 ALREADY RULED THIS EXACT CLASS, and it postdates the sibling precedent: "The only net-new piece (a causal cycle among non-succession facts) is unmeasured, YAGNI" — verbatim in the Round 493 entry. A requires-cycle is a causal cycle among non-succession facts; R493 governs it directly and defers it. The sibling-precedent ground fails too: canon-order and the branch forest are acyclic BY CONSTRUCTION (the mutate API literally cannot express the bad state — continuity.rs:145 "a cyclic declaration is no order"; forks immutable), which is impossible-states-unrepresentable at the type/construction level, not a runtime gate; requires is the opposite, a free-form author-drawn edge the API is designed to let you write (R637's own "the only one an author draws freely"). Making it unrepresentable needs a runtime gate that fires DURING authoring, colliding with the WIP-green contract. And a mid-draft requires-cycle is plausible in a way a mid-draft succession-cycle is not: an author wiring q-a requires q-b, then adding q-b requires q-a while restructuring a mutual dependency, produces a momentary loop = "neither opens yet" = incomplete wiring, not a contradiction. THE RULING: C1 as a validate-continuity acyclicity gate is REFUTED and CLOSED. It is not a contradiction (metadata-only, uncorrupted), it breaks WIP-green (fires during authoring), R493's measured-fault clause is unmet (zero cycles in the sole consumer's 852-fact store; their own knots.py already carries the check, so building it in Mnemosyne unblocks no one), and it fails even by R637's own contradiction-vs-incompleteness line. If anything is ever built it is a REPORT in the play-readiness class — surface a mutually-blocked prerequisite set as an unsatisfiability finding in report-quest-graph, alongside C2/C4 — designed as that named class when an author-claims-DONE gate is actually wanted, never a continuity reject and not as a one-off ahead of the class it belongs to (the scattershot "fix the next thing we tripped over" R633/R637 warned against). One correction to R637's catalogue, forward (R637 is frozen): its C1 row calls the requires-cycle "total silence — write path ACCEPTS, validate-continuity exit 0, report-quest-graph unresolved_quests=[]". The silence is not total: a cyclic quest with no discharger already surfaces in unresolved_quests, and even with dischargers the prerequisites metadata is present in report-quest-graph — what is absent is a NAMING of the cycle qua cycle, which is a report-shaped gap in the unbuilt play-readiness class, not a missing continuity gate.

Round 660 — the compiler forces readers.decision_summary: R660 answers the owner's question — "why can't it detect this?" — by building the detector, and the answer is structural, not sloppiness. THE CAUSE: Rust's exhaustiveness only fires on a `match` OVER the type. `TypedObject::from_exclusive_args` (narrative.rs:453) matches `(Option<String>, Option<String>)`, NOT `TypedObject` — it CONSTRUCTS the enum, so its input never changes when a variant is added and its 2x2 match stays exhaustive and green. The arity `2` is a HAND COPY of the variant count, and it is the exact shape R448 consolidated ("both surfaces had hand-rolled copies") without ever DERIVING. So the compiler forces every READER and zero WRITERS, and the write surface (CLI flag, MCP field, published JsonSchema) is where a leg's whole value lives. Tests could not catch it either, because NOTHING DECLARED the requirement: "a Fact variant must be constructible from the args" lived only in my head. THE FIX USES THE TOOL WE ALREADY OWN, pointed at the half we never covered: `serde_variants` (schema.rs:813) has derived the vocabulary for 6 enums since R624/R629 — ALL read-side. The new test asserts EVERY declared `PredicateObjectKind` is SATISFIABLE from the arg surface: the oracle side is serde-derived, the surface side is measured by actually calling the constructor, and their disagreement is the signal. MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED — the oracle CANNOT read `TypedObject`: `serde_variants` captures through `deserialize_enum`, which serde calls only for EXTERNALLY-tagged enums, and `TypedObject` is `#[serde(tag = "kind")]` (internally tagged) so it routes `deserialize_any` and the capture never fires ("this type is not one"). Every type the oracle feeds today is a plain unit enum for exactly that reason; I found this by running it, not by reading it, and the doc comment now records it so the next agent does not re-derive the failure. Pointing it at `PredicateObjectKind` catches the direction that was ACTUALLY unguarded: a bare `TypedObject::Fact` DOES break `build_typed_claim`'s (object, kind) match, but a bare `PredicateObjectKind::Fact` breaks NOTHING — and that is precisely R659's proof (`add-predicate --object-kind fact` ACCEPTED and PERSISTED while no fact could satisfy it, whole suite green). NON-VACUITY PROVEN BY INJECTION, reproducing reviewer B's half-wire end to end: both variants added, all compiler-forced sites wired (build_typed_claim, object_matches_kind, 3 continuity sites, as_str, from_tag) -> `cargo build --workspace` 0 ERRORS, 193 lib tests + every suite GREEN — and the new test FAILS with "object_kind `fact` is DECLARED but NO arg combination can build an object that satisfies it". Round 665 — the charter ruling refuted 3.decision_summary: R665 IS THE CHARTER RULING R663 DEMANDED, WRITTEN, SENT TO THREE INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWERS, AND REFUTED 3/3 — my third design killed before build in this arc (R625's ancestor, R659, this), and the third time I was confident. THE REFUTATION IS THE ROUND; the ruling is not repaired here because what killed it is worth more than what it claimed. THE DRAFT SAID: R663's question ("do closed-world assertions belong in the substrate, or does the sparse-frame ethos forbid them?") carries a false premise — the ethos is scoped to facts-in-a-frame, registries are already closed-world, invariant 4 routes rather than bans, and the hole is one missing primitive, DECLARED COMPLETENESS. Five of its six claims fell, from three lenses that never spoke to each other. CLAIM 1 IS REFUTED BY THE PROJECT'S OWN WORDS, in the SSOT: R442 generalised the ethos to the DISCOURSE axis BY NAME — `narrative.rs:498-500` "absence of marking is unrecorded, never an assertion that the fact is not a setup (the sparse-frame ethos applied to the discourse axis)", echoed at `narrative.rs:634-636` for disclosure, and R442's own ledger says "the sparse-frame ethos on the discourse axis". My narrow reading was of a sentence the project had already generalised in core, twice. R663 WAS DIRECTIONALLY RIGHT AND CITED THE WRONG SENTENCE — the ethos is real and broader than the sparse-frame line, and correcting the citation does not touch the finding. CLAIM 3 IS AN EQUIVOCATION AND MONOTONICITY KILLS IT: the closed-world assumption is NON-monotonic (an eighth knot must retract "exactly seven"); a registry is MONOTONIC (`add-entity` never invalidates a passing store), and the reject message itself says "add-frame first" — a set whose own violation tells you to extend it on demand is not closed. I also cherry-picked "[load-bearing]" as though it qualified all registries: `entities` is `load_bearing: false` (`schema.rs:556`), and entities is exactly the registry "exactly seven knots" and "every object has a name" run through. CLAIM 5 DIED THREE WAYS — I found it myself before the reviewers reported, and both of them found it independently: the `exclusive` arm (`continuity.rs:2565-2600`) fires only when TWO PRESENT FACTS co-hold, so "at most one" is MAX-cardinality, satisfied VACUOUSLY BY THE EMPTY SET, while every assertion the consumer needs is MIN-cardinality (exactly-seven, every-knot-has-a-mouth). R449 is precedent for the opposite half, and its own interval sibling is precedent AGAINST me: an absent operand returns `Unverifiable`, never `Violated`. MY OPERATIVE CLAUSE WOULD HAVE FORECLOSED WHAT ALREADY SHIPS: I ruled the declaration must live in "a DECLARED artifact naming registry ids, never as core schema" — but `CoverageExpectation` and `PayoffExpectation` are BOTH L0 core schema enums and inv4 holds for both. The charter's real test is MEDIUM-NEUTRALITY, not artifact-externality; my ruling would have banned the shape two of the three shipped instances use. CLAIM 4 SURVIVED, and it is the only survivor: all nine inv4 citations route or scope, none bans — `continuity.rs:655-658` "Rule semantics are game/world vocabulary and never enter L0 … the artifact arrives declared" is a destination. AND THE PREMISE UNDER ALL OF IT IS FACTUALLY FALSE, WHICH IS THE FINDING: "we record only PRESENCE" has been untrue since ROUND 269. `CoverageExpectation::Normative` (an L0 core enum) + no covering binding => `NormativeGap` => `ImplementationMissing` => `severity_coverage.unwrap_or(severity_binding)` => default REJECT. That is negation-as-failure, gated, default-reject, running for ~400 rounds; R589's `zero_fact_scenes` ("sections with no fact anchored") is the absent-REFERENCE class over the section registry, also shipped. The declared-expectation-plus-coverage family has shipped THREE TIMES and the code counts them itself (`disclosure.rs:36-40`: "the THIRD coverage instance after the spec axiom (R389/R390) and payoff (R442)"), and R663's own carry NAMED the primitive in a parenthetical I never cited ("a declared-completeness primitive: 'these are all of them, and the gate enforces it'"). THE FINDING MY DRAFT NEVER REACHED, and the reason this round is worth its commit: R442 ALREADY CONTEMPLATED THIS EXACT GATE AND PARKED IT AS A RECORDED REVISIT TRIGGER — verbatim, "Dangling is deliberately never gated — a WIP story has dangling setups by definition; the dangling list IS the author's todo list, and A RELEASE-TIME NO-DANGLING GATE STAYS CONSUMER-PULL", repeated by R449 ("release-time gates stay consumer-pull"). SO THE QUESTION WAS ANSWERED TWICE, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, ON THE TWO AXES: spec coverage GATES at default-reject (R269, "Active = backed by code"); narrative coverage REPORTS (R442, "a WIP story has dangling setups by definition"). Same shape, opposite enforcement, two published rationales that cannot both be the principle. THAT ASYMMETRY IS THE CHARTER CONFLICT, and my draft declared it nonexistent while walking past it. R663'S GAME IS THE RELEASE-TIME CONSUMER R442 NAMED, so the parking condition is FIRED — but note the trap before anyone rules on it: parking the NORTH STAR behind "consumer-pull" is itself the mis-framing this project has recorded as a recurring error (the game is the north star, not an external consumer we wait on). RECORDED, NOT RULED. AND THE MEASURED FINDING THAT RE-PRICES THE BOARD, a reviewer's and new: THE CONSUMER ALREADY BUILT R662's CANDIDATE RESOLUTION THEMSELVES — `map.json` as the source, a DERIVED `narrative-rules.json` naming only entity ids, gated by our substrate, their `map.json` law reading "노드는 잎만이다" because `exclusive(per:subject)` breaks with containers — AND IT HAS NEVER RUN ONCE: `rules_path` grep = 0 in their toml, no real `validate-continuity` call in their build, `.githooks/` = `commit-msg` only. THE CHARTER WAS NEVER THEIR BLOCKER. ONE TOML LINE WAS. And the route I called "paved twice" has ZERO live adopters including US: our own `mnemosyne.toml` has no `[continuity]` table and no hook or CI wires `validate-continuity` — a fact I ran and READ during R664 without seeing it. THE BOTTLENECK IS ADOPTION AND NON-VACUITY, NOT PERMISSION. Finally, the hand-list trap I nearly walked into: "exactly seven knots" is DERIVED from the store today by the consumer ("knots.py 가 스토어에서 도출한다"), so my declared-completeness artifact would have replaced a DERIVED ORACLE WITH A HAND-LIST — the anti-pattern this project already rules against and whose rot R663 measured on `cast-aliases.json`. Code 0.

THE DRAFT SAID: R663's question ("do closed-world assertions belong in the substrate, or does the sparse-frame ethos forbid them?") carries a false premise — the ethos is scoped to facts-in-a-frame, registries are already closed-world, invariant 4 routes rather than bans, and the hole is one missing primitive, DECLARED COMPLETENESS. My narrow reading was of a sentence the project had already generalised in core, twice. R663 WAS DIRECTIONALLY RIGHT AND CITED THE WRONG SENTENCE — the ethos is real and broader than the sparse-frame line, and correcting the citation does not touch the finding. CLAIM 3 IS AN EQUIVOCATION AND MONOTONICITY KILLS IT: the closed-world assumption is NON-monotonic (an eighth knot must retract "exactly seven"); a registry is MONOTONIC (`add-entity` never invalidates a passing store), and the reject message itself says "add-frame first" — a set whose own violation tells you to extend it on demand is not closed. I also cherry-picked "[load-bearing]" as though it qualified all registries: `entities` is `load_bearing: false` (`schema.rs:556`), and entities is exactly the registry "exactly seven knots" and "every object has a name" run through. CLAIM 5 DIED THREE WAYS — I found it myself before the reviewers reported, and both of them found it independently: the `exclusive` arm (`continuity.rs:2565-2600`) fires only when TWO PRESENT FACTS co-hold, so "at most one" is MAX-cardinality, satisfied VACUOUSLY BY THE EMPTY SET, while every assertion the consumer needs is MIN-cardinality (exactly-seven, every-knot-has-a-mouth). R449 is precedent for the opposite half, and its own interval sibling is precedent AGAINST me: an absent operand returns `Unverifiable`, never `Violated`. MY OPERATIVE CLAUSE WOULD HAVE FORECLOSED WHAT ALREADY SHIPS: I ruled the declaration must live in "a DECLARED artifact naming registry ids, never as core schema" — but `CoverageExpectation` and `PayoffExpectation` are BOTH L0 core schema enums and inv4 holds for both. CLAIM 4 SURVIVED, and it is the only survivor: all nine inv4 citations route or scope, none bans — `continuity.rs:655-658` "Rule semantics are game/world vocabulary and never enter L0 … the artifact arrives declared" is a destination. AND THE PREMISE UNDER ALL OF IT IS FACTUALLY FALSE, WHICH IS THE FINDING: "we record only PRESENCE" has been untrue since ROUND 269. `CoverageExpectation::Normative` (an L0 core enum) + no covering binding => `NormativeGap` => `ImplementationMissing` => `severity_coverage.unwrap_or(severity_binding)` => default REJECT. The declared-expectation-plus-coverage family has shipped THREE TIMES and the code counts them itself (`disclosure.rs:36-40`: "the THIRD coverage instance after the spec axiom (R389/R390) and payoff (R442)"), and R663's own carry NAMED the primitive in a parenthetical I never cited ("a declared-completeness primitive: 'these are all of them, and the gate enforces it'"). THE FINDING MY DRAFT NEVER REACHED, and the reason this round is worth its commit: R442 ALREADY CONTEMPLATED THIS EXACT GATE AND PARKED IT AS A RECORDED REVISIT TRIGGER — verbatim, "Dangling is deliberately never gated — a WIP story has dangling setups by definition; the dangling list IS the author's todo list, and A RELEASE-TIME NO-DANGLING GATE STAYS CONSUMER-PULL", repeated by R449 ("release-time gates stay consumer-pull"). SO THE QUESTION WAS ANSWERED TWICE, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, ON THE TWO AXES: spec coverage GATES at default-reject (R269, "Active = backed by code"); narrative coverage REPORTS (R442, "a WIP story has dangling setups by definition"). Same shape, opposite enforcement, two published rationales that cannot both be the principle. THAT ASYMMETRY IS THE CHARTER CONFLICT, and my draft declared it nonexistent while walking past it. R663'S GAME IS THE RELEASE-TIME CONSUMER R442 NAMED, so the parking condition is FIRED — but note the trap before anyone rules on it: parking the NORTH STAR behind "consumer-pull" is itself the mis-framing this project has recorded as a recurring error (the game is the north star, not an external consumer we wait on). I read TODAY's code and projected it onto a decision 136 rounds in the past. THE PHENOMENON I WAS EXPLAINING DOES NOT EXIST — AND THIS KILLS R665's REPAIRED QUESTION TOO, so two successive questions of mine carried false premises. Spec coverage DOES NOT REJECT IN THE FIELD: every live external workspace with content sets it to advisory (SCE 5 workspaces / 370 sections = explicit `severity_coverage = "warn"` 5/5; tc8-harness 181 sections = explicit `warn`; pinion 75 = inherits `severity_binding = "info"`), and the ONE store that inherits `reject` is ours, whose `report-coverage` reads "normative gap: 0, 100.0% (4/4)" — VACUOUS. Coverage rejects only where it has zero bite and warns everywhere it has content. R442's "report" IS the spec's field posture. There was no asymmetry to explain. AND I CHERRY-PICKED R269 — the entry I was proudest of catching: I quoted "Removed status tombstone-exempt; Superseded + Active + None all trigger" and OMITTED the sentence beside it — "Detection-only this round: severity bucketed under existing severity_binding (C1, YAGNI), Round 270+ carries severity_coverage split decision pending empirical evidence." R269 EXPLICITLY DECLINED TO DECIDE the thing I said it decided, and its own verification records the axiom vacuous at birth ("impl_missing=0 baseline confirmed"). I read that entry and reported the half that supported me. THE REAL DISCRIMINATOR IS THE PROJECT'S OWN, WRITTEN DOWN, AND IT IS THE RIVAL I HANDED THE REVIEWERS AS MY WEAK POINT #2 — `disclosure.rs:20-23`: the gates "operate on TWO stores (the authored plan + the re-extracted prose) — a render-acceptance family distinct from the single-store validate-workspace store-integrity gates". GATE WHERE AN EXTERNAL ORACLE EXISTS (the code cites §X; the re-extracted prose), REPORT WHERE THE QUESTION IS WHETHER THE AUTHOR FINISHED THEIR TODO. It classifies 4/4 shipped instances; my arity story classifies none. Disclosure kills arity outright: ONE declaration axis carries a gate (`disclosure_leak`, R502) AND two reports — same axis, same arity, opposite enforcement. And the defaults run my story backwards: spec expectation defaults to Normative (obligation PRESUMED), narrative to Unmarked (obligation OPT-IN), so a declared `Expected` is an EXPLICIT AUTHORED DEBT — more gateable than the spec's default, not less. WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS THE OPERATIVE FINDING: THE NARRATIVE GATE IS BUILDABLE, NOT IMPOSSIBLE. Round 667 — the placement axis had no ow.decision_summary: R667 BUILT THE THING R663 SAID WAS MISSING — but only after my FIFTH design death, and the kill was that I REFUTED R663 BY SILENTLY CHANGING R663'S EXPERIMENT. My draft claimed road coverage already shipped as R596's `unordered_scenes` and the build would be a duplicate. It does not. R596 filters `n > 0` (FACT-BEARING; its question is renderability, so an empty unplaced scene is deliberately out), and `zero_fact_scenes` filters on content with NO placement predicate at all — so an EMPTY unplaced section was computed NOWHERE and sat in `zero_fact_scenes` indistinguishable from a PLACED empty. R663 injected a BARE `add-section`; I injected one WITH A FACT, got `unordered scenes (1)`, and declared the prior round wrong. On R663's own store with R663's own injection the frontier answers `unordered_scenes = []`. THE REFUTATION WAS IN MY OWN FIRST MEASUREMENT — I ran the bare case, read `unordered scenes: none` beside `zero-fact scenes (1): sc-orphan`, and counted the zero-fact hit as "the capability exists". It is not: `zero_fact_scenes` has no placement axis (proven — `pro-part1`/`pro-part2` are order nodes and sit in the same bucket). THE BUILD: `AuthoringFrontierReport.unplaced_scenes` = `section ∈ registry ∧ ∉ order.nodes()`, content-independent, the placement axis that had no owner; `unordered_scenes` is now DERIVED from it (one resolver); NOT in `total_gaps` (`zero_fact` ⊎ `unordered` partition on `fact_count` and their union covers it — adding it would double-count). Plus `ContinuityReport.sections`, so `validate-continuity` prints `order_nodes=66/67 sections` instead of the lone number that misled R663, with a notice pointing at `unplaced scenes`. REPORT, NOT GATE, and NOT on R442's consumer-pull parking (which R666 buried and my draft reinstated): `FactCanonOffBranch` tolerates the orderless/forward-declared mode over the SAME predicate — a fact sitting AT an unpositioned coordinate is deliberately not flagged, so rejecting the store FOR that section being unplaced would be incoherent. The opposite direction rejecting (`check_store_boundary`) is not a counter: the code says why at its own site — a dangling reference makes the store UNEVALUABLE (`Err`, not a violation), while an unplaced section is INCOMPLETE and nothing breaks. TWO REVIEWERS, TWO KILLS, BOTH MINE TO OWN. Cut 1's notice counted 3 and pointed at a report showing 1 ("its counts are narrower" — false, 3 > 1); I generalised its wording from `belvoir-loop`, whose `zero_fact_scenes = []` makes the split look exact BY CONFOUND. Cut 2 fired on MNEMOSYNE'S OWN SPEC STORE — "5 sit on no declared road", 100% of sections, under a gate the line above declares DISABLED, for a store with no scenes; SCE's ~370 spec sections are the same shape. Both siblings are self-limiting (R614 needs a registered branch, R491 a declared interval rule); mine had no guard. I measured four FINISHED NARRATIVE stores and never ran the probe against the SPEC half of the co-equal north star — the same measurement blind spot twice, relocated from the notice's pointer to its audience. NAME: `off_road_scenes` was wrong and a reviewer caught it — this reads `order.nodes()`, the PRECEDENCE union, and reading a road off that node set IS the R611 defect; worse, `WorldManuscript.sections_off_road` (R456/R615) already owns "off road" for the PER-WORLD axis (`linearize`), so the two would have collided head-on. `unplaced` matches the code's own word (`positioned`). AND R663's LABEL WAS LOOSE: sections are "the medium's DISCOURSE order" (`describe-schema`), while the game's GEOGRAPHY is DEBT-J's weighted spatial map over entity-places, which R662 measured absent ("`MapLocator` IS NOT A SPATIAL MAP AND ITS NAME MISLEADS"). Round 673.decision_summary: R673 removes the file-based map gate of R670-672 and records the ruling that supersedes it. A cost-no-object review (four independent adversarial reviewers + consumer e2e, per the owner's standing preference) found the map gate built on the wrong foundation: a separate map.json file the store cannot reconstruct, holding adjacency the substrate already models as entity-to-entity typed facts, and porting only the gates while leaving build-map.py's derivation (edges to transition rules) unported — so a consumer would still have to run the Python. The owner ruled: everything the map holds (adjacency, entrance, containers) must be STORE FACTS, no Python, no derived file, enforced as store invariants. This round removes the [map] config, the map module, validate-map, containers, and the docs; the gate LOGIC was correct and field-verified, but the file model violates the SSOT north star. R669's entity_kinds registry stays (correct, independent), but the same review found three real defects in it to fix in this arc, not defer again: the AI-first MCP surface cannot register a kind (a north-star regression), validate-workspace does not enforce entity-kind integrity so a half-migration passes, and quest_graph still hardcodes the kind literal. Feasibility measured before removing: adjacency is the identical shape to the store's existing requires/pursues/pred-at facts and needs no new substrate. The R670-672 ledger entries are left standing (frozen, append-only); this supersedes them in prose. The store-native rebuild follows, each round measured against the real store.
changes_bullets: REMOVES the file-based map gate of R670/R671/R672 — the whole `[map]` config section, the `mnemosyne-validate::map` module (MapFile wire + check_map_g1/g2/g4), the `validate-map` CLI verb, `[map].containers`, and both schema-guide `[map]` blocks. This is not a revert-in-shame: the gate LOGIC (G1 node→entity, G2 store-place⊆map, G4 connectivity) was correct and field-verified against the real corpus. What was wrong is the FOUNDATION — a separate `map.json` file the store cannot reconstruct.

THE OWNER'S RULING (2026-07-18, after a cost-no-object review): "전부 스토어안에 있어야돼. py 만들지마. 룰로 박아."
