Round 676.decision_summary: R676 removes the kind:quest entity marker entirely — the third R669-arc defect (C). A quest is now DERIVED from its role in the reserved quest relation (the object of pursues, either endpoint of requires, or the subject of completed_by); an entity used in BOTH a quest role and an actor role (subject of pursues / object of completed_by) is a fail-loud reversed-slot error. The path was honest and adversarial: the RESUME prescription (quest kind from config) was obsolete since R673 removed config side files, so the first design derived quests from predicates and claimed the marker was redundant. Three independent reviewers refuted that convergently — the marker was NOT redundant (it silently disambiguated an actor mis-typed into a completed_by-subject slot, which the repo structural test relied on), removing it compile-broke schema.rs which publishes the marker as the describe-schema contract, and an infallible kernel reintroduced the R631 silent-drop. I first retreated to a one-line comment fix on cost grounds; the owner rejected that (cost-no-object). Measuring the fixture showed the disambiguation is recoverable and better: derive quests AND actors from opposite roles and fail loud on a dual-role entity. Verified on the real dnd store — derived quest set equals the old marker set exactly, 0 role conflicts, a full correct quest graph with no marker. The A/B/C arc closes.

changes_bullets: handle_result (atomic_cli.rs) error branch: was `print_error(&e, json); Err(anyhow!("{}", e))` — the detail printed here AND reprinted by the top-level anyhow handler in main. Now `print_error(&e, json); Err(AlreadyReported.into())`: print_error stays the SOLE formatter (json blob, or the FAILED header + detail).

New `pub struct AlreadyReported` marker error in atomic_cli — carries no message, impls Display/Error; its only role is to be recognised by `downcast_ref` so the top-level handler suppresses its generic reprint while the process still exits non-zero. The standard "already reported" CLI pattern: one owner of the mutate error print, not a fragile empty-string sentinel.

main error arm: prints `error: {:#}` only when `downcast_ref::<atomic_cli::AlreadyReported>()` is None. Every NON-mutate error path (arg parse, config lookup, store load) is unchanged and still prints through main.

The standard "already reported" CLI pattern: one owner of the mutate error print, not a fragile empty-string sentinel.

main error arm: prints `error: {:#}` only when `downcast_ref::<atomic_cli::AlreadyReported>()` is None. Every NON-mutate error path (arg parse, config lookup, store load) is unchanged and still prints through main.

Round 687.decision_summary: R687 pays DEBT-MCP-BATCH (registered R683): MCP had no transactional batch authoring, so an MCP-only agent had to author a scene as N non-atomic add_* calls and a mid-sequence failure left a partial store. New MCP tools import_facts + import_sections parse a manifest passed as a JSON string (keeping the atomic crate schemars-free — correct layering) and run the ONE atomic primitive the CLI import-facts / import-sections already use, so authoring is all-or-nothing. Parse+write proven end-to-end on a throwaway sidecar; the atomic primitives carry existing transactional-atomicity tests; router test extended. Round 4 of the owner sweep.
changes_bullets: New MCP tools import_facts + import_sections (mnemosyne-mcp) — the transactional batch authoring the surface lacked. import_facts parses a FactsManifest, import_sections a JSON array of SectionImport, then each runs the ONE atomic primitive (atomic::import_facts / import_sections) inside run_mutate, so an MCP-only agent authors a whole scene all-or-nothing; N separate add_* calls are non-atomic and a mid-sequence failure leaves a partial store.

The manifest is passed as a JSON STRING (ImportFactsArgs.manifest_json / ImportSectionsArgs.manifest_json), not a typed schemars field, so the atomic crate keeps its serde-only manifest types and takes NO schemars dependency (correct layering — schemars lives only in mnemosyne-mcp). The tool parses the same shape the CLI import-facts / import-sections read.

Parse failures map to AtomicMutateError::Validation with a shape hint; the atomic primitive owns every content invariant (per-row validation, divergent-rejects-whole-manifest atomicity) exactly as on the CLI.
R680 router test extended: import_facts + import_sections added to the routed-tools assertion.
verification_bullets: Workspace build clean; mnemosyne-mcp router test green with import_facts + import_sections now in the routed-tools assertion (a tool that compiles but is never exposed fails CI).

PARSE + WRITE path proven end-to-end on a throwaway sidecar: a FactsManifest JSON string ({"frames":[{"frame_id":"mcp-batch-proof-frame",...}]}) run through import-facts wrote the frame (receipt "1 frames created", 398 bytes) — the exact serde_json::from_str<FactsManifest> + atomic::import_facts path the MCP wrapper runs. Throwaway cleaned up.

The atomic primitives themselves carry extensive existing tests including transactional atomicity — import_facts_divergent_rejects_whole_manifest, import_sections_intra_manifest_divergent_rejected_no_save — so the all-or-nothing property the tool advertises is already gate-proven at the layer the wrapper delegates to.

PROPORTIONALITY (R680, this session's own precedent): a full stdio/JSON-RPC round-trip is deliberately not built — these are thin run_mutate wrappers over CLI-exercised atomic paths, run_mutate/finish_mutate are shared by every MCP mutate tool, and the genuinely new line (the JSON-string parse) is proven above. Router presence is the precedented surface check.

Round 688.decision_summary: R688 pays DEBT-DUP-REGISTRY (registered R683): fact registry-ref validation was two hand-maintained copies (the write path build_candidate_fact/build_typed_claim, and the out-of-band detector store_registry_violations). A shared fact_ref_resolves (the one place that knows how each facet resolves) and fact_registry_refs (the one enumeration) are now single-copy; the detector iterates them and the write path resolves through the same resolver. FactRefFacet::ALL plus three tests (an enumeration-completeness test and both parity tests asserting their cases cover ALL) bind the write path's hand-enumeration to the enumeration, so a new ref cannot land on one path and silently skip the other — the drift is caught structurally. An independent adversarial reviewer ran BEFORE commit and found the first cut OVERCLAIMED the drift-kill (write path did not consume the enumeration; the parity tests were hand-listed and the test comment was false) plus a LOW within-fact ordering shift; both fixed here, not downplayed. Round 5 of the owner sweep.
changes_bullets: New shared `fact_registry_refs(&NarrativeFact) -> Vec<(FactRefFacet, String)>` — the ONE enumeration of every registry ref a fact carries (frame, branch, entities, canon_from, canon_to, evidence, and the typed predicate/subject/object legs) — plus `fact_ref_resolves(store, facet, value)`, the ONE place that knows HOW each facet resolves (branch via is_known_world, canon/evidence against sections, predicate against the predicate registry). The resolver was "how each facet resolves" duplicated across the write path and the detector; it is now single-copy.

store_registry_violations (the out-of-band detector) rewritten to iterate fact_registry_refs + fact_ref_resolves, its byte-stable messages moved to store_registry_ref_message. The two non-resolution structural checks (evidence non-empty; a typed entity leg listed in entities) stay explicit.

The write path (build_candidate_fact + build_typed_claim's check_entity_leg) resolves frame / branch / entities / canon_from / canon_to / evidence / typed subject+object through the SAME fact_ref_resolves instead of raw contains_key / is_known_world. Author-guiding messages unchanged. The typed predicate keeps its inline `.get()` (needs the declaration for the object-shape check); fact_ref_resolves(TypedPredicate) is its parity-guarded twin.

FactRefFacet::ALL is the facet authority. Three tests bind the two paths to it structurally (not by discipline — the fix for the review's overclaim finding): fact_registry_refs_enumerates_every_facet asserts a fully-populated fact emits every facet; both parity tests (detector + write-path) assert their corruption cases cover exactly ALL. A variant added to the enum forces an exhaustive resolver arm + message arm (compile) AND a push in fact_registry_refs (enumeration test) AND a case in BOTH parity tests — so a ref cannot land on one path and silently skip the other.

changes_bullets: DEBT-FACT-REFS-CLONE: fact_registry_refs now returns Vec<(FactRefFacet, &str)> borrowing from the fact instead of Vec<(FactRefFacet, String)> cloning every ref value. The detector (store_registry_violations, the only consumer) passes each straight to fact_ref_resolves(&str) / store_registry_ref_message(&str), and the NarrativeFact outlives the enumeration — so N allocations per fact per validate-workspace scan are gone with no behavior change.

atomic_cli.rs: the `pub struct AlreadyReported` + its Display/Error impls are deleted; `handle_result` is inlined into `finalize_mutate` (the FINALIZE-MUTATE-WRAPPER ride-along), which now returns `Result<(), CliError>` and is the ONE site that prints a mutate error and returns `CliError::AlreadyReported`.

atomic_cli.rs: all ~53 pub `cmd_*` and their shared helpers now return `Result<(), CliError>`; their `bail!` sites became `return Err(anyhow!(..).into())`; two `bail!` stay idiomatic in the `parse_fact_verb_args` anyhow-value helper (which still returns `anyhow::Result`).

main.rs: `main` matches `CliError::AlreadyReported` (silent, exit non-zero) vs `CliError::Message(e)` (prints `error: {:#}`), with no `downcast_ref`; `run()` and the `COMMANDS.run` fn-pointer field now return `Result<(), CliError>`; the 36 non-atomic dispatch closures lift their anyhow error via `.map_err(CliError::from)` (atomic closures return `CliError` natively, so they are unchanged).
mutate_error_output_smoke.rs: the header comment is updated off the deleted `downcast_ref` mechanism; the test itself is unchanged (the asserted behavior is invariant across the rework).

Round 697.decision_summary: R697 BUILD (store-native map, arc step 2): the narrative-continuity transition rule reads the map's edges from STORE FACTS, not a file allowed pair list. NarrativeRuleSpec::Transition { allowed: Vec<[String;2]> } becomes { adjacency: String, undirected: bool }: adjacency names the predicate whose facts ARE the edges, and scan_continuity derives the allowed step set from the store (an adjacent(a,b) fact admits (a,b); when undirected, also (b,a)). The file allowed leg and build-map.py's derive() disappear — the 룰로 박아 core. MID-BUILD design fix (not in R696, which said blanket-symmetrize): measured across the real experiment rules, most transition rules are ONE-WAY state machines (alive→dead, operational→destroyed, machine→deviant — irreversible), so a blanket symmetrize would silently admit the reverse; directedness is preserved (undirected default false, an explicit declared symmetry), only the MAP declares undirected:true. Measured first, then an independent adversarial reviewer on the diff (verdict SAFE-TO-COMMIT). Overclaim caught + fixed not downplayed: directed reproduces the old ALLOWED SET exactly, but end-to-end store-native adjacency requires the fact subject to be a registered entity, so a directed SCALAR state machine must model its states as entities (the old file list did not) — free for the entity-place MAP, verified, recorded. Proven: 1000 workspace tests green, clippy clean, and a CLI e2e dogfood on the real tide store (20 adjacent facts imported; walk dyke-mouth→dike→village admitted 0 violations; non-adjacent village→mulmok caught; reverse village→dike rejected directed / admitted undirected). Round 700.decision_summary: R700 DESIGN (store-native map, arc step 4 — the baseline-guard + G1-kind answer): endpoint kinds become PREDICATE-DECLARED and WRITE-PATH-ENFORCED. The R696 design's G1 said an `adjacent` endpoint must resolve to a `kind:place` entity but never said HOW the check learns `place`, and invariant 4 (ARCHITECTURE sec 6; the EntityKind doc: there is no `Place` variant and there must never be one) forbids core hardcoding a kind — so G1 as written was under-specified and would violate it. Owner decision, cost-no-object: declare the required endpoint entity-kind ON THE PREDICATE (a registered `entity_kinds` ref, fail-loud, never free text — the R661 discipline) for BOTH the subject leg (new; the subject leg is unconstrained today) and the object leg (object_kind=Entity today says `some entity`, not `an entity of kind K`), and ENFORCE it at the WRITE PATH so a wrong-kind endpoint is rejected at write time — unrepresentable via the mutate API, not merely detectable by a gate that may not run. G1 then falls out by construction and moves from a read-side continuity check to a write-path predicate invariant, SUPERSEDING R696 sec 4 G1 and sec 7 (`G1 in continuity`); the G2 completeness/leak and G4 connectivity legs (graph properties over the whole fact set) correctly stay read-side. An independent adversarial reviewer (fresh subagent, not a fork) returned BUILD-WITH-FIXES; all 5 findings accepted, none downplayed: #1 HIGH — `set_predicate` (lib.rs:4865) is a THIRD write path (predicate re-type) whose guard checks object SHAPE only, so a tighten could bless a pre-existing off-kind fact (the R295 half-enforced bug), folded into THREE enforcement sites plus a field-invariant parity test (R305); #2 HIGH — `baseline-guard RESOLVED/moot` was an overclaim: the set_predicate and non-API-load paths carry no net, and the sec 4 deferral reason (`validate-workspace cannot know which predicate is the map`) EVAPORATES once the kind is on the predicate, since a predicate-agnostic baseline is now trivially cheap, refined to `write-path primary plus now-cheap baseline defense-in-depth, build or honestly defer`; #3 MED — `unrepresentable` scoped to `via the mutate API`; #4 MED — the subject check belongs in build_typed_claim beside check_entity_leg (:3999), not the shared context-free fact_ref_resolves (:4568); #5 MED — enum-enrichment pinned over a flat field, which would admit scalar plus a kind-constraint. Confirmed sound: invariant 4 preserved; build_typed_claim (:3972) is the sole fact builder (add_fact, import-facts, amend_fact, import_typing_proposals all route through it); adjacent and contains are TypedClaims; migration is serde-default backward-compatible; no added-then-removed carry. Owner decision, cost-no-object: declare the required endpoint entity-kind ON THE PREDICATE (a registered `entity_kinds` ref, fail-loud, never free text — the R661 discipline) for BOTH the subject leg (new; the subject leg is unconstrained today) and the object leg (object_kind=Entity today says `some entity`, not `an entity of kind K`), and ENFORCE it at the WRITE PATH so a wrong-kind endpoint is rejected at write time — unrepresentable via the mutate API, not merely detectable by a gate that may not run. Round 701.decision_summary: R701 BUILD (store-native map, arc step 4 — endpoint kinds predicate-declared + write-path enforced): implements the R700 design. `Predicate` gains two optional registered-`entity_kinds` refs — `subject_kind` (subject leg, new) and `object_entity_kind` (an entity-shaped object leg) — declaring the entity KIND each endpoint must be. The fact write path (`build_typed_claim`, the SOLE typed-fact builder that add_fact / import / amend / import_typing_proposals all route through) REJECTS a fact whose endpoint entity is not the declared kind, at write time — so `adjacent(place, object)` (a road to a non-place) is unrepresentable via the mutate API. This is the spatial-map G1 (DEBT-MAP-G1-KIND) enforced by construction, moved from a read-side continuity check (which would have violated invariant 4 by hardcoding `place`) to a write-path predicate invariant; the required kind is a consumer-declared registered ref, never hardcoded in core. THREE enforcement sites keep it from being half-enforced (the R295 trap): `build_typed_claim` (both legs); `set_predicate` re-type (a full-declaration offender check — object shape AND endpoint kinds — via a new `use_satisfies_declaration` twin, closing the R700-review-#1 gap where re-type guarded object shape only, so a tighten over an off-kind use could silently break the store); and `build_predicate`'s combo guard (`object_kind=scalar` + `object_entity_kind` rejects) plus `validate_predicate_kind_refs` (registered-ref, fail-loud) shared by add_predicate / set_predicate / manifest. DEVIATION from the design's enum-enrichment PIN, measured first (수치≠추론): `PredicateObjectKind` is `Copy`, matched 30+ sites, serialized as a bare tag in every predicate — enriching it drops `Copy`, churns all sites, and forces an on-disk migration; the flat-field + guard variant (which the R700 review #5 explicitly sanctioned) achieves the identical invariant with automatic backward-compat, so BUILD took it. schema_version 24 to 25 (additive-optional; a pre-v25 predicate loads as `None` = no constraint; the bump guards against a stale older binary silently dropping the fields on save and erasing the gate). CLI `--subject-kind` / `--object-entity-kind` on add/set-predicate, MCP args + descriptions, describe-schema manifest keys. An independent adversarial reviewer (fresh subagent, not a fork) returned COMMIT-WITH-FIXES; both findings folded, none downplayed: #1 MED the schema_version bump was missing (FIXED to 25 with the v24 to v25 comment; the reviewer supplied the concrete stale-binary silent-erase scenario), #2 LOW the MCP tool descriptions were stale (FIXED). Confirmed sound: no write-path bypass, add/set declaration-guard parity, invariant 4 preserved, write-path and retype-twin agree (non-vacuous parity test), backward-compat, empty-kind correctly rejects a Some constraint. Proven: full workspace tests green, clippy -D clean, 4 new unit tests + a COMMITTED CLI e2e smoke (`predicate_endpoint_kind_smoke.rs`, real binary). The map.json to store migration G1 gate-release is now MET. NEXT = R702. Design doc claudedocs/store-native-map-design.md sec 10-12.

Round 703.decision_summary: R703 BUILD (store-native map, arc step 6 — the G2 completeness/leak invariant): the read-side checks that the `adjacent` + `contains` fact set is a COMPLETE map with no leaked containers or off-map members. Three new `ContinuityViolation` variants in `scan_continuity`'s transition arm — `MapInventedPlace` (a place-kind entity that is neither a node nor a container: completeness), `MapContainerAsNode` (a `contains` subject that also appears in an `adjacent` fact: a container walked on as a position), `MapContainedOffMap` (a `contains` object that is not a node: a region holding an off-map place). The `Transition` rule gains a `containment: Option<String>` field (an in-place extension, no vN) so the SAME map's rule names BOTH its `adjacency` and its `containment` predicate — one declaration, both legs of the map. The place kind the completeness check enumerates is DERIVED from the adjacency predicate's Round 701 `subject_kind` OR `object_entity_kind` — core NEVER hardcodes the string place (ARCHITECTURE invariant 4); the check is INERT when the map declares no node kind, and reading EITHER leg closes the half-enforced hole an object-leg-only declaration would open (review #1, R295/R699 trap). Direction-agnostic (place structure, unlike G4's undirected-only connectivity): runs for directed and undirected rules alike. `nodes` is materialized in the SAME pass as `edges` (self-loops included: a self-loop place is on the map, flagged once as a self-loop, never ALSO as an invented place — the R699 one-model discipline, no divergence). Entrance (the `outside` designation) is DEFERRED to the migration round (design sec 5: captured at migration; R703 is a capability round, not the migration, and the bit has no read-side consumer — G4 is root-independent). An independent adversarial reviewer (fresh subagent, not a fork) returned COMMIT-WITH-FIXES with 5 findings, all folded or dispositioned, none downplayed: #1 the completeness check silently disarmed when only `object_entity_kind` was declared (FIXED — read either leg + a pinning test); #2 two maps sharing one place kind mass-flag each other (design sec-1 single-map scope; DEBT-MAP-G2-SINGLEMAP registered, same family as R696 review #6); #3 a kinded off-map contained place double-reports (both statements true, R698 cosmetic-minor precedent; commented); #4 a scalar-object `containment` mis-declaration over-flags (symmetric with `adjacency`, R697; commented); #5 the direction-agnostic claim was untested (FIXED — a directed-rule test). Round 705.decision_summary: R705 BUILD (object-shape closure, step 1 — the Token shape): adds a THIRD typed-object shape `TypedObject::Token{token}` beside `Entity{id}` and the free-text `Value{value}` (Value NOT removed — that is step 4). A predicate declares `object_kind=token` + a CLOSED vocabulary `object_tokens` (a BTreeSet on `Predicate`); the write path REJECTS a `Token` whose value is outside the declared set (the R436 typo guard one level down), so the machine slot becomes ENUMERABLE — the AI can ask "what values does this predicate take", closing the north-star self-consistency hole R661 named. Measured warrant (R704): 522 authored Token uses across the real corpus + the ~100 re-extraction leaks a closed vocab would catch (self-extraction stops being blind). ADDITIVE and lowest-risk (Value stays; the two-homes ambiguity and its removal are step 4). The R660 oracle (`every_declared_object_kind_is_satisfiable_from_the_arg_surface`) FORCED the wiring: adding `PredicateObjectKind::Token` failed that test until `from_exclusive_args` gained a `token` parameter, whose arity change then broke every CLI call site — the R625/R659 half-wired-green defense, and the design reviewer #2 precondition was thus already built (R660). THREE enforcement sites, no half-enforced invariant (R295/R701): `build_typed_claim` (the write path) + `use_satisfies_declaration` (the `set_predicate` re-type re-check, so a tighten dropping a used token rejects) share the membership check via a trim-symmetric compare; `build_predicate` (the ONE declaration interpreter, shared by add/set/manifest) requires a NON-EMPTY vocab under token (an empty set would re-open the free-text hole) and rejects tokens on a non-token kind. Wired end-to-end: CLI `--object-tokens` (comma-split) + `--typed-object-token`; MCP `object_tokens` arg + the `TypedObject` JsonSchema auto-exposes the variant (R692); describe-schema object_kind gloss + typed_object_wire prose. schema v25→v26 (additive-optional BTreeSet, serde default + skip-if-empty; a pre-R705 binary rejects a token store LOUDLY via serde unknown-variant, so there is no silent-drop risk — the bump is kept for audit consistency). An independent adversarial reviewer (fresh subagent, not a fork) traced EVERY write path and found NO half-wired bypass; verdict COMMIT-WITH-FIXES, all 4 folded: #1 MED the describe-schema predicates gloss omitted token (a self-contradiction with the same output listing it — fixed); #2 MED/LOW no schema bump / ledger note (fixed → v26 + the ledger note); #3 LOW stale docs (TypedObject "two-shaped", the from_exclusive_args MCP claim, the AmendFactArgs comment, the quest-shape "a scalar" prose — all fixed); #4 LOW/note CLI comma-expressiveness (acceptable — MCP takes a Vec so it is strictly more expressive, and the blank-member guard backstops the non-CLI paths). Proven: 1015 workspace tests green, clippy -D clean, fmt clean; 3 unit tests + a COMMITTED CLI e2e `token_vocabulary_smoke.rs`. NEXT = step 2 (Quantity + a units registry). Design doc claudedocs/object-shape-closure-design.md sec 2.

Round 706.decision_summary: R706 BUILD (object-shape closure, step 2 — the Quantity shape + a units registry): adds a FOURTH typed-object shape `TypedObject::Quantity { n: i64, unit: String }` beside `Entity{id}`, free-text `Value{value}`, and `Token{token}` (Value NOT removed — that is step 4). `n` is an EXACT integer (all measured live uses are integer counts; f64 is deliberately avoided — it reintroduces 10-vs-10.0 serialization and equality fuzz). `unit` is a REGISTERED ref into a NEW top-level `units` registry (`AtomicStore.units`, keyed by unit id), fail-loud — never free text (invariant 4, the R700 place-kind lesson one axis over: a game measures minute, a legal store day; core must not enumerate them, a bare unit string would drift min/minute/분). The registry is NEW substrate mirroring entity_kinds (R661): a `Unit` struct, an `add_unit` primitive, `add-unit` CLI + MCP, a `UnitImport` manifest kind staged before facts, and a `unit_registered` verdict. DECISION (design sub-fork): the unit lives on the OBJECT only (registry-checked per fact), NOT pinned per-predicate — so add_predicate/set_predicate stay at their current arity and no PredicateDecl bundle is forced this round. The unit check is wired through the R688 shared registry-ref system: a new `FactRefFacet::TypedUnit` (resolved against `units` via the one `fact_ref_resolves`), so the write path (`build_typed_claim`) and the out-of-band detector (`store_registry_violations`) enforce the SAME "is a registered unit" verdict from one enumeration — a half-enforced invariant is structurally impossible (the EnumIter completeness tests force the variant into fact_registry_refs + both parity lists). Unlike entity_kinds (an entity-level ref that needs its own detector), the unit is a FACT-level ref already covered by the facet, so NO standalone detector was added (the R705 precedent added no unregistered_tokens; an independent review caught and removed an early redundant `unregistered_units` that carried a false "the ONE detector both gates call" comment — the R636 overstatement correction). Round 707.decision_summary: R707 BUILD (object-shape closure, step 3 — the Fact object shape + delete-path referential integrity): adds the FIFTH typed-object shape `TypedObject::Fact { id }` beside Entity / Value / Token / Quantity (Value NOT removed — that is step 4). A `Fact` object references another fact of this store (the tide `opened_by = f-*` class, and the reification axis DEBT-J will ride). The CORRECTNESS-CRITICAL distinction from the earlier shapes (R659's proven finding, why two designs in this family died): a fact-ref has STAGING semantics, so unlike Token/Quantity it is NOT checked in phase-1 build_typed_claim and is NOT a phase-1 registry facet (FactRefFacet). Instead it is resolved in PHASE 2 (`validate_and_stamp_fact_refs`, against `visible` = store ∪ staged) beside conflicts_with / pays_off — so a legal SAME-MANIFEST FORWARD ref (fact A's object points at fact B declared later in one import) is accepted, which a phase-1 `store.contains_key` would wrongly reject. build_typed_claim's (Fact,Fact) arm does SHAPE + non-empty only. A shared `check_typed_fact_ref` holds the one verdict (existence in visible + self-reference ban); it is called from `validate_and_stamp_fact_refs` (covering add_fact / import_facts / amend_fact — the three build_candidate_fact paths) AND from `import_typing_proposals`, the FOURTH write path that fills a typed leg WITHOUT the rest of phase 2 — R659 named this exact gap, and leaving it unrouted would let a Fact-ref escape unguarded. The DELETE-path guard is the R625 killer (a write path forbidding what the delete path creates = the canonical half-enforced anti-pattern; R625 measured `opened_by` refs accepted at write but orphaned by retract): `inbound_fact_refs` now detects a fact referenced as another fact's `Fact` typed object, so `retract_fact` refuses-or-defers exactly as it already does for conflicts_with / supersedes_in_frame / pays_off — one detector, symmetric. The R660 oracle (`every_declared_object_kind_is_satisfiable_from_the_arg_surface`) FORCED the CLI wiring: adding `PredicateObjectKind::Fact` failed it until `from_exclusive_args` gained a `fact` parameter (`--typed-object-fact`), whose arity change broke every CLI call site; the build_typed_claim / object_matches_kind / conforms matches are wildcard-free, so the variant broke every one (the R625/R659 half-wired-green defense). schema v27→v28 (a Fact object is a fact-identity ref like conflicts_with, NOT a new top-level registry). Wired end-to-end: CLI `--typed-object-fact`; MCP `TypedObject` JsonSchema auto-exposes the variant (R692) + the add_predicate object_kind description; describe-schema object_kind gloss + typed_object_wire (5 variants). Fact has NO live migration executed here (R704: tide's 16 `opened_by` values are the eventual re-author target, deferred to the migration round; the shape lands first so the migration is executable — the R625 executability lesson). This closes the north-star self-consistency hole R661 named: the machine slot the substrate could not enumerate no longer exists, so self-extraction is never blind on the object leg. The owner chose the full removal NOW (accepting the live tide store bricks until its own-repo migration) over holding for the migration. Removal is the INVERSE of the additive R705-707 rounds — it must BREAK every exhaustive match, which is exactly the forcing function that enumerates every reader (build_typed_claim / object_matches_kind / the R660 conforms oracle / continuity's typed_object_key,display,scalar / quest-shape / derived_registries / describe-schema wire) so none is silently left half-migrated. `from_exclusive_args` drops its `value` param + the `--typed-object-value` CLI flag; the MCP `TypedObject` JsonSchema auto-drops the variant. THE LOAD-BEARING RISK is a store still carrying EITHER removed wire token — a `{kind:value}` OBJECT or a `object_kind:"scalar"` PREDICATE: the strict parse fails, and `load` turns that into a NAMED migration work-list (a lenient JSON fallback `removed_value_shape_error` → the `RemovedValueShape` error listing BOTH the offending value-object fact ids AND the scalar predicate ids) rather than a silent drop or a cryptic serde "unknown variant" (the R625 brick lesson — the migration is executable, so the store says exactly what to re-author). The independent reviewer caught that the first cut named only the objects (a scalar-predicate-only store still bricked with a raw serde error) — folded, with a negative control proving a DIFFERENT corruption propagates the original serde error, not a false RemovedValueShape. Round 709.decision_summary: R709 DESIGN (DEBT-J — reified edge-cost, code 0): the design round that decides HOW the map edge cost (walk minutes, living only in map.json today — the R696 carry) moves into the store. The object-shape arc gave cost its NUMBER shape (Quantity{n,unit}, R706); DEBT-J gives the number a HOME on the edge. MEASURED FIRST (R668 — read build-map.py's LOGIC, not just map.json): the cost is a SINGLE EXACT integer in MINUTES per edge (20 edges, unit=minute → Quantity{i64, minute} verbatim), SYMMETRIC (map.json stores one `walk` per undirected edge, so it cannot be directionally asymmetric by construction — this RESOLVES the object-shape design's flagged open question about the b→a direction: one cost per undirected R698 adjacent fact covers both ways), and FRAME-INVARIANT ground truth (the owner INVENTED the numbers — map.json `open`: "걷는 분을 내가 지어 넣었다" — so there is no section evidence, no per-frame/per-branch variation, and future revision is game-parameter re-tuning that git history covers). Its only consumer is a DERIVED read (minutes-within-a-tide = tide_budget − Σ movement-cost; build-map.py lines 34-40: stay-time is DERIVED from map+chain+tide-length, never authored). THE DESIGN FORK the measurement exposed, adjudicated by an independent adversarial reviewer (fresh subagent, DESIGN review before any code): (A) REIFICATION — a cost fact whose SUBJECT is the adjacent fact, requiring `TypedClaim.subject` be generalized from a bare String to a `TypedSubject{Entity|Fact}` enum (the arc's biggest substrate change, ~38 sites + a facet split + the R707 phase-2/delete-guard mirror on the subject leg); vs (B) SIDE-TABLE — a top-level `AtomicStore.edge_costs: BTreeMap<fact_id, Quantity>` registry keyed by the adjacent fact id, no subject-leg change. DECISION = (B), DECISIVELY. The cost has NONE of the four properties fact machinery serves (frame/branch/evidence/supersession), so (A) buys ZERO measured capability while (a) being the arc's largest change and (b) opening a NEW structural hole the reviewer named HIGH: `check_entity_leg` forces a subject to be a registered entity IN the fact's `entities` list ("the entities list is THE retrieval key"), and a `Fact{id}` subject fails both — exempting it (unlike the R707 OBJECT-Fact, tolerable because objects were never guaranteed entities) yields a fact with NO forced entity retrieval key, a hole needing yet MORE machinery atop the 38-site change. No clean third option exists (object-leg Fact can't carry both the edge-ref and the Quantity in one binary object slot; subject=endpoint-entity can't name both neighbor and cost; a `NarrativeFact.edge_cost` field pollutes the universal struct on every fact). A future PERSPECTIVAL cost (a character's mistaken belief about travel time) is a SEPARATE fact (subject=character, believes-cost predicate), NOT a reification — so nothing ever forces the edge's ground-truth cost to become a reified fact. (A) stays a NAMED, UN-BUILT capability (R661 licensing — build it only when a genuinely evidenced/perspectival edge attribute is measured). (B) mirrors the units/entity_kinds top-level `BTreeMap<String,_>` registries exactly, with Quantity{i64,unit} the R706 shape. The R709 review's decisive reason to pick this over reifying the subject leg (option A): the cost is FRAME-INVARIANT ground truth (owner-invented map minutes, no section evidence, no per-frame/branch variation), so it needs none of the fact machinery (frame/branch/evidence/supersession) that generalizing `TypedClaim.subject` to `TypedSubject{Entity|Fact}` would carry — and A opened a HIGH structural hole (a Fact-subject cannot be in the fact's `entities` list, the retrieval key). `add_edge_cost` primitive gates three ways fail-loud: the keyed fact must EXIST, `n` must be POSITIVE (build-map.py's G3 — 0/negative = a free teleport), and the unit must be REGISTERED (the R706 units registry, invariant 4); A2-consistent (absent→create / byte-identical→no-op / divergent→reject) via the shared stage_registry_entry. Out-of-band integrity: `edge_cost_violations` (a key whose fact is gone, or an entry whose unit is unregistered) folded into `store_registry_violations` — the boundary and baseline gate enforce the same set; the write path + cascade-drop cannot produce either, only an out-of-band edit can. Round 711 — map edge-cost adjacency sema.decision_summary: R711 BUILD (DEBT-J — the map edge-cost adjacency SEMANTIC, the R710 LOW-3 deferral): a validate-continuity check that an `edge_costs` side-table entry (R710, a map EDGE cost keyed by the adjacent fact id) is keyed by a fact that IS a map edge — a fact whose predicate is some transition rule's `adjacency` predicate. A cost keyed to a non-adjacency fact (a walk-cost on something that is not an edge) is flagged `EdgeCostNotAnEdge` and gates under `[continuity].severity`. This lives at the validate layer, NOT the store's `add_edge_cost` gate, for the same reason G1/G2 do: the store cannot know which predicate is the map's adjacency without the rules config (invariant 4 — core never hardcodes "place"/"adjacent"), so `add_edge_cost` only checks fact-exists + n>0 + unit-registered and ACCEPTS a cost on any existing fact. The two layers are proven end-to-end through the real binary: add-edge-cost on a non-edge SUCCEEDS, then validate-continuity — which holds the rules — catches it. The check keys off the transition rule's `adjacency` predicate (NOT its state `predicate`), is checked against the UNION of every transition rule's adjacency predicate so a second map's edge cost is not falsely flagged (unlike the per-rule MapInventedPlace / DEBT-MAP-G2-SINGLEMAP scope), and is INERT when no transition rule is configured. LAYERING: `scan_continuity` calls `check_store_boundary` FIRST, which runs the R710 `edge_cost_violations` (orphan fact / unregistered unit) and returns Err, so the R711 loop only ever sees present, unit-valid facts — the missing-fact branch is belt-and-suspenders. FOLDED from the independent adversarial review (COMMIT-WITH-FIXES, no correctness defect, both load-bearing claims independently confirmed): the MED remediation gap — the old hint pointed at remedies that do not clear the finding (attach to another fact) or are BLOCKED by referrers (retract_fact refuses a referenced fact), leaving a stray cost on a legitimate/referenced fact with NO exit — is closed by a new symmetric primitive `remove_edge_cost` (drops a cost off a kept/referenced fact without retracting it, and cleans an out-of-band orphan cost; fail-loud when there is nothing to drop; acknowledged in the R630 every-remover tripwire as a leaf that strands no ref), and the hint reworded to name `remove-edge-cost`. A LOW inert-notice finding is NAMED-deferred (a general "map data but no map rule" surface, not an edge-cost-only one). SEPARATELY, this round establishes that CANDIDATE 1 (the derived stay-time READ, the R710-named DEBT-J consumer, minutes-within-tide = tide_budget - Sum(cost)) is BLOCKED, not deferred by preference: build-map.py only DESCRIBES stay-time in prose (no implementation), and map.json `open`[0] reserves the tide length (tide_budget) as owner-undecided with the edge costs marked provisional ratios — so the read cannot be computed without inventing an owner-reserved number, which CORRECTS the R710/RESUME claim that "the stored n:i64 + G3 is sufficient" (that is the Sum(cost) half only). Independent adversarial reviewer verdict + folded findings recorded below. NEXT = owner steers among the remaining unblocked debts (the map.json deletion prerequisites, DEBT-MAP-G2-SINGLEMAP, R698 uniqueness legs, interval unit-blindness) — candidate 1 waits on the owner setting the tide length; the tide DATA migration is tide-repo work.

INERT when no transition rule is configured (the store cannot know which predicate is the map's adjacency without rules config, invariant 4); a key whose fact is GONE is skipped (the R710 store boundary already errored on it), so no double-report; the union across rules avoids the per-rule DEBT-MAP-G2-SINGLEMAP false-positive.

A cost keyed to a non-adjacency fact (a walk-cost on something that is not an edge) is flagged `EdgeCostNotAnEdge` and gates under `[continuity].severity`. This lives at the validate layer, NOT the store's `add_edge_cost` gate, for the same reason G1/G2 do: the store cannot know which predicate is the map's adjacency without the rules config (invariant 4 — core never hardcodes "place"/"adjacent"), so `add_edge_cost` only checks fact-exists + n>0 + unit-registered and ACCEPTS a cost on any existing fact. Round 713 — nesting spatial piece design.decision_summary:
R713 DESIGN (code 0) -- piece 1 of R712's three independent spatial pieces: NESTING, the structural foundation the other two attach to. Answers R712's three open questions (tree-vs-DAG; the per-scope adjacency scope model + cross-depth ambiguity; frame-scoped refinement exclusivity) and hands a BUILD plan (R714). GROUNDED FIRST (R668, read continuity.rs not a memory of it): the transition arm builds ONE flat `edges` map + flat `nodes` set with G4/G2 over them; the load-bearing forcing fact is that the R703 2-level containment checks CANNOT represent 3 levels -- `contains(campus,school)` + `contains(school,hall)` forces `school` to be a node (MapContainedOffMap: a contained thing must be a node) AND not a node (MapContainerAsNode: a container must not be a node), a contradiction at continuity.rs:3001/3016 -- so nesting must GENERALIZE (and partly repeal) those checks, not add to them.

DECISIONS. (1) tree-vs-DAG = START TREE (v1): at most one direct container per place within one (frame,branch) query-world; a co-scoped second parent is a new ContainmentMultipleParents fail-loud; DAG deferred (its weaker "shares a common descendant means compatible" comparability defers with it). WHY: parent() must be a total, unambiguous function for scope derivation + ancestry, and the authored world is strictly hierarchical (map in school in rooms) -- multi-parent is speculation (YAGNI). (2) per-scope adjacency = SIBLINGS-ONLY, scope = the shared direct container, DERIVED from the tree (no stored scope field: one source, no drift with the tree). A cross-container edge (parents differ) is a new AdjacencyCrossScope violation. PORTALS (exit-the-building) are the CONTAINER participating as a node in its parent's scope (adjacent(school,quad), both children of campus), NOT a cross-depth edge -- so the container/node dichotomy DISSOLVES: a place is a NODE in its parent's scope and a CONTAINER in its own, roles that are scope-relative. WHY siblings-not-LCA: the least-common-container is ambiguous when the two endpoints sit at different depths (R712's open question); requiring siblings makes the scope trivially unambiguous (= the shared parent) and turns every cross-depth edge into a free integrity finding. (3) refinement-aware exclusivity: two co-holding at-values conflict ONLY if NOT comparable in the containment order (ancestor/descendant = a refinement, a finer + coarser statement of one location, compatible; siblings/disjoint = a real conflict), a containment twin of order.comparable (continuity.rs:499), read holds_at-scoped in the pair's frame-world at the co-hold point. Round 714 — refinement-aware exclusivity.decision_summary:
R714 BUILD (code) — the FIRST of two build rounds for the R713 NESTING design: REFINEMENT-AWARE EXCLUSIVITY (the exclusive-arm half). SCOPE SPLIT (measured, flagged): R713.10 numbered the nesting build 0-5 across `continuity.rs`'s most intricate arms; R714 delivers the pieces that live in the EXCLUSIVE arm (which ALREADY iterates per-(frame,world) via `for_each_world_pair`), leaving the transition-arm map-scan refactor (containment-tree integrity = multiple-parents/cycle, per-scope adjacency, `AdjacencyCrossScope`, remove `MapContainerAsNode` / keep+generalize `MapContainedOffMap`) to a later round. The seam between the two arms is clean and each half is its own commit + independent adversarial review (the commit-sized-round principle; the design bundled them because they share the containment tree, and the shared substrate `contains_comparable` built here is exactly what the map-scan round reuses).

WHAT: `NarrativeRuleSpec::Exclusive` gains an optional `containment` predicate (IN-PLACE, no vN — the R712/R713 Finding-2 fold, because the exclusive rule had no containment source and reading `contains` store-wide would be ambiguous / invariant-4-unclean). When declared, the exclusive gate becomes REFINEMENT-AWARE: two co-holding non-keyed values that are COMPARABLE in the containment order (one transitively contains the other, e.g. at(p,classroom) + at(p,school) with classroom in school) REFINE one location (a finer + a coarser statement of the same place) and are NOT flagged; siblings / disjoint places still conflict. New fn `contains_comparable` is a containment-order twin of `CanonOrder::comparable`, built holds_at-scoped in the pair's frame-world (R713.5/R713.7 frame/branch axis; the TIME axis of the MAP scan stays a later round); cycle-safe by its own visited-set (the containment-tree integrity gate is the later round's, so the walk must terminate on any store, R440 out-of-band). Invariant-4: the containment predicate is the rule's DECLARED field (`referenced_predicates` typo-guards it, fail-loud on a misspelled predicate), nothing hardcoded; inert without the field (backward-compatible) and inert for values the containment tree does not name (per:object custody holders). `forbid_transition_legs` still forbids adjacency/undirected/containment on INTERVAL; the exclusive arm now forbids only the EDGE legs (adjacency/undirected) and reads `containment`. describe-schema documents the new field. narrative-rules is FILE-authored (no add-rule primitive), so no mutate-API/CLI/MCP wiring; and no store schema bump (rules live in narrative-rules.json; violations are computed, not stored).

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER (fresh subagent, not a fork) = REQUEST-CHANGES -> 2 PROVEN silent-accept modes folded (none downplayed), the other 5 verification claims independently confirmed holding against the code. F1 (MED, BUILD, folded): `key_of` used the coarse `typed_object_key` for the object leg (a Quantity's `unit`-only borrow) while the exclusive gate compares via `claim_leg`/`typed_object_display` (collision-free) — two distinct quantities {5,floor} and {3,floor} collapsed to "floor", hit the a==b short-circuit, and FALSELY REFINED a real conflict (the "one field, two read paths, different invariant" anti-pattern CLAUDE.md bans, R305). FOLD: the refinement now keys on `claim_leg` (the SAME identity as the gate) and `contains_comparable`'s node identity is `typed_object_display`; a Quantity regression test guards it. F2 (LOW-MED, DESIGN, folded): the scan dismissed the whole pair on the FIRST co-hold point being a refinement, so a later co-hold conflict where the containment has LAPSED was missed (not triggerable while containment is static, but R714 adopts holds_at scoping so the door is open). FOLD: the scan now finds the FIRST co-hold point that is NOT a refinement (a genuine conflict), preserving both the co-held-but-all-refine skip and the never-co-held unordered accounting; a time-scoped-lapse regression test guards it. VERIFIED HOLDING (the reviewer tried to break and could not): frame/world scoping (a.frame is the pair's frame; a different-frame containment cannot leak in, a legitimately-holding same-frame one is not excluded); the wire/parse split (exclusive rejects adjacency/undirected + accepts containment + blank-containment rejects; interval rejects all three; the typo-guard covers the exclusive containment); scope-split soundness (refinement over a non-tree store is PERMISSIVE-safe — first-container-per-contained only REDUCES reachability, never false-skips; every parent edge is a real fact; the cycle guard never returns a false true); backward-compat (serde-default None, `if let Some(cont)` guard fully inert without the field). per:object inertness is an AUTHORING ASSUMPTION (custody holders are not contains nodes), documented, not structurally guaranteed. 8 unit tests (ancestor/descendant skip, siblings conflict, inert-without-field, cycle-safe, quantity-not-collapsed, lapse-still-flags, transitive-multi-hop, wire accepts-containment/rejects-edge-legs) + a committed CLI e2e (`refinement_aware_exclusivity_end_to_end`: the SAME castle+hall store gates WITHOUT the field and passes WITH it, through the real binary). 1039 workspace tests green; clippy/fmt clean; validate-workspace + validate-code-refs 0 violations. SCOPE SPLIT (measured, flagged): R713.10 numbered the nesting build 0-5 across `continuity.rs`'s most intricate arms; R714 delivers the pieces that live in the EXCLUSIVE arm (which ALREADY iterates per-(frame,world) via `for_each_world_pair`), leaving the transition-arm map-scan refactor (containment-tree integrity = multiple-parents/cycle, per-scope adjacency, `AdjacencyCrossScope`, remove `MapContainerAsNode` / keep+generalize `MapContainedOffMap`) to a later round. The seam between the two arms is clean and each half is its own commit + independent adversarial review (the commit-sized-round principle; the design bundled them because they share the containment tree, and the shared substrate `contains_comparable` built here is exactly what the map-scan round reuses).

WHAT: `NarrativeRuleSpec::Exclusive` gains an optional `containment` predicate (IN-PLACE, no vN — the R712/R713 Finding-2 fold, because the exclusive rule had no containment source and reading `contains` store-wide would be ambiguous / invariant-4-unclean). When declared, the exclusive gate becomes REFINEMENT-AWARE: two co-holding non-keyed values that are COMPARABLE in the containment order (one transitively contains the other, e.g. at(p,classroom) + at(p,school) with classroom in school) REFINE one location (a finer + a coarser statement of the same place) and are NOT flagged; siblings / disjoint places still conflict. New fn `contains_comparable` is a containment-order twin of `CanonOrder::comparable`, built holds_at-scoped in the pair's frame-world (R713.5/R713.7 frame/branch axis; the TIME axis of the MAP scan stays a later round); cycle-safe by its own visited-set (the containment-tree integrity gate is the later round's, so the walk must terminate on any store, R440 out-of-band). Invariant-4: the containment predicate is the rule's DECLARED field (`referenced_predicates` typo-guards it, fail-loud on a misspelled predicate), nothing hardcoded; inert without the field (backward-compatible) and inert for values the containment tree does not name (per:object custody holders). `forbid_transition_legs` still forbids adjacency/undirected/containment on INTERVAL; the exclusive arm now forbids only the EDGE legs (adjacency/undirected) and reads `containment`. describe-schema documents the new field. narrative-rules is FILE-authored (no add-rule primitive), so no mutate-API/CLI/MCP wiring; and no store schema bump (rules live in narrative-rules.json; violations are computed, not stored).

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER (fresh subagent, not a fork) = REQUEST-CHANGES -> 2 PROVEN silent-accept modes folded (none downplayed), the other 5 verification claims independently confirmed holding against the code. F1 (MED, BUILD, folded): `key_of` used the coarse `typed_object_key` for the object leg (a Quantity's `unit`-only borrow) while the exclusive gate compares via `claim_leg`/`typed_object_display` (collision-free) — two distinct quantities {5,floor} and {3,floor} collapsed to "floor", hit the a==b short-circuit, and FALSELY REFINED a real conflict (the "one field, two read paths, different invariant" anti-pattern CLAUDE.md bans, R305). FOLD: the refinement now keys on `claim_leg` (the SAME identity as the gate) and `contains_comparable`'s node identity is `typed_object_display`; a Quantity regression test guards it. F2 (LOW-MED, DESIGN, folded): the scan dismissed the whole pair on the FIRST co-hold point being a refinement, so a later co-hold conflict where the containment has LAPSED was missed (not triggerable while containment is static, but R714 adopts holds_at scoping so the door is open). FOLD: the scan now finds the FIRST co-hold point that is NOT a refinement (a genuine conflict), preserving both the co-held-but-all-refine skip and the never-co-held unordered accounting; a time-scoped-lapse regression test guards it. VERIFIED HOLDING (the reviewer tried to break and could not): frame/world scoping (a.frame is the pair's frame; a different-frame containment cannot leak in, a legitimately-holding same-frame one is not excluded); the wire/parse split (exclusive rejects adjacency/undirected + accepts containment + blank-containment rejects; interval rejects all three; the typo-guard covers the exclusive containment); scope-split soundness (refinement over a non-tree store is PERMISSIVE-safe — first-container-per-contained only REDUCES reachability, never false-skips; every parent edge is a real fact; the cycle guard never returns a false true); backward-compat (serde-default None, `if let Some(cont)` guard fully inert without the field). per:object inertness is an AUTHORING ASSUMPTION (custody holders are not contains nodes), documented, not structurally guaranteed. 8 unit tests (ancestor/descendant skip, siblings conflict, inert-without-field, cycle-safe, quantity-not-collapsed, lapse-still-flags, transitive-multi-hop, wire accepts-containment/rejects-edge-legs) + a committed CLI e2e (`refinement_aware_exclusivity_end_to_end`: the SAME castle+hall store gates WITHOUT the field and passes WITH it, through the real binary). 1039 workspace tests green; clippy/fmt clean; validate-workspace + validate-code-refs 0 violations. NEXT = the map-scan nesting build round (per-query-world containment tree + multiple-parents/cycle + per-scope adjacency + AdjacencyCrossScope + remove MapContainerAsNode / keep MapContainedOffMap kind-independent), its own commit + adversarial review. Design doc = claudedocs/hierarchical-spatial-statechart-design.md (R713 section; R713.10 = the build plan). SSOT = this entry.

R715 BUILD (code) — the SECOND of the R713 NESTING build rounds: containment-tree INTEGRITY (the tree foundation; the per-scope map partition — AdjacencyCrossScope, per-scope G4/G2, MapContainerAsNode removal — is the next and final nesting round). WHAT: a new post-pass `scan_containment_tree` in `scan_continuity` validates that EVERY declared containment predicate — a transition rule's map `containment` (Round 703) OR an exclusive rule's refinement `containment` (Round 714), deduped — forms a TREE within each (frame, branch) query-world: at most one direct container per place (`ContainmentMultipleParents`) and acyclic (`ContainmentCycle`). Two new `ContinuityViolation` variants (structural, ride `severity`) + verdict arms + a describe-schema note + a committed CLI e2e. Node identity = the collision-free `typed_object_display` (Round 714), so two distinct Quantity contained legs never collapse to a false shared child. FRAME-scoped (the R713 review's Finding 3: cross-frame containers naming one child are both-true — a belief-frame hierarchy differing from ground truth — not flagged; only a same-(frame, world) pair is) and BRANCH-scoped via `visibility`. This is the foundation the per-scope partition sits on and the invariant the Round 714 refinement walk assumes; it does NOT touch the flat Round 702/703 G4/G2 (that per-scope generalization is the next round). No store schema bump (rules are file-authored; violations are computed).

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER (fresh subagent, not a fork) = COMMIT-WITH-FIXES -> 1 HIGH design defect folded (none downplayed) + 2 LOW notes; the cycle detector independently verified panic-free and terminating on every shape (self-loop, rho-tail, disjoint cycles, deep chains), dedup-by-minimum-member correct, and the flat G4/G2 verified untouched. F1 (HIGH, folded): the gate was TIME-BLIND (it filtered `contains` facts by `visibility` only, not `holds_at`), so it HARD-REJECTED legal time-varying containment — a place MOVED between containers across DISJOINT canon extents (vault [ch1-2] then museum [ch3+], never co-holding) false-flagged as multiple-parents, and an early-then-reversed containment (`a` contains `b`, later `b` contains `a`) false-flagged as a cycle; worse, it disagreed with Round 714's `contains_comparable`, which reads the SAME relation through `holds_at` (the two-readers-one-field split CLAUDE.md bans), and its remediation advised deleting a still-true fact. The design's TIME-axis deferral (R713.7) was sound for an under-reporting DETECTOR but UNSOUND for a hard-reject GATE that over-rejects. FOLD: `scan_containment_tree` now evaluates the containment as a per-canon-point SNAPSHOT via `holds_at` — only facts co-holding at a point form that point's tree — so a move / reorganization across disjoint extents is one container per point (never a conflict); the two variants gained an `at` field naming the co-hold point, and the remediation now says "these co-hold at <point> — end one before the other begins (a move is fine), do not delete a true fact." This reconciles R714<->R715 on the one relation. F2 (LOW): a cycle closing only through a NON-first container when the place also has multiple parents is under-reported — but the store is still gated by the multiple-parents finding, so it is NOT a silent accept; noted in code. F3 (LOW / informational): the Entity/Token same-string identity is the module's established convention (shared with R714 and the exclusive gate), not an R715 defect. 6 unit tests (multi-parent same-frame flagged, cross-frame not flagged, cycle flagged, clean tree silent, moved-place-not-flagged, reorg-not-cycle) + a committed CLI e2e (a place with two co-holding containers gates with `containment_multiple_parents` through the real binary). 1046 workspace tests green; clippy/fmt clean; validate-workspace + validate-code-refs 0. NEXT = the per-scope map partition round (the third/final nesting build). Design doc = claudedocs/hierarchical-spatial-statechart-design.md (R713 section; R713.10 = the build plan). SSOT = this entry.

Round 716 — per-scope spatial map (per-c.decision_summary:
R716 BUILD (code) — the THIRD and final nesting build round: the PER-SCOPE SPATIAL MAP. The flat single-graph map scan (R702 connectivity + R703 G2 containment checks) is generalized to a PER-SCOPE, per-(frame,world) projection: adjacency edges are PARTITIONED by the endpoints' shared direct container (from the R715 containment tree), an edge between non-siblings is a new AdjacencyCrossScope, connectivity (MapDisconnected) + completeness (MapInventedPlace) + off-map (MapContainedOffMap) run PER SCOPE, and MapContainerAsNode is REMOVED (its residue — a container adjacent to its own child — is a cross-scope edge, caught kind-independently). A "portal" (exit-the-building) is the container participating as a NODE in its parent's scope, so the container/node dichotomy dissolves. This changes `contains` semantics from R703's "grouping" (all nodes one graph) to "scope boundary" (siblings-only edges), the R713.2 design. New shared helpers `containment_snapshot` + `snapshot_parent` are the SINGLE tree reader for BOTH R715 (tree integrity) and R716 (partition) — SSOT, they cannot disagree.

OWNER-DIRECTED DESIGN FINDING (revises R712's "3 independent pieces"): the owner asked for "the most long-term-correct method, cost no object." The correct answer is a PER-CANON-POINT map — and that unifies the nesting-partition (piece 1) with the adjacency-time-scoping (piece 2), because a place's container and an edge's existence both vary over authored canon (holds_at), so sibling-ness is per-point and a flat partition is a lossy collapse that cannot represent a changing map. REFERENCES that make per-point correct: (1) the store's own model — holds_at/canon_from/canon_to is THE time primitive, and EVERY other continuity check (frame-conflict, exclusive, interval, the R715 tree gate) is per-canon-point; the flat map scan was the LONE anomaly. (2) R715's F1 fold already moved the tree gate flat->per-point for this soundness reason; leaving the map flat would be an R715<->R716 two-time-models split. (3) CQRS read-side: "the map at time T" is a projection over the timeline. (4) R712's LAYERING LINE puts authored-canon time INSIDE Mnemosyne (only playthrough state is the consumer's). So AdjacencyCrossScope is evaluated per-canon-point (a MOVED place makes an edge sibling early + cross-scope late); only piece 3 (VERIFIED GUARDS) stays a separate later round.

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER (fresh subagent, not a fork) = REQUEST-CHANGES, and it REFUTED the load-bearing backward-compat claim by building + running four probe stores; 2 HIGH folded (none downplayed), the node-identity / SSOT-with-R715 / self-loop-reverse-dup / frame-world scoping / per-scope-partition axes explicitly VERIFIED SOUND. F1 (HIGH, folded): MapInventedPlace + MapContainedOffMap were evaluated PER CANON POINT over TIMELESS entities (entities carry no canon_from), so a place whose only map edge appears in a LATER chapter was false-flagged "invented / off-map" at earlier points — normal incremental authoring rejected. F2 (HIGH, folded, REFUTED "degenerates to R702/R703"): MapDisconnected was per-point too, so a bridge authored to appear in ch5 false-flagged ch1 as disconnected — directly the tide-changing-the-map content this arc exists to support, and a violation of R713.9's own falsification test. Round 717 — verified guards piece design.decision_summary:
R717 DESIGN (code 0) — the VERIFIED GUARDS piece, the LAST of R712's spatial arc (nesting piece 1 + its time axis piece 2 were unified by R716 into the per-canon-point map; only guards was genuinely independent). Decides HOW an adjacency edge carries a place-access GUARD (a condition the edge requires, e.g. "requires low tide / a key"). THE LAYERING LINE (the R712 review's non-negotiable constraint): v1 = DANGLING-REF ONLY — Mnemosyne integrity-checks that a guard resolves to a real declared fact and NEVER evaluates whether it holds now (that is the consumer's playthrough-state job); no satisfiability, no dead-content-under-guards, no boolean composition, no reification. DECISION: model a guard as `AtomicStore.edge_guards: BTreeMap<edge_fact_id, condition_fact_id>` — a side-table MIRRORING R710/R711 edge_costs (a guard is edge METADATA like a cost; R709's reification-vs-side-table fork already adjudicated this shape decisively FOR the side-table), with a fact-ref VALUE (the condition fact, R707 TypedObject::Fact{id} shape) integrity-checked for existence (dangling-ref, R707 check). add_edge_guard gates both facts exist (invariant-4: NOT that the keyed fact is a map edge — the store can't know the adjacency predicate; deferred to validate-continuity EdgeGuardNotAnEdge, mirroring R711). remove_edge_guard = the symmetric peer (R711 remove_edge_cost). DELETE two sides: retract the EDGE fact -> cascade-drop the guard; retract the CONDITION fact -> REFUSE (the guard references it; symmetric with conflicts_with/pays_off/the R707 Fact-object; escape hatch = remove_edge_guard).

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER (fresh subagent, not a fork) = COMMIT-WITH-FIXES. THE TWO AXES I asked it hardest to break HELD, affirmatively: (F5) the side-table shape is CORRECT on frame/branch — frame variance rides fact identity (a belief-frame passage is a separate adjacency fact; scan_spatial_map already scans per (frame,world)), so no frame slot is needed; only the LINK is metadata, the CONDITION is a full fact. (F6) the design is GENUINELY EVALUATION-FREE — every check reads only existence or the edge fact's predicate, never what the condition means or whether it holds; it deliberately does NOT check condition/edge window overlap (that would be the satisfiability creep the layering line forbids). THE REAL FLAW is methodological (F4): R709 MEASURED the cost (20 edges) before adopting the side-table; R717 has ZERO in-corpus guard instances (tide_closes is SCE's and does not even fit a condition-ref shape), so it substituted "a guard looks like a cost" for measurement — and on THREE axes a guard demonstrably differs from a cost, all now NAMED as deferred instance-dependent choices (R709's discipline of naming unmeasured extensions): (F1, TIME) a guard has a lifecycle independent of the edge window (a troll guards A-B ch1-4 then dies; geography unchanged) — a single timeless value can't express it; "timeless like the cost" is partially REFUTED (NOTE: pure time-ACCESS is already the R716 edge window, this is the finer guard-sub-window case). (F2, DIRECTION) guards are often directional (a one-way locked door) but the owner's map is undirected (one fact per edge, R709), so a guard keyed by it applies both ways — the undirected assumption was inherited silently. (F3, CARDINALITY) "single guard, the consumer ANDs them" is incoherent (nothing to AND if one is stored); a "low tide AND a key" edge forces a composite condition fact that loses per-condition dangling-ref tracking. FOLDED: the design now NAMES all three as measure-before-building choices (value shape = bare String vs BTreeSet vs +canon-window, pinned by the first real instance, not guessed); softens the R661 license to substrate-ahead-of-instance; corrects the F7 build note (the condition-side refuse is NEW machinery, not a pure inbound_fact_refs mirror — the guard ref lives in a side-table, not the facts map); adds the F8 note (a place-access guard IS an adjacency guard via R716's portal model, so it passes EdgeGuardNotAnEdge). Invariant-4 holds (F9): no domain concept hardcoded, opaque fact-refs throughout.

CONCLUSION + THE SCOPE FORK (review F4, surfaced not auto-derived): the BUILD is a genuine owner decision, because there is no measured instance to pin the three axes. DEFER (R709-discipline-honest, recommended): capture the design, hold the build until the authored world creates a concrete guard that measures time/direction/cardinality, meanwhile continue the secondary store-internal debt slate. BUILD-NOW-AS-SUBSTRATE: the owner verbally pulled guards (R712) and the primitives are cheap + proven evaluation-free (F6) + frame/branch-correct (F5); build the minimal edge_guards side-table (bare-String value, the three axes named-deferred), accepting the first instance may force an in-place shape edit (pre-release, no compat cost). Either way the DESIGN stands; the fork is only whether to write the code now. code 0; SSOT = this entry; design doc = claudedocs/hierarchical-spatial-statechart-design.md (R717 section, LIVE).

R718 BUILD (code) — the SECONDARY-DEBT slate, item 1: the R706-DEFERRED INTERVAL UNIT-BLINDNESS (a real correctness gap). Owner mandate: "부채 전부 청산 / 비용 무시하고 가장 장기적으로 올바른 방향". The interval-rule evaluator (NarrativeRuleSpec::Interval, the relation value(left) − value(right) op bound, R489) read a Quantity{n,unit} operand's NUMBER and DROPPED THE UNIT, so it (a) subtracted across units as raw numbers (`15 day − 10 hour` computed 15−10=5) and (b) de-duped two DISTINCT holding values {10,day}/{10,minute} for one (subject,predicate) on `n` alone (collapsed as "the same value restated"). Both violate the R450/R485/R489 no-silent-skip discipline (an ambiguous or non-comparable operand is SURFACED as interval_unverifiable, never silently compared). R706 introduced Quantity+units and explicitly deferred this. FIX (both halves): (1) new `operand_unit(o) -> Option<&str>` — Some(unit) for a Quantity, None for a bare scalar Token/Entity/Fact number; (2) resolve_operand de-dups on the TYPED identity (num, unit) instead of `n` (so {10,day} ≠ {10,minute} = ambiguous → Unverifiable, while two numerically-equal bare scalars "10"/"10.0" both unit-None still collapse — the R489 all-scalar legacy preserved), carrying the unit up via a new Operand::Value.unit field; (3) interval_verdict rejects a compare when left_unit != right_unit (Unverifiable), and a PREDICATE bound whose unit differs from the difference's unit. UNIT-COMPATIBILITY rule: two operands are compatible iff Option<unit> is EQUAL (both None = both unitless/legacy = compatible; both Some(u) = same registered unit; Some vs None or two different units = mismatch → Unverifiable). A CONST bound is unit-agnostic (an author's bare number read in the difference's own unit — the R489 legacy, and the only alternative "const only vs a unitless diff" would regress every const rule over the now-Quantity timeline; documented in describe-schema).

Round 719 — secondary-debt slate closure.decision_summary:
R719 BUILD (code — comment/disposition only) — the SECONDARY-DEBT SLATE CLOSURE (owner: "부채 전부 청산 / 비용 무시하고 가장 장기적으로 올바른 방향"). After R718 paid the one REAL debt (the R706-deferred interval unit-blindness), the remaining three slate items were INVESTIGATED against the actual code + the measured live map (R668 measure-first discipline), and each is a NON-DEBT — a correctly-placed, structurally-prevented, or design-correct behavior that must NOT be mechanically "fixed" (closing them would introduce false positives or hot-path complexity for garbage-in). This round records the dispositions and makes two HONESTY comment fixes so a future session does not re-litigate them:

(1) "R698 uniqueness legs → write path" — NON-DEBT by INVARIANT-4. A self-loop `adjacent(a,a)` / reverse-duplicate cannot be rejected at the write path (add_fact) because the store layer cannot know WHICH predicate is the map's `adjacency` without the rules config (atomic/lib.rs ~4855 states this; it is the same reason G1/G2 and the edge-cost semantic all live at the validate layer). Moving the check to the write path would require the store to hardcode the adjacency predicate = an invariant-4 violation. The validate-layer placement (AdjacencySelfLoop / AdjacencyReverseDuplicate in scan_continuity) is CORRECT. No change.

(2) DEBT-MAP-G2-SINGLEMAP disjoint-top-level tail (R716 F3) — NON-DEBT, the CORRECT nested-model relaxation. R716 checks connectivity PER SCOPE, so two internally-connected but mutually-unreachable top-level containers produce no MapDisconnected. R702's whole-map connectivity was the SINGLE-scope special case; re-imposing it would FALSE-POSITIVE on a legitimately disjoint authored world (two islands; a dream vs the waking world). A nested model makes a container a first-class "separate sub-map" declaration; an author who wants two containers connected declares an adjacency between their parent-scope nodes (a portal — a container as a node in its parent's scope), and THAT scope's connectivity then checks it. So the guarantee is exactly "every scope you declared edges within is connected" — the right invariant for a model with explicit containment. MEASURED: the live tide map is flat / 0 containers = one root scope = the R702 whole-map check, so no live case is affected either way. FIX: the R716-F3 code comment was reframed from "NAMED LIMITATION … weaker than R702" to this correct-relaxation framing (it was mislabeling correct behavior as a debt).

(3) mis-declared Quantity-object map node-identity (R716 F5) — NON-DEBT, structurally prevented by R701. `typed_object_key` (a Quantity's unit-only borrow) vs the containment snapshot's `typed_object_display` diverge ONLY for a Quantity object. But R701 forbids a Quantity object on any predicate that declares `object_entity_kind` (the write path rejects a non-entity object there, atomic/lib.rs ~3835), and a KINDED spatial map declares it — so a Quantity endpoint is UNREACHABLE on a real map. The only residue is an UNKINDED Quantity-object adjacency, doubly garbage-in (a spatial edge to a NUMBER), which the mutate API does not produce and which is inert for the kind-gated G2 anyway. MEASURED: the live tide map's endpoints are all `ent-*` entities. FIX: a clarifying comment at the map-partition site records that R701 makes this unreachable on a real map (documented tolerance, not a live divergence).

NO logic change — the two edits are code COMMENTS + this disposition record. 340 validate lib tests green (unchanged); clippy/fmt clean; validate-workspace + validate-code-refs 0. NET RESULT: the secondary store-internal debt slate is CLEARED — item 1 (interval unit-blindness) FIXED (R718), items 2/3/4 shown NON-DEBTS with measured reasons, so nothing on the slate remains open. Round 720 — verified guards build (edge_.decision_summary:
R720 BUILD (code) — the VERIFIED GUARDS piece (R717 design, piece 3 of 3, the LAST of the R712 spatial arc). Owner chose BUILD-NOW and reframed the design decisively: "소설을 쓰고 증명해" + "므시모시네가 소설에서 키가 있을 때와 없을 때 어떻게 나눠져야 하는지 전부 알고 있어야 하는 거 아니야? 게임에서는 키가 있냐 없냐만 알면 되고, 나는 게임이 복잡해지는 게 싫어." So the guard is not a thin opaque edge-ref alone — it CONNECTS the spatial map to Mnemosyne's BRANCH engine: MNEMOSYNE holds the FULL branching (the got-key world-line AND the no-key world-line, both fully authored as forked branches), and the GAME only evaluates the boolean ("has key?") and follows the branch Mnemosyne already authored. The branching complexity lives in Mnemosyne (static authored structure); the game stays thin (dynamic evaluation). This keeps the R712 layering line EXACTLY (Mnemosyne never evaluates whether the guard holds) while grounding the guard in a REAL authored instance — resolving the R717-review F4 measurement gap by AUTHORING one.

SUBSTRATE (mirrors R710/R711 edge_costs, a fact-ref value): `AtomicStore.edge_guards: BTreeMap<edge_fact_id, condition_fact_id>` (schema v30→v31, additive). `add_edge_guard` gates BOTH facts exist (the dangling-ref check, R707) + rejects a self-guard; `remove_edge_guard` = the peer (R711). DELETE, both sides: retract the EDGE fact → CASCADE-DROP the guard (metadata follows the edge); retract the CONDITION fact → REFUSE (a guard references it — NEW machinery vs edge_cost, because the ref lives in the side-table not the facts map, the R717-review F7 correction). `edge_guard_violations` (out-of-band: gone edge/condition fact) folds into store_registry_violations. validate-continuity `EdgeGuardNotAnEdge` (mirror R711 EdgeCostNotAnEdge): the keyed fact must be an adjacency fact of some transition rule (INERT with no rule, union across rules, invariant-4); reads ONLY the edge fact's predicate, NEVER the condition — no evaluation. CLI add-edge-guard/remove-edge-guard + MCP + describe-schema RegistrySpec. remove_edge_guard acknowledged in the R630 remover tripwire (a leaf: the entry is a referrer of its condition, referenced by nothing). Three axes stay NAMED-DEFERRED per R717 (time/direction/cardinality; value = bare String condition id, first-instance measured below did not pull any of them). NO reification, NO expression composition, NO evaluation — the anti-creep boundary held.

THE PROOF (the "novel"): a committed CLI e2e (edge_guard_smoke.rs) authors the key-guard story through the REAL binary — a hall adjacent to a vault (the door edge f-door), a got-key branch (the hero holds the iron key f-has-key → steps into the vault f-in-vault) and a no-key branch (stuck in the hall f-stuck), forked at the door; add-edge-guard f-door f-has-key. It proves: (1) validate-continuity is CLEAN (the guard is on a real edge, never evaluated); (2) both world-lines' manuscripts are HELD and DIFFER (report-playthrough-manuscript --world got-key reaches the vault; --world no-key is stuck) — Mnemosyne holds the full branching; (3) retracting the condition fact is REFUSED naming the referring edge; and a second test proves (4) a guard on a NON-edge fact is flagged edge_guard_not_an_edge.

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER (fresh subagent, not a fork) = COMMIT-WITH-FIXES; the load-bearing claims VERIFIED SOUND (it tried to break both delete sides + the layering line and could not): NO DANGLING GUARD is reachable — (a) retract EDGE cascade-drops, (b) retract CONDITION refuses BEFORE the remove and catches EVERY referring guard, (c) retract_fact is the SOLE fact-removal site (the only narrative_facts.remove; add/import/amend only insert), (d) add_edge_guard cannot create a dangling entry (both-exist gate + stage_registry_entry rejects a divergent overwrite); the both-roles case (a fact that is an edge AND a condition) is safe (condition-refuse precedes the cascade). ZERO evaluation creep (every check reads only existence or the edge predicate). EdgeGuardNotAnEdge is a faithful EdgeCostNotAnEdge mirror with the store-boundary running first. The remover-tripwire ack, idempotency, the additive v31 bump (a v30 store loads with empty edge_guards; a v31 store on a v30 binary rejects loudly), and describe-schema all verified. FINDINGS: F1 (MED, not a defect — this cadence entry IS the fix: the code cites Round 720 which must exist in the store before the commit gate passes — appended here); F2 (LOW, NOT a defect — the e2e's "both branches differ" is guard-independent BY DESIGN (the guard never touches the manuscript, the layering line), and the guard mechanism is genuinely exercised by the condition-refuse + EdgeGuardNotAnEdge assertions). 1060 workspace tests green (2 substrate unit + 2 committed e2e new); clippy/fmt clean; validate-workspace + code-refs 0 (post-this-entry). NEXT = the R712 spatial arc is COMPLETE (nesting R713-716 + guards R717/R720); the frontier returns to the north star (AAA narrative self-authoring / pinion) or the owner's steer. SSOT = this entry; design doc = claudedocs/hierarchical-spatial-statechart-design.md (R717 section).

R721.1a deferred K-of-N as authoring-infeasible/not-pulled; that was right at that scale and is now PULLED — not for cost but because the intent is UNREPRESENTABLE, turning an authoring slip into a silent logic hole. DECISION: a threshold ON the guard — edge_guards value BTreeSet<String> -> EdgeGuard{conditions:BTreeSet<String>, threshold:Option<usize>}; None=require ALL (AND, the CANONICAL AND, Some(len) normalizes to None on write, review F3); Some(k)=at least k, stored IFF 1<=k<len. ONE struct not two side-tables (R305: never split a field's invariant across write paths). WIRE FORM = the object shape ONLY (review F1 dropped the bare-array deserializer as YAGNI by R721.2's own no-populated-store-fail-loud precedent + a miscited R692 pattern R692 is not; edge_guards is empty in Mnemosyne, R722 array-form unpushed, no game store migrated); schema v32->v33, the monotone >CURRENT guard fails an old binary loud. PRIMITIVES: NEW set_edge_guard_threshold gated 1<=k<=len (normalize k==len->None); add_edge_guard carries k unchanged (never silently mutated); remove_edge_guard_condition REFUSES a removal dropping len below k (refuse over clamp); edge_guard_violations adds a k-range out-of-band check; retract cascade + referenced-condition refuse + EdgeGuardNotAnEdge unchanged. LAYERING LINE HOLDS (review-verified SOUND): store conditions+k, check 1<=k<=len (a DECLARATION-check, structurally identical to the existing dangling-ref check), NEVER count >=k-hold-now (the consumer's, exactly as it never evaluates the AND) — zero evaluation creep. COLLAPSES: 3-of-5 = 10 edges+30 calls -> ONE edge {5 conditions, Some(3)}; the threshold-INVISIBILITY half is closed (k stored + gated), N-COMPLETENESS still unvalidated (a dropped condition -> a well-formed 3-of-4, same as any AND guard — review F2 rescoped the overclaim). OUT (named-deferred, layering-safe): NEGATION (monotone threshold cannot encode NOT), WEIGHTED, a nested AND/OR EXPRESSION TREE (R717-killed); vocabulary = {AND=None, K-of-N=Some(k), OR=multiple edges}.
