Round 725 — intent-verification bottlene.decision_summary: R725 MEASUREMENT (code 0) — the AUTHORING INTENT-VERIFICATION BOTTLENECK measured head-on, plus a SELF-CORRECTION retracting a mistaken build recommendation. Authoring stress tests this session (a 13-scene 2-detective heist + an NPC/reaction scenario) went gate-clean but surfaced a bug class the reject-gate MISSES: a branch-differentiating fact (a suspect's reaction) placed on the shared spine LEAKS into both world-lines — validate-continuity passes (a shared fact IS structurally valid), and only a per-world manuscript comparison reveals it. A controlled INJECTION SWEEP (the R453 trap-corpus method: a gate-clean intended baseline + one seeded intent-violation per class, classified by detecting tool) quantified it into THREE TIERS: (a) STRUCTURAL = reject-gated 1/6 (NPC location double-booking -> validate-continuity rule_exclusive_overlap); (b) PER-WORLD-DERIVABLE = report-visible-but-ungated 2/6 (fork-leak reaction via the manuscript showing it in both worlds; per-world dangling setup via report-payoff-coverage pinpointing [DANGLING] in the specific world); (c) SEMANTIC = invisible 3/6 (wrong-frame mis-attribution; orphan reaction to a never-encountered clue; guard unsatisfiable per-world = INVISIBLE BY DESIGN, the R712 layering line puts guard evaluation on the consumer). THE SELF-CORRECTION (the round's real value): I first flagged case (b)-per-world-dangling as 'the one clean promotable (b)->(a) gate' and recommended building it opt-in. VERIFYING BEFORE BUILDING (citation hygiene, R255) showed this WRONG — R442 DELIBERATELY decided 'dangling is never gated: a WIP story has dangling setups by definition, the dangling list IS the author's todo list', and named a release-time no-dangling gate as a CONSUMER-PULL revisit trigger; R449 reaffirmed 'a no-dangling-setups release gate is recorded, not built'. So the 'promotable' case is precisely the gate R442/R449 twice-deferred as consumer-pull — a sound decision, not an oversight. Building it now would REVERSE an affirmed decision AND build a consumer-pull item with NO consumer pulling it (only this session's self-authored injection) — the exact R724-F6 substrate-ahead-of-consumer trap. RETRACTED: the gate is NOT built; my 'promotable' call was the error (I measured detection coverage but did not check whether the gap was INTENTIONAL — it was). REFINED CONCLUSION: intent-verification is (a) gated-structural / (b) DELIBERATELY report-only (consumer-pull) / (c) irreducibly-semantic — the (b) gap is a decision, not a hole, and the (c) half (frame-attribution, encounter-causality, guard-satisfiability) is WHY the north-star is AI-FIRST AUTHORING: deterministic gates are a structural safety net, not a replacement for the AI author's semantic judgment. Capabilities confirmed with no new substrate (NPC deterministic location, per-world reaction present/absent, all mechanics combined gate-clean); the deferred axes (negation/direction/time) stayed unpulled at scale. code 0; SSOT = this entry.

(c) INVISIBLE 3/6 — wrong-frame mis-attribution, orphan reaction (a reaction to a never-encountered clue; no encounter model), guard unsatisfiable per-world (INVISIBLE BY DESIGN — the R712 layering line puts guard evaluation on the consumer).

Build it only when a real consumer (a release process / SCE / pinion) pulls it, and define that consumer FIRST. Promoting it now would reverse an affirmed decision + build a consumer-pull item with no consumer (the R724-F6 substrate-ahead-of-consumer trap).

THE INTENT-VERIFICATION MODEL (durable, the round's finding): authoring intent splits into (a) STRUCTURAL = deterministically gated (exclusivity / adjacency / containment / guard-integrity); (b) PER-WORLD-DERIVABLE = deliberately REPORT-ONLY (payoff-coverage dangling, a manuscript branch-divergence read) — a DECISION (a todo-surface), not a hole; (c) SEMANTIC = irreducible (frame-attribution intent, encounter-causality, guard-satisfiability-in-world) — needs the AI reader or domain substrate, or is by-design-consumer (the layering line). This is the quantified basis for AI-FIRST authoring: gates are the structural SAFETY NET, the AI author owns semantic intent.

A KNOWN authoring HAZARD (not a substrate defect): a branch-differentiating fact (e.g. a reaction that causes a fork) placed on the SHARED spine leaks into all descendant world-lines; validate-continuity PASSES (structurally valid), only a per-world manuscript read reveals it. Author the differentiator POST-FORK on its own branch (surfaced + fixed in the heist stress test).

CAPABILITIES CONFIRMED this session (probe + stress test, NO new substrate): multi-protagonist alternating POV; NPC DETERMINISTIC location at any canon point (at + exclusive per:subject + report-frame-view, exactly one place); per-character items (holds/custody) + evidence (belief frames); character REACTION present/absent per world (report-frame-view 3-state holding/not_holding/unknown; a positive non-reaction fact for a hard "does not react"); item guards + K-of-N threshold guards (R724) combined in one real scenario, gate-clean. The deferred axes (negation/direction/time) stayed UNPULLED at scale (negation via positive-complement, direction via undirected map, time via canon-time).

Round 728.decision_summary: R728 (code 0, DESIGN of DEBT-K, the accumulating numeric parameter economy). Owner explicit pull ("DEBT-K 지금 갚아") overrides the R726 registered-not-built gate — the owner is the consumer-pull authority, so the explicit pay-now IS the pull signal (distinct from a self-authored probe, the R724-F6 trap). DEBT-K = accumulating meters (affection/karma/stat/currency) + numeric-value-threshold choice gates ("romance if affection >= 4"). MEASURED (R668) against the code: gap (b) — the R489 interval rule is a GLOBAL point-wise binary invariant (scan_interval_rule loops every world x fact; value(left)-value(right) op bound; surface-only OFF by default), not a per-choice gate; gap (c) — the store is snapshot-only (no deltas/sum). Gaps 1 (boolean-proxy silent hole) and 4 (K-of-N cannot express a signed/weighted sum) rest on the discarded "The Courtship" scratch test (asserted, not repo-reproducible). PRINCIPLED PATH (RESUME) = an edge_costs-style side-table (R710/R711), consumer accumulates+evaluates (the R712 layering line). DESIGN = three pieces mirroring units(R706) + edge_costs(R710) + edge_guards(R720): (A) a parameters registry (== units, empty-does-not-pass); (B) a parameter_deltas side-table (BTreeMap<fact, BTreeMap<param, i64>>, signed delta != 0, A2-per-key); (C) a parameter_gates side-table (a numeric threshold on a choice — the thing K-of-N cannot express). The layering line held: Mnemosyne stores the declaration and integrity-checks its shape, and NEVER computes a running sum or whether a gate holds now (the consumer playthrough job). INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (fresh subagent, not a fork) = COMMIT-WITH-FIXES, 2 real defects folded (F1 HIGH killed the reachability violation as a layering-line crossing; F2 MED dropped the spatial edge-check on the gate) + F3-F7. Build SPLIT: R729 = parameters+deltas, R730 = the gate + report + the IntervalOp lift. SSOT = this entry; design doc = claudedocs/debt-k-parameter-economy-design.md (gitignored scratch).

Round 731.decision_summary: R731 (DEBT-L — multiset/quantity custody; the DISTINCT part after DEBT-K paid currency as a global meter). Singular `holds` custody (a per:object Exclusive rule, one holder per thing) had no shape for a COUNT tied to a custody edge (5 potions). MEASURED FIRST (R668/R726 falsification, scratch sidecar): the only shape available today — a SEPARATE, disconnected count fact (stack-size 5) — has a SILENT HOLE: retract the custody fact and the stray count fact SURVIVES, validating clean (registry 0, continuity 0) = a phantom stack with no holder (the DEBT-K boolean-proxy analog). FIX: a fact-keyed side-table AtomicStore.fact_counts BTreeMap<fact_id,i64> (a POSITIVE count keyed BY the fact), mirroring edge_costs/parameter_gates; because it is keyed by the fact, retract_fact CASCADE-DROPS it -> the orphaned-count silent hole is UNREPRESENTABLE (make-unrepresentable, the DEBT-K hole-1 approach). KEY DESIGN DECISION (owner: "비용 무시 가장 장기적으로 올바른"): the count RIDES ANY FACT, with NO custody-predicate check, because anchoring to the per:object Exclusive rule is SEMANTICALLY INVERTED — a multiset count is meaningful precisely for FUNGIBLE items, which are exactly the ones NOT under exclusivity (a unique token has one holder and count 1; a fungible stack is not under the Exclusive rule, which would false-flag two holders as double-custody). The only machine-knowable custody signal is the per:object Exclusive rule (invariant 4 — core has no `holds`), so anchoring would REJECT the count where it is meaningful and ACCEPT it only where it is redundant — inverted, not merely narrow; there is no coherent middle. So the count is a GENERAL per-fact cardinality (holds is the motivating case; killed(A,goblin) x5 / carries(A,arrow) x20 are equally legit) — the R728 review F2 lesson (a side-table over a broad predicate class must not be pinned to one rule-predicate); NAMED fact_counts, not custody_counts, for honesty (the parameter_gates naming discipline: name = the shape, doc = the motivating case). A bare i64 (no unit — the thing counted is the fact's object leg), unlike EdgeCost's number+unit. PARITY-COMPLETE: fail-loud at the write path (add_fact_count) AND re-checked at the scan boundary (fact_count_violations: fact-exists + count>0), the edge_guard/parameter_delta precedent, not the n>0-blind edge_cost one. A2 via stage_registry_entry (a flat i64, not parameter_delta's nested hand-roll). Singular-custody stays UNCHANGED (the per:object Exclusive rule's job; the count is a store-side DECLARATION, Mnemosyne NEVER sums counts across facts or evaluates the multiset — the R712 layering line). NO report primitive (YAGNI — a count is a single per-fact value, no DEBT-K accumulation-invisibility gap; visible via query). schema v35->v36 additive; RegistrySpec (describe-schema) + CLI add-fact-count/remove-fact-count + MCP tool fns + the store_registry_violations extend wire; the R630 every-remover tripwire acked (remove_fact_count = a leaf, the edge_cost class). INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (fresh subagent, not a fork) = COMMIT-AS-IS, NO defect — all 7 load-bearing claims (layering line via full grep, write<->scan parity via a neuter-and-fail injection, cascade/orphan-unrepresentable via the sole-removal-site proof, the semantic-inversion decision, the schema bump, half-wired-green, test non-vacuity) held under attack; 1 LOW = the pre-existing R730 carry (no iter()-forced completeness meta-test over the now-FIVE side-table detectors edge_cost/edge_guard/parameter_delta/parameter_gate/fact_count), NOT regressed by R731, a named follow-on (the removers already have such a forced meta-test, which R731 correctly extends). MEASURED against the real binary (the R668/R726 scratch-sidecar method, three probes): (A) a reusable sub-scene IS expressible today as per-branch occurrences — two questlines each consult an Oracle on their own branch, validate-continuity clean, each returning to its own continuation; the reuse is authoring DRY because each invocation is a DISTINCT canon-time event, so authoring per-occurrence is correct, not lossy. (B) MERGE (N predecessors converge on ONE shared occurrence, then one continuation) is first-class in the canon DAG (validate clean). (C) the ONLY non-expressible piece — a SINGLE shared node with PER-CALLER return-binding (entered from thief-1 return to thief-2; entered from knight-1 return to knight-2) — needs to know WHO called, i.e. the call stack = a playthrough position; it FAILS the R712 layering test and is therefore a RUNTIME concern = pinion / CQRS read-side, the same bucket as R711 candidate-1 stay-time and R727's out-of-scope player-progress and render items. SCHEMA v37→v38 — a genuine SHAPE change (rename+retype), so load() runs migrate_entity_kind_parent_to_parents on the raw JSON when on-disk schema_version < 38, rewriting legacy "parent":"x" → "parents":["x"] BEFORE the typed parse would silently drop the field (EntityKind has no deny_unknown_fields = data loss); null/absent ⇒ empty set ⇒ a root kind (exact backward-compat — every flat store + the tide island unchanged). Round 739.decision_summary: R739 (the R661 kind-tree extension item 2 — a parent-mutation setter; owner pull "미루는거 없이 … yagni 무시", the R738 batch). R732 deliberately omitted a parent-mutation setter because re-parenting an EXISTING kind can close a multi-node cycle — add_entity_kind's new kind is always a leaf pointing only at pre-existing kinds, so it never can. set_entity_kind_parents REPLACES a kind's parents: BTreeSet and is where that guard lives: every new parent must be registered + not self, AND none may be at-or-below kind_id in the current graph (is_kind_or_subkind(p, id) true ⇒ p is a subkind of id ⇒ making it a super-kind loops id→p→…→id). Checking the CURRENT graph is SOUND: any newly-created cycle must use one of id's new outgoing edges, so a minimal cycle is id→p→…→id using exactly one new edge, and its p→…→id subpath predates the replacement — so is_kind_or_subkind(p,id) catches it; and the resolver returns the instant it reaches id, before expanding id's own (soon-replaced) edges, so the pre- and post-replacement checks are exactly equivalent (no false positive). The R738 scan detector (entity_kind_parent_violations) re-checks the same acyclicity at rest = write↔scan parity. Fail-loud on an absent kind (add creates, set mutates — one creator per registry, the set_predicate R658 precedent); NO partial write on a rejected setter (the mutation is the last statement, after all guards); idempotent on the identical set; an empty slice roots the kind. INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (fresh subagent, not a fork) = COMMIT-AS-IS, no defects: the cycle guard proven sound by proof AND a 68k-op differential fuzz vs an independent acyclicity oracle (0 mismatches, 8186 genuine cycle-rejects ≈12%, no partial write on any reject). Round 740.decision_summary: R740 (the R661 kind-tree extension item 3 — remove_entity_kind, the last of the three; owner pull "미루는거 없이 … yagni 무시", the R738 batch). add_entity_kind had no inverse — a mis-declared kind could not be un-added, leaving a hand-edit or a banned vN id (the R658 brick lesson one registry over). remove_entity_kind is that peer, and REFERENTIAL INTEGRITY is its whole contract (the R630 every_remover_pairs_with_an_inbound_scan discipline, the remove_predicate R658 precedent): an entity_kind is an IDENTITY referenced by exactly three row types — (a) an Entity.kind, (b) another kind's parents (a child super-kind link), (c) a predicate's subject_kind / object_entity_kind (the R701 endpoint gate). A removal that stranded any would leave a ref pointing at nothing while the store still round-trips — the orphan the write paths forbid (add_entity / add_entity_kind / set_entity_kind_parents / add_predicate all reject an unregistered kind ref). So it REFUSES while any inbound ref exists, naming the offenders; an absent kind REJECTS (not an idempotent no-op — the remove_predicate precedent); a kind naming ITSELF as a parent does not block its own removal (the ref leaves with the node); no partial write (the entity_kinds.remove is reached only after the inbound scan is clean). The R630 meta-test now acknowledges entity_kind as a referenced-identity remover (a future unacknowledged remover still fails). CLI remove-entity-kind, MCP remove_entity_kind. Round 748 — branch cycle scan shared-mem.decision_summary: R748 (the R745 review's R2 perf follow-on CLOSED — the owner pulled "남은 follow-on 1개(LOW)도 닫아", the last logged residual). R745's branch_lineage_cycle_violations (the out-of-band branch-lineage cycle scan) called mnemosyne_core::world_membership(&store.branches, id) once per branch; world_membership recomputes the shared ancestry from scratch on each call, so a DEEP fork chain was O(N^3) — MEASURED on the real binary: validate-workspace on b1<-b2<-...<-bN took N=250 2.1s, N=350 5.9s, N=500 22.2s (roughly cubic). CLOSED the SSOT-PRESERVING way (the most-long-term-correct: a bespoke cycle-only DFS would be O(N+E) but a SECOND definition of "branch cycle" that could drift from world_membership, reversing R745's whole rationale): a shared memo across the sweep. A NEW mnemosyne_core::world_membership_memoized(branches, world, &mut memo) exposes the caller-owned memo; world_membership now delegates to it with a fresh memo (world_membership == world_membership_memoized(.., &mut fresh), a faithful generalization). branch_lineage_cycle_violations creates ONE memo and threads it through the branch loop, so each world's membership is computed ONCE across the whole sweep — O(N^2) not O(N^3). POST (real binary): N=250 0.05s, N=500 0.17s (a 127x drop at N=500). The VERDICT IS UNCHANGED: a world's membership is root-independent (exactly why membership_of already memoizes WITHIN one call), the per-root cycle guard (on_stack) stays FRESH per call, and only fully-computed ACYCLIC memberships enter the memo (membership_of's Err path, on the on_stack back-edge, memoizes NOTHING — a cyclic node is structurally impossible to memoize), so a cyclic branch and a branch reaching a cycle both still fail loud identically and no memo hit can mask a cycle regardless of iteration order. Round 749 — 2d-projection-experiment des.decision_summary: R749 (DESIGN, code 0 — the owner's steer: start an end-to-end authoring experiment for a NON-point-and-click genre, beginning with the Ao-Oni-style 2D RPG-Maker (tsukuru) genre, and verify the SAME narrative projects onto BOTH a visual-novel axis AND a tsukuru axis, both dialogue/monologue-centric, not prose-centric). Designed claudedocs/phase1-2d-projection-experiment/v1/ (premise.md + author-brief.md + render-vn-brief.md + render-tsukuru-brief.md + extractor-brief.md + judge-brief.md + manifest.json + runbook.md), sha-pinned pre-execution. THESIS: genre difference = projection thickness, not substrate difference — hold ONE blind-authored fact store fixed and split only the render into two genre axes; if both project cleanly with only the render-brief differing, the map_locator seam's genre-agnostic pointer claim (R557) is demonstrated on a non-point-and-click genre pair. PREMISE "The Room at the End of the Long Hall" (~18-22 scenes, original, no IP): a locked-building night horror with a kind:place room-graph, edge-guarded locked doors forming an order-real key chain (R717/720/722 place-access guards as the locked-door mechanism), an antagonist as its own frame (geot knows the party's location while the party does not know its — the epistemic-frame engine on a hostile non-party agent, the horror = the knowledge gap), three withheld secrets, and one fork into two roads with per-road quest divergence. FOUR deterministic pins: PIN-1 authoring-clean; PIN-2 spatial+quest structure (>=6 places + adjacency graph + >=2 edge-guards + order-real key chain + geot knowledge gap + >=4 kind:quest + per-road divergence); PIN-3 map/surface resolves (every quest-giver + every withheld-secret surface -> MapLocator, 0 unresolved); PIN-4 (headline) PROJECTION INVARIANCE — from ONE store, both a blind VN render and a blind tsukuru render (each dialogue/monologue-centric) are leak-clean + fidelity-clean over their own blind re-extraction AND the two re-extractions agree on the withheld-secret reveal order, so the axis difference localizes to render form not the fact set. Plus 3 blind judges (per-axis game-feel + a same-night cross check). PRE-REGISTERED PULL: the substrate expresses place-ACCESS as a condition (edge-guard, K-of-N, R717/720/722/723) but DISCLOSURE timing as a single ordinal (first_at, R506); in non-linear tsukuru exploration a secret can be earned at whichever of several spatial triggers the player reaches first, which one first_at cannot express — so the tsukuru render may railroad or invent a trigger while the linear VN render is served exactly. If that pull lands, the BUILD target is giving disclosure timing the same condition/first-reached vocabulary the access axis already has — the exact generalization a real-time 3D consumer would also need; this experiment is the consumer whose pull decides it. Contamination firewall (R469): this lineage writes the design only; blind subagents author / render each axis / re-extract each / judge. THIS ROUND IS DESIGN (code 0); EXECUTION (spawning the blind stages) is the EXPERIMENT-EXECUTION consent gate. SSOT = this entry + the manifest.

Round 751 — disclosure-timing generaliza.decision_summary: R751 (DESIGN, code 0 — the disclosure-timing generalization the R750 experiment pulled, pinned before the build; the R738 schema-change-design-in-entry pattern). PROBLEM (R750): DisclosureOverride.first_at is a single ordinal per world (BTreeMap<branch, single-section-coord>); a non-linear walked (tsukuru/3D) render cannot honor it without straining (R750 saw a page-carry railroad + a premature leak + a content-split), while a linear (VN) render honors it trivially. DESIGN: generalize the per-world first_at VALUE from a single coord (String) to a FIRST-REACHED-OF-A-SET trigger with an optional K-of-N threshold, mirroring the ACCESS-axis EdgeGuard shape (R717/720/722/723). NEW struct mnemosyne_core::DisclosureReveal { coords: BTreeSet<String>, threshold: Option<usize> } in narrative.rs — the exact SHAPE-mirror of EdgeGuard { conditions: BTreeSet, threshold: Option }. SEMANTIC (world W): the fact is first legitimately disclosed at the k-th-EARLIEST coord of `coords` by W's canon order, k = threshold.unwrap_or(1) = FIRST-REACHED (the earliest of the set) by default. NOTE the default differs from EdgeGuard on purpose: EdgeGuard None = require-ALL (AND, access is conjunctive); DisclosureReveal None = FIRST-reached (k=1, reveal fires at the earliest trigger). Normalization mirrors edge-guard's discipline but on the respective canonical default: reject Some(0) (vacuous) and Some(k>len) (unsatisfiable), NORMALIZE Some(1)->None (first-reached is the canonical default), so Some(k) is stored only for 2<=k<=len; each k is a DISTINCT semantic (unlike edge-guard where Some(len)==None), so Some(len)=last-reached (max) is NOT normalized away. LAYERING (verified): CanonOrder lives in mnemosyne-validate, mnemosyne-core does NOT depend on it — so core STORES the declaration order-free and the VALIDATE layer resolves the k-th-earliest with the order. The R510 resolver EffectiveDisclosure.first_at changes Option<String> -> Option<DisclosureReveal> (the world's reveal DECLARATION, order-free); a NEW validate-layer helper resolves the declaration to the effective coord (k-th-earliest by order) where needed. RIPPLE (deliberate, the payoff): MapLocator.first_at (the pinion seam) changes Option<String> -> Option<DisclosureReveal> so pinion receives the trigger SET + threshold and resolves FIRST-REACHED against the player's actual non-linear path at runtime (the "declaration stored, never evaluated" edge-guard layering line, R712 — pre-flattening to one coord would re-impose the single-ordinal limit the pull is about). Round 755 — prose-provenance DESIGN: sto.decision_summary: R755 (DESIGN, code 0 — the P5 INTERACTIVITY MIGRATION arc's final sub-step; objects/ladders/knots done, this closes the prose-provenance hole the arc named). PROBLEM: the engine's Line is provenance-airtight (crate-private fields + a single fact_id-joining constructor, the R643 detectable->unrepresentable doctrine at the type boundary, born of the tide field-report "invented narrative" bug), but that guarantee covers only ONE of the two things a player reads. A scene is (a) a fact-clue overlay = provenance-bound Lines, and (b) STORY PROSE = the narration/dialogue the player actually reads, a plain Vec<String> with NO fact_id and ENTIRELY outside the engine (the engine reads only scene.title/section/begins; Rung.question is a bare pass-through String, "not re-checked here"). The story prose is the BULK (tide: ~128K chars across 56 segments of segment-prose.json + 5 ladders/19 questions + epigraphs, vs a small fact-clue overlay). So "invention is unrepresentable" is INCOMPLETE: it holds for clues, is silent on the story, and a new engine consumer (a second game, pinion) could fabricate story prose freely. The prose is NOT unanchored, though: it is a fail-loud projection of the Markdown manuscripts via TEXT/positional anchors (prose-anchors.json 50-char verbatim prefixes, derive-prose.py); there is NO EPUB and 0 of 66 sections carry an epub_locator. So there are already TWO content-SSOTs (the atomic store for facts, the manuscript for prose) and two provenance chains, but the KERNEL owns only the fact chain. FORK: (1) collapse-to-store-fact = make every rendered sentence a fact — REJECT (a question/epigraph asserts no world-claim; distorts the fact model, overloads the store with non-facts, violates fact-store purity + the structured-fact doctrine "free narrative asserting no structured fact stays in prose, where AI judgment belongs"); (2) content-anchored prose = a rendered unit is provenance-bound to EITHER a store fact_id OR a resolvable content-anchor into the manuscript/content-SSOT — RECOMMEND; (3) two chains, engine owns only facts — REJECT AS TARGET (tide's chain IS closed but per-consumer; the kernel guarantee stays incomplete for any future consumer; a good interim, not the destination). DECISION = fork-2, realized as TWO provenance-bound SIBLING types, NOT a dual-provenance Line (keep Line's fact_id invariant pure): a NEW Passage (crate-private fields + a single constructor joining a resolvable ContentAnchor, no public ctor / no Deserialize = the Line forgery guard applied to prose) carries authored narration; a rendered narrative unit is a fact-Line OR a content-Passage, neither fabricable. ContentAnchor { source, locator: Prefix(String) today = tide's verbatim manuscript prefix | Cfi(String) later } is abstract over the substrate; a Passage carries (anchor, projected text) with fail-loud resolution (the text is what is AT the anchor) + a text-hash drift check = the normative_excerpt EPUB-projected-cache model (R393 epub_locator ingestion / R403 projected cache / R404 offline text-hash drift) generalized from spec sections to narrative prose. This respects the structured-fact SSOT principle (prose lives once in the content-SSOT; the kernel holds a pointer + a fidelity-checked projection, never a restatement) AND fact-store purity AND closes R643's fabrication hole — the three doctrines reconciled, not traded off. It is the SAME CQRS seam and migration shape as objects/ladders/knots (a tide mechanism lifted into the provenance-bound kernel, tide keeping runtime + presentation); the prose mechanism (prose-anchors.json + derive-prose.py) is the LAST one outside the kernel. PHASING: Phase 1 (the BUILD) = engine Passage + ContentAnchor + fail-loud resolution, consumer-SUPPLIED content-SSOT + anchors (no store schema change, defers the store question); Phase 2 = tide migration (segment-prose.json / ladders.json -> engine Passages); Phase 3 (future) = store-owned anchors (generalize epub_locator / normative_excerpt to narrative sections); Phase 4 (future) = Prefix->Cfi, Markdown->EPUB (a substrate swap). OPEN (named): anchor granularity (section vs sub-section; EPUB sub-section-CFI = the contract's open question), one passage stream vs interleaved in SceneView (Phase 2 render), Markdown vs EPUB SSOT (Phase 4). Round 757 — field-report §5 root: B-maxi.decision_summary: R757 (DESIGN, code 0 — the field-report §5 ROOT fix; owner-chosen B-maximal, 2026-07-23). The field-report bug (a consumer offered UNDISCLOSED entities as interaction choices via a parallel identity the kernel could not see — a first-night call naming people the player has never met) was fixed on the CONSUMER side in tide (§4, tide `eefa7c9`: the call/substitute cast axis migrated off a hardcoded `NameId`/`name_key`/`[JONGDEUK,BUNOK,PANSU]` array onto `cast.askable` gated by disclosure). That cured the instance but left the KERNEL BLIND-SPOT: the engine's store-projection gates watch only what flows through the store, so a consumer that builds its own identity/data space bypasses them, and a future consumer (pinion) re-introduces the class. DOCTRINE (the default-engine-into-Mnemosyne directive 2026-07-21, itself triggered by a tide field-report bug): the provenance invariant lives in the ENGINE layer so fabrication is inexpressible. PRINCIPLE (owner: ignore YAGNI/cost, most long-term-correct): CQRS to the limit — drive consumer-held world-data to ZERO. The boundary is AUTHORED world-truth (store write-SSOT + engine read-projection: entity identity/kind, disclosure order, prose, quest structure, AND PRESENCE) vs the LIVE play-session (the consumer's cursor/known/taken + presentation chrome/i18n/layout/input). Round 759 — prose-provenance P3c DESIGN:.decision_summary: R759 (DESIGN, code 0 — P3c of the R755 prose-provenance arc; pays both debts R756 carry_forward named; owner asked "cost-no-object, most long-term-correct" 2026-07-23). TWO gaps remain after P3a/P3b/R758. GAP 1: NormativeExcerpt (spec, R393/R403/R404; mnemosyne-atomic/src/lib.rs:254) and ContentExcerpt (narrative, R756; lib.rs:320) DUPLICATE text + text_sha256 + recompute_text_sha256 + text_sha256_matches (byte-identical impls) and scan_content_drift re-hashes each family separately — the same provenance shape (a positioned, verbatim, drift-hashed projection) held as two types. GAP 2: the engine's Rung.question is still a bare pass-through String (types.rs:373 "novel-anchored upstream ... not re-checked here" -> projection.rs:260 copies it into Door::Ask), so a manuscript-less/generic consumer (pinion) can fabricate a ladder DOOR LABEL freely (the leak gate checks reveals, never the question prose) — R643's fabrication hole, open on the last authored-prose surface the P3 arc had not reached (R755 sec 7 closed it only CONSUMER-side in tide 5d48c9d). PART 1 DECISION: ContentExcerpt is the ONE substrate (provenance = content-SSOT anchor + verbatim text + drift hash; ContentAnchor is already medium-neutral, a new Locator variant being the substrate swap not a redesign). NormativeExcerpt becomes a spec-facing WRAPPER: { excerpt: ContentExcerpt, anchor_url, source_revision }. KEY distinction between two things that COINCIDE today and DIVERGE later: the content-SSOT anchor (excerpt.anchor, ultimately the EPUB per epub_ssot_architecture) vs the upstream origin (anchor_url + source_revision, which external standards doc + revision the baseline was captured from). Today there is no EPUB baseline so the URL looks like the content-SSOT; the moment one exists, excerpt.anchor becomes an EPUB CFI while anchor_url stays the W3C URL — independent facts, so BOTH are kept. REJECTED "drop anchor_url, make the URL the permanent anchor" (conflates current-location with origin, LOSES the upstream URL once the anchor becomes an EPUB CFI) and "share only a text+text_sha256 tuple" (leaves two anchor families forever, never converges onto ContentExcerpt). Migration v41->v42 is total and blocker-free: synthesize excerpt.anchor from epub_locator IF the section carries one, ELSE from anchor_url (source = anchor_url, locator = Prefix(text) — the passage IS its own verbatim text within the cited doc, the SAME Prefix model narrative uses, so NO new Locator variant); pure field-reshuffle, no field dropped, no data invented, never panics on a missing fragment / query string. Cost-no-object does NOT mean backfilling EPUB CFIs now (that is the SCE-PoC-gated epub_ssot arc); it means the TYPE is EPUB-forward-compatible while the DATA migrates when a baseline lands. VALIDATOR PARITY (CLAUDE.md multi-write-path rule / R305): text/sha invariants live in ONE place — the shared ContentExcerpt validator both import-content-excerpts (narrative) and build_normative_excerpt (spec) route through; the spec-only invariants (anchor_url absolute-http(s)-with-host, source_revision non-blank) layer at the NormativeExcerpt constructor; no field carries two conflicting invariants (anchor.source is legitimately polymorphic — URL for spec, manuscript id for narrative — the URL check being an ADDITIONAL spec-path invariant, not a loosened shared one); a field-invariant-parity test feeds the same edge inputs through both write paths. PART 2 DECISION: Rung MUST stay Deserialize (StaticOverrides::load reads ladders from JSON, overrides.rs:116), so the Passage forgery guard (no Deserialize, sole ctor = resolve) cannot apply directly — which is exactly why the residual could not be a standalone round before P3 (no store resolution path). Now there is one (P3b store_passages / Passage::from_excerpt). So Rung gains question_anchor: Option<ContentAnchor> (plainly constructible / Deserialize — an anchor is consumer INPUT, like Rung.reveals; the guarantee is resolution, not unconstructibility); at projection (Door::Ask assembly) when question_anchor is Some the engine RESOLVES the question text from the section's store content_excerpt and FAILS LOUD if it does not resolve, the resolved text being what the player sees (never the free question); question: String STAYS as the un-anchored fallback for pure interactive chrome (asserting no manuscript prose). The doctrine: a provenance-bound consumer supplies question_anchor and a fabricated door label becomes inexpressible for that consumer — R755 fork-2 ("a rendered unit is provenance-bound to a fact_id OR a content-anchor") extended to the ladder question, the last bare-String authored-prose surface in the engine (mnemosyne-atomic is already an engine dep since R757 B1b, so resolving a store excerpt inside projection is in-crate). PHASING: P3c-1 (store/atomic: converge NormativeExcerpt onto ContentExcerpt + extras + shared validator with the R305 parity test + scan_content_drift reads ne.excerpt + schema v41->v42 + total migration arm + fixture round-trip + repoint the SCE-facing consumers to ne.excerpt.text/ne.anchor_url) -> P3c-2 (engine: question_anchor + fail-loud projection resolve + injection-proven). Disjoint crates, each commit-sized. This round is DESIGN (code 0). Scratch = claudedocs/prose-provenance-design.md section 11. SSOT = this entry.

PART 1 DECISION: ContentExcerpt is the ONE substrate (provenance = content-SSOT anchor + verbatim text + drift hash; ContentAnchor is already medium-neutral, a new Locator variant being the substrate swap not a redesign). NormativeExcerpt becomes a spec-facing WRAPPER: { excerpt: ContentExcerpt, anchor_url, source_revision }. Resolution is a new free fn resolve_rung_question: None -> the free question verbatim; Some(anchor) -> the section's Passage MUST exist AND its anchor MUST equal the declared anchor, else EngineError::RungQuestionUnresolvable { section, anchor, reason: RungQuestionFault::{SectionHasNoExcerpt | AnchorMismatch} }. Round 762.decision_summary: R762 (DESIGN, code 0 — P4a: promote the interaction fresh-effect RULE to the default engine, resolving the tide field-report 2026-07-24 §5 dead-"go"-door). Owner picked (b) "the rule belongs in the default engine" over (a) a tide-local patch, and pushed the architectural point: a bug in REACTING to a selection is a BASIC feature the default engine must cover, not something each consumer re-fixes locally. §5 root cause verified in code (tide engine/src/lib.rs): (1) choose_by_key("go:dest") (lib.rs:1909) sets world.at and discloses nothing, while the on-screen tableau is driven only by a `did` beat or a `known` delta — a bare `at` flip changes nothing, so "go" is a dead button; (2) the "no dead door" invariant is HALF-ENFORCED — objects_here (lib.rs:804) and cast_here (lib.rs:850) skip a door whose facts are all already known, but places_here (lib.rs:746) offers a go: for any place with >=1 line with NO known-check. Defect 2 IS the CLAUDE.md half-enforced-invariant anti-pattern (three door-builders, two apply the freshness invariant and one does not) — which is exactly why one kernel-owned rule, shared by all builders, is the correct fix: a second tide patch re-applies the check in a third place but cannot make the FOURTH omission impossible; kernel ownership does. DESIGN DECISION (v2, review-corrected): the kernel gains ONLY the disclose-freshness RULE, as a READ QUERY. A disclose-door is LIVE for a reader holding `known` iff door.discloses() \ known is non-empty; the fresh disclosure IS that set. Kernel surface: Door::discloses() -> &[String] (Examine->reveals, Ask->slice::from_ref(reveals), Fork->&[]); a free fn fresh_disclosure(reveals, known) -> Vec<&str>; PlayableProjection::live_doors_at(world, section, known) -> Vec<Door> filtering the kernel's OWN Examine/Ask doors by freshness and passing Fork through. CQRS-PURE (R643/R337): `known` is a QUERY COORDINATE like world/section — f(frozen_store, coords) -> view; NO reducer (the kernel never computes the next state), NO Standpoint type (v1's carried an `at` field no kernel rule reads), store untouched. §5 fixed with NO dual-write: tide's places_here filters candidates through fresh_disclosure (defect 2); tide's choose_by_key go-arm feeds fresh_disclosure into the EXISTING reveal_probe so the screen changes because known grows (defect 1, "go = move + reveal") — the kernel returns a QUERY, tide's reveal_probe stays the SOLE writer of known and prices the reveal into the summon/count economy (no second write path). An R305-style field-invariant-parity test asserts all disclose-door builders agree on the same (reveals, known) edge cases — the anti-pattern's prescribed remedy. REJECTED v1 (this round's own first draft, demolished by THREE independent adversarial reviews; kept in scratch section 9 so it is not re-proposed): a kernel Standpoint{at,known} type + an apply(view,sp,door)->(sp',revealed) reducer + live_doors/visible_lines fns + a Door::Move{place,reveals} variant + a GateViolation::DeadDoor gate. Why each fails — (review 1/CQRS) apply+Standpoint is an event-sourced aggregate command handler smuggled into a read kernel and no kernel rule ever reads Standpoint.at; (review 2/does-it-fix-§5) Move.reveals is forced to be two different sets (liveness vs arrival-disclosure) so either defect 1 stays unfixed or arrival DUMPS and kills the destination's sub-doors, the dialog rung is act-priced not reveal-priced so the rule stalls ladders, and visible_lines loses ladder framing; (review 3/scope) tide's transition is not a pure fold (reveal_probe prices everything) so apply forces a second write path to known, the DeadDoor gate runs over doors_at and literally cannot see consumer-fed Move doors (voiding the "gate-locked for every consumer" justification), and Door::Move creates a third place model vs the store adjacency seam. v2 removes every one: no reducer, no Standpoint, no visible_lines, no Move, no gate; act-priced dialog rungs stay in tide (a different effect class); `known` is a bare read coordinate. PHASING: P4b (kernel: Door::discloses + fresh_disclosure + live_doors_at + unit/injection tests; pure/read-side; PUSH-gated) -> P4c (tide: route places_here/objects_here/cast_here through the shared rule + go-arm reveals-on-arrival via reveal_probe as sole writer + the parity test + e2e keylog replay; MN_PIN bump; local commit, no remote). Scope is BOUNDED to the three disclose-door builders + the go-arm + the test — NOT the whole hot loop (routing, pricing, act-rungs, ladder framing, irony all stay in tide). Round 764 — build-time projection DESIGN.decision_summary:
R764 (DESIGN, code 0) — projection at BUILD time, and the sub-section coordinate that makes it need no consumer script. Origin: the tide lift request claudedocs/MNEMOSYNE-LIFT-REQUEST-projection-at-build-time.md (pinned at 08e71f0), which measured PlayableProjection::from_workspace re-projecting the whole store on every run and asked for ONE thing: Deserialize on PlayableWorldReport so the projection could be baked at build time and read back at runtime. The owner then gave the directive that reshapes the answer — remove runtime validation, make it all compile-time — and, when my first shape pushed derivation work into a consumer build script, the one-word correction: the store.

REJECTED, the request as written. Two independent reasons, either sufficient. (a) serde is structurally incapable of compile-time verification: unknown fields are ignored and a missing Option silently becomes None, so a baked JSON survives every engine type change without a word. For a build-time artifact JSON is the worst available medium precisely on the axis the directive cares about. (b) It would widen a provenance hole that mnemosyne-engine's own module doc claims is closed. That doc says invention is unrepresentable, a compile error and not a test to remember, and Line really is locked (non_exhaustive, pub(crate) fields, a sole crate-private from_disclosed ctor) — but its INPUT is not: PlayableProjection::from_report is pub and PlayableWorldReport with its twelve nested types are all pub-field with no non_exhaustive, so a downstream crate can hand the kernel a fabricated report and the kernel mints Lines from the forgery. The guarantee is one layer too shallow TODAY; the derive would have turned a Rust-only fabrication path into a file-shaped one. Recorded so the request is not re-proposed unchanged: ForkTreeBranch.converges carries skip_serializing_if Vec::is_empty with no serde default, so every fork or standalone world omits the key and the naive derive fails to deserialize the first real report — the repo pairs default with skip in all 31 of its Deserialize sites.

THE HONEST FORM OF THE DIRECTIVE. rustc cannot read the store, so "all compile-time" is two things, and conflating them would be an overclaim. Store-DATA checks (a dangling locator, an unresolvable anchor, grounding, the ladder prose gates) move to BUILD TIME, into the one place that holds the store, where they become a build failure instead of a runtime one. What rustc actually carries is the SHAPE contract between the generated artifact and the engine types: change an engine type and the build breaks — the thing JSON can never give. The slogan is therefore not "delete the checks" but "delete the input that needs checking": zero runtime validation because zero runtime input. Explicitly NOT claimed: GateViolation and the quest preconditions are game rules over player state rather than artifact validation, and they stay at runtime.

NO CONSUMER SCRIPT. cargo's only build-time hook is build.rs, so the hook stays; what must not stay is logic inside it. The consumer's build.rs is a one-line delegation into a mnemosyne crate, and everything else — reading the store, declaring cargo:rerun-if-changed, emitting the tables — lives here. My first shape failed this: it asked tide to move its Objects and Ladders loading into build time, which is to say it asked a consumer to CREATE a derivation script in its own repo, the exact artifact class the engine census pass condition is driving to zero. The owner's "why a script?" killed that shape, and the answer to "then where does Interactivity come from?" was: the store.

WHAT MAKES THAT POSSIBLE, read from the programs rather than the data (R668's sign). The objects axis is already store-derived: tide's Objects::ids() is the key set of its object-names.json, and tide's own G1/G2 test asserts that set EQUALS the store's kind:object entities in both directions via mnemosyne_engine::store_entity_kinds — so the emitter filters store entity kinds and needs no consumer input and no schema change, while object-names.json stays the consumer's because names are presentation. The ladder axis is store-owed structure plus a rule that belongs in the default engine: ladder-anchors.json declares nothing but store coordinates (a carrier entity, a prose-prefix anchor, needs and reveals fact ids, an object entity), and ladders.rs derive() is a program over store prose — it locates each declared anchor verbatim and uniquely inside the seat's content_excerpt, requires the anchors to appear in prose order, requires a non-empty frame, and cuts each span into question (the first line) and answer (the rest). A declaration plus the program enforcing it means the program is the spec, and this program reads the store and belongs in the kernel (the R762/R763 precedent that the RULE belongs to the default engine, and R758's precedent that the grounding CHECK moved into the engine rather than being re-implemented per consumer).

THE ROOT GAP THE TWO FINDINGS SHARE. The store's coordinates stop at the section: canon refs, content_excerpt anchors, and DisclosureReveal coords are all section-granular. The playable layer needs a SUB-SECTION coordinate — this fact opens at THIS LINE of that seat — and tide built one out of mnemosyne's own ContentAnchor, Locator::Prefix, and Passage types because the store cannot express it. The same gap is why R761's P3c-2 has no consumer: it requires the declared anchor to EQUAL the section's excerpt anchor, so a rung question, which IS a slice of the seat's store excerpt, has no anchor it can declare. Correct the record: tide's ladder questions are store prose today, and the ladders.rs comment calling them un-anchored authored chrome is inaccurate — the None is an expressiveness gap on OUR side, not a provenance opt-out on theirs. And rung reveals is not a structure parallel to R752's DisclosureReveal but its sub-section refinement: the store says a fact is revealed at a section, the ladder says at which rung within it and gated on what.

DECIDED SEQUENCE, four commit-sized rounds, each PUSH-gated. R765 store: the sub-section coordinate plus the ladder declaration on the section, dangling-ref validation against facts/entities/sections, schema v42 to v43 with a total migration arm; coordinates only, no derived prose stored, since the content_excerpt already holds it. R766 engine: store_interactivity(root) — objects from store entity kinds, ladders derived from the declaration by the kernel running the locate/order/frame gates fail-loud — and question_anchor expressible at sub-section granularity, so R761's guarantee reaches its first real consumer. R767: a new crate mnemosyne-engine-build (mirroring the sce_build precedent tide's build.rs already uses) carrying StaticProjection (all &'static and const-constructible), an INFALLIBLE PlayableProjection::from_static, and emit_playable_projection writing OUT_DIR with its rerun-if-changed declarations, proven by a fixture-store equivalence test across every public query; the same round narrows from_report out of the public API so the module doc's claim finally becomes true. tide's half runs in a tide session per the cross-repo rule.

REVERSED ON PURPOSE, and not quietly. quest.rs states that the kernel reads the store at RUNTIME so that the compile-time snapshot a consumer would otherwise bake in cannot drift from the store. The anti-drift property comes from DERIVING FROM THE STORE, not from the timing: an artifact regenerated under cargo:rerun-if-changed and never committed cannot go stale, and the compile-time contract is strictly stronger, since an engine type change breaks the build where a JSON snapshot would pass. The honest residual is that a pre-built distributed binary is pinned to the store revision it was built from — the same class of trade tide already makes by pinning mnemosyne to a git rev. That sentence gets corrected in R767 rather than left contradicting the shipped design.

WEAK POINTS, recorded so they are not rediscovered as objections. StaticProjection must expose pub fields for generated code to construct a static, so the fabrication surface MOVES from a runtime file to a build script instead of vanishing; that is an improvement, not forgery-proofing, and a malicious consumer was never the threat model. A large generated file trades startup milliseconds for compile seconds. And most of the PERFORMANCE win is in the first half — removing the store read — while the infallible from_static buys verification LOCATION rather than speed; emitting the report as a Rust literal and calling from_report would have been roughly ninety percent of the speed with the runtime Result left intact, and the remaining tenth is bought for the provenance and the type contract, not the milliseconds.

(a) serde is structurally incapable of compile-time verification: unknown fields are ignored and a missing Option silently becomes None, so a baked JSON survives every engine type change without a word. For a build-time artifact JSON is the worst available medium precisely on the axis the directive cares about. (b) It would widen a provenance hole that mnemosyne-engine's own module doc claims is closed. That doc says invention is unrepresentable, a compile error and not a test to remember, and Line really is locked (non_exhaustive, pub(crate) fields, a sole crate-private from_disclosed ctor) — but its INPUT is not: PlayableProjection::from_report is pub and PlayableWorldReport with its twelve nested types are all pub-field with no non_exhaustive, so a downstream crate can hand the kernel a fabricated report and the kernel mints Lines from the forgery. The guarantee is one layer too shallow TODAY; the derive would have turned a Rust-only fabrication path into a file-shaped one. Recorded so the request is not re-proposed unchanged: ForkTreeBranch.converges carries skip_serializing_if Vec::is_empty with no serde default, so every fork or standalone world omits the key and the naive derive fails to deserialize the first real report — the repo pairs default with skip in all 31 of its Deserialize sites.

THE HONEST FORM OF THE DIRECTIVE. rustc cannot read the store, so "all compile-time" is two things, and conflating them would be an overclaim. Store-DATA checks (a dangling locator, an unresolvable anchor, grounding, the ladder prose gates) move to BUILD TIME, into the one place that holds the store, where they become a build failure instead of a runtime one. What rustc actually carries is the SHAPE contract between the generated artifact and the engine types: change an engine type and the build breaks — the thing JSON can never give. The slogan is therefore not "delete the checks" but "delete the input that needs checking": zero runtime validation because zero runtime input. Explicitly NOT claimed: GateViolation and the quest preconditions are game rules over player state rather than artifact validation, and they stay at runtime.

NO CONSUMER SCRIPT. cargo's only build-time hook is build.rs, so the hook stays; what must not stay is logic inside it. The consumer's build.rs is a one-line delegation into a mnemosyne crate, and everything else — reading the store, declaring cargo:rerun-if-changed, emitting the tables — lives here. My first shape failed this: it asked tide to move its Objects and Ladders loading into build time, which is to say it asked a consumer to CREATE a derivation script in its own repo, the exact artifact class the engine census pass condition is driving to zero. The owner's "why a script?" killed that shape, and the answer to "then where does Interactivity come from?" was: the store.

WHAT MAKES THAT POSSIBLE, read from the programs rather than the data (R668's sign). The objects axis is already store-derived: tide's Objects::ids() is the key set of its object-names.json, and tide's own G1/G2 test asserts that set EQUALS the store's kind:object entities in both directions via mnemosyne_engine::store_entity_kinds — so the emitter filters store entity kinds and needs no consumer input and no schema change, while object-names.json stays the consumer's because names are presentation. The ladder axis is store-owed structure plus a rule that belongs in the default engine: ladder-anchors.json declares nothing but store coordinates (a carrier entity, a prose-prefix anchor, needs and reveals fact ids, an object entity), and ladders.rs derive() is a program over store prose — it locates each declared anchor verbatim and uniquely inside the seat's content_excerpt, requires the anchors to appear in prose order, requires a non-empty frame, and cuts each span into question (the first line) and answer (the rest). THE ROOT GAP THE TWO FINDINGS SHARE. The store's coordinates stop at the section: canon refs, content_excerpt anchors, and DisclosureReveal coords are all section-granular. Correct the record: tide's ladder questions are store prose today, and the ladders.rs comment calling them un-anchored authored chrome is inaccurate — the None is an expressiveness gap on OUR side, not a provenance opt-out on theirs. REVERSED ON PURPOSE, and not quietly. quest.rs states that the kernel reads the store at RUNTIME so that the compile-time snapshot a consumer would otherwise bake in cannot drift from the store. TWO CORRECTIONS TO R764, stated here in prose because the ledger is frozen and append-only.

FIRST, R764 said this round would carry a TOTAL migration arm. It does not, and should not. The field is ADDITIVE with a serde default, which is the v39-to-v40 content_excerpt and v40-to-v41 scene_cast pattern the schema comment block already documents as deliberately arm-less: a pre-v43 section has no `ladder` key, serde fills `None`, serialization skips `None`, and an un-laddered store stays byte-identical to what a pre-v43 binary wrote. A migration arm exists for SHAPE changes to existing data (v38-to-v39 first_at, v41-to-v42 normative_excerpt); inventing one for an additive field would be ceremony that reads as data movement and is not. A test pins the byte-identity claim rather than leaving it asserted in a comment.

SECOND, and larger: R764 said this round would introduce the sub-section coordinate. It already existed. `mnemosyne_core::ContentAnchor { source, locator: Prefix | Cfi }` is a Layer-0 type the store has held since R756, `ContentExcerpt.anchor` is one, and `mnemosyne_engine::ContentAnchor` is a RE-EXPORT of it rather than a sibling — so there was never a coordinate to build, only a rule that refused to accept one. R761 requires a declared rung anchor to EQUAL the section's excerpt anchor, which is what makes a hold part-way down a scene inexpressible and is why the first consumer passes `question_anchor: None`. That narrowing is a RESOLUTION rule and it is the engine's to relax (R766), not the store's. What this round adds is therefore not the coordinate but the DECLARATION that uses it.

WHAT THE STORE CHECKS, AND WHAT IT REFUSES TO. Every reference is checked present before the save, never a partial import: `needs` and `reveals` must be `narrative_facts` keys, `carrier` and a rung's `object` must be registered entities, the anchor must name a non-empty source and carry a non-empty `Locator::Prefix`, and two rungs of one ladder may not declare the SAME anchor. A ladder whose coordinates dangle is a gate that silently never opens, which is exactly the failure a store is for. A CFI locator is REJECTED rather than stored: a sub-section coordinate into authored narrative prose is a prefix today, and accepting a CFI would store a coordinate nothing in the pipeline can resolve.

What the store deliberately does NOT check is whether each prefix actually occurs in the section's `content_excerpt`, exactly once, in the declared order. That is the resolution rule, the engine owns it (it is the one that slices the excerpt at these anchors), and duplicating it here would make one invariant answer to two write paths — the half-enforced-invariant class CLAUDE.md names. The store stores coordinates; the engine judges whether they land. For the same reason the declared rung ORDER is stored verbatim rather than normalized: whether it must agree with the prose order is a question about resolution, so the store keeps what the author said and leaves exactly one place to judge it.

NO PROSE IS STORED. A rung carries no rendered word — its prose IS the excerpt's own text from its anchor line to the next rung's. So the declaration cannot smuggle in a sentence the store does not already hold, and the Line/Passage provenance invariant carries down one level of resolution for free rather than needing a second grounding check.

VERIFICATION: 3 injection tests in mnemosyne-atomic. The write path sets the field, keeps rung order, reports an unmatched section id rather than erroring, and REPLACES on re-import (a shorter re-import shrinks the ladder, never appends). The reject test injects TEN malformed ladders one at a time — no rungs, unknown carrier, blank carrier, unknown revealed fact, unknown needed fact, unknown object, CFI locator, blank prefix, sourceless anchor, two rungs at one anchor — and after each one asserts the previously-imported good ladder is still intact, so fail-BEFORE-save is proven by state rather than by the error type alone. The third test pins both halves of the additive-field contract: an un-laddered store emits no `ladder` key at all, and a laddered one survives save/load verbatim at v43. 1185 workspace tests green via scripts/verify.sh (+3 on R763's 1182), clippy -D warnings clean, cargo fmt clean, validate-workspace T1 orphan = 0 and T3 reject = 0, validate-code-refs 0 violations. The CLI was reinstalled at this revision BEFORE the entry was appended, because bumping CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION to 43 means the previously-installed v42 binary would hit the monotone guard on the first store save (the RESUME stale-binary trap, paid immediately rather than left for the next session to trip over).

NEXT is R766, the engine half: store_interactivity(root) deriving objects from store_entity_kinds (already exact — the first consumer's own gate asserts set equality in both directions) and ladders from this declaration, with the locate/order/frame gates run by the KERNEL. That round carries a debt this one uncovered and did not touch: PrefixSlices::new, the kernel's existing slicing primitive, is strictly WEAKER than the consumer's derive() it would replace — it takes the first occurrence of a prefix silently where the consumer rejects an ambiguous one, sorts anchors by offset silently where the consumer requires declared order to match prose order, and overwrites a duplicate anchor silently where the consumer rejects it. That defect is in the kernel today, independent of any consumer.

Round 766 — the kernel's prose slicer st.decision_summary:
R766 (BUILD, engine-only, no store change) — the kernel's prose slicer stops guessing. `PrefixSlices::new` is the engine's one implementation of "cut a document at its declared anchors", and R765 found it strictly WEAKER than the consumer slicer it is meant to replace: where the consumer rejects an ambiguous anchor, this took `text.find`, i.e. the FIRST occurrence, silently; and where the consumer rejects a duplicated anchor, the slice map's `insert` overwrote the twin silently. Two declared holds, one surviving slice, no error. Moving the ladder rule into a primitive with those holes would have been a regression wearing a promotion's clothes, so the debt is paid BEFORE the promotion rather than after it, and it is paid for every consumer at once. Two new fail-loud faults: `ProseError::PrefixAmbiguous { source, prefix, occurrences }` and `ProseError::DuplicateAnchor { source, prefix }`.

SCOPE CORRECTION TO R765's CARRY, stated in prose because the ledger is frozen. R765 said R766 would tighten the slicer AND land `store_interactivity`. It lands only the tightening. The tightening is complete, independently correct, and useful to every current caller with no consumer in sight; bundling it with the interactivity projection would have made a round whose two halves fail for unrelated reasons. `store_interactivity` moves to R767 and the emitter crate to R768.

WHAT I GOT WRONG FIRST, RECORDED BECAUSE THE TEST CAUGHT IT AND NOT ME. I initially tightened a THIRD invariant into the same place: that the declared anchor order must equal the prose order (the consumer's G3). The engine's own test suite rejected it immediately — `a_passage_projects_the_manuscript_slice_at_its_anchor` feeds deliberately unsorted anchors and the doc comment called the input order-independent, on purpose. That is right and my change was wrong: `PrefixSlices` is a GENERIC slicer, an anchor set may legitimately arrive from a map, and a generic slicer has no business demanding that a caller's iteration order match a document. Order is meaningful for a LADDER, whose nth rung must be the nth passage — it is a property of that caller's semantics, not of slicing. Pushing it down here would have made every unordered caller pay for one ordered caller's rule, which is the same category error as putting a markdown parser in the fact engine (the W-rejection). So the order check is NOT here.

But it must not be re-implemented upstairs either — a second `find` walk in the ladder layer would be a second locator, free to drift from this one. The primitive therefore EXPOSES the ordering it already computed: `PrefixSlices::in_prose_order() -> &[ContentAnchor]`, the anchors in the order their prefixes occur, built during the one locate pass. An ordered caller judges its declared order against that. One search, one truth, and the semantic question is answered by the layer that owns the semantics — the same split as R765's store-stores-coordinates / engine-judges-resolution line.

WHY AMBIGUITY AND DUPLICATION ARE DIFFERENT FROM ORDER, and belong here: neither depends on any caller's semantics. A prefix occurring twice names no single place for ANY caller, and picking an occurrence is picking a slice on the author's behalf; the remedy is to extend the prefix, which is an authoring fix, not a guess the kernel should make. A duplicated anchor is a caller declaring one coordinate twice and getting one slice, which is never what was meant. Both are true regardless of whether the anchor set is ordered, which is exactly the test for whether an invariant belongs in a shared primitive.

Round 767 — a rung takes hold part-way d.decision_summary:
R767 (BUILD, engine-only, no store change) — a rung may now take hold part-way down a scene. This is the round the whole arc exists for: R761 bound a ladder question to store prose but required the declared anchor to EQUAL the section's excerpt anchor, and a rung question is one LINE of a scene, not the whole scene. So the only expressible anchor was the useless one, the first provenance-bound consumer declared `question_anchor: None` for every rung, and the guarantee never reached a real ladder. `resolve_rung_question` is replaced by `resolve_ladder_questions`, which resolves a whole section's ladder at once against the section's `content_excerpt`.

THE NEW RULE: an anchor must name the SAME document as the section's excerpt and must LOCATE within its text. Locating goes through R766's tightened `PrefixSlices`, so a prefix naming two lines is refused rather than resolved to the first, and a hold declared twice is refused rather than silently collapsed. A hold's question is then the LINE it starts at, not its slice: the slice runs to the next hold and carries whatever follows the question, which is the scene's business and not the door's label.

WHY A WHOLE LADDER AT ONCE, and not a rung at a time. The order invariant needs the ladder. R766 deliberately kept "the declared order must be the prose order" OUT of the generic slicer — a slicer must not demand that a caller's iteration order match a document — and left `in_prose_order()` exposed so an ordered caller could judge for itself. This is that caller: the nth declared hold must be the nth passage, or the author's numbering does not describe the scene they wrote. Resolving per-rung would have had no place to ask that question, and re-deriving the offsets here would have been a second locator free to drift from the first. One search in the primitive, one judgment in the layer that owns the semantics.

TWO NEW FAULTS on `RungQuestionFault`: `Unlocatable(Box<ProseError>)` carrying the slicer's own cause (wrong document, absent prefix, ambiguous prefix, duplicated hold) and `OutOfProseOrder`. `AnchorMismatch` is GONE, not deprecated — it named the narrowing this round removes, and keeping it would leave a variant no code can produce (no-legacy-carry). The payload is boxed because carrying `ProseError` inside `EngineError` widened every `Result` on the read path past clippy's `result_large_err` threshold; the fault is rare and the return is not, so the box goes on the rare thing. That was clippy's catch, not mine, and it is fixed at the cause rather than allowed away.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT LOOSEN. An un-anchored rung still keeps its free question — un-anchored interactive chrome is a legitimate thing for a consumer to author, and the store never claimed it. A section carrying NO anchored rung no longer needs an excerpt at all (previously any ladder forced the lookup); a section with even one anchored rung and no excerpt is still `SectionHasNoExcerpt`, fail-loud. The guarantee remains RESOLUTION rather than unconstructibility, because `Rung` must stay `Deserialize` for `StaticOverrides::load` — that only changes when the runtime override-loading path goes away, which is R769's business.

VERIFICATION: 3 injection tests, each non-vacuous in BOTH directions rather than merely asserting a reject. The capability test puts TWO holds at two different lines of one excerpt and asserts each door's label is ITS line — not the free string, not the whole excerpt, and not the first line for both, which is what a naive implementation would produce. The order test rejects the same two anchors declared backwards AND asserts the identical pair in prose order is accepted, so the reject is the order and not the anchors. The ambiguity test rejects a prefix naming two lines AND asserts the extended prefix resolves, so the reject is the ambiguity and not a refusal to anchor on a recurring name. 1191 workspace tests green via scripts/verify.sh (+3 on R766's 1188), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace T1 orphan = 0 and T3 reject = 0, validate-code-refs 0.

With that, a consumer stops constructing its interactive layer from its own files, which is what makes the build script of R769 a delegation with no logic in it.

Round 767 — a rung takes hold part-way d.publishable_decision_summary:
R767 (BUILD, engine-only, no store change) — a rung may now take hold part-way down a scene. This is the round the whole arc exists for: R761 bound a ladder question to store prose but required the declared anchor to EQUAL the section's excerpt anchor, and a rung question is one LINE of a scene, not the whole scene. So the only expressible anchor was the useless one, the first provenance-bound consumer declared `question_anchor: None` for every rung, and the guarantee never reached a real ladder. `resolve_rung_question` is replaced by `resolve_ladder_questions`, which resolves a whole section's ladder at once against the section's `content_excerpt`.

THE NEW RULE: an anchor must name the SAME document as the section's excerpt and must LOCATE within its text. Locating goes through R766's tightened `PrefixSlices`, so a prefix naming two lines is refused rather than resolved to the first, and a hold declared twice is refused rather than silently collapsed. A hold's question is then the LINE it starts at, not its slice: the slice runs to the next hold and carries whatever follows the question, which is the scene's business and not the door's label.

WHY A WHOLE LADDER AT ONCE, and not a rung at a time. The order invariant needs the ladder. R766 deliberately kept "the declared order must be the prose order" OUT of the generic slicer — a slicer must not demand that a caller's iteration order match a document — and left `in_prose_order()` exposed so an ordered caller could judge for itself. This is that caller: the nth declared hold must be the nth passage, or the author's numbering does not describe the scene they wrote. Resolving per-rung would have had no place to ask that question, and re-deriving the offsets here would have been a second locator free to drift from the first. One search in the primitive, one judgment in the layer that owns the semantics.

TWO NEW FAULTS on `RungQuestionFault`: `Unlocatable(Box<ProseError>)` carrying the slicer's own cause (wrong document, absent prefix, ambiguous prefix, duplicated hold) and `OutOfProseOrder`. `AnchorMismatch` is GONE, not deprecated — it named the narrowing this round removes, and keeping it would leave a variant no code can produce (no-legacy-carry). The payload is boxed because carrying `ProseError` inside `EngineError` widened every `Result` on the read path past clippy's `result_large_err` threshold; the fault is rare and the return is not, so the box goes on the rare thing. That was clippy's catch, not mine, and it is fixed at the cause rather than allowed away.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT LOOSEN. An un-anchored rung still keeps its free question — un-anchored interactive chrome is a legitimate thing for a consumer to author, and the store never claimed it. A section carrying NO anchored rung no longer needs an excerpt at all (previously any ladder forced the lookup); a section with even one anchored rung and no excerpt is still `SectionHasNoExcerpt`, fail-loud. The guarantee remains RESOLUTION rather than unconstructibility, because `Rung` must stay `Deserialize` for `StaticOverrides::load` — that only changes when the runtime override-loading path goes away, which is R769's business.

VERIFICATION: 3 injection tests, each non-vacuous in BOTH directions rather than merely asserting a reject. The capability test puts TWO holds at two different lines of one excerpt and asserts each door's label is ITS line — not the free string, not the whole excerpt, and not the first line for both, which is what a naive implementation would produce. The order test rejects the same two anchors declared backwards AND asserts the identical pair in prose order is accepted, so the reject is the order and not the anchors. The ambiguity test rejects a prefix naming two lines AND asserts the extended prefix resolves, so the reject is the ambiguity and not a refusal to anchor on a recurring name. 1191 workspace tests green via scripts/verify.sh (+3 on R766's 1188), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace T1 orphan = 0 and T3 reject = 0, validate-code-refs 0.

With that, a consumer stops constructing its interactive layer from its own files, which is what makes the build script of R769 a delegation with no logic in it.

Round 768 — the interactive layer stops.decision_summary:
R768 (BUILD, engine + one ops read, no store change) — the interactive layer stops being consumer-built. `store_interactivity(workspace_root) -> Interactivity` derives from the store the half of the interactive layer that is world STRUCTURE, leaving the consumer only what is genuinely its own. This is the round that makes the build script of R769 a delegation with nothing in it: a consumer that no longer constructs its interactive layer has no derivation to run at build time.

TWO HALVES, BOTH ALREADY THE STORE'S. `objects` is every registered entity of kind `object` — and this was exact before anyone relied on it, which is why it can be taken without ceremony: the first consumer's own gate asserts its object-id set EQUALS the store's `kind:object` set in BOTH directions, so reading it here reproduces that set by construction rather than by agreement. Object NAMES stay the consumer's; a name is a word of the novel, not world structure. `ladders` is each section's authored `SectionLadder` (R765) expanded into the kernel's rung model, and only DIALOGUE ladders become ask-ladders: an observation ladder's facts are opened by examining its object, which is the objects axis, and offering them as questions as well would put one fact behind two doors.

THE SPLIT THIS ROUND KEEPS. `store_interactivity` reads COORDINATES and never prose: a derived rung carries its hold's anchor and an EMPTY question, and the label is resolved later by R767's per-ladder resolver against the section's own excerpt. Empty rather than a plausible-looking placeholder is deliberate — a bug that skipped resolution then shows as a blank door rather than as a sentence nobody wrote. This is the same line R765 drew inside the store (the store stores coordinates, the engine judges whether they land), now drawn once more between the two engine reads.

`free_investigate` is NOT derived and stays at its default. It is policy about how a consumer's own investigate verb behaves — whether the rest of a scene opens freely once its dialogue holds are gated — and not a fact about the world. The caller sets it: `Interactivity { free_investigate: true, ..store_interactivity(root)? }`. Deriving it would have been the easy symmetry and the wrong one.

A DEFECT IN R767 THAT THIS ROUND FOUND AND FIXED, stated plainly because the next reader will otherwise wonder why the resolver dedupes. The kernel prices a rung PER REVEALED FACT while an author writes ONE hold, so a hold opening three facts arrives as three rungs sharing one anchor. R767's resolver collected every anchored rung's anchor and handed the list to the slicer, which — correctly, per R766 — refuses a duplicated coordinate. So the very first multi-fact hold `store_interactivity` produced would have failed as `DuplicateAnchor`, and R767's tests never saw it because none of them fanned out. The resolver now dedupes while preserving order, so the sequence judged against the prose is the sequence of distinct HOLDS. The store still refuses a duplicated anchor within a single declaration; those are different questions and both answers are right. Two rungs at one hold are the same hold, priced twice; two holds at one coordinate are an authoring mistake.

VERIFICATION: 2 injection tests. The derivation test uses a v43 store carrying one dialogue ladder (two holds, the second opening two facts), one observation ladder, and two entity kinds — and asserts objects is exactly the `kind:object` entity (a place is not examinable furniture), that the observation ladder does NOT become an ask-ladder, that the dialogue ladder fans out to 1 + 2 = 3 rungs in declared order with each hold's needs carried, that the two rungs of the second hold share ONE anchor while the first hold's differs, that no question text is invented, and that `free_investigate` stays the consumer's. The resolver test puts three rungs at two holds through the projection and asserts each priced rung carries ITS hold's line. That second test was PROVEN non-vacuous by injection rather than by argument: with the dedupe removed it fails with exactly `Unlocatable(DuplicateAnchor)`, and it passes with it restored. 1193 workspace tests green via scripts/verify.sh (+2 on R767's 1191), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace T1 orphan = 0 and T3 reject = 0, validate-code-refs 0.

ALSO CORRECTED: `store_entity_kinds`'s doc said "`Interactivity::objects` is FED, not derived here". That sentence is false as of this round and is rewritten rather than left standing — a doc comment that describes a rule the code no longer follows is the same decay class as a stale citation.

NEXT is R769, the emitter crate: `mnemosyne-engine-build` with `StaticProjection` (all `&'static`, const-constructible), an INFALLIBLE `PlayableProjection::from_static`, and `emit_playable_projection` writing `OUT_DIR` with its `cargo:rerun-if-changed` declarations, proven by a fixture-store equivalence test across every public query. That is two rounds' worth and its halves fail for unrelated reasons, so this round lands the SEAM (complete, verified, useful on its own) and R770 lands the emitter crate that writes parts as Rust source, narrows `from_report`, and corrects quest.rs.

WHY `from_parts` CAN BE INFALLIBLE, which is the only interesting question here. Not optimism: every check that `from_workspace` runs has already run by the time parts exist. The store read happened, the locator join happened, the ladder questions resolved against real prose (R767). What comes back in is the RESULT of those checks, not their input. So there is nothing to validate — and the deeper point is that this is not "we skipped the checks", it is "there is no untrusted input left to check". A consumer that bakes does no startup validation because it takes in nothing that could be wrong: the artifact is generated from the store by its own build and type-checked by its own compiler.

WHY PARTS AT ALL, rather than emitting the runtime types directly. `Line` and `CastMember` keep crate-private fields so that invention is unrepresentable — which also means generated code in ANOTHER crate cannot construct them. Hence `LinePart` / `CastPart`: pub-field mirrors the engine converts back inside the crate, where the private constructors are reachable. Everything else in the projection (`Door`, `Fork`, `Rung`, `ChoiceEntityRef`, `Interactivity`) already has public fields, so only those two needed a mirror. The guard this does NOT weaken is the one that matters: a RENDERER still cannot mint a sentence, because a renderer holds a `Line` and never a part. The guard it DOES move is the ingestion one — and that was already open at the report boundary (R764 weak point 1). A build-time forger and a report forger are the same forger, and neither is the threat model. R770 narrows the OTHER ingestion door (`from_report`) so there is one instead of two.

DETERMINISM IS PART OF THE CONTRACT, not a nicety: `to_parts` emits every map in sorted key order and the divergent-ending set sorted, so the same store produces byte-identical generated source and a rebuild that changed nothing changes nothing. Without that, `cargo:rerun-if-changed` would still fire correctly but every rebuild would churn the generated file and its downstream compile.

VERIFICATION: one equivalence test, and it is the whole claim of the arc stated as an assertion — a projection that goes out through `to_parts` and back through `from_parts` answers EVERY public query identically: `telling`, `spine`, and per world per section `walk`, `is_divergent_ending`, `lines`, `title`, `cursor_of`, `cast_at`, `forks_at`, `scene`, `referenceable_entities`, `live_doors_at`. It also asserts the ask doors survive with their RESOLVED labels, which is what lets a runtime with no store still show store prose, and that `to_parts` is idempotent across the round trip.

The test was made honest twice over. First, its fixture was THICKENED after the thin one proved little: a one-scene one-world report leaves `cast`, `forks`, and `divergent_endings` empty, so dropping any of those fields in `from_parts` would have passed. It now runs two worlds, a fork tree, and scene cast, and asserts up front that the fixture actually carries cast and a fork before comparing anything. Second, non-vacuity was PROVEN by injection rather than argued: dropping `cast` from `from_parts` fails the test, dropping `forks` fails it, and restoring each passes.

A NEAR-MISS worth recording, because it looked like a kernel defect and was not. The first thick fixture gave one world a scene WITH cast and its sibling the same scene WITHOUT, and `cast_at` came back empty — the projection lets the first world to carry a section fix its cast, and worlds iterate in sorted order, so the empty one won. That is not a bug: scene presence is authored on the SHARED section, so every world walking it sees one cast, and the fixture had built a state the store cannot produce.
