Round 887.decision_summary: The carry was a cost judgement wearing a note, and the gate it deferred had a hollow job inside it
changes_bullets: Paid the carry R886 left instead of carrying it. The reason given there — that pulling in a YAML parser for one assertion was a dependency decision worth making separately — was deferring a real defect on a cost judgement, which this repo's round discipline does not allow. The owner asked why it was left; there was no good answer.

Three gates over this repo's own workflows, in the same file as the declarations because one of them is a cross-check between the record and the CI config. `every_shipped_workflow_parses_and_declares_work`: every tracked workflow parses and declares at least one trigger and one job — R583 lost an unknown stretch of CI to a workflow that did not parse, and GitHub says so nowhere the author looks. `the_replay_workflow_still_replays`: the checkout takes full history, some step passes `--ignored`, and every `--test` target named anywhere in the job exists. `the_path_filter_covers_every_file_the_replay_reads`: every input, config, and declaration a replay reads is matched by the push trigger's path filter.

The gate is a parser, not a text match, and that is not a preference: the R886 workflow names `fetch-depth: 0` and `--ignored` in its own comments, so a substring check passes on prose while the job is hollow. `yaml-rust2` with `default-features = false` — 4 transitive crates, dev-dependency only, never in a shipped binary. Not `serde_yaml`, which is deprecated upstream; adopting a dead crate is the legacy-carry pattern this repo forbids.

The `paths:` matcher supports exactly the two pattern shapes this workflow uses and PANICS on any other. A matcher that quietly mis-read a pattern it did not understand would report coverage it had never checked, which is the same failure the gate exists to catch.
verification_bullets: 1342 green (+3), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace clean.

Injections, self-reported. J2 (drop `-- --ignored`) reddened the replay gate alone — that is the vacuous-pass this round is really about: without it the job runs the cheap tests twice, goes green, and replays nothing. J3 (`fetch-depth: 1`) reddened it alone. J4 (narrow the filter to `claudedocs/phase1-2d-*/**`) reddened the coverage gate alone, naming the uncovered files.
J1 (a tab-indented broken block) reddened THREE — every test that loads this file. Correct and reported as three: an unparseable workflow is unreadable to all of its readers, not one.

J5 was MIS-AIMED and the green was mine, not the gate's: I renamed the test target in the first of the two steps that name it, and the assertion only read the step carrying `--ignored`. So the check was reading one of the two places a rename can land. Generalised it to every `--test` target in the job, with a non-vacuity count, and re-ran BOTH placements — each reddens now.
The path-filter check has no discriminating fixture in the tree as it stands: every declared input already lives under one prefix, so it can only be shown to discriminate by injection, which J4 does.
carry_forward_bullets: GitHub disables scheduled workflows on repositories with no activity for 60 days. If this repo goes quiet the weekly replay stops, and the stopping is silent — the same shape as R583, one level up. Nothing here can see that from inside the repo.
The weekly cadence remains a guess, not a measurement: a yanked dependency has no known arrival rate here.

The gates read the workflow, not GitHub's schema. A file that parses and satisfies all three could still be rejected by GitHub for a key it does not recognise; only a real run settles that, and this workflow has not had one.

The gate is a parser, not a text match, and that is not a preference: the R886 workflow names `fetch-depth: 0` and `--ignored` in its own comments, so a substring check passes on prose while the job is hollow. `yaml-rust2` with `default-features = false` — 4 transitive crates, dev-dependency only, never in a shipped binary. Not `serde_yaml`, which is deprecated upstream; adopting a dead crate is the legacy-carry pattern this repo forbids.

The `paths:` matcher supports exactly the two pattern shapes this workflow uses and PANICS on any other. A matcher that quietly mis-read a pattern it did not understand would report coverage it had never checked, which is the same failure the gate exists to catch.

J1 (a tab-indented broken block) reddened THREE — every test that loads this file. Correct and reported as three: an unparseable workflow is unreadable to all of its readers, not one.

J5 was MIS-AIMED and the green was mine, not the gate's: I renamed the test target in the first of the two steps that name it, and the assertion only read the step carrying `--ignored`. So the check was reading one of the two places a rename can land. Generalised it to every `--test` target in the job, with a non-vacuity count, and re-ran BOTH placements — each reddens now.

Round 888.decision_summary: CI was red for four commits, and the thing that noticed was me reading the runs by hand
changes_bullets: `mnemosyne-validate` CI has been failing on every push, at BUILD, before a single test ran, and the failure is one missing package: `mnemosyne-server`'s build script runs tonic-build, which shells out to `protoc`, and the hosted runner does not ship one. Both jobs install it now, from the runner's own apt source rather than a third-party action — one less thing to trust, and the version question belongs to prost-build, which takes what Ubuntu ships. The `msrv` job needed it too: `cargo check --workspace` builds the same script.

Found by looking at `gh run list` after the R884-R887 push, not by any gate. The four most recent runs on main were all red — R872, R874, R877, R883 — so this had been the state for at least eleven hours and four commits while local `cargo test --workspace` stayed green the whole time. The local pre-commit and pre-push hooks cannot see it: they run on a machine that HAS protoc.
verification_bullets: The diagnosis is the runner's own words, read from the job log rather than inferred: "Could not find `protoc` ... Error: Custom { kind: NotFound }" from `mnemosyne-server`'s build script. Locally `protoc` is 3.12.4 at /usr/bin/protoc, which is why the same command passes here and has for every round.
Not verified: that the fix works. Only a push settles it, exactly as R886 said of its own workflow, and this commit has not been pushed.

Verified in the same session, and this is the part worth keeping: the R886 workflow RAN on GitHub and was not a hollow green. 7m22s, exit 0, and the log says "36 replays across 23 revisions", "34 replays reproduced their declared digest, 2 blocked as declared". So three things that were open are now observed — GitHub accepts the workflow, `fetch-depth: 0` really does let it extract 23 historical commits, and 23 historical `Cargo.lock` files still resolve against crates.io from a hosted runner, which is the residual risk R880 recorded as UNOBSERVED.

It also closes an R885 carry that was honestly open: the 34 digests were measured on one machine, and nothing proved a path or environment value had not leaked into the store bytes. They reproduce byte-for-byte on GitHub's runner, on different hardware and a different OS image.
carry_forward_bullets: Nothing tells this repo its CI is red. That is the whole finding here and it is not fixed: the gate that catches a hollow workflow (R887) does not catch a workflow that runs and fails, because the result lives on GitHub and nobody here reads it. Four red runs went unnoticed across eleven hours. A local hook cannot answer it either — the hooks pass because this machine has what the runner lacks.

The two workflows install a toolchain the local machine happens to have. Any other build-time system dependency added later will fail the same way, at build, only on CI, and only where someone happens to look.
`actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/cache@v4` are annotated as targeting a deprecated Node.js 20 and are being forced onto Node 24. Both workflows use them. Not a failure yet.

Round 889.decision_summary: The gates needed history and the job that runs them had none; protoc had been hiding that
changes_bullets: `mnemosyne-validate`'s validate job now checks out full history. `cargo test --workspace` includes the R884-R887 declaration gates, and those resolve pinned historical commits — a shallow clone has none of them, so the gates could not run in that job at all. R886 measured this exact constraint and fixed it in the workflow it was writing; the job that runs ALL the tests kept the default depth. My own gate was the thing failing on the first CI run that got far enough to execute it.

Two defects were stacked and the outer one hid the inner one. R888's missing `protoc` killed the workspace build before a single test ran, so these gates had never once executed on CI. Fixing protoc uncovered mine — the msrv job went green in the same run and validate advanced from failing at BUILD to failing inside a test.

The failure now names its cause. A shallow clone made every declaration report `revision does not resolve`, which reads as a corrupt record and sent me hunting; the test asks `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` first and says what is actually wrong. It FAILS rather than skips: a gate that quietly stops asserting where the history is thin is worse than a red one.

New gate `every_job_that_could_run_these_gates_checks_out_full_history` — the check that would have caught this at commit time. It is R887's shape one axis over: R887 asserted the CI path filter covers what a replay reads, this asserts the requirement the gates place on their runner against the runner's own configuration, rather than leaving it remembered. The recogniser defaults to "this command could run these tests" and only backs off on an explicit `--test` or `-p` naming something else, because being wrong in the other direction is what produced a gate that could not run and said nothing.
verification_bullets: 10 green in the file (+1), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace clean.

The shallow predicate discriminates, measured on both sides: a `--depth 1` clone of this repo answers `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` with `true`, this tree with `false`, and in that clone the pinned revision is `fatal: Not a valid object name` — the confusing message the new assertion replaces.

Injections, self-reported. J1 (delete the `fetch-depth: 0` I just added — the R889 defect restored) reddened the new gate alone, naming the file, the job, and `fetch-depth: Some(None)`. J2 (blind the recogniser so no command matches) reddened it on the non-vacuity clause instead, which is the direction that matters: a recogniser that stops matching would otherwise leave the loop asserting nothing while looking thorough.

SELF-REPORTED PROCESS ERROR: I reverted J2 with `git checkout -- <test file>`, which restored the file to its last COMMITTED state and deleted this round's implementation. That is the exact hazard my own notes record from R817 — revert from a copy, never with git checkout, because the round's work is not committed yet. Caught it on the next run (9 passed where 10 were expected), re-applied, re-verified.

NOT verified: that CI is green. Only a push settles it, and this round is the second time in a row that a fix uncovered another failure underneath, so the honest expectation is that the next run may find a third.
carry_forward_bullets: Still nothing tells this repo its CI is red — R888's finding, unchanged. Two rounds have now been spent on failures that a human reading `gh run list` found, and nothing in the repo asks that question.

`fetch-depth: 0` makes the validate job clone the full history on every push and PR. That is a real cost paid by every run for the benefit of gates that only some changes touch; it was not measured against a partial-depth alternative.
The gates read the workflow, not GitHub's schema, so a file that satisfies all four could still be rejected for a key GitHub does not recognise.

Round 890.decision_summary: The repo could not see its own red CI, and a hook can only see the commit before
changes_bullets: Closed the finding R888 and R889 left open: nothing in this repo could see a red CI, and both of those rounds were defects a human found by typing `gh run list`. Two halves, because one mechanism cannot cover it.

The pre-push hook now reports the CI state of the commit the push builds ON — `origin/main` as this clone last saw it. That is the moment it matters most: about to stack more work on a published base that may already be failing. It would have spoken on the second of the four red pushes rather than the fifth.

It REPORTS and never blocks, and the history is what argues for that rather than a wish to be lenient: the R888 and R889 pushes were both made deliberately while CI was red, in order to fix it. A gate would have been wrong both times. What was missing was knowledge, not restraint.

`RULEBOOK.md` takes the half a hook structurally cannot: reading the run the push you JUST made started. The hook can only ever see the previous commit's runs, so a failure introduced by the final push of a session is invisible to it until the next session. That is stated in both places rather than left as a gap someone rediscovers.

Every branch prints — gh missing, gh unreachable, no `origin/main` ref, no runs recorded. A check that goes quiet when it cannot answer is indistinguishable from one that answered "fine", which is the shape of the failure this whole thing is about.
verification_bullets: All four branches exercised against the real `gh`, not reasoned about. GREEN: `origin/main` 99eda22 reports `evidence-replay completed success` and `mnemosyne-validate completed success`, and the red clause does not fire. RED: the same query against b4478b8 — a commit whose run genuinely failed an hour ago — returns `mnemosyne-validate completed failure` and the red clause fires. So the discriminating input is real data from this repository, not a fixture.

Degraded paths, each forced: `gh` absent (PATH without /usr/bin) prints the NOTE and proceeds; `gh` unable to reach GitHub (GH_HOST=nonexistent.invalid) exits nonzero and takes the NOTE branch without blocking; a missing ref (`origin/nonexistent-branch`) yields an empty base and takes its own NOTE. None of them fail the push, and none of them stay silent.

Two environment facts measured rather than assumed, and both changed the implementation: this `gh` has no `--commit` or `--branch` flag, so the run list is filtered client-side by `headSha`; and `jq` is not installed on this machine, so the filter uses gh's built-in `-q` instead.
1343 green, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace clean.

Not verified: that the hook behaves identically on a machine other than this one. It depends on `gh`'s JSON field names, and this version already lacks flags a newer one has — the degraded branches are what keep that from being a push-blocking problem.
carry_forward_bullets: The hook is not gated by a test. Nothing asserts it still contains this check, the same way nothing asserts any other line of it; deleting the block would be silent. Whether the hooks themselves deserve gating is a question this round did not open.

It reports the runs of `origin/main` as the local clone last saw it. A stale ref reports stale runs, and nothing here fetches first — adding a network fetch to every push was not worth it, but the staleness is real.

`actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/cache@v4` are annotated on every run as targeting a deprecated Node.js 20, forced onto Node 24. Both workflows use them. Not a failure yet, and not touched here: bumping a major action version without reading its changelog is how a working CI becomes a broken one.

Round 891.decision_summary: R891 (BUILD — the map axis reaches the work-list). The authoring frontier (R589) describes itself as "every coverage gap an unattended generate-gate-repair loop pulls its next work from", JOINed from the scattered projections. THE MAP AXIS WAS NEVER IN THAT JOIN. It was built afterwards and in pieces — R697 made the edges store facts declared by a rule, R710 added costs, R722 added guards — and its read arrived only at R875, three hundred rounds after the frontier was written. None of those rounds reached back. R875 even listed the reads it had NOT reached (report-playable-world, report-quest-graph, the consumer's own bake) and the loop's work source was not on that list, because nobody was looking at it. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE FAILURE CLASS THIS SUBSTRATE EXISTS TO REMOVE: a store can register places with no way between any of them, and the work-list reports its other gaps and stays SILENT on this one — an absence that reads as health. Measured on the deepest end-to-end authored narrative this repo holds, the R873 dnd-quest store: 136 facts, 25 entities, 4 world-lines, 56 order nodes, four authored quest-giver surfaces, and the frontier's answer says nothing about whether a player can walk anywhere. THE FIX IS A JOIN, NOT A NEW DERIVATION: map_frontier calls transition_map, so the frontier, the read and the gate share one answer to "what is an edge" — the SSOT shape R875 established in the other direction. What it adds is the subtraction nobody had written: the adjacency predicate declares its leg kinds (R701 subject_kind / object_entity_kind), those kinds admit a registered entity set under the R738 subkind resolver, and the places that set holds MINUS the map's nodes are the authoring work. Core never learns the word "place" — the rule names the predicate, the predicate names its kinds, and the consumer's vocabulary stays the consumer's (invariant 4). THE THIRD STATE IS THE POINT, NOT A DETAIL. Zero transition rules is not zero map work: with no rule there is no declared adjacency predicate and the store genuinely cannot know which facts are edges, so the render says that sentence rather than omitting the section (R864). The same discipline one level down: when the adjacency predicate declares no leg kind, the registered place set cannot be asked for, and place_kinds being empty carries that discriminator rather than a parallel bool free to drift from it. An empty list that means "unaskable" must never render like an empty list that means "complete" — omitting the axis is precisely how it stayed invisible for three hundred rounds. ALSO CORRECTED IN THIS ROUND, against my own first draft: costs and guards keyed to a non-edge do NOT belong here. They are already continuity violations the gate rejects and the R875 read echoes, and this report is the never-gated todo surface (R442) — counting a defect as authoring work conflates two categories and gives the datum a third home. Removing them also removed the only line of the derivation no test covered.
changes_bullets: validate/continuity.rs: `map_frontier(store, rules)` — a pure read DERIVED from `transition_map` (R875) rather than re-deriving edges, so the frontier cannot disagree with the read about what an edge is. Per declared map it resolves the adjacency predicate's `subject_kind` / `object_entity_kind` (R701) and subtracts the map's node set from every registered entity those kinds admit under `is_kind_or_subkind` (the R738 one resolver). New `MapFrontierReport` / `MapFrontierView`.

ops/lib.rs: `authoring_frontier_report` gains a `rules_override` parameter and resolves the narrative-rules artifact through the SAME resolver the gate and `transition_map_report` use — the rule is what DECLARES the adjacency predicate, which core must not know (invariant 4). The report gains `map_frontier`, and `total_gaps` absorbs its count.

cli/main.rs: `report-authoring-frontier` gains `--rules <path>` and renders the axis, with the no-transition-rule case given its OWN sentence rather than an omitted section. mcp/main.rs: `rules_path` arg + the tool description states the third state explicitly.

Deliberately NOT carried: costs/guards keyed to a non-edge. They are already continuity VIOLATIONS (`EdgeCostNotAnEdge` / `EdgeGuardNotAnEdge`, R710/R722) that `transition_map` echoes, and this report is the never-gated todo surface — counting a defect as authoring work conflates the categories and gives the datum a third home to drift in. A first draft carried them; removing them also removed the only untested line in the derivation.
verification_bullets: Measured BEFORE writing code, on the deepest end-to-end authored narrative this repo has (the R873 dnd-quest fixture rebuilt from tracked inputs: 136 facts, 25 entities, 4 world-lines, 56 order nodes): `report-authoring-frontier --telling delve` reports 6 gaps across dangling setups and one unresolved quest, and says NOTHING about the map. `report-transition-map` on the same store returns `transition_rules: 0`. Source-confirmed, not inferred: the JOIN in `authoring_frontier_report` reaches scene/fact structure, payoff (R442), quest (R568) and disclosure (R507), and no map arm exists in it.
1347 workspace tests green under --no-fail-fast (+4, 130 binaries, 0 failed); clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --all --check clean.

The derivation's fixture is built through the REAL write path (`import_facts`), which rejected two drafts before the assertion was reachable (a typed subject absent from the fact's entities list) — the R873 lesson that a struct-mutated fixture can encode a store the mutate API would refuse.

5 injections, each anchor asserted `count == 1`, each restored from a COPY. J1 (drop the kind filter) reddens the unit test and the CLI smoke — both fixtures hold a non-place entity. J2 (exact kind instead of subkind) reddens the unit test ALONE and correctly leaves the CLI smoke green, because only the unit fixture holds a subkind place. J3 (stop subtracting the map's nodes) reddens both. J4 (alter the no-rule sentence) reddens the third-state CLI test alone. J5 (drop the map gaps from the frontier total) reddens the CLI total alone.

MY INJECTION HARNESS WAS DEFECTIVE AND I REPORT THE INVALID RUN: `shutil.copy2` restores the pre-injection MTIME, so cargo judged the restored file up-to-date and re-ran the artifact built for the PREVIOUS injection. J4 and J5 and the final green check were all reading J3's binary. Caught because the closing "confirming green" was red on a clean tree. Harness fixed to touch the file after restore; all five re-run from fresh builds, and only those results are counted.

ONE OF MY OWN ASSERTIONS WAS VACUOUS AND WAS FOUND BY ASKING WHAT J5 WOULD REDDEN: the CLI smoke first asserted `total_gaps >= 1`, which holds with the map gap dropped entirely — that workspace declares no canon order, so its one scene is already an unordered gap. Replaced with the exact `== 2`, which is what J5 now reddens.
carry_forward_bullets: The axis still has NO dogfood corpus in this repo. Round 892.decision_summary: R892 (MEASUREMENT, code 0 — the seam I suspected was under-built is not, and my own NEXT was the speculation). R891 closed the map axis's work-list gap and left a NEXT that leaned on R875's carry line: report-playable-world hands a consumer an unweighted graph, so measure whether making the consumer JOIN two reads is a hidden cost R875 named and walked past. MEASURED, THE ANSWER IS THAT R875 WAS RIGHT AND MY NEXT WAS WRONG. The playable world is a scene walk plus disclosure pointers; the map is a place graph; these are two axes, and the boundary between them is not a missing feature. The join key exists and is type-correct: MapLocator.object is a registered entity and every one in the corpus is place-kind, which is the same entity space the map's nodes live in. THE REAL NUMBER IS THAT THE KEY IS PRESENT ON 4.4 PERCENT OF LOCATORS — 16 of 361, being 4 authored surfaces across 4 world-lines — so for 345 pointers a runtime holds a scene and no place. THAT IS A DATA FACT, NOT A SUBSTRATE FACT, and the distinction is the whole round: a derived seat has no authored surface because the author never placed one, which is exactly what an authored surface MEANS. I THEN CHASED THE ONE HYPOTHESIS THAT WOULD HAVE MADE IT A SUBSTRATE FACT, AND THE MACHINE KILLED IT. If scene_cast (R757) bound a scene to a place, the join would be total rather than 4.4 percent, and the absence of a read composing them would be ours. It does not. Its closed modality vocabulary is observed / guessed / told / remembered — an EPISTEMIC axis, how a character KNOWS, carried with can_answer and a quote. A scene's PLACE is not a thing that vocabulary can say, and it is not a thing the store can know at all: deriving it would be core inventing domain semantics, which invariant 4 forbids. So the narrative half of the scene-place seam is NOT OURS TO BUILD, and the half that is ours R891 already built. THE PROBE FOUND A SECOND CAUSE I WAS NOT LOOKING FOR: scene_cast's anchor is a ContentAnchor pinning a quote by sha256 against the section's content, and this corpus has no prose — the continuity gate says so itself. So 0 of 56 sections carry a cast because the primitive needs a manuscript a fact-first store does not have, not because an author skipped it. Counting that emptiness as authorial neglect would have been the wrong reading, and it is the reading I would have written from a grep. THE ROUND'S VALUE IS THE BUILD THAT DID NOT HAPPEN. R891's NEXT proposed carrying edge references into report-playable-world; on this measurement that would have duplicated a join the consumer can already make, given the axis a second home to drift in, and asserted a scoping this substrate does not perform.
changes_bullets: No code. This round's output is numbers and a named cause, and its conclusion is that the build my own R891 `NEXT` proposed must NOT happen.
verification_bullets: `report-playable-world --telling delve` on the R873 dnd-quest store (rebuilt from tracked inputs): per world-line the payload is `manuscript` + `locators` and nothing else — zero edges, zero places, by construction.

The only possible join key to the map is `MapLocator.object`, and it is present on 16 of 361 locators (4.4 percent): 4 authored surfaces x 4 world-lines. All 4 objects ARE `place`-kind entities, so the join is type-correct exactly where it exists; for the other 345 the locator carries a scene and no place.

I hypothesised `scene_cast` (R757) was the missing scene-to-place binding and MEASURED IT INSTEAD OF ASSUMING: the write path rejects `modality: "present"` and names its closed vocabulary — `observed | guessed | told | remembered`. That is an EPISTEMIC axis (how a character knows), carried with `can_answer` and a prose-anchored quote. It answers "who is in this scene and how do they know", never "where is this scene". Mechanically it does reach the read (`ManuscriptScene.scene_cast` is populated from the store and serialized), but it is the wrong axis.

The same probe found a second reason it is empty here: `anchor` is a `ContentAnchor` struct carrying a quote pinned by sha256 against the section's content, and this corpus holds no prose — the continuity gate says so in its own words ("0 unverifiable — an evidence section holds no prose"). So `scene_cast` is 0 of 56 sections not by authorial omission but because the primitive needs a manuscript this fact-first store does not carry.

Two of my own guesses were wrong and the machine corrected both, which is the reason this round ran the verbs instead of reading them: `modality: "present"` (the vocabulary is epistemic) and `anchor: ""` (it is a struct, not a string).
carry_forward_bullets: The map axis still has NO dogfood corpus (the R891 carry, unchanged and now sharper). Authoring edges into the dnd-quest fixture is NOT available: it is a frozen blind-author record plus a provenance-documented migration, and inventing map content into it would destroy the evidence it exists to be.
Whether a per-world map is worth having stays open on its own merits (R696 review finding 6, deferred at R875). This round did not test it; it tested whether the SEAM was under-built, and it is not.

The prose finding is bigger than this round and is not chased here: a fact-first store with no manuscript cannot use any primitive that pins a quote. `scene_cast` is one such primitive; whether there are others was not enumerated.

Round 893.decision_summary: R893 (BUILD — the deprecation was visible on every run for months, and nothing here could read a warning). The owner picked this scope from the two ungated alternatives R892 left. BOTH ACTIONS THIS REPO USES DECLARE THE DEPRECATED NODE 20 RUNTIME: checkout@v4 and cache@v4 carry `runs.using: node20`, GitHub deprecated it on 2025-09-19, and the runners now force them onto Node 24 regardless. The fix is a version bump, and the version was MEASURED rather than taken off the announcement — node24 begins at checkout v5 and cache v5, read from each tag's own `action.yml`, and no v4 patch has it, including the v4.4.0 published the same day as the newer lines. The target is checkout v7 / cache v6, with every intervening major's changelog read against what these workflows actually do rather than skipped: v6's credential-file change touches nothing here, v7's fork-PR blocking applies to `pull_request_target` and `workflow_run` which neither workflow uses, and both need a runner >= 2.327.1 which this repo's hosted runner satisfies at a measured 2.336.0. THE BUMP IS THE SMALL HALF. The reason it sat is that R890 taught this repo to read a CI CONCLUSION, and a conclusion is one word: every run went green while its ANNOTATIONS said this, back to the oldest run GitHub still lists (2026-05-07), where the wording is still the earlier pre-forcing form — so the message itself escalated and nothing here noticed that either. That is R887's green-and-hollow class one axis over: not a workflow that passes without doing anything, but a workflow that does its work and tells you something no one collects. SO THE PRE-PUSH HOOK NOW REPORTS ANNOTATIONS ALONGSIDE THE CONCLUSION, report-only for R890's reason — the R888 and R889 pushes were both made deliberately into a red CI in order to fix it, and a gate would have been wrong both times. A THIRD PLACE CARRIED THE SAME DEFECT AND IT FACES OUTWARD: the copy-paste CI snippets in README.md, README.ko.md and SCHEMA_GUIDE.md hand consumers checkout@v4, so anyone pasting ours inherits the warning. Bumped in the same change, because a half-cleanup leaves the defect alive precisely where this project ships it. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT is a tree-local gate asserting that an action's runtime is current: that fact does not live in this tree, it lives upstream and arrives only as an annotation, so the mechanism for this class IS making the annotation legible.
changes_bullets: `.github/workflows/mnemosyne-validate.yml` + `.github/workflows/evidence-replay.yml`: `actions/checkout@v4` -> `@v7` (3 sites), `actions/cache@v4` -> `@v6` (3 sites). The reading behind the target versions is recorded once, in the primary workflow; the other file points at it rather than repeating it.

`.githooks/pre-push`: the CI report block (R890) now reads the base commit's ANNOTATIONS as well as its conclusion. Distinct annotations are printed with their level, headed by `<n> distinct of <m> reported` so a per-check-run read that falls short of the declared count is visible rather than passing as the whole story. Report-only, unchanged from R890's semantics and for R890's reason.

`README.md`, `README.ko.md`, `docs/SCHEMA_GUIDE.md`: the copy-paste CI snippets we hand to consumers recommended `actions/checkout@v4`. Bumped with the workflows — a consumer who pastes ours inherits whatever we shipped, and this one shipped a deprecation warning.
`RULEBOOK.md`: the PUSH gate's "read the run it started" clause now says a green conclusion is not the whole of what the run said.

NOT BUILT, on purpose: a local gate asserting that an action's runtime is current. That fact does not live in this tree — it lives upstream and arrives here only as a GitHub annotation, so a tree-local assertion could only restate the version literal back to itself. Making the annotation legible IS the mechanism for this class, and that is the hook change above.
verification_bullets: The target versions were MEASURED from each tag's own `action.yml`, not read off the blog post: `runs.using` is `node20` for checkout v4 / v4.4.0 and for cache v4 / v4.2.4, and `node24` from checkout v5 and cache v5 onward (v5, v5.1.0, v6.1.0, v7, v7.0.1 for checkout; v5, v5.1.0, v6, v6.1.0 for cache). The v4 lines never got a node24 build, including the v4.4.0 published 2026-07-20 alongside the newer lines, so no patch-level bump exists that fixes this.

Every major between the minimum fix and the chosen target was read rather than skipped, and each was checked against what these workflows actually do. checkout v6 persists credentials to a separate file (nothing here uses git credentials after checkout — no push, no submodule, no private dependency); v7 blocks fork-PR checkout for `pull_request_target` and `workflow_run` (neither trigger exists in either workflow) and v7.0.1 skips that check when `ref` is defaulted, which is the case at all three sites; cache v6 is an ESM migration. checkout v5.0.0 and cache v5.0.0 both declare a minimum runner of 2.327.1.
That runner floor was MEASURED, not assumed: the last green run's job log reports `Current runner version: '2.336.0'` on this repo's GitHub-hosted runner.

How long it sat, measured: the oldest run GitHub still lists for this repo (2026-05-07) already carries a Node 20 annotation, and its wording is the earlier "are running on Node.js 20 and may..." form. The message escalated to "are being forced to run on Node.js 24" somewhere in between. Nothing in this repo read either version of it. Every commit sampled across the last 100 runs carries the annotation; the count is 2 or 4 depending on how many jobs ran.

The R887 workflow gates still pass (10 tests) and are version-agnostic by construction, which was checked in the source rather than inferred from the green: they match `uses` with `starts_with("actions/checkout")` and assert on `with.fetch-depth`, so the bump cannot have neutered them.

The hook's new block was run against real data, not a fixture: `pre-push: CI annotations on 794ad8cb — 1 distinct of 2 reported:` followed by the Node 20 warning. The dedup is load-bearing — the same annotation is emitted once per job.

Four injections, each forcing one branch of the new block, each reverted from a saved copy: J1 (select filter raised past any real count) prints `no CI annotations on 794ad8cb`; J2 (`origin/main` temporarily pointed at a locally fabricated commit the remote has never seen, then restored) prints `no CI runs recorded` AND `could not list check runs ... annotations unknown`; J3 (`GH_TOKEN` set to an invalid token) takes both NOTE branches without blocking; J4 (per-check-run endpoint pointed at a nonexistent path) prints one NOTE per check run plus `reports 2 annotation(s), none readable`. No branch is silent and none blocks the push.
1347 green, clippy `-D warnings` clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace clean (entries 639, T1 orphan 0, T3 reject 0).

NOT VERIFIED, and only a push can: that GitHub accepts checkout v7 / cache v6 in these workflows and that the annotation disappears. The bump is unobserved until the next run, which is exactly the thing the RULEBOOK clause added here says to go read.

NOT DISCRIMINATED by real data: the zero-annotation branch. Every run in this repo's visible history is annotated, so there is no commit to point the check at that would exercise it; J1 forced it instead. The bump itself should produce the first real one.
carry_forward_bullets: The hooks are still not covered by a test (R890's carry, unchanged and now carrying more): deleting this block would be silent, exactly as deleting R890's would be. Whether the hooks themselves deserve gating stays unopened.

Annotations are read one page per check run. The declared count is printed next to the distinct count so a shortfall shows, but a check run emitting more than a page of them would be reported short rather than fully.

The floating major tags mean the action content can change under this repo without a commit here. SHA pinning was considered and NOT adopted: nothing in this tree would ever update a pin, and an unmaintained pin is a worse failure than a moving first-party tag. Named rather than silently chosen.

The hook makes the next deprecation of this class VISIBLE. Nothing makes anyone act on it, and by R890's own argument nothing should block on it — the gap between "printed" and "read" is now the whole remaining exposure for this class.
`actions/checkout` and `actions/cache` are the only actions either workflow uses. If a third is ever added, nothing here checks its runtime; the annotation is still the only authority.

Round 894.decision_summary: R894 (MEASUREMENT, code 0 — I ran the verbs R892 had only read, and the first one refuted R892). R892 closed by naming an un-enumerated carry: a fact-first store holding no prose cannot use any primitive that pins a quote, `scene_cast` is one such primitive, and the rest were never counted. THIS ROUND COUNTED THEM, AND THE COUNT STARTS BY OVERTURNING THE EXAMPLE. Run against the very corpus R892 measured — R873's dnd-quest fixture, 56 sections, 0 with prose — `import-scene-cast` APPLIES. It never consults the section's `content_excerpt`; the quote it carries is a `ContentExcerpt` whose invariant (R759) is a non-blank source, non-blank text, and a hash the store computes for itself, with nothing resolving it against prose the store holds. So `scene_cast` is 0 of 56 in that corpus because THE AUTHOR DID NOT WRITE ONE, which is the reading R892 explicitly ruled out. R892 warned that a grep would have misread this and then made the mirror-image error: it read the TYPE, saw a content anchor, and concluded a block the machine does not enforce. THE CLASS IS REAL BUT IT HAS TWO MEMBERS, NOT ONE, AND NEITHER IS `scene_cast`. `import_ladders` (R765/R815) rejects a rung anchored into a section carrying no `content_excerpt`, and `import_evidence_reviews` (R806) rejects an affirmation against a section holding no prose — both fail loud, both name the cause, and both say in their own message that this is a reject and never a skip so the check cannot go vacuous. AND THE CLASS COLLAPSES FURTHER: one `import-content-excerpts` call putting 37 characters of prose on one section made BOTH rejected inputs apply unchanged. There is one prerequisite, one verb supplies it, and the verb requires nothing of the store. `import_epub_excerpts` is not a member at all — it refreshes a spec `normative_excerpt` and reports narrative sections as unmatched. So the correct statement is NOT that a prose-less store cannot use quote-pinning primitives; it is that two primitives are gated on prose being in the store, and nothing about a fact-first corpus prevents putting it there. WHAT THE ROUND FOUND WITHOUT LOOKING FOR IT is on the read side: `validate-content-drift` on this corpus prints `sections=56` and `drift: total=0`, where `sections` is the store's section count and not the number carrying an excerpt. Zero of the 56 hold prose. Every number is true and the line reads as coverage — the same zero-that-cannot-say-which-thing-it-means that R891 printed a sentence for and R864 named. That is a defect, it is not fixed here because this round is a measurement, and it is the next round of this session.
changes_bullets: No code. The output is an enumeration, a measurement of each member against the corpus R892 drew its conclusion from, and the RETRACTION of that conclusion.

One defect found and NOT fixed here (it is the next round's, this session): `validate-content-drift` cannot distinguish "no prose drifted" from "no prose exists". Naming it in a MEASUREMENT round rather than fixing it in passing keeps the two round types honest; deferring it past this session would not be acceptable.
verification_bullets: The corpus is R873's dnd-quest fixture rebuilt from tracked inputs exactly as `dnd_quest_map_seam_smoke.rs` rebuilds it (frozen `sections.json` / `order.json` / `narrative-rules.json` plus the fixture `facts.json`): 56 sections, 136 facts, and MEASURED 0 content_excerpt, 0 scene_cast, 0 ladder. The same store R891 and R892 measured.

`import-scene-cast` against that store: APPLIED, exit 0, one section's cast written. It does not consult `section.content_excerpt` at all — the quote it carries is validated by `validate_content_excerpt` (R759) for a non-blank source, non-blank text, and a hash the store itself computes, and nothing resolves it against the section's prose. R892's stated cause is REFUTED by its own corpus.

`import-ladders` against the same store: REJECTED, naming the cause — "anchors a rung into a section carrying no content_excerpt ... this is a reject, never a skip, so the check is never silently vacuous".
`import-evidence-reviews` against the same store: REJECTED, same shape — "carries no content_excerpt — nothing to affirm against".

THE DISCRIMINATING STEP: `import-content-excerpts` applied 37 characters of prose to one section (accepted; the store required nothing of itself to take it), and then the SAME two rejected inputs both applied. So the block is one prerequisite with one supplier, not a property of the store class.

`import-epub-excerpts` is a different axis, not a member: it refreshes a section's `normative_excerpt` (the spec corpus) and reports every narrative section as unmatched, erroring "no entry matched a refreshable excerpt" rather than silently no-opping.

READ SIDE, measured on a clean rebuild: `report-playthrough-manuscript --world claim` renders in full — 36 scenes, every fact one-liner, `unplaced=0` — so the north-star read does not want prose at all. `report-playthrough-manuscript --world delve` fails loud on an unregistered world rather than rendering empty, which is the behavior the third-state rule asks for.

`validate-content-drift` on the same store prints `sections=56 severity=reject unrevalidatable=0` and `drift: total=0`. Read in the source: `sections` is `store.sections.len()`, not the number carrying an excerpt, and the scan iterates sections and finds nothing to check. Every number is true and the reader is told 56 sections are clean when 0 of them hold prose.

NOT MEASURED: whether any primitive outside `mnemosyne-atomic`'s import surface pins a quote. The enumeration is of the atomic write layer plus its CLI verbs, which is where R892's claim was made; the engine's `Passage` resolution is a read path and was not swept.
carry_forward_bullets: `validate-content-drift` reports section COUNT where a reader hears coverage. The next round of this session fixes it; the general shape (a zero that cannot say which of two things it means) is the one R891 and R864 already named, now found in a third verb.

The two rejecting primitives are gated on prose being IN THE STORE, and `import-content-excerpts` will accept any text unless the caller passes `--grounding-source`. So the substrate does not stop an author from inventing prose into a frozen record — the R892 objection to authoring into the dnd fixture stands, but it is an EVIDENCE argument, not a substrate one, and this round is why the difference is now stated.
The engine-side read path (`Passage`, `PrefixSlices`) was not swept for the same question. If a consumer's render is what actually needs prose, that answer is in the engine, not here.

Round 895.decision_summary: R895 (BUILD — an empty finding list answered two questions and said the same word to both). R894 measured a 56-section store carrying no prose at all and watched `validate-content-drift` report `sections=56 ... drift: total=0`. Every number in that line is true and the line as a whole reads as coverage: `sections` is the store's section count, not the number of sections the scan could examine, and the empty finding list means BOTH "every cache still hashes to its pin" and "there was no cache to hash". THE FIX IS THE SCAN REPORTING ITS OWN REACH, derived from the walk that already produces the violations. `scan_content_drift` now returns an `ExcerptCensus` alongside them — how many caches it examined, how many it skipped as unrevalidatable, and how many sections carry a cache at all — and when nothing was examined the CLI stops printing a bare zero and prints the sentence instead. A SECOND WALK WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WRONG SHAPE: two passes, one answering "what is wrong" and one answering "how much did you look at", are free to drift apart, which is the half-enforced class this project already refuses elsewhere. THE ROUND FOUND A SECOND, OLDER DRIFT WHILE WIRING IT. The `unrevalidatable` number the CLI printed came from `excerpt_hash_backfill_report` (R402), which counts `normative_excerpt` and nothing else, while this scan has covered three excerpt kinds since R756 and R757 generalized it. So a context number narrower than the thing it sat beside had been reporting 0 for any store whose only hashless caches were narrative — full coverage, by omission. It now comes from the census. The R402 report keeps its verb: it answers which spec excerpts need a hash backfilled, which is a different question and legitimately a different number. AND THE STORE THIS REPOSITORY KEEPS IS IN THE SAME STATE — 5 sections, 0 with an excerpt — so the verb has been answering "clean" here for its whole life, to a reader who had to type it, since it is in neither CI workflow. That last part is named and NOT fixed here: whether this scan should gate a push is a decision about gating, not a rider on a reporting fix.
changes_bullets: `mnemosyne-validate::scan_content_drift` returns a `ContentDriftScan` — the violations plus an `ExcerptCensus` (examined / unrevalidatable / sections_with_excerpt) counted by the SAME walk. Signature changed in place with every caller updated in the same change; the tests route through one `drift()` helper so what they assert on did not move.

`validate-content-drift` prints `with_excerpt=N` in its header and, when nothing was examined, replaces the bare `drift: total=0` with a sentence naming which zero it is. `--json` gains `sections_with_excerpt` and `examined_count`.

The CLI's `unrevalidatable` number now comes from the census instead of `excerpt_hash_backfill_report()`. That report counts `normative_excerpt` only and this scan has covered three kinds since R756/R757, so the number beside the scan was narrower than the scan. The R402 report keeps its own verb and its own question.
Two stale doc claims corrected in the same change: the module header's "the CLI surfaces that count separately for context", and the smoke test's scope list.
verification_bullets: On the corpus that found it — R894's dnd-quest rebuild, 56 sections, 0 with prose — the verb now prints `sections=56 with_excerpt=0` and `drift: total=0 over 0 excerpt(s) examined — 0 of 56 section(s) carry an excerpt cache, so this scan compared NOTHING`. Before this round the whole of its answer was `sections=56 ... drift: total=0`.

THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN STORE IS IN THE SAME STATE AND WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: 5 sections, `with_excerpt=0`. `validate-content-drift` has been answering "clean" here for as long as it has existed, and it is not in either CI workflow, so that answer was only ever read by a person asking for it by hand.

The discriminating unit test is a PAIR, not an assertion that the census is populated: two stores whose violation lists are both empty — one carrying two clean caches, one carrying none — must not produce the same census. The old return type could not express the difference at all.

Census semantics pinned by two more unit tests: a drifted cache still counts as `examined` (otherwise the count collapses exactly when the scan works hardest), and a section carrying one hashed normative excerpt plus a hashless content excerpt and a hashless scene quote splits 1 examined / 2 unrevalidatable (a normative-only count would say 0 and read as full coverage).

CLI arms both ways: a store with no excerpts prints the sentence and exits 0 (nothing to check must not gate), and the existing three-excerpt fixture prints `sections=3 with_excerpt=3` and `drift: total=1 over 2 excerpt(s) examined` and must NOT contain the `nothing to check` wording.

Four injections, each reverted from a saved copy, each hitting exactly one test: J1 (drifted caches stop counting as examined) fails `a_drifted_cache_still_counts_as_examined`; J2 (the third-state branch made unreachable) fails the no-excerpt CLI arm; J3 (`sections_with_excerpt` becomes the section count) fails the discriminating pair; J4 (`unrevalidatable` counted for the normative kind only) fails the three-kind census test. 1 failed / 15 passed in each of the three unit runs, 1 failed / 4 passed in the CLI run.
1352 green (+5), clippy `-D warnings` clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace clean.
NOT DONE: `validate-content-drift` is still not run by either CI workflow. Wiring it in is a separate decision about what gates a push, not a rider on a reporting fix.
carry_forward_bullets: The verb is absent from `mnemosyne-validate.yml`, so nothing runs it on a push. A scan that now reports its own reach still reports it to no one on a schedule; whether it belongs in CI is an unopened question about gating, and this round deliberately did not answer it in passing.

`report-excerpt-hash-backfill` (R402) still answers the narrower normative-only question, and the two numbers will legitimately differ on any store carrying narrative excerpts. That is two questions, not two answers to one — but a reader comparing them without knowing that will misread it.
The same "which zero is this" audit was not run over the other report and validate verbs. R891 fixed it for transition rules, R895 for content drift; nothing has swept the surface for the rest.

Round 896.decision_summary: R896 (BUILD — the audit R895 left, and the test that finds this class is only half a method). R895's carry asked whether other verbs share the defect it fixed: a zero that cannot say whether nothing is wrong or nothing was there. THE TEST IS MECHANICAL — run every verb on a rich store and on an empty one and compare byte for byte, because two different states rendering the same words IS the defect. All 31 `report-*` / `validate-*` verbs were run on R873's dnd-quest corpus and on this repository's own store: 16 differ, 6 need an argument, 9 came back byte-identical. AND SEVEN OF THOSE NINE ARE NOT DEFECTS. They read inputs NEITHER store holds — pre-v5 bindings, confirmation events, meters, unset config, transition rules — so identical output is identical state, correctly reported. The byte-identical test finds CANDIDATES; a candidate is only a defect once you have shown the two stores differ in the input that verb actually reads, and this round nearly recorded seven that do not. `report-transition-map` is the sharpest of them: it matches because R891 gave it the honest "the store cannot know which facts are edges" sentence, so byte-identical there is the signature of a verb that is already right. TWO SURVIVED AND ARE FIXED. `report-entity-kind-migration` said "0 unregistered kinds — every in-use kind is registered" in the same words on a store with 25 entities and a store with none; it now prints the store's entity count and, at zero, says nothing was checked. `report-excerpt-hash-backfill` — the R402 report R895 named while taking its number away — said "0 excerpt(s) lack a text_sha256" identically whether every excerpt is hashed or no excerpt exists; it now prints `N of M`, and the discriminator had to be CONSTRUCTED because neither real store carries a normative excerpt. AND MY FIRST FIX WAS WRONG IN THE WAY THIS ROUND IS ABOUT. The entity-kind branch reached for the report's `total_entities`, a name that says store total and a value that counts entities naming an UNREGISTERED kind — zero by construction on exactly the branch that wanted a denominator. Re-running the comparison printed "over 0 entity(ies)" on the 25-entity store; the field is renamed `entities_naming_an_unregistered_kind` and a real count added. A misleading name produced a fix that looked like a fix and measured nothing, which is the same failure one layer up from the zeros this round went hunting.

7 OF THOSE 9 ARE NOT DEFECTS AND THE METHOD SAID SO ONLY AFTER THE SECOND STEP. `report-binding-migration`, `report-confirmation`, `report-parameter-economy`, `validate-confirmation`, `validate-spec-drift`, `validate-verifies-linkage` and `report-transition-map` read inputs NEITHER store holds (pre-v5 bindings, confirmation events, meters, unset config, transition rules), so identical output is identical state correctly reported. `report-transition-map` is the sharpest case: it is byte-identical BECAUSE R891 gave it the honest "the store cannot know which facts are edges" sentence, so here byte-identical is the signature of a correct verb.

CONFIRMED, each against an input that genuinely differs: `report-entity-kind-migration` printed "0 unregistered kinds — every in-use kind is registered" identically on a store with 25 entities and a store with none. `report-excerpt-hash-backfill` needed a constructed pair, because neither real store carries a normative excerpt: two sections with hashed excerpts vs two sections with none produced the same "0 excerpt(s) lack a text_sha256".

Re-running the comparison printed "over 0 entity(ies)" on the 25-entity store. Renamed, and a real count added.
Both comparisons re-run after the fix: entity-kind now differs (25 vs 0), backfill now differs (`0 of 2` vs `0 of 0` plus its sentence).

Round 897.decision_summary: R897 (DEBT — the number Round 896 owed, and the carry it named on the wrong axis). Round 896 left one debt in the open: its entry recorded the sweep as 16 differ / 6 needing an argument / 9 byte-identical, the ledger is frozen, and so the correction had to arrive as prose in a later entry. IT IS NOT A TYPO, IT IS A TRIPLE THAT DESCRIBES NO MOMENT. Measured twice rather than reconstructed — at HEAD and again at 443c667 in a separate worktree — the sweep is 16 / 8 / 7 after that round's fixes and 15 / 9 / 7 before them. Round 896 took its differ count from after, its byte-identical count from before, and its argument count from neither: the same bullet enumerates SEVEN verb names while calling them six. Writing a number from memory instead of from the machine is the failure that round went hunting, one layer up from the zeros it found. AND THE MOVEMENT FROM 9 TO 8 IS THE THESIS SURVIVING ITS OWN FIX. Only `report-entity-kind-migration` left the byte-identical set; `report-excerpt-hash-backfill` is still byte-identical on the two real stores AFTER being fixed, and correctly so — both print `0 of 0` and the sentence saying no section carries a normative excerpt, because the two stores are genuinely in the same state. The fix made it say WHICH zero without making it differ. Byte-identical remained a candidate, not a defect, even for the verb the round repaired. THE SECOND CARRY IS DISCHARGED FOR 5 OF 7 AND CORRECTED FOR THE OTHER 2. Round 896 said the seven argument-taking verbs were "missing work rather than impossible work" because the dnd corpus has a telling and a frame. Run here on that corpus, five of them do exactly what that predicted: disclosure coverage over 136 facts, a 4-quest graph across 4 worlds, a playable world of 36 scenes and 94 locators, entity views of 32 and 12 facts, a frame view holding 41 at one coordinate and 1 at the same coordinate through another frame. BUT `validate-render-fidelity` AND `validate-disclosure-leak` ARE NOT DISCRIMINATED BY A TELLING OR A FRAME. Their input is `--against <re-extracted store>`, an artifact outside the store entirely, so the claim was checked against the wrong axis — and this tree's only tracked instance does not load: schema 23, five predicates still declaring `object_kind: scalar`, twenty-one facts carrying `{kind:value}` objects, shapes Round 708 removed. The verb is blameless and loud, naming every offending id. What rotted is the record: the same rot Round 873 repaired on the AUTHOR half of this experiment and never reached on the EXTRACT half. AND THE REPAIR IS NOT MECHANICAL, WHICH IS WHERE THIS ROUND STOPS. Of the extractor's twenty-one value objects, ZERO are tokens the author-side migration declared — Round 873 derived closed vocabularies from the author's short labels, while the blind extractor wrote sentences. Reviving the pair means mapping blind prose onto a token vocabulary, which is authoring on top of the record whose blindness is the evidence (Round 469), and that is a gate, not a chore.

The sweep was re-run at HEAD and again at 443c667 (Round 895, the commit before the fixes) in a separate worktree with its own target dir, both against R873's rebuilt dnd-quest store and against that revision's own repository store. HEAD: 16 differ / 8 byte-identical / 7 needing an argument. Pre-fix: 15 / 9 / 7. Round 896 recorded 16 / 6 / 9.

THAT TRIPLE DESCRIBES NO MOMENT. 16 is the post-fix differ count, 9 is the pre-fix byte-identical count, and 6 is wrong at both — the same bullet enumerates SEVEN verb names while calling them six. A number written from memory instead of from the machine is the failure the round itself was about, one layer up.

THE CLASSIFIER IS MECHANICAL: a verb counts as needing an argument only when BOTH stores exit non-zero with byte-identical output, and every one of the 7 was read rather than assumed — all print `error: --telling/--entity/--frame/--against arg required`.

`report-entity-kind-migration` now discriminates on the two REAL stores (`0 unregistered kinds over 25 entity(ies)` vs `over 0 entity(ies) — the store registers no entities, so nothing was checked`), which is the whole of the DIFFER count's movement from 15 to 16.

`report-excerpt-hash-backfill` IS STILL BYTE-IDENTICAL ON THE TWO REAL STORES AND CORRECTLY SO. Both print `0 of 0 excerpt(s)` plus the sentence saying no section carries a normative excerpt. Its fix made it say WHICH zero without making it differ, because the two stores are genuinely in the same state. Today's 8 = Round 896's honest 7 plus this one; Round 896's own thesis survived its own fix.

THE CARRY IS DISCHARGED FOR 5 OF 7. On the dnd corpus: `report-disclosure-coverage --telling delve` = 136 facts, disclosed 133 / hidden_by_design 3 / never_planned 0; `report-quest-graph --telling delve` = 4 quests over 4 worlds with q-main honestly unresolved; `report-playable-world --telling delve` = 4 worlds, 36 scenes and 94 locators on `claim`, unplaced 0; `report-entity` = 32 facts on `crown`, 12 on `lanternboy`; `report-frame-view --frame gt --at sc-20` = holding 41 / not_holding 2 / unknown 0, and `--frame warden` at the same coordinate = holding 1.

AND IT IS FALSE FOR THE OTHER 2, WHICH IS THIS ROUND'S FINDING. Round 896 argued the sweep's gap was mere effort because "the dnd corpus has a telling and a frame" — but `validate-render-fidelity` and `validate-disclosure-leak` are not discriminated by a telling or a frame. Their input is `--against <reextracted store>`, an artifact OUTSIDE the store, and the claim was checked against the wrong axis.

THE ONLY TRACKED INSTANCE DOES NOT LOAD. `claudedocs/phase1-dnd-quest-experiment/v3/run/extract/reextracted.atomic.json` is schema 23 with 5 predicates still declaring `object_kind: scalar` and 21 facts carrying `{kind:value}` objects — shapes Round 708 removed. Both verbs refuse on all 4 world-lines. The refusal is located mechanically, not by eye: `f-00a-03` is present in the re-extraction and absent from the migrated fixture, and every other verb loads the same store fine, so the offending record is the `--against` file.

THE VERB IS NOT AT FAULT. It refuses loudly, names all 21 fact ids and all 5 predicates, and says what migration each needs. What rotted is the record — the same rot Round 873 repaired on the AUTHOR half of this experiment and never reached on the EXTRACT half.

AND THE REPAIR IS NOT MECHANICAL, WHICH IS WHY THIS ROUND STOPS HERE. Measured: of the extractor's 21 value objects, ZERO are tokens the author's migration declared. Round 873 derived closed vocabularies from the author's short labels (`cause_of_rising: exposed | hidden`); the blind extractor wrote sentences ("a living hand feeds fresh dead to the floodwater", "weary, no wrath"). Reviving the pair means mapping 21 blind sentences onto a token vocabulary — authoring on top of the record whose blindness IS the evidence, the Round 469 boundary.

Round 899.decision_summary: R899 (BUILD — the gates that gate everything else were gated by nothing). Round 890 built the CI-state report into `pre-push` and wrote in its carry that nothing asserts the hook still contains the check, so deleting the block would be silent. Round 893 then ADDED logic to that same hook and repeated the carry verbatim, calling the question unopened. Two rounds named it and two rounds moved on, while 515 lines across three hooks went on rejecting hallucinated citations, malformed commit messages, version-postfix identifiers, unformatted code and lint regressions — every one of them deletable without a sound. THE HOOKS ARE NOW EXERCISED, NEVER COPIED. `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/git_hooks_smoke.rs` builds a throwaway git repo whose `core.hooksPath` points at THIS repository's own `.githooks/`, holding the smallest tree the cargo gates can run on plus a stub `scripts/mn` that logs the verb it was asked for and honours a forced exit code. A copied hook would be free to drift from the one that actually runs, which is the rot Round 873 found on one half of an experiment kit and Round 897 found still open on the other. Ten tests, 0.9 seconds, and CI already runs them: `cargo test --workspace --locked` is what `mnemosyne-validate.yml` invokes, verified by reading the workflow rather than assumed. EVERY GATE HAS A PAIR, BECAUSE ONE DIRECTION IS NOT A TEST. The workspace gate is asserted to run when the atomic sidecar is staged AND not to run when it is not — the positive alone would pass with the condition deleted. The vN ban is asserted to reject `parse_v2` AND to accept `schema_version`, which is the documented exemption a bare `_v` match would break. The separate-workspace gate is asserted to reject an unformatted `tools/sub` AND to pass a formatted one. commit-msg carries seventeen messages, each rejection asserted on its REASON rather than merely on failure. ★A MEASUREMENT CHANGED THE TEST BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN: an unformatted file the crate root does not reach is invisible to `cargo fmt --all`, because rustfmt reads the module tree and not the directory. The first probe put the unformatted code in an orphan file, the gate correctly did nothing, and had that been written up as the expected case the suite would have asserted the opposite of the truth. The case edits a reachable file and says why in a comment. ★TEN INJECTIONS, EACH REVERTED FROM A SAVED COPY, AND ONE OF THEM CORRECTED ME. Nine landed on exactly the intended test. The Gate 2 injection fired TWO, and that was my injection being coarser than my expectation rather than a defect: replacing the `if ! <verb>` condition removes the CALL along with the rejection, and the end-to-end case independently noticed the verb was never invoked. Re-run keeping the call (`<verb> && false`), it fires exactly one. Both results are recorded, because the redundancy is real coverage and the first reading was mine to fix. ★AND THE NAIVE WAY TO TEST THE `gh not installed` BRANCH WOULD HAVE PASSED FOR THE WRONG REASON: filtering PATH down to directories without a `gh` also removes `git`, since this machine keeps both in `/usr/bin`. Measured, not assumed. The case builds a shim directory of symlinks plus a stub cargo instead, and the four branches of a PRESENT gh (unreachable / no runs / red / annotated) run against a stub that answers all three of the hook's calls. A robustness hole was closed by reasoning about CI rather than by a failure: the fmt and clippy gates spawn a nested cargo, and an inherited `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` would aim it at the outer build's target directory in the middle of the test run, so every git and hook invocation now carries the fixture's own. Each hook finally points at the test, since the reason this gap was named twice and closed neither time is that nothing pointed anywhere.

The fixture: a minimal cargo crate the fmt/clippy gates can run on, a stub `scripts/mn` that logs its verb and honours `MN_STUB_EXIT`, and a stub `gh` answering all three `pre-push` calls by `GH_STUB_MODE`.

Coverage per gate: citation exit code (2), sidecar-conditional workspace gate (3, both directions), rustfmt (4), clippy (5), separate in-repo workspace (5b, both directions), vN ban with its `_version` exemption (6); pre-push delete-only + empty stdin + workspace exit code + all five CI-report branches; one end-to-end `git commit` proving the `core.hooksPath` wiring itself.
Every git and hook invocation pins `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` into the fixture, so the nested cargo the gates spawn can never contend on the outer build's target lock.
All three hooks gain a comment naming the test and asking that a new gate arrive with a case. Comment-only — verified by diffing for any added or removed non-comment line.
The vN case assembles its banned identifier at run time (`format!`), because writing it literally would make this file uncommittable by the gate it proves.
verification_bullets: 1365 green (+10), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --all --check` clean, validate-workspace clean. Both cargo runs went through `scripts/verify.sh`, so the full log is retained and the exit code is the command's own.

TEN INJECTIONS, EACH APPLIED WITH A UNIQUENESS ASSERTION AND REVERTED FROM A SAVED COPY (never `git checkout`, which would take this round's own work with it). J1 gate-2 rejection / J2 gate-3 sidecar condition / J3 gate-4 fmt / J4 gate-5 clippy call / J5 gate-6 vN rejection / J10 gate-5b fmt rejection / J6 pre-push delete-only skip / J7 pre-push annotation header / J8 commit-msg emoji rule / J9 commit-msg bullet cap.

NINE OF TEN FIRED EXACTLY ONE INTENDED TEST. J1 FIRED TWO AND THE FIRST READING WAS MINE TO CORRECT: replacing `if ! "${cli[@]}" validate-code-refs; then` with `if false` deletes the CALL as well as the rejection, so the end-to-end case failed too — on its assertion that the verb was invoked at all. Re-run as `"${cli[@]}" validate-code-refs && false`, keeping the call, it fires exactly one. The redundancy is coverage, not noise.
AFTER EVERY INJECTION THE HOOKS ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE ORIGINALS: `git status .githooks/` empty at the end of the run, and the suite green again at 10/10.

THE FMT CASE WAS WRONG IN ITS FIRST PROBE AND THE MACHINE SAID SO. An unformatted file not reachable from the crate root is invisible to `cargo fmt --all` (rustfmt walks the module tree, not the directory), so the probe's orphan file was correctly ignored and a test written from it would have asserted the opposite of the truth. The case now edits `src/lib.rs`.

THE `gh not installed` CASE CANNOT BE MADE BY FILTERING PATH ON THIS MACHINE — `gh` and `git` are both in `/usr/bin`, so dropping directories containing gh drops git, and the hook would have failed at the fmt gate for an unrelated reason. Measured before the test was written; the case builds a hermetic shim directory instead, and its symlink resolution asserts loudly if a tool is missing rather than skipping.

CI ALREADY RUNS THIS, VERIFIED BY READING `mnemosyne-validate.yml` RATHER THAN ASSUMING: the job invokes `cargo test --workspace --locked`, so no workflow change was needed. The suite is also hermetic with respect to `gh` — the absent-gh case builds its own PATH and the present-gh cases prepend a stub — so it does not depend on whether a runner has the tool.

THE GATE REJECTED THIS ROUND'S OWN COMMIT, AND `--no-verify` IS NOT THE ANSWER. Gate 6 scans added lines in staged `.rs` and covers test data by policy, so the literal the vN case needs made the commit carrying that case impossible. The banned identifier is therefore ASSEMBLED at run time rather than written, which keeps the pattern out of this repository's source while the fixture still hands the hook the real thing. Verified both ways: the staged diff greps clean against the gate's own regex, and the case still asserts the rejection quotes the assembled name — so the gate did see it.
carry_forward_bullets: THE STUB RESOLVER BOUNDS THE CLAIM: these cases prove the hook invokes `validate-code-refs` / `validate-workspace` and honours the exit code. They say nothing about those verbs, which have their own tests. A hook calling the WRONG verb name would still pass, since the stub answers to anything.

The `gh` stub returns lines already reduced the way `gh -q <jq>` would, so a wrong `--json` field or a broken jq expression in the hook is invisible here. Only the hook's HANDLING of each answer is covered.

WHETHER THE HOOKS ARE INSTALLED AT ALL IS STILL UNCHECKED. `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` is a manual per-clone step; a clone that skips it has no gates whatsoever and nothing in the tree says so. This test proves the hooks work when wired, not that they are wired.

The hook comments now cite Round 899, and `.githooks/` is outside the code-citation gate's configured paths (`crates/*/src/`, `crates/*/build.rs`, `tools/*/src/`, `studio/`), so that citation is not machine-checked. Same for this test file: `crates/*/tests/` is not scanned either.

The three remaining defect-shaped debts this round did not touch: the which-zero audit is unfinished for the 5 argument-taking verbs Round 897 ran but did not audit and the 5 whose input no store holds, and `validate-content-drift` still runs in no CI workflow.

Coverage per gate: citation exit code (2), sidecar-conditional workspace gate (3, both directions), rustfmt (4), clippy (5), separate in-repo workspace (5b, both directions), vN ban with its `_version` exemption (6); pre-push delete-only + empty stdin + workspace exit code + all five CI-report branches; one end-to-end `git commit` proving the `core.hooksPath` wiring itself.
Every git and hook invocation pins `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` into the fixture, so the nested cargo the gates spawn can never contend on the outer build's target lock.
All three hooks gain a comment naming the test and asking that a new gate arrive with a case. Comment-only — verified by diffing for any added or removed non-comment line.
The vN case assembles its banned identifier at run time (`format!`), because writing it literally would make this file uncommittable by the gate it proves.
publishable_verification_bullets: 1365 green (+10), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --all --check` clean, validate-workspace clean. Both cargo runs went through `scripts/verify.sh`, so the full log is retained and the exit code is the command's own.

TEN INJECTIONS, EACH APPLIED WITH A UNIQUENESS ASSERTION AND REVERTED FROM A SAVED COPY (never `git checkout`, which would take this round's own work with it). J1 gate-2 rejection / J2 gate-3 sidecar condition / J3 gate-4 fmt / J4 gate-5 clippy call / J5 gate-6 vN rejection / J10 gate-5b fmt rejection / J6 pre-push delete-only skip / J7 pre-push annotation header / J8 commit-msg emoji rule / J9 commit-msg bullet cap.

NINE OF TEN FIRED EXACTLY ONE INTENDED TEST. J1 FIRED TWO AND THE FIRST READING WAS MINE TO CORRECT: replacing `if ! "${cli[@]}" validate-code-refs; then` with `if false` deletes the CALL as well as the rejection, so the end-to-end case failed too — on its assertion that the verb was invoked at all. Re-run as `"${cli[@]}" validate-code-refs && false`, keeping the call, it fires exactly one. The redundancy is coverage, not noise.
AFTER EVERY INJECTION THE HOOKS ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE ORIGINALS: `git status .githooks/` empty at the end of the run, and the suite green again at 10/10.

THE FMT CASE WAS WRONG IN ITS FIRST PROBE AND THE MACHINE SAID SO. An unformatted file not reachable from the crate root is invisible to `cargo fmt --all` (rustfmt walks the module tree, not the directory), so the probe's orphan file was correctly ignored and a test written from it would have asserted the opposite of the truth. The case now edits `src/lib.rs`.

THE `gh not installed` CASE CANNOT BE MADE BY FILTERING PATH ON THIS MACHINE — `gh` and `git` are both in `/usr/bin`, so dropping directories containing gh drops git, and the hook would have failed at the fmt gate for an unrelated reason. Measured before the test was written; the case builds a hermetic shim directory instead, and its symlink resolution asserts loudly if a tool is missing rather than skipping.

CI ALREADY RUNS THIS, VERIFIED BY READING `mnemosyne-validate.yml` RATHER THAN ASSUMING: the job invokes `cargo test --workspace --locked`, so no workflow change was needed. The suite is also hermetic with respect to `gh` — the absent-gh case builds its own PATH and the present-gh cases prepend a stub — so it does not depend on whether a runner has the tool.

THE GATE REJECTED THIS ROUND'S OWN COMMIT, AND `--no-verify` IS NOT THE ANSWER. Gate 6 scans added lines in staged `.rs` and covers test data by policy, so the literal the vN case needs made the commit carrying that case impossible. The banned identifier is therefore ASSEMBLED at run time rather than written, which keeps the pattern out of this repository's source while the fixture still hands the hook the real thing. Verified both ways: the staged diff greps clean against the gate's own regex, and the case still asserts the rejection quotes the assembled name — so the gate did see it.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: THE STUB RESOLVER BOUNDS THE CLAIM: these cases prove the hook invokes `validate-code-refs` / `validate-workspace` and honours the exit code. They say nothing about those verbs, which have their own tests. A hook calling the WRONG verb name would still pass, since the stub answers to anything.

The `gh` stub returns lines already reduced the way `gh -q <jq>` would, so a wrong `--json` field or a broken jq expression in the hook is invisible here. Only the hook's HANDLING of each answer is covered.

WHETHER THE HOOKS ARE INSTALLED AT ALL IS STILL UNCHECKED. `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` is a manual per-clone step; a clone that skips it has no gates whatsoever and nothing in the tree says so. This test proves the hooks work when wired, not that they are wired.

The hook comments now cite Round 899, and `.githooks/` is outside the code-citation gate's configured paths (`crates/*/src/`, `crates/*/build.rs`, `tools/*/src/`, `studio/`), so that citation is not machine-checked. Same for this test file: `crates/*/tests/` is not scanned either.

The three remaining defect-shaped debts this round did not touch: the which-zero audit is unfinished for the 5 argument-taking verbs Round 897 ran but did not audit and the 5 whose input no store holds, and `validate-content-drift` still runs in no CI workflow.

Round 900.decision_summary: R900 (DEBT — the carries, and one of them was not true). The owner asked why a round leaves carries at all, and the honest answer is that three of Round 899's four were work DECLINED, not limits of the world. Naming a gap in a carry reads as rigor, which is precisely how it substitutes for closing the gap — the mechanism by which the untested-hooks defect survived Round 890 naming it and Round 893 naming it again while adding logic to the same file. This round closes what was closable and, more usefully, finds that one of the four was FALSE. CLOSED: `.githooks/` is now inside the code-citation gate. Adding the path naively produced ELEVEN `section_missing` rejects, measured before deciding anything — the hooks cite `COMMIT_FORMAT.md §3` / `§4`, and the gate reads `§<digits>` as this store's own section namespace, the Round 867 whose-numbering question in miniature. The eleven were converted to the house `sec N` convention this repository already uses for design-doc references, the gate reports 0, and the `Round 899` citations the previous round wrote into three hooks are now checked like any other code citation instead of resting on my word. CLOSED for the request contract: the `gh` stub now CHECKS what it is asked rather than only answering — subcommand, the `--json` field list, the headSha filter, and both endpoint shapes, with violations written to a file the test asserts is empty. Dropping `conclusion` from the field list turns exactly one test red on that assertion while every canned answer still arrives, which is the shape of defect the old stub was structurally blind to. What stays genuinely uncoverable is jq SEMANTICS: a stub cannot evaluate the expression, only pin the request. ★CORRECTED, AND THE MACHINE DID IT: Round 899's carry claimed a hook calling the WRONG verb name "would still pass, since the stub answers to anything". That is false. Taking the new defense back out and misspelling the verb — the discipline of removing a defense to see what it was actually worth — still failed 2 of 10 tests, because the existing `mn_calls()` assertions check for the exact verb string. The carry was written from reasoning instead of from a run, and it overstated the hole in exactly the way this round is about. What the tightening buys, now measured rather than asserted: 2 of 10 becomes 7 of 10, and the failure names the cause at the point of the call ("no CLI verb is named 'validate-code-ref'") instead of surfacing as an argv-log mismatch three assertions later. STATED AS A LIMIT AND NO LONGER CARRIED: whether the hooks are INSTALLED cannot be checked from the tree at all. Git runs hooks from `.git/hooks` or `core.hooksPath`, both local configuration, and no tracked file can force or observe either — a property of the tool, not a choice, and it stops being pending work the moment it is named as a limit. The adjacent mode that IS checkable got closed: the helper now asserts the executable bit, because git SILENTLY SKIPS a hook without it and the gate disappears with no message at all. AND ONE ITEM WAS NEVER DEBT: `crates/*/tests/` staying outside the citation gate is a deliberate documented policy in `mnemosyne.toml` (Round 777 — single responsibility per asset class, review-time judgment carrying the residual). Round 899's carry restated it as though it were an open gap. Re-listing settled decisions as debt is its own noise, and it makes the list that matters harder to read.

After the `sec N` conversion: total=0. Had this round added the path without looking, it would have landed a rejecting gate.
