Round 901.decision_summary: R901 (DEBT — D2, the which-zero audit, and the second home of the Round 895 defect). Round 895 fixed a scan whose empty list could not say whether nothing was wrong or nothing was there; Round 896 swept the no-argument verbs for the same shape; Round 897 RAN the five argument-taking verbs but explicitly did not audit them. This round audits the whole remaining surface and finds one real defect. THE SET WAS COUNTED BY MACHINE FIRST, BECAUSE THE PREVIOUS TWO ROUNDS GOT IT WRONG. Re-deriving the classification: 8 byte-identical minus the two already repaired (Round 891's transition map, Round 896's backfill report) = SIX unaudited, and 7 argument-taking minus the two Round 897 proved unrunnable = FIVE. Round 896's carry said "the 5 verbs whose input neither store holds" while its own verification enumerated seven names, and Round 897 copied the 5 forward. That is the third miscount in this lineage, all three from writing a number instead of counting one. THE FIVE ARGUMENT-TAKING VERBS PASS, AND NOT BY LUCK. Every one exits 1 on an unresolvable argument with a message that names this exact hazard — `report-entity` says a typo'd entity "must not read as an empty dossier", `report-quest-graph` and `report-playable-world` say a typo'd telling "must not silently render with no disclosure plan". A registered entity carrying no facts renders `entity ghost (person) — 0 fact(s)` with its description, and a frame holding nothing at a coordinate prints `holding=0 not_holding=1`: the denominator is on the line. FIVE OF THE SIX INPUT-LESS VERBS PASS, EACH BY CONSTRUCTING THE NON-EMPTY STATE RATHER THAN BY READING THE CODE. Registering a meter turns `0 registered meters` into a per-meter economy; recording one confirmation event turns four zeros into `proposed: 1 / debt: 1`; a store rewritten to schema v4 loads and switches `report-binding-migration` to its `v4 -> v5` branch, so that branch is reachable rather than dead; `validate-verifies-linkage` already prints `examined=0` beside its findings; and three of them answer `disabled` / `skipped` / `not configured` rather than a bare zero. ★AND `validate-spec-drift` HAS THE ROUND 895 DEFECT. It printed `sections=56 ... drift: total=0` on a store where NOT ONE section carries a `normative_excerpt` — the number is true, the line reads as coverage, and `scan_spec_drift` skips exactly those sections. Both real stores in this tree are in that state, so this verb has only ever answered "clean" here, and its `--json` called the store total `valid_section_count` — a name that is honest over in `validate-code-refs`, where it means the section space a citation may resolve to, and misleading here, where it sits where a denominator goes. THE REPAIR IS ROUND 895'S, DELIBERATELY: `scan_spec_drift` returns a `SpecDriftScan` carrying a `SpecMirrorCensus` counted in the SAME walk (examined / exempt_by_status / sections_with_excerpt, with examined + exempt == with_excerpt), the CLI prints the reach beside the store size, and at examined == 0 it prints the sentence instead of the bare total. One pattern, one resolver shape, two verbs.
changes_bullets: `scan_spec_drift` now returns `SpecDriftScan { violations, census }` — renamed in place, both call sites updated, no parallel entry point.
New `SpecMirrorCensus { examined, exempt_by_status, sections_with_excerpt }`, counted in the walk that finds the drift so the reach cannot answer a different question than the finding.

`validate-spec-drift` text output gains `mirroring=` and `exempt_by_status=`, and at zero examined prints the which-zero sentence. `--json` gains `sections_with_excerpt` / `examined_count` / `exempt_by_status_count`, and `valid_section_count` is renamed `section_count` (the old name reads as a denominator it never was).

Seven gates: the discriminating PAIR at unit level (both violation lists empty, censuses must differ), drifted-counts-as-examined, exempt-counted-but-not-examined with the sum invariant, and the CLI pair (case viii / case ix) that case vii had left as an exit-code-only assertion.
verification_bullets: 1370 green (+5), clippy `-D warnings` clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace clean. Both cargo runs through `scripts/verify.sh`.

THE AUDIT CONSTRUCTED EVERY NON-EMPTY STATE INSTEAD OF READING FOR IT (the Round 894 lesson: reading a verb and concluding is how the last wrong answer was reached). `add-parameter` + `add-parameter-delta` -> `1 meter(s)`; `add-confirmation-event` -> `proposed: 1`; `schema_version` rewritten to 4 -> the migration branch renders, so it is reachable; `[workspace.spec_source]`, `[verifies_catalog]` and a catalog file each switch their verb out of `skipped`. Only `severity_confirmation` was left unmeasured — my probe put the key in `[continuity]` and TOML rejected it, and I did not chase the right table.

FOUR INJECTIONS, EACH ANCHORED WITH A UNIQUENESS ASSERTION. J1 (examined never counted) fails 4 tests; J2 (which-zero branch unreachable) fails EXACTLY case viii; J3 (exempt counted as examined) fails 2; J4 (drifted not counted as examined) fails exactly 1. Baseline and post-restore both green.

★MY FIRST INJECTION RUN REPORTED FIVE FAILURES FOR J2 — A CLI-ONLY EDIT BREAKING UNIT TESTS, WHICH IS IMPOSSIBLE. The harness restored with `shutil.copy2`, which preserves the pre-injection mtime, so cargo saw nothing to rebuild and re-ran the PREVIOUS injection's binary. This is the Round 891 harness defect verbatim, recorded in memory, and I reproduced it. Re-run with an explicit `utime`, the numbers above are the honest ones and the suite is green after restore — the tell was that the post-restore run was still red.
★AN EXISTING TEST CAUGHT A REGRESSION I INTRODUCED: rewriting the `--json` block dropped `workspace_revision`, and `case_iii` failed on it immediately.

★AND MY OWN NEW ASSERTION WAS LOSSY, WHICH COST A ROUND-TRIP: `assert!(out.status.success(), "no drift here")` printed no payload. With stderr added it said in one line that the wire form is lowercase `superseded`, not `Superseded`.
carry_forward_bullets: `severity_confirmation` was never exercised: the key is not under `[continuity]` and this round did not find its table. `validate-confirmation` therefore stays audited only in its `disabled` branch — the one state that IS loud about not running.

The five argument-taking verbs are audited for the unresolvable-argument and empty-but-valid cases. Their INTERIOR zeros (a quest with no completion fact, a world with no locators) were not enumerated one by one.
The two blocked verbs (`validate-render-fidelity`, `validate-disclosure-leak`) remain outside this audit for the Round 897 reason, unchanged.

D3 remains: `validate-content-drift` and `validate-spec-drift` both run in no CI workflow, so both which-zero repairs are read only when a person types the command. That is the gating decision this round did not open.

Round 902.decision_summary: R902 (DEBT — D3, and the measurement turns it from a build into a decision). The last item on the debt ledger asked whether the two which-zero drift scans belong in a CI workflow. Measured on this repository's own store before deciding anything: `validate-content-drift` reports `0 of 5 section(s) carry an excerpt cache, so this scan compared NOTHING`, and `validate-spec-drift` skips outright because `[workspace.spec_source]` is unset. Both exit 0. ADDING EITHER TO A WORKFLOW TODAY LANDS A GREEN STEP THAT ASSERTS NOTHING — the Round 887 green-and-hollow class three rounds of this session have been closing one verb at a time. So the answer is NO, and D3 closes as a decision rather than as deferred work. THIS IS NOT "THE VERBS DO NOT MATTER". Both were repaired this week — Round 895 for content drift, Round 901 for spec drift — precisely so that their zero is legible instead of passing for coverage. The repair is real; the INPUT is absent. A gate placed over an absent input measures the absence, and it would report success for it. THE TRIGGER THAT REOPENS THIS IS STATED SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT: the moment this store starts carrying excerpt caches of any kind — any `import-content-excerpts` authoring landing here, including the map-corpus experiment if it ever writes prose — `validate-content-drift` becomes non-vacuous and the CI question is live again. `validate-spec-drift` reopens only if this workspace itself mirrors an external standard, which it does not and is not planned to: that is the consumer's shape (the SCE compliance ledger), not this tree's. AND ONE OPTION IS EXPLICITLY WRONG RATHER THAN MERELY UNCHOSEN: adding the step with a guard that fails when `examined == 0`. That inverts the contract Round 895 built — the zero was made LEGIBLE, not fatal — and would fail this repository on every push for a state that is correct. A gate that rejects a true state teaches everyone to bypass it.

Round 903.decision_summary: R903 (MEASUREMENT — the push tail, and the baseline that was not a baseline). Code 0. Rounds 897 through 902 are on `origin/main` at `1ee7e18`, and this round discharges the tail RULEBOOK attaches to the PUSH gate: after a push lands, read the run it started — the conclusion AND the annotations (Round 893). ROUND 893'S CARRY CLOSES AS OBSERVED RATHER THAN REASONED. That round bumped `actions/checkout` to v7 and `actions/cache` to v6 and wrote that the bump itself was unobserved, because whether GitHub accepts the new majors and whether the Node 20 deprecation annotations disappear are visible only after a push. Both are measured now: every workflow is green on `1ee7e18`, and the annotation count runs 2, 2, 0, 0, 0 across `b138804`, `794ad8c`, `3bbdaf3`, `43cc1a6`, `1ee7e18`, with the vanished warning naming exactly `actions/cache@v4, actions/checkout@v4` as the actions forced off Node 20. BUT THE FIRST MEASUREMENT WAS NOT A MEASUREMENT, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS A ROUND AND NOT A NOTE. I first took `43cc1a6` as the pre-bump baseline and read 0 there and 0 at `1ee7e18` — except the bump landed at `3bbdaf3`, THREE COMMITS EARLIER, so both arms were post-bump. Zero on both sides reads as "the bump changed nothing", which is the exact inversion of the truth, and the comparison was perfectly happy to say it. This is the Round 865 class: a discriminating input exists only if the two arms actually differ somewhere, so a before/after that returns the same number on both sides must make THE PAIR the first suspect instead of the finding. What caught it was reading the commit graph for which round did the bump — not the measurement, which had no way to complain. THE 0-ANNOTATION BRANCH NOW HAS A REAL-DATA WITNESS. Round 893 recorded that this repository held no discriminating input for that branch because every run in visible history was annotated, forced it with injection J1, and predicted this bump would produce the first real one; `1ee7e18` is that instance, so the injected branch and the field now agree. AND THE STEERING WHEEL WAS STALE: the RESUME memory read "R897-R902 UNPUSHED, ahead 6" while the repository reports ahead 0 and `update by push`. That is wrong in the cheap direction — it claims pending work that does not exist — but it is the one line RULEBOOK calls the steering wheel, and a session trusting it would have tried to re-push rather than read the run.
changes_bullets: No code and no gate. The deliverable is the measurement: Round 893's bump carry closes as OBSERVED rather than as reasoned, and the RESUME position line is corrected from UNPUSHED to PUSHED.

The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/cache@v4, actions/checkout@v4`. Round 893's one-page-per-check-run limit does not truncate this arm — 2 annotations across 2 check runs is one each, so the declared count and the read count agree.

READING THE ENTRY BACK CAUGHT A DEFECT IN WRITING IT. The first append of this entry passed wrapped bullet files, and `parse_bullets_file` is strictly one line per bullet, so half-sentence fragments landed as standalone audit bullets. The store was reverted before any commit (only `workspace.atomic.json` was modified, and the entry count returned to 649 with the entry gone), the files reflowed to one line per bullet with a 1:1 line-to-bullet assertion, and the entry re-appended. carry_forward_bullets: THE TAIL RAN A SESSION LATE, AND THE RULE FOR IT WAS ALREADY WRITTEN. RULEBOOK's PUSH gate says verbatim "After a push lands, read the run it started and report the result", and the session that pushed ended at the push anyway; the reading waited for this load. So the gap is COMPLIANCE, not text — and writing the rule again, louder, would be the theater of patching a mechanism's seat with a note. There is no mechanism on the push side either: git has no `post-push` hook (verified above), and pre-push by construction reports the commit being built ON, never the one just sent, which is the limit Round 893 already stated. The only thing that could catch it is an out-of-band watcher reading the run after the fact. That is buildable and unbuilt, and it is a COST JUDGEMENT in the Round 902 sense rather than a limit — a small round if the owner wants the watcher instead of the note.

The 0-annotation state is true of TODAY'S upstream, not pinned. Floating major tags mean `actions/checkout@v7` and `actions/cache@v6` can change content without a commit of ours. Round 893 considered SHA pinning and REJECTED it with an argument (no machine in this tree refreshes a pin, and an abandoned pin is worse than none). Restating it as debt would be the noise Round 900 named.

Nothing asserts "annotations are 0" — the pre-push hook REPORTS them and Round 893 chose report-only deliberately, because Round 888 and Round 889 were both pushes made to FIX a red CI and a gate would have blocked both. Also a settled decision rather than an open gap.

Round 904.decision_summary: R904 (EXPERIMENT — the map corpus, run on the owner's word against the protocol Round 898 froze). Two blind authors, fresh context each, firewalled to their own directory; no render, no re-extraction, no judges. THE ORACLE IS OUR OWN VERB OUTPUT, SO THE CLAIM IS EXERCISE AND DISCRIMINATION, NOT CORRECTNESS (Round 884). E1 CAME BACK YES AND IT IS NOT AN ARTIFACT OF ITERATION: given a fiction brief containing no map vocabulary and the 211-line contract, the Stage A author declared a rule of class `transition` with `adjacency`, `undirected: false` and `containment` — and `order.json` and `narrative-rules.json` are BYTE-IDENTICAL between the frozen first submission and the green store, so the map was right before any error message came back. Both authors independently chose directed edges and both explained it the same way unasked: a descent that cannot be climbed back is inexpressible if an edge admits both directions. E2 CAME BACK NO, TWICE, WITH THE SAME DEFECT: neither first submission imports, and both fail on `sections.json` being an object where the loader wants a bare array. Two authors who never saw each other's work produced the same wrong guess because THE CONTRACT GIVES NO WIRE SHAPE FOR THE SECTIONS FILE AT ALL, and each flagged it as a guess in the sealed self-report before running anything. The second error in each log is a cascade, and that was checked rather than believed: the fact manifests differ from their frozen originals by nothing that touches adjacency, and Stage B's imported with no content change whatever. THE EVIDENCE IS WHAT THE BRIEF DID NOT MANDATE, AND IT IS THREE CONTRACT GAPS, EACH REPRODUCED HERE ON AN ISOLATED STORE RATHER THAN TAKEN FROM AN AUTHOR'S REPORT. `parent_doc` is required on every section and appears ZERO times in the contract; both authors guessed a value and both were accepted, which as Stage B put it means "accepted is not correct" and the two commands they had could not tell them which. The contract under-declares the fact manifest by exactly one array, `units` — counted from the type, where `FactsManifest` has eight fields — and that single omission plus the contract's "Declared via add-unit" sentence led BOTH authors to conclude a Quantity is unauthorable from files and to author a workaround, a conclusion that sits in Stage A's SEALED report and is FALSE. And the manifest ignores unknown keys, so a typo of a real key returns exit 0 with zero created and no mention. THAT LENIENCY IS DELIBERATE AND LOAD-BEARING, NOT AN OVERSIGHT — `evidence_replay_smoke` states it and depends on it to tell a manifest that parses from one that BUILDS — SO THE DEFECT IS NOT THE PARSER BUT THAT THE CONTRACT HANDED TO AUTHORS NEVER MENTIONS IT, which is precisely what made the `units` gap undiscoverable: a correct guess and a typo are byte-identical. E3 DISAGREED IN OPPOSITE WAYS AND BOTH WAYS ARE FINDINGS. Stage A claimed thirteen locations against `12 node(s), 29 edge(s)`: edges exact, and the missing node is the unreachable place the brief demanded, authored with no adjacency at either end — the map READ cannot show an isolated place because a map's nodes are derived from its edges, and the GATE is where it surfaces, as `map_contained_off_map`. Stage B's counts agree exactly, and the disagreement moved to the question: its author reported a place UNREACHABLE while the frontier reports `unconnected places: none`, both true of different questions, with no read in this substrate answering the first. The two stages also split on the frontier itself — Stage B declared `subject_kind`/`object_entity_kind` on `adjacent` and Stage A did not, which is the whole difference between the Round 891 subtraction computing and printing `not derivable`; a blind author reproduced, from the contract alone, the exact shape Round 898 recorded as the reason Round 891's J2 could not fail through the CLI. C1: the previously empty branches ran, the Round 703 G2 checks fired on authored data, and `validate-continuity` REJECTS BOTH CORPORA — 27 violations in A and 12 in B, dominated in both by `adjacency_cross_scope`. THAT ONE REPLICATES ACROSS BOTH AUTHORS AND IS A FINDING, NOT AN AUTHOR ERROR: both authored quarters holding locations exactly as the brief asked and both wrote passages between locations in different quarters, which is what a town is, and the check treats a non-sibling edge as a violation while the contract mentions `cross_scope` zero times and describes G2 in three clauses that never say an edge must stay inside one container. Declaring `containment` silently tightens the gate in a direction the author cannot see. Whether the check is right or over-strict is a design question this round records and does not settle. C2: of the seven verbs Round 896 left byte-identical after its repairs, EXACTLY ONE now differs with this corpus as a third arm, and it is `report-transition-map`, the one Round 896 called the sharpest case of an honest byte-identical. The corpus discriminates on the axis it was built for and on no other, which is the honest result rather than a disappointing one. AND THE LANDING CORRECTED THE DESIGN: Round 898 specified `revision_provenance: "exact"`, a term the gate's closed vocabulary does not contain, so the pin lands as `declared-at-run`, the existing name for the same thing and the first kit in this tree to use it.
changes_bullets: `claudedocs/phase1-map-corpus-experiment/` lands tracked: both authors' manifests, both frozen first submissions, both sealed self-reports, both verbatim first-import logs, the iteration notes, the verb output, `map-corpus-report.md` and `v1/manifest.json`.

`v1/replay.json` registers both corpora as `kit-replay/v2` replays at `revision_provenance: "declared-at-run"`, so `evidence_replay_smoke` rebuilds them and CI's evidence-replay workflow triggers on this kit's own path filter.
`.gitignore` drops the two per-author copies of `contract.txt`, which are byte-identical to the one tracked `v1/run/contract.txt`.
No production code changed. Every gap this round found is recorded, not repaired.
verification_bullets: E1 IS NOT AN ITERATION ARTIFACT, AND THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: `diff -q` reports `order.json` and `narrative-rules.json` byte-identical between `stage-a-first-submission/` and the green `stage-a/`, so the transition rule predates every error message. Stage A's `facts.json` differs by 13 lines, none of which touch adjacency.

E2's logs are frozen verbatim with both exit codes and no filtering, captured BEFORE anything was handed back, and the store was untouched by the failure (58 bytes, unchanged) so the rejection is clean rather than partial.

THE THREE CONTRACT GAPS WERE REPRODUCED HERE, NOT ACCEPTED FROM THE AUTHORS: on an isolated scratch store, a manifest carrying a key that does not exist returns exit 0 / 0 created / 0 bytes and names nothing, as does `"frame"` for `"frames"`; `{"units": [...]}` imports as `1 units created`, proving the array real; and `grep -c parent_doc contract.txt` is 0 against a field the loader requires. The manifest's true field count is 8, read off the `FactsManifest` type rather than counted from the tally string.

The `adjacency_cross_scope` intent was read from the source before being called a finding: the scan's own doc comment defines it as "a non-sibling edge", and the contract's G2 paragraph never states that constraint.

Round 905.decision_summary: R905 (MEASUREMENT, code 0 — the gate was right, the contract was thirteen rounds stale, and the guard that should have caught it was grading itself). Round 904 left the largest finding open as a design question for the owner: `adjacency_cross_scope` rejected 24 of the 39 violations across two independently authored corpora, both of which built the container hierarchy the brief asked for. THAT QUESTION IS ANSWERED WITHOUT ASKING, BY READING THE MACHINE. `AdjacencyCrossScope` is not Round 703's check at all: Round 716 replaced the flat map with a PER-SCOPE projection, and its entry says so in as many words — "MapContainerAsNode is REMOVED", "this changes `contains` semantics from R703's grouping (all nodes one graph) to scope boundary (siblings-only edges)", "a portal is the container participating as a NODE in its parent's scope, so the container/node dichotomy dissolves". Under that model a quarter MAY be adjacent to a sibling quarter and movement between quarters goes through the quarters' own edges. THE CHECK IS CORRECT AND THE CORPUS IS WRONG — BUT THE AUTHORS ARE NOT. `describe-schema`'s containment field is still annotated "Round 703" and still tells an author that a region is "a container: a search-key, not a position" and that "a container must not be walked on". That is the exact semantic Round 716 deleted, and both blind authors paraphrased it back before being rejected for it: Stage A's sealed report says the quarters "are searchable places to be in rather than positions to move between", Stage B's says "containers, never adjacency endpoints". THE CONTRACT DID NOT MERELY OMIT THE MODEL, IT STATED THE SUPERSEDED ONE, AND TWO AUTHORS OBEYED IT. `describe-schema` never contains the words portal or cross-scope on this axis; its only two hits for sibling are about world-line roads. AND THE SECOND HALF IS WORSE, BECAUSE A GUARD EXISTS AND DID NOT FIRE. `manifest_wire_prose_names_every_serde_key` asserts that every serde key is named in the wire prose — but its oracle is A HAND-WRITTEN EXAMPLE MANIFEST INSIDE THE TEST, and that example contains `"units"` zero times, so the guard never asked about the one array the prose omits. This is the Round 624 / Round 777 hand-list class in its purest form: the oracle is a second copy of the artifact it polices, so anything missing from BOTH copies is invisible. THE DERIVED FORM ALREADY EXISTS ONE CRATE AWAY — `evidence_replay_smoke::facts_manifest_keys` takes the key set FROM the `FactsManifest` type with the comment "a field added to the manifest joins this set on its own; a hand-copied list would not" — and this guard does not use it. The sections manifest has no wire prose at all: `parent_doc` appears zero times in `schema.rs` against a `SectionImport` field the loader requires, which is why two authors independently guessed the file's shape and both guessed wrong. SO ROUND 904'S SCOPE FORK DISSOLVES INTO A BUILD, and the build is not "fix the words" — words drift, and these drifted for thirteen rounds under a green guard. It is: derive the manifest and section key sets from their types so the prose cannot omit an array again, and correct the containment prose to the model the code has enforced since Round 716.

THE STALENESS IS LOCATED, NOT ASSERTED: `crates/mnemosyne-validate/src/schema.rs:1242` opens the containment description with "Round 703 (store-native map)" and carries "a search-key, not a position" and "a container must not be walked on" — the superseded model, in the contract handed to every author.

The authors' paraphrase was checked against their SEALED reports, written before any verb output reached them, so it cannot be hindsight: Stage A "searchable places to be in rather than positions to move between", Stage B "containers, never adjacency endpoints".

THE GUARD'S ORACLE WAS READ, AND ITS BLIND SPOT MEASURED: `manifest_wire_prose_names_every_serde_key` walks a hand-written example manifest declared in the test body, and `grep -c '"units"'` over that example is 0. The guard is green and has never asked about `units`.

The derived alternative is present in this tree and was read rather than imagined: `evidence_replay_smoke::facts_manifest_keys` builds the key set by serializing an all-default `FactsManifest`, and `FactsManifest` has 8 fields counted from the type.
`grep -c parent_doc crates/mnemosyne-validate/src/schema.rs` is 0, against a required field of `SectionImport` (`crates/mnemosyne-atomic/src/lib.rs:3028`).

Round 904's replay registration was verified end to end rather than assumed: `evidence_replay_smoke -- --ignored` ran 38 replays across 24 revisions in 336s and reported "36 replays reproduced their declared digest, 2 blocked as declared", passing. carry_forward_bullets: THE BUILD IS SPECIFIED AND UNBUILT, AND THE SPEC IS DELIBERATELY NOT "FIX THE WORDS": derive the fact-manifest key set from `FactsManifest` and the section-import key set from `SectionImport` so the wire prose cannot omit an array or a required field again; correct the containment description to Round 716's scope-boundary/portal model; name the eighth array `units`; and state that unknown manifest keys are ignored, which Round 904 established is deliberate and load-bearing rather than a parser bug.

NO GUARD IS PROPOSED FOR PROSE-VERSUS-SEMANTICS, AND THAT LIMIT IS NAMED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. A derived key set catches a MISSING key; nothing catches a description that names every key and describes the wrong model, which is exactly what happened to containment for thirteen rounds. Pinning English against behaviour is not something this round knows how to do deterministically, and a string-match on phrases would be theatre.

The two corpora stay rejected by `validate-continuity` and Round 904's replay covers the import only. Re-authoring them to the portal model would make them gate-clean, but that is authoring on top of a blind-authored record, which the Round 469 bound and the Round 883 no-edit-in-place rule both forbid; a gate-clean map corpus would be a NEW authoring run, not a repair of this one.

Whether the corpora's rejection should have been foreseeable to the orchestrator is worth stating plainly: it was not, because the orchestrator read the same contract the authors did. The design lives in the Round 716 entry and the variant's doc comment, and neither is where an author looks.

Round 906.decision_summary: R906 BUILD (code) — the contract is derived from the types where it can be, and says the model the gate actually enforces where it cannot. R904 sent two blind authors at describe-schema with 211 lines of contract and a fiction brief; both submitted a sections manifest the loader rejects, both reported in sealed notes that a Quantity cannot be authored from a file, and 24 of their 39 gate findings were adjacency_cross_scope — three separate failures with one shape: the contract had drifted from the types and from the enforcement, under a guard that stayed green. This round closes all three at their source. (1) THE ORACLE WAS A HAND COPY. manifest_wire_prose_names_every_serde_key walked a hand-written FactsManifest literal in the test body; when `units` was added to the type, the literal stopped compiling and the repair was `units: vec![]` — an empty array recurses into nothing, so the guard went quiet by being repaired, and the overview went on saying "seven arrays" for thirteen rounds. The R624/R777 hand-list class in pure form: the oracle was a second copy of the thing it watched. The roster is now DERIVED (set-equal to FactsManifest's serde keys), the overview is GENERATED from it so the count word cannot drift, and an empty array in the sample is now a test failure with a named reason. The derived form was already one crate away — evidence_replay_smoke::facts_manifest_keys, whose comment reads "a hand-copied list would not". (2) THE CONTRACT DESCRIBED THE SECTIONS MANIFEST NOWHERE: `parent_doc` appeared zero times in schema.rs, which is why two authors who could not see each other guessed the same wrong shape — a guess two isolated readers make identically is a contract gap, not two mistakes. New SchemaContract.sections_wire, reflection-pinned to SectionImport. (3) CONTAINMENT SAID THE SUPERSEDED MODEL. schema.rs still carried R703's "a container is a search-key, not a position" and "must not be walked on" while scan_spatial_map had, since R716, treated containment as a SCOPE BOUNDARY with the container participating as a node in its parent's scope — a portal. Both authors quoted the stale sentence back and were rejected by the live gate for obeying it. THE CHECK WAS RIGHT AND THE CONTRACT WAS THIRTEEN ROUNDS STALE; the corpora are not repaired here (R469: authoring on a blind record destroys the evidence). WHAT THIS ROUND LEARNED ABOUT ITS OWN FIX: my first draft of the sections prose offered coverage_expectation "normative"|"informative" — the two-state vocabulary R422 removed and R870 had already caught hand-retyped in five surfaces — and every key-level assertion passed on it, because a key-set walk checks that keys are NAMED and says nothing about what VALUES a closed-enum key accepts. So the closed vocabulary is pinned to serde_variants::<CoverageExpectation>() too. 5 new tests, 6 injections all firing exactly one test each, and every documented claim walked against the real loader in a throwaway store rather than asserted from reading: the bare array imports, the object-with-a-sections-key is rejected with "invalid type: map, expected a sequence", an omitted parent_doc is a parse error, and a Quantity is created from a file. NEXT = sweep describe-schema's remaining hand-authored tier-3 prose (canon_order, disclosure_encoding, invariant_enforcement, registry descriptions) for the same drift — this round found one because R904 walked into it; nothing swept the rest.
changes_bullets: describe-schema's manifest array ROSTER is now derived, not counted by hand: manifest_kinds() is the single ordered list (apply order, which serde cannot recover), the new manifest_kinds_cover_every_facts_manifest_array holds it set-equal to FactsManifest's real serde keys, and manifest_wire.overview is GENERATED from it (its type changed from &'static str to String) so the count word and the list cannot drift from each other or from the type.

The eighth array `units` is named, with the fact two blind authors got wrong stated outright: a Quantity IS authorable from a file — declare the unit here, then write {"kind":"quantity","n":…,"unit":<unit_id>} on the typed leg.

manifest_wire_prose_names_every_serde_key now REJECTS an empty array in its sample. That empty vec was the whole failure: `units` joined FactsManifest, the hand-written struct literal stopped compiling, and the repair `units: vec![]` recursed into nothing — a guard that went quiet by being repaired.

The manifest overview states that unknown keys are IGNORED DELIBERATELY, why that leniency is load-bearing (parse-vs-build are two questions, and evidence_replay_smoke::classify depends on separating them), and the consequence for the reader: a correct guess and a typo are byte-identical at the parse, so the roster is the only way to learn a kind exists. manifest_tolerates_unknown_keys_and_builds_nothing pins the behaviour with its discriminating pair.

NEW SchemaContract.sections_wire — the structure half of an authoring run, which this contract described NOWHERE (`parent_doc` appeared zero times). Round 907.decision_summary: R907 BUILD (code) — the sweep R906 named, measured before it was built, and the number it produced was mostly noise. R906 ended by naming the obvious next move: describe-schema's OTHER hand-authored prose surfaces might have drifted the same way containment did. This round measured that instead of assuming it, and the measurement changed the answer twice. FIRST, THE MECHANICAL AXES ARE CLEAN. Every verb-shaped name the contract hands its reader (30 of them: add-unit, report-authoring-frontier, validate-continuity, propose-verdict, ...) and every backticked snake_case mechanism (43) exists in this tree — 0 missing on both. SECOND, THE LEDGER-SUPERSESSION FINDER IS NOT A DEFECT LIST, AND MEASURING IT IS WHAT SHOWED THAT. It flags a contract citation when a later entry names that round near supersession language, and it fired on 24 of the 32 rounds the contract cites — a number that reads like a finding. Four were then read in full and ALL FOUR ARE FALSE POSITIVES: R696 describes itself as R676-COMPATIBLE, and R891 / R873 / R877 do not touch the claims they were flagged against. One known true positive exists in the list (R703, fixed by R906), so the honest statement is a finder with poor measured precision, not twenty-four stale surfaces. Reporting the 24 would have been the R860 class exactly: a countable thing asserted rather than counted. WHAT WAS BUILT is the axis that IS decidable — the contract's verb names must be verbs this binary dispatches — plus a second test the injections forced into existence. THE INJECTION THAT REFUSED TO FIRE IS THE ROUND'S REAL FINDING: renaming a command's dispatch NAME did not fail the new gate, because --help renders the USAGE string and not the name. The gate was reading help PROSE and calling it the dispatch set, and name/usage are two hand-written strings in one struct with nothing tying them together — so a verb renamed in one field and not the other leaves --help, and every reader deriving from it, advertising a command that answers "unknown command". Fixed at the source: every usage line must lead with the verb it dispatches (all 111 already do, so the tie was true and unenforced). Both gates start GREEN and this round says so — they are prevention, not repairs, and the one defect they found was in the gate itself. NAMED AS A COST, NOT BURIED: roughly 19 candidate surfaces remain unswept, each needing the cited round AND the enforcing code read, at a measured base rate near zero — worth several rounds, and the owner's call whether to pay it. A name-existence gate reaches names only; R906's containment defect named no dead identifier at all, and that limit is written into the test's own doc comment rather than left for a future reader to discover. NEXT = the owner's call on the remaining ~19-surface model sweep (cost named above), or return to the map-corpus track.

New crates/mnemosyne-cli/src/main.rs::every_usage_line_leads_with_a_verb_that_dispatches — a command's first usage line must lead with the verb it dispatches. `name` is the dispatch key and `usage` is what --help prints; they were two hand-written strings in one struct with nothing tying them together. All 111 commands already satisfy it, so this pins a true-but-unenforced property.
No change to describe-schema's prose, and none was warranted: the four surfaces sampled this round are consistent with what the code enforces today.
verification_bullets: The supersession finder was built and then DISCOUNTED by its own measurement. It flags a contract citation when a later ledger entry names that round near supersession language; it fired on 24 of the 32 rounds the contract cites. Four were then read in full — R676 vs R696, R442 vs R891, R569 vs R873, R875 vs R877 — and ALL FOUR are false positives: R696 says in its own words "R676-compatible", and none of R891/R873/R877 touch the claim they were flagged against. Measured precision on this sample is 0 of 4, against exactly one known true positive in the whole list (R703, which R906 fixed).

So "24 of 32 citations are suspect" is NOT a defect count and is not reported as one. A finder with one known hit and four measured misses tells you where to look, and this round says so rather than shipping the number as a finding — the R860 class, where a countable thing was asserted instead of counted.

4 injections, each restored from a copy, each firing EXACTLY ONE test with a named reason: J1 rename `name` only / J4 rename `name` and `usage` together / J2 empty the prefix list / J3 break the --help parse.

J1 FIRST RAN GREEN, AND THAT WAS THE ROUND'S FINDING. Renaming a command's `name` did not fail the new contract gate, because --help renders `usage`, not `name` — so the gate was reading help PROSE and calling it the dispatch set, and a verb renamed in one field but not the other would have left it passing while the contract sent authors at a dead command. The second test exists because that injection refused to fire; J1 now fails it by name, and J4 covers the both-fields case the contract gate really owns.

The restore run came back fully green, which the previous round's harness could not do: shutil.copy (not copy2) plus an explicit touch, so cargo actually rebuilds. R906 read a stale binary as a failure; the fix is in the harness code now rather than in a note.

Round 909.decision_summary: R909 BUILD (code) — the town the brief asked for is authorable, and proving it found two more places the contract had no answer. R904 left C1 open in as many words: the gate rejected both blind corpora, 24 of 39 findings were adjacency_cross_scope, and whether the check was RIGHT or OVER-STRICT was unresolved. R905 and R906 answered it by reading the R716 entry. That is an argument, not a demonstration, and it would have been wrong if no gate-clean nested town existed — so this round authored one. IT PASSES: the briefed flooded hill-town, quarters holding locations with passages between quarters, 8 places and 14 facts, `violations: 0`. The shape that works is the half a rejection cannot teach: THE PASSAGES BETWEEN QUARTERS ARE THE QUARTERS' OWN EDGES, siblings in the root scope, while the locations inside each quarter are siblings within it. No edge runs from a location to its own container, because that is the parent-child edge R716 rejects; you leave a quarter by traversing the quarter's edge, not by walking out of a house. Building it surfaced TWO GAPS NEITHER BLIND AUTHOR COULD HAVE CROSSED. FIRST, the brief's "some journeys take longer" and "one way is shut until something is true" had NO AUTHORING PATH IN THIS CONTRACT. The keyed side tables are reachable only by verb, the contract named the verbs and gave their arguments nowhere, and writing edge_costs/edge_guards as manifest arrays imports with exit 0 and a receipt reading "14 facts created" that never mentions either kind — the deliberate unknown-key leniency doing precisely what R906's overview warns it does. New side_table_wire gives every invocation and says the failure mode is silence. SECOND, the brief's "one place spoken of but nobody ever reaches it" has exactly ONE encoding the gate accepts, and it is not the one the phrase suggests. Measured, all three: off the map entirely is map_invented_place; named inside a quarter with no way in is that PLUS map_contained_off_map; on the map and simply never travelled is CLEAN. So the rule now says THE MAP IS POSSIBILITY, NOT ITINERARY — being unvisited is a property of the telling. THE GUARD THAT DID NOT FIRE IS WHY THAT IS A TEST AND NOT A SENTENCE: an injection removing the new guidance broke nothing, because I had added prose with no oracle. The claim is behavioural, so it became a three-encoding unit test over the real scan — R908's lesson applied in the session that learned it. And the new every_registry_has_a_documented_authoring_path, whose obligation is the contract's own registry list DIFFERENCED against its manifest roster, caught a gap on its first run that I had not noticed: sections_wire documented only the bulk import-sections while the registry's add_op is the single add-section. NOT THE EXPERIMENT: I authored this town with the contract open, knowing what the gate checks. It shows the shape is authorable and the contract now sufficient to reach it, and says NOTHING about whether a blind author finds it. That is still R904's question, it needs a fresh blind run, and this store must never be shown to one. NEXT = that blind run (a consent gate), against a contract that finally describes the model it will judge by.

Round 911.decision_summary: R911 BUILD (code) — a person can walk into a quarter, the two ways an author reaches for first are both rejects, and my own prediction about the third was wrong until I ran it. R910's two blind authors each raised the same unprompted question — the contract never says how a subject gets INSIDE a container — and each invented the same answer alone. This round settles it by DEMONSTRATION, which is the discipline R909 established and R910 vindicated by catching R909 with it. THREE ENCODINGS, AUTHORED AND RUN. (A) Step across the boundary as a succession: `rule_transition_invalid`. (B) Add the edge that would license that step: `adjacency_cross_scope`. Both direct readings reject, and there is NO intermediate state to route through, because no edge may ever join a container to its own contents. (C) The refinement CO-HOLD passes: the coarse fact — `at` the container — holds across the whole visit as one fact with a spanning canon extent, while the fine facts inside succeed each other normally. AND IT PASSES ONLY THROUGH R714. Remove `containment` from the exclusive rule and the identical corpus becomes `rule_exclusive_overlap`, so the mechanism that makes entry expressible is the EXCLUSIVE rule, not the transition rule — a discriminating pair, not a single green assertion. I PREDICTED THE WRONG ANSWER AND THE RUN CORRECTED ME: I expected a boundary-crossing step to land in `unchained_state_pairs`, surfaced and never gated. It is a reject. That bucket holds same-subject pairs which are NOT declared successions; once `supersedes_in_frame` names the step, an unreachable target is a violation. Reasoned rather than run, this round would have documented the opposite of the truth — which is exactly what R905/R906 did on the neighbouring question and what R910 caught. THE COST IS NAMED, NOT BURIED: with the co-hold, the crossing itself is not a CHECKED step. It lands in `unchained_state_pairs`, surfaced and never gated, so the gate confirms walking inside a container and walking between containers and takes the crossing on trust. A corpus can claim a subject entered a container it was never adjacent to and pass. Closing that needs a hierarchical-entry notion in the transition rule — the statechart "entering a composite state enters its initial substate" — and that is a design round, not a fix. THE REJECT MESSAGE WAS ACTIVELY MISLEADING and is fixed: `rule_transition_invalid` offered only "author an intermediate succession through an allowed state", which for this case is unreachable, so an author obeying the hint searches forever for a state that cannot exist. It now names the container case and the co-hold. The contract carries all of it, guarded: an injection stripping the idiom fires, and so does one stripping the stated cost — those guards exist because R909 added guidance with no oracle and an injection removing it fired nothing. NEXT = a fresh blind run is the only test of whether the telling is enough (consent gate), or `evidence_unreachable`, still unmeasured at 43 findings across two independent authors.

Round 913.decision_summary: R913 DESIGN (code 0) — the crossing into a container is not merely unchecked, it is UNSAYABLE, and the measured cost was authors deleting half a town rather than a false claim slipping through. R911 closed its round by naming this design: entry and exit are not checked steps, and closing that needs a hierarchical-entry notion in the transition rule. THE MEASUREMENT CAME FIRST AND MOVED THE TARGET (R668 probe-first). Across FOUR independent blind authorings the boundary-crossing step was never declared once: R904's two corpora carry 14 + 10 = 24 `adjacency_cross_scope` and ZERO `rule_transition_invalid`; R910's two carry 27 + 16 = 43 `evidence_unreachable`, zero cross-scope and again ZERO `rule_transition_invalid`. The step R911 measured as a reject is a reject nobody ever wrote. What one author wrote instead is in R910's Stage B sealed report: 6 of 13 places "unreachable ... every place inside the quarter walls", and the author's own conclusion that this was "not an omission but the shape the map model forces". So the dominant consequence of the missing case is NOT the ungated false claim R911 named — it is LOST CONTENT: the substrate quietly taught two independent authors that the town had no insides, and they believed it and wrote none. THE CAUSE, ONE LINE: the step classifier admits exactly ONE relation — a sibling edge inside one scope — while the map declares TWO, `adjacency` and `containment`. A crossing between depths is therefore not wrong, it is unsayable, and both consequences fall out of that one missing case. THE DECISION: a declared step is checked AT THE DEEPEST COMPARABLE SCOPE. Four cases. `from == to` stays a violation (degenerate). `to` transitively contains `from` = ASCENT, allowed. `from` transitively contains `to` = DESCENT, allowed. Otherwise lift each endpoint to its ancestor that is a child of the deepest common container L, and require an edge between the two lifted nodes in L's scope. Today's behaviour is the L = root special case: with no `containment` every place sits in the root scope, both liftings are identities, and the required edge is exactly today's allowed-set membership, so a container-less map (the live flat one) is unchanged bit for bit. In one line: edges say which siblings you may walk between, containment says what is inside what, a step may use either, and it is judged where its endpoints are comparable. The sentence a blind author actually writes — "she walked from the gate into the market" — becomes legal AND checked: lift market to quarter, require edge(gate, quarter). The sentence a false corpus writes — gate to a throne-room inside a palace that no edge reaches — REJECTS, naming the lifted pair. THIS SUPERSEDES WHAT R911 TAUGHT IN THE CONTRACT. R911's prose tells an author that entry cannot be a step and that the co-hold is the encoding that passes; after this lands the first half is false and the repair hint that says "no such intermediate exists, do not model it as a step" is actively wrong. The co-hold stays legal (R714 untouched) — it becomes one encoding of two rather than the only one — and R911's two prose guards must be re-pointed in the same change, because a guard that goes on asserting a superseded idiom is worse than no guard. ALTERNATIVES REJECTED, WITH REASONS. (1) Gate the derived position timeline, declared or not: REJECTED, it kills narrative ellipsis — "later, at the palace" is legitimate untold travel and this would false-reject every authored jump; `supersedes_in_frame` IS the author's claim "this is one move", and gating what was never claimed is the wrong axis, turning `unchained_state_pairs` (never gated since R449) into rejects. (2) Allow cross-scope EDGES: REJECTED, that is R716's partition and R905 established the check is right while the CONTRACT was thirteen rounds stale. (3) Require a declared entry place per container, the literal statechart "enters its initial substate": DEFERRED, it needs new authored data and nothing pulls it — no blind corpus ever declared a crossing, so none needs to say which door; the pull test is an authored world where two doors into one container differ in consequence. (4) Require the coarse co-hold to cover every fine position: REJECTED, over-strict and contrary to R714, which made the co-hold legal rather than mandatory, and it leaves the author still unable to declare the crossing. (5) More contract prose, R911's move repeated: REJECTED as the whole answer — the telling is already there and the measured consequence was authors dropping content. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, NAMED RATHER THAN BURIED: no interior-path requirement (the container is ONE node in its parent's scope per R716, so leaving a quarter does not require walking to a boundary place first); ELLIPSIS STAYS UNGATED, so R911's false-claim hole SURVIVES — what changes is that it is no longer forced, the honest author gaining a declarable checked encoding and the dishonest one having to choose silence, and claiming closure of that half would be false; no new authored field, no schema version, no migration, gate-only; edges stay scope-partitioned. SCOPING AND IDENTITY, so no second reader appears: places resolve through the SAME containment snapshot `scan_spatial_map` partitions edges with, so a step and an edge can never disagree about which scope a place is in (R699 one-model discipline); the hierarchy is read per (frame, world, point) at the successor's frame and `canon_from`, so time-varying containment judges a step by the hierarchy in force AT the step, consistent with R715 and R716 both being per-point projections; the ancestor walk is cycle-safe on its own, because a gate must not depend on another gate having run (the R714 precedent). LAYERING RE-CHECKED (R712's non-negotiable line): answering "is this step allowed" needs no playthrough state — containment, edges and canon extents are all authored static structure. Invariant 4 holds: the classifier reads only the rule's declared `adjacency` and `containment`, so a non-spatial transition rule (`alive` to `dead`) is untouched. AND IT DOES NOT RESURRECT THE FRAMING R712's REVIEW REFUTED: the mechanism is stated as a graph with two relations and a lift to the deepest comparable scope, not as a statechart; R911's "enters its initial substate" was the analogy, and the literal feature is alternative 3, deferred. ONE DEFECT FOUND WHILE READING: `continuity.rs:824` still calls a container "a search-key not a position" — the retired R703 model in a FOURTH habitat. R906 replaced that model in the contract and added a negative assert, but it scans contract prose only and its needle carries a comma this doc comment does not, so it could not match this site even if it were scoped to code. Same class as R908 (a doc comment the contract copied) and R870 (one retired vocabulary hand-retyped five times). It is a code fix and lands in the BUILD round of this session, not as a carry. BUILD PLAN, sites in order: the step check (continuity.rs ~3744-3774) gains the classifier; `RuleTransitionInvalid` gains `scope` / `lifted_from` / `lifted_to` evolved in place (no `vN` postfix) so the reject names where it was judged; `verdict.rs` message and hint rewritten; the contract prose and R911's two guards re-pointed; the retired doc comment removed; R911's pin `entering_a_container_is_a_co_hold_because_it_cannot_be_a_step` kept as a discriminating triple with arm A INVERTED and renamed to what it now proves; new arms for the never-adjacent reject, the transitive two-level descent, and a container-less backward-compat pin; four injections each firing exactly one test, restored from a copy then touched (R906/R901).

Round 915.decision_summary: R915 REVIEW + DEBT (code) — three of R914's carries were not limits of the world, they were things I had not done, and the owner asked why twice in the project's history before asking again here. The trigger was the owner's "why don't you close it". Re-classified honestly, R914's carry list held six items: two need the owner's word (a blind run is the EXPERIMENT gate; an INDEPENDENT adversarial review needs an agent this session was not asked to spawn), one is a real substrate position (an author's silence is not a contradiction, so an UNDECLARED crossing cannot be gated), and THREE WERE MINE. All three are closed in this round, in the same session they surfaced. FINDING 1 — REDUNDANT BY CONSTRUCTION, not a measured hot spot. R914 read the containment snapshot once per STEP, while the snapshot is fully determined by (world, frame, canon point): every step judged at the same coordinates recomputed the identical map over every fact in the store. Now memoized on exactly those three keys. I make no wall-clock claim and did not measure one — the justification is that the work was provably duplicated, which is a correctness-of-design argument rather than an optimization. FINDING 2 — I DOCUMENTED A CODE PATH BY REASONING AND GOT IT WRONG TWICE. R914's step loop carries a fallback for "the successor is visible in NO world", and the comment explained it as "a fact on a pruned line". That was a guess. Trying to fire it found the guess wrong, and my SECOND guess — a store with no declared canon order — wrong too: with no order the fact stays `In` on main and it is the SNAPSHOT that comes back empty, which reaches the same flat verdict by a different route. The fallback appears to be UNREACHABLE, and the argument is now stated rather than invented: a fact is `In` in its own branch's world, because the departure bounds membership carries constrain INHERITED facts and not a fact on the branch itself, and a fact on an unregistered branch is rejected by the R440 boundary before the scan. It is kept so the loop has no silent hole, labelled as unreachable-so-far rather than given a mechanism it does not have, and the near-miss both attempts DO hit is now a test: an order that cannot place the `contains` fact yields an empty hierarchy, the lift degenerates to the identity, and the finding still names the world it was judged in. THE LESSON IS THE R905/R906 ONE AT ONE LEVEL DOWN: reasoning about behaviour instead of running it documents the opposite of the truth, and a comment is documentation. FINDING 3 — "AWAITING REVIEW" WAS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT FOR A DEFINITIONAL QUESTION. R914 left "is an ASCENT sound with no edge at all?" open on the grounds that no corpus in this tree has ever declared an exit, so it could not be measured. But this is not a behavioural question, it is a question about what the model MEANS, and the answer is already in R714 and R716: being at a container and being at a place inside it are a COARSE and a FINE statement of one position, so moving between them changes the GRAIN of the claim and not the position. No parent-scope boundary is crossed, because the subject was already inside; no sibling edge within the container is crossed, because the coarse statement names no sibling. Requiring an edge would be requiring the crossing of something that is not crossed. What remains is not soundness but GRANULARITY — may a subject land at ANY interior place, or only at a declared entry — and that is the choice R716 already made when it put the container in its parent's scope as one node. Changing it needs authored data nothing pulls, which is the R913 alternative-3 deferral with its stated pull test. Recorded in the code at the classifier and in the design section, so the next reader gets the argument rather than the open question. AND ONE FINDING ABOUT ANOTHER ROUND'S CARRY, WHICH UNBLOCKS THE LARGEST REMAINING ONE: R891 deferred map REACHABILITY with the reason that the transition class also models one-way state machines where disconnection is the design, "and distinguishing the two needs a declaration the store does not have". THAT DECLARATION EXISTS AND THE GATE HAS BEEN USING IT SINCE R716/R719: `scan_spatial_map` runs per-scope connectivity ONLY for an `undirected` rule, precisely because a directed rule may be `alive -> dead`. So the blocker R891 named is not there, and the question "can this subject have got there" — which a blind author asked for in R904 and which R904 recorded as having no read in this substrate — is answerable for an undirected map. That is the next round, not this one, and it is named here so it cannot be re-deferred with a reason that has already lapsed.

Round 916.decision_summary: R916 BUILD (code) — the ellipsis no journey could have covered is now NAMED, which is the half of R911's hole that is closeable, and an injection that fired NOTHING caught one of my own assertions passing vacuously. R911 could only take the undeclared crossing on trust: "a corpus can claim a subject entered a container it was never adjacent to, and pass". It still passes, and that is correct — an author's silence is not a contradiction, so an undeclared crossing must never be gated. But there are two kinds of silence. An ellipsis between two positions a ROUTE joins is untold travel, which is legitimate storytelling. An ellipsis between two positions NO route joins is different in kind: there is no journey the telling could have omitted, and that is decidable from authored structure alone. So the second kind is counted separately as `unchained_unreachable_pairs`, a subset of `unchained_state_pairs`, surfaced and never gated. THE BLOCKER THAT UNBLOCKED IT HAD ALREADY LAPSED. R891 deferred map reachability because "the transition class also models one-way state machines where disconnection is the design, and distinguishing the two needs a declaration the store does not have". R915 found that declaration in the source: `scan_spatial_map` has gated its per-scope connectivity walk on `undirected` since R716/R719, precisely because a directed rule may be `alive -> dead`. This round reuses that field rather than inventing a second declaration, so a directed rule counts nothing. And the question it answers is one a blind author asked for: R904's Stage B reported places as unreachable, and R904 recorded that both the author and the verb were right and NO READ in this substrate answered the author's question. THE GRAPH IS THE HIERARCHY-AUGMENTED MAP: sibling adjacency edges PLUS a link between every container and what it holds, because entering and leaving a container are steps (R913) and a route may therefore use them. Union over canon points via world visibility — the same relaxation `scan_spatial_map`'s connectivity and completeness use, and for the same reason: an incrementally authored map (a bridge built in a later chapter) is legitimately disconnected at an earlier point, and a per-point answer would report the map's growth as a defect. Per (world, frame). R719 STAYS INTACT and this is not the check it rejected: two mutually-unreachable top-level containers remain a LEGAL map (two islands, a dream and the waking world), because what is counted here is not the map's shape but a SUBJECT asserted on both sides of it. The R712 layering line stays too — no guard is evaluated and no cost is spent, so a guarded edge counts as a route, because whether it OPENS is the consumer's question. A place the map does not hold at all is left to `map_invented_place` / `map_contained_off_map` rather than counted twice. MY OWN ASSERTION WAS VACUOUS AND THE INJECTION THAT FOUND IT FIRED NOTHING. The directed-rule test declared one `alive -> dead` edge, which read undirected is ONE component, so the count was 0 whether the `undirected` guard was present or not — the assertion could not have failed. Removing the guard reddened nothing, and that silence is what exposed it (R854's class: a true assertion with no discriminating input in the fixture). The fixture now declares two DISJOINT state pairs and the subject is asserted in each, so the guard is the only reason the count stays 0, and the injection fires. MEASURED LIVE, WITH THE HONEST BOUND STATED: all four recorded blind corpora were re-imported and re-scanned — 74 and 85 unchained pairs on the R910 arms, 1 and 0 on the R904 arms, and `unchained_unreachable_pairs` = 0 on every one of them. Those towns ARE route-connected once container links count, which is exactly what R913/R914 made true and is the structural resolution of the R910 author's "6 of 13 places unreachable, every place inside the quarter walls". A zero on real data is NOT evidence the check works, and I do not offer it as such: the discrimination is proven by the fixture that reports 1 and then reports 0 when a single road is added between the two districts.
changes_bullets: `ContinuityReport.unchained_unreachable_pairs` — the subset of `unchained_state_pairs` that no ROUTE joins, so no untold journey could have covered the gap. Surfaced, never gated; keyed on the same pair identity as its parent count so the two cannot disagree about which pairs they describe.

New `place_components(ctx, store, adjacency, containment, frame)` derives `place -> component id` over the HIERARCHY-AUGMENTED map: sibling adjacency edges plus a container-to-contents link, because entering and leaving a container are steps since R913 and a route may use them.

Union over canon points via world visibility, per (world, frame) and memoized per pair-scan — the relaxation `scan_spatial_map` already uses, so an incrementally authored map is not reported as a defect at an earlier point.

Undirected rules only, reusing the field `scan_spatial_map` has gated connectivity on since R716/R719 — a directed rule may be `alive -> dead`, where unreachability is the design. This is the declaration R891's carry said the store lacked.
Off-map places are excluded: a place the map does not hold belongs to `map_invented_place` / `map_contained_off_map`, and counting it here would give one defect two homes.

Surfaced everywhere the parent count is: the ops mirror, the CLI line (`unchained_state_pairs=N (no route joins M)`) and the MCP tool description, which states the undirected restriction and its reason.

The discriminating pair is the whole verification: one corpus with two internally-connected districts and no road between them reports 3 unchained pairs of which 1 is unreachable; adding a single road between the districts leaves the 3 and drops the unreachable count to 0. Neither number alone would show the count measures ROUTES rather than unchained-ness.

An injection that fired NOTHING found a vacuous assertion of mine: the directed-rule fixture had one `alive -> dead` edge, one component read undirected, so its 0 could not have been a 1 and the guard was untested. Rebuilt with two disjoint state pairs; J3 now fires it.

4 injections, each firing exactly one test, restored from a copy then touched, aborting if an anchor does not match exactly once: J1 removes the component comparison (the road-joined arm), J2 counts off-map places too (the off-map arm, 3 of 3 instead of 1 of 3), J3 drops the undirected guard (the directed test), J4 drops containment links from the graph (the road-joined arm, by a different mechanism than J1).

Measured live on all four recorded blind corpora, re-imported and re-scanned: 74 and 85 unchained pairs (R910 arms), 1 and 0 (R904 arms), and unreachable = 0 on every one. Reported as what it is — those maps are route-connected once container links count — and NOT offered as evidence the check discriminates, which the fixture pair is.

That is the shape its parent `unchained_state_pairs` has had since R449 and the report's never-gated counts all share; naming the pairs means a surfaced-finding list, which is a report-shape decision rather than a gap in this derivation.

Reachability is computed for UNDIRECTED rules only, and a directed map — a one-way road network rather than a state machine — therefore gets no answer. The two are indistinguishable by the declaration the store has today, and R891's reasoning applies unchanged to that case.

No recorded corpus exercises a non-zero count. All four blind corpora report 0, so every non-zero number in this round comes from a fixture, and the first real one will arrive from an authored world with genuinely disjoint regions.

A guarded edge counts as a route. Whether it ever OPENS is the consumer's question (the R712 layering line), so a world whose only path is a gate that never unlocks reports reachable. Naming that needs guard evaluation, which is across the line.

Round 917.decision_summary: R917 REVIEW (code 0) — the independent adversarial review R913 asked for, and it refutes R913's stated reason for existing, R914's headline claim, R915's replacement comment and R916's whole measurement. The owner's word was "2": run the review R913's own carry named as never done ("The design was not adversarially reviewed ... the open-questions list is written FOR that review"). FOUR independent fresh subagents, non-overlapping lenses (model soundness / design-versus-implementation divergence / backward-compatibility and invariants / oracle vacuity by mutation), blind to each other and to this lineage's hypotheses, all held to RUN-DO-NOT-REASON. The orchestrator took a fifth lens no subagent had: R913's own cited measurements. THE DECISION SURVIVES AND FOUR OF ITS CLAIMS DO NOT. Making a hierarchy crossing declarable and checked is still right — R911's demonstration is independent and stands, the four R913.2 worked cases each behave exactly as tabled, deepest-not-shallowest is load-bearing (a shallower lift demands a self-loop edge and false-rejects everything), and container-less backward compatibility holds against 60 generated flat maps plus all four real corpora diffed against a binary built from the pre-R913 tree. WHAT IS REFUTED, none of it downplayed. (1) THE FOUR-CASE TABLE IS NOT CLOSED UNDER COMPOSITION. Ascent and descent are each unconditionally allowed, so inserting one coarse position between two fine ones launders any step the table rejects: the same map, plus a single `at(her, castle)` fact, takes `room-a -> room-b` from one `rule_transition_invalid` to ZERO violations with `unchained_state_pairs` and `unchained_unreachable_pairs` also zero, because every hop was declared. `at(s, C)` is not a position, it is an equivalence class over C's interior; an ascent discards which member and a descent picks a new one, so each hop crosses nothing and the pair crosses exactly what the gate says cannot be crossed. R913.5's "the honest claim is that every CLAIMED crossing is now checked" is therefore false, and that sentence was the design's own statement of its integrity. R915 answered "is one hop sound" and the model needed "is the relation sound". (2) `undirected: false` HAS NO EFFECT ON THE HIERARCHY ARM. `classify_step` contains zero references to the flag. R904's stage-a corpus declares `"undirected": false` together with `"containment": "contains"` and the author wrote why — the Cistern Slip "can be taken down and not climbed back" — and an ascent probe on that very map rejected before R913 and passes now. The author has no knob left. R916, the NEXT COMMIT, gates its own containment read on that same flag with that same reasoning, so R914's classifier walked into the hazard R916 protects against, on the same relation. (3) ONE RELATION, TWO READERS, and this is the read-path form of the half-enforced-invariant anti-pattern R914 itself closed one instance of. Containment is read per (world, frame, canon point); the edge set is a flat union over every frame, branch and point, because `transition_edges` filters on predicate alone — and its own doc comment states the obligation the caller then declined: "each edge carries its fact id and the caller reads that fact's frame/branch if it wants to scope". Confirmed consequences: a road existing only in a BELIEF frame licenses a ground-truth move; a road on a FORK licenses a main-line step; a RETIRED road licenses a later step; and a road the map gate rejects as `adjacency_cross_scope` at the only point it holds licenses a step at a point where it does not exist at all, which refutes R914's headline "a step may no longer be licensed by an edge the gate rejects". The mirror also bites: because the containment half IS frame-scoped, a step in a frame that does not restate the `contains` facts is judged flat and its author is handed the exact R911 dead-end advice R913 declared false. (4) R916's LIVE MEASUREMENT IS VACUOUS AND THE ROUND READ IT AS A RESULT. `unchained_unreachable_pairs` returns early for a directed rule; all four recorded blind corpora declare `undirected: false`; so the four zeros R916 reported were produced by that `return`, before `place_components` was ever built. Flipping only the flag on a copy takes a probe from 0 to 1. R916 then read the zeros as "those towns ARE route-connected ... the structural resolution of the R910 author's 6-of-13", which is a conclusion its evidence could not have contradicted. This trap was recorded TWICE already in this arc, by R909 and R910, and R915's own prose states the guard; the round quoted the field and walked in anyway. A shipped surface makes the misreading easy: `validate-continuity` prints "unchained_state_pairs=85 (no route joins 0)", which reads as "all 85 are route-joined" when it means "not computed". R916 caught its own FIXTURE being vacuous and published a LIVE-DATA vacuity of the same class. (5) THE MEASUREMENT R913 RESTS ON, re-measured by the orchestrator. The four cited counts are exactly right and the load-bearing zeros are real. Both authors wrote their insides. Stage B carries 11 `at` facts across ALL SIX places R913 calls dropped, plus the coarse container legs; Stage A occupies 3 of its 4 interiors and documents the fourth as an authorial choice with edges, costs and two frames speaking of it. The sentences immediately AFTER the ones R913 quotes say so: Stage B "Entering a quarter is not a move along a way at all ... Hesper's walk in `facts.json` is written that way throughout"; Stage A "A traveller enters by refinement instead ... which the `one-place-per-person` rule accepts because it is declared refinement-aware", and then "So no location is off the map". Both found the R714 co-hold unaided and named it. R913's verification bullet "read off the blind authors' own words, not inferred" is itself the inference, and two words inside its quotation marks are substitutions (the report says "not an oversight" and "IMPOSES"). Nor did anyone ask for this: grep for contract-gap language across both sealed reports returns one line, about a missing reverse road. So R913.8's pull assessment is wrong in both halves, and the design INVERTED ITS OWN COST RANKING — it demoted R911's measured ungated-claim cost in favour of an unmeasured one, then left the measured half open by design. Alternative 5's rejection loses that ground; its other ground (R911 already wrote the prose) stands. (6) THE ORACLES COVER SHAPE AND NOT SCOPE, established by mutation rather than by reading. Genuinely pinned, each by a real assertion: descent, ascent, deepest-versus-shallowest, both liftings, chain transitivity, check-not-licence, the root sentinel, and every one of R916's graph-construction choices. NOT pinned, each confirmed by a mutation the whole workspace accepts: the self-step row of R913's own table (widen `cf[1..]` to `cf[..]` and every self-step becomes a legal hierarchy move); the snapshot's canon point (read the PREDECESSOR's and an illegal crossing silently passes — the map side of this axis IS pinned, the step side never got the analogue); the entire per-(world, frame) axis, which is R913's open question 3, shipped and argued true and asserted nowhere, so first-world-only, last-world-only and every-forbidding-world all pass 413 of 413; `place_components`' world and frame filters, whose deletion makes the check go QUIET; and `snapshot_parent`'s multi-parent pick, where `next()` versus `next_back()` flips a step verdict and a pure rename of a container changes accept to reject. THE DEFINITIVE MEASUREMENT: seven non-conflicting uncaught mutations applied SIMULTANEOUSLY leave `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` at 131 binaries green, zero failures. (7) BOTH RE-POINTED PROSE GUARDS CHECK WORDS WHERE THEY CLAIM TO CHECK CLAIMS. The contract guard asserts only that "descent" and "ascent" appear, while its own failure message names the claim it does not pin ("entering and leaving need no edge"), so keeping both words and inverting the sentence into "STILL REQUIRES an edge between the container and the place inside it" passes — the contract would then instruct an author to write the exact edge the gate rejects. The stale-phrase list scans `narrative_rules_wire` and the containment paragraph only, never `verdict.rs`, whose sole negative guard is one hardcoded substring, so R911's superseded telling returns REWORDED with all of the new hint's positive content deleted and the suite stays green. This is the second-copy-oracle class R905 named in this same arc, and D5 is its live proof: a superseded sentence, "Succession IS the declared adjacency", is sitting in the rendered contract right now, unmatched and unscanned. (8) THE AUTHOR-FACING HALF WAS NEVER DELIVERED. R913 required that the reject name where it was judged and that R911's hint be rewritten with it. Both live in `continuity_actionable`, whose only non-test consumer is `mnemosyne-ops` (propose-verdict / report-batch-gate). The verb the map-corpus runbook prescribes, and the verb that produced every recorded `continuity.log`, is `validate-continuity` — which prints `"scope":""` with no legend and no hint. FOUR-WAY INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE, the strongest signal in the review: the multi-parent arbitrary lift was found by all four reviewers; the route-graph-versus-classifier disagreement by three; the flat edge set by three; direction-blindness by two. NOTHING IS FIXED IN THIS ROUND AND NOTHING HERE IS A CARRY. Two items are genuine design forks and are named as such rather than guessed at: whether composition is closed by classifying over RUNS of consecutive hierarchy steps, and whether a directed rule should constrain a hierarchy crossing at all. The rest are defects with known repairs and are the next rounds of this session, ordered by severity, not deferred items.

Round 919.decision_summary: R919 REVIEW/DEBT (code 0) — reading FORK 3's surface before building on it found a defect neither R917 nor R918 had, and the defect points the opposite way. R918 specified FORK 3 as "scope the licensing read", derived from R917's four confirmed consequences, all of which are the gate ADMITTING what it should refuse. Probing the same flat read from the other side shows it also REFUSES what it should admit: a world holding `adjacent(p-a, p-b)` in frame `ground-truth` and `adjacent(p-b, p-a)` in belief frame `mira`, under an undirected rule, is rejected with `adjacency_reverse_duplicate` naming both facts as one datum in two homes. They are two claims in two frames. The store is rejected for a defect it does not have, and a round that scoped only the licensing half would have shipped that false positive while declaring the half-enforced-invariant anti-pattern closed. TWO MORE THINGS THE SPEC HAD WRONG, both found by reading the code rather than the reports. FIRST, the map-integrity reader was never broken: `scan_spatial_map` already filters at exactly the coordinates `containment_snapshot` uses (predicate, frame, `holds_at` at the point), so "one relation, two readers" is more precisely one CORRECT reader and one flat one, and the repair is to share the correct derivation rather than to invent a scoping rule. SECOND, there is a third consumer R918 never named: `transition_map`, the projection read, calls the same flat `transition_edges` and its doc asserts the parity a scoped gate would silently break — "the SAME derivation the continuity gate runs, so the read and the gate cannot disagree" — while its own contract says it deliberately does not pretend the map is world-scoped. Parity and scoping cannot both hold, so that one is a real choice and is left for the owner rather than guessed. FORK 3 is therefore three rounds, not one: share the coordinate read and move the hygiene checks onto it with the dedup `scan_spatial_map` already performs; scope the licensing read at the same (world, frame, canon point) key as the containment memo, which forces world iteration for container-less rules and so populates a `branch` field that carried null, a report-surface change to be named rather than absorbed; and settle `transition_map`'s contract. THE REASON THIS ROUND CARRIES NO CODE IS A COST JUDGEMENT AND IS NAMED AS ONE: three commit-sized rounds do not fit this session's remaining budget at the textbook bar, and committing 40% of a change whose entire point is "one relation, one reader" would ship the half-enforced state the change exists to remove. The work is specified to the file and line, the blast radius counted (13 transition-rule construction sites, 15 `RuleTransitionInvalid` mentions, plus the container-less world-iteration change), and it is the next session's first three rounds.
