Round 921.decision_summary: R921 BUILD — the arc's load-bearing measurement is now produced by the code that ships, and producing it corrected the number. R918 rested FORK 1's scope and the whole "all three defects are unwitnessed" framing on M2: 86 authored steps, every one a lift, zero hierarchy crossings. That number came from a session-local re-implementation of `classify_step`, corroborated against R914's recorded 8 but never executed, and R920 had just measured what that class of instrument costs when a prose regex answered for the data and under-counted one-way roads by half. So this round makes the classifier say it itself. `judge_steps` is now the ONE place a declared step is classified; the inline walk moved into it verbatim and the gate became a CALLER, passing a closure that pushes a `rule_transition_invalid` for the first unlicensed judgement per step and returns false to stop — the pre-R921 `break` expressed as a return value rather than control flow the function must understand. `ContinuityReport.step_judgements` carries every (step, judging world) verdict with its shape, scope, lifted pair, licence, frame, branch and canon point, ALWAYS populated because a knob may decide whether an axis fails and never whether it is measured (R663), and `validate-continuity` prints the split so a run with no crossings and a run that never classified any no longer look identical. RE-DERIVED THROUGH THE SHIPPING CODE, against the four recorded corpora copied to scratch: v1/stage-a 30 judgements with 5 unlicensed, v1/stage-b 27 with 3, v2/stage-a 31 with 0, v2/stage-b 25 with 0, and ZERO hierarchy crossings in all four. The unlicensed 5 and 3 are precisely R914's recorded 27-to-32 and 12-to-15, and the violation totals 32, 15, 27, 16 reproduce its re-measurement. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES AND THE UNIT DOES NOT: the shipping classifier counts 113, not 86, because it judges once per (step, WORLD) and a step visible in two worlds is judged twice — v2/stage-a, the only corpus without branches, is 31 under both counts. That is exactly the discrepancy no re-implementation can reveal about itself. The split is pinned by a DISCRIMINATING PAIR rather than a green assertion: one store is all lifts with the illegal pair caught, and the same store plus one coarse position is two hierarchy crossings catching nothing — all four corpora have zero crossings, so a `hierarchy` count hardcoded to 0 would pass every live measurement this arc has ever taken, and this pair is what forbids that. The oracle was injection-proven: mislabelling `StepShape::Hierarchy` as "lifted" at its single construction site fails the laundered arm, and restoring from a pristine copy returns it to green. A BUILD ERROR THIS ROUND CAUSED IS REPORTED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED: inserting the new test above an existing one stole that test's `#[test]` attribute, so `rule_transition_catches_disallowed_step` silently stopped being a test while the suite stayed GREEN; `clippy -D warnings` caught it as an unused function and `cargo test` alone did not, and the fix was verified by asking the harness to LIST the tests rather than by counting the suite, because the count had already disagreed with my arithmetic and a total is not an answer to whether one specific test runs. No verdict changed anywhere: the extraction is behaviour-preserving and 1387 tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt and validate-workspace are all green, so every defect FORK 3 and FORK 1 exist to repair is still open.

Round 925.decision_summary: R925 BUILD — FORK 1, the last of the three forks R918 resolved by measurement: the unit a transition rule judges is no longer the authored hop but the RUN. A maximal chain of consecutive hierarchy crossings by one subject, in one frame and one world, is ONE positional move — judged between the last place before the chain and the first place after it, with the finding attached to the fact that CLOSES the run and naming the interior as the route it went through. This is the model's own answer rather than a patch: R913's grain doctrine, following R714 and R716, says a crossing changes the GRAIN of a position claim and not the position, so a chain of crossings moves nobody either. Without it a step the map forbids is licensed by writing it THROUGH a container, and R918 reproduced exactly that in a store rather than arguing it (its M6): room-a to room-b with no door between them is one rule_transition_invalid, and inserting a single at(her, castle) fact between them takes the same world to violations 0 with both unchained counters also 0 — nothing anywhere recorded the laundering. THE EQUAL-ENDPOINT CLAUSE IS PART OF THE DECISION, NOT AN EXCEPTION TO IT: a run that returns to its start is `unmoved` and needs no edge, because she never left the room (R918's M7, found by probing the proposed repair rather than reasoning about it — a naive outer-endpoint lift ships a FALSE REJECT on a corpus that is correct today). It lives in its own function `classify_run` so that it cannot reach a lone a-to-a succession, which is R698's self-loop and still rejects; the injection that moves the clause into `classify_step` turns exactly that arm red. WHAT THE BUILD FOUND THAT THE DESIGN DID NOT: R921's own observability fixture WAS the laundering. Its second store is room-a to castle to room-b with no room-a/room-b door, and it asserted `unlicensed 0` with the comment "each hop is individually allowed — this is the laundering R918 measured". That assertion is now `unlicensed 1`, one lifted run reported once. The arm was rewritten rather than deleted and a LONE ASCENT arm added beside it, because the `hierarchy` count still needs a witness that a hardcoded 0 would fail — and the DIRECT arm of that test is untouched, which is the honesty axis: this round moved the unit of judgement, not the classifier under it. ANSWERED WITH DATA RATHER THAN CARRIED: R918's open question about worlds. The run is assembled PER WORLD, and one authored chain of two facts is TWO ordinary steps in a world with no hierarchy and ONE run in a fork where the castle holds the rooms — so the classifier may not be hoisted out of the world loop. MEASURED: the four recorded blind corpora, re-measured through the shipping binary, give violations 32 / 15 / 27 / 16 and steps judged 30 / 27 / 31 / 25, identical to R924, with hierarchy crossings 0, runs 0 and `unmoved` 0 in all four. Round 926.decision_summary: R926 DEBT — R925 shipped two per-world guards with no test, and an injection said so before a reviewer could. R925's run walk asks, in both directions, whether a neighbouring hop was judged in THIS world before composing it into a run; both checks passed the entire suite when blinded, which is the R909 class — guidance with no oracle. The pair is not decorative: the map is read only at coordinates a hop is actually judged at, so composing a hop the world cannot see reads a coordinate that was never filled. R925's carry called the mirror case "handled by construction, no arm of its own"; that was not a limit of the world, it was work not done, and this round does it. THE FORWARD half is ordinary authoring rather than a corner: the castle holds the rooms, one chain walks room-a to castle to room-b, and a fork departs at the castle — that world sees a woman step out of a room and stop, which is a crossing, allowed, complete as far as that world goes, while the world that stayed catches the whole run. THE BACKWARD half needed a PARTIAL canon order to construct at all, and the construction is the finding: within one branch an earlier fact is visible wherever a later one is, because succession never crosses a branch and both consult the same departure bounds, so COMPARABILITY is the only axis on which they can differ. With `ch-2` joined to nothing in the order, a fork departing at `ch-4` inherits `ch-1` and `ch-3` and cannot decide `ch-2`: the middle of the chain is Unknown there while both its ends are In, and that world must judge `castle -> room-b` as the descent it is rather than reach back through a position it cannot place. Both arms were then re-injected: each blinding now turns exactly one named test red, and nothing else.
changes_bullets: `a_world_that_leaves_mid_chain_judges_only_the_crossing_it_saw` — the forward guard's oracle: a fork departing at the castle judges the crossing it saw, while `main` catches the whole run through it.

Round 927.decision_summary: R927 DEBT — R917's five missing oracles, re-measured before being paid, and TWO OF THEM WERE ALREADY DEAD. The list is nine rounds old, so the round began by re-running every mutation against today's tree rather than working through the list. R925's arm E — written so a lone `a -> a` succession cannot become a return trip — also kills the self-step widening (`cf[1..]` to `cf[..]`), and R926's backward arm asserts an EXACT judgement list, so reading the hierarchy at the PREDECESSOR's canon point moves that list and turns it red. Neither round knew it was paying this debt, and writing the two arms R917 asked for would have produced a second copy of a test that already exists. THREE WERE STILL OPEN and are closed here. (1) THE PER-WORLD SHORT-CIRCUIT. `judge_steps` reports a forbidden unit ONCE, in the first world that forbids it; this is stated in three places — the `emit` contract, the gate's `false // one finding per step`, and the R921 comment above the call — and was asserted in none, so turning that `break` into a `continue`, and letting every forbidding world file its own finding, passed the entire workspace suite. The arm puts a forbidden unit AND a licensed one in front of two worlds: the licensed one is judged TWICE, which is what proves both worlds are live judges rather than a fixture where the second never looked, and the forbidden one is reported once. (2) AND (3) THE ROUTE GRAPH IS READ AT ONE (world, frame), and both halves of that coordinate were unpinned. Deleting either filter makes the check go QUIET, which is the dangerous direction: a road only a belief frame states, or a road only a fork built, joins two places the asserting world cannot walk between, and the ellipsis no journey could cover stops being named. One test moves ONE road between four coordinates — `mira` believes it (still named), a fork built it (still named), the ground truth holds it on the main line (unnamed), and the fork holds it with the traveller moved onto that branch (unnamed). The fourth arm is what keeps the second honest: a scoping assertion of this kind normally goes vacuous by the road failing to import, and only a coordinate where the SAME road DOES join can tell those two apart. That arm also replaced a first attempt that was simply wrong — a per-world `map_disconnected` read, which returns an empty list in every arm, because two districts that are both containers leave the root scope with no edge to disconnect. THE FIFTH IS NOT OMITTED BUT NOT ORACLE-SHAPED. `snapshot_parent` takes `conts.iter().next()`, so `next()` versus `next_back()` flips a step verdict and RENAMING a container — pure spelling, no change to the world — turns an accept into a reject. A test pinning `next()` would make an arbitrary pick the contract, which is precisely the R925 lesson about a fixture that ends up asserting the verdict it was written to condemn. The pick and its arm are ONE change, R917's debt item 6, and the next round.

Round 930.decision_summary: R930 DEBT — the superseded sentence was unscanned because the SURFACE was, and the probe R929 set up said so in one run. Adding `Succession IS the declared adjacency` to `SUPERSEDED_CROSSING_TELLINGS` and running the whole workspace changed NOTHING. The list already had three readers; the sentence was sitting on a FOURTH — the transition RULE-CLASS description, which nothing had ever scanned. So R917's item is not "a phrase missing from a list" but a contract surface with no coverage at all, and the phrase was merely what happened to be sitting on it. WHAT THE SENTENCE CLAIMED, and why both readings had to go: it is ambiguous between "succession supplies WHICH pairs are steps" (true, and the reason unchained pairs are surfaced rather than judged) and "a succession must BE an adjacency edge" (false since R913, because a crossing needs none). The neighbouring clause settled it toward the false one — "must form an ADJACENT `(from, to)` step" — so an author reading the rule-class prose learned that entering a container has to be an edge, which is precisely the R911 dead end R913 falsified and which `adjacency_cross_scope` then rejects. The same sentence sat in `continuity.rs`'s own type doc, so the code read as the contract did. Both now say what is true: succession says which pairs are steps, the declared map says which steps are allowed, and the two are NOT one relation. THE WIRE WAS SILENT ABOUT THE STEP SIDE, AND SILENCE READS AS THE OLD MODEL. Its containment paragraph described only the EDGE consequences of declaring containment — scopes, `adjacency_cross_scope`, the container as a portal node in its parent's scope — and said nothing about crossings, so an author who read the wire and not the rule-class prose knew the edge rule and nothing else, and reached the superseded conclusion by omission rather than by being told it. Round 934.decision_summary: R934 DEBT — the map's completeness class was silently inert, its two readers disagreed, and the contract blamed the wrong declaration. R933's arm C exposed a store that answers the map brief halfway and passes every gate: stage-b declares no predicate leg kinds, so `report-transition-map` prints all 21 edges while the frontier answers that the registered place set cannot be asked for. MEASURING BEFORE REPAIRING CHANGED THE ANSWER TWICE. First, requiring the declaration would reject THREE OF SIX recorded corpora — one author per arm, all three arms — which is the R924 error of gating a question no author was asked, so this round does NOT gate. Second, the hole is bigger than arm C showed: `map_invented_place` rides `severity` and is kind-gated, so on those three corpora a REJECT-SEVERITY class evaluated nothing and the run read `violations: 0`, and its own type doc already said "inert when neither leg declares a kind". The gate now NAMES the rule and the predicate whose completeness could not be asked — the R924 counter distinction applied to a finding CLASS, and the contract keeping its own stated word that a gate which evaluated nothing must never read like a gate that passed. Two readers of one relation are collapsed into one resolver: the gate took the FIRST declared leg while the frontier's map view took the UNION, so a predicate declaring two kinds had the ADVISORY surface policing more than the gate — the R919 mirror defect with the strict half on the wrong side. And the contract is corrected where it was actively WRONG rather than merely silent: both surfaces credited every completeness check to wiring `containment`, which all six authors did, so the three who declared no leg kind had every reason to believe the class was on. Also closes R933's harness defect at the runbook: the seeded toml no longer names a rules file the author is forbidden to read.
changes_bullets: ONE RESOLVER for the entity kinds a transition map treats as its nodes (`map_node_kinds`), read by BOTH the gate's completeness check and the map view the authoring frontier renders. The gate took the FIRST declared leg (`subject_kind.or(object_entity_kind)`) while the view took the UNION, so a predicate declaring two different kinds gave the reject-severity check a narrower place set than the advisory report beside it. `map_invented_place` now also names the kind the entity was actually judged against rather than the first leg.

`ContinuityReport.completeness_unaskable` (new `UnaskableCompleteness`), threaded through `ContinuityScanReport`, and a `validate-continuity` NOTICE naming the rule AND the predicate whose completeness class could not be asked. NOT a violation, by decision — see the verification.

The contract stops MISATTRIBUTING the turn-on. Both surfaces that described the completeness checks credited them to wiring `containment`; `map_invented_place` additionally needs the adjacency predicate's leg kind, and both now say so, with claim pins on each surface.
Harness fix in the map-corpus runbook: the seeded `mnemosyne.toml` no longer names a rules file, and the read step passes `--rules` explicitly, which is what all three arms already did in practice.
verification_bullets: MEASURED BEFORE REPAIRING (R927/R930 discipline), AND THE MEASUREMENT CHANGED THE ANSWER. The obvious repair — require a leg kind when a predicate is named as a transition rule's `adjacency` — would REJECT THREE OF THE SIX RECORDED CORPORA: v1/stage-a, v2/stage-a and v3/stage-b declare no leg kind on any predicate at all, one author per arm across all three arms. Rejecting half the corpus over a question no author was asked is exactly the R924 error, so the decision is NOT to gate. The contract already carried the right rule for this case in its own words — a gate that evaluated nothing must never read the same as a gate that passed — and this round is the gate keeping that word.

THE CLASS WAS SILENTLY INERT AND THE SOURCE SAID SO. `map_invented_place` rides `severity` yet sits inside `if let Some(pk) = place_kind`, and its type doc read "inert when neither leg declares a kind". Half of every blind authoring on record ran with a reject-severity class evaluating nothing and reported `violations: 0`.

TWO READERS OF ONE RELATION, WITH THE STRICT ONE ON THE ADVISORY SIDE (the R919 mirror class, and CLAUDE.md's two-write-paths anti-pattern applied to a read path): the frontier said "not derivable" while the gate said nothing, and on differing legs the frontier policed MORE than the gate. Nothing on record declares two different kinds, so the union change is verdict-neutral on every authored store and the discriminating input had to be constructed; the test asserts the fixture built it (`assert_ne!` on the two legs) rather than passing vacuously under the old single-leg code (the R854 class).

SIX CORPORA REBUILT AND GATED ON THIS TREE: violations 32 / 15 / 27 / 16 / 0 / 0 and steps 30 / 27 / 31 / 25 / 20 / 45, both UNCHANGED from R933's sweep, and hierarchy crossings 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 2 / 3 unchanged. The new NOTICE fires on exactly the three corpora the census predicted, and on all six it now AGREES with the frontier: NOTICE present if and only if the frontier says the place set is not derivable. That agreement is the mirror defect closed, measured rather than argued.

INJECTIONS, each naming one test, reverted from a copy: J1 first-leg-only reddens `both_declared_legs_are_read_not_only_the_first` alone; J2 dropping the record reddens `an_unaskable_completeness_class_is_named_rather_than_read_as_clean` alone; J3 recording unconditionally reddens BOTH, which is correct because both pin the silence; J4 removing the wire's exception and J5 re-attributing the turn-on to `containment` each redden `transition_containment_documents_the_scope_boundary_model` alone. One further injection did not compile and was DISCARDED, not counted, and one injection script's `count == 1` assertion caught a non-matching pattern before it could report green.

Round 936.decision_summary: R936 BUILD (the PLACE axis reaches the kernel) — mnemosyne-engine gains its fourth door, MapProjection, over the Round 875 declared-map read; plus the bake emitter emit_map_projection and the input declaration that keeps a baked map from going silently stale. THE ROUND STARTED BY KILLING ITS OWN NEXT. The RESUME memory and R932's closing carry both named the north-star step as "report-quest-graph BUILD"; that verb was BUILT at R568, hardened at R569, consumed as a runtime would at R857, and given a CI-loaded fixture at R873. A stale one-line memory hook was copied into the ledger at R932 and carried forward by R933, R934 and R935 without anyone re-measuring it — the same failure mode as a hallucinated citation, arriving through memory rather than through invention. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND INSTEAD, all of it run rather than recalled: the store's map READ exists (R875) and reaches CLI and MCP; mnemosyne-engine, the kernel a consumer links, still contains ZERO uses of it, exactly as R875 measured before building the read — it holds MapLocator only as a disclosure pointer and uses its object field as a line's carrier, so the kernel had no notion of a place graph at all; and the bake has three doors (playable, quest, passages) whose shared contract module already says in its own text that "a fourth door must link here". The gap is therefore ours and not the store's: R892 established that report-playable-world must NOT carry edges because the map is neither telling-scoped nor order-scoped and a consumer joins the two axes itself — and the in-repo consumer that was supposed to do that joining had not been written. THE PULL IS FIELD-MEASURED, NOT ARGUED: tide's engine/src/map.rs still records, in its own words and read read-only, that the kernel gives this axis write-only, that it opened our store sidecar by hand at 1,843 allocations and 1.79 MB per start, that it then moved that parse to a build-time bake, that its store shape is now bitten in two places which will diverge, and that the swap point waiting on us is one function. THE BOUNDARY IS CARRIAGE, NOT COMPUTATION, and it is written into the module rather than left to be rediscovered: undirected is carried and applied only where the declaration says so (steps_from reads the flag, never assumes two-wayness); a guard is carried and never evaluated (R712); a cost is carried in its registered unit and nothing here sums or compares one, because whether two units are commensurable is domain knowledge core must not hold (the invariant-4 line R711 drew when it established the derived travel-time read is not ours); and the map stays flat, each edge carrying its frame and branch with neither resolved (R696 finding 6, deferred at R875). ONE DEFECT WAS FOUND AND FIXED WHILE BUILDING: projection_inputs declares the config, the canon order and the sidecar, and no projection before this one opened a narrative-rules file — so a map bake would have watched everything except the artifact that decides which facts are edges at all. That is not slight staleness; a changed rule silently bakes a DIFFERENT map. transition_map_inputs now resolves the rules path through the same narrative_rules_path resolver the read uses, so the file declared and the file opened are one decision (the R772 rule). AND R875'S OWN HONEST CARRY IS CLOSED: it wrote "not dogfoodable here — every number in this round is from a fixture or the consumer's tree", which stopped being true when the map-corpus arms landed blind-authored towns. The kernel is now pinned on one, rebuilt in CI from the tracked manifests where they already live rather than copied into a fixtures directory, because a copy is a second site biting the same shape and two sites diverge.
changes_bullets: BUILD: mnemosyne-engine/src/map.rs — the kernel's PLACE axis, sibling of the scene walk (PlayableProjection) and the journal (QuestProjection). MapProjection + DeclaredMapView / MapEdgeView / EdgeCostView / EdgeGuardView / MapSelfLoopView, from_workspace reading mnemosyne_ops::transition_map_report in process, from_report crate-private FROM THE START (the two sibling axes reached that only by correction at R771 and R773), and the parts mirror + to_parts/from_parts baked-ingestion door linking the one contract in baked_ingestion rather than restating it.

DeclaredMapView::steps_from(node) — the one navigational read the axis exists for. It walks a back edge only where the map DECLARES undirected, returning each road paired with the far endpoint; it consults no guard and orders by nothing, because deciding a guard and pricing a route are both the consumer's.

mnemosyne-engine-build: emit_map_projection + render_map, emitting `pub fn map_projection() -> &'static MapProjection` with both side-table values on every edge — the fields a naive bake drops, and the exact fields whose absence sent a live consumer to parse our sidecar. Dogfooded like its three siblings: build.rs bakes a fixture exercising every emitted form (two maps, both undirected values, containment present and absent, an edge with both side tables and one with neither, a K-of-N guard and an AND guard, a self-loop, both unattached lists, and the nasty string in a place id) and the crate compiles its own output.

FIX (R772 class, found while building): mnemosyne-ops gains narrative_rules_path, one resolver for WHICH rules file a read opens, used by both resolve_narrative_rules and the new transition_map_inputs — so a map bake declares to cargo the artifact it actually reads. projection_inputs never listed a rules file because no earlier projection opened one.
mnemosyne-engine::transition_map_inputs — the read-through so a consumer talks to its kernel rather than past it into ops, the shape projection_inputs already had.
verification_bullets: MEASURED BEFORE BUILDING, on today's tree rather than recalled: report-quest-graph exists in CLI + MCP + ops + validate and its ledger entry R568 describes the build, so the inherited NEXT was dead; grep for transition/edge_cost/edge_guard over mnemosyne-engine returns 0 non-MapLocator uses; the bake has exactly three emitters. Arm D's corpus was rebuilt from its tracked manifests and report-transition-map reproduced the recorded 12 nodes / 20 edges of `cairnwell-map`.

A SECOND MEASUREMENT CHANGED WHAT THE TESTS HAD TO BE: across the five recorded transition-map logs (v1 stage-b, v3 stage-a/b, v4 stage-a/b) every map is `directed` and not one uses edge_costs or edge_guards. So the undirected branch and both side tables have NO witness in authored data; their oracles are built fixtures and the authored smoke asserts their ABSENCE explicitly, so a green run cannot be read as having proven them present.

1415 tests green (+11), 132 binaries; clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --all --check clean; validate-workspace clean (T1 0, T3 reject 0, entries 682, citation-gate 0 unscanned).

Real-data pin: crates/mnemosyne-engine/tests/authored_map_smoke.rs rebuilds arm D from the tracked manifests IN PLACE and asserts the kernel reproduces the recorded numbers, that every edge names its declaring fact, that the market's three roads and the one-way descent come out as declared, and that an unknown place answers empty rather than erroring.

INJECTION SELF-REPORT, 6 surgical edits, each anchor asserted count == 1, restore from a COPY: steps_from hardcoding two-way reddened 3 (the built pair, the authored e2e, and the baked-artifact test — all three assert directedness); the cost dropped on ingestion, K-of-N flattened, and the unattached lists dropped each reddened 2 (their own named test plus the round-trip, which reads the far side directly rather than comparing parts to parts); the emitter dropping a guard reddened only the baked-artifact test; and the bake ceasing to declare the rules file reddened only a_map_bake_declares_the_rules_file_it_reads. Six for six, no injection silent.

The round-trip fixture is deliberately the awkward one — every optional field populated on one edge and absent on its neighbour — because a round-trip over a fixture with no optional content passes while dropping every option, and byte-equal parts also hold when both directions drop the same field.

Whether that is the contract failing to lead an author there or authors genuinely not wanting it is NOT decided here, and chasing it would reopen the contract-precision arc R932 closed.

tide's swap remains tide-repo work and its map.rs still records the pre-R875 absence, so the consumer does not yet know the read exists, let alone the kernel door. Delivery is judged by the recipient's document, not by ours.

Round 938.decision_summary: R938 BUILD (option B, the owner's choice) — a reading surface can now say WHERE a scene is and where it leads, and it derives that from what the author already wrote rather than from a new coordinate anyone has to author. THE MEASUREMENT THAT MADE IT SMALL: every piece was already declared and nothing new had to be invented. The transition rule carries its own `predicate` — arm D's says `at` — and that is what the continuity gate has always used to make a pair of facts a STEP, so "which predicate says where someone is" is the author's declaration, not a guess and not a consumer override. A `Line` already carries its typed predicate (surfaced at R814 so a consumer could route journal facts without the kernel guessing a policy). The map's node set already IS the place space. So the join is: a line the scene DISCLOSED, carrying the map's own location predicate, naming an entity that is a node of that map. Measured on authored data before designing anything: 19 of arm D's 20 scenes carry exactly one place this way and none carries two. THE ONE THING THIS ROUND HAD TO GET RIGHT IS THAT IT READS THE DISCLOSED SCENE AND NOT THE STORE. The continuity gate already knows where every subject stands at every step — `StepJudgement` has carried subject, from, to and the canon point since R921 — and using it here would have been a LEAK: a telling is allowed to withhold that a character is at the drowned quarter, and a reading surface showing it anyway discloses by the back door exactly what the disclosure plan spent its design withholding. So the join asks the scene, and where the telling says nothing the answer is honestly nothing, proven by a PAIR (the same fact, disclosed and withheld, everything else identical). WHAT IT DOES NOT ANSWER, said in the doc rather than left to be assumed: "where is the PLAYER". The kernel does not know which character the screen belongs to — a live consumer bakes its own viewpoint from a `plays` predicate — so this returns every place the scene disclosed someone at, sorted, and a scene cutting between two rooms yields two rather than one picked quietly. ALSO LANDED: `TransitionMapView.predicate` on the R875 read, because a consumer holding that report could see the roads and could not ask who was standing on one; and the renderer's `Theme::place` hook, whose default prints the place and its exits and whose empty return prints nothing at all, so a surface opts out of the axis rather than the engine deciding for it. The exits are what the DECLARATION allows and not what is passable now — a road whose guard does not hold is still listed, carrying its guard, because evaluating one is the consumer's (R712 kept whole through the presentation layer).

Round 939.decision_summary: R939 (MEASUREMENT, code 0) — the kernel's READ surface counted against the store's WRITE surface, once, as a whole set, so this stops being an axis chased one at a time. THE ANSWER IS TWO, and both are evidenced by a live consumer rather than by our taste. The store holds 18 written fields; `mnemosyne-ops` exposes 37 public functions; the kernel calls 9 of them. The 15 report-shaped ops reads it does not call are NOT 15 gaps, and saying so is most of this round's work: authoring frontier, disclosure coverage, disclosure leak, render fidelity, edge candidates, typing candidates, the two import-proposal reads, payoff substantiation and timeline gaps are AUTHORING AND GATE surfaces, which a playing runtime has no business holding; and fork tree, playthrough manuscript and payoff coverage are reached INDIRECTLY, being the inputs the playable-world and quest-graph reads are JOINs over. THE DECISIVE INSTRUMENT IS NOT OUR ENUMERATION BUT THE CONSUMER'S SOURCE: which paths open our store sidecar by hand. There are 14 such sites in the tide tree, and 12 of them are correct. Seven are tests and gates, and a gate SHOULD hand-parse — one reading through our API could not detect our API being wrong, which is the reason their own map.rs keeps `WalkMap::from_json` beside the baked path and says so. One is a graph tool. Three are bakes that call our emitters. That leaves TWO runtime-facing paths that hand-parse because the kernel hands back nothing, and the map axis that R936 closed was the third. GAP 1, THE PARAMETER ECONOMY, AND THE CONSUMER'S STATED REASON FOR IT IS WRONG WHILE THE COMPLAINT IS RIGHT. Their `bake_meters` records that `report-parameter-economy` is "a human summary, not a consumer seam". It is not a human summary: it returns a typed `ParameterEconomyReport` of `ParameterEconomyRow`s. But every row is an AGGREGATE — `delta_count`, `sum_positive`, `sum_negative` — so the per-beat datum a runtime must actually apply, which fact carries which delta on which meter, is summed away before it reaches anyone. A read that exists, is typed, and is the wrong SHAPE is the same failure R937 named one axis over, where R875's answer arrived as a CLI subprocess for a consumer that links emitters. Round 940.decision_summary: R940 (BUILD) — the kernel gains a public typed-claim query, and the private copy of it in the quest axis becomes its first caller. This is the smaller of the two gaps Round 939 counted: a live consumer's build scans our sidecar with serde_json for the subject of the facts carrying one predicate, while the kernel held that exact scan privately for `opened_by`, so the capability existed and only the door was missing. `mnemosyne_ops::typed_claims` reads every typed claim keyed by predicate; `mnemosyne_engine::store_typed_claims` is the read-through a consumer links, beside `store_entity_kinds`. MEASUREMENT DECIDED THE SHAPE, TWICE, AND BOTH TIMES AGAINST THE OBVIOUS ANSWER. First: a row carries FRAME and BRANCH, not just subject-predicate-object, because both coordinates are authored. The arm-D corpus holds one typed claim outside ground truth — the townsfolk say the drowned bell rings itself, typed `state = ringing` in the `townsfolk` frame — so a frame-blind read hands a consumer a rumour with the authority of a fact, which is Round 922's map defect arriving on the claim axis. The first consumer's store spreads one character's `pursues` claims across three branches, so a branch-blind read flattens a fork's claim into the trunk's. Neither coordinate is FILTERED here: the kernel carries them and the consumer decides, the R936 carriage-not-computation line. Second: the read is UNFILTERED by predicate. A `predicates` argument would have to answer what an empty list means, and both answers are traps — "empty = all" is a footgun, "empty = none" makes a not-computed result indistinguishable from an absent one (the R924 class). Keyed by predicate, a consumer's filter is a map lookup. THE QUEST AXIS KEEPS ITS OWN RULE AND ONLY THAT: which object shape is a checkable precondition (a Fact bridge, R707/R708). Frame and branch now ARRIVE at that call site and are deliberately not filtered, stated in the code rather than left for a green run to imply — every recorded precondition claim is ground-truth and each quest's claims sit on one branch, so a filter would be a rule written against no data. The shape that would discriminate is a precondition declared in a belief frame; write one and the decision is due again. The kernel no longer loads the raw store anywhere: `load_atomic_store` was in its reach for this one private scan and is now out of it, replaced by a typed read. TWO DEFECTS FOUND IN THE BUILDING, BOTH BY INJECTION RATHER THAN BY READING. A sort by fact id inside the read was a no-op — `narrative_facts` is already keyed by fact id — so it was a guard no test could discriminate, and it was removed while the ordering promise stayed pinned against the OUTPUT. And the first version of the precondition test was VACUOUS on the arm it claimed to cover: every undeclared claim in its fixture was entity-shaped, so the object-shape filter caught them and deleting the predicate policy entirely changed no answer. A fact-shaped claim under an undeclared predicate is the discriminating input, and it is in the fixture now.

Round 941.decision_summary: R941 (BUILD) — the parameter economy's delta axis gets the per-beat row its gate sibling always had, and the kernel gets a door onto it. This is the second and last of the two gaps Round 939 counted, and the one its own NEXT warned was not an obvious repair: Round 730 built this read deliberately verdict-free (the R728 review killed a reachability verdict outright), so "add a per-delta row" had to be probed rather than assumed. THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED IT IS INSIDE THE READ ITSELF: the same report already returns the GATES per fact — `ParameterEconomyGateRow {fact, op, threshold}` — and returned the DELTAS only as a count and two sums. One report, two axes of the same side-table family, one of them per-beat and the other aggregated. That asymmetry is not a neutrality decision; neutrality is about refusing a verdict, and a fact-to-delta binding is authored data, strictly MORE neutral than a Σ over it. WHAT THE OLD READ COULD NOT SAY, demonstrated rather than argued: two stores where the same meter ends at the same totals through different beats produced BYTE-IDENTICAL reports. The test that now forbids this asserts the DIFFERENCE between two stores, not either store alone, because a per-beat row filled from the wrong side would satisfy a single-store check. That information loss is why the first consumer's build parsed our sidecar for `parameter_deltas` and wrote in its own comment that the report was "a human summary, not a consumer seam" — half wrong, since it is typed, and half exactly right. THE LAYERING LINE IS UNTOUCHED AND IS THE REASON THIS IS SAFE: the store hands over the authored delta and never accumulates one. No running sum, no gate verdict, no reachability claim — R712's line, which R730 held by deleting `ParameterGateUnreachable`. The aggregates stay beside the rows as declared projections of them (`delta_count` = `deltas.len()`, the two Σ over the same rows), the way an entity dossier keeps `fact_count` beside its facts, and a test asserts they agree rather than trusting them to. THE DOOR IS `store_parameter_economy`, because the shape a consumer can use is a linkable function and not a CLI subprocess — the mistake Round 937 named one axis over. The printed report gained the beats too: a read whose wire shows only Σ teaches its reader that the Σ is all the store holds, which is the model the consumer's build was written against. WITH THIS, BOTH GAPS ROUND 939 COUNTED ARE CLOSED, and the count it terminated on was two.

Round 941.publishable_decision_summary: R941 (BUILD) — the parameter economy's delta axis gets the per-beat row its gate sibling always had, and the kernel gets a door onto it. This is the second and last of the two gaps Round 939 counted, and the one its own NEXT warned was not an obvious repair: Round 730 built this read deliberately verdict-free (the R728 review killed a reachability verdict outright), so "add a per-delta row" had to be probed rather than assumed. THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED IT IS INSIDE THE READ ITSELF: the same report already returns the GATES per fact — `ParameterEconomyGateRow {fact, op, threshold}` — and returned the DELTAS only as a count and two sums. One report, two axes of the same side-table family, one of them per-beat and the other aggregated. That asymmetry is not a neutrality decision; neutrality is about refusing a verdict, and a fact-to-delta binding is authored data, strictly MORE neutral than a Σ over it. WHAT THE OLD READ COULD NOT SAY, demonstrated rather than argued: two stores where the same meter ends at the same totals through different beats produced BYTE-IDENTICAL reports. The test that now forbids this asserts the DIFFERENCE between two stores, not either store alone, because a per-beat row filled from the wrong side would satisfy a single-store check. That information loss is why the first consumer's build parsed our sidecar for `parameter_deltas` and wrote in its own comment that the report was "a human summary, not a consumer seam" — half wrong, since it is typed, and half exactly right. THE LAYERING LINE IS UNTOUCHED AND IS THE REASON THIS IS SAFE: the store hands over the authored delta and never accumulates one. No running sum, no gate verdict, no reachability claim — R712's line, which R730 held by deleting `ParameterGateUnreachable`. The aggregates stay beside the rows as declared projections of them (`delta_count` = `deltas.len()`, the two Σ over the same rows), the way an entity dossier keeps `fact_count` beside its facts, and a test asserts they agree rather than trusting them to. THE DOOR IS `store_parameter_economy`, because the shape a consumer can use is a linkable function and not a CLI subprocess — the mistake Round 937 named one axis over. The printed report gained the beats too: a read whose wire shows only Σ teaches its reader that the Σ is all the store holds, which is the model the consumer's build was written against. WITH THIS, BOTH GAPS ROUND 939 COUNTED ARE CLOSED, and the count it terminated on was two.

Round 942.decision_summary: R942 (DESIGN, code 0) — the corpus where the map and the telling finally meet, designed after measuring that they never have. Round 938 built the disclosed-place join and closed by admitting it had no authored witness; Round 939 counted the kernel's read gap and Round 941 closed the last of it, so what remains on this axis is not a missing door but a missing STORE. THE GAP WAS RE-MEASURED RATHER THAN INHERITED, over all 90 stores on disk: eight declare a spatial map and every one of them carries an empty disclosure_plans; thirteen carry a telling and not one declares an adjacency predicate. The both-axes cell is zero. TWO CORRECTIONS CAME OUT OF THE MEASURING AND ONE OF THEM WAS MY OWN INSTRUMENT: keying the map axis on class `transition` finds six corpora and is wrong about five, because that class also models one-way state machines and continuity-stress declares exactly one (gate_state, barred/cracked/open, obsolete `allowed` field, zero places) — Round 891 had already excluded reachability for this reason, so the correction is not a discovery but the harness now keys on `adjacency`, which is the token that actually discriminates. The second: R938's carry called the dnd-quest store 'essentially no roads' when it declares no transition rule whatsoever. AND ONE FINDING SHARPER THAN THE CARRY IT CAME FROM: `mnemosyne-render`, the shipping consumer of the join, has never been run on authored data and cannot be — it requires a telling, and against all four map corpora it fails loud on all four; the single tracked authored store that HAS a telling is pre-R708 schema and refuses to project. The witness count is zero not because nobody looked but because the two halves have never coexisted in one store. WHY NO AUTHOR EVER PRODUCED BOTH IS ALSO MEASURED, AND IT IS NOT AN AUTHORING FINDING: the map contract teaches the disclosure layer in full — the wire, both write-time gates, a dedicated section on the withhold-plus-first_at idiom — while the map BRIEF never asks for a telling and the disclosure brief never asks for a map. The map runbook's own read step even says 'the telling, if one exists', anticipating one nobody was ever asked for. So the fix is a new arm, not a new gate. THE ARM: two blind authors, one flooded hill-town, the map-corpus protocol with one axis added — one character whose middle-of-the-story location a reader must not be able to work out until near the end, one whose movements are plain throughout, both readings of the same world without changing what is true in it. Stage A names neither capability (discoverability); Stage B names both, in fiction. The sealed self-report must say which locations a reader cannot place a character at until which scene, and THAT SENTENCE IS THE ORACLE: the render's place line must be absent before the reveal scene and present at or after it. That is the authored analogue of the built pair R938 pinned, and it discriminates in both directions — a leaking join shows the hidden place early, and a join reading the gate's ground truth instead of the telling shows it in every scene. ONE NEW HARNESS STEP, named as the patch it is: the renderer resolves its rules file through mnemosyne.toml alone, so the orchestrator rewrites rules_path after the submission is frozen, keeping the R934 no-pin seed and changing one variable.

Round 943.decision_summary: R943 (EXPERIMENT) — the renderer finally ran on authored data, and the half of the join nobody had questioned is the half that is wrong. Round 938 built the disclosed-place join with no authored witness; Round 942 measured that the witness count was zero because the two axes had never coexisted in one store, and that mnemosyne-render could not be run on anything authored. Two blind authors, fresh context each, firewalled to their own directory, wrote a flooded hill-town apiece against the protocol frozen in the runbook before execution. Both stores carry a declared map AND a telling. The renderer ran on both, twice each, exit 0. THE WITNESS COUNT IS NO LONGER ZERO. E1 ANSWERS YES ON ALL FOUR SUB-ANSWERS IN THE ARM THAT WAS TOLD NOTHING: Stage A's brief named neither capability and the author reached the transition class with an adjacency predicate, two disclosure plans, per-fact overrides, and typed legs on both — quoting the contract's own reason for the leg kinds, which is Round 934's repair read back by someone who never saw Round 934. So Round 942's diagnosis was half right: it said the fix was a new arm rather than a new gate because the map brief never asked for a telling, and the stronger result is that the brief did not have to ask. What was missing was never discoverability. THE POSITIVE HALF OF E3 HOLDS EXACTLY: swap the telling over an identical fact base and precisely the withheld placements move, nothing else — so the join is not reading the gate's ground truth, which is the failure direction the runbook was built to catch. THREE FINDINGS AGAINST THE OTHER HALF, EACH WITNESSED BY BOTH AUTHORS INDEPENDENTLY. FIRST, the map half of the join never looks at the telling: transition_map_report takes no telling parameter, so the edge set is always ground truth, and the renderer prints those exits under every disclosed place. Stage A leaks the Lamp Cellar one scene before its existence is disclosed — and prints no place line at all in the scene that actually reveals it. Stage B leaks at full scale: all thirteen roads and all seven containment facts read never_planned under a withholding default, so the author withheld the entire road network, and the place lines with exits are byte-identical across both tellings. This is the back-door disclosure that places_disclosed_in's own doc-comment warns against, arriving through the exits instead of through the place. SECOND, DisclosedPlace carries no frame and no branch — the exact defect Round 940 repaired on the claim axis, still open on the place axis Round 938 built two rounds earlier. A town-talk rumour renders as a place indistinguishable from ground truth: Stage B's sc-15 discloses the Skiff Mooring solely because the town falsely says so, and Stage B's SEALED SELF-REPORT ASSERTS THE OPPOSITE — "machine-readable as belief and never as position". The author modelled the belief exactly as the contract prescribes and was wrong about what the engine would do with it; that is the Round 934 pattern again, not silence but a reasonable belief the substrate licensed. THIRD, a reveal pinned at the scene its fact stops being current never renders: both authors designed "reveal the middle at the end", both pinned first_at to a scene where a successor takes over, and in neither store does the withheld placement itself ever become a visible place line. Stage A's oracle survives only by the accident that a different character walks into the room at that scene. NO REPAIR IS PROPOSED HERE — this arm measures, and what to do about a telling-blind map, an unframed disclosed place, and a reveal that never fires is the next decision, not this one.

Round 943.publishable_decision_summary: R943 (EXPERIMENT) — the renderer finally ran on authored data, and the half of the join nobody had questioned is the half that is wrong. Round 938 built the disclosed-place join with no authored witness; Round 942 measured that the witness count was zero because the two axes had never coexisted in one store, and that mnemosyne-render could not be run on anything authored. Two blind authors, fresh context each, firewalled to their own directory, wrote a flooded hill-town apiece against the protocol frozen in the runbook before execution. Both stores carry a declared map AND a telling. The renderer ran on both, twice each, exit 0. THE WITNESS COUNT IS NO LONGER ZERO. E1 ANSWERS YES ON ALL FOUR SUB-ANSWERS IN THE ARM THAT WAS TOLD NOTHING: Stage A's brief named neither capability and the author reached the transition class with an adjacency predicate, two disclosure plans, per-fact overrides, and typed legs on both — quoting the contract's own reason for the leg kinds, which is Round 934's repair read back by someone who never saw Round 934. So Round 942's diagnosis was half right: it said the fix was a new arm rather than a new gate because the map brief never asked for a telling, and the stronger result is that the brief did not have to ask. What was missing was never discoverability. THE POSITIVE HALF OF E3 HOLDS EXACTLY: swap the telling over an identical fact base and precisely the withheld placements move, nothing else — so the join is not reading the gate's ground truth, which is the failure direction the runbook was built to catch. THREE FINDINGS AGAINST THE OTHER HALF, EACH WITNESSED BY BOTH AUTHORS INDEPENDENTLY. Stage A leaks the Lamp Cellar one scene before its existence is disclosed — and prints no place line at all in the scene that actually reveals it. Stage B leaks at full scale: all thirteen roads and all seven containment facts read never_planned under a withholding default, so the author withheld the entire road network, and the place lines with exits are byte-identical across both tellings. This is the back-door disclosure that places_disclosed_in's own doc-comment warns against, arriving through the exits instead of through the place. A town-talk rumour renders as a place indistinguishable from ground truth: Stage B's sc-15 discloses the Skiff Mooring solely because the town falsely says so, and Stage B's SEALED SELF-REPORT ASSERTS THE OPPOSITE — "machine-readable as belief and never as position". The author modelled the belief exactly as the contract prescribes and was wrong about what the engine would do with it; that is the Round 934 pattern again, not silence but a reasonable belief the substrate licensed. Stage A's oracle survives only by the accident that a different character walks into the room at that scene. NO REPAIR IS PROPOSED HERE — this arm measures, and what to do about a telling-blind map, an unframed disclosed place, and a reveal that never fires is the next decision, not this one.

Round 944.decision_summary: R944 (DEBT, code 0) — the corrections R943 made at the keyboard flow back into the runbook, because the one that bit us had already been corrected once and nobody carried it home. R943 ran the disclosed-place arm and had to depart from its own frozen protocol four times; it recorded all four honestly and then left the runbook saying the wrong thing, which is the carry-instead-of-close failure this project keeps naming. THE DECIDING ARGUMENT IS NOT TIDINESS, IT IS A MEASURED RECURRENCE: `revision_provenance: "exact"` does not exist in the gate's vocabulary — the accepted set is derived-upper-bound and declared-at-run and an unknown value panics — and Round 898's design used that same non-existent word, and the map-corpus run corrected it at execution time, and the correction lived only in that run's replay.json, so Round 942 wrote the retired word back into a fresh runbook by copying from a design instead of from the code. Left alone it would have come round a third time. FOUR INSTRUCTIONS CORRECTED, EACH AGAINST WHAT R943 MEASURED RATHER THAN AGAINST TASTE. The rules pin: the step commanded a printf that rewrites the whole config, and both authors had already wired `rules_path` themselves, 2 of 2, so the patch was unnecessary AND destructive — applying it would have deleted Stage A's authored `interval_severity = "reject"` line, which is editing an author's output, forbidden twice elsewhere in the same file. It now says verify, and append only the missing line if it is genuinely missing. The seal: the file claimed the self-report "is sealed at first submission and is never revised", which reads as a rule the author keeps, and the author is never told it — Stage B revised theirs in good faith. It now says the freeze is the mechanism, names the frozen path E3 must read, requires the diff to be recorded, and states why the author is deliberately NOT told: a writer who knows a document is about to be frozen writes a different document. The E3 oracle: "the place line must NOT name it in any scene before N" is under-specified and read strictly manufactures a false disagreement, because Stage B's hidden location was also legitimately disclosed early for a different told stretch. It is now a (character, location, scene-range) triple keyed on the disclosing fact id, and it tells the next orchestrator that a missing reveal is finding 3 and not a near miss. The provenance string: corrected, with the accepted set quoted, the file that owns it named, and the general rule stated — grep the code that reads a machine-checked literal before writing it into a runbook. TWO OPERATIONAL FACTS R943 LEARNED THE HARD WAY WERE ADDED RATHER THAN LEFT IN A REPORT NOBODY WILL RE-READ: a self-referential pin costs two commits by construction, and kits are discovered by `git ls-files` so the suite must be staged before it is run and the replay COUNT must be read, or the green belongs to somebody else's kit. AND THE FILE NOW SAYS WHICH TEXT v1 ACTUALLY RAN UNDER: the pre-commitment is the version at 636c91d, not this one. Without that line a later auditor would read the corrected protocol as the one two blind authors were run against. The arms' own frozen files are untouched — fix the runbook, never the evidence, which is the Round 934 precedent this round is following.

Round 945.decision_summary: R945 (BUILD) — a rumour stops rendering as a place, and the repair found a second victim the experiment had not seen. Round 943's finding 2: `DisclosedPlace` carried `map`, `place` and `fact_id` and no epistemic frame, so the place axis flattened exactly the distinction `Line::is_belief`'s own doc-comment forbids flattening — "a renderer that flattens the two robs the player of the distinction". THE CONTRACT HAD ALREADY DECLARED THE RULE ONE TYPE OVER; the place axis, built two rounds before Round 940 settled it on the claim axis, simply never read it. Repair: the row carries `frame`, taken from the disclosing line and never invented, and the kernel still refuses to filter — carriage, not computation, the Round 940 line held on a third axis. ONE RESOLVER, NOT A SECOND COPY: the belief predicate moves out of `Line`'s private `impl` into `types::frame_is_belief`, and both `Line::is_belief` and the new `DisclosedPlace::is_belief` read it, which an injection confirms by reddening BOTH axes' guards when the single resolver lies. THE DEDUP KEY WAS THE OTHER HALF AND THE EXPERIMENT HAD NOT SEEN IT: the join deduplicated on (rule, place), so a place named by the world AND by a rumour collapsed to one row wearing whichever frame sorted first. Re-rendering the two authored corpora shows the cost that carry never named — Stage A gains `p-stair [orin]` at sc-09 and BOTH `p-lamp-cellar [orin]` and `p-lamp-cellar [town-talk]` at sc-20, Stage B gains `p-water-stair [town-talk]` at sc-11 — four beliefs that were not merely mislabelled but SILENTLY DROPPED, every one of them swallowed by a ground-truth placement that happened to name the same room. Round 943 measured the flattening; it could not measure the erasure, because an erased row leaves nothing to look at. The default theme now names the frame it is quoting, which is the same refusal one layer up: the kernel declines to decide a rumour is not worth showing, and the theme declines to show it as a fact.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-engine/src/types.rs` — `frame_is_belief` + `GROUND_TRUTH_FRAME` become the crate's one resolver for "is this hearsay"; `Line::is_belief` / `is_ground_truth` now read it instead of owning it.

`crates/mnemosyne-engine/src/map.rs` — `DisclosedPlace` gains `frame`, populated from the disclosing line; the dedup and sort keys become (rule, place, frame); `DisclosedPlace::is_belief` / `is_ground_truth` delegate to the shared resolver.
`crates/mnemosyne-render/src/lib.rs` — the default `Theme::place` marks a believed place with the frame that claimed it (`p-mooring [town-talk]`) and leaves the world's own places unmarked.
Three new tests: two frames naming ONE place stay two rows; an unframed disclosure reads as ground truth; the rendered place says whose it is.
No store, corpus, manifest or frozen read from Round 943 is touched. The `reads/` directory remains the evidence of what the renderer did BEFORE this repair.
verification_bullets: 1433 tests pass workspace-wide, 0 fail (1430 before, plus this round's three); `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0; `cargo fmt --all --check` exit 0.

INJECTION 4 OF 4, each reddening the guards that name it and no others. J1 drop `frame` from the dedup key: the two-frames-one-place test and the render test. J2 the theme stops marking belief: the render test alone. J3 the shared resolver claims nothing is ever hearsay: the new tests AND the pre-existing `Line` guards (`marker_theme_styles_by_semantic_axis`, `projects_disclosed_lines_at_the_locator_seat`) — which is the evidence that the resolver is genuinely shared and not a second copy. J4 the row invents `ground-truth` instead of carrying the line's frame: the two-frames test, the unframed test, and the render test.

THE DISCRIMINATING INPUT IS TWO FACTS AT ONE PLACE. A fixture with a lone belief would pass a join that dropped the frame from the dedup key while keeping it on the row, which is half the defect; the pair fails it.

VERIFIED ON AUTHORED DATA, against Round 943's frozen renders. Stage B `told`: `p-mooring` becomes `p-mooring [town-talk]` at sc-15 — the exact line whose author asserted in a sealed report that the engine could never read it as a position — and `p-water-stair [town-talk]` APPEARS at sc-11 where it had been swallowed. Stage A `withheld-place`: `p-quay` becomes `p-quay [town-talk]` at sc-08, and `p-stair [orin]`, `p-lamp-cellar [orin]` and `p-lamp-cellar [town-talk]` appear where they had been swallowed.

THE ERASURE WAS NOT IN ROUND 943'S FINDINGS and is reported here as a correction to it: four of the five authored changes are rows that did not exist before, not rows that were mislabelled. A dropped row leaves no evidence, so the experiment could not have counted them; only the repair made them visible.

VERDICT-NEUTRAL ON THE GATE, measured not predicted: `validate-continuity` on the Stage B corpus still reads `violations: 0 (structural=0 interval=0)`. This round changes what a reading surface shows, not what the store is judged to be.

Branch is deliberately NOT carried on the row, and this is a decision rather than an omission: `places_disclosed_in` takes a `SceneView` the caller already fetched for one world (`render_playthrough` passes `MAIN_BRANCH`), so a `branch` field could only ever echo the caller's own argument back at it. Round 940 carries branch on typed-claim rows because that scan crosses branches; this read does not. A field no test could discriminate is the no-op guard Round 940 deleted.

Round 946.decision_summary: R946 (BUILD) — the roads a reader was never told about stop being exits, and the third finding turns out to have been misdiagnosed by the round that found it. Round 943's finding 1: `MapProjection` is built by `transition_map_report`, which takes no telling, so the edge set is always ground truth; the renderer printed those exits under every disclosed place, and one authored corpus withheld all thirteen of its roads and all seven of its containments and printed every one of them anyway, byte-identically under the withholding telling and the open one. The place honoured the telling; the roads out of it did not. Repair: `DeclaredMapView::steps_disclosed_from` filters `steps_from` by set membership on the DECLARING fact id, and the playthrough accumulates what it has disclosed as it walks. DIRECTION IS NOT RE-DECIDED — the new read filters what `steps_from` already resolved, so `undirected` cannot come to mean one thing for a gate and another for a reader, and the whole map stays available to the gate that needs it whole. On authored data the two tellings finally differ where they always should have: 21 exit lines under the open telling, ZERO under the withholding one, and Stage A stops naming the Lamp Cellar at the scene before its existence is disclosed. AND THEN THE SAME CHANGE EXPOSED THAT I HAD DIAGNOSED FINDING 3 WRONG. Round 943 said "a reveal pinned at the scene its fact stops being current never renders" and blamed supersession. The mechanism is simpler and larger: `mode: withhold` makes the projection skip the fact before it can seat a locator at all — deliberately, as a comment there records, because a prior consumer had deleted its own withhold filter on the premise that withheld facts emit no locator, and that premise was made true rather than left accidental. Supersession is not involved. THE DISCRIMINATING WITNESS WAS ALREADY IN THE CORPUS AND I HAD NOT LOOKED: Stage A's `f-c-cellar` is withheld with a pin at sc-07, supersedes nothing, is superseded by nothing, and never renders. The pin is inert on the OTHER surface too — the premature-leak gate reports any match of a withheld fact as a leak and records `first_at: None` whatever the pin says. So `withhold` + `first_at` is a coordinate the store accepts and no surface reads, and BOTH blind authors wrote it meaning "hidden until here, then told". `state` with the same pin is the shape that actually discloses late. THE REPAIR IS TO SPEAK, NOT TO GATE, and that follows Round 924's own measurement rather than taste: requiring the correction would reject both recorded corpora, so `report-disclosure-coverage` now names each inert pin, names the world and the coordinate, and says what to write instead. On Stage A it fires on all five withheld facts; on Stage B, on the one.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-engine/src/map.rs` — `DeclaredMapView::steps_disclosed_from(node, told)`: the roads out of a place that the reader has been told about, filtered from `steps_from` by the declaring fact id so direction is resolved once.

`crates/mnemosyne-render/src/lib.rs` — `render_scene` takes the told set; `render_playthrough` accumulates it across the walk, adding each scene's disclosed facts BEFORE that scene renders so a road named in this scene is an exit in it.
`crates/mnemosyne-validate/src/disclosure.rs` — `DisclosureCoverageReport::inert_reveal_pins`: every `withhold` override that also carries a `first_at`, sorted, advisory, never gated.
`crates/mnemosyne-cli/src/main.rs` — `report-disclosure-coverage` prints each inert pin with the world, the coordinate, why it does nothing on either surface, and the shape to use instead.

Three new tests: an undisclosed road is not an exit (paired against the told half); a road told once stays told for the rest of the walk; a withheld fact that also pins a reveal is named, while a bare withhold and a pinned `state` are not.
No store, corpus or frozen read from Round 943 is touched.
verification_bullets: 1436 tests pass workspace-wide, 0 fail (1433 before, plus this round's three); clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings` exit 0; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

INJECTION 4 OF 4 AFTER ONE WAS DISCARDED. J5 the exits filter becomes a no-op: `an_undisclosed_road_is_not_offered_as_an_exit` alone. J6 the walk forgets (the told set is rebuilt each scene): `a_road_told_once_stays_told_for_the_rest_of_the_walk` alone. J7 the advisory stops checking the mode, so a working `state` pin is reported as inert: the new coverage test alone. J8 the advisory drops the world coordinate: the same test. A FIFTH ATTEMPT AT J7 IS DISCARDED AND NOT COUNTED — it chained an iterator with itself and changed no behaviour, so its green said nothing; a non-firing injection is only evidence when the injection was real. J8's first form was REFUSED by the injector's `count == 1` assertion (the pattern matched three places), which is that assertion doing its job before a vacuous green could be reported.

THE EXIT GUARD IS A PAIR, not a bare absence: the same scene and the same map rendered once with the road told and once without. Without the told half, "no exits" is also what a renderer that lost the map entirely produces.

VERIFIED ON AUTHORED DATA. Stage B: exit lines go from 21 under `told` to 0, while `told-open` keeps its 21 — the two tellings differ on the map axis for the first time. Stage A: sc-06 goes from `p-granary -> p-lamp-cellar, p-market` to `p-granary -> p-market`, which is exactly what its author described and the render had been contradicting.

FINDING 3'S MECHANISM IS CORRECTED AGAINST THE CODE, not re-argued: `crates/mnemosyne-validate/src/continuity.rs` skips a `Withhold` disclosure before seating a locator, and `crates/mnemosyne-validate/src/disclosure.rs` takes the `is_withhold` branch with `first_at: None` before ever reading the pin. Round 943's supersession explanation is refuted by its own corpus: `f-c-cellar` is withheld with a pin, participates in no succession in either direction, and still never renders.

The advisory fires on recorded data, which is what distinguishes it from a check nobody's store can reach: five inert pins in Stage A (`f-c-cellar`, `f-cond-cellar`, `f-e-granary-cellar`, `f-sella-at-04`, `f-sella-at-05`) and one in Stage B.
SPEAK-NOT-GATE IS THE MEASURED ANSWER (Round 924's rule applied, not invoked): making the correction a requirement would reject 2 of 2 recorded corpora.

This round corrects its diagnosis and makes the shape audible; it does not decide whether `withhold` + `first_at` should MEAN a late reveal. That is a disclosure-semantics decision with a real cost either way — teaching the pin to un-withhold collides with the deliberate "a withheld fact seats no locator" invariant a prior consumer's bug forced this tree to make true on purpose.
The advisory has no gate and no CI teeth: it prints where an author or an orchestrator will read it, and nothing fails if they do not.
`render_scene`'s signature changed. It is public and its callers are all in-tree today, so nothing external broke, but a consumer holding it would have to pass the set.
The accumulated told set is per-WALK. A consumer rendering one scene in isolation must decide for itself what its reader has been told; the kernel does not remember across calls and should not.

Round 947.decision_summary: R947 (DEBT) — the semantics question closes with no semantics change, because the capability was already there and one authored field was being thrown away. Round 943's finding 3 asked whether `withhold` + `first_at` should MEAN a late reveal. Round 946 corrected its mechanism and then gave advice that was itself wrong: "use mode `state` with the same pin". IT IS NOT THE PIN THAT MOVES A DISCLOSURE. The locator seats at `surface.scene` when the author writes one and at the fact's own `canon_from` otherwise; `first_at` seats nothing on either surface, being a premature-leak constraint on re-extracted prose. So `state` plus the same pin would have left the line exactly where it already was, and an author following Round 946's sentence would have got no reveal and no explanation. THE ANSWER CAME FROM RUNNING IT, NOT FROM ARGUING IT. On a scratch copy of the Stage B corpus, with the author's own `surface: {scene: "sc-20", object: "e-cistern-lid"}` untouched and ONE field changed from `withhold` to `state`, the render places Yrsa in the Old Cistern at scenes 4, 20 and 21 — her legitimate early visit, then eleven scenes in which the reader cannot place her at all, then the reveal at the scene the lid lifts. That is the sealed self-report's own sentence, produced by the author's own data. The author had written the correct seat and `withhold` discarded it before it could be used. SO THE VOCABULARY IS COMPLETE AND NOTHING SHOULD CHANGE: `state` + `surface.scene` tells a truth late, `withhold` never tells it, and the two together are a contradiction — not a gap. Teaching the pin to un-withhold would have collided with the deliberate invariant that a withheld fact seats no locator, which this tree made true on purpose after a consumer deleted its own withhold filter on that very premise. What changes instead is what the advisory SAYS: it now carries the seat the author already wrote, and where there is one it stops giving generic advice and tells them their store is one word from what they described. On the recorded corpora the two messages split exactly as the data does — five pins with no seat get the general form, and the one that has a seat is told to change the mode and edit nothing else.

Round 949.decision_summary: R949 (BUILD) — the carry that said "nothing checks this" was right, and the thing it named lets a telling state what the store says is not yet so. Round 947 closed the reveal question and left one line in its carry: nothing checks that an authored `surface.scene` is not EARLIER than its fact's `canon_from`. Asked to measure it rather than restate it, I built one. THE STORE TOOK IT WITHOUT COMPLAINT — write-time validation checks only that the seat is a registered section and the carrier a registered entity, never their order — and the render then printed, in scene two, a fact the store says becomes true in scene twelve. THE SAME SCENE PUT ONE WOMAN IN TWO ROOMS: she is at the shrine, and she is in the cellar with the hatch shut over her, which is precisely what the exclusive rule exists to forbid. AND THE LEAK ROUND 946 CLOSED CAME BACK THROUGH ANOTHER DOOR: a place withheld until scene seven was named at scene two, not through the map's exits this time but through a disclosure seated early. Every gate was silent — `validate-continuity` read `violations: 0`, coverage said nothing, and the frontier said `0 gap(s)`. The gate judges fact EXTENTS, which were never wrong. Nothing was reading the SEAT. Round 924's rule decides where this lands and it decides the OPPOSITE way from the last two times it was asked: of 63 recorded overrides carrying a surface, 3 seat somewhere other than `canon_from` and all 3 seat LATER — so a check on earlier-seating rejects zero recorded stores, and this one is worth gating rather than merely saying. WHERE it lands was decided by the substrate, not preference: `validate-continuity` takes no telling and is telling-agnostic by construction, and a write-time reject cannot compare the two coordinates because the ordering lives in the canon-order artifact the atomic store does not hold. The authoring frontier is the one surface holding rules, telling and order at once, so the seat becomes a frontier gap that counts toward `total_gaps`. ★AND THE FIXTURE I FIRST WROTE FOR IT WAS VACUOUS, WHICH THREE INJECTIONS SAID BEFORE ANY REVIEWER COULD: what I described as three arms — before, at and after — was really early, equal and EQUAL, there was no unorderable pair at all, and `total_gaps >= 1` was already satisfied by the store's own zero-fact scenes. All three injections stayed green against it. The repaired fixture has four load-bearing arms and asserts the tally as a DELTA against the same store read without a telling, and the same three injections then each reddened it.

Round 950.decision_summary: R950 (BUILD) — the runbooks get a gate of their own, and it reaches the runbook nobody can see. Round 948 removed the third home of `revision_provenance: "exact"` and closed with the honest carry that nothing checks the runbooks STAY consistent with the gate; this builds that check. THE DEFENCE SITS AT THE SHAPE THAT GETS COPIED, NOT AT THE WORD. `taught_literals` scans only for the copyable `field: "value"` form, so a runbook may NAME a retired value while recording that it was retired — which is exactly what both corrected runbooks now do — but may not write it in the shape whose only use is to be pasted into a record. Nobody reasoned their way to `exact` either time it landed; they copied it. That narrowing is also what keeps the kits REPORTS out of scope: the disclosed-place report writes the retired form deliberately, to record that it does not exist, and evidence is frozen (Round 934 — fix the runbook, never the record), so a check that reached it could only ever be satisfied by editing the thing it exists to preserve. THE ORACLE IS THE GATE OWN VOCABULARY, NOT A COPY OF IT: `CHECKED_LITERALS` pairs each machine-checked field with the const the parser already asserts on, and `declarations` was rewritten to consult that same table, so there is one vocabulary with two readers and a field that gains a parser check without gaining a row PANICS in `vocabulary` rather than reporting no violations for a field nothing scanned. DISCOVERY IS THE FILESYSTEM, NOT `git ls-files`, and that is measured rather than defensive: `/claudedocs/*` is ignored by default, so a runbook is untracked from the moment it is written until a `.gitignore` exception lands — Round 898 found its own runbook in exactly that state — and this tree holds 23 runbooks of which one is untracked TODAY. Tracking-based discovery would be blind for the entire window in which a runbook is being read and copied from, which is the window this check exists for. The reach is therefore wider locally than in CI, which is the correct direction: the writing moment is where catching it is cheapest, and a file CI does not have cannot make CI red. WHAT IT CANNOT COVER IS WHY IT STANDS WHERE IT DOES. The retired word FIRST home is the Round 898 changelog entry itself, which instructs that the corpus land with `revision_provenance` EXACT; the ledger is frozen and append-only, so the design that seeds every copy is permanent and unfixable. The only place a mechanical check can stand is the artifact the copy lands in.

The four parser assertions (`schema`, `revision_provenance`, `role`, `expect`) now read that table through `vocabulary`, so there is one vocabulary with two readers.

Round 953.decision_summary: R953 (BUILD) — the seal reaches the whole run tree, and the role says only what is true. Round 952 sealed every DECLARED input and left the reach unmeasured; this round measured it from the filesystem side and the answer was 425 of 552. The 127 sealed artifacts under kit `run/` trees were the manifests and the frozen submissions; outside them sat the manuscripts the judges read, the judges' own reports, the label map that made them blind, the briefs the authors were handed, and every captured log — all pinned by nothing, and 51 of them under `factsfirst-craft`, a kit that had NO record at all, which is the worse half because there was not even a document to declare them in. THE VOCABULARY DECISION ROUND 952 DEFERRED IS ANSWERED BY CLAIMING LESS, NOT MORE. The obvious move was three or four provenance roles — orchestrator input, judge output, tool transcript — and it was measured and rejected: assigning 425 provenances from one sampled file per class would put inferred claims into a record whose whole value is that its claims are true, which is the exact ground on which Round 952 refused to call `mnemosyne.toml` raw agent output. The new role `run-artifact` says the file is part of this kit's frozen run tree and that this record pins its bytes, and says nothing about who produced it. That is the whole truth available, and it is not a catch-all: the audit's load-bearing provenance — the frozen first submissions, the sealed self-reports, the authored rules — is already held by the sharper roles and stays there, `run-artifact` may be used ONLY under a run tree (a constraint neither sibling carries), and no replay step may feed it. COVERAGE IS ASSERTED FROM THE FILESYSTEM, NOT FROM THE RECORD: a gate that walked the declarations and checked they resolve would pass on a record naming one file in fifty, and the R884 lesson is that a list only looks where it was told to look. THE SCHEMA MOVED TO `kit-replay/v3` because the accepted document set grew a case v2 could not describe. `factsfirst-craft` produced no sections manifest and no facts manifest in any arm — its evidence is prose, canon orders and narrative rules — so no verb can build a store from it and there is nothing to pin a revision for. Such a record declares an empty `replays`, states WHY in `no_replay`, and declares no `revision_provenance`, there being no pin for one to describe. Under v2 it would have been accepted in silence, which would exempt a whole kit from the replay half with nothing to notice.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/evidence_replay_smoke.rs` — `every_tracked_run_artifact_is_declared_by_its_kit` walks every tracked file under a kit `run/` tree and requires an owning record that declares it. Ownership is the NEAREST ancestor holding a `replay.json`, because kits nest and an outermost rule would let `disclosure-craft` claim `v3/run/`. The two shortfalls are reported TOGETHER in one assertion: an artifact under a record can be declared in it, an artifact under none needs the record written first, and splitting them would hide the second behind the first and teach a reader the gap is smaller than it is.

Same file — `INPUT_ROLES` gains `run-artifact`, with the two constraints that keep it from being a catch-all checked in `roles_are_from_the_declared_vocabulary_and_every_one_is_used`: no step feeds it, and it sits under a run tree of its own unit. That test now iterates `INPUT_ROLES` instead of naming a hand-typed pair, so a role added to the vocabulary and used nowhere is a distinction the corpus does not draw and fails.

Same file — `REPLAY_SCHEMAS` moves to `kit-replay/v3`, and `declarations` enforces the new conditional: empty `replays` requires a `no_replay` reason over 30 characters and forbids `revision_provenance`; a non-empty `replays` forbids `no_replay` and requires the provenance as before. `a_kit_with_no_replay_states_why_and_declares_no_pin` states the rule where a reader looks for it and fails if no kit exercises it.

`tools/experiment-harness/src/declare.rs` (new) + the `declare-run-tree` subcommand — writes a `run-artifact` entry for every tracked run-tree file a record owns and does not yet declare. Ownership is computed against EVERY tracked record, not just the ones named on the command line, so passing one record cannot claim a nested kit's tree; an artifact already declared anywhere is left alone, because the gate requires each path exactly once and re-declaring it would break that in the act of satisfying it. Two unit tests pin the path normaliser and the nearest-ancestor rule.

29 `replay.json` records — 425 artifacts declared and sealed, taking the corpus to 567 declared inputs (99 `replay-input`, 43 `raw-agent-output`, 425 `run-artifact`). `claudedocs/phase1-factsfirst-craft-experiment/replay.json` is new: 51 artifacts, no replays, and a stated reason.

The two live runbooks — the landing step now names `declare-run-tree` and `stamp-inputs` and says what stays unpinned until they run. The gate's own failure message names the same two commands, because a wire that is silent about a step teaches the next author the old model just as well as a wrong wire does (Round 930).
