THE PROVENANCE ALTERNATIVE WAS PROBED, NOT ASSUMED AWAY. The classes are legible, but they are not uniform across 26 kits and `mnemosyne.toml` alone is orchestrator-seeded in one kit and author-wired in another by that kit's own record — which is why the role that ships claims membership rather than authorship.

carry_forward_bullets: THE 425 ARE PINNED AND UNCLASSIFIED, AND THAT IS A DECISION WITH A REOPENING CONDITION, NOT AN OMISSION. Sharpening `run-artifact` into provenance roles needs per-kit evidence — each kit's runbook and report record who produced what — and the method is exactly that: read the owning kit's runbook, not one sampled file per class, because the classes are not uniform across 26 kits. What makes it worth doing is that the R469 contamination bound is an argument about who saw what, and a record that can name the judges' packet as something the orchestrator assembled says more than one that calls it a run artifact. The manifest now carries both, applied AFTER facts through the STANDALONE VERBS' OWN BODIES, extracted as shared cores — one field with two write paths must have one invariant set, and a pasted second copy is the half-enforced-invariant anti-pattern this repo names by name. THE MANIFEST IS A DECLARATION, NOT A PATCH: a guard's threshold is re-declared on every import, so dropping it returns the guard to AND rather than silently keeping the old k, and the two-step test is what separates that from an implementation that sets k once and never looks again. ★THE INJECTIONS FOUND A DEFECT THIS ROUND CREATED THE CONDITIONS TO SEE, AND IT WAS PAID HERE. Deleting the ENTIRE `edge_costs` contract row left the suite green: the gate that existed checks a DECLARED kind's prose against its serde keys, and nothing checked that a kind was declared at all. An array with no contract entry is invisible in `describe-schema`, the document every blind author reads — so a new authoring surface could ship and remain unreachable in practice, which is precisely the condition this round exists to end. The new gate asks the TYPE which arrays exist and requires a row for each.

Those three are the standalone verbs' own bodies, extracted so both doors share ONE enforcement — a second copy of these checks on one field is the half-enforced-invariant anti-pattern this repo names in CLAUDE.md.

Round 961.decision_summary: R961 (EXPERIMENT) — the wire carried the authors, and the arm that was told nothing reached both tables. Two blind authors, fresh context, isolated directories, given only the authoring contract and a fiction in which a long climb and a shut sea-gate are necessary. Stage A's brief names NO machinery — not cost, guard, edge, side table, threshold, condition, K-of-N, manifest array, verb, or either table by name — and that author put 18 `edge_costs` rows and 3 `edge_guards` rows into the fact manifest anyway. Stage B, asked in fiction to make a route totallable and a shut way visible without prose, wrote 20 and 3. ★THE DISCRIMINATING FACT IS THE FILE, NOT THE TABLE: reaching these by hand-calling `add-edge-cost` is the Round 943 outcome and would mean the wire did not carry the author. Neither directory holds a shell script, neither self-report mentions a verb, and both first submissions imported GREEN — the iterate-to-green loop never ran. The count moves against Round 959's corrected baseline: `edge_costs` 0 to 2, `edge_guards` 1 to 3. Against Round 936's number this report would have said 0 to 2 for guards and been wrong by a corpus. E3 found NO disagreement on either arm, checked on condition fact ids: every cost prints with the ordering the frozen self-report claims, every guard on exactly the named edge, and both authors' deliberate one-way guard on the counting-house door shows as an absence on the outbound edge. ★THE TWO BRANCHES THAT STILL HAVE NO WITNESS NOW HAVE A REASON RATHER THAN A SILENCE. Directed was CHOSEN, not defaulted — "the stair costs more going up than coming down and an undirected edge cannot say so" — and `threshold` was declined by both because every shut way in this world had exactly one opener. Round 936 counted five corpora choosing directed; it could not have learned why. Stage A also stated the layering line unprompted: "I never sum these anywhere. The numbers are carried, not added." Stage B's continuity gate fired twice on its own exclusive rule and is RECORDED, not resolved: the rule is declared `per: object` on `held_by(thing, person)` and the self-report describes it as "one holder per thing", which is `per: subject` — a contract-reading question this arm did not ask.
changes_bullets: STAGE A WAS TOLD NOTHING AND REACHED BOTH TABLES. Its brief names no machinery — not cost, guard, edge, side table, threshold, condition, K-of-N, manifest array, verb, `edge_costs` or `edge_guards`. It gives a fiction in which both properties are necessary (a long stair against a few steps; a sea-gate at low water and a door needing a key) and one sentence of requirement: "the engine must be able to answer both of those from your data alone, without reading your prose." The author put 18 `edge_costs` rows and 3 `edge_guards` rows into `facts.json`.

THE DISCRIMINATING FACT IS THE FILE, AND IT ANSWERS YES ON BOTH ARMS. Reaching these tables by hand-calling `add-edge-cost` is the Round 943 outcome and means the wire did not carry the author. Neither directory holds a `.sh`, neither self-report mentions running a verb, and both import receipts carry the tables: Stage A `18 edge-costs + 3 edge-guard-conditions created`, Stage B `20 edge-costs + 3 edge-guard-conditions created`.

BOTH FIRST SUBMISSIONS IMPORTED GREEN, so the iterate-to-green loop never ran and no error was ever handed back. Each self-report is byte-identical to its frozen copy — no post-freeze revision to record, unlike Round 943.

E3 FOUND NO DISAGREEMENT ON EITHER ARM, checked on condition fact ids rather than place names. Every cost the frozen self-reports describe prints on its edge with the ordering the prose claims — Stage A's 15-minute Long Stair up against 6 down, Stage B's 14 against 6 — and every guard prints on exactly the named edge with exactly the named conditions. Both authors deliberately left the outbound counting-house edge unguarded and both said why; the map read shows the asymmetry.

THE AUTHORS EXPLAINED THE TWO BRANCHES THAT STILL HAVE NO WITNESS. `undirected`: Stage A chose directed BECAUSE of the cost table — "the stair costs more going up than coming down and an undirected edge cannot say so." `threshold`: declined by both, Stage A stating "I used one condition per guard because each shut way here has exactly one thing that opens it." Round 936 recorded five corpora choosing directed and never reaching K-of-N; this run has an author saying why, which a count could not.

STAGE A STATED THE LAYERING LINE UNPROMPTED: "I never sum these anywhere, and no file of mine claims a total journey time. The numbers are carried, not added." That is carriage-not-computation, reached from the contract alone. Stage B built the same boundary into fiction, registering a branch in which `f-tide-high` supersedes `f-tide-out` so the guard's condition fails on that world-line: "The engine never evaluates the guard; it holds the declaration and the two roads."

STAGE B'S CONTINUITY GATE FIRED TWICE AND IS RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED. `rule_exclusive_overlap` on `one-holder-per-thing`, `f-ev-ledger` against `f-key-verrick` at `sc-04`, on both world-lines. The mechanical facts, each read from the author's own files: the rule is declared `per: "object"`; both facts are typed `held_by` with `object: e-verrick`; and the frozen self-report describes the rule as "one holder per thing … which makes the letter's passage from Mella to Old Tomsen a succession rather than two holders at once." With `held_by(thing, person)`, `per: object` scopes exclusivity to the PERSON, so the declaration and the description are not the same rule. Which one the author meant is not decided here.

THE ORCHESTRATOR PATCHED NOTHING, 2 OF 2 FOR THE THIRD ARM RUNNING. Both authors wrote `rules.json` and wired `rules_path` into `mnemosyne.toml` themselves; `grep -n rules_path` resolves in both, so the runbook's conditional patch step stayed unused, as it did in Round 943.
verification_bullets: THE COUNT MOVED, against the Round 959 baseline and not Round 936's: `edge_costs` 0 -> 2, `edge_guards` 1 -> 3. Reporting it against Round 936 would have said "0 to 2" for guards and been wrong by a corpus.

THE SEED'S SCHEMA VERSION WAS DERIVED, NEVER TYPED — `describe-schema | sed -n '1s/.*schema v\([0-9]\+\).*/\1/p'` returned 44, matching the constant. Round 958 found live runbooks seeding 23, which still imports because the loader migrates, so the stale literal produces no error at all.

`report-transition-map` IS the witness read and it was verified against a scratch store at Round 957 before this arm existed, so a blank would have been the corpus's answer rather than an untested projection. It is not blank: 18 edges all costed with three guards on Stage A, 20 edges all costed with three guards on Stage B.

`validate-continuity` WAS READ WHOLE, not just its `violations:` line. Stage A: 0 violations, 25 steps judged, rules=3. Stage B: 2 violations (recorded above), 44 steps judged, rules=3. On BOTH stores `interval_unverifiable=not-declared interval_severity=off` — that class was never evaluated, because neither author declared an interval rule, so the green does not speak for it (the Round 934 shape).

`report-authoring-frontier` evaluated `unconnected places` on both maps and answered `none` — not "not derivable" — so the read is doing work on both corpora. Stage A 0 gaps; Stage B 1, which is the author's stated design (the lamp setup is paid off on `main` and deliberately unpaid on the shut-gate world-line).

THE MACHINE-CHECKED LITERALS WERE READ OUT OF THE CODE THAT PANICS ON THEM, not copied from a design: `REPLAY_SCHEMAS = ["kit-replay/v3"]`, `PROVENANCE_KINDS = ["derived-upper-bound", "declared-at-run"]`, `INPUT_ROLES = ["replay-input", "raw-agent-output", "run-artifact"]`, all in `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/evidence_replay_smoke.rs` (the Round 944 rule).

BLINDNESS: each author was a separate subagent with fresh context, given only the firewall and the verbatim brief — never this runbook, the changelog, a design doc, or the other author's work. Both worked in isolated directories. The orchestrator ran every command, authored no manifest, and repaired no file.
carry_forward_bullets: WORLD LIMIT: n=2, one world premise, one lineage orchestrating. One instance, not a distribution. Both authors were given the same fiction, so their agreement is weaker evidence than two premises would be.

NOT MEASURED, with the reason now on record: `threshold` / K-of-N still has NO authored witness, and this run says why rather than leaving it a silence — both authors declined it because every shut way in this world had exactly one opener. A premise requiring two-of-three conditions is a different arm, and it is the only way to close that branch.

The `undirected` branch also still has no authored witness, and now has a measured cause: both authors chose directed IN ORDER to give one way different costs in each direction. Whether an undirected map is reachable at all from the contract is untested; every corpus on record has chosen directed.

ALREADY DECIDED, not a debt: `parameters` / `parameter_deltas` / `parameter_gates` / `fact_counts` stay verb-only. Round 959 measured zero recorded demand for them and wrote the resume condition — build the wire when a brief asks for a meter.

OPEN FOR A LATER ROUND, found by this arm and not repaired by it: whether the contract leads an author to read an exclusive rule's `per:` against the typed leg's direction. Stage B declared `per: "object"` on `held_by(thing, person)` and described it in prose as "one holder per thing", which is `per: subject`. The gate caught the divergence; nothing checks that a rule's declaration and an author's understanding of it agree.

Round 965.decision_summary: R965 (BUILD) — the contract described a leg by the role it plays, and two blind authors read it opposite ways. Round 961 left Stage B's `validate-continuity` violations 2 unresolved: the rule is named `one-holder-per-thing`, declares `per: object`, and both offending facts carry the same object. Measuring before touching anything (the Round 924 discipline) answered a bigger question than the one asked — a census of EVERY exclusive rule on record, 82 rules across 43 authored files, finds the predicate `held_by` declared with `per: subject` in one corpus and `per: object` in another, both named for custody, both meaning to say one holder per thing. ★ONE OF THEM IS SIMPLY INVERTED AND THE CONTRACT CAUSED IT. `held_by(thing, holder)` puts the thing on the SUBJECT leg, so 'one holder per thing' is `per: subject`; the `object` gloss read 'at most one HOLDER per OBJECT', naming the leg it keys on and describing the other leg by the ROLE it plays — a role that is only stable when the predicate is written holder-first. An author who writes the same relation the other way round reads that sentence, agrees with it, and gets the opposite rule under the name of the intended one. Both glosses now lead with the leg relation and give the role reading second WITH the predicate ordering it assumes, and the class line stops claiming which key is location and which is custody at all. ★NO GATE IS POSSIBLE AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO: nothing in a predicate's declaration marks which leg is the holder, so a rejection rule would either reject correct corpora or assert a naming convention this substrate does not have. What IS checkable is that each gloss names both legs — and the leg names are read off the `ExclusiveKey` variants, never typed into the test.
changes_bullets: MEASURED BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING, the Round 924 discipline, and the census answered a bigger question than the one asked. Every exclusive rule on record: 82 rules across 43 authored files. The predicate `held_by` appears with `per: subject` in one corpus (`disclosure-craft`, rule `custody-exclusive`) and with `per: object` in another (`side-table` stage B, rule `one-holder-per-thing`). Same relation, same intent, opposite key.

WHICH ONE IS RIGHT IS NOT A MATTER OF TASTE. `held_by(thing, holder)` puts the thing on the subject leg, so "one holder per thing" means at most one OBJECT value per subject — `per: subject`. The side-table author wrote `per: object`, which is at most one thing per holder: the opposite rule, under a name that says the intended one. That is the Round 961 Stage B `validate-continuity` violations 2, and the author's sealed self-report describes the rule correctly while the declaration says something else.

★THE CONTRACT CAUSED IT, and the mechanism is one word. The `object` gloss read "at most one HOLDER per OBJECT (conservation/custody: one holder per thing)". It named the leg it keys ON and described the other leg by the ROLE that leg plays — but a role is only stable if the predicate is written holder-first. Write it thing-first and the sentence is still readable, still agreeable, and now describes the inverse of what the value does.

BOTH GLOSSES NOW STATE THE LEG RELATION FIRST and give the role reading second, WITH the predicate ordering it assumes spelled out (`holds(holder, thing)` versus `held_by(thing, holder)`), plus the measured evidence that two corpora disagree. The class-level `exclusive` line stops asserting which key is location and which is custody at all: that depends on how the author's predicate orders its legs, not on the rule's name.

`every_exclusive_key_gloss_names_both_legs` — the checkable residue. Each gloss must name EVERY `ExclusiveKey` variant, and the leg names are not typed into the test: they ARE the variants, read off the enum through the same `serde_variants` oracle the contract renders from. A gloss that names only its own leg is, by construction, describing the other one by role.

THE PAIR ASSUMPTION IS ASSERTED, NOT ASSUMED. "Both legs" is read as "every variant", which is the right rule only while `ExclusiveKey` is a pair; the test says so and fails on a third variant rather than quietly checking something weaker.
verification_bullets: J8 — NON-VACUITY AGAINST THE REAL PRIOR WORDING, not a constructed probe. Both glosses were restored to their pre-Round-965 text by pattern-replacing them back (asserted to land exactly once), and the gate went red naming the `subject` gloss and quoting it. Both old glosses fail it: one names `subject` and calls the other leg a "co-holding value", the other names `object` and calls it a "holder".

THE CENSUS IS REPRODUCIBLE AND WAS RUN OVER THE WHOLE CORPUS, not a sample: every `*rules*.json` under `claudedocs/`, every rule with `class: exclusive`. 82 rules, 43 files. The `held_by` split is 2 rules `per: object` and 2 rules `per: subject`.

Round 975.decision_summary: R975 (DEBT) — the one excuse that made a claim about a store was wrong in both of its halves, and the kit had said the true thing all along. Round 974 settled 65 of 108 banner-carrying artifacts and excused 43, and 42 of those excuses name a mechanism: a harness this job does not build at a pinned revision, a runbook that appends an exit code so a verb's stdout is only a prefix of the recorded bytes. The forty-third was the one Round 974 called its only finding about the evidence itself, and it read: "the recorded run reports 23 placed sections where importing the declared manifests yields 22, so the bytes are evidence of a store the record does not describe". ★BOTH FACTUAL HALVES OF THAT SENTENCE ARE FALSE. The run did not place 23 sections — it placed 22 of 23, which is the SAME placed count as the rebuild, and the difference is entirely in the total. That direction matters rather than being a slip: the surplus section is UNPLACED, and an unplaced section with no fact anchored to it is exactly the shape of a stray, which is what it turned out to be. ★AND THE RECORD DESCRIBES THAT STORE PRECISELY, IN TWO PLACES, ONE OF THEM A SEALED INPUT OF THE SAME UNIT. The author's `run/stage-a/iteration-notes.md` — declared, sha-pinned, role `run-artifact` — has a section headed "Store side effect I could not undo" naming `sc-probe`, its title, its parent doc, the probe that created it, and stating that `order.json` does not place it, no fact names it, `sections.json` does not contain it, and it will surface as an unplaced section in any frontier report. The experiment report goes further and states the very consequence Round 974 rediscovered by diffing: "it never entered the tracked corpus — sc-probe appears zero times in stage-a/sections.json, so the registered replay rebuilds a store without it; the pollution lived only in the gitignored scratch store the frontier was read from". ★THE MECHANISM IS MEASURED AND NOT INFERRED. Importing the kit's declared manifests into a fresh workspace yields 22 sections with no `sc-probe`; adding exactly the one section the notes describe flips `order_nodes=22/22` to `order_nodes=22/23` and prints the NOTICE line the recorded transcript ends with. ★THE ERROR IS THE CLASS ROUND 974 ITSELF NAMED. That round stopped deriving commands from banners because a guess was wrong 36 of 74 times, and then derived a claim about a store from the manifests and concluded the record was silent — the answer was in the kit, in a file the search did not open. A negative existential over a record is not settled by reading part of it. ★THE RULE THE FIX LEAVES IS THAT AN EXCUSE NAMES A MECHANISM AND THE NUMBERS GO IN FIELDS. Measured before it was written: 43 excuses, 4 distinct texts, and exactly one carries a digit — the wrong one. A mechanism is true at every revision and therefore needs no count; a count is state, and state is something a program can settle. This is Round 959's rule (a number no program reads does not belong in shipped prose) reaching a field that had nowhere else to put one, so the fix is the somewhere: `reproduced_exit` for a status, and a new `store_surplus` for what the run's store held that the replay does not create. ★THE TWO ARMS MAKE THE FALSE CLAIM UNWRITABLE rather than merely correcting this instance. A named id must be created by no step of the unit's replay, which is what makes a command impossible; and it must be found in that unit's own sealed evidence, which is what makes "the record does not describe it" false about it. An id that fails either arm is not a surplus, it is a guess about a store.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/evidence_replay_smoke.rs` — `store_surplus` on an input: the ids the recorded run's store held that this unit's replay does not create. It exists because the prose that carried this claim was wrong in both halves and nothing could tell, and it is a list of ids rather than a sentence because an id is a thing two checks can resolve.

Same file — `an_excuse_names_a_mechanism_and_leaves_the_numbers_to_the_fields` rejects a digit in `unreproducible`. An excuse says what STOPS a command from existing, which is true at every revision; a count is state and has fields that settle it. Measured before building: of 43 excuses and 4 distinct texts, the three right ones are structural and carry no digit, so the rule has no false positive to pay for on this tree.

Same file — `an_excuse_that_blames_the_store_names_what_the_record_describes` holds both arms. A named id must be created by no applied step of the unit's replay, and must occur in at least one OTHER sealed input of the same unit. A kit that declares a surplus must declare a replay for the claim to be about, and a surplus without an excuse is a field with no claim behind it.

Same file — `ids_a_step_creates` and `ids_a_unit_creates` derive what a replay puts in a store, and the citation walk now reads through the same resolver instead of extracting section and fact ids inline. Two rules were about to ask one question; what they would have drifted about is the whole of what both decide.

Round 979.decision_summary: A round's census reaches the frozen ledger as data, and no wire into it accepts a number. Round 976 refused a word-list gate on census prose and named the reopen condition: a census carried in a FIELD, the way Round 975 gave `store_surplus` one, so what a later round inherits is data rather than a sentence. Round 977 built the recount and the tracked report FIRST, on the argument that a field with no program behind it is a hand-typed count in a new place. This is the other half, built so that the order Round 977 insisted on cannot be undone later: `AtomicChangelogEntry.population_census` holds `{axis, left_label, left, right_label, right}` per axis, audit-only with no publishable twin, and BOTH wires take a boolean. `append-changelog-entry --record-census` and the MCP tool's `record_census` read the counts from the `[census] report` the workspace declares in `mnemosyne.toml`; there is deliberately no flag, in either wire, through which a count can be typed. The tracked report is now the serialization of the store's own `PopulationCensus` type, so the file format is not a second contract that could drift from the field.
changes_bullets: `PopulationCensus` + `AtomicChangelogEntry.population_census` (schema v44 to v45, declarative new-field-default: no migration arm, a pre-v45 entry re-serializes byte-identically). Self-describing on purpose — the ledger is frozen and the program that recounts an axis is not, so `10` against `27` means nothing once the labels are gone. That is Round 452 self-containment applied to a struct. Audit-only with NO publishable twin: the publishable layer exists so prose can be redacted, there is no prose here, and a mutable copy of a count is exactly the hand-typed number the field exists to make impossible.

`check_population_census` at the primitive, the shared enforcement surface for both wires (the Round 305 lesson: two writers with one invariant set each is a field with no invariants). Rejects a blank or untrimmed axis, a blank side label, and one axis stated twice. The COUNTS are deliberately unvalidated — a universal is true exactly when one side is empty, so rejecting a zero side would refuse the reading a census is most often taken to settle.

`[census] report` in the workspace config, read by BOTH the gate that blesses the report and the append path that fills the field, so the path is one datum. `ops::render_population_census` / `ops::workspace_population_census` are the single render and the single resolver; the CLI and MCP wires call the resolver and pass a boolean, which is why there is no second reading to diverge from. `claudedocs/population-census.txt` becomes `population-census.json` (typed, `.gitignore` exception retargeted); the one-line-per-axis rendering survives as `PopulationAxis::line` for messages.

`validate-workspace` gains the contemporaneity gate, and its question is narrow because only the narrow one has a right answer: not "does every recorded census match today" (which would fail on every honest older entry) but "does the census this commit is ADDING match this tree". Decidable via `git show HEAD:` on the sidecar; every way of not knowing — no `[census]`, no git, no HEAD, an unreadable committed store — yields no violation rather than a guess.
verification_bullets: Measured before building, and the demand was on the record: Rounds 970, 972 and 976 each measured an axis by hand, Round 968 took its baseline from Round 961's sentence and reported a move from zero when the truth was two to five, Round 915 took one from Round 914's sentence. The inheritance chain Round 924 to Round 936 to Round 961 to Round 968 is the harm end to end.

The new ledger gate is RED ON TODAY'S TREE WITHOUT ANY INJECTION and names exactly what is missing: `every_axis_the_ledger_recorded_is_one_this_tree_still_recounts` fails with "no ledger entry records a population census, so this gate passes without reading anything" until this entry lands. That is the non-vacuity floor asserting itself rather than being claimed.

5 primitive invariant tests (blank axis / blank side label / untrimmed axis / an axis stated twice reject; an EMPTY SIDE is accepted, which is the assertion that keeps the counts unvalidated on purpose; the field round-trips through serialization and does not read as a publishable divergence; an entry that records nothing writes no key).

6 wire tests through the REAL binary: the recorded rows equal the report's `axes` verbatim (compared against bytes this test renders through `render_population_census`, never against literals — a hand-typed expectation passes whenever the wire and the test make the same mistake); an append that does not ask records nothing; a missing `[census]`, a non-JSON report and a report with no axes each refuse AND leave no entry behind.

The contemporaneity gate is tested in the order the defect happens: append against the current report (clean) — move a count while the entry is still uncommitted (REJECTS, naming the entry and the axis) — commit, move a count again (CLEAN, because history is supposed to disagree with a population that moved on). Either half alone is the wrong gate.

`both_wires_take_their_census_from_the_one_resolver` reads both wires' sources with the site count asserted, because a check that silently found nothing would report "parity holds" for a tree in which nobody writes the field.

Two structural gates already in the tree caught this change and were answered rather than worked around: `ref_field_classification` demanded all three new string places be classified, and `docs_match_reality_smoke` demanded `[census]` be documented in both schema guides.

The resume condition is unchanged and is now cheaper to act on: a round that needs one of those baselines writes the walk, and the field files it from that moment on.

THE FOUR SENTENCES ROUND 976 BOUND BY HAND STAY BOUND BY HAND, and that is a property of the freeze rather than an omission. Rounds 934, 956, 961 and 967 cannot grow a field, so `the_ledger_census_claims_this_tree_can_recount_are_recounted` remains the only way to make leaning on them fail. Two homes for "which ledger claims are bound" is the cost the append-only ledger charges, and it stops growing here: every claim from this round forward can carry its own.

THE CONTEMPORANEITY GATE PASSES VACUOUSLY IN CI, by construction — nothing is uncommitted there — so it bites only in the tree that wrote the entry, on the `validate-workspace` the pre-commit hook already runs. That is the same reach as the runbook-tracking gate and for the same reason: a defect that can only exist before a commit has to be caught before the commit. A workspace that commits its store without running the hook gets no protection, and nothing here tells it so.

`both_wires_take_their_census_from_the_one_resolver` reads both wires' sources with the site count asserted, because a check that silently found nothing would report "parity holds" for a tree in which nobody writes the field.

Two structural gates already in the tree caught this change and were answered rather than worked around: `ref_field_classification` demanded all three new string places be classified, and `docs_match_reality_smoke` demanded `[census]` be documented in both schema guides.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: WHAT THIS DOES NOT REACH IS AN AXIS THAT HAS NO PROGRAM. Round 976 counted 25 census claims in the ledger at its tightest reading and three that could be recounted at all; the rest — no corpus has ever declared an exit, no authored corpus registers a meter, no author produced both a map and a telling — name axes nobody has written a walk for, and `--record-census` can only file what `census::axes` can count. The resume condition is unchanged and is now cheaper to act on: a round that needs one of those baselines writes the walk, and the field files it from that moment on.

THE FOUR SENTENCES ROUND 976 BOUND BY HAND STAY BOUND BY HAND, and that is a property of the freeze rather than an omission. Rounds 934, 956, 961 and 967 cannot grow a field, so `the_ledger_census_claims_this_tree_can_recount_are_recounted` remains the only way to make leaning on them fail. Two homes for "which ledger claims are bound" is the cost the append-only ledger charges, and it stops growing here: every claim from this round forward can carry its own.

THE CONTEMPORANEITY GATE PASSES VACUOUSLY IN CI, by construction — nothing is uncommitted there — so it bites only in the tree that wrote the entry, on the `validate-workspace` the pre-commit hook already runs. That is the same reach as the runbook-tracking gate and for the same reason: a defect that can only exist before a commit has to be caught before the commit. A workspace that commits its store without running the hook gets no protection, and nothing here tells it so.

THE REPORT'S FIRST-WITNESS RENDERING IS GONE, deliberately. Round 977's line carried "(first <label>: <path>)" as a convenience; the report is now exactly the type the field stores, and adding the witness back would put an arbitrary sorted-first path into every entry that records a census. Round 977's own resume condition for widening to witnesses is unchanged: the first time a count moves inexplicably.

Round 980.decision_summary: A verdict of "no violations" is worth what the reach behind it is worth, and Round 979's contemporaneity check reported only violations. It has four ways of finding nothing and three of them are not "nothing is wrong": a workspace that declares no census, one where no entry has recorded one, and one where which entries this commit ADDS cannot be known (outside a repository, before the first commit, or with a committed store that will not parse). All four printed the same thing — nothing at all — so a workspace that had never installed the pre-commit hook read exactly like one the gate had just cleared. Round 979 named that silence in its own carry ("A workspace that commits its store without running the hook gets no protection, and nothing here tells it so") and left it as a reach statement rather than a defect. It is a defect by this repo's own rule: Round 854 established that a zero out of a population of zero is not a clean bill, and every other axis in the same report prints its population. `CensusReach` now names the four states and `validate-workspace` prints one on every run.
changes_bullets: `CensusReach` — a typed four-arm answer to "what could the check see": `NotDeclared`, `NothingRecorded`, `Undecidable {reason}`, and `Measured {recorded, uncommitted, rows_checked}`. `render_plain` matches it arm by arm, so EXHAUSTIVENESS IS THE COMPILER'S: a fifth state cannot be added without a rendering, which is the half no test can hold.

Every not-knowing carries its own reason rather than collapsing into one word — git is not runnable / no committed store at HEAD / the committed store does not parse. A consumer reading "UNDECIDABLE" needs to know which, because the remedies differ and only one of them is "commit something".

`census_contemporaneity` replaces `uncommitted_census_disagreements`: same narrow question, but it now returns the population it read beside the violations, and it asks whether the workspace declares a report FIRST so that "off" is distinguishable from "clean".
verification_bullets: Four workspaces in four states through the real binary, and NO TWO MAY SAY THE SAME THING — the pairwise-distinctness assertion is what makes the four arms evidence rather than four spellings of silence. The measured arm additionally asserts the numbers it read (`1 uncommitted`, `2 row(s)`), so a line that printed a plausible constant would fail.

Two injections, each restored from a copy. Collapsing `NothingRecorded` onto `NotDeclared` fires with "`no [census] table` and `nothing recorded` are different states and say the same thing"; silencing the line fires with "the measured state does not report the population it read: ". THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THE FIRST INJECTION DID NOT APPLY — rustfmt had rewrapped the match arm the anchor named — AND THE TEST WAS GREEN. A green under an unapplied injection is not evidence; the anchor was re-read from the formatted source and the injection redone.

carry_forward_bullets: THE ROUND 978 CARRY IS CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT, AND THIS IS THE RECORD OF IT — the measurement existed one round before this sentence did, and Round 979 failed to file it. Round 981.decision_summary: The second write path into `population_census` had never been executed. Round 979 put a field in the frozen ledger with two wires and checked their parity by READING both sources — that neither accepts a count — which is a real check and cannot see the thing that actually breaks a wire: a serde key that never deserializes, or an argument read into nothing. `record_census` would then be silently false forever, and an entry an agent appended through MCP would record no census while the round believed it had. Nothing in this repository executed an MCP tool at all, so half of a parity claim about a frozen field rested on prose. It did not need the crate reshaped: `mnemosyne-mcp` is a bin with a `#[cfg(test)]` module and a public `MnemosyneServer::new`, so the tool is callable in-process. The oracle is the CLI's own answer — the recorded rows must equal what `ops::workspace_population_census` yields for the same workspace — so the test cannot pass by agreeing with a mistake spelled twice.
changes_bullets: `mcp_append_records_the_census_the_shared_resolver_yields` — the first test in this repository to CALL an MCP tool. The arguments arrive as JSON, the way an agent sends them, so a key that does not deserialize fails here rather than defaulting to false; the entry is then reloaded from disk and its rows compared against the shared resolver's answer. A second append WITHOUT the flag asserts the non-vacuity half: the field's default is not what the first assertion is measuring.
`append_changelog_entry_schema_exposes_record_census` — an agent can only call what the schema shows it (the Round 690 rule applied to the flag that decides whether a census is recorded at all).

The source-scan parity check now reads PRODUCTION ONLY, cut at `#[cfg(test)]`. The new MCP test builds a `PopulationCensus` as its oracle and the scan read that as a wire minting its own count — a false positive that would have forced the behavioural test back out of the tree. The cut asserts it actually happened (a marker that stopped matching would silently scan the whole file again, which is how the check first went wrong).
verification_bullets: Both injections fired in their own arm, restored from a copy. Reading the flag into nothing (`if false && args.0.record_census`) fails with `left: []` against the resolver's row — the silent-false failure mode, printed. Renaming the serde key to `recordCensus` fails TWICE and differently: the deserialization assertion says "the flag deserialized as false", and the schema assertion prints the agent-visible property list with `recordCensus` in it.

The new test found a defect in the check it was added beside: `both_wires_take_their_census_from_the_one_resolver` went red on this change, and it was right about the letter and wrong about the question. Scoping it to production is the repair, not an exemption — a wire that minted a count in production still fails.
Workspace 1493 tests (Round 979 shipped 1490), 6 tests in `mnemosyne-mcp` where the census pair now sits, clippy -D clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace clean.

Round 982.decision_summary: Round 980 wrote that telling a consumer to install the pre-commit hook was "a limit of where the tool sits, not an omission", and that is true of the sentence and false of the question. The question is not whether the tool can see a consumer's hooks; it is whether the check needs one. It does not. Round 979 built the contemporaneity check against the WORKING TREE, which is decidable only before a commit, and concluded from that that the reach ended at the pre-commit hook. Asking the TIP COMMIT the same question decides it after the fact: the entries HEAD added that HEAD~1 did not, checked against the census report as THAT COMMIT LEFT IT. That arm needs no hook, runs wherever `validate-workspace` runs, and in a consumer's repository that means CI. It is deliberately bounded to one commit back — asking "what did the report say when THIS entry landed" for an arbitrary entry is a pickaxe walk over every revision of a multi-megabyte store, and a gate that costs that is a gate someone turns off — and what falls outside the bound is counted and printed rather than left to read as clean.
changes_bullets: `CensusReach::Measured` gains `landed_at_head` and `out_of_reach` beside `uncommitted`, and the printed line names all three. The bound is a design decision, so it is reported as a population rather than described in a comment: a reader sees how many entries the check did not reach.

`git_store_entries` / `git_census_report` — the two bounded git reads the new arm needs (the store at `HEAD~1`, the report at `HEAD`). Every failure is a `None` that moves entries to `out_of_reach`, never a violation: a shallow clone, a first commit, a report tracked under a different path back then, and a workspace that adopted `[census]` later are all states in which the honest answer is "not reached".
The printed sentence no longer claims the check "reaches only UNCOMMITTED entries" — it said that while shipping an arm that reaches further, which is the class of defect Round 980 existed to close.
verification_bullets: THE STRONGER CHECK IMMEDIATELY FOUND A DEFECT IN THIS ROUND'S OWN TEST FIXTURE. Phase 3 of `a_census_being_added_must_match_the_tree_and_a_committed_one_need_not` committed the entry together with a report it did NOT match — which is exactly the sequence Round 979 named as the window derivation alone cannot close — and called the result "history is free to disagree". The old check could not see it; the new one rejects it. The fixture now puts the report back in agreement before committing, and a separate test asserts the bad sequence IS caught: `a_round_that_lands_a_disagreeing_report_is_caught_after_the_commit`, with no hook anywhere in it.

AN INJECTION APPLIED, COMPILED, AND LEFT ALL EIGHT TESTS GREEN — and that is a measurement, not a pass. Swapping the tip comparison from the report at `HEAD` to the report in the working tree changed nothing any test could see, so the suite did not actually distinguish the two. Phase 3b closes it: the report moves in the working tree and is NOT committed, and the landed entry must stay clean, because an uncommitted edit cannot retroactively make a finished round wrong. With that phase the same injection fires.
The other injection — treating the tip commit as out of reach, which is Round 979's behaviour — fails both affected tests by name.
Workspace 1494 tests, clippy -D clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace clean, and its own line now reads "1 entry(ies) record one, 0 uncommitted, 0 landed at HEAD, 1 older than this check walks".
carry_forward_bullets: THREE ROUNDS RUNNING, THE UNREGISTERED DEBT WAS THE SAME SHAPE: something written into a carry as a LIMIT that a program could still decide. Round 979 wrote "nothing here tells it so" and Round 980 had to build the reporting. Round 980 wrote "no gate inside the tool can know that" and this round had to build the arm. Round 981's was the same in a different register — a parity claim held by reading source rather than by running it. The rule this leaves is narrow enough to apply: before writing that something is a limit of where the tool sits, state the question the tool cannot answer, and check whether it is the question that matters. Both times it was not.

WHAT IS OUT OF REACH IS COUNTED AND WILL GROW. Entries older than the tip commit are never re-checked against the report they were filed against, and this tree already has one. The bound is deliberate, and the resume condition is a round that needs an older answer badly enough to pay for it: the cost is a pickaxe walk over the sidecar's history, which is why it is not paid speculatively.

THE TOOL STILL HAS TO BE RUN. This arm removes the hook from the requirement and puts the check anywhere `validate-workspace` runs, which for this repository is CI on every push. A consumer whose CI never runs it gets nothing — and that one IS a limit of where the tool sits, in the sense the phrase should be reserved for: the tool is not executed at all.

Measured over the whole ledger — 2759 carry bullets, 45 of them in 43 rounds assert a negative capability of the tool ("nothing tells", "no gate", "cannot know", "a limit of where"). That population is large enough that a gate would not be speculative, and reading it says a gate is the wrong answer anyway: most of the 45 are correctly classified (a predicate declaration genuinely cannot say which leg holds; an advisory genuinely has no CI teeth by decision), and three different readings of "does this bullet carry a reopening condition" give three different answers — the Round 976 signature for an axis no word list settles. SO THE GATE IS NOT BUILT, AND THAT IS THE MEASUREMENT'S ANSWER RATHER THAN A DEFERRAL. What the measurement DID produce is a live instance nobody had found by reading: Round 976's own carry says a consumer with `entry_id_prefix = ""` gets neither half of the dating protection "and nothing here tells them so" — and nothing did. `validate-workspace` now names that state.
changes_bullets: `EntryIdDating` — `NotDemanded` when the workspace configures no `schema.entry_id_prefix` (the Round 976 gate stands down, so no entry id has to carry a number and every count in the ledger's prose is undated), `Demanded {dated, total}` otherwise. Printed on every run, so a workspace that HAS the guarantee and one that never could no longer print the same clean.

`dated` is counted with `project::parse_round_number`, production's own resolver — the same one the projection keys on and the same one Round 976's gate is paired with — so this line cannot say one thing while the gate does another.
The prefix is resolved through `workspace_entry_id_prefix`, the shared path the append gate uses, for the same reason.

Round 984.decision_summary: The last live build item from this session's audit, and the premise had to be checked before it could be paid: Round 981 carried that `validate-workspace` prints the citation gate's file counts off the DISK, so a reader with a clone cannot reproduce them — the production instance of Round 978's rule. The tree already had a VCS axis over the read set (Round 864), which would have made this carry wrong, and it does not: that axis asks `--others --ignored`, whether a read file is BUILD OUTPUT, and a work-in-progress source is neither ignored nor in the record, so it is invisible there. The predicate the count needs is `--others` alone — is this file one a clone would have. The walk stays a filesystem walk on purpose, and that decision is now stated with its direction rather than implied: reading an untracked source is the gate biting at the writing moment, before the file is staged, and a superset can only scan more, never miss. What was wrong was that the printed number did not say how much of itself a clone would not have. It does now, in both states, advisory.
changes_bullets: `VcsRecordAxis` + `vcs_absent_from_record_among` — the read set's population question, with three states for the Round 856 reason ("none absent" and "nobody asked" are different facts). `validate-workspace` prints it directly under the coverage counts it decomposes: "N of M read file(s) are absent from the record — a clone counts M-N".

The git query is now ONE site, `ls_files_others_among`, taking the differing flag as an argument, because two hand-copied bodies differing by `--ignored` is how one of them silently loses the other's pathspec scoping or its `-z` handling. `vcs_ignored_among` keeps its exact behaviour and its extension histogram moves to a shared helper.

The walk itself is unchanged. Asking `git ls-files` for the READ SET would have narrowed what the gate reads, which is the wrong direction for a check whose value is catching a hallucinated citation at the moment it is written.
verification_bullets: The fixture makes one of two read files untracked, because a tree where everything is tracked reports zero absent and would pass against an axis that answered zero unconditionally.

Both injections fire in their own arm, restored from a copy. Giving the record axis the BUILD-OUTPUT predicate (`--ignored`) fails with `left: 0` against the fixture's one untracked source. Deleting the shared query's intersection with the caller's set fails naming `target/junk.rs`.

THE SECOND INJECTION LEFT EVERY TEST GREEN ON ITS FIRST RUN, and that is a measurement of the tests rather than a pass: no fixture held a file the query would return and the walk would not read. `crates/alpha/src/target/junk.rs` is that file — skipped by the walk (`is_skipped_dir`), untracked, and not ignored in this fixture — and with it the same injection fires. This is the third time this session an applied, compiling injection came back green and the test set was the thing at fault.
Workspace 1496 tests, clippy -D clean, fmt clean, and this repo's own line reads "0 of 105 read file(s) are absent from the record — a clone counts 105".
carry_forward_bullets: WHAT IS DECOMPOSED IS THE READ SET, not every number on the coverage line. "233 rust source(s), 97 scanned" are counts from the same walk and are not file sets this axis holds; if an untracked source existed it would appear in the read set too, so the class is covered, but a reader wanting those two numbers decomposed would need the walk to carry its own sets. The resume condition is a consumer who reports a difference in them between a developer and CI.

THE AXIS IS ADVISORY AND WILL STAY THAT WAY UNTIL SOMETHING MEASURES OTHERWISE. What it buys is that a difference between two machines is now readable instead of silent.

Round 985.decision_summary: R985 (MEASURE -> BUILD) — two of the three census claims Round 976 filed as unfalsifiable were not merely walkable, they were already false, and the third is refused for a reason worth more than the axis. Round 976 measured that no word list can tell a census sentence from a rule at append time, refused the prose gate, and left three claims naming an axis "a later round could give a program": no corpus in this tree has ever declared an exit (Rounds 913, 914, 915), no authored corpus registers a meter (Round 941), no author ever produced both a map and a telling (Round 942). Its resume condition was "a round that needs one of those baselines badly enough to write the walk". This round wrote them, and what the walks say is that the sentences had gone stale under a growing record while nothing could see it. STAR THE EXIT CLAIM IS REFUTED BY SIX CORPORA. A step is a position fact that supersedes another in the same frame — the author's own claim "this is one move" — and it is an ascent exactly when the place it arrives at transitively contains the place it left, which is Round 913's own classification. Recounted over the record: six map corpora declare one, against twenty-four that declare none. STAR AND THERE WAS NO RESOLVER TO BORROW, WHICH IS WHY THE CLAIM COULD ONLY EVER BE ANSWERED BY LOOKING. `continuity.rs` classifies a declared step against this same containment relation but collapses ascent and descent into one `Hierarchy` arm, deliberately: Round 915 settled that leaving crosses nothing and needs no parent-scope edge, so the gate has no reason to tell the two directions apart and does not. The question Rounds 913 and 914 asked is one the shipping gate does not ask, and that is exactly the shape of a claim that goes stale in silence. STAR THE BOTH-AXES CELL IS TEN, AND THE ARM THAT FILLED IT WAS DESIGNED BY THE ROUND WHOSE SENTENCE STAYED. Round 942 measured the map-and-telling join as empty and designed a new arm to fill it; the disclosed-place and k-of-n corpora carry both halves today. Ten recorded submissions carry a map and a telling against twenty-four carrying one. Round 968 is the measured case of a later round taking such a sentence as its baseline, so all five sentences are now bound to the axes that refute them and a baseline drawn from any of them fails a test that prints the sentence. STAR ROUND 942 COUNTED A POPULATION THE RECORD DOES NOT HOLD, WHICH IS ROUND 978's DEFECT IN A SECOND PLACE. It measured over "all 90 stores on disk"; measured at this round, the tracked JSON under `claudedocs` holds exactly one artifact shaped like a store. That population was the authoring machine's rather than the record's — the same defect Round 978 found in Round 972's counts, and Round 976 listed the axis as programmable without noticing it. So the axis is keyed on SUBMISSIONS, which is what the record does hold: a facts manifest is the artifact an author hands in, and the map it was written against is the rules artifact beside it. STAR THE METER AXIS IS REFUSED, AND ITS REOPENING CONDITION IS A TEST RATHER THAN A SENTENCE. An authored corpus cannot register a meter: `FactsManifest` is the whole of what a submission may declare and it has no slot, the only door being the `add-parameter` primitive, which is an operator's call. A census there would report zero out of every corpus on record and read as a finding about what authors chose when it is a fact about the manifest schema — Round 854's rule, that a zero over a population with no door is not a clean bill, in the exact form it would have shipped in. The refusal is therefore carried as an executable condition: a manifest declaring a meter is imported through the real binary and the registry stays empty, with both halves of the non-vacuity asserted beside it. The day `FactsManifest` grows the slot that test fails, which is the day the census becomes worth building, and nothing has to remember. STAR A TYPE THIS ROUND DESIGNED WAS KILLED BY ITS OWN MEASUREMENT. Both new claims are negative-existence claims, so the axes looked like they would need a declared evidentiary shape — an enum separating "refutes a universal, and is evidence while both sides are populated" from "asserts one side is empty" — because the standing invariant demands heterogeneity and an empty side would have forced it to be loosened for every axis at once, which is this repo's half-enforced-invariant ban. The walks then returned six against twenty-four and ten against twenty-four. Both are heterogeneous, the existing invariant applies unchanged, and the enum is not built.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/evidence_replay_smoke.rs`, `mod census` — `boundary_crossing_census`, a fifth axis: recorded map corpora split by whether the author ever declared a step that LEAVES a container. The relation is not guessed — a transition rule names both the predicate that states a position and the predicate that states containment, and the walk reads the ones that rule names.

Same module — `map_and_telling_census`, a sixth axis: authored submissions split by whether one carries BOTH halves of the disclosed-place join. The population is submissions rather than stores because the record holds one store, and a census whose witnesses no reader can fetch is the defect Round 978 named.

Same module — `declares_a_telling` reads `disclosure_plans` in both shapes, a list in a submission manifest and a map in a store, because an empty one of either is no telling at all. That distinction is what Round 942 turned on: every store it found with a map carried an empty registry.

`the_ledger_census_claims_this_tree_can_recount_are_recounted` — five sentences bound where there were three. Rounds 913, 914 and 915 against the corpora that declare an exit, Round 942 against the submissions carrying both halves. Each is stated in the DIRECTION of the finding, so it does not rot as the corpora grow.

`no_authored_manifest_can_register_a_meter_which_is_why_that_axis_is_refused` — the refusal of the third axis, carried as its own reopening condition. It runs the wire rather than reading the struct, and both assertions count through ONE reader, so a zero cannot be an artifact of the pointer it was read through.
`claudedocs/population-census.json` — regenerated in this commit, which is where the two new axes enter the file's history.
verification_bullets: STAR THE MEASUREMENT DECIDED THE SHAPE OF ALL THREE AXES, AND IT DISAGREED WITH THE PLAN IN EVERY ONE. Two claims Round 976 called unfalsifiable are refuted by the record; the third cannot be given a walk at all; and the type designed to hold negative-existence axes was killed because neither new axis turned out to be one.

INJECTION A, no step is ever an ascent: three arms fired together and each named its own job — the ledger binding printed Round 913's sentence with "0 map corpora ... against 30", the heterogeneity gate reported the axis homogeneous, and the tracked-report drift gate refused the file.
INJECTION C, no manifest ever declares a telling: the same three arms fired, printing Round 942's "The both-axes cell is zero" beside a recount of 0 against 30.

INJECTION D, the map keyed on `class: transition` instead of `adjacency`: ONLY the drift gate fired, which is the correct arm — a wrong token still finds corpora carrying both, so the binding cannot see it and the checked-in count can. It revived exactly the false positive Round 942 recorded, `continuity-stress` declaring that class for `gate_state` with zero adjacency facts, taking the axis from 10-against-24 to 11-against-28.

INJECTION E, the meter reader pointed at a key the store does not have: the second assertion fired — "the operator's door registered nothing THIS READER CAN SEE, so the zero above is a fact about the reader". That is the vacuous pass the one-reader construction exists to forbid.
INJECTION F, a new axis naming its witnesses by absolute path: the witness gate fired and listed 6 of 390, so the two new axes are inside Round 978's rule rather than beside it.

STAR INJECTION B WAS GREEN AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A PASS. Deleting the requirement that a step and the step it supersedes share a frame left all 34 tests in the file green, because the loose and the frame-scoped readings return the same population over today's record. The scoping is kept for agreement with the gate's semantics and the code now says in place that nothing tests it, so a later round does not read it as protected.
Every injection was reverted by restoring a COPY taken before the first one, never by `git checkout`, and each was applied by a script asserting its anchor occurs exactly once.
1497 workspace tests pass (1496 before), 0 failed, `--no-fail-fast`, full log retained under the session scratchpad; clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean.
`validate-workspace` T1 orphan 0, T3 reject 0, entries and sections otherwise unchanged; `validate-code-refs` violations 0.

Citation hygiene (R255): Rounds 854, 913, 914, 915, 941, 942, 968, 972, 976 and 978 verified present with `query --changelog-entry`, and Round 985 verified absent, before this entry was appended and before any round reference in the code landed. Every cited fragment was resolved in the frozen ledger first — `ledger_unit` requires each to occur in exactly one prose unit of the round that states it.
carry_forward_bullets: STAR ROUND 976's CARRY IS DISCHARGED, AND ITS FRAMING WAS WRONG IN A WAY WORTH KEEPING. It called the three claims "true as far as anyone knows and unfalsifiable by any program that exists". Two were false and the program that falsifies each is thirty lines; the third is unfalsifiable BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by absence of effort. "Nobody has written the walk" and "there is no door to walk" are different answers, and only the second is a limit — this is the fourth round in a row where a carry naming a limit turned out to name a thing not yet done.

THE FRAME SCOPING OF THE EXIT WALK IS UNTESTED AND SAID SO IN PLACE. Deleting it changes nothing over today's record. Reopen when the record holds a corpus whose position facts cross frames; until then no test can tell the two readings apart, and this is stated in the walk rather than left for a later round to discover by trusting it.

THE EXIT AXIS COUNTS CORPORA, NOT CROSSINGS, AND THE TWO ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. Six corpora declare an exit; the walk that found them saw twelve individual ascents and twenty descents. The census carries the corpus-level split because that is the shape the refuted sentences are about ("no corpus has ever"), and a round that needs the step-level number has the walk but not the field.

A SUBMISSION IS A FACTS MANIFEST, WHICH COUNTS A STAGE AND ITS FIRST SUBMISSION AS TWO. That is deliberate — both are artifacts an author handed in and the record holds both — but it means the map-and-telling axis is not a count of AUTHORS. The claim it refutes is about what was produced, so the shape fits; a claim about how many authors did it would need a different denominator and does not have one today.

THE METER AXIS IS REFUSED RATHER THAN DEFERRED, and the resume condition is the failure of a named test rather than a line here. Round 941 already stated what would change it — an authored corpus that registers a meter — and that requires `FactsManifest` to grow the slot first. Nothing about this is waiting on effort.

A census there would report zero out of every corpus on record and read as a finding about what authors chose when it is a fact about the manifest schema — Round 854's rule, that a zero over a population with no door is not a clean bill, in the exact form it would have shipped in. The refusal is therefore carried as an executable condition: a manifest declaring a meter is imported through the real binary and the registry stays empty, with both halves of the non-vacuity asserted beside it. The day `FactsManifest` grows the slot that test fails, which is the day the census becomes worth building, and nothing has to remember. Round 986.decision_summary: R986 (MEASURE -> BUILD) — the agent-facing surface has 122 optional arguments, one of which anything proves the handler reads, and the reason nobody knew is that neither the compiler nor any test can say. Round 981 found that `population_census` had two write paths and that the second had never been executed, naming the failure a source scan cannot see: an argument that deserializes and is then read into nothing. It closed that one wire and left the shape of the rest unmeasured. This round measured it and built the accounting that makes it impossible to lose again. STAR THE COMPILER DOES NOT CATCH IT, PROVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Stopping one handler from reading one of its fields while the siblings are still read leaves `cargo clippy -D warnings` at exit 0. Removing `Debug` from the derive does not change that: `Deserialize` constructs the field and rustc counts construction as a use, so `dead_code` never fires. The compiler speaks only when the dropped field was the handler's ONLY read, and then it complains about the unused `args` binding rather than about the argument. STAR AND NO TEST CATCHES IT. With `query_term` stopped from reading `case_insensitive` the whole suite stays green — an agent asking for a case-insensitive search gets a case-sensitive one, reported as success, and the store or the answer it acts on is wrong with nothing anywhere saying so. That is the live form of the Round 981 defect and it is the reason this is a store-integrity question and not a tidiness one: the store is the agent's memory, and a mutation that silently does less than it was asked writes a wrong memory that reads as a right one. STAR THE POPULATION IS THE ROUTER'S OWN SCHEMA, NOT A LIST SOMEBODY TYPED, and that mattered immediately: reading the source for `#[serde(default)]` counts 88, while the schema an agent is actually shown carries 122, because an `Option` field is optional on the wire whether or not it carries the attribute. The gate walks `ToolRouter::list_all()` and takes every property absent from `required`, so the population cannot drift from what agents can send. STAR EVERY PAIR IS DECLARED EXERCISED OR NOT, AND NEITHER LIST MAY BE WRONG. A pair in neither list fails, so a new tool or a new optional argument cannot join the silent set by being added; a declared pair the router no longer exposes fails too, so the accounting cannot describe a surface that has gone. Both lists print on every run, because a check that reports only violations reads exactly like one with nothing to report (Round 854). Today that is 2 exercised against 120. STAR THE EXERCISED HALF IS DIFFERENTIAL BY CONSTRUCTION. A tool that ignores an argument still succeeds and still writes a record, so asserting on one store proves only that the tool ran; the pattern is two workspaces identical but for the argument, which must not end up with the same bytes. `add_entity.description` is that shape at its plainest — the argument is authored prose and a handler that drops it loses what the agent wrote while telling the agent it was saved. STAR AND THE COMMENT THAT ARGUED THIS WAS ENOUGH IS RE-POINTED IN THE SAME CHANGE. The Round 680 router smoke justified stopping at presence because "the tools are thin `run_mutate` wrappers over CLI-exercised atomic paths". Round 981 found a wrapper whose argument was never read. Round 987.decision_summary: R987 (BUILD) — the accounting Round 986 shipped had a hole in the half it was proudest of, and closing it is what made filling the list cheap. R986 walked the router's own schema for the 122 optional arguments an agent can send, declared each one exercised or not, and made a pair in neither list a failure. STAR BUT `EXERCISED` WAS A HAND-WRITTEN LIST, WHICH MEANS IT WAS A CLAIM THAT A TEST EXISTED AND NOTHING CHECKED IT. A pair could be lifted out of the silent set by editing one line, which is the exact move the gate was built to stop — an argument reading as covered while nothing exercises it is worse than one honestly named unexercised, because the first reads as assurance. This round found it the way such things are found: a script moved four pairs into `EXERCISED` and the tests it was supposed to move them with had not been written yet, and everything stayed green. STAR SO THE ROW AND THE TEST ARE NOW EMITTED BY ONE MACRO INVOCATION, AND THE COMPILER IS WHAT HOLDS THEM TOGETHER. `exercised!` generates `EXERCISED` from the same invocations that generate the test functions: a row cannot exist without its test, and deleting a case removes the row with it, so the pair falls back into the silent set and the gate fails naming it. STAR THE ONE CASE THE MACRO CANNOT EXPRESS IS SEPARATED RATHER THAN SMUGGLED IN. Round 981's `record_census` needs a workspace declaring a `[census] report` and its oracle is the shared resolver rather than a needle in the bytes, so it lives in `EXERCISED_BESPOKE` with the doc comment saying plainly that this list is weaker — nothing checks the named test exists — and that it is kept short for that reason. Naming the weakness is the difference between a second list and a loophole. STAR THE PATTERN IS DIFFERENTIAL AND ASSERTS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS, because they catch different failures: the store bytes must DIFFER with and without the argument, which catches the handler that ignores it, and the value must be FINDABLE in the bytes, which catches the handler that changes something else instead. A test with only the first would pass against a tool that stamps a timestamp. STAR FIVE ARGUMENTS MOVED OUT OF THE SILENT SET, all of them authored prose on a registry write — `add_entity`, `add_entity_kind`, `add_frame`, `add_parameter`, `add_unit`. That is the plainest shape of the harm and the right place to start: the agent writes a description, the tool answers success, and if the handler drops it the prose is gone with nothing anywhere saying so. The count is now 6 exercised against 116, and each further one is a line of data rather than a fresh piece of scaffolding.

Round 987.publishable_decision_summary: R987 (BUILD) — the accounting Round 986 shipped had a hole in the half it was proudest of, and closing it is what made filling the list cheap. R986 walked the router's own schema for the 122 optional arguments an agent can send, declared each one exercised or not, and made a pair in neither list a failure. STAR BUT `EXERCISED` WAS A HAND-WRITTEN LIST, WHICH MEANS IT WAS A CLAIM THAT A TEST EXISTED AND NOTHING CHECKED IT. A pair could be lifted out of the silent set by editing one line, which is the exact move the gate was built to stop — an argument reading as covered while nothing exercises it is worse than one honestly named unexercised, because the first reads as assurance. This round found it the way such things are found: a script moved four pairs into `EXERCISED` and the tests it was supposed to move them with had not been written yet, and everything stayed green. STAR SO THE ROW AND THE TEST ARE NOW EMITTED BY ONE MACRO INVOCATION, AND THE COMPILER IS WHAT HOLDS THEM TOGETHER. `exercised!` generates `EXERCISED` from the same invocations that generate the test functions: a row cannot exist without its test, and deleting a case removes the row with it, so the pair falls back into the silent set and the gate fails naming it. STAR THE ONE CASE THE MACRO CANNOT EXPRESS IS SEPARATED RATHER THAN SMUGGLED IN. Round 981's `record_census` needs a workspace declaring a `[census] report` and its oracle is the shared resolver rather than a needle in the bytes, so it lives in `EXERCISED_BESPOKE` with the doc comment saying plainly that this list is weaker — nothing checks the named test exists — and that it is kept short for that reason. Naming the weakness is the difference between a second list and a loophole. STAR THE PATTERN IS DIFFERENTIAL AND ASSERTS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS, because they catch different failures: the store bytes must DIFFER with and without the argument, which catches the handler that ignores it, and the value must be FINDABLE in the bytes, which catches the handler that changes something else instead. A test with only the first would pass against a tool that stamps a timestamp. STAR FIVE ARGUMENTS MOVED OUT OF THE SILENT SET, all of them authored prose on a registry write — `add_entity`, `add_entity_kind`, `add_frame`, `add_parameter`, `add_unit`. That is the plainest shape of the harm and the right place to start: the agent writes a description, the tool answers success, and if the handler drops it the prose is gone with nothing anywhere saying so. The count is now 6 exercised against 116, and each further one is a line of data rather than a fresh piece of scaffolding.
publishable_changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-mcp/src/main.rs` — `exercised!`, one macro emitting both the `EXERCISED` row and the differential test for each (tool, argument) pair. This is the repair: Round 986's list was a claim that a test existed, and this makes the claim and the test the same declaration.

Same file — five cases: `add_entity.description`, `add_entity_kind.description`, `add_frame.description`, `add_parameter.description`, `add_unit.description`. Each is a registry write whose optional argument is authored prose, which is the plainest form of the harm.

Same file — `EXERCISED_BESPOKE`, holding the one pair the macro cannot express (Round 981's `record_census`, which needs a `[census]` workspace and a resolver oracle). Its doc comment states that nothing checks the named test exists and that the list is kept short for exactly that reason.
Same file — the gate unions the three lists, so a pair declared in the generated set and the bespoke set at once fails as declared twice, and the printed line counts both as exercised.
publishable_verification_bullets: STAR THE HOLE WAS FOUND BY A FAILED EDIT, NOT BY REVIEW. A script moved four pairs into `EXERCISED` before their tests existed and the suite stayed green; that is the whole argument for generating the rows from the tests.

INJECTION K, one `exercised!` case deleted: the gate failed naming the pair, "1 of 122 agent-facing optional argument(s) are in neither list: [(\"add_unit\", \"description\")]". The row went with the test, which is the property the macro exists for.

INJECTION J, `add_frame` stops passing the description through: its differential case failed with "what the agent sent as `description` is nowhere in the store add_frame wrote", and the other eleven tests stayed green — the same measurement of invisibility Round 986 recorded, now with the case in place to catch it.

INJECTION J DID NOT APPLY ON ITS FIRST RUN AND THE GREEN WAS DISCARDED RATHER THAN READ. The anchor did not match the handler's actual body, so the suite passed with nothing injected; the anchor was re-read from the source and the injection re-run. A green under an unapplied injection is not evidence.
THE GATE'S OWN "DECLARED TWICE" ARM FIRED DURING THE WORK, when the four moved pairs were still listed as unexercised, so that assertion is exercised rather than decorative.

1503 workspace tests pass (1499 before), 0 failed, `--no-fail-fast`; clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean; `validate-workspace` T1 orphan 0 and T3 reject 0; entries and sections unchanged.
Every injection was reverted by restoring a COPY taken before it, and each was applied by a script asserting its anchor occurs exactly once — which is what caught the unapplied one.

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: 116 OF 122 REMAIN, AND THE REMAINDER IS WORK RATHER THAN A LIMIT. The five landed here are the cases needing no prerequisite call; the next band needs one setup call before the tool under test (an entity kind before `add_entity.kind`, a section before `add_section.parent_section`), which the macro does not take yet. That is a parameter to add, not a question to answer.

THE DIFFERENTIAL PATTERN PROVES AN ARGUMENT IS READ, NOT THAT IT IS READ CORRECTLY. The needle assertion narrows it — the value has to appear in the bytes — but a handler writing it into a neighbouring field would still pass. Where a tool has a CLI twin, that twin's answer is the stronger oracle, and Round 981's bespoke case is the example of using it.

`EXERCISED_BESPOKE` IS THE ONE PLACE THE COMPILER IS NOT HOLDING THE CLAIM. It has one entry today. If it grows, the reason is that the macro is missing an ability, and the answer is to give the macro that ability rather than to add a line here.

Round 988.decision_summary: R988 (BUILD) — the silent set goes from 116 to 102, and the two changes that made it possible are both about what the test can express rather than about how many were written. Round 987 tied each `EXERCISED` row to the test that earns it, and left the remainder needing two things the macro did not have. STAR THE FIRST IS A SETUP CALL, because most optional arguments are REFS: `add_entity.kind` names a registered entity kind, `add_section.parent_section` names an existing section, and neither can be sent at all until something else exists. The macro now takes any number of bracketed `given` calls that run on the same server before the tool under test, IN BOTH ARMS, so the difference the test asserts is the argument and never the setup. STAR THE SECOND IS THAT WHAT THE AGENT SENDS AND WHAT THE STORE SHOULD SHOW ARE NOT THE SAME STRING, and pretending they were is what a list-valued argument exposed: `parents` is sent as `["place"]` and lands as `place`. They are now separate — the value is what goes on the wire, the needle is what has to appear in the bytes — and separating them is more honest even where they coincide, since an id an agent sends can be normalised before it is stored. STAR AND SPLITTING THEM SURFACED A VACUITY THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED. The needle was asserted as PRESENT in the with-argument store, which discriminates for fresh prose and asserts NOTHING for a ref: the setup call has already written `place` into the registry, so `contains` is true in both arms and only the byte-difference was carrying the test. Six of the cases landed in this round are that shape. The assertion is now that the needle occurs MORE times with the argument than without — once for the registration, twice once something references it — which discriminates for both shapes. The injection says it plainly: with `add_entity_kind` stopped from reading `parents`, the failure reads "`place` occurs 1 time(s) without and 1 time(s) with". STAR FOURTEEN ARGUMENTS LEFT THE SILENT SET, all of them writes into the agent's own memory: the kind an entity is registered under, the parent a section is filed beneath, the symbol a binding names, the reason an inventory entry was closed, the refs and carried items an appended round states. What remains is 102 and it is the same table one line at a time.
changes_bullets: `crates/mnemosyne-mcp/src/main.rs` — `exercised!` takes bracketed `given` setup calls, run on the same server in both arms before the tool under test. Most optional arguments are refs and cannot be sent until the thing they name exists; without this the macro could only reach arguments that need nothing.

Same file — the case grammar separates the VALUE sent from the NEEDLE expected in the store (`."parents" = ["place"] seen "place"`), because a list-valued argument does not land as the string it was sent as, and an id can be normalised on the way in.

Same file — the needle assertion counts occurrences instead of asking whether the needle is present. A ref-shaped argument names something the setup already registered, so presence is true in both arms and asserts nothing.

Same file — fourteen further cases: `add_entity.kind`, `add_entity_kind.parents`, `add_section.parent_section`, `set_entity_kind_parents.parents`, `add_predicate.description`, `add_predicate.subject_kind`, `add_disclosure_plan.description`, `add_inventory_entry.reason`, `add_inventory_entry.source`, `set_inventory_status.reason`, `set_section_parent_section.parent_section`, `add_section_binding.symbol`, `append_changelog_entry.impact_refs`, `append_changelog_entry.carry_forward_bullets`. The count is 20 exercised against 102.
verification_bullets: STAR THE VACUITY WAS FOUND BY WRITING THE REF CASES, NOT BY REVIEWING THEM. Presence of the needle is true in both arms whenever the setup registered the id, which is every ref-shaped argument — six of this round's cases. The assertion was changed to compare occurrence counts before any of them landed.

INJECTION L, `add_entity_kind` stops reading `parents`: the case failed with "`place` occurs 1 time(s) in the store add_entity_kind wrote WITHOUT `parents` and 1 time(s) with it", which is the same evidence that the presence check would have passed. The other 25 tests stayed green.

THE INJECTION'S FIRST ANCHOR MATCHED TWO SITES AND WAS REFUSED RATHER THAN APPLIED TO BOTH — `add_entity_kind` and `set_entity_kind_parents` share a line — so it was re-targeted at the handler by position. A `count == 1` assertion is what made that visible instead of injecting two defects and reading one result.

FOUR CASES FAILED ON THEIR FIRST RUN BECAUSE THE FIXTURE USED VOCABULARY THE TOOLS REJECT, and each tool named the closed set in its own error (`default_mode` expects withhold|state|hint|imply; inventory status expects active|deprecated|reserved). The fixtures were corrected to the tools' vocabulary rather than the checks loosened.
THE GATE'S "DECLARED TWICE" ARM FIRED TWICE DURING THE ROUND, once per batch, while the moved pairs were still listed as unexercised — so the union of the three lists is checked rather than assumed.
1517 workspace tests pass (1503 before), 0 failed, `--no-fail-fast`; clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean; `validate-workspace` T1 orphan 0 and T3 reject 0.
Citation hygiene (R255): Round 987 verified present with `query --changelog-entry` and Round 988 verified absent before this entry was appended.
carry_forward_bullets: 102 OF 122 REMAIN AND THE MACRO NOW REACHES ALL OF THEM. What is left needs no new ability: `add_fact` and `amend_fact` carry ten optional arguments each and want a frame, a section and a predicate registered first, which is four `given` lines; the threshold and disclosure arguments want an edge or a plan. It is a table to fill.

COUNTING OCCURRENCES IS STRONGER THAN PRESENCE AND STILL NOT AN EQUALITY. A handler that wrote the argument into a neighbouring field of the same record would raise the count and pass. Where a tool has a CLI twin the twin's answer is the exact oracle, as Round 981's bespoke case uses; that is the upgrade path for any argument where the count proves too coarse.

THE `given` CALLS ARE NOT THEMSELVES EXERCISED BY THE CASE THEY SET UP. If a setup call silently ignored one of ITS optional arguments the case would still pass, since both arms run the same setup. That is correct — each argument is proven by its own case — but it means a `given` line is not evidence about the tool it invokes.
